title: NonFarm Payroll October 2026 Lecture
head: Unrealized dealing range / "Event horizon" (50% of a projected range)  (aliases ICT uses: event horizon, mid-range reading, finite specific arrays, "phantom zone")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / entry model component
- **What ICT says:**
  - "Event horizon" is his name for the midpoint (50%) of a dealing range that has not been fully realized yet: one end is a real, already-formed high (here the short-term high made after the NFP release), the other end is an old daily high that price has not reached (the June 22, 2026 daily high of the December NQ contract, 31,285).
  - It does not matter whether price ever gets to the old high. It is a forecast: "we're predicting, not reacting to price."
  - Both ends are "finite, specific arrays" that cannot be hidden; the middle of the range is the level to hunt for shorts because a price run into premium of that range is expected to be sold.
  - On its own, the event-horizon level means nothing. "Isolated levels are useless"; it needs a convergence of several smart-money concepts to be viable.
  - The market-efficiency logic: the new leg higher will leave buyers' sell-stops (sell-side liquidity) resting below the post-news low. Shorting from the event horizon gives willing sellers a lower target to pay out into.
- **How to identify:**
  1. Mark the 8:30 news release. Wait roughly 15-20 minutes into the session (do not guess ahead of it).
  2. Wait for a short-term high to form after the first rip and a retracement.
  3. Wait for price to take that short-term high out (a shift in market structure on the lower timeframe); only then can the unrealized range from that new high to the old daily high be measured. (He anticipates it before price gets there.)
  4. Draw a fib with the 50% (equilibrium) of that range; the 0.5 is the event horizon.
  5. Make sure the fib sits "on air" (anchored exactly on highs/lows, not on candle bodies).
- **How to use:**
  - Look for shorts at/near the event horizon when the daily draw is higher (he was bullish for the day but was fading a news-driven intraday run). He is "contrarian" intraday: he scalps against the grain of the daily range.
  - Stop loss goes above the entry array (above the gap's upper boundary / CE zone), not far above the level.
  - Set an extreme final take-profit (see Targets below) and bank partials along the way.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Dec contract, 1m, Friday of NFP week (October 2026 NFP; exact date not stated). At 8:30 NFP prints and price rips higher (price had been drawing up toward the old daily high; 9:30 opening came later). A short-term high forms at 8:38 (about 31,146.75, caption-garbled "838" and "31146.75 ... the high of that candlestick"). Price retraces, then rallies again through that high. Projecting the 8:38 high to the old daily high 31,285 gives a 50% level (his "event horizon") of about 31,216 (arithmetic from his numbers; he does not say the figure). Price trades up to the event horizon, where he sells.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:07:30](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=450) — explains the unrealized dealing range from the first high to the June 22 daily high
  - [0:10:42](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=642) — "if I know this level and this level, I want the middle of that range: event horizon"
  - [0:36:23](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=2183) — recap: two ways to use the high; mid-range reading is the event horizon
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He stresses this is "a volatility-based, news-driven, once-in-a-while scenario", not an every-day Silver Bullet-style setup, and "it's not going to appear every single time." Intended for advanced students who already have models; he says newer students should not try to copy it. Note: it relies on a prior directional draw (higher NQ prices).

title: NonFarm Payroll October 2026 Lecture
head: Pre-8:30 range framing + negative standard-deviation projections (-1, -1.5, -2, -2.5)  (aliases ICT uses: standard deviations, calibration, "pre-market session hours between 7:00 and 9")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - When a high-impact driver prints at 8:30, frame the range from 7:00 to 8:30 (not just a 9:00 reference): take the highest high and the lowest low between 7:00 and 8:30.
  - Anchor the fib on the low and draw it up to the high ("drawing it from low to high"), with negative levels so projections extend above the range.
  - He steps through the levels: -1 (a "big purple line"; one standard deviation delivered "beautifully" but he's "not interested at that level because it's isolated"), then adds 0.5 steps (-1.5, -2) and finally -2.5. The -2.5 level lands right on the event horizon midpoint, creating the convergence.
  - He claims this specific combination is not found in "retail books."
- **How to identify:** Draw 7:00-8:30 high/low on the 1-minute chart; extend negative levels on the fib's level list; note where one of them coincides with the event-horizon 50% (here -2.5).
- **How to use:** The convergence of the projection level and the event horizon is the zone to look for a short entry; then confirm with candle behaviour (below). Isolated single levels are not traded.
- **Example in this video:** 7:00 candle's high is the top of the pre-news range; lowest low also in 7:00-8:30 range. Fib low-to-high; -1 reached earlier (not used); -2.5 coincides with the event horizon zone. (Exact -2.5 price not stated.)
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:03:24](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=204) — frames the 7:00-8:30 range and anchors the fib low to high
  - [0:11:30](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=690) — "isolated levels are useless", walks through -1
  - [0:13:54](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=834) — -2.5 hits the event horizon: "I'm going to save you a lot of time. It's not [in the books]."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Caption wording of the level list is partly garbled ("add a 0.5 ... it's going to be two, -2 ... 2.5"); my reading is -1, -1.5, -2, -2.5. Mark as (caption unclear).

title: NonFarm Payroll October 2026 Lecture
head: Inversion FVG / SIBI that fails to reach its consequent encroachment (entry confirmation)  (aliases ICT uses: iFVG, sell side imbalance buy side inefficiency / "sibby", bearish fair value gap, consequent encroachment)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - After price runs into the event horizon, he sells while a bold bullish candle prints (an aggressive early entry of 3 contracts), then adds 3 more at the event-horizon line (2 fills), then one more as price starts to pass down through again.
  - Confirmation seen on candles: a bullish candle into the area "fails to touch the consequent encroachment" of the inverted gap; that failure shows weakness, "a weak member of the herd."
  - An inverted FVG must behave as a bearish FVG: price may poke up into the gap, even go into the upper quadrant (above the CE) briefly, but must leave quickly and the bodies must keep closing back down.
  - Stop loss sits just above the gap (he says "Stop loss above here is fine").
  - If price goes into the premium half of the gap, it "needs to stay there briefly and then leave" (like a wick that tags near the CE and immediately retreats).
  - Every upward poke into the gap is smart money selling into public buyers wanting all-time highs: "accumulation of shorts."
  - He refined his gap box during the trade (he cancelled one gap order, re-drew on the next break lower) and notes this is on the recording.
- **How to identify:** (1) a prior bullish FVG/BISI gets traded through to the downside = inversion; (2) the next candle(s) rally into it but do not reach its 50% (CE) or reach it only with a wick and close back below; (3) the following candle trades lower.
- **How to use:**
  - Enter short on those failures at/near the event horizon; stop above the array; use a trailing stop on what is left.
  - Take partials into the next imbalance and into rejection blocks (see below).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, after 9:00 (execution time not stated; before the 9:30 opening). Candle 1 prints bold bullish (he says "203 right about there", likely ~31,203, caption unclear); ICT sells 3 at that candle, 3 more at the red event-horizon line (2 filled), adds 1 more. Next candle tries up and fails at the CE; next candle lower. He sells again at the second SIBI, which tags CE then drops to the low of the previous candle's close/open (the entire SIBI). Partials at ~31,115 and ~31,140; "singles off" as it rebounds; final two contracts stopped at the trailing stop.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:19:27](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1167) — adds executions to the chart
  - [0:21:52](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1312) — candle fails to touch CE: why he sells there
  - [0:30:42](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1842) — second SIBI, stop above, reverts down
  - [0:31:31](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1891) — SIBI behaving as a bearish FVG; shorts accumulate in it
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He insists the whole read comes from each candle's open/high/low/close, "time-based", visible to all, not from volume or order counts. The caption renders "SIBI" as "sibby/cibby" and "buy side balance sell side efficiency"; the standard terms are SIBI = sell-side imbalance buy-side inefficiency and BISI the opposite.

title: NonFarm Payroll October 2026 Lecture
head: Waiting 15-20 minutes after a news release; fade the reaction rather than front-run it  (aliases ICT uses: two-stage delivery, "the wake", fading NFP)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Never position ahead of the 8:30 NFP number; he calls that guessing/gambling and says he lost heavily doing it in his 20s (indicators, signal services). Being right on direction does not save you.
  - Wait about 15-20 minutes into the session; see "what liquidity ... will be left in its wake."
  - After the first burst, look for a meaningful retracement and then measure from the resulting high; "whatever they do first, I will trade back into the range that was delivered because of the news."
  - Same for CPI and PPI ("I'm generally wrong" ahead of them; he calls NFP/CPI/PPI "the three-letter trades" to avoid). You do not have time to read the data, decide and execute, and limit orders will not work.
  - FOMC is "many times treated the same way": a move at 2:00, then at 2:30 usually a retracement the other way. Not always: sometimes the 2:00 move runs straight to the close (trend days "if you didn't get in, your chances are you're probably not getting in anyway").
  - He anticipates a deeper retracement going into the 9:30 opening after an 8:30 straight-up move.
- **How to identify:** a one-directional rip from 8:30 with no retracement; then the first pullback leaves a short-term high/low.
- **How to use:** trade the retracement back into the news range (shorts from premium after a rally, per this example); he wagers only part of his position for deeper levels.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:04:14](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=254) — do not position ahead of NFP; wait 15-20 min
  - [0:34:46](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=2086) — NFP/CPI/PPI "will hurt you"; no time for limit orders
  - [0:37:57](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=2277) — two-stage delivery; FOMC 2:00 then 2:30 reversal tendency
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He frames this for advanced, contrarian students only; do not encourage newer students to engage with NFP at all.

title: NonFarm Payroll October 2026 Lecture
head: Extreme final target and partials on news days  (aliases ICT uses: best case scenario, bank it, limit order at the extreme)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (trade management)
- **What ICT says:**
  - On news-driven trades he always places an extreme final take-profit way beyond what he expects, as a resting limit order, in case the move runs ("then you can sail off into the weekend").
  - But NFP can take unrealized profit away quickly, so partials must be banked along the way: "Just because it trades to your level and you haven't taken anything off, don't fall in love with it."
  - Here the best-case target was the low of the 8:30 candle (price came "real close" but did not deliver while he was still in).
  - He wagers only some of the position for the deeper levels; the rest is taken at nearby imbalances/rejection blocks.
- **How to use:** (1) enter on the failure/CE rejection; (2) take partials at fair value gaps/rejection blocks on the way; (3) trail the remainder; (4) leave a limit order at the extreme.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:17:52](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1072) — extreme target limit order, partials
  - [0:33:07](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1987) — singles off, trail stop takes the last two
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He reports a P&L "just less than $25,000" in under half an hour (futures, several contracts).

title: NonFarm Payroll October 2026 Lecture
head: Rejection block (body-based) and wick/body relationships as a PDA  (aliases ICT uses: rejection block, "another PDA")
body:
- **Kind:** example only / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - At the low of the drive down he looks "not simply at the low" but at the bodies: the area where the bodies stop is a rejection block; if trading there he wants some position off before it turns on him.
  - At the end of the session he shows two candles "sharing the space" with wick low and wick high; "see where the bodies are stopping? That's not random."
  - If he had been still in, he would have taken one off at the gap down there, just below the high of that candle.
- **How to identify:** a drop that leaves wicks with bodies clustering at a boundary; draw the wick extremes and mark where bodies stop.
- **How to use:** target/partial zone and a reaction point; no entry rules given.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:32:19](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1939) — rejection block at the low
  - [0:40:21](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=2421) — wick low/high and bodies stopping
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Only shown, not defined in detail.

title: NonFarm Payroll October 2026 Lecture
head: Keep the toolbox small: draw on liquidity first, a few PD arrays  (aliases ICT uses: note the draw on liquidity, "you only need a couple things")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (process)
- **What ICT says:**
  - The first lecture topic is knowing the draw on liquidity (where price is going and why). With that, you only need a couple of PD arrays: inversion FVG, bullish FVG, bearish FVG, a breaker, and perhaps an immediate rebalance (it signals speed afterward).
  - "You got 80% of this game licked" by spending time on why price should go to a specific level.
  - You do not need SMT, Commitment of Traders, volume profile or indicators on every trade. He did not use SMT today or yesterday, nor COT.
  - Choose the one PD array that clicks for you first; stay with what you identify easily in hindsight; do not chase new tools.
  - Futures markets share one high, low, open and close for everyone, so the candlestick's OHLC is the only data needed. He argues volume-profile traders already single out time but over a broad range of what has already happened; he predicts what is not there yet.
  - Do not look at the crowd: "I don't want to be where the majority is"; smart money hunts singly or in small packs and will be in the herd without doing what the herd does.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:27:28](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1648) — only a couple PD arrays; 80% rule; no SMT/COT needed
  - [0:23:26](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1406) — candlestick book vs volume totals
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Directly rebuts adding every concept from his channel to each trade.

head: RTH Opening Range Gap (Monday's / Tuesday's) as a draw on liquidity  (aliases ICT uses: regular trading hours opening range gap, "first minute fair value gap"-style gap between prior RTH close and 9:30 open)
body:
- **Kind:** example only / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Earlier in the week (Monday/Tuesday) he stated price would likely rise at least into the CE of Monday's RTH opening range gap; today (Wednesday) it did that and went on to close the whole gap.
  - Tuesday also has its own RTH opening range gap, shown on the 1-minute chart as a gray shaded zone from the gap to the opening price; price was "extended beyond" it.
  - Each session is read in relation to the previous session; ICT says this is what he has been suggesting "in terms of each session and how it relates to the previous session."
  - The chart is switched to regular trading hours to see these gaps clearly.
- **How to identify:** Set chart to RTH; gap between the prior day's RTH close and the 9:30 open; use its CE (50%) as the first target and the far edge as the full-fill target.
- **How to use:** As the target/draw for a long: aim for the CE, expect large-range candles once price clears the lower portion of the gap's remaining unfilled half.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily: small consolidation between lows and a high. 1m: Monday's RTH ORG is the large orange-shaded zone above price. At the 9:30 open price took out a low, rallied, hit Monday's gap CE, pulled back into a "weird consolidation," then rallied to close the entire gap.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:00:00](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=0) — daily view; prior call that price would go to Monday's gap CE
  - [0:02:28](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=148) — switches to RTH to show Monday's and Tuesday's gaps
  - [0:05:52](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=352) — 9:30 open takes the low, rallies through the CE of Monday's gap
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Caption says "early trading hours"; context makes clear it means regular trading hours (RTH). He says the gap was filled completely, "I didn't require it do the entire thing" for his own trade.

title: NQ AM Session Review 09/30/2026
head: News-driven failure swing / London-to-NY reversal during the 7:00-9:00 pre-market  (aliases ICT uses: failure swing, 7:00 hour reversal, news driver)
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price consolidated 7:00-9:00 until the 8:30 news release, then "rockets up." A bullish FVG formed in the failure swing at the 7:00 hour and the news sent price higher, running against everything London had done (London session had moved lower); anyone short got "destroyed."
  - Relatively equal lows sat below (he felt price "could have done a better job of going down for it" and was surprised it did not take them); the news instead drove the buy side.
  - On the morning of the video he posted a quiz on Twitter marking two blue price levels (a low and a high) and asked which would be purged first. The answer was the low at the 9:30 open, after the news had already pushed price up through the high.
- **How to identify:** Pre-market range 7:00-9:00 that holds until 8:30, then displacement on the news in the opposite direction of London.
- **How to use:** Useful as context: do not assume equal lows will be raided just because they are close; news can run the other side first.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:01:40](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=100) — 7:00-9:00 consolidation then rocket on the 8:30 news
  - [0:04:10](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=250) — London-to-7:00 reversal, failure swing, shorts destroyed
  - [0:04:59](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=299) — Twitter quiz of which blue level gets taken first
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The specific news item is not named in the transcript. No prices given.

title: NQ AM Session Review 09/30/2026
head: Inversion FVG entry (close-proximity market/buy-stop entry)  (aliases ICT uses: iFVG, inversion fair value gap, reclaimed bearish FVG)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example only
- **What ICT says:**
  - After the 9:30 open ran up into Monday's gap CE and made a small consolidation, he treated a small gap there as an inversion FVG, even though it was not annotated in his execution recording.
  - Two things were "blended": the top of the gap and the upper half of the wick. He did not get in on the initial drop or at the tap of the iFVG; he took a close-proximity entry instead: a market buy "just above that wick high." He says it would have been equivalent to a buy stop at that candle's high.
  - Stop was placed on the other side of the setup (exact level not clear in caption).
  - He expected large up-close candles because (a) the upper half of the gap he wanted to close had not yet traded, and (b) small ranges inside the consolidation, then "once we get above here, large ranges would incur" - a range-expansion expectation.
  - Management: partials taken on the way up, final order placed "on the out last octant" (caption unclear; likely a pre-set final target), exited on the highest candle. He wanted to add during the run but "didn't feel inspired."
- **How to identify:** a gap that gets traded through and reclaimed as the opposing type; small-range candles forming below the high; unfilled upper half of a higher-timeframe gap above as the draw.
- **How to use:** Enter at market or via a buy stop at the high of the candle sitting just above the wick, with a stop under the setup; target the unfilled gap above.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, 9:30-9:40ish (times not stated): the open takes the low, rallies up, hits Monday's gap CE, drops into a small consolidation. He buys just above a wick high, stops below, and price closes the entirety of Monday's RTH ORG. He scales out, last order at the final target, exits on the highest candle.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:06:42](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=402) — identifies the inversion FVG and the unfilled portion of Monday's gap
  - [0:07:29](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=449) — fill just above the wick high; same as a buy stop at that candle's high
  - [0:08:17](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=497) — why he expected large candles; fill, partials
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Mentions he could not get in during the drop or at the inversion FVG tag, i.e. a missed entry replaced by a worse-priced continuation entry.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** Entry on an iFVG anchored to Tuesday's opening range cap. The gap runs from a specific high to a specific low.
- **How to identify:** Formed within the structure of the Asian session; identified as a gap with defined anchor point to prior session opening range.
- **How to use:** Go long from the iFVG entry; expect price to run into liquidity pools above; use stop loss below the gap candle.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Asian session, iFVG goes long, price runs from ~18450 area into multiple liquidity pools above, eventually being stopped near 18720.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:09](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=9) entry, [0:09:28](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=568) first partial hit, [0:31:07](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1867) stop out.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The iFVG must be anchored to a clear structural reference (here, Tuesday's opening range cap) to be valid.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Used as a defensive support level; price should not go below the consequent encroachment (wick level) of prior gaps or structures. Used to verify viability of the trade; if price violates this, consider it a sign of deeper retracement.
- **How to identify:** Look at the wick extremes of prior candlesticks/gaps and their consequent encroachment levels.
- **How to use:** Place stop loss below the CE level; if price violates it, the trade is likely negated or needs restructuring.
- **Example in this video:** Multiple references to "don't want to see it go below the wick consequent encroachment" at ~18515 area; this acts as the final line of defense.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:16](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=916) explains CE concept, [0:24:01](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1441) details defensive use.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** CE is part of a 3-PD array defensive framework, not for entries, only for trade viability checks.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Double Tap Exit Strategy (Head Shot & Center Mass)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (exit management)
- **What ICT says:** Take profits at two tiers: head shot (best case target, full hit) and center mass (second tier, chest hit). Metaphor from shooting range: aim for the best target but take what you can get.
- **How to identify:** Identify multiple liquidity pools ahead; the highest is the head shot, the middle tier is center mass.
- **How to use:** Exit partial positions at each level to lock in profit and fund remaining runners; this reduces need to hit the ultimate target.
- **Example in this video:** First partial taken above 709 level (center mass), head shot targeted around Monday's opening range cap, then additional partials at event horizon midpoint (~725 area).
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:10](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=310) introduces double tap, [0:23:12](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1392) detailed metaphor.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a partition of larger trade, not required to hit single terminus.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Order Block (Defensive)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Part of the defensive PD array; the gap candle's order block (candle #2 in gap sequence) is used for stop loss placement. Don't place stop below the entire gap, but use the order block to bracket risk tightly.
- **How to identify:** The second candle in a fair value gap sequence.
- **How to use:** Stop loss is placed just below the order block candle's low, not the entire gap range.
- **Example in this video:** Stop is placed below candle #2 of the entry gap at the start; later tightened as profit accumulates.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:11](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=671) mentions "my stop is below the gap candle, number two candle in the gap."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Differentiates between gap range and order block placement for tighter risk management.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Volume Imbalance
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Gaps in candles showing imbalance; used to confirm continuation and measure next liquidity targets. Creates a "ladder" leading to higher prices as price respects each imbalance without filling them.
- **How to identify:** Visual gaps on the chart where no trading occurred between candles.
- **How to use:** Expect price to run over/respect volume imbalances; they don't require level 2 data or footprint analysis.
- **Example in this video:** Multiple volume imbalances identified as price runs upward; each is respected or targeted as the "ladder" unfolds.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:48](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=768) "everything becomes just like a little ladder, a step leading up to higher prices."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Volume imbalance does not require fancy tools; simple candlestick observation suffices.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Event Horizon (Measurement Method)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** When two pools of liquidity exist, measure the midpoint between them (event horizon); price can be taken off there as a partial, staggering exits.
- **How to identify:** Identify two clear liquidity pools; measure the distance between them.
- **How to use:** Exit partials at the event horizon to fund the position without requiring the final target.
- **Example in this video:** Event horizon measured between upper and lower liquidity pools; partials taken near midpoint (~725 area).
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:16](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=916) explains event horizon concept, [0:26:27](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1587) execution "if we can get five contracts off there."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Allows staggered profit-taking without single dependency on terminus target.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Stop Loss Placement Rule
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Never place stop so wide it covers excessive risk; use the order block (candle #2) of the gap. Must follow rules even if stop is tight; if stopped out, accept it — the rules protect you in the long run.
- **How to identify:** Mark the second candle low in the gap sequence.
- **How to use:** Tight stop below order block candle; raise stop as profit accumulates and trade proves viable.
- **Example in this video:** Initial stop below order block; raised multiple times as partials are taken and CE/support holds.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:11](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=671), [0:26:27](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1587) (raise stop after each partial).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Accept stop-outs; they prove the framework works by limiting damage when conditions fail.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Three-PD Array Defensive Framework
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Three price delivery (PD) arrays used defensively: (1) CE of entry gap, (2) Monday's opening range gap low, (3) buy-side liquidity / sell-side efficiency. If price violates all three levels, the trade is no longer viable and stop is triggered appropriately.
- **How to identify:** Identify three structural support levels on the chart.
- **How to use:** Use these to frame the risk/reward of the position; stop loss placed to respect all three. If price breaches all three, the trade's thesis is negated.
- **Example in this video:** Three defenses stacked at ~18440-18515 area; trade stopped out when price finally violates all three.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:01](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1441) details the three PDAs, [0:31:07](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1867) final stop out "below it."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a defensive framework, not for pyramiding new entries; it's for trade viability only.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Partial Exit / Position Pyramiding
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Add to position on dips into support; take partials at targets. Example: add 3 contracts here, remove 3 there. This funds the position so you don't need the final target to be profitable.
- **How to identify:** Track entry price, support levels (CE, order blocks, volume imbalances), and exit zones.
- **How to use:** Pyramid into weakness; distribute exits at multiple levels (head shot, center mass, event horizon, etc.). Never require single target.
- **Example in this video:** Initial entry, added 3 more contracts at support, partial off at ~709, another at center mass, more at event horizon; final runner left for ultimate target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:12](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=252) adds 3 more, [0:09:28](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=568) first partial, [0:23:12](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1392) discusses rationale.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Must respect support when adding; don't pyramid into weakness if price is breaking structure.

title: NQ December Asian Session Execution 09/29/2026
head: Opening Range Gap (Monday's RTH Open)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The high and low of the opening range from Monday's regular trading hours (RTH); used as reference level for support and target zones.
- **How to identify:** Identify the first candle(s) of Monday's regular trading hours (9:30 ET) and mark the high/low.
- **How to use:** Price running into these levels often encounters liquidity; use as target zones and support levels.
- **Example in this video:** Monday's RTH opening range gap low (~18530 area) used as target on the way up; also as support on pullbacks.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:57](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=57) "Monday's record trading hours open range gap cap," [0:13:37](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=817) "low of Monday's regular trading hours opening range gap low."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Must be identified correctly (Monday RTH, not Asian session or previous day).

title: NQ December Commentary 09/29/2026
head: First Presented Fair Value Gap (FPFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The first FVG that forms after session open, marking a specific time milestone. At 9:33 AM ET (33 minutes after 9 AM open), the first gap forms and becomes a reference tool for later intraday moves.
- **How to identify:** Mark the time of session open (9:00 AM or 9:30 AM ET); identify the first candlestick gap after that timestamp.
- **How to use:** Use as a breakout trigger and to measure subsequent moves; price often uses it for continuation or rejection tests.
- **Example in this video:** First presented FVG at 9:33 AM ET; price used it to break into liquidity, tested the midpoint consequent encroachment, and used lower quadrant as a discount sensitivity area.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:15](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=255) "33 minutes after 9:00 a.m. Eastern time, this is your first gap that forms," [0:05:54](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=354) "midpoint consequent encroachment of first presented fair value gap."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Only the very first gap after open qualifies; not every gap thereafter.

title: NQ December Commentary 09/29/2026
head: Opening Range Gap (Magnetic Attractor)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The high and low of the opening range (here, 9:30–11:00 AM for RTH); acts as a magnet attracting price repeatedly. Even if price fails to reach it on the first attempt, it will gravitate back to it.
- **How to identify:** Mark the opening range: for RTH open, use 9:30 ET and the first 1–2 hours of trading.
- **How to use:** Expect price to revisit opening range levels multiple times during the day; use as support, resistance, and target zones.
- **Example in this video:** Tuesday's RTH opening range gap low at ~18430; price drifted lower during NY lunch, then gravitated back up to the opening price (9:30 ET opening, anchored 30,708.75 on ES basis).
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:28](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=208) "today's regular trading hours opening range gap," [0:06:42](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=402) "So, while we didn't get to it here, look what it did. It gravitated right back up into it there."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Acts as a magnet even if initially missed; will be revisited intra-day.

title: NQ December Commentary 09/29/2026
head: Session-by-Session Price Behavior Framework
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Define market behavior by session:
  - **London session (2–5 AM ET):** Often trends (directional).
  - **Morning session (7–9 AM, then 9:30–11 AM):** May consolidate, then reverse, then consolidate again, then break.
  - **NY lunch (11:30 AM–1:30 PM):** May drift in one direction (often lower), testing new lows, then rallying back.
- **How to identify:** Note the timestamp and session name from market calendars.
- **How to use:** Anticipate the type of move each session typically delivers; don't expect sustained trends during consolidation sessions.
- **Example in this video:** London (2–5 AM): trended. 7–9 AM: consolidation. 9:30–11 AM: reversal then consolidation then broke lower. 11:30–1:30 PM: drifted lower, tried again, rally back.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:01](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=61) starts session breakdown, [0:02:40](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=160) "entering into the 2-hour New York lunch."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Not rigid; event-driven or gap-driven days may violate typical session patterns.

title: NQ December Commentary 09/29/2026
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE) as Extension Target
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** The CE of prior gaps (especially opening range gaps) acts as an upside target during rallies. For example, the CE of Monday's RTH opening range gap is an extension target that price may aim for.
- **How to identify:** Identify a prior gap; mark its wick extremes (the consequent encroachment point).
- **How to use:** Use as an intraday rally target; expect price to gravitate toward it if conditions are bullish.
- **Example in this video:** Monday's RTH opening range gap CE (midpoint) is identified as a likely target if price continues higher.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:28](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=208) "I'd like to see it trade to consequent encroachment," [0:07:30](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=450) "Monday's regular trading hours opening range gap consequent encroachment in the midpoint."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** CE is aspirational (what ICT "likes to see"), not guaranteed; price must prove capacity to get there.

title: NQ December Commentary 09/29/2026
head: Discount Sensitivity (Lower Quadrant of Opening Range)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** The lower half of the opening range gap can act as a discount sensitivity area. When price trades into the lower quadrant, it signals weakness but also provides a zone where buyers may step in.
- **How to identify:** Identify the opening range gap; divide it into quarters; mark the lower quadrant (lower 50%).
- **How to use:** Price testing the lower quadrant of an opening range is a discount opportunity for long entries (if other conditions align); it's a friction zone.
- **Example in this video:** Tuesday's RTH opening range gap's lower quadrant; price pulled back into it and used it as a support friction zone before rallying.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:54](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=354) "lower quadrant of today or Tuesday's regular trading hours opening range gap" used as discount sensitivity.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Not a guaranteed bounce point; context (overall trend, liquidity above) must confirm.

title: NQ December Commentary 09/29/2026
head: Liquidity Pools from Highs and Lows
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Each new high and each prior low holds resting liquidity. When price reaches a new high, that high becomes an anchor point for future buy-side liquidity; old lows hold sell-side liquidity.
- **How to identify:** Mark every swing high and every swing low on the chart.
- **How to use:** Use these as target zones; when price runs upward, look for highs ahead as resistance; when price runs downward, look for old lows as support.
- **Example in this video:** London session lows hold liquidity; Tuesday morning highs hold liquidity; these are identified as next salient levels.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:28](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=208) "buy side there" at opening range high, [0:07:30](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=450) "both of those are pools of liquidity that I think are going to be salient."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Not every high/low holds liquidity; only those that represent swing turning points.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Regular Trading Hours (RTH) Opening Range Gap
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The gap between Friday's 4:14 PM ET close (RTH settlement) and Monday's 9:30 AM ET open (RTH resume). This gap is the primary structural reference for intraday trading. Must be graded (divided into 8ths and 4ths with Fibonacci) to identify key levels (octant, quadrant, half, three-quarter closure points).
- **How to identify:** On daily chart with RTH only (not electronic hours): mark the close at 4:14 PM previous Friday; mark the open at 9:30 AM current trading day. The void between is the RTH opening range gap.
- **How to use:** Use Fibonacci to divide the gap into 8 equal points (octants). Lowest octant and lowest quadrant are failure points (if price can't even touch these, it's weak). Use standard deviations of the gap width for downside targets; -1 and -2 SD levels below the gap define key support zones.
- **Example in this video:** NQ opened lower on 09/28 (discount gap). Lowest quadrant and octant levels were identified around 18430 area. Two SD of the gap drop to ~18370 area, aligning with Thursday's daily low at 18370.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:36](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=396) "discount regular trading hours opening range gap," [0:07:26](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=446) "grade that by simply having the fib on it," [0:26:08](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=1568) standard deviations explained.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Do not confuse with "opening range" (first 30 minutes of session, 9:30–10:00). RTH opening range gap is overnight gap only, not intraday.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Standard Deviations of Gap Projections
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Use the width of the RTH opening range gap (high to low) as a unit. Extend one and two standard deviations below the low of the gap to project downside targets. These levels often align with prior daily liquidity (e.g., Thursday's low), making them high-probability targets.
- **How to identify:** Measure gap high to gap low. Subtract that distance once (-1 SD) and twice (-2 SD) from the gap low.
- **How to use:** Expect price to run toward -1 SD first; if that fails, -2 SD becomes the ultimate target. If both align with daily structure (e.g., daily low), conviction is high.
- **Example in this video:** RTH opening range gap low ~18430; gap width ~60 points. -1 SD projects to ~18370; -2 SD projects to ~18310. Thursday's daily low sits at ~18370, confirming the -1 SD as salient.
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:08](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=1568) "standard deviations and projections," [0:27:43](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=1663) "negative one level," [0:28:29](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=1709) "two standard deviations."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Not taught by other frameworks (volume profile, Elliot Wave, etc.); unique to ICT methodology.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Macro Times (Spooling Windows)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Algorithmic order clustering at specific times: last 10 minutes of every hour + first 10 minutes of the next hour (e.g., 10:50–11:10 AM ET). Institutions schedule major order flow into these windows to avoid moving the market aggressively. During macro time, price "spools" (elongates, protract, creates volatility) because order flow arrives scheduled, not reactive. Volume doesn't need to be high; one contract can create movement if order flow is timed.
- **How to identify:** Mark 10:50, 11:50, 12:50, 1:50 PM ET, etc., on 1-minute chart.
- **How to use:** Anticipate major price moves into and out of macro times. If first 10 minutes (10:50–11:00) don't show spooling, expect it in the last 10 minutes (11:00–11:10). Use macro time perspective to know when to expect momentum and when to wait.
- **Example in this video:** Market dropped into macro window 10:50–11:10 AM ET, hitting the two-SD target of the RTH opening range gap and Thursday's daily low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:00](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2100) "The market trades down into 1050," [0:35:48](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2148) detailed macro window logic.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Criticism that macros don't exist (e.g., from fake students) is ignorance; ICT emphasizes macros are not about volume, they're about order-timing spooling.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Order Flow (Real Definition vs. Volume Misconception)
body:
- **Kind:** definition (correcting misconception)
- **What ICT says:** Real order flow is NOT the number of buys/sells at a level (that's past execution, not flow). Flow is movement timing: *when* orders are scheduled to arrive on the market (macros, algorithmic clustering). Price movement is caused by order *timing* and the *rate of change*, not by contract count. You only need one contract to create price movement if order flow timing is right.
- **How to identify:** Observe candlestick bodies and wicks; where they close relative to key levels (octant, quadrant, half) indicates institutional intent (whether they're done pushing or continuing).
- **How to use:** Don't count volume; instead, observe body placement. Body closing above/below key level = bullish/bearish intent. Consistent pattern of bodies failing to reach a level = weakness confirmed.
- **Example in this video:** Bodies failing to touch the -2 SD level and the daily low at open signaled weakness (bearish). Later, bodies staying in upper half of wick and below 9:30 open signaled exhaustion of the move upward (time to exit).
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:31](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=691) "real order flow is" bodies and wicks, [0:12:18](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=738) flow is movement state, not past execution.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicitly contradicts volume profile, VSA, footprint analysis, Level 2 data fixation; volume followers are chasing past data, not predicting next data.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE) of Daily Wicks
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** On the daily chart, each candlestick has a wick (high-low extremes). The midpoint of that wick is the consequent encroachment. For daily chart support, look for the CE of the prior day's wick (e.g., Thursday's wick CE is a magnet for bounces on Friday and the following session).
- **How to identify:** On daily chart: mark the high and low of a candlestick; divide by 2 to find the midpoint.
- **How to use:** Intraday, if price reaches the daily low, the CE (half-wick) often acts as a secondary target (bounce area or accumulation zone). If body doesn't go below CE, price may consolidate there before continuing.
- **Example in this video:** Thursday's daily low 18370; its wick CE 18456. Intraday, price bounced and accumulated at the wick CE level (showing institutional buying).
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:29](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=149) "midpoint or consequent encroachment," [0:04:09](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=249) CE used as support.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Must be identified on daily chart first; intraday charts then reference these levels.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) Entry Mechanics
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** When a wick extends beyond a gap, grade that wick (high to low) and measure its midpoint. Price trades into that wick's midpoint and bounces. The wick becomes an "inversion FVG" entry zone: buy into the lower half of the wick; expect the bounce to use the gap as a target.
- **How to identify:** Identify a wick that extends into the gap below. Grade the wick (high to low). If price enters the lower half of the wick zone, it's an inversion FVG entry.
- **How to use:** Enter long into the lower half of the inversion wick; stop below wick low; target the gap high or gaps above.
- **Example in this video:** Morning inversion FVG identified in the wick below the opening range. Entry at ~18397; stop below ~18370.
- **Timestamps:** [0:43:01](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2581) "inversion fair value gap," [0:47:55](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2875) entry execution "not sexy, but it fits the criteria."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Differs from standard FVG (which is above price, not below).

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Institutional Referral Entry Drill
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** When price comes down to a discount zone (lower quadrant, half-wick, or consequent encroachment of a daily chart structure) and bodies accumulate there without closing below, institutions are "drilling" — establishing entries at discounted prices before pushing higher. This accumulation is a buy signal.
- **How to identify:** Price pulls back to a low or support level; candle bodies cluster around the midpoint of that level without closing below; bodies show minor wicks (tight closes).
- **How to use:** When you see this institutional drilling, expect the next push to target higher liquidity. This is a low-risk entry point.
- **Example in this video:** Accumulation at Thursday's wick CE (18456) and at half-wick before final push higher at 11:10 AM macro window.
- **Timestamps:** [0:44:38](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2678) "institutional referral entry drill," [0:49:32](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2972) "institutional order flow entry drill at last Thursday's consequent encouragement."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Key concept for identifying institutions buying at discounts.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Narrative Technique (Retail Expectation vs. Smart Money Direction)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Retail traders are fed narratives (news, headlines) that prime them to expect a certain direction. Smart money trades *opposite* to the retail narrative to "clean out" stop losses. Example: morning news suggests US-Iran talks may calm tensions (bullish narrative), so retail expects higher prices. ICT went short because the chart structure (gap, daily low targets) was bearish, opposite the narrative.
- **How to identify:** Read the morning news; note what retail would expect; look at daily chart structure and identify where smart money likely targets (often opposite retail direction).
- **How to use:** Use narrative as a contrarian indicator; when retail is primed bullish, check if daily structure is bearish, and vice versa.
- **Example in this video:** Geopolitical news (US-Iran talks) primed retail bullish; daily chart structure and gap projections targeted downside; ICT shorted and hit the low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:14](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=1034) "bit of business come out today," [0:22:53](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=1373) "I don't believe that the news headlines can be consistently and routinely used," [0:24:30](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=1470) "narrative that would be viewed as bullish by less informed street money."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Narrative is a filter, not a rule; chart structure is primary.

title: NQ AM Session Low Of Day Long Review
head: Bodies and Wick Placement as Order Flow Signature
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** The location where a candle's body closes relative to key levels (octant, half-wick, gap low, etc.) reveals institutional intent. Body below level = weakness. Body above level and closing at upper portion = strength. Bodies clustering around a support = drilling/accumulation. Bodies closing below key support = breakdown imminent.
- **How to identify:** Mark key levels on chart; observe each candlestick's body location relative to those levels.
- **How to use:** Use body placement as confirmation of reversal or continuation; bodies failing to reach expected level = signal to exit or reverse.
- **Example in this video:** At open, bodies couldn't touch the -2 SD or daily low = bearish. Later, bodies staying in upper half of wick and not closing above 9:30 open = bullish move exhausted, time to exit.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:07](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=787) "look where it closes below," [0:16:24](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=984) "two signatures," [0:46:19](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2779) "bodies staying inside of the upper half of that wick."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Simplicity: open, high, low, close + time = all you need.

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: Inside Days (Back-to-Back Range Containment)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When two consecutive days' trading ranges do not extend beyond each other's highs and lows, they form "inside days." Example: Monday high, Monday low, Tuesday high, Tuesday low all remain within a contained band. This pattern signals consolidation before a breakout (usually 3 or more days before expansion).
- **How to identify:** Mark Monday's high and low; mark Tuesday's high and low; if all four points remain clustered (not extending beyond each other), it's inside days.
- **How to use:** Expect range expansion after inside days (usually within 1–3 days). Use the inside day highs/lows as breakout boundaries.
- **Example in this video:** Monday and Tuesday formed inside days; price was contained until Wednesday FOMC, when it broke downward through the Monday low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:48](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=168) "inside days back-to-back."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Not a guarantee of expansion; FOMC or other catalysts trigger the breakout.

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: Relative Equal Highs / Lows (REH/REL)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Swing highs or lows that are at approximately equal prices across multiple sessions. When price reaches REH or REL, it often acts as liquidity resistance/support. Breaking above REH or below REL confirms directional bias.
- **How to identify:** Mark all swing highs across multiple sessions; identify those at similar price levels = REH. Same for lows = REL.
- **How to use:** Use as breakout trigger; wait for close above REH or below REL to confirm direction; buy-side liquidity rests at REH, sell-side at REL.
- **Example in this video:** Tuesday's high and Monday's high are at similar levels (REH); price pierced this twice on Wednesday pre-FOMC, then broke through on the second attempt post-FOMC.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:24](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=264) "relative equal highs," [0:05:12](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=312) "Tuesday's daily high and the relative equal highs... we pierced that already at 2:00."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Visual smoothness of REH/REL (when charted) indicates strength of the liquidity level.

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: Daily Suspension Block
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A price zone between consecutive daily lows (e.g., between Monday low and Tuesday low) that acts as a consolidation area. During FOMC or other big moves, price often targets this zone as a mid-range support before continuing lower (or higher, depending on direction).
- **How to identify:** Identify the low of day N and day N+1; the void between them is the suspension block.
- **How to use:** Expect price to trade into this block during large directional moves. It acts as a magnet or rest area before continuation.
- **Example in this video:** Daily suspension block shaded between Monday and Tuesday lows (around 18650–18600 area); post-FOMC, price targeted this block and then broke below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:20](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=500) "daily suspension block that's shaded in blue," [0:10:47](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=647) "sets the stage and tone for the market wanting to reach down into that daily suspension block."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First FOMC meeting may see wider suspension block testing due to uncertainty; ICT took partials rather than running full to Monday low.

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: FOMC Two-Stage Delivery
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** FOMC meetings typically deliver price moves in two stages: (1) pre-decision expectation move (before announcement), (2) post-decision response move (after announcement). Price may test resistance twice before breaking, using the second break to enter the main directional move.
- **How to identify:** Track price action in hours before FOMC announcement (usually 2 PM ET); observe the pre-move rally/sell-off; then watch the post-announcement move.
- **How to use:** Anticipate two attempts at resistance (REH/REL); the second break often confirms the direction. Entry on the second break is lower-risk.
- **Example in this video:** Pre-FOMC, price pieced Tuesday's high at 2:00 PM, came down, then at 2:40 PM (post-announcement ~2:15 PM) broke through again and continued downward.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:12](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=312) "FOMC is usually a two-stage delivery," [0:14:00](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=840) "2:40 to 2:50 p.m. Eastern time that's usually when the sweet spot entry forms."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First FOMC with new Fed chair may be more volatile; ICT's caution about taking earlier partials reflects this uncertainty.

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) Post-Breakout Entry
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** After price breaks above a resistance level (REH/REL), look back for any inefficiency (gap or imbalance) formed just before the breakout. That inefficiency becomes an iFVG entry zone; price often retraces into it, allowing a pullback entry into the confirmed direction.
- **How to identify:** Identify the breakout point (close above REH); look back 1–3 candles for a gap or volume imbalance (candlestick body doesn't cover entire range).
- **How to use:** Enter into the iFVG when price pulls back; stop below the wick low; target the next liquidity.
- **Example in this video:** After breaking REH, price created an iFVG at 29,467–29,483 range; this became the retracement entry zone.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:47](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=407) "inversion fair value gap," [0:08:20](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=500) "absolute characteristics of an inversion fair value gap."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Must identify within the context of a confirmed breakout (two-stage FOMC pattern, in this case).

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: Swing Projections (Fibonacci Expansion)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** After identifying a swing low and high, use Fibonacci expansion (100%, 150%, 200% of the swing range) to project downside targets. Example: measure wick from high to low; add equal distance below the low (100%) or 1.5x the distance (150%) to find support zones.
- **How to identify:** Mark a swing high and low; measure the distance; project downward from the low using multiples of that distance.
- **How to use:** Use these projections alongside other support levels (daily lows, suspension blocks) to confirm targets.
- **Example in this video:** Wick from high to low measured; 100% projection taken below low confirms alignment with daily suspension block and Monday low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:59](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=599) "swing projections," [0:09:59](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=599) "100 percentiles to the range."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Not magic; just mathematical extension of price structure.

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: Volume Imbalance in Candlesticks
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When a candlestick's body doesn't fill the gap between the prior candle's close and current candle's open, a volume imbalance exists. If the body doesn't touch the wick extremes, the imbalance is even more notable. This signifies institutional step-and-repeat movement.
- **How to identify:** Look for gaps between candle bodies (not filled by wicks); note bodies that stay within upper or lower half of the wick.
- **How to use:** Use as entries into the imbalance zone; expect price to respect the imbalance.
- **Example in this video:** Body at open 29,467; prior close 29,467 even (no volume imbalance at open); but wick highs created imbalance above and below the body.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:47](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=407) "volume imbalance there, you can see between the difference between the bodies."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Must also check if candlestick wick high has a gap (if body's gap is too small).

title: NQ Dec Futures September FOMC Trade Review
head: FOMC Sweet Spot Timing (2:40–2:50 PM ET)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Historical pattern: FOMC decisions are typically announced ~2:15 PM ET (15 minutes before end of statement release). The sweet spot entry window is 2:40–2:50 PM ET (25–35 minutes post-announcement), when initial reactions have played out and institutional orders begin clustering. This 10-minute window often marks the beginning of the main directional move.
- **How to identify:** Mark 2:40–2:50 PM ET on 1-minute chart on FOMC days.
- **How to use:** Avoid trading the first 15–25 minutes post-announcement (initial whipsaw); wait for 2:40 PM window; enter confirmed direction at that time.
- **Example in this video:** Entry executed at 2:43 PM ET, matching historical sweet spot.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:00](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=840) "2:40 to 2:50 p.m. Eastern time that's usually when the sweet spot entry forms," [0:14:00](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=840) "2:43 baby."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Based on historical observation; not guaranteed every FOMC.

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: Backtesting properly (ICT's method): recorded price, hypothetical trades, no market replay
body:
- **Kind:** rule | process
- **What ICT says:**
  - Do NOT use market replay. It shows you a candle's open and then its close; you miss the "breath and lifespan" of each candle: how it opens, the flurry, whether it makes a higher high or lower low while still active, where it settles. The logic applies at any timeframe (1m to weekly); "1-minute chart's not moving any faster than the weekly chart." Replay-based mentors pause and describe, which he calls shameful.
  - Instead, watch recorded price action (live or delayed data both work, because you are studying price that has already happened). On Windows: hold Alt + Windows key and tap R to start a screen recording (microphone on) and record observations in your own voice; avoid a screensaver coming on. Free TradingView real-time data is not necessary; he says real-time data is cheap ("$7 on TradingView") and he will not pay for students' data feeds.
  - Backtesting = pattern recognition and characteristic observations; "all setups are not equal ... they rhyme" and don't have an identical fingerprint but share key characteristics. Record small deviations from what you expect.
  - Minimum: 6 weeks of back data and then 6 weeks forward (live/recorded) — "I promise you your ability to see price action will be so far ahead." Repetition conditions the subconscious so you can read the tape live.
  - Define "backtesting" as: a hypothetical entry, a hypothetical stop, and how price delivered. Don't just take a picture after the fact; trace over every individual candlestick (e.g., a candle that opened and traded right back up to the previous candle's low = "immediate rebalance"; a retrace that stops "shy of the close" is only respecting the wick). Use empty chart space with A/B/C legend markers for longer explanations.
  - Add price notes (TradingView "price note") to anchor exact prices of key highs/lows/opens/closes; increase font size. Be precise: his analogy is a cash business, where missing $2.25 of a 562.25 vs "560-ish" matters because "it's your business." Precision in logging is a precondition for precision in trading.
  - Log charts as annotated static pictures or electronically; don't worry about a naked chart if you annotate. Review everything on the weekend.
- **How to use:** Record each day's 7–9 pre-market range, opening range, 10:00 hour, annotate hypothetical entries, stops and targets as if real; compute risk, drawdown and heat.
- **Example in this video:** NQ (September 2026 delivery contract per the caption) 1-minute day, logged with pre-market range, RTH gap and 10:00 hour annotations (below).
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:37](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=157) — market replay is useless; [0:03:25](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=205) — lifespan of each candle; Alt+Win+R recording; [0:05:49](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=349) — 6 weeks back, 6 weeks forward; [0:21:37](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1297) — what backtesting is: hypothetical entry, stop, delivery, trace each candle; [0:43:52](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2632) — avoid replay "like the plague."
- **Nuance / caveats:** Strong claims: AI/software "can't see the subtle nuances"; reading a candle while it is forming (rather than waiting for the close) is the skill. The rest of the video's rhetoric about complainers and begging for funded challenges is skipped.

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: Pre-market range (7:00–9:00 a.m. ET): grading and projecting it  (aliases: "pillar 1", "pre-market session hours")
body:
- **Kind:** rule | definition (recap of part 4 plus how to chart it)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Pillar 1: the pre-market session hours, 7:00 to 9:00 a.m. ET. Mark the highest high and lowest low and the relative equal highs and lows inside that range; determine its phase (consolidation, trending/expansion) and how that usually impacts the morning session.
  - Draw a Fib across the 7–9 range to grade it, then stop the lines at 9:00 a.m. (he teaches his son to do so), and project them into the day, so that when you grade the opening range (9:30–10:00) you can see whether any opening range levels agree with the pre-market levels; agreement makes them stronger key levels for the PD array framework.
  - The algorithm "will absolutely refer back" to relative equal highs and lows inside the 7–9 range.
- **How to use:** The pre-market high/low is a reference for sells/buys, qualifier for a fair value gap, and a draw.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: at 9:30 price rallied away from the pre-market high, created a high, then sold off from a premium bearish FVG for over 100 handles (he later says 94 handles from the pre-market key level); price retraced into the CE of the bearish FVG and the pre-market session high (they coincided), then moved lower to clear relative equal lows from pre-market at 29,370.50 (caption value). The prior premium high acts as discount when price later trades above it. He stresses writing a confident observation ("I was pleased to see how the pre-market session high was used to qualify a key level for the (caption: 11:09) a.m. FVG").
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:45](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=585) — fib across 7–9 and stop lines at 9:00; [0:15:14](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=914) — premium high flipping to discount; [0:16:01](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=961) — pre-market high qualifies the FVG; [0:16:50](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1010) — relative equal lows 7–9 as target.
- **Nuance / caveats:** The FVG time ("11:09 a.m.") in the caption is garbled/unclear (price run 100+ handles stated at first; 94 handles from the key level later).

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: Hypothetical trade framing on a bearish FVG (entry at CE or lower half, stop at the high + 1 tick)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model | refinement (backtest convention)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Realistic hypothetical entry: consequent encroachment of the bearish FVG, or one tick below it (never "I would have sold the exact high"). Characteristic of a bearish FVG: if order flow is bearish the BODY should stay below the high (wicks can occur above, "they can do the damage"). Entering in the lower half is where "premium sensitivity" exists. If price goes higher into the upper half you can note an add/pyramid opportunity (one more contract).
  - Stop: the high of the candle plus one tick (record the high of any candle that wicks above). He wants stops logged as real hard stops, not labeled "hypothetical." Entry at or one tick before the level is "permissible" since you need to be filled.
  - Target: the pre-market buy-side/premium high area (the point where you calculate the hypothetical return).
  - You will be forced to size small (micros) when the stop is wide; build realistic expectations: "you have no skill yet, no experience yet"; don't fantasize about quitting your job in 3 weeks.
  - He does not think in reward-to-risk because his concepts are "already built in 3:1, 5:1" (setups generate that by default).
  - Record: total risk, the drawdown/heat the idea incurred, how many minutes and how many points price moved against you before working. This conditions you to know that wanting to be in does not mean it moves in your favor immediately; market replay never conditions you to live in the drawdown.
  - Partials: hypothetically two micros; take one off at the low-hanging fruit (relative equal lows / the 10:00-hour low), and over time condition yourself to hold for longer protractions toward the pre-market (7–9) relative equal lows.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: relative equal highs made, then price up into a bearish FVG; hypothetical short at CE (-1 tick), stop at the candle high +1 tick, target back down into the pre-market buy-side/premium region; sell reference quoted as 29,562.25 for what NOT to claim as an exact top.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:38](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1058), [0:18:26](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1106) — CE entry and body-below-high rule; [0:19:13](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1153) — pyramid, stop +1 tick, target; [0:41:28](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2488) — record risk and drawdown; [0:43:04](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2584) — partials on two micros.

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: Positive, confident journaling ("love letters to yourself") to build pseudo experience
body:
- **Kind:** rule (psychology/journaling)
- **What ICT says:** In your annotations write only constructive praise and confident observation ("I love how ...", "I was pleased to see ..."), never second-guessing, anger, or dollar losses. The subconscious wants comfort; writing it as if you knew builds confidence and speeds up experience ("pseudo experience" that converts into usable experience). Even when you start trading real money and lose, record what you should have seen, as if you did it that way; do not log "I lost $25,000" or "I blew the account." Your journal is private; you can express excitement at first-time observations without fear of being judged. "You have to parent that inner child that eventually will grow up to be an adult trader." Fill the chart's empty space with details every day for weeks.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:22](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=682), [0:12:08](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=728), [0:23:13](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1393), [0:23:59](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1439).
- **Nuance / caveats:** This is his stated recommendation (and a controversial one); it conflicts with the usual "journal your mistakes" practice, so flag it as his view for the book.

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: RTH Opening Range Gap: discount/premium definition, mid gap, and -1.0 fib projections
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule | refinement (new: standard-deviation projections)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Use the regular trading hours (RTH) chart, not electronic. Reference points: the previous day's RTH closing price (final print 4:14 p.m. ET on the 1-minute chart) and the 9:30 a.m. opening price. Between them is the opening range gap. Opening lower than the settlement = DISCOUNT opening range gap; opening higher = PREMIUM opening range gap. Where it opens at 9:30 determines the type.
  - Watch how the consequent encroachment (mid gap) is traded to after the open.
  - New: Fib standard-deviation projections off the gap. Draw the fib from the open to the settlement and add -1.0: the level hits the high of the AM session; draw from the settlement to the open and add -1.0: it hit the AM session low "to the tick" (also a further "duplicated down" projection of the 69-handle range delivered the lunch-macro lower low — caption unclear).
  - RTH relative equal highs and lows (smooth areas formed in the last 15–20 minutes of the previous day's trading, "previous market on close macro") must be observed in RTH view because the gap will refer back to them; it doesn't matter if electronic-hours price (London/Asia) already traded through them.
  - Record the range from low to target and what it offered; assume you took a trade idea there.
- **How to identify:** Chart set to RTH; previous day last 1m candle 4:14 p.m. close vs 9:30 open.
- **How to use:** Expect the CE (mid gap) to be traded to; project -1.0 fibs from the gap for AM-session extremes; use RTH-smooth highs/lows as references; log the gap size in handles and the time the CE was delivered.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: discount opening range gap of 69 handles. At 9:30 first candle wicked but did not take out the low; a second attempt, then price rallied to the RTH CE (mid gap) just 5 minutes after 9:30. The AM session high was nailed by the -1.0 projection; the AM session low (caption: 29,386.25, at about 11:12 a.m. ET) was nailed initially by the -1.0 projection from settlement to open, then swept by a later lower low; price subsequently worked inside the gap with a lunch-macro draw toward 10:00-hour lows and delivered to a "perfect standard deviation" (69 handles) lower — "to a tick."
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:47](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1487) — RTH, 4:14 p.m. settlement; [0:25:33](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1533) — discount vs premium gap; [0:26:22](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1582) — 69-handle gap, CE hit within 5 minutes; [0:27:11](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1631) — -1.0 projection hits AM high; [0:27:57](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1677) — -1.0 hits AM low; [0:28:45](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1725) — RTH smooth highs/lows.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the first stated use of -1.0 (standard deviation) projections for the opening range gap in these notes; whether he applies the same projection up and down on each day is not fully clear from captions. He says doing this trains "turtle soup" (pattern recognition of stop runs).

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: First Presented FVG (10:00 hour / Silver Bullet) and First Presented FVG with Displacement  (aliases: "first instance of FVG", "reflection FVG")
body:
- **Kind:** definition | refinement | entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Silver Bullet 10:00 hour: always mark 10:00 on the chart, but not as a vertical line across the whole chart, so you can see whether the 10:00 candle forms an imbalance.
  - Definition: the first presented FVG is "by definition the very first fair value gap, absolutely the very first one." It was taught the day before this video (classification and rule). Highlight it. But "there has to be something in here to make us want to be short": by itself it is not enough. You are "blending conceptual ideas to build a very strong narrative."
  - Narrative blend in the example: (1) first FVG at 10:01 (a SIBI created by a down-close candle; he marks the gap between one candle's high and a later candle's low); (2) the lunch macro: the market will seek a low that forms during the 10:00 hour — so shorting right on the candle that formed that low isn't wise; (3) a relative equal low next to the 10:00 low; (4) price retraced up, cleared minor buy side, tagged the gap and did not close outside it while closing below its midpoint = "wonderful shorting opportunity."
  - Upgrade: First presented FVG WITH DISPLACEMENT: a later up-close candle (BISI) that also takes out highs, i.e., displaces higher, leaving a range. He says it "takes greater command over price delivery than a simple initial formation" and "trumps" the first one. This BISI candle is also a "reflection fair value gap" in addition to being a bearish inversion FVG of the first gap (the first gap was from a down-close candle).
  - Two shorting uses: (a) with price up there, short toward the rejection block (the lowest down-close candle) and the low formed in the 10:00 hour — you don't need that low to be taken because it is formed within the 10:00 hour structure, the pullback target of the lunch macro; (b) a second opportunity when price returns to relative equal highs (minor buy side) and creates a second FVG that is lower than the first, with wicks not outside it and bodies not closing at the midpoint (trading in the lower half) — order flow bearish.
  - Entry: anywhere in the lower half of that FVG ("the most realistic for you"). Stop: the high of the last candle whose OPEN is outside the buy-side imbalance/sell-side inefficiency (not just a wick), +1 tick, and include the volume imbalance (two buy-side bodies) in that frame. That makes the stop wide, forcing micros.
  - Targets: first partial at the 10:00-hour low/relative equal lows (low-hanging fruit, lunch macro); a longer hold toward the 7–9 a.m. pre-market relative equal lows. Hypothetical: two micros, one off at the first target.
  - The dealing range / opening range is 30 minutes (9:30–10:00); "I don't care how many people tell you it's a 5-minute or 15-minute opening range ... they're all wrong."
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, 10:00 hour (day unspecified; caption): first FVG at 10:01 (SIBI); price rallied, made a BISI with displacement above highs, returned to the first gap, closed below its midpoint, sold off — "NQ used the first presented FVG to sell off for over 175 handles."
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:07](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1867) — Silver Bullet hour, how to mark 10:00; [0:32:41](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1961) — first presented FVG definition; [0:33:33](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2013) — lunch macro low formed in the 10:00 hour; [0:36:42](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2202) — FVG with displacement; [0:37:29](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2249) — reflection FVG/bearish inversion FVG; [0:39:53](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2393) — second lower FVG, entry lower half, stop rule.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The idea of ranking FVGs (displacement beats a plain first FVG) is a new refinement; the example descriptions rely on garbled captions (which candle is which), so read this as concept, not exact candle IDs.

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: Lunch macro (as used here)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** The market will seek a low that forms during the 10:00 hour as part of the lunch macro; a low in the 10:00 hour, especially one relatively equal to another low, is a draw for the lunch session. Used as the narrative anchor for shorting after the 10:00 FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:33:33](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2013), [0:35:54](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=2154).

title: How New Students Should Start Part 5 \ Back Testing Properly
head: Three pillars of smart money concepts (recap)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** From part 4: (1) the 7:00–9:00 a.m. ET pre-market session with its high/low, relative equal highs/lows, and its phase (consolidation vs. trending/expansion) and how that impacts the morning; (2) the RTH opening range 9:30–10:00 and its consequent encroachment; (3) the Silver Bullet at 10:00. Every individual conceptual idea can be a model; no need to go beyond these to start.
