title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Buy-Side Taken / Inefficiency Traded To (aliases: liquidity sweep, buy-side liquidation)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern description
- **What ICT says:** When price breaks above a resistance level and sweeps buy-side liquidity (stops above that resistance), that's "buy-side taken." After the sweep, price often reverses or corrects. This is institutional targeting stop losses. Once taken, use the inefficiency it created as an iFVG target on the retracement.
- **How to identify:** Watch for a spike above a level (buy-side), then a quick pullback or reversal.
- **How to use:** Once buy-side is taken, expect price to return into the inefficiency left behind. Use that as a short or reversal target.
- **Example in this video:** Dollar Index: "buy-side that was taken there. We pulled that back down into this inefficiency and use this as an inversion fair value gap."
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:47](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=47) (buy-side taken, pulled back, used as iFVG).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Buy-side taken is followed by iFVG usage; it's a two-step pattern.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Premium Array vs. Discount Array (aliases: upper/lower inefficiency zones)
body:
- **Kind:** zone classification
- **What ICT says:** A premium array is the upper portion of a range or inefficiency (where price is expensive). A discount array is the lower portion (where price is cheap). When price breaks below an inefficiency, the inefficiency becomes a premium array on retracements (price unlikely to reach it again, more likely to reverse below). When price breaks above, it becomes a discount array (cheap, likely to be retested).
- **How to identify:** Mark an inefficiency; note which side price breaks below/above; that determines whether it's now premium or discount.
- **How to use:** Premium arrays are resistance on retracements; discount arrays are support on retracements. Use these terms interchangeably with support/resistance, but understand the institutional context.
- **Example in this video:** Pound Dollar: "should we trade lower, they should treat it as a premium array and then attack that minor sell-side."
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:57](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=237) (treat as premium array).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Premium/discount are directional terms; they clarify whether an inefficiency is now a resistance or support zone based on which side broke.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Mohawk Wick (aliases: small wick, acceptable wick)
body:
- **Kind:** iFVG validation detail
- **What ICT says:** When validating an iFVG, small wicks (called "mohawk" wicks for their small, sharp appearance) into the opposite side of the gap are allowed. They don't disqualify the iFVG. It's when BODIES fail to reach consequent encroachment that the iFVG is confirmed. Wicks are noise; bodies are order flow.
- **How to identify:** Look for small, sharp wicks into the gap's upper or lower side while bodies stay on the opposite side.
- **How to use:** Don't invalidate an iFVG because of a small wick. Check where bodies are trading; that's the signal.
- **Example in this video:** Euro Dollar: "It's a tiny tiny little mohawk, I call it. And then we distribute." Wicks into the gap are OK; bodies staying inside = iFVG confirmed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:23](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=143) (tiny little mohawk; body stays inside).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Mohawk is Michael's casual term; the principle is that small wicks don't break iFVG structure.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Stop Hunt / Stop Loss Sweep (aliases: stop hunt, liquidity grab, spike and reverse)
body:
- **Kind:** institutional pattern
- **What ICT says:** A stop hunt is when institutional traders spike price to sweep stops (take out stop losses) and then reverse. Example: Crude oil spike higher to take out sell-side stops, then reverse down. This is predatory order flow targeting retail stop losses. Recognize it and don't get caught.
- **How to identify:** Watch for a sharp spike or trend reversal that seems unmotivated by news, followed by a quick reversal (often at the market open or during thin liquidity).
- **How to use:** When you spot a stop hunt, don't chase the spike. Wait for the reversal and trade in the opposite direction.
- **Example in this video:** Crude oil: "to me, I you know, I I I suspect that crude oil's going to go higher. Nothing's really changed over in the Middle East... But this market's going to be affected greatly because of that." Michael suspects crude will be manipulated (stop hunted) and warns to stay away.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:32](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=332) (this was a stop hunt).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Stop hunts are often news-driven (Judas swings); use order flow, not headlines.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Capitulation High (aliases: exhaustion high, distribution high)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern + reversal signal
- **What ICT says:** A capitulation high is when price makes a series of highs (high, higher high, possibly an even higher high) in a parabolic fashion, exhausting buyers. Once the final higher high is made and price sells off, that's capitulation—institutional sellers finishing distribution and dumping the market to retail. After capitulation, expect significant downside.
- **How to identify:** Watch for three+ progressively higher highs with increasingly sharp reversals; then a hard close below the range. That's capitulation.
- **How to use:** After capitulation highs, expect much lower prices. Use them as shorting opportunities or risk reduction signals if you're long.
- **Example in this video:** Dow: "we have three highs. So we have a high, high, higher high and then giving up the ghost." Michael identifies this as capitulation high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:31](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=571) (three highs: high, high, higher high, giving up the ghost = capitulation).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Capitulation highs are distribution patterns; they're followed by much lower prices.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Relative Equal Lows (aliases: REL, equal lows, liquidity pool)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Two or more lows at the same price level within a range or across multiple days. These are pools of sell-side liquidity (resting sell orders). When price breaks below RELs and shows commitment (bodies stay down), expect lower prices.
- **How to identify:** Scan the daily chart backward; find two or more local lows within a few ticks of each other.
- **How to use:** RELs are targets and stop-out points. Price often tests and breaks through them cleanly. Use as partial-profit zones for shorts.
- **Example in this video:** Euro Dollar, Pound Dollar, ES, NQ: all had relative equal lows marked as targets for lower prices.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:23](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=143) (relative equal lows where sell-side resides) · [0:12:38](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=758) (relatively equal lows on ES).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** RELs are clusters of institutional sell orders; they're sweeps that accelerate moves down.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Sell-Side Liquidity Pool and Minor Sell-Side (aliases: SSL, minor SSL, secondary pool)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A sell-side liquidity pool is a zone where sell orders cluster (above/below a level). Minor sell-side is an intermediate pool; major sell-side is the deepest or furthest away. Use minor sell-side for first targets; major for best-case targets.
- **How to identify:** Identify inefficiencies at different price levels; mark each as minor (closer) or major (further away).
- **How to use:** Use minor SSL for partial profit; major SSL for runner targets. If price sweeps minor SSL, expect continuation to major SSL.
- **Example in this video:** Multiple markets had identified minor and major sell-side pools: Euro, Pound, Gold, Silver, etc.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:36](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=96) (relative equal lows where sell-side resides) · [0:03:57](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=237) (minor sell-side and more prominent sell-side liquidity).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Minor/major classifications depend on proximity; closer inefficiency = minor.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) with Consequent Encroachment Validation (aliases: CE close validation)
body:
- **Kind:** rule + validation
- **What ICT says:** An iFVG is confirmed when: (1) price trades through/beyond it, (2) on retrace, bodies fail to reach CE, (3) close is outside the iFVG (below for bearish iFVG). Check the close price against CE: if close < CE, it's a confirmed bearish iFVG. This is the definitive validation.
- **How to identify:** Mark the FVG high and low; identify CE. Watch for a close outside the FVG below (for bearish) or above (for bullish) CE.
- **How to use:** Once iFVG is confirmed by close, expect continuation in that direction.
- **Example in this video:** Crude Oil: "If we were unable to close below the consequent encouragement level. See, look at the close here. Look at that close. 87.76 and that's lower than 88.25, which is consequent encouragement of that wick right there."
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:46](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=286) (close 87.76 < CE 88.25 = confirmed bearish iFVG).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The close is the validation; don't rely on wicks or intraday swings.

title: Futures Review & Commentary \ June 07, 2026
head: Sell-Side Imbalance / Buy-Side Inefficiency (aliases: bearish inefficiency, weak buyer structure)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When there's sell-side imbalance (sellers willing at lower prices) and buy-side inefficiency (no buyers at those lower prices), it creates a bearish gap/inefficiency. Price is likely to drop into it.
- **How to identify:** Look for a candle that opens lower than the previous close; sellers show willingness at lower; buyers absent.
- **How to use:** Use as a target for shorts or as a bounce zone on retracements.
- **Example in this video:** Pound Dollar: "sell-side imbalance buy-side inefficiency below the inversion fair value gap."
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:10](https://youtu.be/UTrm6uCOUZo?t=190) (sell-side imbalance, buy-side inefficiency).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the opposite of buy-side imbalance/sell-side efficiency (bullish).

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: First Presented Fair Value Gap (fpFVG) Within Context and Narrative (aliases: first FVG with context, operational fpFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern + identification
- **What ICT says:** Multiple FVGs can exist on a chart, but the first presented FVG is the one that matters in "context and narrative." It's the FVG that forms as price is breaking structure (taking liquidity, displacing through swings). Not every gap is the fpFVG; you must consider the price action leading into it. Example: if price breaks through buy-side, then breaks through swing lows, and then an FVG forms, THAT's the fpFVG—it's in the context of the displacement. Other gaps nearby are secondary.
- **How to identify:** Identify where price first displaces (breaks structure with conviction); the FVG that forms in that directional move is the fpFVG. Look for: break of swing, displacement, FVG in that sequence.
- **How to use:** Trade the fpFVG with high conviction; it's the institutional reference. Other FVGs nearby are secondary and may not be tradeable.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: Michael identified two FVGs. One was first formed but NOT used as an iFVG (didn't act inversely). The second was the fpFVG because it formed after a displacement (break of swing lows, take of buy-side). "First presented fair value gap within the context and narrative of what price is likely to do."
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:59](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=239) (why is this one the first presented? Because it's in context of the displacement, swing low break, and relative equal highs).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Context matters; you can't identify fpFVG without understanding the displacement/break that preceded it.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Displacement (aliases: strong move, aggressive break, violent move)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern / directional indicator
- **What ICT says:** A displacement is a strong, committed move through structure (swing lows, support levels) with bodies showing aggression and minimal retracement back into the broken level. Displacements signal institutional participation and continuation. When you see a displacement, the direction it goes is the institutional direction.
- **How to identify:** Look for candles with bodies committed to one side, breaking through a swing low or high, and not retracing back into that level immediately.
- **How to use:** Trade in the direction of the displacement. Expect continuation. Use the displacement as confirmation of your bias.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "This displacement in form of a sell side imbalance buy side inefficiency, this candlestick breaks through this swing low." Displacement down = expect lower prices.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:48](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=288) (displacement in form of sell-side imbalance, breaks through swing low).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Displacement is conviction; it's different from a bounce or a wick back.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Buy-Side Imbalance / Sell-Side Inefficiency (aliases: bearish gap, sell-off indicator)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When there's buy-side imbalance (buyers willing at higher prices, creating a gap) paired with sell-side inefficiency (no sellers stepping in; sellers absent), the gap is bullish. Conversely, when sell-side is willing (buyers gap up, then no sellers) and buy-side is inefficient, it's bearish. The structure signals who's in control.
- **How to identify:** Look for a gap up or down; identify which side is willing and which is absent.
- **How to use:** Use the inefficient side as reversal target. If buy-side is imbalanced and sell-side absent, expect price to eventually drop (sell-side inefficiency).
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "There's a buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency prior to this high being taken." This structure eventually led to price dropping into it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:49](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=49) (buy-side imbalance, sell-side inefficiency).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The imbalance itself is neutral; the inefficiency (absence of the opposite side) is the signal.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: SMT Divergence / Smart Money Technique Divergence (aliases: intermarket divergence, NQ vs ES divergence)
body:
- **Kind:** macro confluence / warning signal
- **What ICT says:** SMT divergence is when two correlated markets (NQ and ES, for example) move in opposite directions or show unequal strength. Example: NQ makes higher high while ES refuses to break above its high. This divergence signals institutional disagreement; often it precedes a sharp reversal (Judas swing trap). When correlated indices diverge, smart money is likely setting a trap for retail.
- **How to identify:** Compare two correlated markets (NQ vs ES, or ES vs Dow); look for one making higher high/low while the other refuses or lags.
- **How to use:** When you spot SMT divergence, expect a reversal. If NQ goes higher while ES stays weak, shorts into NQ are high-probability; ES is showing weakness.
- **Example in this video:** NQ made higher high; ES made lower high (refused). This divergence preceded a sharp sell-off in both. "We had heavy distribution. S&P at the same time and Q higher. See that? So, the Judas right there and creating the SMT divergence."
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:25](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=145) (Nasdaq made higher high when ES was unwilling) · [0:11:12](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=672) (SMT divergence: NQ higher, ES lower high).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** SMT divergence is a macro-level warning; use it to confirm shorts or to avoid long entries.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Judas Swing (aliases: trap rally, trap move, institutional trap)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern + psychology
- **What ICT says:** A Judas swing is a rallies or spike designed to trap retail traders into long positions before a sharp reversal. Often accompanied by positive news or SMT divergence (one index higher while another weak). The institutional purpose: get retail long at the top, then dump. Recognize Judas swings and fade (short) them.
- **How to identify:** Watch for a rally that's not supported by all correlated markets (SMT divergence), or a rally on news that doesn't align with underlying order flow.
- **How to use:** Short Judas swings with conviction. Often they're good 2-3 hour scalps into sharp reversals.
- **Example in this video:** NQ rally into new high while ES weak = Judas swing. "The morning session's going to go up into lunch macro time. Goes into first presented fair value gap, consequent encroachment. Trades back above June 1st daily high and taps it one more time on the low right there... starts to work lower."
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:11](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=431) (Judas: morning session goes up into lunch macro; this high is the trap before reversal).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Judas swings are confirmation of reversal bias; they're not entries by themselves.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Lunch Macro (aliases: lunch period, 11:30 AM–1:30 PM ET, 12:30–1:30 PM preferred hold)
body:
- **Kind:** timing rule
- **What ICT says:** The lunch period is 11:30 AM–1:30 PM ET. Setups usually form in the first hour (11:30 AM–12:30 PM). Delivery to target often happens in the second hour (12:30 PM–1:30 PM). Michael prefers to hold through at least 12:30–1:30 PM to give the algorithm time to execute. If a target isn't hit by early afternoon, it might re-run in the PM session.
- **How to identify:** Mark 11:30 AM and 1:30 PM on your 1m chart; note when setups form and when targets are hit.
- **How to use:** Set entries in the first hour; let targets play out through second hour. Don't exit early expecting a reversal.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: setup formed in morning; Judas swing into lunch; target hit inside the first hour of lunch macro (12:30). "It went right down to it handsomely here... inside the first hour of the lunch macro."
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:11](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=431) (lunch macro 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM; setup forms in first hour, deliver in first hour or hold for 12:30-1:30) · [0:08:46](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=526) (delivered within first hour of lunch macro handsomely).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Lunch macro is reliable; give it time to work before exiting.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Minor Buy-Side Liquidity (aliases: minor BSL, intermediate buy-side pool)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Within a downtrend or selling move, there are pockets of buy orders (buy-side liquidity) that create small resistance bounces. These minor BSL pools are between the major bounces and are often swept on the way down. Recognize them as pause zones, not reversal zones.
- **How to identify:** On a down move, mark small rallies; these are minor BSL bounces.
- **How to use:** Use minor BSL as a place to add shorts or to avoid getting stopped out. Price is likely to retrace slightly into minor BSL, then continue down.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: after hitting relative equal lows, "minor buy side liquidity pool there. Sweeps it. We break lower."
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:46](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=526) (creating a minor buy-side liquidity pool; sweeps it; break lower).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Minor BSL is swept easily; don't treat it as major resistance.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Relative Equal Lows and Relative Equal Highs (aliases: REL, REH, equal highs/lows)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + targeting
- **What ICT says:** REL = two+ lows at same price; acts as a sell-side liquidity cluster (support that's also a target for shorts). REH = two+ highs at same price; acts as a buy-side liquidity cluster (resistance). These are institutional reference points.
- **How to identify:** Scan the daily chart; find two or more equal highs or lows within a few ticks.
- **How to use:** Use REL as partial target for shorts; REH as partial target for longs. These are stepping stones, not final targets.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "target here was the relative equal lows." Michael exited into REL.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:25](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=145) (takes out relative equal highs) · [0:05:36](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=336) (target: relative equal lows).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** REL/REH are liquidity clusters; they're profitable exits, not final targets.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Partial Taking and Trade Management (aliases: profit taking, phased exit)
body:
- **Kind:** risk management
- **What ICT says:** When you have a winning trade, take partial profits at intermediate targets (REL, minor zones) rather than holding the entire position to final target. Example: if you have 10 contracts and REL is 50% down from entry, take 5 contracts off; hold 5 as runners to final target. This locks in profits and reduces emotional burden.
- **How to identify:** Identify REL, minor zones, and final targets before entering; plan where to take partials.
- **How to use:** Set alerts at each partial level. When you hit a partial, take the planned amount off. Let runners ride to next target.
- **Example in this video:** Michael mentions: "I would have the lapse the trade here with a partial. And then when it ran back up here, I would have added the partial here, taken off you see probably would have been half off."
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:23](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=383) (would have taken partial here, added partial there).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Partials reduce stress and lock profits; they're better than running entire position to zero.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 03, 2026
head: Swing Low and Swing High (aliases: swing point, local high/low)
body:
- **Kind:** reference structure
- **What ICT says:** A swing low is a local low (lower than the candle before and after it). Swing high is a local high. These are institutional reference points. When price breaks through a swing high or low with displacement, it signals institutional participation in that direction.
- **How to identify:** Mark the highest and lowest points in a recent range; identify swings.
- **How to use:** Use swing breaks as confirmation of directional bias. When price breaks through a swing and displaces, expect continuation.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "this candlestick breaks through this swing low. When there's an S&P divergence... the market displaces lower."
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:48](https://youtu.be/7M-AO01cAZ8?t=288) (breaks through this swing low).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Swing breaks are high-probability continuations.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Dead Time (5:00 AM – 6:00 AM ET) and 6:00 AM Start Time (aliases: dead zone, low-liquidity time)
body:
- **Kind:** timing rule
- **What ICT says:** Between 5:00 AM and 6:00 AM ET (after London close, before pre-session officially starts), price action is low-probability. Price runs can occur, but they're not to be trusted. 6:00 AM is the earliest that higher-probability price runs can materialize. Michael prefers to wait for 6:00 AM before looking for scalps.
- **How to identify:** Mark 5:00 AM and 6:00 AM on your chart; avoid trading 5:00–6:00; watch for setups forming at 6:00+.
- **How to use:** Use 5:00–6:00 AM for observation and setup identification, not execution. At 6:00 AM, if a setup is forming, you can enter with higher conviction.
- **Example in this video:** Michael waited until 6:00 AM to start watching for the price run. He notes: "6:00 a.m. is the earliest that the higher probability price runs can be trusted."
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:36](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=96) (dead time 5:00-6:00 AM; 6:00 AM start; 6:00-7:00 AM window; 7:00-9:00 pre-session).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Pre-market before 6:00 AM is thin; avoid it unless you have a specific edge.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Relative Equal Highs (aliases: REH, equal highs, liquidity cluster)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + reference
- **What ICT says:** Two or more highs at the same price level. These form pools of buy-side liquidity (limit orders resting above). When price approaches REH from below, expect a test or break above. Once taken, expect pullback or reversal.
- **How to identify:** Scan recent price action (especially overnight/London session); find two+ highs within a few ticks of each other.
- **How to use:** Use REH as targets for long trades or as stop-out points for shorts. Once REH is taken (break above), prepare for volatility and potential reversal.
- **Example in this video:** "Relative equal highs formed during the London session." Later: "relative equal highs, be mindful that they'll probably utilize that as a next draw on liquidity." Michael uses them as directional markers.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:48](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=48) (REH formed London session) · [0:07:55](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=475) (REH as next draw on liquidity).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** REH is a two-way level; it's both a target and a reversal point depending on direction.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Pre-Session Time (6:00 AM – 9:30 AM ET) and Macro Timing (aliases: early bird window, pre-market hours)
body:
- **Kind:** timing framework
- **What ICT says:** Pre-session is 6:00 AM–9:30 AM ET. Within this, there's a favorable 6:00 AM–7:00 AM window where price runs can materialize. Michael uses "early bird gets the worm" as a concept: be ready for moves in the pre-session window, especially on NFP (non-farm payroll) weeks when volatility is high. Also note: 5:50 AM macro (algorithmic window) can trigger moves.
- **How to identify:** Mark 6:00 AM, 7:00 AM, and 9:30 AM on your chart; watch for structures forming in 6:00–7:00 window.
- **How to use:** Scout for setups in 5:00–6:00 AM dead time; execute in 6:00–7:00 AM window; let them run into 9:30 RTH open if needed.
- **Example in this video:** Michael set up his short before the 5:50 AM macro, anticipating the run into 6:00–7:00 AM window.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:36](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=96) (6:00 start time, 6:00-7:00 AM window, 7:00-9:00 pre-session) · [0:03:10](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=190) (5:50 AM macro time).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Pre-session moves are often sharp and clean because fewer traders are active; they're high-probability.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Buy-Side and Sell-Side Liquidity Sweeps (aliases: sweep sequence, double-sweep, buy then sell)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern + execution framework
- **What ICT says:** When price sweeps buy-side liquidity first, then sell-side second, it's a "buy side taken, sell side taken" sequence. This double-sweep creates inversion fair value gaps and validates the directional move. Smart money uses this sequence to take out both retail longs (at buy-side highs) and retail shorts (at sell-side lows) before executing the true directional move.
- **How to identify:** Watch for price spike above a level (buy-side swept), then pullback and spike below (sell-side swept). Each sweep creates an inefficiency/gap.
- **How to use:** After buy-side is taken and pull back occurs, watch for the sell-side to be taken next. That second sweep validates the direction.
- **Example in this video:** "Convenient how it ran up above taking that buy side. We broke down traded down into that low there clearing out that area. So buy side taken first then sell side."
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:23](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=143) (buy side taken, then sell side swept; sequence).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The sequence is key: buy-side first validates the algorithm is "running" that direction.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap with Close Validation (aliases: iFVG close requirement, body below CE)
body:
- **Kind:** rule + distinction
- **What ICT says:** To confirm an iFVG, you MUST see a close outside the gap. A wick into the gap doesn't count. Example: inversion iFVG between two candles; on retrace, price wicks into upper half but closes below it = iFVG confirmed. Michael emphasizes: "iFVGs require the close. Order block does not require close. Inversion fair value gaps require the close." This is critical distinction.
- **How to identify:** Mark the FVG (low of lower candle to high of higher candle); watch the next retracement; check where it closes.
- **How to use:** Only trade iFVGs once close is outside the gap. Don't guess based on wicks; wait for close.
- **Example in this video:** "We have a candlestick close outside of this buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency which validates this becoming an inversion fair value gap... We want to see it trade down. This is not validating it. It's just wicking down through it."
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:56](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=236) (close outside = validates iFVG; wick alone doesn't validate).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Close validation is non-negotiable; it's what separates true iFVGs from guesses.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Upper Quadrant of Buy-Side Imbalance / Sell-Side Inefficiency (aliases: upper portion, upper half of gap)
body:
- **Kind:** measurement
- **What ICT says:** Divide a gap or inefficiency into quadrants (four 25% sections). The upper quadrant is the top 25% of the gap. When price rallies and stops in the upper quadrant before reversing, it shows weakness; price didn't reach consequent encroachment (the wick's high or top of gap). This is a rejection signal.
- **How to identify:** Mark the gap; divide into 4 equal parts; note which quadrant price reaches.
- **How to use:** If price reaches only the upper quadrant and reverses, expect continuation of the down move (for bearish structure).
- **Example in this video:** "The rally up, we stop in the upper quadrant of this buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency. And then we aggressively leave the range."
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:56](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=236) (stop in upper quadrant; aggressively leave range).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Quadrants are finer detail; they help you see where exactly the weakness is.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Position Scaling and Adding (aliases: layering, position building, adding on weakness)
body:
- **Kind:** risk management + execution
- **What ICT says:** Instead of entering a full position at once, start small (e.g., 2 contracts) at the first signal. As price confirms and moves in your direction, add more. This reduces entry risk and lets you scale in as conviction builds. Example: enter 2 contracts at first iFVG target, add 5 more when price breaks sell-side, add 2 more on next weakness.
- **How to identify:** Define your levels before entry; plan where you'll add.
- **How to use:** Enter small at first signal; add at confirmation levels. This gives you better average fill and reduces drawdown.
- **Example in this video:** "I threw in a small position with just simply two contracts... anticipating... then I added the lines portion of the position I wanted to assume... took off below here. I added them right back on... I added another exit as it went through."
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:44](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=284) (two contracts initial entry, add 5 more, add 2 back).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Layering reduces emotion and improves execution; you're not forcing full position at uncertain price.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Market Maker Sell Model (MMSM) Structure (aliases: accumulation → reversal → distribution sequence)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern structure
- **What ICT says:** MMSM has a specific sequence: original consolidation → first stage accumulation (sometimes just one stage in fast moves) → smart money reversal → low-risk sell → first stage distribution → second stage distribution → drop below original consolidation. The final drop is the largest, easiest move. Identifying this structure predicts where price will go.
- **How to identify:** Scan the chart; find consolidation, then count stages.
- **How to use:** Once you identify the stages, expect the second stage distribution to be the biggest move. Let it run; don't exit early.
- **Example in this video:** "Original consolidation. First stage accumulation... Smart money reversal. Low risk sell. First stage distribution. Second stage redistribution. And then the biggest move takes place there."
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:32](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=332) (full MMSM structure identified).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** MMSM is a reliable pattern; second stage distribution is the best trade.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE) as Entry and Exit Level (aliases: CE level, wick low, deep point)
body:
- **Kind:** precision timing
- **What ICT says:** Consequent encroachment is the wick's deepest point (or top for bullish setups). Use CE as a precise entry point. Example: Michael entered his short "right at consequent encroachment of that little inversion fair value gap." CE levels are where smart money is likely trading; they're high-probability entries.
- **How to identify:** Mark the wick's deep point; that's CE.
- **How to use:** Use CE as your entry zone; stop just beyond it.
- **Example in this video:** "First entry with the two contracts right at consequent encroachment of that little inversion fair value gap."
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:20](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=380) (first entry at CE).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** CE is the most precise entry; use it when you have high conviction.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Breaker (High-Low-Higher High) (aliases: breaker formation, swing structure)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern
- **What ICT says:** A breaker is a short-term high, a low below it, then a higher high (but still lower than the original short-term high). This structure is a reversal signal. Michael uses it as one of many confluences for direction confirmation.
- **How to identify:** Mark a swing high, then a lower low, then a test back up.
- **How to use:** Breaker formations are reversal filters; use them to confirm turns.
- **Example in this video:** "We have a breaker which is a high, low, higher high."
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:10](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=190) (breaker: high, low, higher high).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Breaker is a component of larger patterns; use with other confluences.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ June 02, 2026
head: Terminus Objective (aliases: final target, ultimate target)
body:
- **Kind:** measurement / targeting
- **What ICT says:** The terminus objective is the ultimate, deepest target for a move. It's often a previous swing low or a calculated level far below/above current price. Michael mentions having a "terminus objective" but not showing it initially; later he adds it as an additional exit.
- **How to identify:** Identify the lowest low or highest high the market could theoretically reach (lowest REL, oldest swing low, etc.).
- **How to use:** Use as a final runner target; most traders won't reach it, but it's there if conviction holds.
- **Example in this video:** "Targeting that. Once it went through it... I added another exit." (The terminus objective is the ultimate profit-taking level.)
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:32](https://youtu.be/bqmqylAuLcI?t=332) (targeting the terminus objective).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Terminus is not always reached; use it as a "dream target" while taking partials on the way.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Two Pools of Liquidity and Range Grading (aliases: dual-level liquidity, high and low pools)
body:
- **Kind:** framework / measurement
- **What ICT says:** To define a trade zone, identify two pools of liquidity: a higher pool (upper level) and a lower pool (lower level). Grade these two levels; the range between them is your operational zone. Use this range to identify equilibrium (midpoint), premium side (above midpoint), and discount side (below midpoint). Shorts are taken on the premium side; longs on discount. This framework predicts where price will consolidate and where it will break.
- **How to identify:** Scan the daily/15m chart; find two significant support/resistance zones (old lows, inversion FVGs, swing points); mark them as high and low pools.
- **How to use:** Use the range to frame your trading zone. Target breaks below the lower pool or above the higher pool for true directional moves.
- **Example in this video:** Michael identified two pools: 30,055.75 (high) and 29,886 (low). The range between them (169.75 points) was the zone. Equilibrium = 30,055.75 - 29,886 = ~29,970. Above equilibrium = premium (short zone); below = discount (long zone).
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:32](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=332) (two pools of liquidity, grading) · [0:10:33](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=633) (equilibrium between two pools; 30,055.75 and 29,886).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This framework is institutional; price oscillates between pools, and breaks predict the next move.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Equilibrium and Premium/Discount Sides (aliases: midpoint, range midpoint)
body:
- **Kind:** measurement / zone classification
- **What ICT says:** Equilibrium is the midpoint between the two pools of liquidity. Above equilibrium is the premium side (where shorts are taken); below is the discount side (where longs are taken). When price is in premium and showing weakness, expect a drop to equilibrium and then to the lower pool. Conversely, when in discount and strong, expect a run to equilibrium and then to upper pool.
- **How to identify:** Calculate: (High Pool + Low Pool) / 2 = Equilibrium.
- **How to use:** Use equilibrium as a first-take profit zone for shorts (from premium). Use as a reversal point for longs (from discount).
- **Example in this video:** Equilibrium = roughly 29,970 (between 30,055.75 and 29,886). Michael planned to "sell short in the premium side of that range... divided by this little red dashed line here. That's equilibrium."
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:10](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=430) (equilibrium divides range; short premium side) · [0:13:42](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=822) (equilibrium at 30,055.75 and 29,886; signal when market gets through halfway point).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Equilibrium is precise; it's where smart money often adjusts positions.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Deferred Delivery (aliases: delayed move, two-stage vs. one-stage drop)
body:
- **Kind:** pattern refinement
- **What ICT says:** Sometimes price moves in the expected direction but not in the expected structure. Michael expected a two-stage drop (down-consolidate-down), but price "ripped the entire daily range down all in one fell swoop." This is still a valid move—it's just a deferred delivery (delayed structure). The market still hit the targets; it just took a different path. Don't disqualify a move because it doesn't match your time/structure expectation.
- **How to identify:** Compare expected structure vs. actual price action; if direction is right but structure differs, it's deferred delivery.
- **How to use:** Trust the direction and targets even if the structure isn't textbook. Deferred delivery still delivers.
- **Example in this video:** Expected two-stage drop over multiple candles; instead, price dropped in one candle move. Still delivered to the correct level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:32](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=332) (expected two stages; actually prolonged and deferred delivery; had to come back up and then sell-off).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Flexibility on structure beats rigidity on timeline; focus on targets, not timing.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Stop Hunt (aliases: stop loss sweep, false reversal)
body:
- **Kind:** institutional pattern
- **What ICT says:** A stop hunt is when price spikes in one direction to sweep stop losses (rout out traders), then reverses. Example: price runs up, triggers sell-side stops, then drops. Michael notes: "It was a stop hunt. It runs low." Recognize these and don't get shaken out; they're opportunities to add or re-enter.
- **How to identify:** Watch for a spike that wicks above/below a level, then immediately reverses without closing in that direction.
- **How to use:** When you spot a stop hunt, prepare to trade in the direction AFTER the hunt (when price resumes). Don't panic-exit; the hunt is often followed by the true directional move.
- **Example in this video:** Price ran up, triggered stops above a high, then dropped sharply. The drop was the true move.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:56](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=536) (stop hunt: runs low, took out short-term high, it was a stop hunt).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Stop hunts are predatory institutional tactics; recognize them and turn them to your advantage.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Buy-Side Imbalance / Sell-Side Inefficiency with Gradient Level Anchoring (aliases: anchored iFVG, grid-aligned inefficiency)
body:
- **Kind:** validation method + pattern
- **What ICT says:** An iFVG is more reliable if its candlestick "lays on top of" a gradient level (a graded support/resistance from the two pools of liquidity). This anchoring validates that the inefficiency is on the institutional radar. Michael emphasizes: "The candlestick has to be laying on a gradient level. That's what validates your smart money concept."
- **How to identify:** First, grade your two pools of liquidity and create gradient levels between them. Then, identify candlesticks that sit directly on these grades. If a candlestick is on a grade and contains a buy-side imbalance, it's a high-probability iFVG.
- **How to use:** Prioritize iFVGs that align with gradient levels. These are institutional reference points; trade them with higher conviction.
- **Example in this video:** A buy-side imbalance / sell-side inefficiency candlestick was sitting directly on a gradient level from the two pools. Michael noted: "What makes this one so good is because it's anchored to a gradient level." This validated it as a tradeable iFVG.

head: Algorithmic Macro (9:50–10:10 ET) (aliases: morning macro, 9:50 macro)
body:

- **What ICT says:** 9:50–10:10 ET is an algorithmic macro window when institutional order flow has higher probability of executing moves. Michael notes: "We have the market running out of an algorithmic macro, which is 950 to 1010. It starts its run." Price often breaks out of consolidations or accelerates during this window.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Speed, Distance, Velocity Confirmation (aliases: momentum confirmation, acceleration signal)
body:
- **Kind:** confirmation signal
- **What ICT says:** Once price breaks through a key level (like equilibrium or consequent encroachment), look for speed, distance, and velocity—i.e., accelerating movement without hesitation. This is confirmation the institutional move is real. If price breaks slowly or with retracements, conviction is questioned.
- **How to identify:** After price breaks a key level, check: does it move fast and far without reversing back? If yes = strong; if no = weak.
- **How to use:** Use speed/distance/velocity as a filter. If your break doesn't show these characteristics, the move may fail. If it does, hold and let it run.
- **Example in this video:** "I wanted to see speed and distance and velocity. Once we get through the halfway point or consequent encouragement between these two pools of liquidity..." Michael was waiting for acceleration after equilibrium break.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:42](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=822) (speed, distance, velocity signal once through equilibrium) · [0:13:42](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=822) (confirmation when speed shows the move is on).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Speed/distance is intuitive; it's what pros see immediately, amateurs miss.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Low-Resistance Liquidity Run Conditions (aliases: clean price action, efficient movement)
body:
- **Kind:** environment recognition
- **What ICT says:** When price shows "willingness to escape and really run and leave little inefficiencies," that's low-resistance liquidity run conditions. Contrast this with choppy price action (many candles sitting inside one inefficiency, lots of retracements). Low-resistance conditions = tight stops, big runners. Choppy conditions = skip or dial back.
- **How to identify:** Watch for inefficiencies followed by clean, quick retracements (1–2 candles), then a run. Repeat this pattern = low-resistance.
- **How to use:** In low-resistance conditions, dial down risk per trade; let winners run. In choppy conditions, take profits earlier; don't add; maybe skip altogether.
- **Example in this video:** ES showed clean inefficiencies with small retracements = low-resistance. NQ had consolidations with many candles = choppy. Michael preferred ES structure.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:32](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=1112) (low-resistance liquidity run conditions: inefficiencies with small retracements) · [0:19:19](https://youtu.be/NS5EcfChL3o?t=1159) (high-resistance choppy conditions: many candles in one inefficiency).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Environment recognition is key to position sizing; don't over-size in choppy markets.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 28, 2026
head: Price and Time Alignment (aliases: convergence, setup maturity)
body:
- **Kind:** principle
- **What ICT says:** "If those things occur, chances are you probably got the tiger by the tail." When price reaches its target AND time aligns (macro, fibonacci time, swing high/low timing), the move is validated. Focusing solely on price without time is incomplete.
- **How to identify:** Combine price targets (FVGs, liquidity) with time confluences (macros, swing counts, Fibonacci time).
- **How to use:** Wait for BOTH price and time to align before entering with size. Setups that align both are highest probability.
- **Example in this video:** Michael identified price targets (two pools, equilibrium, lower pool); also noted macros and timing. When both aligned, conviction was highest.

head: Gradient Levels (aliases: graded levels, range subdivisions)
body:
- **Kind:** measurement tool
- **What ICT says:** Gradient levels are intermediate levels graded between the two main pools of liquidity. They're shown as light lines between the high and low pool. These serve as micro-targets and confirmation points. When a candlestick sits on a gradient level, it's on institutional radar.
- **How to identify:** Between your two pools, divide the range into multiple sub-levels (e.g., every 25–50 points).
- **How to use:** Use gradients as interim targets and as validation anchors for inefficiencies.
- **Example in this video:** Michael showed gradient levels between 30,055.75 and 29,886; candlesticks sitting on these lines validated their institutional importance.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Fair Value Gap (FVG / volume imbalance)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule + entry model
- **What ICT says:** Volume imbalance—an inefficiency where price traded—forms when candles do not overlap; can act as support (bullish FVG), resistance (bearish FVG), or become an inversion FVG if price approaches from the opposite side. After a big blow-off run, these gaps want to be filled for price to feel "balanced" and "fair."
- **How to identify:** Look for candlestick bodies that do not touch a gap left above/below them. High of one candle < low of next candle = bullish FVG. Low of one candle > high of next candle = bearish FVG.
- **How to use:** Target low of FVG (bullish) or high (bearish) as a magnet on price. If FVG is utilized first as bullish (filled as support), and price later approaches from below, it becomes an inversion FVG and will likely offer resistance on the way down. Enter at best price within the gap. Exit or take profit when price leaves the gap cleanly.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily, May 27, 2026. High-of-day run left a volume imbalance at ~676.25. Price later fell and used that gap as inversion FVG, respecting its high and consequent encroachment on the way down.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:02](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=302) — importance of volume imbalance post-runup · [0:18:23](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=1103) — perfect precision of FVG bodies · [0:33:20](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2000) — how first utilization predicts inversion FVG behavior
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Must identify whether gap was used as bullish or bearish first; only then can you predict its next role. Do not "cherry-pick" gaps; use strict rules about which ones to trade.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / rule
- **What ICT says:** The high or low of the candlestick that completes a fair value gap (the body reaching into it). Must be respected as a boundary; if price breaks below CE on a bearish move, it signals weakness; if price cannot return to CE on a retracement, it shows the lower area is strong. CE is literally part of the PD array; you must not skip it in your analysis.
- **How to identify:** Draw the FVG high or low, then identify the first candlestick body that entered the gap; the extreme of that body is your CE level.
- **How to use:** Use CE as a tighter stop loss than the full gap. Enter short only if you trust price won't return to CE; if it does, exit or reduce. Use CE as a clue: if price barely penetrates CE and cannot return, weakness is confirmed.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, May 27, 2026 PM session. Bullish FVG in pre-market had a CE line; on the bear move, price sliced right through it, and bodies could not even return to touch CE on retracements—textbook weakness signal.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:54](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=1434) — CE must be broken cleanly · [0:37:20](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2240) — CE performance tells story of strength/weakness · [0:42:03](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2523) — CE as tight entry buffer
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The bodies respecting CE is the key (not wicks); if a second retracement low is higher than the first, it's "hawkish" and you should demand it.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Standard Deviations for Price Targeting
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage + refinement
- **What ICT says:** Use standard deviations (same tool used for Asian range, Central Bank Dealers Range, opening range gaps) to project a price move. Measure a key price range (high to low, or body to body), then move it down (or up) by one, two, or more deviations. Example: if a range is 100 points, one deviation down gives a target. Apply negative-two deviation to the day's range to find support zones that are statistically likely to be tested.
- **How to identify:** In TradingView, set up standard deviations on the daily or intraday chart. Read the negative-two line; watch price gravitate toward it.
- **How to use:** Negative-two std dev line acts as a magnet and key support/resistance. If price trades below a key high and low, project deviations downward; use that level as a target on short setups. Combine with FVGs for confirmation.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily, May 27, 2026. Negative-two std dev = 29,878.75. Price was aimed at that level and hit it. In the 1m intraday chart, measured the blow-off range, duplicated it downward using Fibonacci, then applied standard deviations to find the exact low area (~877.5 actual vs 878.75 projected—very tight).
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:37](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=397) — standard deviations on daily · [0:30:11](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=1811) — Fibonacci duplication method · [0:31:45](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=1905) — negative-two reading and use
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is "market wizardry" and precision teaching; ICT emphasizes not to teach it publicly because it will "stop working" due to collective awareness.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Climax Reversal Patterns
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The "flavor of 2026" teaching. A climax is a parabolic, unsustainable blow-off run at the end of a directional move (daily high achieved on pre-market spike, then continued intraday spike), followed by fast reversal. Use it as a signal that the move has exhausted itself and shorts become high-probability in that direction.
- **How to identify:** Look for sustained up-move, then a parabolic "grand finale" spike (micro spike, volume spike, wicks extended). Price often leaves a gap or volume imbalance at the top.
- **How to use:** After a climax spike, expect a fast reversal into the gap left behind. Short entries become valid. Use FVG and CE rules to fine-tune entry and exit.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily and 1m, May 27, 2026. 7 weeks of consecutive up closes + all-time high reached + pre-market parabolic spike = climax. Immediately reversed hard into volume imbalance. Reward-to-risk was excellent.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:14](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=254) — climax described as "grand finale" · [0:15:14](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=914) — parabolic pre-market as climax signal
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Requires 1–2 years experience to trade confidently. Beginners should focus on longs; shorting requires conviction and discipline.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + refinement
- **What ICT says:** When a bullish FVG (gap created on an up move) is later breached from above, it becomes an inversion FVG and acts as resistance on the way down. Price will respects its high and CE the same way it respected the low on the way up. The first utilization dictates the second role.
- **How to identify:** Identify the original bullish FVG (or any FVG), watch whether price uses it, then observe when price approaches from opposite direction. That opposite-direction approach uses the gap as iFVG.
- **How to use:** Treat iFVG high / CE as resistance on retracements during downside moves. Do not expect price to exceed iFVG high on rallies; if it does, the iFVG is "overruled" and you must re-evaluate bias.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, pre-market bullish FVG at ~9:26–9:30. On the PM session bear move, that gap became iFVG; price's body could not even touch its high on the way down, showing conviction in the downside.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:37](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=1057) — inversion FVG described · [0:42:03](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2523) — testing the iFVG high and failing
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** An iFVG can be overruled; if price enters and closes above it solidly, assume the direction has shifted.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Relative Equal Lows
body:
- **Kind:** definition + use
- **What ICT says:** When the market creates a low, then retraces, and later creates another low near the same price, that level becomes a magnet on price. Market makers target these for liquidity runs and stop sweeps. On daily charts, relative equal lows are key resistance to the downside in bear moves.
- **How to identify:** Look at prior swing lows; if a new low is within ~5–10 points (on NQ), it qualifies as a relative equal low.
- **How to use:** In bull markets, target relative equal highs (upside). In bear markets, target relative equal lows (downside). These are "universal" targets; accumulate shorts when aimed at them; use them as targets on short entries.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily, May 27, 2026. "Relatively equal lows" from prior month to current level were discussed as magnet on price for potential downside draw.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:27](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=207) — relative equal lows taken out in May · [0:40:29](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2429) — planning entry near relative equal lows
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** ICT uses this as a universal rule for all markets; applies to equities, forex, futures.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Shorting in Primary Bull Markets
body:
- **Kind:** refinement + psychology / mindset
- **What ICT says:** Can be done profitably at intraday levels when you identify climax reversals or FVG setups, BUT requires 1–2 years minimum experience. Beginners should stick to longs; shorting too early causes fear-based exits and losses. When shorting, conviction and stop-loss discipline are essential. Start small; do not over-leverage.
- **How to identify:** High-probability short setups in bull markets: (a) climax spike creating gap, (b) inversion FVG that has been utilized as bullish, (c) failed retracement back to a prior level (weakness signal), (d) bodies not reaching CE on bounce attempts.
- **How to use:** Enter in upper half of iFVG (buffer position), aim for FVG low / prior level. On first entry, keep size small. If conviction confirmed by price action (e.g., bodies can't return to CE), scale into larger shorts on next pullback.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, ~9:31 and after. Entry just below open at upper consequent encroachment of iFVG; aimed for low near 877.5; took small heat but had buffer from prior long entry, so net profit; covered all in one shot (did not pyramid on the down move).
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:45](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=585) — "I'm teaching climax reversal patterns this year" · [0:11:18](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=678) — experience requirement for shorting · [0:42:03](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2523) entry and fill
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Bias beginners toward longs; biased shorters toward deep experience and small size.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Trade Management via Time & Consequent Encroachment
body:
- **Kind:** rule + execution
- **What ICT says:** After identifying a down target (e.g., FVG low), watch how fast price gets there. If it's slow/lethargic, you may be wrong; if it's fast and direct, conviction in the downside is strong. Also track whether price can/cannot return to CE on retracements—repeated failures to return = strong signal to stay short and add size.
- **How to identify:** Track the clock; observe the pace of down moves vs horizontal grinding. Look at candlestick bodies: can they touch CE? If not, that's weakness confirmation.
- **How to use:** If move is slow, reduce or exit short; assume you're wrong. If move is fast and CE is broken hard, scale in larger on the next pullback. Use CE failures as your "permission" to pyramid shorts.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, PM session. Initial drop from ~9:26 to ~9:37 was very fast (one directional), hitting the initial target at 877.5 in that range. Then bodies couldn't return to CE—ICT wanted to take more shorts but market had already done the move, so he just took what was there and exited.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:54](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=1434) — time pace as conviction signal · [0:37:20](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2240) — bodies respecting CE as weakness
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the "central tenant" of the approach: time tells you whether to trust the move or not.

title: NQ Futures Review & Commentary \ May 27, 2026
head: Position Sizing & Buffer Entries
body:
- **Kind:** rule / execution
- **What ICT says:** On entries in high-volatility markets (first 10 min post-open, e.g., 9:30–9:40 ET), build in a buffer. Take a small long entry in the pre-market, then use the profit as a cushion to allow an aggressive short entry at open with some adverse price action tolerance. Do not risk more than you can afford to lose; use micro contracts if your account is small.
- **How to identify:** Identify your conviction level; size accordingly.
- **How to use:** Recommended approach: micro contracts for small accounts or prop-firm attempts (alleviates margin/rules issues). For entries near open, take a small long buffer trade 5–10 min before, then use its profit to cushion a short entry.
- **Example in this video:** NQ. Entry long in pre-market / early AM, gains ~50–100 points. Then entry short at open within iFVG; initial risk is offset by prior long gain. Reduces forced stop-out risk.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:51](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=111) — micro contracts recommended for prop firms · [0:42:03](https://youtu.be/qf5qokimwO4?t=2523) — buffer entry structure
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Critical for risk management; "beat them by a thousand paper cuts" rather than one big bet.

title: Oil Review & General Commentary
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) on multi-timeframe setup
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** On the 15m chart, crude oil had a buy-side imbalance / sell-side inefficiency (BISI) that, once breached on the downside, became an inversion FVG (would act as resistance on rallies). On the 1m chart, same inefficiency was visible and served as entry confirmation.
- **How to identify:** On 15m: identify the gap, mark it. Drop to 1m and observe price trading into it; watch where body respects the high/low and consequent encroachment.
- **How to use:** Use multi-timeframe to confirm: if 15m shows iFVG forming, drop to 1m for precision entry point. Stop loss placed just above the iFVG high.
- **Example in this video:** Crude oil. 15m showed a BISI → iFVG post-gap-down. On 1m, price traded into the iFVG high, created a whipsaw (bodies touching high, then reversing). Entry was on the dip back into that iFVG; stop placed above the high; target was the relative equal low below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:23](https://youtu.be/dwMgP2zkH0w?t=143) — iFVG identified on 15m · [0:03:14](https://youtu.be/dwMgP2zkH0w?t=194) — execution on 1m into iFVG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Whipsaw occurred (bodies went up into iFVG high before reversing); this is normal price action; stop placement must accommodate this.

title: Oil Review & General Commentary
head: Capitulation & Market Mania
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / psychology
- **What ICT says:** When markets become parabolic and everyone is excited (mania), the top is near. Once capitulation occurs (final exhaustion dump), the move is over. Gold and silver both showed this pattern; Bitcoin also. When ICT tells you to stay away, it is because he recognizes the mania phase and knows the capitulation dump is coming. Retail traders, lacking experience, see parabolic moves and assume they continue; they do not.
- **How to identify:** Parabolic run + mania in the news/social media = top forming. Sudden sharp dump after a run = capitulation.
- **How to use:** Do not chase parabolic moves. When ICT says "stay away," he is protecting your capital. After capitulation, do not expect higher prices immediately; wait for structure to reset.
- **Example in this video:** Gold and silver had parabolic runs; ICT warned to stay away; they capitulated lower (like the "Hunt Brothers" manipulation of 1980). Bitcoin aimed for $1M, peaked at $127k, then reversed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:24](https://youtu.be/dwMgP2zkH0w?t=384) — capitulation and mania teaching · [0:07:11](https://youtu.be/dwMgP2zkH0w?t=431) — "Hunt brothers" reference to 1980 collapse
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** ICT emphasizes that his "stay away" advice is not for his benefit; it is for the trader's protection, especially beginners.

title: Oil Review & General Commentary
head: DXY (US Dollar Index) as Market Driver
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** DXY (Dollar Index) is stuck in a range on the daily chart; when DXY does not move, USD pairs do not move. Therefore, trading EURUSD, GBPUSD, etc., will be frustrating and choppy. However, exotic pairs (non-USD pairs) will have movement even when DXY is stuck. The correlation is critical to recognize.
- **How to identify:** Check daily DXY; if it is in a range with no breakout, expect USD pairs to be choppy.
- **How to use:** When DXY is stuck, avoid USD pairs; trade exotics (EURJPY, AUDJPY, GBPJPY, etc.) instead. Wait for DXY to break range before re-engaging USD pairs.
- **Example in this video:** DXY stuck = EURUSD, GBPUSD, etc., not moving. ICT acknowledges this and pivots to non-USD pairs.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:49](https://youtu.be/dwMgP2zkH0w?t=289) — DXY daily review · [0:05:37](https://youtu.be/dwMgP2zkH0w?t=337) — DXY stuck explanation for pairs
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Exotic pairs still move even when USD pairs are stuck.

head: Bitcoin Consequent Encroachment & Support Levels
body:

If Bitcoin closes below CE on a daily or swing basis, it signals weakness and opens the door to lower prices. Specific support targets mentioned: 49,677 (if CE breaks), then 24–26k zone, and "favorite" level at 0 (humorous but implies very deep capitulation).

title: Tapereading \ Practice Session Final Hour ES
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) as Entry Foothold
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** From prior structure (earlier in the day or prior day), a bullish FVG was formed. Now approaching from below, that same gap acts as a foothold to climb higher. Price will use the low / consequent encroachment (the "in" point of the gap) as a launch point to spring up and treat the gap as resistance on rallies.
- **How to identify:** Mark the prior bullish FVG; as price approaches from below, watch for a candlestick body that touches the gap; that touch is your confirmation that the iFVG is acting as a foothold.
- **How to use:** Buy side imbalance / sell-side inefficiency → if price comes down and touches the low of that gap, expect it to spring higher. Entry is at that touch point or just inside the gap.
- **Example in this video:** ES final hour. Price came down into a buy-side imbalance (from earlier structure), touched it, then sprang up. Treated the gap low as a foothold and climbed higher. Entry at that foothold; target was relative equal highs above.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:50](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=110) — buy-side imbalance identified · [0:03:11](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=191) — iFVG explained as foothold · [0:04:05](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=245) — treating gap as foothold on climb
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The iFVG must be approached from the correct direction (below) to act as a foothold; arrival from above would be different.

title: Tapereading \ Practice Session Final Hour ES
head: Relative Equal Highs as Targets
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** Throughout the day, price creates multiple highs at similar levels (or with small wicks near the same level). These become targets on up moves. Use relative equal highs as accumulation and scaling points.
- **How to identify:** Mark intraday swing highs; if multiple candles top out near the same price, that level is a relative equal high.
- **How to use:** On up moves, target relative equal highs. Scale out at each equal high. Use them as reference for where price "wants" to reach.
- **Example in this video:** ES final hour. Multiple prior highs near 3400, 3450, 3475, 3500 area. Used each as a scale-out point. Price attacked these "clean highs" repeatedly.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:53](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=53) — relative equal highs as targets · [0:05:12](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=312) — accumulating toward highs · [0:13:16](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=796) — clean highs to target
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Clean highs" do not need to be exact twins; even relative equal highs within a few ticks are valid targets.

head: Macro Windows (3:15–3:45 PM ET)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The 3:15–3:45 PM ET window is a "macro" (algorithmic trading window) where the market often produces clean, tradeable price action. This is one of the known killzones / algo windows. During this window, expect strong directional moves with less noise, spoof, or whipsaw.
- **How to identify:** Clock time: 3:15 PM to 3:45 PM ET on a 1m or 5m chart.
- **How to use:** During the macro window, focus on accumulating in foothold areas and targeting the higher / lower levels with conviction. The action is usually clean during this window.
- **Example in this video:** ES final hour, 3:15–3:45 PM. ICT notes that price "came alive" at 3:30 and the move was "brilliantly implemented." The clean action matched expectations for the macro window. Price did not go lower after a certain point (respecting support structure) and ripped higher within the window.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:03](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=423) — macro terminology · [0:14:18](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=858) — 3:15–3:45 macro confirmation · [0:18:09](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=1089) — macro window performance
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** ICT notes that people misusing the term "macro" are trading at wrong times (e.g., 10:40 is not a macro); also cautions that the 3:15–3:45 window is specifically for the final hour of RTH and is algo-driven.

title: Tapereading \ Practice Session Final Hour ES
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE) as a Stop Point
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In order blocks and FVGs, CE is the boundary. On upside accumulation, if you are going to take risk via a stop loss, place it just below the consequent encroachment of a prior PD array or order block. If CE is taken out, the structure is broken and your assumption is wrong.
- **How to identify:** Identify the PD array (FVG, order block); find the body that enters it; the extreme of that body is the CE.
- **How to use:** Place stop loss just below CE. As price moves up, raise the stop to just below the next PD array's CE. Trail stops up the chain of PD arrays.
- **Example in this video:** ES. Entry at buy-side imbalance; stop placed below the consequent encroachment of that order block. As price climbed and formed new PD arrays, stops were raised to just below the CE of each new level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:53](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=53) — stop placement below low (CE) · [0:04:05](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=245) — raise stop up to reduce risk · [0:15:06](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=906) — CE as foothold
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** None stated.

head: Order Block & PD Array Accumulation
body:
- **Kind:** rule + execution
- **What ICT says:** After identifying a PD array (order block, FVG), price often returns to it and bounces / accumulates inside it. Use the order block as a "footing" from which to scale positions. Add to longs at each subsequent order block; trail stops tighter.
- **How to identify:** Mark order blocks (reversal candles, supply/demand zones); watch for price to return to them.
- **How to use:** On up moves, add (scale up) at each order block; on down moves, add shorts at each order block. Scale out at targets (relative equal highs/lows).
- **Example in this video:** ES. Price came down into order block / FVG, accumulated there (body stayed inside, small candles), then sprung up. As it climbed, it touched other order blocks and accumulation points, each used as a scale-up point.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:05](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=305) — added inside gap and order block · [0:08:48](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=528) — accumulating, then snap up
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Order blocks may have small gaps (volume imbalances) inside them; these are valid accumulation zones.

title: Tapereading \ Practice Session Final Hour ES
head: Spoof Identification & Market Conditions
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Spoof candles are artificial price moves (likely market maker manipulation) that do not follow natural order flow. They appear as sudden wicks or bodies that reverse sharply without reason. On certain days ("lazy afternoons"), spoofs are prevalent. Recognize them and trade around them.
- **How to identify:** Look for candles with exaggerated wicks that reverse immediately or bodies that gap and reverse without trading through order blocks naturally.
- **How to use:** When you see a spoof, do not react; let the market settle. Use the spoof to your advantage: if price spoof-wicked into a stop, it will likely bounce; if you're short and see a spoof wick up, expect it to reverse down.
- **Example in this video:** ES final hour. ICT notes "lazy afternoon," sees several spoofs / artificial highs, and comments "anytime spoofs" (meaning the spoofing was obvious). He hopes the summer does not continue this pattern.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:57](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=657) — lethargic, slow price action · [0:11:57](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=717) — spoof recognition "too clean" · [0:18:09](https://youtu.be/7zlblhLGraA?t=1089) — "spooze" and macro window interaction
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Too clean" price action can indicate spoofing or algorithmic manipulation; natural order flow has more friction.
