title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Bodies Cannot Touch (Key Levels) — Algorithmic Signature of Bearishness
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** When price is in a bearish phase (downtrend, breaking lows), candlestick bodies will not close above certain key levels, even if wicks reach those levels. This is an algorithmic signature that smart money is preventing price from holding above that level. Once you spot this signature (bodies unable to touch a level multiple times), you know the market is bearish and price will go lower. This rule applies universally: lower quadrants of daily suspension blocks, event horizon levels, old resistance turned support, etc.
- **How to identify:** Watch a key level (e.g., lower quadrant of daily suspension block). If price retraces back up to it during a downtrend, do the bodies close above that level or stay below it? If bodies consistently stay below, it's bearish.
- **How to use:** This is your confirmation signal. Do not switch your bias until bodies finally breach and close above the level. The longer bodies refuse to touch it, the more bearish the signal.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ daily chart: lower quadrant of daily suspension block at ~25,000. During the downtrend, price retraced up multiple times; bodies never closed above this level, confirming bearishness each time. When price finally ran lower, it proved the signature was correct.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:26](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=806) asks "do bodies touch that level?" as confirmation of bearishness; [0:15:02](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=902) emphasizes body placement as algorithmic rule, not coincidence.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the core of ICT's institutional order flow teaching. No other methodology (Wyckoff, Elliott Wave, Volume Profile, Supply/Demand) teaches this.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Lower Quadrant (aliases: 25% level, lower quarter of suspension block, Q1)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A suspension block (large volume imbalance) can be divided into four equal parts (quadrants). The lower quadrant is the bottom 25% of that range. This level acts as support during downtrends and resistance during uptrends. Bodies that fail to close above the lower quadrant signal continued bearishness.
- **How to identify:** Suspension block low + [(high - low) × 0.25] = Lower Quadrant level.
- **How to use:** During downtrends, use as a retracement target and reversal zone. If price retraces into the lower quadrant and bodies cannot hold above it, the downtrend resumes. If price is below the lower quadrant, look for it to drop lower (to lower octant or event horizon).
- **Example in this video:** MNQ daily: lower quadrant at ~25,000; bodies repeatedly failed to hold above this level during the downtrend, confirming each attempt to find support was rejected.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:12](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=372) marks upper quadrant and lower quadrant visually; [0:13:26](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=806) applies lower quadrant rule to bearishness.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Lower quadrant is not a definitive support; it's a filtered key level where bodies matter more than wicks.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Upper Quadrant (aliases: 75% level, upper quarter of suspension block, Q3)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The upper quadrant is the top 25% of a suspension block. This level acts as resistance during downtrends and support during uptrends. The upper quadrant of a daily suspension block is often a retracement ceiling in downtrends.
- **How to identify:** Suspension block low + [(high - low) × 0.75] = Upper Quadrant level.
- **How to use:** In downtrends, if price retraces back up to the upper quadrant, that's a bearish retracement ceiling. Price should not hold above it on a close. In uptrends, use as support.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ daily: upper quadrant marked; price retraced to it during downtrend but failed to break above it, confirming bearishness.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:12](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=372) marks both quadrants; [0:11:00](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=660) shows upper quadrant as retracement boundary.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Upper quadrant is a precise level; bodies that cannot touch it are strong signal.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Daily Suspension Block (aliases: daily FVG, daily range inefficiency, gray box)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The daily suspension block is the largest, clearest volume imbalance on the daily chart. It brackets a range with a high and low, creating a gray-shaded box on the chart. Intraday price will gravitate toward and eventually fill this range. The low of the daily suspension block is often the deepest intraday target.
- **How to identify:** On the daily chart, find the clearest volume imbalance (where bodies don't connect between two days). Shade it. This is your daily suspension block.
- **How to use:** Use as an intraday target for shorts (if price is above it and expected to drop) or for longs (if price is below it and expected to bounce). Partial profits at the edges (quadrants, octants, midpoint) of the daily suspension block.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ: daily suspension block spanned a huge range (gray box); ICT used it to grade all intraday price action. The low of this box was the intraday target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:57](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=177) identifies daily suspension block; [0:06:12](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=372) divides it into quadrants and octants; [0:08:39](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=519) shows price using it as support/resistance.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Not every daily chart has a clean suspension block; wait for one that's obvious before using it.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Event Horizon (aliases: midpoint of daily suspension block, center void, balance point)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The exact midpoint of the daily suspension block appears empty (a void, the ether), but price gravitates to it with algorithmic precision. This "event horizon" is a balance point where the market pauses or reverses temporarily. It's not marked on most charts, but it exists as pure geometry.
- **How to identify:** (Daily suspension block high + low) ÷ 2 = Event Horizon.
- **How to use:** Use as a mid-point reversal zone, pullback target, or continuation staging point. If price overshoots event horizon, expect it to come back.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ: event horizon calculated; price touched it, bounced, and used it as a reference multiple times.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:16](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=1096) shows price reaching event horizon and reversing.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This level doesn't exist visually; it's pure math. That's why most traders miss it.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Discount Sensitivity (aliases: bullish body placement, upper half usage)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When a PD array is at discount (premium level, resistance), and price pulls back, if bodies enter and close in the upper half of that array (above the 50% line) without entering the lower half, price is showing "discount sensitivity" or bullish bias. The bodies are saying, "We respect this level as discount, but we're still bullish enough to hold above mid-range."
- **How to identify:** Mark a PD array's 50% line. On pullback, watch where bodies close. If in upper half, it's discount sensitivity. If in lower half, it's weakness.
- **How to use:** Discount sensitivity = continuation signal. When price shows it, expect another run higher after the pullback. If bodies breach into lower half, bullishness is broken.
- **Example in this video:** Not directly shown, but the inverse is shown: bodies failing to reach levels = lack of discount sensitivity = bearishness.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:00](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=660) references discount sensitivity concept (bodies in upper half = bullish).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This concept is best understood through its inverse (bodies failing to show discount sensitivity = bearishness).

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Premium Sensitivity (aliases: bearish body placement, lower half usage)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When a PD array is at premium (discount level, support), and price bounces, if bodies enter and close in the lower half of that array (below the 50% line) without entering the upper half, price is showing "premium sensitivity" or bearish bias. The bodies are saying, "We found support, but we're not really bullish; we're still fighting to go lower."
- **How to identify:** Mark a PD array's 50% line. On bounce, watch where bodies close. If in lower half, it's premium sensitivity (bearish). If in upper half, it's strength.
- **How to use:** Premium sensitivity = continuation signal downward. When price shows it, expect another leg lower after the bounce fails. If bodies breach into upper half, bearishness is broken.
- **Example in this video:** Implied in the teaching; bodies failing to touch the lower quadrant during retracement = lack of premium sensitivity = strength to lower side.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:26](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=806) applies this indirectly.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Premium and discount sensitivity are context-dependent; they flip based on whether you're in uptrend or downtrend.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Relative Equal Highs / Lows (aliases: equality of swings, matched highs/lows, second and first swings)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When two swing highs are at roughly the same price level, or two swing lows, the market is creating "relative equal highs" or "relative equal lows." These are key reference points for breakouts and breakdowns. If price breaks below a relative equal low, it signals weakness; above a relative equal high, strength.
- **How to identify:** Plot swings on a daily/weekly chart. If two highs (or lows) are within 50–100 points of each other, mark them as relative equal.
- **How to use:** Relative equal lows act as support; relative equal highs act as resistance. Breaks of these levels confirm directional intent.
- **Example in this video:** Implied in the review (price uses old lows as reference).
- **Timestamps:** Mentioned but not deeply explored in this video.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** None stated.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 08, 2026
head: Algorithmic Precision (aliases: smart money logic, institutional order flow, scripted market moves)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The market is algorithmically driven. When bodies refuse to touch a level multiple times, it's not coincidence; it's a rule. Smart money executes orders such that bodies honor key levels while wicks test them. Once you recognize the pattern (bodies cannot touch), you've found the algorithm's signature. Every move to a key level is pre-planned, not random.
- **How to identify:** Track key levels over multiple candles/days. If bodies consistently refuse to close above or below a level, the algorithm is active there.
- **How to use:** Use this recognition to trade with conviction. Do not ask "why" the bodies refused; just accept that they did and plan your trade accordingly.
- **Example in this video:** The entire 25-minute review is demonstrating algorithmic precision: bodies refusing to touch the lower quadrant = algorithm = bearish = price goes lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:49](https://youtu.be/3Uu2IB6kI28?t=949) makes the claim: bodies cannot touch this line because there's an algorithm directing them not to.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is ICT's core thesis. If you don't believe the algorithm exists, this methodology won't work for you.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Tape Reading (aliases: reading price action, reading the tape, live price observation)
body:
- **Kind:** skill
- **What ICT says:** Tape reading is the disciplined act of watching each candlestick form in real-time, noting how it respects (or breaks) key levels, and building an internal narrative of where price is likely to go next. It's not about trading; it's about observation. The goal is to develop the ability to say, "Okay, price is here, key levels are there, so price should draw to X or Y." Once you can do that consistently (6–8 weeks of daily observation), you're ready for paper trading.
- **How to identify:** Watch a chart at real-time speed. Watch each 1-minute candle open, run through its high/low, and close. Do this live, not in market replay or on video playback (which misses detail).
- **How to use:** Before any trade, spend weeks just observing and predicting. Predict where price will draw. When it does, note if your prediction was right. Build a journal of these predictions; measure accuracy. Once you're consistently correct (60%+), move to paper trading.
- **Example in this video:** ICT tapes reads MNQ: identifies opening range gap, daily suspension block, sell-side/buy-side liquidity. He says, "I expect price to draw to the low of the daily suspension block." He doesn't take a trade; he's just reading. The market goes where he predicted, validating his reading ability.
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:21](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=1581) emphasizes tape reading as the primary skill; [0:27:55](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=1675) says don't use market replay.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the hardest sell to new traders. They want to trade immediately. But ICT insists: tape read first, trade later. The return on time invested is exponential.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: 6-8 Week Development Cycle (aliases: training period, baseline study, foundational phase)
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:** There is no shortcut. Spend a minimum of 6–8 weeks watching price action live (1 hour per day is enough) without placing any trades (demo or real). Keep a journal of your predictions for where price will draw. After 6–8 weeks, you'll have 40–50 days of baseline data. Then, and only then, paper trade for another 6–8 weeks. Only after this 12–16 week foundation are you ready for real trading. Skipping this is how people blow accounts.
- **How to identify:** Your own commitment level. If you can't commit to 6–8 weeks of no-trade observation, don't bother starting.
- **How to use:** Use the first phase to build confidence that the methodology works. Use the second phase to practice execution. Use the third phase to trade with real money, knowing you've prepared thoroughly.
- **Example in this video:** ICT says, "I promise you... 6 to 8 weeks. You have to. If you don't give it 6 weeks, I can't help you. You're going to blow your accounts."

- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is non-negotiable in ICT's framework. He repeats it multiple times, showing its importance.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Fear of Entry (aliases: entry anxiety, hesitation, emotional blocks)
body:
- **Kind:** psychology
- **What ICT says:** Most traders struggle with taking the entry pull the trigger. They've identified the setup, but when the moment comes, fear paralyzes them. They either overshoot the entry or miss it entirely. The remedy: practice entries on paper (not real money) without worrying about the outcome. Place limit orders, watch them hit or miss, and remove the emotion. After 6–8 weeks of this, the fear diminishes.
- **How to identify:** Do you see a setup and hesitate to enter? Do you second-guess your levels? Do you feel your heart rate rise when the price approaches your entry? That's entry fear.
- **How to use:** Therapy: place entries live (paper trading) and accept that some will hit and some won't. The more you do it, the less scary it becomes. It's exposure therapy for traders.
- **Example in this video:** ICT says many traders are "afraid to get in" and this holds them back. The solution is practice without money at risk.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:06](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=1866) identifies fear of entry as a common block; [0:34:23](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2063) addresses it as a training issue.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is normal and universal among developing traders. ICT's message: it's trainable and can be overcome.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Scar Tissue (aliases: trauma from losses, loss aversion, emotional residue)
body:
- **Kind:** psychology
- **What ICT says:** When a trader takes a big loss, they develop "scar tissue." Every subsequent trade feels like it might be another big loss. They flinch at normal market moves, expecting them to be catastrophic. The scar tissue makes you tentative and prevents you from entering trades at all. The remedy: avoid big losses through position sizing and stops. If you do take a loss, don't rush back in; give yourself time to process it. Eventually, the scar tissue fades.
- **How to identify:** Do you feel like every candle is going to hurt you? Do you avoid setups that look similar to ones that lost you money? That's scar tissue talking.
- **How to use:** Acknowledge it's there. Then deliberately place small trades to prove to yourself that not every trade is a disaster. Build winning trades to replace the emotional imprint of the losing one.
- **Example in this video:** ICT says if you get hit by a 400-handle candle (which can happen in volatile markets), the scar tissue will make you scared of every subsequent 1-minute candle. You'll avoid trading altogether.
- **Timestamps:** [0:40:46](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2446) discusses scar tissue from large losses; [0:55:09](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=3309) emphasizes that scar tissue is common and manageable.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is emotional/psychological, not technical. ICT acknowledges it as a real barrier to success.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Slow is Smooth, Smooth is Fast (aliases: patience, tempo, process over outcome)
body:
- **Kind:** philosophy
- **What ICT says:** The fastest way to get good is to go slowly and methodically. Don't rush tape reading. Don't skip paper trading. Don't overtrade. When you slow down, you see details; when you see details, you trade better; when you trade better, you make more money faster than if you'd rushed. The irony: patience is the accelerant.
- **How to identify:** Are you trying to compress 6–8 weeks into 2–3 weeks? Are you jumping to live trading without paper trading? That's rushing.
- **How to use:** Stick to the timeline. 6–8 weeks tape reading. 6–8 weeks paper trading. Then live. Don't deviate. Trust the process.
- **Example in this video:** ICT says, "Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast. Doing it a different way, racing around or trying to skip over things, it's not it."
- **Timestamps:** [0:33:35](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2015) states the phrase directly; [0:41:31](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2491) applies it to the development timeline.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This cuts against the culture of instant results. ICT is explicit: there's no faster way.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Knowing When to "Pull It" (aliases: knowing when to stop, discipline to exit, cutting losses)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Once you've achieved your target or once the setup breaks, you exit. Period. You do not keep running because you got one right. You do not hold hoping for more. You take your win and move on. If the setup breaks (bodies close above a key level, rejection block is breached), you exit immediately. Discipline here separates professionals from gamblers.
- **How to identify:** Have you made your draw? Is the setup still valid? Answer both: if either is no, you pull it.
- **How to use:** Set your target before you enter. When price reaches it, exit. Set your stop before you enter. When price hits it, exit. No adjustments mid-trade (except for scaling out at partial targets).
- **Example in this video:** ICT says, "You have to know when to pull the plug" and "this is your interim report." He exits when the target is hit, even if price continues lower. He doesn't kick himself for leaving money on the table.
- **Timestamps:** [0:38:19](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2299) emphasizes knowing when to stop; [0:39:07](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2347) shows an example of pulling the plug.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is anti-greed and pro-capital-preservation. Most traders struggle with this.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Screen Recording for Delayed Tape Reading (aliases: reviewing recorded sessions, market replay alternative, OBS recording)
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:** If you can't watch the market live, record your screen using OBS (free software) or similar. Then, after you're off work/school, replay the recording at live speed and tape read it. You won't have the real-time feeling, but you'll be able to pause, annotate, and study in detail. This is better than using TradingView's market replay tool (which is choppy and doesn't show every candle's detail).
- **How to identify:** Can you watch live? If not, are you willing to record and replay?
- **How to use:** Set up OBS on your computer. Start a session recording at 9:30 ET. After work, load the file and tape read it at real-time speed. Annotate levels, make predictions, check accuracy. Build your journal.
- **Example in this video:** ICT mentions OBS as his tool; he records through it to YouTube for his streams.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:55](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=1675) criticizes market replay; [0:27:07](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=1627) recommends recording screen + reviewing at real-time speed.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Live is better, but recording + replay is better than market replay or no practice.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Simple Setups vs. Complex Models (aliases: keeping it simple, Occam's razor, Elegance in Trading)
body:
- **Kind:** philosophy
- **What ICT says:** Don't create 20 different entry models. Don't layer on multiple indicators. Don't over-complicate. The simplest setups—fair value gaps, old lows, opening range gaps—are the most reliable. Pick one or two and master them. Complexity is the enemy of consistency.
- **How to identify:** Have you read 10+ books on trading and still can't pick one approach? You're overcomplicating.
- **How to use:** For the first 6–8 weeks of tape reading, focus ONLY on identifying where the daily suspension block is and whether price will fill it. That's it. Once you master that, add one more level of detail. Iterate slowly.
- **Example in this video:** ICT says, "Nothing easier than what I just showed here today. There's nothing easier than that." He's referring to: opening range gap + daily suspension block + bodies on levels = your entire toolkit for the morning.
- **Timestamps:** [0:38:19](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2299) emphasizes simplicity; [0:42:18](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2538) says less moving parts = better results for beginners.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This will feel too simple. Fight the urge to add more. Simple beats complex in this game.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: Arrogance vs. Humility Balance (aliases: Dr. Jekyll vs. Mr. Hyde, confidence vs. overconfidence, ego management)
body:
- **Kind:** psychology
- **What ICT says:** There's a spectrum from fearful (not confident enough to enter) to arrogant (overconfident, risking too much). The sweet spot is Dr. Jekyll: calm, confident, knowing what you're looking for, but humble enough to respect losses. Mr. Hyde (ICT's alter ego on stream) is the arrogant version that emerges when you're winning big. You need to guard against becoming Mr. Hyde; it leads to recklessness.
- **How to identify:** Do you brag about wins online? Do you feel invincible after a few profitable days? That's Mr. Hyde emerging.
- **How to use:** Trade with confidence, but journal every trade (win or loss). Review your journal regularly. When you feel the arrogance creeping in, step away and recalibrate.
- **Example in this video:** ICT says, "When you're making lots of money, you feel invincible, and you dare people to hit me with a bus, bro." That's Mr. Hyde. You need to stay as Dr. Jekyll (calm Michael) in your trading.
- **Timestamps:** [0:37:32](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2252) describes the psychological spectrum; [0:38:19](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=2299) advises encapsulating the calm analyst.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is ongoing mental work; it's not a one-time fix.

title: ICT 2026 OR Tape-reading \ April 08, 2026
head: First Hour Focus / First 30–40 Minutes (aliases: session bias, opening hour, first trades of the day)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** All learning and most profitability comes from understanding the first hour (9:30–10:30 ET). Don't try to trade the lunch hour or the close; you're not ready. Learn the opening range gap, consequent encroachment, and how price uses the daily suspension block in that first hour. Master it. Then, only then, expand to swing trading or position trading using the same logic.
- **How to identify:** Are you trying to trade lunch hour? Close? You're overextending before mastering the opening.
- **How to use:** For the first few months, trade only 9:30–10:00 or 9:30–10:30. Get comfortable with this window. Once you can trade it profitably and consistently, add other hours/days.
- **Example in this video:** ICT focuses the entire tape reading on the opening hour logic.
- **Timestamps:** [0:52:33](https://youtu.be/yqBvOeOKcBM?t=3153) says, "Only need to really carve out the first 35 to 40 minutes."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the quickest path to profitability; ignore it at your peril.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Event-Driven Markets (aliases: geopolitical volatility, news-driven, fundamentally unstable)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Event-driven markets are those where major news (war, leadership changes, policy shifts) temporarily overrides technical analysis. Algorithms are paused; manual intervention increases; price moves become unpredictable. You cannot apply normal tape reading rules because the rules are suspended by events. The best traders do not fight event-driven markets; they sit out.
- **How to identify:** Watch for geopolitical headlines, major policy announcements, and wars/conflicts. When these are active, expect chop, reversals, and 400-handle candles. Markets will also be illiquid (wider spreads).
- **How to use:** When event-driven, reduce size by 50%+ or step away entirely. Accept that you will be wrong more often. Do not demand normal profitability; be grateful if you break even. Consider shifting to education (tape reading) instead of trading.
- **Example in this video:** ICT references Trump's threats to attack Iran, then a sudden ceasefire announcement, causing crude oil to gap down 18+ dollars in minutes. This is event-driven. Normal tape reading rules don't apply.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:19](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=139) introduces the event context; [0:10:20](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=620) emphasizes risk in event-driven markets; [0:21:36](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=1296) admits personal limits in event-driven trading.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** ICT is explicit: even a 34-year veteran cannot "consistently correct" in event-driven conditions. This is humbling and real.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Manual Intervention (aliases: human intervention, direct influence, not algorithmic, hedge fund positioning)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Smart money and governments place large bets ahead of announcements, then use the announcements to trigger their favorable moves. This is "manual intervention"—a human decision to execute a large order at a strategic time, not an algorithm following price action rules. The evidence: a move happens right after a headline, not because the headline changed long-term fair value but because someone was ready to execute.
- **How to identify:** A major headline drops, and price moves 500+ handles in minutes. That's manual intervention, not algorithmic movement. Also, look for moves during off-hours (Asian session, pre-market) that are disproportionate to the news.
- **How to use:** Expect these moves during major events. Use wide stops. Do not hold without stops. If a manual intervention move is against you, size is critical; if your position size is too large, you're wiped out before you can react.
- **Example in this video:** Crude oil gapping down 18+ dollars (9+ points per contract) within minutes after ceasefire announced. This isn't supply/demand; this is a pre-positioned short being executed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:43](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=523) discusses manual intervention on crude oil; [0:20:47](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=1247) explains manual intervention in crypto/equities too.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** ICT is suggesting this is insider trading or at minimum, pre-positioning before announcements. This is a serious allegation but not directly actionable for individual traders.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Rug Pull (aliases: reverse, bait-and-switch, false breakout into trap)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A rug pull is when price makes a strong move in one direction, stops retail traders into that direction (triggering their alarms), then violently reverses and takes the other side. Example: price rallies hard on war fear, stops longs above a key level, then news drops that ceasefire is likely, and shorts are in control. The rally was the rug pull; retail thought it was the main move.
- **How to identify:** Price makes a strong move; you see clips online of traders bragging about their wins; then suddenly price reverses violently. That was a rug pull.
- **How to use:** Don't fall for the initial move. Wait for confirmation that the move is sustained. Use stops to protect yourself if you're caught.
- **Example in this video:** War fear rallies in equities; Trump threatens attacks; retail chases the rally. Then news of ceasefire; rally reversed. The initial rally was the rug pull.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:43](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=523) references the rug pull structure implicitly.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Rug pulls are more obvious in crypto; in equities/futures, they're subtler but same concept.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Volatility Expansion (aliases: large range candles, speed of moves, magnitude increase)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Event-driven markets show extreme volatility: 1-minute candles spanning 400+ handles, 5-minute candles spanning 1,200+ handles. This is not normal. Normal markets have tight, predictable ranges. Event-driven markets break those assumptions. You must respect this by using tight stops and small size.
- **How to identify:** Watch the range of individual 1-minute candles. If you see a 400-handle 1-minute, that's expansion. If you see multiple 1-minute candles with 100+ handle ranges, that's expansion.
- **How to use:** Respect it. If your position size assumes normal volatility (20–40 handle stops), you'll be wiped out by a 400-handle candle. Reduce size or use wider stops (but then you can't take as many trades).
- **Example in this video:** MNQ 1-minute candle: opened 24,600, high 24,748, low 24,360. That's 388 handles in 60 seconds. This is extreme.
- **Timestamps:** [0:39:10](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=2350) shows the 400-handle 1-minute candle; [0:42:21](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=2541) repeats this to emphasize risk.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a wake-up call. If you trade without respecting this volatility, you're taking unnecessary risk.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Education vs. Live Trading Stance (aliases: responsibility teaching, stepping away from live, shifting focus)
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:** ICT decides to step away from live trading and focus only on education because he has influence over many traders. If he calls out a draw and traders follow him into an event-driven market, they may lose money due to forces beyond both their control. This is a moral responsibility. Instead, he'll teach concepts, show historical tape reading, and let traders practice without capital at risk. Once markets normalize, he'll resume live trading.
- **How to identify:** Is your mentor live trading during volatile markets and encouraging you to follow? That's irresponsible. Is your mentor telling you to sit out and practice tape reading? That's responsible.
- **How to use:** Apply this to your own trading: when conditions are unpredictable, don't trade. Teach yourself; practice; wait for clarity. Responsibility to yourself and your capital comes first.
- **Example in this video:** ICT explicitly says, "I'm going to take the responsibility and elevate it in my hands because I want to be able to sleep at night."
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:12](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=1632) makes the decision to shift focus; [0:27:59](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=1679) explains the moral reasoning.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is rare to hear from a mentor; it shows integrity.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (aliases: inverted FVG, gap in trend-opposite direction)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** An inversion FVG is a gap that forms in the opposite direction of the trend. When price trades back into and above an inversion FVG, it confirms continuation of the original trend. This is a strong continuation signal.
- **How to identify:** In an uptrend, a down-gapped candle creates an inversion FVG. In a downtrend, an up-gapped candle creates one.
- **How to use:** When price re-enters and closes above an inversion FVG (in an uptrend) or below one (in a downtrend), expect continuation.
- **Example in this video:** Implied in USD/JPY and EUR/USD reviews; gaps form, then price re-enters them.
- **Timestamps:** [0:28:48](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=1728) references inversion FVG in EUR/USD context.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** In event-driven markets, these setups are less reliable.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Premium / Discount Zones (aliases: overbought/oversold, supply/demand zones, high/low price zones)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Price trades in zones: premium (above fair value, resistance-heavy), equilibrium (fair value), and discount (below fair value, support-heavy). Identify these on daily charts using suspension blocks and opening range gaps. Use them to frame intraday trades.
- **How to identify:** Is price above the midpoint of the daily range? Premium. Below? Discount. At midpoint? Equilibrium.
- **How to use:** Premium zones: look for sells, reversals, short entries. Discount zones: look for buys, bounces, long entries. Equilibrium: expect consolidation.
- **Example in this video:** Currency pairs are analyzed by identifying where they trade relative to daily ranges.
- **Timestamps:** Multiple references throughout (not timestamped individually).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** None stated.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Consequent Encroachment on Wicks (aliases: wick midpoint, wick rejection level, consequent curvature)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When a candlestick forms a large wick (rejection), the consequent encroachment (midpoint) of that wick becomes a key level. If price breaks above that wick midpoint, the wick rejection is breached and bearishness is broken. If price stays below it, the wick rejection holds.
- **How to identify:** Measure the wick high to wick low (or wick to body). Find the 50% point.
- **How to use:** This is a precision level for stops and partial exits. If you're short and price breaks above wick consequent encroachment, the setup is broken; exit.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ tape reading: consequent curvature of wicks used to judge whether bearish tone persists.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:58](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=958) uses this concept; [0:21:33](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=1293) applies it to risk management.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a sub-level of detail; use when you've mastered the main levels.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 07, 2026
head: Relative Equal Highs / Lows (aliases: equality levels, matched highs/lows)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When two swing highs (or lows) are at nearly the same level, they form a relative equal high (or low). These are key breakout/breakdown levels. A break of relative equal highs is a strong bullish signal; a break of relative equal lows is bearish.
- **How to identify:** Plot daily swings. When two swing highs or lows align, mark them as relative equal.
- **How to use:** Relative equal highs act as resistance until broken; then they act as support. Relative equal lows act as support until broken; then they act as resistance.
- **Example in this video:** Pound/Dollar and EUR/USD analyzed using relative equal highs as targets.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:10](https://youtu.be/zpLCZ1Y46Yk?t=1870) shows relative equal highs on cable (GBP/USD).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** In event-driven markets, these levels may be blown through.

title: ICT 2026 Opening Range Tape Reading \ April 07, 2026
head: Opening Range Gap (ORG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule
- **What ICT says:** Yesterday's regular trading hours (RTH) open and close establish the RTH opening range gap for the next day. The gap between 4:14pm ET close and 9:30am ET open forms the structure. If 9:30 open is below the prior close, it's a discount gap (bullish setup likely).
- **How to identify:** Compare 4:14pm ET close to 9:30am ET open; note the high and low of the gap range and subdivide by octants (1/8ths) and quarters.
- **How to use:** Use ORG levels as support/resistance and potential rally/selloff targets. The 50% and 70% retracement levels are common targets.
- **Example in this video:** NQ opened 9:30 at a discount (below prior close); immediately rallied to ~70% of the ORG and failed, indicating weakness. Then traded back into and below the ORG low, confirming further downside potential.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:29](https://youtu.be/gLt8kAG7noQ?t=209), [0:33:38](https://youtu.be/gLt8kAG7noQ?t=2018), [0:34:25](https://youtu.be/gLt8kAG7noQ?t=2065)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** On high-uncertainty days (like this one with geopolitical risk), price action is "wild and woolly" and less precise. ORG analysis is still valid but requires more patience to see clean execution.

title: ICT 2026 Opening Range Tape Reading \ April 07, 2026
head: Liquidity Sweeps (Buy-Side / Sell-Side)
body:
- **Kind:** rule | entry model
- **What ICT says:** On a bearish sentiment day (engineered by news/geopolitical risk), market makers first run price up to take out shorts' stops (buy-side liquidity), then run it down to take out longs' stops (sell-side liquidity). Order of execution matters: if buy side is taken first on a bearish day, sell side remains and should be the next target.
- **How to identify:** Watch for a sharp move that "traps" a logical group of traders (e.g., shortsellers on a bearish day), then reverse. Mark the short-term highs and lows where stops would logically be placed.
- **How to use:** After buy-side (BSL) is swept on a bearish day, expect sell-side sweep next. Don't trade until both sides are cleared, as traders on both sides are "unseated."
- **Example in this video:** 9:30 price ran higher, sweeping shorts' stops. Then it failed to break above ORG high and reversed lower, setting up the sell-side sweep around the lower quadrant/octant levels. By 9:30am, both BSL and SSL were tagged.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:53](https://youtu.be/gLt8kAG7noQ?t=833), [0:16:17](https://youtu.be/gLt8kAG7noQ?t=977), [0:20:29](https://youtu.be/gLt8kAG7noQ?t=1229), [0:35:11](https://youtu.be/gLt8kAG7noQ?t=2111)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a special case of the market maker buy/sell model applied to opening ranges on sentiment-engineered days.

title: ICT 2026 Opening Range Tape Reading \ April 07, 2026
head: Tape Reading & Price Action Interpretation
body:
- **Kind:** rule | definition
- **What ICT says:** Reading the tape means observing which liquidity pools are hit, in what order, and what remains. It's "reading what the market maker is trying to do" by watching what they take out first. The real skill is discerning narrative: geopolitical sentiment → trader positioning → liquidity location → execution order.
- **How to identify:** Chart key price levels (ORG, prior day high/low, BSL, SSL, prior wicks). Watch live candles form and see which levels hold or break.

body:

- **How to use:** Don't trade with sentiment; trade against it once you confirm the setup. But on extremely high-uncertainty days, the risk may be too high.

head: Octant & Quadrant Subdivisions
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Subdivide a gap (ORG, FVG, etc.) into 8ths (octants) and 4ths (quadrants). The lower quadrant (lowest 25%) and lower octants are key support; upper quadrant/octants are resistance. Wicks and bodies often stop at these Fibonacci-like levels.
- **How to identify:** Measure the gap height, divide by 8 and 4, mark the levels on the chart.
- **How to use:** Expect price to find support/resistance at these levels before continuing.
- **Example in this video:** The sell-side wick at 25:54 "touched the lower quadrant or...octant 0.625 (the low of yesterday's RTH opening range gap)." Price body stayed there.

head: Time Distortion & Multiframe Reconciliation
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule | refinement
- **What ICT says:** Choppy, unclear price action on the 1-minute chart is often explained by a higher-timeframe inefficiency (FVG, wick, volume imbalance) being used or awaited. To "clear up time distortion," move to a 5-minute chart; the erratic 1-minute movement becomes a coherent use of a 5-minute-level PD array. If still unclear on 5-minute, zoom out further. The rule: if you see shared ranges or chop with no clear direction on your working timeframe, go up one or more timeframes and find the inefficiency you're inside.
- **How to identify:** Tight, jagged candles with bodies crossing sideways; inability to trend; wicks extending in both directions on 1-minute but no directional bias.
- **How to use:** Don't trade the 1-minute chop directly. Identify the higher-timeframe structure first. Then wait for a setup that aligns both timeframes (e.g., bodies failing to touch a 5-minute inversion FVG midpoint on 1-minute bars).

head: Premium Gap vs. Discount Gap & Opening Range Gap (ORG) Targets
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule | entry model
- **What ICT says:** Premium gap = open above prior close. Discount gap = open below prior close. On a premium gap day, the first protocol is to expect price to trade back into the ORG (back towards or below the opening price, seeking the low of the gap). On a discount gap, expect price to extend higher first, then consolidate. For premium gaps: first target is the opening price itself (9:30); second target is the midpoint (consequent encouragement); full gap closure is the best-case scenario but often won't occur (use a "low-hanging fruit objective"). Time window: 9:30 AM to 10:00 AM (first 30 minutes). Probability: ~70% of the time, at least to the midpoint.
- **How to identify:** Compare prior day's close (4:14 PM ET) to 9:30 AM ET open price. Gap = the difference. Subdivide by octants and quadrants. Mark as "premium" (higher) or "discount" (lower).
- **How to use:** Use ORG levels as natural S/R. Expect partial or full gap retracement within 30 minutes. Stops above (for shorts) or below (for longs) the ORG extremes. Targets at the midpoint or at full closure depending on market structure and time of day.
- **Example in this video:** NQ opened at a premium (above prior close). ICT expected downside penetration to the opening price or the midpoint within the first 30 minutes. This was achieved by ~9:50 AM.

head: Order Flow Logic: Bodies Refusing to Touch PD Array Levels
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule | refinement
- **What ICT says:** When a candlestick body fails to touch the high or midpoint of a PD array (FVG, inversion FVG, wick inefficiency) even though the wick reaches it, this is a "signature" or "big neon sign" of bearish order flow. Wicks can "color outside the lines," but bodies signal intent. If bodies refuse a level = no conviction = weakness = likely to drop. This is NOT supply-and-demand myth; it's institutional algorithm behavior. "If bodies can't even touch the midpoint, I'm looking for it to go lower."
- **How to identify:** Draw a PD array (especially inversion FVG). Watch the candlesticks: if wicks touch the upper boundary but closes stay in the lower half or midrange, bodies are avoiding that level. Multiple candles with this pattern = stronger signal.
- **How to use:** Bodies refusing to touch = bearish; expect a continuation move lower. Conversely, if bodies are consistently closing above the midpoint of a range, that's bullish. Use this to filter entries and set stops. If you're considering a long into an inversion FVG and bodies won't touch the high, don't go long.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5-minute inversion FVG: bodies consistently failed to reach the high end even though wicks did. This signaled that the move up was weak and downside was likely. Later, price dropped to the opening range gap target and closed below it.

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 06, 2026
head: Wicks as Inefficiencies in PD Array Context
body:
- **Kind:** refinement | definition
- **What ICT says:** A wick (especially a one-sided wick) is itself an inefficiency. When a wick is in close proximity to an FVG or imbalance, the wick takes precedence in price's hierarchy of attention. When stop-loss placement or entry logic points to an FVG, always verify: is there a wick nearby? If yes, price may defer to the wick over the FVG. The wick range (high to low) is often where price will work inside before breaking further.
- **How to identify:** Mark wicks separately from candlestick bodies. Note wick-body separation (premium or discount). Use wick high/low as micro-S/R.
- **How to use:** Stop placement: if shorting into an FVG gap, place stop above the nearby wick, not just above the FVG. Entry bias: if price is oscillating within a wick range, it may not break the adjacent FVG immediately. Wait for a candle that closes outside the wick and the FVG.
- **Example in this video:** EUR/USD: "When the area in close proximity the wick is going to be the more salient PD array. It's going to be the one that price is going to factor in more importance, more sensitivity." YM: "This wick takes precedence over that FVG right here."

head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition | refinement | entry model
- **What ICT says:** An inversion FVG is formed when price rallies into a region where it previously had a discount (FVG below), or sells into a region where it previously had a premium (FVG above). The iFVG is the inverse of the prior gap. When a price pulls back into an iFVG after a rally, the bodies not touching the high of the iFVG indicate weakness in the uptrend and forecast a reversal. Conversely, sellers being stopped at the low of an iFVG suggest strength in the downtrend.
- **How to identify:** After a significant move, check if price is retracing into a region that previously had a one-sided gap (now inverted in structure).
- **How to use:** Use iFVG levels to set stops and targets. Entries: if going short into an iFVG rally and bodies won't touch the iFVG midpoint/high, that's a bearish signal for a short. Targets: the iFVG low or the prior FVG below it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5-minute inversion FVG: price rallied into an iFVG, bodies refused to touch the high, and it subsequently dropped to test the opening range gap and prior FVG lows.
- **Timestamps:** [1:20:16](https://youtu.be/5ycp9oGKPms?t=4816), [1:23:28](https://youtu.be/5ycp9oGKPms?t=4808), [1:38:58](https://youtu.be/5ycp9oGKPms?t=5938)

title: ICT 2026 Market Review \ April 06, 2026
head: Volume Imbalance (as distinct from FVG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition | refinement
- **What ICT says:** A volume imbalance is a gap between two candlesticks where there is no overlap in the high/low range. Unlike an FVG (which has a 1–2 candle gap), a volume imbalance can span multiple candles or be a large single-candle gap. Price often revisits and "uses" these imbalances as targets or levels. They work similarly to FVGs in terms of order flow logic.
- **How to identify:** Look for candlesticks with no overlap in range (daily charts often show these clearly). Mark the gap.
- **How to use:** Price targets; support/resistance. When price approaches a volume imbalance, expect to see similar order flow signatures (bodies avoiding, wicks testing, reversals).
- **Example in this video:** Crude oil, Gold, Bitcoin: ICT noted "volume imbalances right there" and stated that traders should keep them on their charts. Also EURUSD and GBPUSD futures daily charts had volume imbalances in daily gaps.

head: Rejecting Higher Timeframe Inefficiencies
body:
- **Kind:** rule | refinement
- **What ICT says:** When price moves into a higher-timeframe inefficiency (e.g., weekly or daily FVG) but wicks out without closing in the upper half, that's a rejection. Bodies not reaching into the range = rejection = likely reversal. This is a strong signal for a counter-directional move.
- **How to identify:** Mark daily/weekly PD arrays. Watch how price interacts: if wicks reach but closes don't, rejection.
- **How to use:** After rejecting a higher-timeframe level, expect a reversion or at least a pullback. Targets: the opposite inefficiency or prior support/resistance.

Analogy: a small child coloring outside a coloring book—you don't scold them; you teach them. Same with price action: permit wicks, read the bodies.
- **How to identify:** Identify candles with long wicks that extend beyond PD array boundaries. Note where the body closes.
- **How to use:** Don't panic when wicks penetrate your expected range. Wait for the body close to confirm the direction.

head: "Phil" — Algorithmic Manipulation & Manual Intervention
body:
- **Kind:** definition | observation
- **What ICT says:** "Phil" is not a real person. It's ICT's label for market manipulation: sudden, localized price spikes or drops that don't align with order flow logic. When ICT calls out "Phil," he means the market maker (or an algorithm) manually intervening to create chaos, stop-hunt, or squeeze shorts/longs. Phil can't do it all day (too obvious), but at opportune moments, you'll see it. The telltale is: a sharp move that trades into a level, then immediately reverses without building conviction (bodies fail to sustain).
- **How to identify:** Sudden sharp moves (1–3 candlestick) with no follow-through. A price spike to a key level that reverses the next candle. Wicks that go far out and close back in the opposite direction.
- **How to use:** When you see Phil, note it but don't trade it. Wait for the reversal or ignore the move. Use Phil as evidence of manipulation to confirm that the opposite move is likely (e.g., if Phil rips it up with no body conviction, short the reversal).
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "I didn't call it um manipulation at the time, but it was happening so quick. I said, 'I like that. We're going to pull back into the range.' And we watched it trade down."

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Suspension Block
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule
- **What ICT says:** A suspension block is a range-bound level where price has consolidated but not broken (yet). As long as bodies trade above the suspension block, it remains supportive (bullish). If price closes below it, the block breaks and downside likely follows. The suspension block is a "line in the sand"—a clear structural boundary. On the daily dollar chart, a suspension block was in play; ICT was watching to see if it would hold.
- **How to identify:** Look for a multi-candle consolidation range (daily or weekly) where price has stopped a move. Note the low of that range as the suspension block threshold.
- **How to use:** Use the block low as a stop-loss level. If holding a bullish position (e.g., long dollars), place stop just below the block. If price breaks the block on a body close, exit or reverse.
- **Example in this video:** Dollar index: a suspension block was in place; as long as no body traded below it, ICT maintained a bullish dollar bias. If the block broke (close below the low), he would shift to bearish.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:23](https://youtu.be/m_ND0oO67cU?t=323), [0:06:12](https://youtu.be/m_ND0oO67cU?t=372), [0:07:48](https://youtu.be/m_ND0oO67cU?t=468)

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Wick Precedence Over Adjacent FVGs
body:
- **Kind:** refinement | rule
- **What ICT says:** When a wick is in close proximity to an FVG, the wick takes precedence in price's attention hierarchy. Price will often work inside the wick range before confirming a move through the FVG. This is especially important for stop placement: if shorting into a FVG and a wick is nearby, set stop above the wick, not just above the FVG. The wick's high becomes the more sensitive level.
- **How to identify:** Mark wicks separately from bodies. Note when a wick sits on the edge of or overlaps with an FVG.
- **How to use:** Set stops above wicks, not FVGs. When price approaches a FVG with a nearby wick, expect price to test the wick range first. Don't assume a direct break through the FVG.
- **Example in this video:** MES: "This wick here. And that's what's being the challenging factor there. Not that swing low. Okay, not that liquidity below that low. It's that wick. It's It's It's staring you in your face, but you don't see it because you don't see an inefficiency."

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Buy-Side / Sell-Side Imbalance with Sell-Side Inefficiency
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A PD array can be defined as "buy side and balance sell side inefficiency." This means: the buy-side imbalance is a gap where buyers eagerly bid price up with no sellers (inefficient); the sell-side inefficiency is the lower level where sellers have concentrated orders. When price trades into this structure, it first "takes" the buy-side, then reverses to "take" the sell-side. Both sides must be tagged for the move to complete.
- **How to identify:** Mark an area of chop or consolidation. Identify where the last rally peaked (buy-side) and where the last dip bottomed (sell-side). The range between is the imbalance.
- **How to use:** Trade into the sell-side after the buy-side has been "taken" (hit). Set targets at the sell-side and below.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "This big buy side and balance sell side inefficiency... That midpoint here. Or consequent encroachment. Uh I want to see does it use this then to make a run higher?"

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Opening Range Gap (ORG) Application on Premium Gap Openings
body:
- **Kind:** rule | entry model | refinement
- **What ICT says:** On a premium gap opening (open above prior close), the first protocol is to watch if price can make it back to the opening price (9:30) within the first 30 minutes. This is the minimum expectation. If bulls want to run higher, they need to at least defend the 9:30 level and start sending it higher from there. Conversely, if they can't hold 9:30, expect downside toward consequent encouragement (the midpoint of the ORG).
- **How to identify:** Compare prior-day close to 9:30 open. If open is higher (premium gap), mark the 9:30 price level.
- **How to use:** On premium gap days, watch the 9:30 level closely. If price closes above it, bulls are defending; if it closes below, bears are winning. Use 9:30 as a pivot for intraday entries.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "This is a 9:30 opening price. We went below it here. We came right back to it now. So bulls, if they really want to send it higher, this would be the minimum expectation here."

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) as Potential Reversal
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule | refinement
- **What ICT says:** After a swing move up or down, if a prior FVG sits at the exact level of a new rally/dip, that prior FVG becomes an "inversion fair value gap"—a potential reversal zone. Price reaching an iFVG and failing to close above/below it (depending on direction) signals weakness in the trend. Entry: short into an iFVG rally if bodies refuse to touch the iFVG midpoint/high.
- **How to identify:** Mark a prior FVG. Note where price rallies into it later. If that prior FVG aligns perfectly with the new high of the rally, it's an iFVG.
- **How to use:** Use iFVG levels as reversal targets. Short into iFVG rallies; cover at the iFVG low or prior support.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "This could potentially become a inversion fair value gap, which is basically laying right top of that same level there, okay?"

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Turtle Soup (False Breakout)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** Turtle soup is a false breakout; price breaks above a key level (relative equal high, resistance) but fails to sustain it, reversing back into the range. Entry: short the breakout at the high; cover at the range midpoint or prior lows. This is a reversal setup.
- **How to identify:** Watch for a candle that closes above a resistance level. If the next few candles close back inside the range, it's likely a turtle soup.
- **How to use:** Short the candle that breaks out above resistance. Set stop above the breakout high. Target: midpoint of the range or prior support.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: "Using this as turtle soup, it's a false breakout, okay? And then expect it to pull back down into the range."
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:26](https://youtu.be/m_ND0oO67cU?t=1586)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Works best in consolidating, non-trend markets; less reliable in strong trends.

head: Octant Levels & Fibonacci Subdivisions
body:

- **How to use:** Use octant levels for stops and micro-targets. Expect bodies to hesitate or reverse at these levels.

head: Low-Resistance Liquidity Run Conditions
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule
- **What ICT says:** Low-resistance liquidity run conditions are price moves where there is minimal supply/demand interference—smooth, fast breakouts with no pullbacks or consolidation. These are ideal for momentum trading and large directional moves. Conversely, choppy, sideways moves with lots of wicks are high-resistance (ugly) conditions and should be avoided or only scalped lightly.
- **How to identify:** Watch candlestick patterns: smooth bodies, minimal wicks, consistent direction = low resistance. Lots of wicks, small bodies, multiple reversals = high resistance.
- **How to use:** Trade only in low-resistance conditions. If market is ugly and choppy, reduce size, avoid leverage, or sit out.
- **Example in this video:** MES: "I don't like markets like this. This is not clean price action...I don't like it. I think it's ugly. I think it shouldn't be taken in terms of using real leverage against it with money and equity."

Phil can't run the market all day (too obvious), but at strategic times, you'll see sudden spikes or drops with no conviction. The signal: wicks extend far, bodies fail to follow through.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Swing High / Swing Low Definition
body:
- **Kind:** definition | refinement
- **What ICT says:** A swing high is NOT just the wick high; it's the highest body close in a series of bodies (or the highest open if the open is higher than the close). A swing low is the lowest body element. When looking for a prior FVG to create an iFVG, you must identify the swing high by its body, not its wick. The wick's damage may have extended beyond, but the swing high for structural purposes is the body.
- **How to identify:** Look at a series of candles. Find the highest close or open (whichever is higher) among the bodies. That's the swing high. Do the same for lows.
- **How to use:** Use swing highs/lows (based on bodies) to find prior FVGs for iFVG setups. Use them as entry/exit levels.
- **Example in this video:** MES: "Swing highs and swing lows are not limited just to the wick high and the wick low of it, okay? So, if we're comparing swings you want to look at the bodies in the rotation that creates a swing high."

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ April 06, 2026
head: Reclaimed Fair Value Gap (Bearish or Bullish)
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule
- **What ICT says:** When price revisits a FVG and closes back inside it (after leaving it earlier), it "reclaims" the gap. A reclaimed bearish FVG occurs after a strong downmove when price pulls back up into the FVG but fails to close above the top (bodies stay in lower half). This reclamation is a continuation pattern: expect downside to resume. Conversely, a reclaimed bullish FVG (after a pullback into it from below) forecasts upside continuation.
- **How to identify:** After price leaves a FVG and moves away, watch if it comes back to touch the FVG. If it closes inside the gap (not above/below it), it's being reclaimed.
- **How to use:** After reclamation, expect the move to continue in the original direction (bearish reclaim = more downside; bullish reclaim = more upside).
- **Example in this video:** MES: "Let's see if this can become a reclaimed bearish fair value gap."
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:18](https://youtu.be/m_ND0oO67cU?t=1398), [0:48:19](https://youtu.be/m_ND0oO67cU?t=2899)

head: Volume Imbalance in Commodities & Precious Metals
body:

- **How to identify:** Look for large single-candle gaps (or multi-candle gaps) where no candlestick overlaps the preceding one. Mark the gap as a volume imbalance.
- **How to use:** Volume imbalances are targets when price moves away from them. Use them for profit-taking or to set additional targets.

head: Tape Reading vs. Trading (Observation Without Capital Risk)
body:
- **Kind:** psychology | process
- **What ICT says:** When returning from vacation or getting out of sync with price, tape reading is the primary activity: observe how price uses levels, where it gets trapped, how it reverses. Do NOT take real trades during this re-acclimation period. Tape reading is learning; it's free. Trading is capital risking. For new traders, tape reading for weeks is required before any live trading.
- **How to identify:** Yourself: are you taking real positions? If yes, you're trading. If you're just annotating and observing, you're tape reading.
- **How to use:** Spend weeks tape reading before trading. Journal your observations. Compare predictions to actual price action. Build confidence first.
- **Example in this video:** "When I come back from uh like a vacation or getaway or if I fall ill and I'm away from price action and I'm not able to really digest price and see what it's doing watching it trading it, even tape reading it. Uh what I generally do is I don't really try to record any new levels. I'm just watching. I'm just observing."

title: ICT 2026 1st Hour Dealing Range \ March 28, 2026
head: First Hour's Dealing Range (FHDR)  (aliases: "first hour's range", "first hour's dealing range")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - The algorithm's reference range is the first *hour* of the regular session, 9:30 to 10:30 ET, not the 5-, 15- or 30-minute "opening range breakout" ranges that influencers trade.
  - Mechanics on the chart: mark 9:30 and 10:30 ET, then snap the range box to the highest high and lowest low printed between them.
  - He says he writes the FHDR levels on his notepad the moment 10:30 passes, then watches time and price against them for the rest of the day.
  - He is explicitly not a breakout trader (does not buy broken resistance or sell broken support). He uses the range to judge where manipulation vs. real delivery happens.
  - He offers it as a side study: collect data, see if it adds to what you already do. He does not demand you replace a working model.
- **How to identify:** 9:30–10:30 ET high and low (use Eastern time on the chart regardless of where you live). The first 30 minutes (9:30–10:00) is the opening range and sits inside it. Equilibrium = 50% of the FHDR.
- **How to use:**
  - If price is one-sided from the open (example: gapped lower, never retraced into the gap, made the low at 10:00) the FHDR is one-sided and shorts are the profitable side. That is what entices retail to chase the "breakout", which sets up the shallow stop run and turtle soup below the low (see Turtle Soup entry).
  - The equilibrium of the FHDR is a valid retracement target for the lunch macro (see Lunch macro).
  - Project the range (see Projections entry).
- **Example in this video:** MNQ 1-minute, Friday Mar 27, 2026 (video recorded Mar 28). Price gapped below the RTH open (9:30 ET open), never traded into the gap ("gap and go"), made the FHDR low around 10:00, retraced to the FHDR 50% / 10:00-high area in the 10:30–11:30 window, was rejected, broke the low shallowly, and trended lower into the PM session.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:35:17](https://youtu.be/6DuByzKLDsc?t=2117) — announces the lesson ("first hour dealing range")
  - [0:43:30](https://youtu.be/6DuByzKLDsc?t=2610) — draws 9:30–10:30 and snaps to the lowest low

- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** New in the 2026 series; he says it is "what the algorithm refers to". Contrasts with generic ORB ranges. He stresses he said all of this live in the Friday stream before it happened and tells viewers to go check that recording (9:30–10:30 portion).

title: ICT 2026 1st Hour Dealing Range \ March 28, 2026
head: RTH Opening Range Gap (RTH ORG) and its consequent encroachment
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule of thumb
- **What ICT says:**
  - The gap is between the prior RTH settlement price (the 4:14 PM ET candle close on Thursday, in this example; he calls it "4:14's regular trading hours settlement price") and the 9:30 ET open.
  - The side above is labelled RTH ORG **high**, the side below is RTH ORG **low**. In the example the 9:30 open was below the prior close, so the prior close is the ORG high and the open is the ORG low (sell-side delivery with the opening price gap).
  - Putting a fib across the two points gives 50%, the consequent encroachment of the gap.
  - Rule: in the first 30 minutes (9:31–10:00 ET) always allow for price to try to reach the midpoint of the opening range gap; he states a 70% likelihood.
  - The gap only exists on the RTH chart. On an electronic trading hours (ETH) chart overnight price action fills the space, so "make sure you're looking at the right chart".
- **How to identify:** compare 4:14/4:15 PM ET prior-day RTH close vs 9:30 AM open on a futures chart (use RTH session settings).
- **How to use:** expect an attempt at the gap CE between 9:31–10:00; but he was reluctant to short the retracement from the gap on Friday (holiday-type conditions, TGIF) and wanted more evidence.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ Friday: gap down at 9:30; price did not reach the gap CE ("gap and go"); the first retracement up to the gap he had marked before it happened but did not trade.
- **Timestamps:**

head: Wick consequent encroachment as a dominant PD array ("bodies tell the narrative, wicks do the damage")  (aliases: wick CE, wicks are the dominant PDA)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A wick that sits next to (just left of) a fair value gap can be the dominant PD array: price can poke a wick outside it but the bodies stay inside, and that defines the boundary. EURUSD example: two consecutive SIBIs plus a wick; bodies stayed inside the wick while wicks poked out.
  - Put a 50% fib across a candle (open to low for a down candle) to get its CE. A body *closing below* that CE (EURUSD, the 23rd candle) is indicative of continuation, i.e. more probable that it goes lower.
  - On the NQ session: when a candle closes below the CE (midpoint) of a specific wick inside the first hour's range, "in many ways a confirmation" that the PM session continues lower. He said live that he would not return for the PM session but the afternoon should be bearish.
  - "Chihuahua on the porch": price breaks out of the range shallowly then runs back inside; if it keeps going it will continue, but if it returns inside it was a false run.
  - Wicks can "color outside the lines" of a bearish FVG as long as the bodies stay in the lower half; he asks students to be forgiving and flexible because markets are not perfect.
- **How to identify:** Mark CE of the wick (50% of the wick candle range). Judge by where *bodies close*, not where wicks poke.
- **How to use:** A close below the wick CE in the first hour is the confirmation for a PM-session continuation. If price instead returns into the range and keeps bodies above, the bias is in doubt.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD daily; MNQ 1-minute Friday first-hour wick CE closing break; wicks outside the FVG but bodies inside the lower half (reclaimed bearish FVG, below).
- **Timestamps:**

head: Reclaimed Bearish Fair Value Gap  (aliases: reclaimed bearish FVG, inversion FVG, bearish FVG that was reclaimed)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement of iFVG
- **What ICT says:**
  - When price trades up through a sell-side imbalance / buy-side inefficiency (a SIBI), then closes back below it, the gap becomes an inversion / "reclaimed" bearish FVG. Any retracement into it afterward is a premium array to sell from.
  - Order flow check: for a bearish FVG the bodies should stay in the lower half of the gap (below CE). Wicks may poke up through the upper half; bodies must not.
  - Sequence he walked: price reaches a PD array, fails to reach even the CE, then drops. A failure to reach CE shows weakness, "if you can't even meet me halfway, why bother".
  - After buy-side is run and bodies close back below the gap, the bodies confirm the run was a stop hunt; then look for the next premium PD array to short.
- **How to identify:** Candle closes through the gap then returns to retest it; bodies' location in the gap halves tells order flow.
- **How to use:** Sell the retracement into the reclaimed gap (or the first gap after the range break, see below). Be flexible with wicks.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ Friday PM session: several runs up into reclaimed bearish FVGs failed (sometimes wicks through, bodies below) and each preceded more downside, sell-side cleared; a wick through the last gap was labelled a stop run.
- **Timestamps:**

  - [0:59:28](https://youtu.be/6DuByzKLDsc?t=3568) — bodies in lower half; wicks can come up

If the gap exists, include it in the FVG/wick boundary (e.g. close 35 3/4 vs open 35 1/2 means volume imbalance exists, include it; close 77 3/4 vs open 78 also).

  - The run just below the low (the "test") is not the break; the real break happens after the test and retrace. After a test and retrace the first gap after blowing through is the trade.
  - If the retracement into that gap cannot reach CE, that is the signature of weakness and the run continues.
  - He also warns against others "teaching" that he never said (e.g., entering the wrong gap).
  - "In a trending day, how do we know it's going to be a trending day?" — by the earlier criterion: a closing basis break below the wick CE inside the first hour's range sets up lower prices in the afternoon.
- **How to identify:** After the FHDR low is taken, find the first FVG formed in the down move.
- **How to use:** Short the retracement into that FVG (bodies below CE). Stops above the gap's high. Trail with the three-candle rule (below).

head: Three-Candle Trailing Stop  (aliases: trail every three candles, strangle the unrealized profit)
body:

No swing highs required. If stopped out, walk away. Do not use this on every trade, only when conditions make a reversal likely and targets are not being reached. The partials he takes on up-close candles use the same logic.
- **How to use:** Also helpful to avoid overnight/weekend gap risk (Sunday gap opening can go against you).
