title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** core entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:** An iFVG forms when price trades *above* a bullish gap (SIBI/volume imbalance), then pulls back into it. If it re-enters and refuses to lay a body in the upper half (stays in lower half), it becomes valid. An iFVG is *not* a zone idea; it's an inefficiency defined by open/close on specific candles. Must measure with precision: open and close matter, not just high/low.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Spot a swing low, price drops, creates volume imbalance (gap).
  2. Price trades up above it, bodies leave the gap.
  3. Price retraces back into the gap.
  4. Check: if body *closes below* the midpoint (consequent encroachment), it is a bearish iFVG.
  5. If body refuses upper half when it re-enters, rejection is confirmed.
- **How to use:** Bearish iFVG = anticipate lower prices. If price fails to enter the lower half or spends too much time in the gap (time distortion), the setup is compromised. When invalid, it may act as a balanced price range instead. Use as entry bias on lower timeframes after confirming on higher timeframe structure.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, ~9:31 ET: price creates volume imbalance (SIBI) off swing low. At 0:04:46–0:06:25, price dips into first present-to-iFVG, which becomes valid as inversion. By 0:20:42–0:27:52, ICT enters short into consequent encroachment of an iFVG wick with minimal risk, exiting below 24,351 1/4. Price then delivers lower as the iFVG expected.
- **Timestamps:** 
  - [0:04:46](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=286) — first present-to-FVG identified (volume imbalance, 1-minute)
  - [0:20:42](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1242) — iFVG bias setup and why NOT to trade Friday morning
  - [0:27:52](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1672) — short entry on consequent encroachment; exit below 24,351 1/4
  - [0:45:01](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=2701) — Bitcoin example: sell-side inefficiency becomes iFVG; fails to touch consequent encroachment = immediate bearish feedback
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** 
  - An iFVG is *not* valid until price lays a body in it. Only re-entry + body closure in lower half = valid.
  - If too many candles (>2) spend time inside the gap, it loses power (time distortion weakness). Price should enter in 1–2 candles and *leave immediately* if the gap is truly valid.
  - iFVG trades *above* the gap first, then retraces into it (unlike a standard FVG which is hit first).
  - On Fridays (TGIF), iFVGs are less reliable because gap risk from Sunday open overrides intraday moves.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Consequent Encroachment
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Split any gap or wick in half. That midpoint is consequent encroachment. If price reaches it but fails to touch it, that is immediate feedback on the direction. Failure to touch midpoint = weakness in the opposite direction.
- **How to identify:** Measure gap/wick high and low, divide by 2. Draw a line at that midpoint.
- **How to use:** 
  - Bearish signal: if price runs up but refuses to touch consequent encroachment midpoint of a daily wick, expect reversal lower.
  - Entry signal: when price re-enters an iFVG and trades to consequent encroachment of that wick, that's a premium entry point.
  - Stop placement: if shorting and price gets a body above consequent encroachment of a gap, consider closing the trade.
- **Example in this video:** Daily chart, March 9 wick: price fails to reach the halfway point (consequent encroachment). This is distribution; even on a 1-minute chart, the failure to touch the daily wick's midpoint signals lower prices coming. ~0:13:35–0:14:22.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:13:35](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=815) — daily wick graded; consequent encroachment marked and how failure to reach it = distribution
  - [0:29:31](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1771) — entry at consequent encroachment of a wick separation; tight, precise entry
  - [0:45:50](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=2750) — Bitcoin: "split the range in half. That's consequent encroachment. It trades up to it, but it fails to touch it. This is just like immediate rebounds."
- **Nuance:** Consequent encroachment is *always* the midpoint; it is a precise level, not a range. It is used to measure both gaps and wicks.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Fair Value Gap (FVG) – Present-to-FVG Entry Recognition
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** A volume imbalance (gap between candle open and prior close with no trade between) is a FVG. When price pulls back into it after moving away, that's the entry opportunity. A "present-to-FVG" is the first FVG to form in a session or structure.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Spot a candle whose open is more than 1 tick away from the prior candle's close.
  2. Measure that gap; it is the FVG.
  3. When price re-enters it, measure consequent encroachment of that gap.
  4. Entry occurs as price approaches the consequent encroachment.
- **How to use:** Present-to-FVG acts as the first bias entry for the day or sequence. After the first FVG delivers, subsequent gaps have less weight. Use to anchor initial bias and initial stop placement.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, 9:31: first present-to-FVG identified at 0:04:46. Price then dips to that level and sets up the trade. The video uses this FVG as the foundational bias for the morning setup.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:04:46](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=286) — first present-to-FVG (volume imbalance on open)
  - [0:19:05](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1145) — returning to the first present-to-FVG, explaining why it's the first bias
- **Nuance:** Present-to-FVG is most relevant at session open. Later FVGs may act differently depending on time of day and prior context.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Volume Imbalance (Order Block / PD Array)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** A candle with an open and close that creates a gap to the previous candle (no trade between them) is a volume imbalance. It is a specific inefficiency that price is likely to revisit. Do not treat it as a zone; treat it as a precise range to be filled or respected.
- **How to identify:** Compare prior candle close to current candle open. If there's a gap (no bodies in between), that is the imbalance. Measure it by the open and close of the candle that created it.
- **How to use:** Price returning to the imbalance (FVG) can act as continuation, reversal, or balanced price range depending on context and how price interacts with consequent encroachment.
- **Example in this video:** 0:04:46, 0:05:33 — volume imbalance on the 9:31 1-minute candle with open 13 1/4, close 13 1/2 (1-tick imbalance). This becomes the first-present-to-FVG reference.
- **Nuance:** Volume imbalance and FVG are used interchangeably here; the term depends on context (imbalance = the raw gap; FVG = imbalance with price action interpretation).

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Tape Reading / Order Flow Observation
body:
- **Kind:** process / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Tape reading is *visual* observation of open, high, low, close (OHLC) to determine intent without looking at footprint, order book, or data crunching. If price can't reach a level it "should," that's feedback: it's weak in that direction. If it does reach it quickly and decisively, that's strength. Your job as a beginner is to *observe*, not to trade. Watch price interaction with PD arrays and document whether it behaves as expected.
- **How to identify:** When learning, don't place trades. Instead, draw levels and watch price:
  - Does price reach the level it should?
  - Does it leave a body or just a wick?
  - How fast does it move through/away from the level?
  - How much time does it spend in inefficiencies?
- **How to use:** Use tape reading as a *defensive practice*. If a level *should* be hit but isn't, that's a sign not to trade, or to scale out of a position. Document this feedback loop to refine your model. Do not force trades; let the market confirm your bias through observable price behavior.
- **Example in this video:** ~0:33:54–0:37:01 — ICT watches price action and notes that the inversion FVG is not delivering as expected (lethargic, time distortion). Rather than forcing a short, he sits out, observing. By 0:34:40–0:36:13, he walks through what should happen vs. what is happening, using that gap to decide *against* trading.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:33:54](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=2034) — "tape reading purposes, while you're learning… you're not trying to take a demo entry… you want to measure the willingness"
  - [0:47:48](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=2868) — "when you're tape reading, you're not trying to hold yourself to being right or wrong… you're trying to collect information"
- **Nuance:** Tape reading is *not* a trade method; it is a *learning* method. Only after weeks of observing should you attempt small paper trades.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Time Distortion in Gaps (Weakness Indicator)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** If price spends too much time (more than 1–2 candles) inside a FVG, the gap has lost validity. A strong gap is entered and exited in 1–2 candles *maximum*. Time inside = hesitation = weakness. Prolonged candles in a gap means the market is not in a hurry to move, which contradicts the premise that the gap should be filled/rejected urgently.
- **How to identify:** Count how many candles price spends with bodies inside the gap. If >2, flag it as weak.
- **How to use:** 
  - If you're short and price lingers in a gap for 3+ candles, consider taking off a position.
  - If gap time distortion occurs, do not anticipate immediate continuation in your bias direction.
  - Use time distortion as a stop or pivot signal: if price *should* be moving but isn't, it's a warning.
- **Example in this video:** ~0:16:48–0:17:34 — "See how many times it's used that little area? Now, compare contrast that with when the market's really wanting to move, it'll go on there one candle and then it's gone. Elvis has left the building." Also at 0:31:08–0:31:57: "Too many candlesticks inside a fair value gap. It needs to be one, maybe two at most, and leave."
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:16:48](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1008) — multiple uses of the same gap area = weakness
  - [0:31:08](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1868) — "Too many candlesticks inside a fair value gap… they're not going to waste your time… [if valid] they're going to try to run"
  - [0:98:46](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=5926) — "See how much time [is] staying in that gap? We don't want to see time distortion inside of inefficiencies."
- **Nuance:** Time distortion is most relevant when you have a clear directional bias. If price should move quickly to an objective but doesn't, it's a sign of trapped traders or a lack of conviction on that move.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL) / Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL) and Liquidity Pools
body:
- **Kind:** definition / concept
- **What ICT says:** Liquidity rests at certain levels. A high where many traders have stops above is "sell-side liquidity" (SSL); a low where stops are placed below is "buy-side liquidity" (BSL). Market makers hunt these levels. You must identify them on your structure and expect price to run to them. Sell-side imbalance = inefficiency below a high (e.g., gap down after a high). Buy-side imbalance = inefficiency above a low (e.g., gap up after a low).
- **How to identify:** 
  - Identify swing highs and lows.
  - Assume stops are placed just beyond them (e.g., 2–5 ticks above a high, 2–5 ticks below a low).
  - That aggregated stop placement = the liquidity pool.
  - When a gap forms adjacent to such a level, it is imbalance near liquidity.
- **How to use:** 
  - Bias towards price running to liquidity (e.g., if you're bullish, look for price to run to a prior swing high's SSL).
  - Use liquidity objectives as targets, not precise entry triggers.
  - Recognize that liquidity hunts are a market maker behavior; expect sudden runs and reversals at these levels.
- **Example in this video:** 0:07:12–0:08:46 — daily chart shows "an intermediate-term sell side liquidity pool" below the daily suspension block. ICT notes this as a target or resistance if price continues lower. On the 1m, multiple references to "buy side here" and "sell side there" throughout.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:07:12](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=432) — sell-side intermediate-term liquidity pool on daily
  - [0:19:05](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1145) — buy-side order imbalance in opening range gap
  - [0:34:40](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=2080) — daily buy-side imbalance / sell-side inefficiency trade example
- **Nuance:** Liquidity pools are not precisely defined; they are inferred from structure. Precision comes from the imbalance (gap) adjacent to them, not the exact high/low.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Judas Swing / False Move
body:
- **Kind:** pattern / rule
- **What ICT says:** A Judas swing is a move in one direction (e.g., down) that pulls traders in, then reverses sharply against them. It is often followed immediately by the opposite move. Used to trap traders and generate liquidity for the real move.
- **How to identify:** Price breaks a level or takes out a low, then reverses hard. The break can be 1 tick or several ticks; the key is the false direction followed by sharp reversal.
- **How to use:** 
  - Do not chase breakouts blindly.
  - Expect Judas swings around key levels.
  - If you see a break followed by quick reversal, assume it was a Judas swing and expect the opposite direction to dominate next.
- **Example in this video:** 0:26:58 — "this Judas swing there. We gave up the ghost came back up inside here." Price runs down, traps shorts, then reverses.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:26:58](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1618) — Judas swing on daily chart, Wednesday session
- **Nuance:** Judas swings are common before large moves. Expect them and use them to filter out early entries.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Consequent Correction
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement (related to consequent encroachment)
- **What ICT says:** "Consequent correction" is the midpoint of a wick (similar to consequent encroachment but applied to a wick structure). If price gaps below a wick and then pulls back up, the midpoint of that wick is resistance; price staying below it confirms bearishness.
- **How to identify:** Measure the wick high and low, find the midpoint, and observe price interaction.
- **How to use:** Entry point: if price gaps below and you want to short, look for a pull-back toward consequent correction of the wick, then short the rejection from there. Stop: place it 1 tick above consequent correction of the wick.
- **Example in this video:** 0:42:39–0:43:26 — gold chart: ICT draws consequent correction of a wick, then says "I'd like to see a gap below that" on Sunday opening. If price gaps below and stays heavy (not returning into the upper half), very bearish.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:42:39](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=2559) — gold gap and consequent correction of wick
  - [0:55:04](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=3304) — consequent correction in real-time chart setup on MES
- **Nuance:** Consequent correction is used when there is a gap (suspension block or open gap). If no gap, use consequent encroachment instead.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: TGIF (Thursday Is FUN) / Day-of-Week Effects
body:
- **Kind:** rule / bias filter
- **What ICT says:** Friday (TGIF) is a high-risk day for shorts because weekend gap risk is extreme. Traders may not hold bearish positions overnight. Instead, the market may keep price rangebound on Friday and gap open radically lower on Sunday at 6 pm ET. Do not assume Friday will deliver bearish moves; use caution. If in doubt on Friday, sit out the trade.
- **How to identify:** It's Friday. Check the calendar.
- **How to use:** 
  - Reduce position size on Fridays.
  - Avoid shorting setups unless the bias is very clear (e.g., a strong break below a key level *with* price already moving decisively).
  - Be willing to miss Friday trades and wait for Monday.
  - Anticipate gap risk; assume the gap will be filled or exceeded on Sunday open.
- **Example in this video:** 0:20:42–0:23:02 — "Because it's Friday, I'm a little reluctant to trust this going down." ICT has a bearish setup but does not take it because it's Friday and TGIF dynamics apply. Also at 0:34:09 onwards: the entire afternoon is spent managing this because it's TGIF and Friday behavior is unpredictable.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:20:42](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1242) — "because it's Friday, I'm a little reluctant"
  - [0:23:02](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1382) — explaining TGIF and why he won't short the setup despite bias
  - [0:49:48](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=2988) — "just be careful… don't marry the vein… Because it's TGIF"
- **Nuance:** TGIF is a contextual filter, not a rule that prevents all Friday trades. High-conviction setups (e.g., a break below a critical structure level) can still work, but require tighter risk management.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Opening Range Gap (ORG) / RTH Opening Range
body:
- **Kind:** definition / context
- **What ICT says:** The opening range gap is the gap between the pre-market or previous day's close and the 9:30 ET RTH open. It can be a gap up (bullish) or gap down (bearish). This gap's size and location relative to prior structure matters. A "deep deep discount opening range gap" means we opened much lower than expected relative to prior price. The low of this opening range and its high are key liquidity points.
- **How to identify:** 
  - Pre-market close or previous day settlement.
  - 9:30 RTH open candle.
  - Measure the gap between them.
  - Identify the high and low of the opening range for the day (typically the 9:30 candle or first few minutes).
- **How to use:** 
  - If it's a deep discount, shorts may be cautious (too good to be true).
  - If it's a gap up into resistance, longs are chasing.
  - Use the opening range high/low as pivotal support/resistance.
  - The liquidity inside the gap is a target for price to visit.
- **Example in this video:** 0:03:08 — "opening price at 9:30 there" (opening range gap low). The opening range high is also identified, and ICT explains that price must clear it to confirm bullish action.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:00:30](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=30) — "I have deep deep deep deep discount opening range gap here"
  - [0:03:08](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=188) — opening price identified; trading hour opening range gap defined
  - [0:19:05](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1145) — "opening range gap low, which is at opening price at 9:30"
- **Nuance:** Opening range gaps are session-specific. On Friday, opening gaps are less reliable guides due to weekend gap risk.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Suspension Block / Breaker Block
body:
- **Kind:** definition / PD array variant
- **What ICT says:** A suspension block (also called a breaker block in some contexts) forms when price consolidates with a high and low that define a range, then breaks out. If it breaks higher and is bullish, price is expected to stay above the midpoint (consequent encroachment) of that block going forward; if bearish, it should stay below. If it re-enters and trades back into the block, the nature of that re-entry (which half it enters) determines continuation or reversal.
- **How to identify:** A candle or multi-candle range with a clear high and low, followed by a break in one direction.
- **How to use:** 
  - If bullish suspension block and price re-enters it, expect it to stay in the upper half and continue higher.
  - If it lays a body in the lower half, that is bearish rejection of the bullish bias.
  - Use consequent encroachment of the block as the dividing line.
- **Example in this video:** 0:06:25–0:07:12 — daily chart: "we have a suspension block here and that is noteworthy… a bullish suspension block, if we trade down in the lower half of it, if we're bearish."
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:06:25](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=385) — suspension block identified on daily
  - [0:07:12](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=432) — explaining suspension block rules
- **Nuance:** Suspension block is a structural concept; the rules depend on whether it is bullish or bearish and how price re-enters it.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Balanced Price Range (BPR)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / PD array state
- **What ICT says:** A balanced price range forms when price trades both above and below a gap/FVG (or any PD array) without committing to either direction. This means the gap has acted as both support and resistance (buy side AND sell side). Once established, a BPR is neutral; price can break either way next.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Price moves above the gap/array.
  2. Price pulls back and trades inside/below the gap/array.
  3. Price re-enters and moves above it again.
  4. Two passes (above and below) = balanced price range.
- **How to use:** Once a BPR is established, do not trade off the gap alone. Wait for price to break decisively in one direction, ideally with additional confluence (e.g., a fresh lower-timeframe FVG, a time-of-day macro, a liquidity level). Do not assume the gap will deliver anymore.
- **Example in this video:** 0:54:50–0:57:13 — MES on 1m: a gap is traded above, then below, then above again. This creates a BPR. ICT notes that the gap is no longer a reliable bias tool after it becomes balanced.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:54:50](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=3290) — price above gap, then below, then above again = balanced price range
  - [0:56:26](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=3386) — "that specific candlestick right there… that's what it's doing. That's the function."
- **Nuance:** A BPR is a neutral state; it does not predict direction. Use it to *avoid* trading, not to set up entries.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Discount / Premium / Equilibrium (Daily Range Context)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / context
- **What ICT says:** 
  - Discount: price in the lower half of a daily range (RTH).
  - Premium: price in the upper half of a daily range.
  - Equilibrium: price at the midpoint.
  Being in deep discount when you're trying to short is a problem: the move has already happened, and price should accelerate lower if the bias is correct, not linger. Linger = weakness.
- **How to identify:** Calculate the daily high and low (RTH only), find the midpoint. Check where current price sits relative to it.
- **How to use:** 
  - If bearish and price is in deep discount, the burden is on price to accelerate lower. If it doesn't, the trade is suspect.
  - If bullish and price is in deep premium, expect a pullback to equilibrium or lower before continuation up.
  - Use discount/premium as a bias confirmation: a strong move should accelerate when it reaches discount/premium, not consolidate.
- **Example in this video:** 0:88:25 onwards — ICT checks where NQ is relative to the daily range, finds it in deep discount. He notes that being short from deep discount means price *should* be accelerating lower, but it's not, which is a warning sign.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:84:21](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=5061) — range calculation and discount/premium concept
  - [0:88:25](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=5305) — "we're in a deep deep deep discount… you don't want to be getting short like this"
  - [0:104:21](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=6261) — "in the lowest portion of [the daily] range"
- **Nuance:** Discount/premium is contextual. On a strong trend day, price can remain in premium or discount for hours. Use it as a *pressure* signal, not a reversal signal.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 27, 2026
head: Market Structure Break / Consequent Encroachment Failure (as a Weakness Signal)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** If price is expected to break a level (e.g., a high) but fails even to reach the midpoint (consequent encroachment) of a gap/wick before that level, that is weakness. It indicates lack of conviction. "Failure to touch consequent encroachment" is immediate bearish or bullish feedback depending on direction.
- **How to identify:** Price moves toward a level, reaches only the midpoint or less of a gap/wick, reverses before reaching the level. That is failure.
- **How to use:** 
  - If you expect bullish breakout and price fails to reach the midpoint of a resistance gap, expect lower prices.
  - If bearish and price fails to reach the midpoint of a support gap, expect higher prices.
  - Use failure as a signal to exit or avoid the trade.
- **Example in this video:** 0:13:35–0:14:22 — "the fact that it can't get up to its halfway point on that daily wick… this is distribution. This is not a bull flag."
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:13:35](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=815) — failure to touch daily wick midpoint = distribution
  - [0:22:01](https://youtu.be/z6AxPV2NQ9U?t=1321) — "this is heavy distribution"
- **Nuance:** Failure is contextual; one instance is interesting, but repeated failure confirms weakness.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 25, 2026
head: Volume Imbalance (Refined: Wicks Bridging the Gap)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / definition
- **What ICT says:** A volume imbalance (FVG) exists when bodies do not fill the gap between candles, even if *wicks* extend into that gap and touch both the prior close and current open. The bodies' absence is what defines the imbalance; wicks don't invalidate it. These imbalances are "pertinent to future price action."
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Spot a gap between candle bodies (prior close to current open).
  2. Check if wicks reach into the gap; they may touch both sides but don't fill with bodies.
  3. If bodies stay above or below, it is still a volume imbalance.
  4. Measure the imbalance by the body extremes (not wick extremes).
- **How to use:** Treat the imbalance as a PD array to be respected or filled. Wicks touching the gap are secondary; bodies matter. Use for higher-timeframe bias on lower-timeframe trades.
- **Example in this video:** DXY daily, ~0:04:12: a candle's high is 99.299, low touches 98.something; wicks bridge the prior gap, but bodies define the imbalance. This imbalance is still pertinent to future price. "Even though the wicks are actually bridging the gap between the two, it's still a volume imbalance."
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:04:12](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=252) — "Even though the wicks are actually bridging the gap… it's still a volume imbalance. And those levels are pertinent to future price action."
- **Nuance:** This is a refinement to clarify that volume imbalances are defined by *body placement*, not wick extremes. Many retail traders dismiss imbalances when wicks touch both sides; ICT clarifies this is wrong.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 25, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) – Context & Confirmation
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / bias filter
- **What ICT says:** An iFVG is valid when price trades *below* a level (bears in control), then pulls back into the gap but refuses to break above consequent encroachment or lay bodies in the upper half. Use iFVGs as bias anchors on daily charts; apply on lower timeframes for entries. "Until I'm proven wrong in this being traded above," treat it as an inversion FVG and expect lower prices.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Price is already trading below a gap (sell-side imbalance intact).
  2. Price rallies back into the gap but fails to close above the midpoint (consequent encroachment).
  3. No body in the upper half.
  4. This is a confirmed iFVG (bearish bias).
- **How to use:** Use on daily as macro bias. Apply on 1m, 5m, 15m to find entries. Example: if daily shows price respecting an iFVG (not breaking above it), enter shorts on lower timeframe reversals from the gap. Targets: sell-side below the gap.
- **Example in this video:** 
  - DXY daily: volume imbalance acts as iFVG; if price gets below it, expect retracement lower into sell-side (0:04:59–0:05:47).
  - EURUSD daily (0:08:54–0:10:30): "Right now, the characteristic that it's under… is that of inversion fair value gap… until I'm proven wrong in this being traded above, I'm looking for Euro dollar to give up the ghost and make a run below this low."
  - GBPUSD (0:13:39–0:15:59): also iFVG on daily; if violated to upside, ICT is wrong.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:08:54](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=534) — EURUSD iFVG definition
  - [0:10:30](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=630) — "If we get back above this… then I would expect this to become a reclaimed bullish fair value gap. But right now… it's that of inversion fair value gap."
  - [0:13:39](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=819) — GBPUSD iFVG; "very formidable… exactly where a market maker sell model would fail"
  - [0:27:03](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=1623) — MNQ: "I want to be watching this… it would need to get above that, then treat that as inversion fair value gap for me to be bullish"
- **Nuance:** iFVGs are broken if price trades above them with a body. Until then, assume bearish bias.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 25, 2026
head: Relative Equal Lows (RELs) / Relative Equal Highs (REHs)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / target
- **What ICT says:** A relative equal low is a prior low that price is likely to revisit or break through on a fresh downside move. A relative equal high is the analog for upside. Use them as targets after confirming direction via FVG/iFVG or intraday structures. They are NOT precise levels but "probable" objectives.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Scan the chart for prior swing lows (RELs) or highs (REHs) that price has not recently touched.
  2. If trading lower off an iFVG, anticipate price will reach at least one prior REL.
  3. If breaking above, anticipate prior REH.
- **How to use:** Use as secondary targets. Primary target: consequent encroachment or imbalance rejection. Secondary: the nearest REL/REH. If price blows past REL/REH, expect continuation to the next level.
- **Example in this video:** 
  - Silver (0:18:20–0:19:07): "we would trade down to consequent encroachment. And if we got below that, we would clear up the smooth levels here. And eventually went down into that little volume imbalance there." Price cleared consequent encroachment, then hit sell-side.
  - MNQ (0:27:03): "You take this below, then come back, and then not go in the lower half… then I would expect it to start going higher" once REHs are available. Relative equal highs act as targets.
  - Intraday ES (0:28:36–0:29:24): "took the sell side into the imbalance here, left the sell side there. Rallied up, pushed it higher, left this high intact." Relative equal highs are tracked and expected to be hit.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:18:20](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=1100) — gold/silver consequent encroachment and smooth levels (RELs)
  - [0:27:03](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=1623) — MNQ REHs as targets if iFVG breaks
  - [0:29:24](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=1764) — intraday ES: relative equal highs tracked
- **Nuance:** RELs/REHs are probabilistic, not certain. Price may overshoot or undershoot; use them as "likely" zones, not hard stops.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 25, 2026
head: Seasonal Tendencies
body:
- **Kind:** context / bias filter
- **What ICT says:** Certain times of year, certain pairs have tendencies (e.g., GBPUSD tends to strengthen in spring). Use seasonal bias as a *filter*: if fundamentals and seasonal align, the setup is stronger. If they conflict (e.g., bearish on GBPUSD during a seasonal bull period), the trade is harder and requires more confluence.
- **How to identify:** ICT references seasonal calendars; if he mentions a pair or commodity in the context of time of year, he's applying seasonal logic.
- **How to use:** 
  - If seasonal bias aligns with technical setup, higher conviction.
  - If seasonal bias conflicts with technical setup, either sit out or require much tighter risk/reward.
  - Example: GBPUSD is seasonally biased to go higher in spring; if ICT is bearish on GBPUSD here (early spring), he notes the conflict, which adds weight to the bearish case if iFVG is still intact.
- **Example in this video:** GBPUSD (0:15:12–0:15:59): "If this can go lower, what it's doing is is it's actually going lower during a time when seasonal tendencies would indicate that it's likely to go higher. So, in and of itself, that would be extremely bearish and very bullish for uh dollar index."
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:15:12](https://youtu.be/UQJW9obxt34?t=912) — seasonal tendency and GBPUSD conflict
- **Nuance:** Seasonal is a weak signal on its own; use as a filter, not a primary bias.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 25, 2026
head: Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL) & Buy-Side Imbalance / Sell-Side Inefficiency
body:
- **Kind:** definition / structure
- **What ICT says:** Sell-side liquidity rests below a market high (stops under the high). When price trades below that region without filling the gap, it creates a buy-side imbalance / sell-side inefficiency (BISI). This is the imbalance in the gap below the high. It acts as support or reversal point.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Price makes a swing high.
  2. Price gaps down and opens below that high without bodies in between.
  3. That gap below the high is BISI.
  4. The SSL is the concentration of stops just below the original high.
- **How to use:** 
  - If shorting and price drops through BISI, trail stops above it.
  - If long, use BISI as a support level; bounce above it and continue higher.
  - Use on daily charts to identify macro targets; apply on lower timeframes for entries.
- **Example in this video:** 
  - EURUSD, GBPUSD: multiple references to "buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency" (BISI).
  - DXY (0:04:59–0:05:47): "if we lose this imbalance and go lower, then you're probably going to see some pressure on dollar index."
  - Intraday ES (0:28:36–0:29:24): "took the sell side into the imbalance here, left the sell side there… If it's going to go below here, this should be used as fuel, kind of like energy to send it lower."

head: Market Maker Buy/Sell Model (MMBM/MMSM)
body:
- **Kind:** concept / mechanism
- **What ICT says:** Market makers operate a model where they long below a low (to collect liquidity and profits) or short above a high (same logic). If price "should" go lower but instead breaks up, it may be because the MM buy model is in effect (long positions being taken, shortstop hunting in reverse). Use this to confirm or negate setups. Example: "exactly where a market maker sell model would fail and go the other direction."
- **How to identify:** Observe price not delivering expected direction despite iFVG or other confirmation. If price should go lower but goes up, assume MM buy model.
- **How to use:** If you see MM model in effect (opposite of expected direction), either sit out or reverse your bias. Use it as a warning: "if I'm wrong here, this is where the MM model is likely at play."
- **Example in this video:** GBPUSD (0:13:39): "It's exactly where a market maker sell model would fail and go the other direction if I'm wrong."

head: Consequent Encroachment (Midpoint / Equilibrium)
body:
- **Kind:** definition (same as L26-114)
- **What ICT says:** Split any gap or wick in half (midpoint = consequent encroachment). If price fails to touch it, that is weakness in that direction. If it respects the midpoint and doesn't close above it when trying to rally into an iFVG, the iFVG is confirmed.
- **How to use:** Use as a filter: if price in an iFVG scenario fails to touch or exceed consequent encroachment of the wick, it confirms bearishness (if iFVG) or bullishness (if bullish FVG).

head: Tomfoolery / Market Manipulation (Geopolitical Context)
body:

- **What ICT says:** Central banks, government agencies, and market makers engage in "tomfoolery" (manipulation): false moves in pre-market (7 am ET) and after-hours to trap retail traders, move prices on non-news days, or prepare for geopolitical events. Example: sudden spike on crude oil before a geopolitical announcement, designed to move positioning. "They know where they want to take it, but they also know there's 2 million of you listening to me… if they do it between the sessions and you can't participate, they are able to do it, that's how they're going to beat you."
- **How to identify:** Sudden spikes or sharp moves during low-volume sessions (pre-market 7 am ET, after-hours, weekends) on news that hasn't been released yet. Overnight gaps on no-news days.
- **How to use:** Avoid trading pre-market and after-hours. Do not hold trades overnight into potential geopolitical events. Assume that moves between sessions are designed to trap you.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 21, 2026
head: Time Distortion
body:
- **Kind:** definition / context filter / core concept
- **What ICT says:** Time distortion occurs when price spends an extended period in a *range* (high to low) without clear directional intent. On a 1-minute chart, this looks chaotic and confusing ("feels like a root canal"); on a 15-minute or higher timeframe, it becomes clear that price is simply working toward a specific inefficiency or target. Time distortion is not price being "hard to trade"; it is *you being on the wrong timeframe*. When you see time distortion on your current timeframe, your protocol is: go UP to a higher timeframe, find what inefficiency or level price is working toward, then come back down to your trading timeframe with clarity.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. You are on a 1-minute chart (or 5-minute, etc.).
  2. Price is moving up and down inside a defined range (high to low), repeatedly testing both.
  3. You attempt 3+ trades and get stopped out or chopped around.
  4. No clear breakout; just oscillation.
  5. This is time distortion on that timeframe.
- **How to use:** 
  1. *Do not try to trade a distorted timeframe.* You will get stopped out repeatedly.
  2. Go up to the next higher timeframe (1m → 5m → 15m → 1h, etc.).
  3. Ask: "What inefficiency or level is price trying to reach on this higher timeframe?"
  4. Once you identify it (e.g., a 15-minute gap), come back to your 1-minute chart.
  5. Now trade *toward* that target, not *within* the distorted range.
  6. Example: price is choppy on 1m, but on 15m, it's clearly working toward a gap at a specific price. Trade 1m entries that advance toward that 15m target.
- **Example in this video:** 
  - Nasdaq 1-minute chart (0:52:40–0:53:27): price is oscillating in a tight range, "feels like a root canal," no clear direction. ICT marks it as "time distortion."
  - Then goes to 5-minute (0:54:13–0:55:00): still distorted, but less so.
  - Then goes to 15-minute (0:55:00–0:55:51): *suddenly clear*—price is working toward a specific inefficiency (a gap). The 1-minute distortion makes sense now.
  - The protocol: start at 1m, see distortion, jump to 5m (still distorted), jump to 15m (clear), then come back to 1m trades with a target.
  - ICT also notes: "Ranges that spend a lot of high resistance on the higher time frame, the way you can combat that is drop down to lower time frames." (The inverse: if 15m is distorted, go to 1h; if 1h shows a range, drop to 15m or lower to find trades within it.)
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:52:40](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3160) — "This is time distortion. This is what's going to beat you up."
  - [0:54:13](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3253) — marking the 1-minute range as time distortion (ugly yellow box)
  - [0:55:00](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3300) — jumping to 5m, then to 15m, where inefficiency becomes clear
  - [0:55:51](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3351) — "Now, I'm going to keep this portion of price distortion annotated… See that? Now, I'm going to keep this… This is what it's been doing."
  - [0:55:51–0:56:39](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3351–3399) — full protocol for fixing time distortion
- **Nuance:** Time distortion is not a market fault; it's a *timeframe mismatch*. The market is always working toward something; you're just on the wrong timeframe to see it. Higher timeframe shows the target; lower timeframes provide entry techniques.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 21, 2026
head: Continuous Contract vs. Delivery Month Contract (Index Futures)
body:
- **Kind:** technical / tool / critical distinction
- **What ICT says:** When analyzing index futures (ES, NQ, YM), use the *continuous contract*, not the delivery month contract (March, June, September, December). The continuous contract automatically rolls from one front month to the next, ensuring smooth price action and no artificial discontinuities from contract rollovers. Delivery month contracts show "spotty" price action at rollovers and miss information. ICT's targets, levels, and analysis are *always* based on the continuous contract; if you use a delivery month contract, you will not see the same levels and will miss opportunities.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Look at the chart title (upper left corner) or symbol in your charting software.
  2. Continuous contract: symbol like "NQ" with *no month code* (no "June," "March," etc., in the title).
  3. Delivery month: symbol like "NQM26" (M = June 2026), "NQZ25" (Z = December 2025), etc. The letter indicates delivery month.
  4. Continuous: smooth price action, no gaps at rollovers. Delivery month: "spotty" price action, visible gaps when rolling from one month to the next.
- **How to use:** 
  1. Always switch to continuous contract for top-down analysis, higher-timeframe targets, and daily/weekly structure.
  2. Trades are *executed* on the delivery month (the front month actively trading), but your *levels* and *targets* come from continuous.
  3. Example: you see a target of 22,779.75 on the continuous NQ chart (summer target). That level is valid because continuous always factors in the front month. If you were only looking at the June contract, you might see the same level but not understand where it came from or why it's significant.
  4. When checking intraday trades, verify your target on continuous, then execute on front month.
- **Example in this video:** 
  - 0:39:52–0:43:50: Detailed tutorial on switching from delivery month (June) to continuous contract in TradingView. Shows how June contract looks "spotty" and shows lows (e.g., March 9 low of 23,999) that continuous shows clearly without artifact.
  - 0:43:50–0:44:36: Continuous shows sell-side at 23,999, which is the target ICT got. Friday's intraday action (down to 23,970.75) confirmed this level was real and continuous-derived.
  - 0:48:39–0:49:27: Comparing June delivery contract (far below continuous lows) to continuous contract (accurate lower levels). Emphasizes that continuous contract is "much more powerful" for analysis.
  - 0:57:25–0:58:16: When executing intraday trades on 1-minute, you're on the delivery month (June), but your targets come from continuous. The gap at 23,999 (from continuous) was hit intraday on Friday.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:40:40](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=2440) — "notice there is no month reference there… everything gets smoothed out"
  - [0:41:29](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=2489) — continuous vs. delivery month visual comparison; delivery is "spotty"
  - [0:42:16](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=2536) — continuous shows the true low (March 9, 2026) seamlessly

- **Nuance:** This is a critical practical tool. Many retail traders use delivery month charts and wonder why their levels don't match ICT's; the reason is the contract choice. Always use continuous for analysis; trades may be on delivery month, but levels must come from continuous.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 21, 2026
head: Order Flow and the "Do Not Trespass" Rule (Body Placement)
body:
- **Kind:** core concept / execution rule
- **What ICT says:** When looking at an inefficiency (gap/SIBI/BISI) in the direction of your bias, price can *wick* into the opposite half (e.g., wick above midpoint while bearish), but it *cannot lay down a body* in that opposite half if the inefficiency is to remain valid. The body placement is the "do not trespass" rule: if you're bearish and price lays a body in the upper half of a sell-side imbalance, that's a violation. When bodies stay in the "correct half," that is real institutional order flow. Wicks can go anywhere; bodies tell the truth.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Spot an inefficiency (SIBI or BISI).
  2. Determine your bias (bearish = expect bodies in lower half; bullish = expect bodies in upper half).
  3. Watch each candle: is the body in the correct half, or has it crossed into the "do not trespass" zone?
  4. If the body never lays in the wrong half, the inefficiency is valid.
  5. If a body lays in the wrong half, that's a violation of the inefficiency and suggests a change in direction.
- **How to use:** 
  - Bearish: "I want to see price stay in the lower half of this gap. Wicks above = okay. Bodies above = violation."
  - Bullish: "I want to see price stay in the upper half of this gap. Wicks below = okay. Bodies below = violation."
  - If violated, consider exiting the trade or reversing the bias.
  - This is a *visual* rule requiring no complex calculation or footprint data; just look at where the close is.
- **Example in this video:** 
  - SIBI (sell-side imbalance, bearish bias): 0:57:25–0:58:16: "You want to see price stay in the lower half of this gap… if it does, as soon as it touches it, you are watching to see what the body does. Does the body close below it? If you do see that, that's real institutional order flow."
  - 0:59:53–1:01:29: Extended teaching on "do not trespass": "Anticipated trading to midpoint. It can wick above midpoint, but it cannot lay down a body in the upper half if you're looking for it to go lower… Do not trespass. You better get the hell off here before I shoot your ass. Well, what does price do? I'm out of here… Bodies in the lower half. Exactly what real institutional order flow looks like visually."
  - 1:01:29–1:02:15: Bullish inverse: "We want to see it trade down into an inefficiency, and then it can wick in the lower half, but it can't leave bodies down there… don't trespass in the lower half."
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:57:25](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3445) — do not trespass rule: bodies in lower half, wick above okay
  - [0:59:05](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3545) — "This is obvious… a sell side imbalance buy side inefficiency… body close below it? That's real institutional order flow… no one can say this isn't an inefficiency"
  - [0:59:53](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3593) — "it cannot lay down a body in the upper half… First of all, he didn't teach that…"
  - [1:00:42](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3642) — "I'm out of here… Bodies in the lower half. Exactly what real institutional order flow looks like visually. It's not complicated."
  - [1:01:29](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=3689) — bullish inverse; respect upper half, bodies in upper half
- **Nuance:** This rule applies to inefficiencies/gaps, not to all price action. The rule is specific: *in the direction of your bias, bodies must respect the correct half*. ICT emphasizes this is "very, very simple" and "not complex" and criticizes retail traders for overthinking it (e.g., trying to use footprint or tick-by-tick analysis when visual body placement suffices).

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 21, 2026
head: SMT Divergence (Market Breadth / Distribution)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / confirmation signal
- **What ICT says:** S&P (500-stock index) Divergence with Nasdaq (or other mega-cap-heavy indices) indicates market breadth weakness. When Nasdaq makes higher highs but S&P makes lower highs (or fails to make new highs), it shows that the overall market is not broadly supporting the move; only a few stocks (mega-cap tech) are driving it. This is heavy distribution: accumulation of shorts, distribution of longs. When market breadth fails like this, the move higher is not sustainable; lower prices are likely.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Plot Nasdaq (NQ) and S&P (ES) on the same timeframe (daily or weekly).
  2. Compare the highs: do they move together or diverge?
  3. If NQ makes a higher high but ES makes a lower high (or fails to reach the same relative level), that's divergence.
  4. This is bearish and indicates heavy distribution.
- **How to use:** 
  - Use as a *confirmation* of bearish bias on the indices.
  - If you have a bearish technical setup (e.g., price below iFVG) AND you see SMT divergence, the bias is confirmed: lower prices likely.
  - If SMT divergence appears but technicals are bullish, be cautious; the breadth weakness may presage a reversal.
- **Example in this video:** 
  - 0:37:28–0:38:16: ICT compares NQ and ES highs side-by-side. NQ high to lower high (lower high on second peak). ES high to higher high (comparably). Result: divergence. "That divergence is indicative of heavy distribution and no new buying… accumulation distribution… that's why I've been sticking to I'm bearish on all the indices."
  - Also: Warren Buffett moving to cash is cited as confirmation of distribution: "nobody with that kind of money… goes to cash… doesn't happen by accident."
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:37:28](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=2248) — visual divergence between NQ and ES
  - [0:38:16](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=2296) — "divergence is indicative of heavy distribution and no new buying"
  - [0:35:47–0:35:01](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=2147–2101) — Warren Buffett in cash = distribution signal
- **Nuance:** SMT divergence is a *confirmation*, not a primary signal. Use with PD arrays and structure for highest conviction.

head: Market Structure Shift / Change in State of Delivery (in the Context of Consolidation)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / context
- **What ICT says:** When price is consolidating (range, time distortion), look at the *higher timeframe* (weekly, monthly) to see if there's been a shift in market structure. ICT refers to "lower low, a lower low, a lower low, and then we have a shift in market structure" on the DXY weekly chart (0:04:51). This indicates that the consolidation on the daily is *respecting* a higher-timeframe shift; the daily lethargic action is price waiting for the fulfillment of a higher-timeframe event or target. Once that higher-timeframe target is hit, the consolidation will break.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Daily chart shows consolidation (time distortion).
  2. Go to weekly chart.
  3. Look for a break in the pattern of lower lows, higher highs, etc.
  4. A "shift in market structure" = a break from the recent pattern (e.g., after 3 lower lows, a higher low).
  5. This indicates the consolidation is likely temporary; price will resolve once the weekly pattern is clear.
- **How to use:** 
  - When you see daily consolidation + time distortion, check the weekly for structure shift.
  - If there's no structure shift on weekly, consolidation will likely continue.
  - If there is a shift on weekly, anticipate the daily to resolve in the direction of that shift soon.
- **Example in this video:** DXY weekly (0:04:03–0:04:51): price is in consolidation, looks like time distortion on daily. But on weekly, there's "a shift in market structure" (after 3 lower lows, a change). This tells ICT the consolidation is temporary; price is waiting to resume the trend once the weekly shift is fulfilled.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:04:03](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=243) — weekly chart consolidation (large, lethargic)
  - [0:04:51](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=291) — shift in market structure; "lower low, lower low, lower low, and then a shift"
- **Nuance:** This is a macro observation: when distorted on one timeframe, look higher for the structure the market is waiting to fulfill.

head: Reclaimed Bullish / Bearish Fair Value Gap
body:
- **Kind:** definition / structure state
- **What ICT says:** A FVG or iFVG is "reclaimed" when price trades above it (bullish reclaim), or below it (bearish reclaim), and then pulls back into it but *does not close bodies back in the gap's original inefficient half*. For example, a sell-side imbalance (bearish iFVG) becomes a "reclaimed bearish FVG" if price re-enters from below and respects it as support (bodies not in the upper half). This converts it from an inversion to a standard FVG acting as support/resistance.
- **How to identify:** 
  1. Start with an iFVG or inversion scenario.
  2. Price trades in the opposite direction and re-enters the gap.
  3. Check: do bodies stay in the "new correct half"?
  4. If yes, it's reclaimed and now acts as support (bullish) or resistance (bearish).
- **How to use:** Once reclaimed, the gap is no longer a reversal tool; it's a continuation support/resistance. Trade *with* the reclaim bias, not against it.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD (0:11:12–0:11:59): "if it's going to trade up there and touch that again, to me, this might trade above it, then use this as footing to go higher. And then the seasonal tendency for euro dollar… might materialize." If EURUSD trades above the iFVG and reclaims it as bullish, higher prices follow.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:05:39](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=339) — DXY monthly: "would need to get above and enter into to area here and then leave this alone to be a reclaimed bullish fair value gap"
  - [0:18:18](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=1098) — Nasdaq: "I want to see it become a reclaimed bearish fair value gap"
- **Nuance:** Reclaimed is a *state change*; once reclaimed, the bias flips from reversal to continuation.

head: Suspension Block (Structural Support/Resistance)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / PD array
- **What ICT says:** A suspension block is a consolidation range (high/low) that price tests and then breaks out from. If the block is bullish (price breaks above), it acts as support on pullback; price should respect the midpoint of the block and not re-enter below it. If bearish (price breaks below), the block acts as resistance above; price should not re-enter above it. (Also called "breaker block" in some contexts.)
- **How to use:** Use as a structural level on daily/weekly. If price breaks below a bullish suspension block on the daily, that's weakness; if it breaks above a bearish block, that's strength.
- **Example in this video:** DXY daily (0:03:15–0:07:13): "This is a suspension block. And the reason why we're having all of this difficulty here after trading to the objective… if we lose this, then I'm I'm not so optimistic for dollar."

- **Nuance:** Suspension block is a structural level; treat as a critical support/resistance, not a zone.

head: Market Maker Models in Consolidation (Geopolitical Context)
body:
- **Kind:** concept / context
- **What ICT says:** When consolidation occurs during geopolitical crisis (war, political uncertainty), market makers are not incentivized to take large positions; they're holding steady. The consolidation reflects fear and uncertainty, not weakness in a single direction. Big money is migrating into event-driven markets (gold, silver, crude) instead of equity risk. This is why the indices are so lethargic: not a directional breakdown, but a flight to safety / reduced risk-on appetite.
- **How to use:** During geopolitical crisis, expect longer consolidations, fewer explosive moves, and wider bid-ask spreads. Use this as a filter: in such environments, reduce leverage and sit out lower-conviction setups.
- **Example in this video:** 0:08:47–0:09:35: "World War III going on… That is a huge catalyst for what's making these markets be reluctant to have sustained price runs… big money, deep pockets, are moving and migrating into those event-driven markets like silver, gold… and out of risk-bearing like stocks. That's why it's been melting down."

  - [0:09:35](https://youtu.be/YrBrgUON9fE?t=575) — event-driven markets seeing flows; equities melting down

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 19, 2026
head: Consequent Encroachment
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / definition
- **What ICT says:** The midpoint between two price levels (e.g., a low and a lower low, or a high and a higher high). Used to grade discount wicks and measure premium/discount relative to range resets. When price trades below consequent encroachment on the daily dollar index, he grades the wick to see if bodies are below it—body placement below consequent encroachment indicates bearish strength.
- **How to identify:** Draw a fib from high to low (or old low to new low); the midpoint is consequent encroachment.
- **How to use:** As a reference for body placement; if bodies close below consequent encroachment, it signals continuation lower (bearish). If bodies stay above it, it may reject.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: 10:13 suspension block at consequent encroachment of Wednesday RTH opening range gap; bodies held below halfway point, validating sell signal targeting 24,809.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:49](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=529), [0:14:28](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=868), [1:01:28](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=3688)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Distinct from support/resistance; it is a mathematical midpoint that resets the range when broken. Price often revisits it as equilibrium before continuation.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 19, 2026
head: Fair Value Gap (FVG) | Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model
- **What ICT says:** An FVG is the gap between a candlestick's close and the next candlestick's open. An inversion FVG (iFVG) is when price trades below a buy-side imbalance (sell-side inefficiency), then re-enters that level from below. For iFVG to be valid: (1) price must close below the midpoint of the original imbalance on the low side, (2) price must be allowed to trade back into the level, (3) when it does, bodies must close below the midpoint to confirm, (4) the first touch of that level on the next break lower is an entry.
- **How to identify:** Look for a buy-side imbalance (open = close of previous candle, creating no volume imbalance); then price fails to get above consequent encroachment; it closes below consequent encroachment. Later, price retraces back up into the imbalance level, bodies close below midpoint—now it's an iFVG.
- **How to use:** Once confirmed, the first re-touch of the imbalance on a break lower is a demo/paper entry. It is "superior to supply and demand" because there are specific rule-based conditions; not just a rectangle drawn on a chart.
- **Example in this video:** GBP/USD daily: buy-side imbalance (sell-side inefficiency) from the original consolidation; waiting for lower prices if it breaks down and validates as iFVG with proper body placement below midpoint.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:15](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=915), [0:23:17](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=1397), [0:39:50](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=2390)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Price can wick above the imbalance but if the body doesn't close above consequent encroachment, it doesn't invalidate the bearish structure. iFVG is superior to simpler "support/resistance" because the rule set is precise and repeatable.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 19, 2026
head: Event Horizon (Midpoint Targeting Strategy)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model
- **What ICT says:** When you have two sell-side liquidity pools (two lows), you can draw a fib between them; the midpoint is event horizon. Use it as a partial exit point when you're bearish and expecting continuation lower. Take 25% off at event horizon on a long downtrend; let the balance run to the lower target. You can also use it as an adding-in point if you're adding to a short.
- **How to identify:** Identify two lows (or one old low and one new lower low); draw fib or measure midpoint.
- **How to use:** As a partial exit (especially if you're nearing the end of a move), or as a point to add to the short if you believe lower prices will follow. On a long-established downtrend, take 25% minimum at event horizon to bank some profit.
- **Example in this video:** Bitcoin daily (hypothetically short): two sell-side pools; event horizon is midpoint. If short Bitcoin, take 25% off at event horizon, then let the runner go to the lower target around 49,577 or lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:14](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=1634), [0:34:22](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=2062), [0:42:30](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=2550)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Event horizon changes in meaning once the range resets; if you break the lower low and treat that as a new range, the old event horizon no longer applies—you measure from the new lows.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 19, 2026
head: Range Reset & Premium/Discount
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** When price takes out an old low (part of a larger run lower), the range resets. What was previously "discount" becomes "premium" if price retraces back to the midpoint of the new range. This is a critical lesson—don't be fearful of taking setups in perceived "deep discount" if the range has reset and you're actually at equilibrium or premium relative to the new lows. Many traders misunderstand discount/premium because they look at a limited snapshot of price action instead of recognizing when a range has been invalidated.
- **How to identify:** When price breaks below a key low that was part of a prior range, that low no longer defines the bottom of the new range. The new low becomes the reference point.
- **How to use:** When you're bearish and shorting, take partials at equilibrium (consequent encroachment of new range) even if it looks like you're "buying at a premium"—you're actually at equilibrium of the new, lower range.
- **Example in this video:** Bitcoin: once price broke the prior established lows and moved lower for months, the range reset. What appeared to be a "premium" retracement was actually equilibrium of the new range, validating further shorts.
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:09](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=2109), [0:37:30](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=2250), [0:38:17](https://youtu.be/w2zTfhjScDg?t=2297)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a common source of confusion; ICT addresses traders who wrongly avoid "deep discount" setups. The discount/premium labels reset when the structural low is broken.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 19, 2026
head: Suspension Block
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example
- **What ICT says:** A candlestick that shows clear bearish close (bodies in lower half, wick above) at a key level like consequent encroachment. It acts as a suspension of bullish momentum and signals continuation lower. On NQ 1m, the 10:13 candlestick was a suspension block—bearish close, bodies below halfway, validating the short setup into the next target.
- **How to identify:** Look for a candlestick with: strong wick up (showing rejections of buyers), body closed in lower half (especially below consequent encroachment), at a key resistance or consequent encroachment level.
- **How to use:** As confirmation to enter short (or add to short) with conviction.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, 10:13 ET: suspension block at the RTH gap consequent encroachment; bodies held in lower half; validated the short targeting 24,809.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 19, 2026
head: Rejection Block
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example
- **What ICT says:** A candlestick showing strong rejection of price trying to move in the wrong direction (e.g., rejecting upside near a sell-side liquidity level on a bearish day). Bodies hold below a key level, wick extends above, closing below. Multiple rejection blocks in sequence reinforce bearish bias.
- **How to identify:** Strong wick above a key level, body closes back below that level; bodies stay compressed/small.
- **How to use:** As confirmation of directional bias; multiple rejection blocks reinforce conviction.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: rejection block patterns seen in the morning session near Wednesday RTH gap levels.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 19, 2026
head: Order Flow & Body Placement
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** You don't need level-2 data or volume profile to read order flow. You can see it visually in the candlestick bodies. When bodies stay below consequent encroachment, that is the footprint of smart money. When bodies are above, it shows different intent. This visual reading is as valid as any proprietary tool—don't overcomplicate it. "These are footprints. You want to talk about footprints and level two and you want to go inside the candlestick... none of that stuff is valuable because it's already happened."
- **How to identify:** Look at where candle bodies close relative to consequent encroachment or a key level.
- **How to use:** Validate or invalidate your bias based on body placement. Bearish validation = bodies below consequent encroachment.
- **Example in this video:** EUR/USD: bodies staying below the consequent encroachment wick indicated continuation lower; no need for volume profile or level-2 data.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 17, 2026
head: Contract Rollover (Rollover Week)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / process
- **What ICT says:** During rollover from one contract month to another (e.g., March to June), there is an artificial influx of buying and selling as traders exit the old front month and enter the new one. This participation is "net sum zero" (no real buying or selling pressure), but algorithms and manual intervention can paint a fake narrative of price direction. Volume imbalances and PD arrays bleed over from old contract to new. During rollover, keep position sizes light, expect to be wrong, and don't try to aggressively trade.
- **How to identify:** When a contract month is approaching expiration (e.g., March delivery ending), rollover occurs; trading activity on the new front month (June) begins.
- **How to use:** During rollover weeks, let volume be very light; synchronize with the new contract rather than trying to build equity. Watch PD arrays and price action for context, but don't assume normal price momentum. After rollover week ends, the contract becomes "pristine" and normal trading resumes.
- **Example in this video:** NQ March-to-June rollover on March 17, 2026; price ran straight up from market open, leaving relative equal lows. ICT collected levels and tape-read but did not actively trade.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:37](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=97), [0:12:05](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=725), [0:22:22](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=1342), [0:23:09](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=1389)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Rollover creates artifacts (false price signals); similar dynamics occur after FOMC or nonfarm payroll. During these events, prioritize staying synchronized over profit-taking.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 17, 2026
head: High Probability vs. Low Probability Setup
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition
- **What ICT says:** A high-probability setup is when price action is "so obvious, absolutely obvious" that it will go one direction—the order flow is clean, bodies validate bias, PD arrays are being respected. You can call "Here is the level I'm looking for. This is what I'm doing." A low-probability scenario is when you can determine both sides of the marketplace; if both directions are equally possible, it's low probability. During low probability, sit still and maintain interest in levels without taking action.
- **How to identify:** Check if the price action respects the PD arrays, if bodies are validating the bias (bullish or bearish), if there is a clean signature. If you can make a case for both bullish and bearish, it's low probability.
- **How to use:** In low probability, don't trade. Wait for a higher-conviction setup or clear feedback. Sit still. This is a core discipline: "Knowing when not to do something is important."
- **Example in this video:** March 17, 2026 pre-10:00 AM: ICT was in low probability—price could run to the gap high or drop into first-presented FVG. Both were possible; therefore, no trade. Sat still until the economic news (pending home sales at 10:00 ET) provided clarity.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 17, 2026
head: First Presented Fair Value Gap (FPFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / definition
- **What ICT says:** The first FVG that forms after the opening of a session (e.g., at 9:32 on March 17). It's the gap between two candlesticks in the first moments of the open. Use it as a target if price is above it (expect it to drop into it) or as a reference for inversion mechanics if price trades above it. Discount sensitivity exists in the upper half; bodies should stay out of the upper half to maintain bearish bias.
- **How to identify:** Look at the opening candle and the first few candles; identify the gap (close-to-open separation).
- **How to use:** If price is above FPFVG and you're bearish, target into it. If price enters the upper half, watch body placement; if bodies stay below consequent encroachment of that FVG, continuation lower is likely.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m on March 17: opened at 9:30, first presented FVG was identified at 9:32. Price traded above it initially, then dipped into the upper half. When bodies failed to go into the upper half and stayed compressed, it signaled intention to break back down into FPFVG. "About 25 handles as a nice little bread and butter setup from here down into first presented fair value gap."
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:01](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=1561), [0:30:24](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=1824), [0:40:11](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=2411)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** On a session open, the FPFVG is often the first target; treat it as a high-probability delivery point if the bias is validated.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 17, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (Revisited)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** When price trades above a sell-side FVG (upper half), consider it as a potential inversion FVG if price later wants to trade back down. It requires specific mechanics: bodies must NOT close in the upper half (discount sensitivity zone); if it does go up there, it must demonstrate reluctance and lack of conviction. Then, on a break lower, the first touch is an entry.
- **How to identify:** Price goes into upper half of FVG with weak body closes; next drop lower is iFVG.
- **Example in this video:** If NQ trades above and bumps the high of FPFVG, it can still be an iFVG setup for lower prices if bodies refuse to close above consequent encroachment.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:59](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=1919), [0:40:58](https://youtu.be/AxLXI00L8zM?t=2458)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The distinction between "just touching upper half" and "invalidating the bias" depends on body placement and momentum—if bodies are weak, it can still be bearish.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 17, 2026
head: Relative Equal Lows / Highs
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Two price lows (or highs) that are very close to each other (within a "handle" or two), indicating a high-probability point for a raid (move in the opposite direction) or at least a significant level. On March 17, the market opened at 9:30, ran higher, then left a low at 24,962.00 and another low at 24,964.25—"relatively equal lows." This made the level a "high probability candidate for a raid or at least in the very minimum consider this a relative equal low because the low to the right of this one is slightly higher."
- **How to identify:** Compare two recent lows; if they're within a few ticks of each other, they're relatively equal.
- **How to use:** As a point of interest for a reversal or as a level to watch for stops.
- **Example in this video:** NQ March 17: relative equal lows at 24,962 and 24,964.25.

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 17, 2026
head: Tape Reading (Visual Order Flow)
body:
- **Kind:** process / tool
- **What ICT says:** Watch candlestick bodies and wicks in real-time; observe willingness (or reluctance) of price to move in a direction. If bodies are small and compressed near consequent encroachment, it shows reluctance. If there's a large wick above a small body, it shows rejection. Use notes/levels to track price and identify when it's respecting or rejecting a target.
- **How to identify:** Observe real-time candles; bodies tell the story—size, placement, color (close relative to open).
- **How to use:** Combine tape reading with pre-identified levels; watch if price is respecting them or painting a fake move. Can be done with a notepad and quote screen (without chart).

title: ICT 2026 Market Commentary \ March 17, 2026
head: Volume Imbalance vs. Inefficiency (Toggle Settings)

They can produce different results based on how they calculate. ICT uses the volume imbalance setting (not the inefficiency setting) for his analysis. Watch which setting reveals the imbalance you want to focus on.

title: ICT 2026 EOD Market Review \ March 13, 2026
head: Immediate Rebalance
body:
- **Kind:** definition / model (ICT's proprietary)
- **What ICT says:** When a discount wick forms (a gap between two candlesticks), the algorithm rushes to deliver price back to the previous day's high or a key level immediately, rather than waiting for a full fair-value-gap correction. The mechanics: price opens, trades down to the consequent encroachment of a discount wick, bounces hard, and delivers directly to the target without intermediate steps. "It's the strongest algorithmic price delivery PD array I've discovered and coined... it's mine and you can't find anywhere else." The trade executes same-day or the next day; if day-two fails, it becomes a "complex reversal" signaling lower prices. ICT taught this extensively in his 2016-2017 paid mentorship but now shares it publicly.
- **How to identify:** Look for a wick that is lower than the prior one; price opens, trades down to the consequent encroachment (midpoint) of that wick, bounces sharply, and runs directly to the previous high or target.
- **How to use:** When you see immediate rebalance form, anticipate a directional run that day or the next. If day-two fails (trades below immediate rebalance), expect a complex reversal and lower prices.
- **Example in this video:** Dollar index March 12-13, 2026: wick formed, price opened, traded down to consequent encroachment, bounced, and delivered right to 104.54—"to the tick." This triggered bearish forex pairs (EUR, GBP) to drop sharply as the dollar firmed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:13](https://youtu.be/l7hRTBvK7to?t=133), [0:04:41](https://youtu.be/l7hRTBvK7to?t=281), [0:07:07](https://youtu.be/l7hRTBvK7to?t=427), [0:11:55](https://youtu.be/l7hRTBvK7to?t=715)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** ICT credits 34 years of experience for discovering this. Emphasizes it never stops working. "Day-two failure" is a reversal signal, not a contradiction of the model.

title: ICT 2026 EOD Market Review \ March 13, 2026
head: Complex Reversal (Day-Two Failure of Immediate Rebalance)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** If immediate rebalance forms but price fails to run up on day-two (instead trades below the immediate rebalance level), it signals a "complex reversal." The market will not protect the upside; instead, it will turn lower. This is a high-conviction sell signal.
- **How to identify:** Day-one: immediate rebalance forms and runs. Day-two: price opens and trades below the immediate rebalance level rather than protecting it.
- **How to use:** As a strong bearish signal; reverse to short bias.
- **Example in this video:** Dollar index: if the bounce doesn't hold on day-two, expect lower prices.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:30](https://youtu.be/l7hRTBvK7to?t=810)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "If day two fails, and it trades below immediate rebalance, that's a complex reversal. It will not run and protect the upside. It'll go the other direction."

title: ICT 2026 EOD Market Review \ March 13, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (Applied to Price Entry)
body:

Example: USD/JPY and EUR/USD formed iFVGs; bodies stayed below consequent encroachment, signaling continuation lower. In the micro-Nasdaq intraday trade, the iFVG served as a target for shorts.
