title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: High Resistance vs Low Resistance Liquidity Run Conditions  (aliases: HRLR / LRLR, "high resistance liquidity run conditions")
body:
- **Kind:** definition (re-explained, with visuals) / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - High resistance means the market is *resisting your ability to find efficient, low-risk trades*; it does not mean support/resistance. On the chart (15-minute NQ example, shaded gray) it is a block where every candle's range overlaps the previous candle's range, "a big block of nonsense". It can look like a bull flag; trying to trade it on a 1-minute chart will "cook" you. Treat it like a rattlesnake; learn to recognise it and simply do not touch it.
  - Low resistance is the opposite: price shows inefficiencies (gaps, wicks) and then does something with them. Pattern: small consolidation, inefficiency forms, price trades back down into it, then makes a higher high (or lower low if bearish). It is "porous" price action with "patchwork": areas where a candle's range needs another touch from price (a partial touch counts, e.g. a wick poking a bit above the prior candle's high inside an order block / IOFED).
  - In low resistance with a bearish bias: up-close candles are repelled lower and down-close candles get "eaten into and consumed". You can read this from price alone, no footprint/level 2/3 needed.
  - Larry Williams cycle (credited): markets alternate large ranges to small ranges; small ranges are the precursor to large ranges. In a bearish low-resistance setting, a small retracement inside a SIBI followed by a small candle means large ranges are coming, with short-term lows as targets.
  - Signature to look for when bearish: stretched-out down-close candles ("black limousines" on his color scheme), expanding range size, contracting counter-direction, and unfilled gaps left in the back part of the run (breakaway/continuation/measuring gaps), meaning the market is weak (captions garbled).
- **How to identify:** Overlapping candle ranges with no clean inefficiency to trade from = high resistance. Visible FVGs/volume imbalances that price returns to and then expands from = low resistance.
- **How to use:**
  - In high resistance do not trade the "scale in, add if it pokes outside the bottom of the gap" approach; the odds fall because volatility and chop are high. In low resistance he does that "90% of the time" (scaling in, adding, adding).
  - Use the 15-minute chart as the bellwether to recognise the condition, then go to the 1-minute/sub-1-minute only if conditions are low resistance.
- **Seasonal rhythm he gives (opinion, from experience):** early-year months are the accumulation phase / high resistance; he deliberately measures risk by not participating the first month or two, then dabbles around the first/second Tuesday of February to gauge the tone (do orders come easily? do I feel in sync? are targets met easily?). Participation normally picks up in the second week of February; March should look clearly different. Summer: mostly high resistance with maybe one or two low-resistance days; fall (from the last two weeks of August or early September through the first/second week of December): low resistance; holiday period back to about 50/50.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15-minute, Fri Feb 27, 2026: gray-shaded overlapping candles (HRLR) versus a later leg with gaps, a wick, an IOFED/order block, a change in state of delivery and small ranges between gaps (LRLR).
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:10:40](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=640) — gray block = HRLR; don't trade it
  - [0:11:28](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=688) — definition "resisting your ability to find efficient low-risk trades"
  - [0:12:16](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=736) — "resistance" does not imply support/resistance
  - [0:13:53](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=833) — LRLR explained, patchwork
  - [0:15:29](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=929) — Larry Williams large/small range cycle
  - [0:25:48](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=1548) — seasonal rhythm through the year
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the video where he answers repeated comment requests for a visual explanation of the term. The seasonal calendar is his rule of thumb, not a statistic.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: Volume Imbalance neutralisation rule (daily chart)  (aliases: volume imbalance, VI, "pink/red box")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A volume imbalance is the gap between two candle *bodies*: one candle's close and the next candle's open, with wicks overlapping it. Annotate them; price trades back and forth through them.
  - He personally stops using a daily volume imbalance once a later daily candle's *body* lays over the entire range (the body must bridge both prices: the first candle's close and the second candle's open). Up or down close does not matter.
  - After that he will not key off it for a new entry or a terminus/target; he may still use it for stop management. It can still be used by price and its gradient levels still matter on a daily chart; it is just no longer given top importance.
  - Toggling the settlement/session setting on the daily chart changes where volume imbalances exist; he picks the setting that shows close-proximity volume imbalances because the market uses them.
- **How to identify:** closing price of candle A vs opening price of candle B (the gap between those prices; wicks may overlap).
- **How to use:** Mark them; use the low (or high) of the daily VI as a draw on liquidity/target (see lunch macro example). Stop using for new entries once a body fully covers it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily, pink/red volume imbalance above price. The Wednesday run took a short-term high and "gave up the ghost"; Friday's buy-side run went to the low of this VI and reversed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:05](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=1025) — what the daily VI is; [0:17:53](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=1073) — neutralised when a body covers the whole range; [1:02:22](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3742) — settlement toggle changes where VIs exist
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Me personally" rule, stated as his practice. Fits his 2026 emphasis on including volume imbalances in gap boundaries.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: Reclaimed FVG vs Inversion FVG  (aliases: reclaimed fair value gap, iFVG, reclaimed BISI)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / distinction
- **What ICT says:**
  - An inversion FVG forms when price trades through a gap of the opposite character (a down-close-candle gap, SIBI, that price goes above, or an up-close-candle gap that price goes below). A *reclaimed* gap is a bullish BISI that price traded through to the downside (or the CE) and then rides back above: it is not inverted; it changes its character but stays bullish (if the same gap had formed on a down-close candle it would be an inversion).
  - Up-close-candle gaps that price trades down through need time and patience for price to get back above.
  - Once above, bodies should respect the upper half. A wick can poke one or two ticks below; wait to see whether the body gets back in the upper half while the candle forms.
  - Setup logic before 9:00 Fri: an "orange inversion FVG" formed overnight; if price got above it, it could act as a run (discount array) toward the high liquidity above.
- **How to use:** In low resistance conditions he buys/scales/adds into that reclaimed gap; in high resistance conditions he doesn't (see HRLR). He says the approach works in either condition if combined with the narrative and time, but odds are poor in HRLR.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Fri Feb 27, before 9:00 ET: gap at the lows expected to turn into a run up to the buy-side high if price traded above it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:45:40](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2740); [0:46:27](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2787) — reclaimed vs inversion; [0:47:13](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2833) — upper-half bodies, scaling in 90% of the time in LRLR; [0:48:00](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2880) — don't do it in HRLR
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** In L26-113 he uses "reclaimed bearish FVG" for the bearish mirror. The caption sometimes says "first resistance fair value gap" where "first presented FVG" is probably meant (caption unclear).

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: First Presented FVG in the opening range (and why it was not a long)  (aliases: first presented fair value gap, first FVG after open)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement / worked example
- **What ICT says:**
  - The first presented FVG after the open formed with the 9:32 candle close (9:30 and 9:31 had no gap). He says that as soon as that candle closed you have a verifiable range on the chart (counting wording in the caption is ambiguous).
  - Many traders read it as a shift in market structure and go long. Wrong in this context: relative equal lows (sell-side liquidity, "too clean, too perfect") sat below, the long-term bias was bearish, it was Friday of a consolidation week (TGIF), and price was still inside the first 30 minutes.
  - The opening range is 30 minutes, not 15 ("Mickey Mouse 15 minutes"). He says institutions factor in the 30 minutes; the first 60 minutes gives even more clarity and he promises to cover it in March (see L26-113 first hour's dealing range).
  - Hypothetical: if price had first taken the lower low and *then* created the FVG with a market structure shift, retracements into the first presented FVG would be viable longs. But with equal lows untouched inside the first 30 minutes you cannot take that long.
  - If instead price had made a low, created the first presented FVG, and run through the buy side, he would wait for the pullback into that gap and treat it as inversion (shorting on the way back through), scale in shorts, take the first partial, and leave runners.
  - You must wait until everything aligns with the narrative: the first 30 minutes "can go all over the place".
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1-minute, Fri Feb 27, 2026: lower lows into the open leaving relative equal lows; first presented FVG at 9:32 (up-close), price dove down, took sell-side and knocked out longs, then ran up to the high near the CE of the RTH opening range gap at about 10:00.
- **Timestamps:** [0:36:05](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2165); [0:53:32](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3212); [0:54:19](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3259); [0:55:06](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3306) — opening range is 30 min; [0:55:55](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3355) — what he would have done instead
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines the "first presented FVG" teaching: context (liquidity, time of day, narrative, opening range) must be satisfied; the gap alone is not a trigger.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: RTH Opening Range Gap (RTH ORG) preparation and 70% midpoint rule  (aliases: opening range gap, RTH settlement, discount/premium gap)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / procedure
- **What ICT says:**
  - Reference price: the previous day's RTH settlement, the 4:14 PM ET close (he also notes you can use the 5:00 PM ET settlement; taught last year). Toggle to the RTH chart session; the gap only appears once the first RTH print at 9:30 occurs.
  - Pre-market routine: note the 4:14 PM settlement (after the close or first thing in the morning); about 30 minutes before the open (around 9:00) compare where price is. If price is well below, label the settlement price RTH ORG high in advance (it is highly unlikely to trade above it before 9:30); you are in for a discount opening range gap (open below the settlement). Above it is a premium gap. He writes "RTH ORG settlement" on his notepad.
  - Once the 9:30 open prints, drag the fib between the open and the settlement price: 50% is the CE.
  - Statistical idea: there is a 70% likelihood price trades to the midpoint of the gap between 9:30 and 10:00. There will be days it never goes there (opens and just drops/goes up). He frames it as a probability inside a narrative, not a guarantee, comparable to his 70% "Tuesday London session makes the weekly high (if bearish) or low (if bullish), else Wednesday" rule.
  - Full gap closure is always possible, but the easier objective is usually the closer liquidity.
  - He calls "too clean" a high that sat one tick above the CE of the gap (nothing else to compare it to on the chart), visible by eye on the price axis without drawing the line.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Fri Feb 27: at about 8:40 price far below Thursday's 4:14 PM settlement, labelled ORG high in advance; the 9:30 open was at a big discount; a high that lined up with the CE (one tick above the CE) printed at about 10:00 (he says he was 2 minutes off in timing), then price entered a messy consolidation.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:57:30](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3450) — Thursday 4:14 PM settlement, charts in NY time
  - [1:00:45](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3645) — how he read it live
  - [1:01:33](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3693) — label as ORG high in advance; 5 PM settlement alternative
  - [1:03:09](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=3789) — 70% between 9:30 and 10:00
  - [1:28:37](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=5317) — notepad routine, premium vs discount gap
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same 70% statement appears in L26-113 (March 28) for the 9:31–10:00 window.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: Gradient Levels of the RTH Opening Range Gap ("time and price multiplication table")  (aliases: gradient levels, eighths and quarters of the opening gap)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Grade the opening range gap (9:30 open to the 4:14 PM settlement) with the fib at the eights (octants) and quarters. Every gradient level is a potential PD array: "that's your order block, breaker, IOFED, propulsion block, Reaper, FVG, first resistance FVG." The hard part (which OB, which FVG, which liquidity pool) goes away because you have built a "multiplication table, the schematic based on time and price".
  - Can also be done with a new week opening gap or new day opening gap.
  - He says he hid this for a long time to avoid others repackaging it; he stresses it is still "elementary" in his toolkit.
  - The level the first presented gap sits on gives validation: on Friday a single-candle BISI lay on the 0.375 level, which validated it as a legitimate entry toward the buy-side liquidity / daily volume imbalance.
  - He calls this "anticipating" (knowing where a gap will form) rather than predicting or reacting.
- **How to identify / use:** Draw fib on the RTH ORG; mark 0.125 increments and quarters; look for FVGs/BISIs/SIBIs that sit on those levels; trade those toward the time-and-price objective (see lunch macro).
- **Example in this video:** NQ Fri Feb 27, 11:30 entering lunch: single-candle BISI on 0.375 gradient level; pyramided on cheaper prices; targeted the buy side above and the low of the daily volume imbalance; position closed after the run to that VI low; figures quoted are unclear in the caption (he mentions "just shy of 9 grand").
- **Timestamps:** [1:07:06](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4026) — gradient levels first mentioned; [1:31:58](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=5518) — graded gap into eighths and quarters; [1:32:45](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=5565) — "that's your order block, that's your breaker..."; [1:40:37](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=6037) — BISI on 0.375
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same family as the octant/quadrant levels he applies to the first hour's range in L26-113.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: Lunch Macro (11:30–1:30) and the "multiplication table"  (aliases: lunch macro, time first then price, 10:00 low objective)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model component
- **What ICT says:**
  - Lunch macro window is 11:30 to 1:30 PM ET (2 hours). 11:30–noon is the start; 1:30–2:00 is the PM session opening range, which sets the stage for 2:00–close; the lunch macro must end at 1:30. (Elsewhere in the transcript a "10:30 to 1:30" macro box is drawn: caption unclear; in L26-113 he allows lunch effects to start as early as 10:30.)
  - If the morning ran up into noon, the lunch macro runs back to the low that formed at 10:00 or the first low after 10:00 (the mirror for a morning decline: the high after 10:00).
  - Think of it as a multiplication table: horizontal axis = time, vertical = price; the algorithm goes back across time to a specific price; "two points of reference where price and time agree". You must start with time.
  - It does not care about your stop size or whether you are in a trade; it takes the liquidity below that low and neighbouring lows.
  - Trending day variant: do not use the very first low after 10:00. Start at 11:30 (first 30 minutes of lunch = "opening range for lunch hours", which starts the look-back) and look back for the most prominent low toward 10:00. The lunch macro is then a turtle soup from the current price down to that low, and he would be done / wait for the PM session.
  - Consolidation day: use the first low after 10:00.
  - Homework: block out 11:30–1:30 on every day of old data and record what forms and where.
- **How to identify:** 10:00 marker, first swing low/high after 10:00 (or most prominent one on a trend day), lunch window box 11:30–1:30.
- **How to use:** Expect the retracement to run that liquidity during lunch; he also expects it to finish right before 1:30.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Fri Feb 27: morning drive up to the low of the daily volume imbalance (taking relative equal highs), then lunch macro dropped to the first low after 10:00 and ran it out right before 1:30 (he jokes "probably random"), followed by a small pool run up and then dull PM price action.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [1:07:53](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4073) — lunch = run back to the 10:00 high or low
  - [1:09:27](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4167) — 11:30–1:30, collect data
  - [1:15:04](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4504) — first low after 10:00 as objective
  - [1:16:38](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4598) — time and price agree
  - [1:17:24](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4644) — trending-day variant
  - [1:19:47](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4787) — 1:30–2:00 PM opening range
  - [1:21:25](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4885) — low run right before 1:30
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Matches the L26-113 lunch macro targets (10:00 high/low) and the "2-hour NY lunch" in L26-121. The trending-day look-back rule is new here.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: Daily volume imbalance as the lunch-macro draw (partial vs full gap closure)  (aliases: draw on liquidity, buy side above, turtle soup at VI low)
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule of thumb
- **What ICT says:** On a day that opened with a discount gap, price can aim for full gap closure (the settlement price) but he does not require it; the easier objective is the low of the daily volume imbalance (red box) once the buy side above it is taken. Enter on the way (BISI on a gradient level), take profit when the VI low is bumped: the run takes buy-side then reverses (turtle soup, "fake out"), which is why he closed his long rather than waiting for full closure.
- **Timestamps:** [1:07:53](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4073); [1:08:40](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4120) — consolidation stacking sell side and buy side, edge is trading up; [1:13:24](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=4404) — why turtle soup and why he closed the long; [1:40:37](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=6037)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Shows the HTF PD array (daily VI) setting the target while the intraday gradient level sets the entry.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: Weekly profile: TGIF retracement  (aliases: TGIF, Friday retracement, weekly range 40%/60%)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / numbers
- **What ICT says:** On Friday price usually retraces 20–30% of the weekly range. If the week is a consolidation week, expect more: a 40% retracement of the weekly range (highest high to lowest low) back toward the middle/median is the minimum, 60% the extreme. Reason for 40 rather than 20–30: in consolidation the pull back to the middle can be more exaggerated. Retracement measured when price has been moving lower Wednesday–Friday (or Thursday–Friday, or just Friday).
- **How to use:** Don't treat a Friday bullish first FVG as a long entry in a bearish narrative; expect the run to the TGIF level to use the liquidity (relative equal lows are taken first, then up). Context that day: geopolitical uncertainty ahead of Sunday's open ("nobody wants to be in a position"), so the algorithm won't sink or rally price strongly; it goes back to the middle of the range and lets Sunday's open play out.
- **Timestamps:** [0:38:30](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2310) — 20–30% usual, 40% in consolidation; [0:40:13](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2413) — 40% minimum, 60% extreme; [0:42:32](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2552) — why a middle-of-range delivery into the weekend
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** New numbers for Friday retracement in a consolidation week; old teaching was the 20–30% general rule.

Noted that "this looks a little too smooth".

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 28, 2026
head: Higher-timeframe narrative: bearish NQ, discount wick, 6-month objective  (aliases: daily bias, 6-month objective)
body:
- **Kind:** example / narrative
- **What ICT says:** He stays bearish NQ with a first-half-of-2026 objective (think July 4th) and says he would reconsider only if price takes the high of the daily volume imbalance. Wednesday's push took a short-term high but failed quickly (Judas-swing-like after Nvidia earnings pumped then gave it back). Near-term: if Sunday gaps lower and trades below Friday's low, first target is last Monday's low (Feb 23); next is the CE of the daily discount wick (halfway); a close below that CE suggests the low will be taken; then speed and magnitude below it decide whether he reaches the first-half objective. The index is held "captive in a range", so lower-timeframe (sub-1-minute) micro market structure matters more than swing setups.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:30](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=210); [0:06:41](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=401); [0:09:04](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=544); [0:37:41](https://youtu.be/FBxxYUvNaY4?t=2261)

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: Daily bias from body-based Inside Day  (aliases: "inside day despite the wick")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** He judges the daily candle by its body relative to the previous day's body. A candle whose body could not go below the prior day's body and could not go above it is an inside day, even if the wick pokes above the prior high. He had warned the prior day that price might bump up and challenge his bearish stance; it hit the high and "gave up the ghost", so he kept the bearish read.
- **How to identify:** Compare today's candle body to yesterday's body, not the wicks.
- **How to use:** Used to decide whether a push up into a high is a real shift or a liquidity grab; here it supported staying bearish.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ daily: price rallied, took out a prior high, wicked above, then came back; he says it "revisited that volume imbalance and took the liquidity" and then lost the level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:21](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=441) — body-vs-previous-body inside-day logic
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He frames this as a concern he flagged earlier ("go back and listen to the presentation"); the specific lecture is not named here.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: News-day rule: PPI / CPI / 8:30 releases  (aliases: economic calendar, red-folder event, sit on your hands)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He is "usually wrong" on PPI and CPI, has a very low strike rate on them, and does not position ahead of them. Rule: sit on your hands and wait for the carnage; then whatever liquidity is left in the wake of the run is what you focus on. These releases act "a little like FOMC": a big run, possibly a trap that "rips people's faces off", and then price goes to where it really wanted to go.
- **How to identify:** The high or low that formed before the 8:30 move is the liquidity to target afterward, even if it is several hundred handles away; price "eventually finds its way back there" (may not happen the same day, e.g. on a Friday).
- **How to use:** Do not be in the market in the seconds before/around the release; watch only. After the spike, plan for the pre-release extreme as the target. He ignores the data itself ("could care less about the data", does not trust it) and follows only price action/liquidity logic.
- **Example in this video:** 8:30 PPI; price swept yesterday's low right at the release then drifted lower; he stays flat and only comments. He notes a close below a wick/low after the release usually "warrants a lower low".
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:19](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=679) — rule of sitting on hands; [0:13:41](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=821) — target the liquidity from before the 8:30 move; [0:40:27](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=2427) — economic calendar as the main driver of distraction/traps
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Repeated disclaimers: not trade advice, do not trade his commentary with real money.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: Event Horizon  (aliases: midpoint between two static price points, halfway-point draw)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / re-teach
- **What ICT says:** When two obvious static price points (old daily lows, old highs, or a NWOG/NDOG above and another below the current price) bracket the market, measure the range between them and mark the halfway point. Price will likely gravitate to that halfway point, and once it breaks beyond it "generally" a sustained price run follows (retracements possible). He says this is the midpoint (a consequent-encroachment-style level) between two key PD arrays. He originally taught it with one new week opening gap above and one below price.
- **How to identify:** Lay a fib across the span between the two points (e.g. yesterday's low to the next old-low pool on the daily). He watches how much "energy" price spends reaching the upper quadrant and then the 50% level.
- **How to use:** Use the 50% as the draw; a break below it (in a bearish case) signals likely sustained delivery toward the far pool. He eyeballs the fib and says it can be "off a couple points".
- **Example in this video:** MNQ daily old lows; yesterday's low (taken at 8:30) to the next outlined pool of sell-side liquidity below; price traded down into the upper quadrant of that range, then made three lower lows on 1m, aiming to gravitate to the halfway point.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:10](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=1090) — static old lows as hard objectives, fib laid over; [0:19:51](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=1191) — gravitate to the halfway point; "that's event horizon"; [0:21:26](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=1286) — NWOG-to-NWOG version
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He stresses that old highs/lows are precise, finite locations ("Wyckoff doesn't talk about that stuff") and that being old PD arrays they invite price to gravitate to the midpoint.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: Daily Volume Imbalance as a higher-timeframe premium PD array
body:
- **Kind:** example only / application
- **What ICT says:** A volume imbalance on the daily chart (red box) is a higher-timeframe PD array. Being bearish, he treats the top of it as the place to sell (premium), its consequent encroachment (CE) as the first draw, and its low as the next objective. He says CE "is always a draw. Always a draw."
- **How to identify:** Daily chart gap between candles (volume imbalance); mark top, CE (dotted midpoint) and low.
- **How to use:** Enter shorts when price trades to the top (even a tick beyond it) and rejects; target the SSL below, then CE, then the low of the VI; expect a possible retracement back up to CE after the low is reached, but if bearish you want it not to do so.
- **Example in this video:** Overnight/London: price runs above, trades into the top of the daily VI (about one tick above it, "colouring outside the lines"), then reverses lower toward the CE and the old-low pool below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:43:46](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=2626) — the pink/red daily VI box in London killzone; [0:47:42](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=2862) — top of VI used; [0:56:22](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3382) — CE is always a draw
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He uses it because price rejected the recent highs on the daily after Nvidia earnings; he calls "Nvidia propping the market up" a retail myth.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: FVG next to a wick: use the wick, not the gap  (aliases: "new extra charge")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (new)
- **What ICT says:** If the SIBI sits directly against a wick (the wick candle immediately adjacent to the gap, with no candle between), the fair value gap is not to be used; instead measure the wick with its gradient levels. In the example there is one candlestick between the wick and the SIBI, so the SIBI is valid and counts as a premium PD array. He says go back to old price data to see the benefit of this distinction.
- **How to identify:** Check whether the wick candle is immediately adjacent to the SIBI's candle structure. If there is a one-candle barrier between them, the FVG is valid.
- **How to use:** Valid SIBI: use as the premium PD array for a short; any short entry inside it; stop above the high of the candle that forms it (setup-timeframe high).
- **Example in this video:** 1m chart in London session after the run to the daily VI top; SIBI with one candle separating it from the wick, so the gap is valid.
- **Timestamps:** [0:46:07](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=2767) — wick vs SIBI; [0:46:55](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=2815) — if wick were immediately left of the SIBI use only wick gradient levels
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Captions are confusing about left/right of the candles; the exact geometry is (caption unclear). Treat the rule as "adjacent wick -> use the wick levels, else the FVG".

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: High-frequency (sub-1-minute) entry: lower half of the small FVG after a close below CE
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** Inside a higher-timeframe PD array, drop to 30s/15s/5s charts and enter in the lower half of the small FVG (for shorts). He wants the 1m bodies to have stayed in the lower half of the gap, then you wait for how the market trades into the upper half. This is the "high frequency trading window of entry". After a candle closes below the FVG's CE, the next candle anywhere below that midpoint but above the low of the gap is an entry area. You may miss the trade if price shoots up and runs; that is fine because many such setups form on small timeframes. Use the smallest leverage, one micro. Do not expect to learn everything from short-form teaching; it is a bullet-point view.
- **How to identify:** 1m FVG (SIBI) formed at the top of the daily VI; a big green candle runs up, then a candle closes below the CE of the 1m gap; entry zone is below CE and above the gap low.
- **How to use:** Entry in the lower half; stop per volatility rule below; target a first scaling point at a nearby SSL pool; use CE of the daily VI as the draw.
- **Example in this video:** London session (2:00-5:00 ET London killzone): price runs, drops into a 1m inefficiency which could be used as a 2022 model entry, stops out; another run higher; then enter in the lower half of a darker-shaded 1m FVG at the daily VI top, stop above the 1m candle high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:09](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=2529) — sub-1-minute topic starts; [0:50:02](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3002) — lower half = entry window; [0:51:39](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3099) — close below CE, next candle entry zone
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He admits entering in the upper half works for him sometimes but advises beginners to use the lower half so they are in the move without fear of missing it.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: Stop placement under high volatility: frame the stop on the setup timeframe
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In normal volatility you could place the stop one tick above the high of the sub-1-minute gap/swing. But when volatility is extreme (e.g. around news), ranges overlap the prior candle's range, so go back to the 1-minute setup timeframe and use its high for the stop. Tight stops on tiny timeframes get stopped repeatedly, and commissions and "paper cuts" compound the pain.
- **How to identify:** Elevated volatility = wide candles, wicks overlapping.
- **How to use:** Stop one tick above the 1m high that formed the setup (or just above the candle high); accept fewer contracts. Entry in the lower half, stop from the higher timeframe where the setup formed. "You're probably going to trade with less contracts, and that's a good thing."
- **Example in this video:** The stop sits above the 1m candle high which formed the SIBI at the daily VI top.
- **Timestamps:** [0:48:29](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=2909) — stop on the 1m high due to volatility; [0:52:29](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3149) — go outside the small-timeframe range; [0:53:16](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3196) — fewer contracts

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 27, 2026
head: Trailing a one-contract position with displacement  (aliases: stop loss management, strangling the position)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / trade management
- **What ICT says:** With one contract you cannot take a partial (it would close the only position). Instead, wait for displacement below a key low (a short-term low that would be a partial point) and move the stop to just above the high of the displacement candle. Displacement means price must go below a key low or above a key high; it creates a short-term low, then dives lower, closes, and the next candle keeps running. Repeat at each key low.
- **How to identify:** Price pierces the key low to the downside and leaves a SIBI; that confirms displacement. A candle that merely creates a new low without piercing the prior low is not displacement.
- **How to use:** Stop moves: initial stop above the 1m high -> above the first displacement candle's high -> above the high of the leg that starts the next run lower, etc. When it reaches the SSL/low of the VI, close (or let the stop take you out), then anticipate a retracement to the VI CE.
- **Example in this video:** Short from the top of the daily VI: price takes out the first key low (displacement, SIBI) -> stop moves to that candle's high; price gravitates to the daily VI CE; below it more SSL; each time price takes a low and leaves a SIBI, the stop is moved to the candle starting the run; final target low of the VI.
- **Timestamps:** [0:57:11](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3431) — move stop under displacement with one contract; [0:58:44](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3524) — pierce low and leave SIBI; [1:00:21](https://youtu.be/TFyk2jbQzdc?t=3621) — displace below the low, then move the stop to that candle's high
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Stop being greedy": he would not have caught the full drop; closing near the VI low is acceptable.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 23, 2026
head: High Resistance vs Low Resistance Liquidity Run Conditions
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Low resistance conditions show volume imbalances and FVGs, big one-sided range candles in one direction, small-body short-lived retracements against it, and longer protractions with more candles in the run's direction. High resistance conditions are the opposite: price stays inside the previous candle's range and inside inefficiencies longer than it should, "not in a hurry to go anywhere". Typical at the start of the year; he expects the shift toward more freely running conditions toward spring (last couple of weeks of March, April, May).
- **How to identify:** Price keeps overlapping the prior candle's range, wicks poke outside and come back, inefficiencies take a long time to fill.
- **How to use:** In high resistance, be highly selective and cherry-pick days; precision is worse (a wick-only deviation outside a range is not a clean signal).
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily: a single small deviation outside the range with a close "a little concerning from a precision stance", but consistent with high resistance conditions.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:43](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=283) — high resistance conditions stated; [0:09:30](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=570) — what low resistance looks like; [0:20:37](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=1237) — conditions to change toward spring
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same family as "high/low resistance liquidity run" conditions in the model list.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 23, 2026
head: Inside Day (two versions) and compression -> expansion  (aliases: inside day on a body basis)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** The classic inside day: today's highest high is lower than the previous day's high and today's lowest low is higher than the previous day's low. His version also counts the day as inside when the body of the candle is inside the previous day's range even if the wicks exceed it. He says this body-inside day "in and of itself is a PD array" signalling compression; compression that builds over days (smaller ranges, inside days) releases like a spring, either higher or lower, giving sustained price runs for a day trader.
- **How to identify:** Compare the daily body with the previous day's high-to-low range (his version) or the full high-low (classic).
- **How to use:** Expect protraction tomorrow/Wednesday. With his bearish bias he expects big down-close candles and an expansion to the downside that explores the relative equal lows. If price takes out the high (the swing high noted below) he revisits whether he is wrong.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ daily Monday Feb 23: Friday's low was 24,677.00; Monday traded to 24,667.75 (almost 10 handles lower), and Monday's high was lower than Friday's high, but the body stayed inside Friday's range. Low was only wick damage.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:32](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=332) — two versions of an inside day; [0:07:08](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=428) — Friday low 24,677 vs Monday low 24,667.75, body inside; [0:07:55](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=475) — compression builds then releases; [0:10:17](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=617) — body-inside = a PD array, anticipating protraction
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same concept as flagged in the Feb 27 video (L26-127). He warns that clipping this as a sound bite makes it sound like he is predicting direction; he opened with a bearish premise.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 23, 2026
head: Discount Wick graded with CE  (aliases: wick consequent encroachment, close below the midpoint of the wick)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The wick below Friday's low is a discount wick (the discount side exploring lower). Grade it with a fib: if price trades below the wick's CE (midpoint) and closes below it, that generally (not always) indicates continuation in that direction. If it cannot close below the wick's midpoint, it usually means high resistance conditions continue and the low will not be explored for now.
- **How to identify:** Draw the fib across the wick; level 0.5 = CE (he shows his fib settings via screenshot, new viewers can copy them).
- **How to use:** Close below the CE of the discount wick -> expect long black down candles toward the lows and then the relative equal lows below ("club 64"). On the upside, a wick above the high is acceptable because of volatility, but a close above it would make him consider himself wrong, and he would then expect a draw toward the high.
- **Example in this video:** Notepad level: the half level at 24,608 must be breached on a closing basis. He removes the fib afterwards to keep the chart pristine.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:52](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=712) — discount wick; [0:12:42](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=762) — close below CE continues, no close keeps high resistance; [0:15:04](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=904) — 24,608 half level on notepad
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Keep the chart clean: "the least amount of things you have on your chart, the easier it is to follow a narrative".

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 23, 2026
head: RTH Opening Range Gap (RTH ORG) — premium vs discount, high/low assignment
body:
- **Kind:** definition (precise)
- **What ICT says:** The gap is between where price opens at 9:30 ET (regular trading hours) and the previous day's RTH close, which prints at 4:14 pm ET on the chart (closing candle; the last 4:14 candle on the time axis). If the 9:30 opening price is above the previous RTH close it is a premium gap: the 9:30 open is the RTH ORG high and the previous close is the low. If the 9:30 open is below the previous RTH close it is a discount gap: the 9:30 open is the RTH ORG low and the previous close is the high. Do this every day and keep several days of levels (he also marks the CE/gradient levels when wide).
- **How to identify:** Toggle the chart to RTH to see the close; then mark the gap. In Monday's case "last trading day" is Friday, so Monday's RTH ORG is also the new week opening gap.
- **How to use:** These levels are the key levels for entries and targets; price reacts at them "to the tick", often during macro times; he keeps roughly a week of ORG levels (Thursday ORG low/high, Friday ORG high/low, Tuesday ORG high/low, etc.) on his chart.
- **Example in this video:** Friday RTH close 25,079.00; Monday 9:30 open 24,981.25 (lower), so a discount gap: RTH ORG high = 25,079.00 (same price as the NWOG top) and RTH ORG low = 24,981.25. Later: Tuesday's RTH ORG high hit at 24,799.5 exactly at a candle high during a macro time, leaving Tuesday's ORG low untouched, then Friday's RTH ORG low was touched.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:27](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=1287) — NWOG and prior close 25,079; [0:22:17](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=1337) — 9:30 open 24,981.25 = ORG low; [0:25:34](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=1534) — premium vs discount rule; [0:43:53](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=2633) — stacking prior days' ORG highs/lows
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Relative to Monday: "Thursday/Friday/Tuesday" ORG levels are from the previous week's sessions. He says the opening range is the 30-minute window starting 9:30, "I don't care what anybody else says".

head: Opening range at 9:30 and the Judas swing: buy-side raid then sell
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** At 9:30 the market runs liquidity in the first 30 minutes: it tends to take close-proximity buy-side and close-proximity sell-side, then "the real move" ensues. A rally into buy-side at 9:30 is the Judas swing (manipulation, trap) designed to induce buyers; smart money takes the other side of that raided buy-side and sells, to drive price toward lower lows (wording about buy stops vs sell stops is caption unclear).
- **How to use:** Anticipate at minimum that price reaches the near buy side; then look for shorts if bearish. A 15-minute time frame is the "bellwether" chart for lay of the land.
- **Example in this video:** 15m, Monday: price rallied into an inefficiency toward the NWOG but could not reach it; at 9:30 it took buy-side (relative equal highs) and tagged a premium SIBI / CISD level on the 15m (pink line) before turning.

He says SMT is "wonderful, but there's a place for it and it's not in every setup"; if you look for it outside liquidity runs or the opening range you are looking at the wrong time. He never settled what the T stands for (smart money tool/technique).

head: Reading weakness with the CE and fib levels after a drop  (aliases: no candles in the upper half, institutional order flow)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** After a sharp drop leaves a gap, you do not want to see the whole gap filled; you want a small portion left open. Bodies cannot get back to CE (0.5); wicks may do the damage. In the example price passed 0.5 and 0.625 on wicks but failed to reach the 0.75 upper quadrant, and bodies stayed below CE: weakness; expect it to work lower, but do not take a tiny-stop short because volatility is exorbitant. A second attempt that did not even reach CE gave a lower high: "nobody is allowed to lay down candles in the upper half" — real institutional order flow. He stresses you don't need level 2/3 data, footprint or volume profile: open, high, low, close in time is enough.
- **How to use:** Larger candles on the down side, more candles down than up, short retracements (1-3 candles) = bearish order flow. If bullish, the same applies in reverse: price not trading into the lower half of a discount PD array.
- **Timestamps:** [0:36:42](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=2202) — small portion left open, bodies can't reach CE; [0:37:31](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=2251) — fib levels 0.625/0.75; lower high = order flow; [0:38:18](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=2298) — no need for level 2, footprint, volume profile; [0:55:46](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=3346) — candle size and count as order flow

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 23, 2026
head: PD array only matters at a key level, at the right time, in line with the draw  (aliases: no man's land)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Any PD array that is not sitting on one of the pre-marked levels (gradient levels of ORGs/NWOG/NDOG, opening range levels) is in "no man's land" and does not interest him. The recipe: (1) the FVG/PD array is right over a gradient level, (2) at the right time (macro/session), (3) in deference to where he thinks the market will draw. With those three ingredients PDs work, "100% strike rate" (hyperbole). An FVG formed by three candles but not at any level is just a common gap. Futures are a "gentleman's market" because everyone sees the same exact tick levels; forex has broker-specific prices.
- **How to use:** Small ranges of 15-30 handles don't need a liquidity pool as a target ("cookie cutter": 20 handles, done). Closest target that makes sense.
- **Example in this video:** The market bounced off Friday's RTH ORG low the moment a candle opened and traded into it (an "easy get in and go"), and meandered between Tuesday's ORG high and Friday's ORG low.

head: First Presented FVG in the opening range (9:31-10:00)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / rule
- **What ICT says:** Use the very first FVG that shows displacement between 9:31 and 10:00 ET. Technically the window is 9:30-9:59 but he says to use minute 31 (so skip the 9:30 candle), because things can go wrong using the 9:30 candle for people who don't fully know what they are doing. Short at the CE of the FVG with the stop one tick above the candle low that forms it; if stopped out, wait for price to trade back below CE, then use any run back up (an FVG or the up-close candle = rejection block) to short again.
- **How to identify:** Displacement candle leaving a gap; the volume imbalance is drawn from the candle close to the next candle open.
- **How to use:** Sell as price trades up to CE; the next retest is the rejection block. It "should not trade above CE if it is weak".
- **Example in this video:** 9:40 ET 1m: FVG high = a candle's low; open 24,928.25, close 24,928.75; CE 24,938.5; the wick failed to reach CE twice, then a candle closed below the opening price and price protracted down to sell-side (Judas swing, high-frequency style); short above that candle's close with stop just above CE.
- **Timestamps:** [0:51:49](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=3109) — 9:40 first presented FVG, minute 31 rule; [0:52:37](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=3157) — 9:31-10:00 rule; [0:53:25](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=3205) — short at CE, stop one tick above; [0:54:12](https://youtu.be/NxwfXE6Zyns?t=3252) — rejection block re-entry

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 23, 2026
head: Discovery mode on DXY / EURUSD / GBPUSD (soft gray area)
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:** After not looking at forex for about six months, he is in a "soft gray area": no evidence of higher or lower, no hard bias, no trade. DXY: bearish lean toward the low, but the market rallied, took the high and filled the rest of an inefficiency. EURUSD: wanted to see a challenge of the high; it traded lower into sell-side liquidity instead; no evidence either way. Plan: check once or twice a week (Tuesdays and Thursdays), tape read, and only move to day-by-day when price shows something conducive. He does not feel bad about missing moves when he has no thesis ("I don't feel any kind of losing face"). Every day isn't the best day to be in the market; cherry-pick the days to engage.

title: ICT 2026 Forex & Futures Commentary \ February 17, 2026
head: Suspension Block (vs Regular Order Block)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** A suspension block is an order block with a volume imbalance at its END (bottom for down-close, top for up-close). The distinguishing feature: bodies don't touch across the gap (separation exists between candlesticks). This creates a "suspension"—the inefficiency is unmet. When price tests this level later, it's a strong reference because the gap was NEVER filled before.
- **How to identify:** Down-close order block. After it forms, look at the gap between its low and the next candle's high. If there's separation (bodies don't touch), it's a suspension block. Mark the gap.
- **How to use:** Suspension blocks act similarly to regular order blocks BUT have higher probability because they show unmet inefficiency over a longer period. Use as strong support (for longs) or resistance (for shorts). Stop loss should respect this level carefully.
- **Example in this video:** Nasdaq daily: Suspension block identified from prior candlesticks. Price later returned to test it, confirming its relevance.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:08](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=488) — explaining suspension block structure; [0:09:43](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=583) — showing suspension block on chart
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Suspension blocks are a refinement of order block theory. Not all order blocks are suspension blocks; only those with volume imbalance gaps at their ends.

title: ICT 2026 Forex & Futures Commentary \ February 17, 2026
head: Relative Equal Highs/Lows & Liquidity Reversal
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** When price makes a high at approximately the same level as a prior high (within a few ticks), it's a "relative equal high." These are magnets for order flow because they're psychological levels. Price often fails at relative equal highs on retest (lower high = weakening), or uses them as springboards.
- **How to identify:** Mark on chart significant prior highs/lows. When price approaches the same level, note it as relative equal.
- **How to use:** At relative equal highs, expect either: (1) failure and reversal lower, or (2) breakout above. Don't sit at the level; use it to anticipate direction. If bearish bias, shorting at relative equal high is high-probability (shorts cover above, pushing it down).
- **Example in this video:** Nasdaq overnight session 7:00 a.m. ET: relative equal highs from prior trading. Price traded to them, failed, reversed lower. This is the draw used for the day's trading plan.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:07](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=727) — "relative equal highs... why is this important?"; [0:13:42](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=822) — showing how market used this level
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Relative equal highs are psychological. They're not perfectly precise levels; use them with inefficiencies (FVGs, order blocks) nearby for confirmation.

title: ICT 2026 Forex & Futures Commentary \ February 17, 2026
head: Gradient Levels (Fibonacci/Octant Subdivisions on Wicks)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule / how to use
- **What ICT says:** Gradient levels = Fibonacci or eighth (octant) subdivisions of a wick or range. When a wick extends above/below a candle's body, the gradient levels show algorithmic precision. Price often respects these sub-divisions to the tick.
- **How to identify:** Identify a wick (highest/lowest point of a candle that the body didn't touch). Apply Fibonacci or eighths from the body's extreme to the wick's extreme. Mark these gradient levels.
- **How to use:** Entry or target placement using gradient levels shows precision and reduces slippage. Targets: consequent encroachment (CE/50%) or octant levels (12.5%, 25%, 37.5%, etc.). This ties to his teaching on "octant levels from RTH ORG" = same concept applied to intraday wicks.
- **Example in this video:** Nasdaq 1-minute: wick from low to high has gradient levels. Price later returns and uses these levels; bodies stop at 25% or 50% of the wick, showing algorithmic behavior.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:42](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=822) — "Measure that. Consequent encroachment, it hits that"; [0:16:05](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=965) — demonstrating gradient level precision
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Gradient levels are tools for CONFIRMATION, not primary signals. Combine with directional bias (SMT, macro, geopolitical) for better odds.

title: ICT 2026 Forex & Futures Commentary \ February 17, 2026
head: Model 2022 & Market Structure Shift
body:
- **Kind:** definition / entry model
- **What ICT says:** Model 2022 = a specific market structure pattern taught in his 2022 mentorship. Involves a shift from one order flow direction to another, marked by specific candlestick patterns (e.g., down-close reversal candle, then up-close impulse). This model shows the transition from distribution to accumulation (or vice versa).
- **How to identify:** Candlestick pattern: first a reversal candle (down-close in uptrend), then confirmation candle (up-close). The model 2022 represents the TURN from sellers to buyers.
- **How to use:** Entry: once the model is confirmed, trade in the new direction. Stop loss: below the reversal candle. Target: trace to next liquidity above.
- **Example in this video:** Nasdaq 1-minute: after a reversal candle (down-close breaking prior low), an up-close follows. This = model 2022. Long from here. The trade then ran higher, confirming the model.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:53](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=1013) — "Model 2022 buy-side shift in market structure"; [0:16:53](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=1013) — showing execution of the model on live 1-minute chart
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Model 2022 is mentioned but not deeply detailed. It's a reference to his paid mentorship content (now free on YouTube, 2016 playlist). The core idea: candlestick patterns signal order flow CHANGES.

title: ICT 2026 Forex & Futures Commentary \ February 17, 2026
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) on Intraday Charts
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example only
- **What ICT says:** An iFVG appears when a candlestick doesn't trade into the opposite direction. Example: a down-close candle leaves a gap below, but price doesn't come back to fill it immediately. Later, price approaches the iFVG from above and uses it as support (iFVG acting like a buy signal).
- **How to identify:** Candlestick with upper gap unfilled (bullish). Note the iFVG level.
- **How to use:** Entry: when price tests the iFVG from above and bounces, go long. Stop: below the iFVG. Target: prior high or next inefficiency.
- **Example in this video:** 1-minute Nasdaq: iFVG identified from earlier candlestick. Price came down, touched the iFVG, bounced = long opportunity.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:05](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=965) — showing iFVG as potential entry; [0:16:53](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=1013) — price using iFVG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** iFVG on intraday timeframes is similar to daily iFVG but with tighter targets and faster exits. Ideal for scalping one micro contract.

title: ICT 2026 Forex & Futures Commentary \ February 17, 2026
head: Range-Bound Market Strategy
body:
- **Kind:** rule / process
- **What ICT says:** In range-bound conditions (consolidation), price will use inefficiencies and stay within the range rather than trend. Do NOT expect breakout continuation. Use inefficiencies as reversal points. If price breaks range, market is shifting to trending mode (high resistance → low resistance or vice versa).
- **How to identify:** Price oscillating between two levels for multiple days/candles without trending directionally. Inefficiencies within the range are being used repeatedly.
- **How to use:** Scalp inefficiencies inside the range. Short highs, buy lows. Don't hold across range breaks. If range breaks on a close, shift to trend-following bias.
- **Example in this video:** S&P 500: currently in heavy consolidation. He would NOT trade ES (too messy), but would trade Nasdaq (slightly better structure).
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:29](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=1109) — "ES is literally a mess. Like, there's nothing in here. I would not touch this."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Range-bound trading is LOW probability for macro directional trades but HIGH probability for scalp entries. Use tight stops and small position sizes.

title: ICT 2026 Forex & Futures Commentary \ February 17, 2026
head: "Unicorn Price Run" & Smart Money Reversal
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example only
- **What ICT says:** A "unicorn price run" is his term for a specific, near-perfect impulsive move where price doesn't touch any inefficiencies or levels until it reaches the target. It's a clean, uninterrupted move—rare and beautiful. Smart money reversal = the moment distribution reverses to accumulation (or vice versa), marked by a sharp candlestick reversal.
- **How to identify:** After smart money reversal candle, price starts running without stopping.
- **How to use:** Once smart money reversal is identified (candlestick closing opposite prior trend), anticipate unicorn run. Don't try to catch every piece; just ride the move to next major level.
- **Example in this video:** Nasdaq 1-minute: after reversal, price had a "unicorn run" up to the target (buy-side inefficiency). The move was clean and didn't pause.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:53](https://youtu.be/z5ytUvVeUoQ?t=1013) — "There's your unicorn price run"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Unicorn runs are rare and only possible when smart money is REALLY pushing. In choppy markets, they don't happen. This is aspirational trading—if you see conditions, take it; if not, don't force it.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 11, 2026
head: RTH Opening Range Gap and half-gap (CE) delivery  (aliases: half gap, gap and go, previous RTH settlement to opening)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry framework
- **What ICT says:** At 9:30 ET the regular-trading-hours gap is the difference between the previous RTH settlement and the 9:30 open. Pull the fib from the previous RTH settlement to the opening price; the half-gap (CE of the gap) has about a 70 percent chance of being traded back to within the first 30 minutes (he also says "by 10:00 in the morning"). A large gap is better: 100 handles or more is ideal because that offers about 50 handles to the half-gap. After it reaches the half, the next question is whether it continues to the 3/4 gap and the full close, or rejects the half-gap and runs in the direction of the gap ("gap and go").
- **How to identify:** Premium gap (open above prior RTH close) -> expect a trade back down to the half; discount gap -> back up. Mark the half gap, plus any pool of liquidity sitting there (here a sell-side pool just under last Wednesday's RTH ORG low).
- **How to use:** In the beginning, coach yourself to submit to the idea that price goes to the usual draw; combined with a short first-presented FVG at 9:31 onward, the half gap is the target. He frames this as "one of the things I had for my son" (look for that move when there is a sizeable gap). Don't take his 70 percent on faith: test it on your own data every day there is a gap, for as long as you can, and keep recording going forward (he cites 34 years of use and data from 50 years before him).
- **Example in this video:** Premium gap on Feb 11: 9:30 open at ...326.75 (last digits). Price ran the pre-session high, took the bearish-breaker area, sold off, and reached the half-gap about 2 minutes before 10:00 ("there's the delivery"). He also writes the ORG levels manually using the last three numbers of price.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:26](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=506) — premium RTH ORG forms; [0:09:48](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=588) — fib from settlement to open, 70 percent to half gap in 30 min; [0:21:34](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=1294) — half gap then 3/4 / full / gap-and-go; [0:36:11](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2171) — half gap delivered before 10:00; [0:37:51](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2271) — 100 handles ideal
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Said 30 minutes and "by 10:00"; also says the opening range is 9:30-10:00, "I don't care who says otherwise, it's 30 minutes". Last Wednesday's RTH ORG levels were still active a week later (low and the half-gap).

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 11, 2026
head: News-day rule: NFP on an unusual day; wait for 9:30
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Employment data came out on a Wednesday, which is atypical, so he treats it as "exploration mode" and does not rush to trade. He thinks no one should trade ahead of 8:30 data, normally Friday or today; wait until the opening bell (9:30) to mitigate unrealistic risk. Reasons: limit orders around NFP usually don't fill, market orders give heavy slippage; much of the NFP activity is lottery trading. After the open, watch whether the market gives reasons to participate; if not, "take a step back" and wait for the afternoon session, or do nothing ("always an option"). He used the session to see whether a 10:00 silver bullet, lunch hour trade or PM session was warranted.

head: Parent and subordinate time frames  (aliases: 1m parent, 15s/5s children)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The 1-minute chart is the parent; the 15-second and 5-second charts are subordinate and hyperactive. While price is consolidating inside the prior candle's range on the 1m, he ignores the lower time frames. When the 1m starts to move and displace, the lower time frames become useful; he also checks the small charts for unruly gaps/inefficiencies left open ("I have to babysit them"). With smaller time frames you get precision and support for an idea.

head: Suspension Block (daily) and its gradient levels
body:

Toggle the chart's volume-imbalance setting (the Settings tab) to see both imbalances; if your toggle differs you won't see the lower volume imbalance and his commentary will confuse you. When a toggle gives two on the same imbalance he favours that one. He then lays the fib from the highest high to the low of the suspension block to draw gradient levels (the horizontal lines) which he extends to the right.
- **How to use:** Gradient levels of the daily suspension block act as targets and as places where he expects FVGs to form; price traded just above the block's top at the open and then moved down through the gradient levels.

head: Pre-session buy-side, 9:30 opening price and first presented FVG
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** Pre-session = anything before 9:30. At 9:30 price runs pre-session high, and the 9:30 opening price is a very sensitive level (annotate it). From 9:31 onward, anticipate any FVG that displaces in the direction you expect price to gravitate. The "first presentation" of an FVG after the open is key; it has to displace toward the target. Price took out a low and closed below it, left the buy-side pool that had absorbed buy stops: "smart money is short here". Entry: the bearish breaker (down-close candle between the high, the low and the higher high) and the opening price; the first presented FVG above; overshoot is allowed ("color outside the lines"). After the sell-off, wait through high resistance conditions; once price moves lower, drop to the lower time frames for inefficiencies, e.g. trade to one, sell off, use the daily institutional block's gradient levels.
- **How to use:** Short into the first presented FVG/breaker with the half-gap as the target. A turtle soup at the high is the context. Use gradient levels as stops/partials.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 11, 2026
head: Smart-money entry, two-stage offset distribution, and the implied dealing range
body:
- **Kind:** definition / model of order flow
- **What ICT says:** Buy stops above the high are buyers entering on a breakout or protecting shorts; smart money sells into them (counterparty) and "will give the liquidity to the pending buy orders". Retail trades patterns (flags, pennants, head and shoulders, trend lines); smart money sees the run as an entry then targets retail longs: those longs protect with sell stops, and when price trades there the stop becomes a market sell, creating liquidity for smart money to buy back cheaply. Smart money buys where others sell at a discount (retail sells at a discount to professionals "all day long"). Offset distribution happens in two places: stage 1 at discount inefficiencies (an FVG below) and the half gap/sell-side pool (partials, banking profit); stage 2 further down at the next sell-side pool (here below the employment-data low and other old lows), where they buy back what remains. The range from the high (entry) to the final low is the implied dealing range.
- **How to identify:** Mark the entry high, the first sell-side liquidity (half gap and SSL pool), and the second pool (old low / data low).
- **How to use:** Frame trades as selling above the high and targeting the first pool for partials, then the second; "you don't need depth of market, book maps or liquidity maps": know the time of day and the old highs/lows.
- **Timestamps:** [0:41:51](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2511) — smart money collected buy stops; [0:42:40](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2560) — handshake with breakout buyers; [0:43:26](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2606) — two places to offset: discount inefficiencies; [0:46:43](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2803) — sell stops become market orders; [0:47:31](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2851) — implied dealing range and partials; [0:49:13](https://youtu.be/V4KPpX-CWXk?t=2953) — two stages of offset distribution
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says ICT-style opening range theory means 9:30-10:00 ET (30 minutes) for the first stage.

head: Higher-timeframe premise from the RTH Opening Range Gap  (aliases: key level, session open/close)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Every trade needs a higher-timeframe premise: something on a higher time frame that leads to why the market should go up or down. The RTH opening range gap (previous RTH close to the 9:30 open) counts as a higher time frame key level, "you can't get any more higher time frame than session closings and session opens". The high and low of the gap are defined just by delineation; no labels are needed. Such levels act like new week opening gaps and new day opening gaps. He says 24-hour trading, if it happens, would make things easier (the gap would simply be defined differently, other tools exist).
- **How to identify:** Compare today's 9:30 open with the previous RTH close (4:14 pm ET print). With ETH shown continuously you do not see that gap (the only thing missing on ETH is the 5-6 pm hour gap), so toggle to RTH or use annotations.
- **How to use:** Anchor on the old gap and expect price to return to it (he had said on Feb 4 he felt price would come back up there). Fib/gradient levels inside it matter: price traded into its upper half, then quickly failed.
- **Example in this video:** Feb 4 (Wednesday) RTH ORG: 25,440 and 25,385. Five days later, overnight, price traded up into it, into the upper half between the two levels (a bull flag everyone likes to trade), then "gave up the ghost" and went lower; at 7:00 it was in the upper half; then the pre-market ran a buy-side and reversed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:26](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=446) — higher-time-frame premise needed; [0:10:45](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=645) — Feb 4 ORG levels 25,440 / 25,385; [0:13:07](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=787) — why the open and close are higher time frame; [0:15:31](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=931) — RTH vs ETH and the 4:14 pm close

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 10, 2026
head: Pre-market session bias: 7:00-9:30 ET two-sided liquidity
body:
- **Kind:** rule / model
- **What ICT says:** At 7:00 ET the pre-market begins and the market starts seeking liquidity before the 9:30 bell in a more uniform way; then the real run of the day ensues. For a brand-new trader: mark two definitive liquidity levels (e.g. relative equal highs above, relative equal lows below). It is not imperative to know which will be hit first; whichever hits first, the opposing side is traded to next. When price runs one side at 7:00, that should act as a false breakout, so you look for signatures supporting the other side as the next draw. This is the session bias for the 7:00-9:30 window (he describes it as about "2 and 1/2 hours" and mentions hour-and-a-half chunks).
- **How to identify:** Look back over the London session for relative equal highs and lows. Choose the obvious, smooth ones; if the market gives a perfect relative equal low, anchor just that and ignore messier candidates.
- **How to use:** If buy-side is raided first at 7:00, treat the relative equal lows as the draw; confirm with a lower time frame inefficiency showing willingness to drop, and with price failing to reach the upper half of the old ORG or its low. Even "whichever" logic works for a total beginner who has no bias.
- **Example in this video:** Overnight price traded to the upper half of Feb 4's ORG; at 7:00 a run on a small buy-side pool above (highs lower to the right = a prime BSL candidate), then reversal into consolidation, then lower toward overnight relative equal lows (the red line) while never retesting the lower ORG level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:42](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=882) — 7:00 pre-market, look for clean levels; [0:17:07](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1027) — equal lows/highs as draws; [0:20:20](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1220) — whichever is hit first, the other is next; [0:21:08](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1268) — false breakout, session bias; [0:25:18](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1518) — smoothest relative equal lows

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 10, 2026
head: Buy-side and sell-side liquidity as stops of the other side  (restated for beginners)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Highs/relative equal highs hold buy stops above them: anyone short places a protective buy stop there. Lows hold the protective sell stops of longs: that is sell-side liquidity. Liquidity is "the lifeblood of any market"; he looks for where the market will draw before volume bars print, whereas volume/footprint data are hindsight.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:32](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1172) — BSL above highs, SSL below lows; [0:24:30](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1470) — liquidity as fuel and anchor points

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 10, 2026
head: Counterparty theory: why smart money shorts old highs
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When price takes out buy-side, smart money sells short into it, using the resting buy orders (breakout buyers and short stop-outs) as counterparties; they keep throwing sell orders to pair off as many as they can. They then need a lower price to get out: the most advantageous places are old lows and relative equal lows close by, where retail longs have their stops (sell stops that become market sells) and sell at a lower price. The lower target can also be a sell-side discount inefficiency. Every setup uses this counterparty logic. Retail does not spoof; retail traders pull orders and close before their full stop is hit, so depth-of-market numbers may not be there when price arrives.
- **How to use:** "Find the counterparty": you don't need to be right initially about direction; know the liquidity, the inefficiency in between, and the next draw. A trader long who dodged a stop by not being taken out but never banked profit will watch price wilt; when price is near the sell side, the setup is easy.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:45](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1665) — buy side taken, who sells short; [0:28:33](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1713) — where they get out (old lows); [0:36:35](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2195) — retail doesn't spoof; [0:39:47](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2387) — handshake with existing interest, counterparty theory

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 10, 2026
head: Institutional order flow entry drill on a small-time-frame FVG (SIBI short)  (aliases: sell-side imbalance buy-side inefficiency, cookie cutter)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** Once the draw is known (here the relative equal lows), drop to the 15-second or 5-second chart. Find a SIBI (the captions read "sell side of bounce by side efficiency" = sellside imbalance, buyside inefficiency) left during the move down. Price must trade up into it, and the upper half must be respected: wicks may enter, but "we don't want to see a body left in it". A weak market will not close the gap in one pass; it trades up into it and rejects. That is the highest-probability FVG: "it needs to show a willingness to stay open". Re-entries are allowed; he shows two separate entries into the same type of gap and a 5-second repeat of the 15-second orange box.
- **How to identify:** The FVG is small, formed within a run toward a defined draw, and the lower half is where bodies stay. He demands a defined dynamic price range (the FVG high to the target low) with enough range to yield 20 handles.
- **How to use:** Enter short as price trades up into it; stop above candle number one's high plus one tick; target one tick below the sell-side pool. If stopped out and price comes back to the lower half, re-enter with the stop again above candle one's high plus 1 tick.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s/5s at about 9:30-9:45 ET after the 7:00 buy-side raid: price consolidated, a SIBI formed during the drop; price traded up into it, respected the upper half (wick only), traded lower, came back up trading just shy of the next inefficiency, then broke lower toward the overnight relative equal lows.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:56](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1856) — institutional order flow entry drill; [0:31:43](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=1903) — weak market won't close the gap; [0:33:20](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2000) — 15s order block CISD, wicks allowed; [0:43:01](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2581) — valid short: body stayed in the lower half
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says this is the "cookie cutter": where is the market going to draw to? He calls it Robin's-cup-winning stuff and says the same skill works on any asset class or time frame.

title: ICT 2026 Smart Money Concepts Lecture \ February 10, 2026
head: Stop and re-entry rules for FVG entries
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Selling inside a SIBI: the stop goes above the high of candle number one (the first candle of the three-candle pattern), plus one tick. Buying inside a bullish inefficiency: stop below candle number one's low, one tick. If you are stopped out and price later returns to the lower half of the same gap (for shorts), that is another entry with the stop again at candle one plus one tick. When a trade looks about to get stopped but pulls away, that is stop-loss management that he will not teach.
- **Timestamps:** [0:43:01](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2581) — stop above candle high; [0:44:36](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2676) — candle number one, one tick; [0:43:49](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2629) — "stop-loss game" he claims he'll never teach

head: Target: one tick below the sell-side liquidity pool; minimum 20 handles
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** For a beginner, don't get greedy: aim to exit one tick below the level you think is the sell-side pool (or one tick short of the target). Expect more protraction beyond it, but the beginner objective is "just below the line". Determine how much range there is; he wants 20 handles (or 20 pips in forex). On a micro that is about $2 per point (20 handles = $40, "the biggest 40 bucks you'll ever make" the first time, in real money).

head: Immediate rebalance entry technique
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** An immediate rebalance: a candle opens leaving a gap, and the very next candle comes right back and closes the gap in one pass. This is the strongest sign that the filling candle either wilts and goes directly in the direction you expect, or the very next candle does. It is "immediate feedback". He uses it as the entry in a no-clean-setup spot after a consolidation at 9:30: a candle closes down, the next candle opens, comes back up closing the gap at once, then the bottom falls out and price runs lower into sell-side delivery, ending at the RTH ORG high (the unfulfilled side) as a micro scalp.
- **How to use:** Look for runs that are not complete, find small gaps and wait for price to trade up into them; that puts you in the direction of the incomplete run.
- **Timestamps:** [0:47:50](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2870) — nothing clean on the lower time frames; [0:48:41](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2921) — immediate rebalance explained; [0:49:32](https://youtu.be/E8EtGkn-x5w?t=2972) — simplified entry for incomplete runs
