title: From Vision To Execution
head: Casting a vision / Draw on liquidity first  (aliases: "cast forth a vision", narrative, "the plot", "where is price drawing to")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (core method)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Every trader is projecting the future of price; if you are not, you are gambling. The "don't predict" line is dismissed as nonsense, since the vision is exactly what you are doing.
  - The first primary skill is knowing where price is likely to go next (the draw on liquidity). Without knowing what price is reaching for, you cannot get in rhythm with it.
  - Veteran students do not try to work out the next two or three runs. They look at price at this moment and ask what it is likely to do now. If nothing is clear, they do nothing, which removes worry and fear of missing out.
  - Once the vision is set (e.g. "price is reaching for overnight lows") you keep it on the chart and "do not abandon the idea" until price proves you wrong and it is obvious.
  - Price can only be doing one of four things: drawing to sell-side liquidity, drawing to buy-side liquidity, running for a premium inefficiency above, or running for an inefficiency below. Only a geopolitical event breaks that.
- **How to identify:** ask "from the market price right now, where is it drawing?" Name the pool (here: relative equal lows from the overnight session) and then judge each candle by whether it serves that plot.
- **How to use:** the vision sets which candles matter and what is "permissible" for price. Ask what limits you would place on price if you controlled it. If you cannot build a narrative for why price should do what you want, you are forcing a setup.
- **Example in this video:** the Dec 2025 NQ day below. Vision: price rallied in pre-market to an old FVG, rejected, so it should go back down and take the overnight lows. The vision held from before 9:30 until the lows were taken in the late-morning macro.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:37](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=337) vision = what every trader does, otherwise gambling · [0:06:25](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=385) vision = the draw on liquidity · [0:20:02](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1202) "do not abandon the idea" until proven wrong · [0:40:00](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2400) only four possible draws
- **Nuance / caveats:** he says this is hard for brand-new students and recommends coming back after three and six months of experience (see Process). He also cites Habakkuk 2:2–3 (write the vision down, make it plain) as the inspiration for the lecture [0:43:12](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2592).

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Simplification: one market, one to three moving parts  (aliases: "not a kitchen sink approach", specialist)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** the compendium is overwhelming and trying to apply everything (COT, seasonals, Judas swing, Model 2022, Silver Bullet all at once) is a mistake he made himself at 20. Look for something with one, two, maybe three moving parts, in one market. Veterans who are "pulling millions" do not stack tools. Being a specialist in one market matters because you can accumulate the recurring levels and behaviors for that market (his notepad is full of them).
- **How to use:** make the concepts your own and keep them simple enough that you can disengage when nothing is there.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:39](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=99) one to three moving parts, one market · [0:04:51](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=291) the "use everything" toolbox mistake · [0:14:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=864) why being a one-market specialist helps
- **Nuance / caveats:** no specific "recommended" set is named, but everything demonstrated in this video is built on: draw on liquidity, first-presented FVG, overnight lows, macros, iFVG/2022 model, daily PD array.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: First presented FVG after 9:30  (aliases: first FVG after the open, opening range FVG, "first presentation")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement (the video's most repeated idea)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Watch the opening range, 9:30 to 10:00 ET, for the first fair value gap that forms after 9:30, specifically in the direction of the plot (here, sell side is the draw, so a sell-side imbalance / buy-side inefficiency, SIBI).
  - That first FVG is "the PDA" (premium array in a bearish plot) that price reacts from. It is not support and resistance; it is the turning point because it is the first presented imbalance.
  - Before 9:30 he is already "waiting for a price run that creates a long protracted down-close candle", i.e. the displacement that will leave that FVG.
  - It acts as a premium array: price should be repelled from it and not trade into its upper half. If price cannot even reach its consequent encroachment, that tells you it is "exceedingly weak" and the plot (sell off) holds.
  - Over December he watched this "hammer opportunities after opportunities" repeatedly. He states he has no intention of changing the algorithm or the teaching, and "the concept of first presentation is very important".
- **How to identify:** after 9:30, the first clear displacement leg that leaves an imbalance (three-candle gap). It lines up with the direction of the draw (overnight lows below = first SIBI).
- **How to use:** expect price to use it more than once ("it's using it here and here"), retrace into it only to its lower portion (bearish case), and reject. It also defines the top of the dealing range (see Range/equilibrium below).
- **Example in this video:** the reviewed NQ day, 1-minute. Pre-market rallies into the old Dec 23 FVG, starts to sell off. Just after 9:30 a long down-close displacement candle leaves the first SIBI. Price retraces to the low of that gap (not into the upper half) and rolls over. About 50% of the whole run down happened fast, the other half was slow give-and-take reaching toward the overnight lows. During the 9:50–10:10 macro price again returns to the low of this first FVG, "breezes" to its low, and is rejected. In the PM session price again approaches this first presented FVG before the afternoon drop.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:52](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1012) opening range 9:30–10:00 and first FVG · [0:27:07](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1627) the PDA that it sold off from is the first presented FVG, not "support/resistance" · [0:27:57](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1677) too weak to reach CE or upper portion · [0:53:42](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=3222) it "hammered" opportunities all December
- **Nuance / caveats:** he warns that without the plot (the draw), you cannot use this. The FVG that matters is the one aligned with the draw, and not every FVG in the opening range counts.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: First presented FVG after a turtle soup  (aliases: first FVG after a liquidity raid; keep it for 20 days)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - After a turtle soup (price runs a swing high, fails, and snaps back down through the prior run), the first FVG that forms during the displacement after that is a level you keep on your chart. Bearish version here: buy-side taken, turtle soup, sell off, first SIBI. He says it can be done on the buy side too (mirror image); for the bullish mirror he describes it as the first FVG after a sell-side raid that then runs higher.
  - The market does not need to actually reverse or even take the opposing swing low. Price just has to show displacement through a short-term swing and leave a gap that "stands out". If it jumps off the chart when you zoom out, it counts.
  - Zoom out (not in) so your eye jumps to the standout swing highs and lows where the manipulation occurred.
  - Keep that FVG on the chart and project it forward. In line with the updated ranges (the shortest lookback being 20 days) he keeps it on the chart for 20 days (caption unclear on the exact phrasing). He says that is why his Dec 23 level was still useful.
  - Doing so puts you "in the future": you know the level will matter long before volume profile or Elliott wave stuff shows it, and you then wait for time to agree with the price.
- **How to identify:** (1) a recognizable raid of a short-term high/low (turtle soup); (2) displacement through the swing the other way; (3) the first FVG left by that move.
- **How to use:** log it (TradingView workspace, or paper notepad "old school" as he does), carry it 20 days, and watch for price to return to it (as a premium array if it is a sell-side imbalance, or discount for the mirror).
- **Example in this video:** Tuesday Dec 23, 2025, NQ 1-minute, around 9:54 ET. Price ran straight up from the 9:30 open, made a short-term high, rallied above it (false break), turtle-souped back down into the initial run, then displaced below the swing low. The first FVG after that turtle soup is the standout. A few trading days later, pre-market price runs straight up to this FVG's high and rejects, which is the setup for the reviewed day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=624) Dec 23 9:54 a.m. 1m turtle soup and displacement · [0:12:00](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=720) "first presented FVG after turtle soup" · [0:13:35](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=815) keep it on the chart for 20 days, project forward · [0:52:55](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=3175) pre-market ran to the old Dec 23 displacement FVG
- **Nuance / caveats:** he says some such items sit on his "notepad" that he does not want to teach yet (to control questions before the book). This one he is giving for free. The transcript does not make clear if the FVG's high, CE, or the whole gap is the reaction point beyond "that's the high of that" (caption unclear).

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Overnight range lows as sell-side liquidity draw  (aliases: overnight lows, midnight-to-7:00 range, Asian/London lows)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (routine)
- **What ICT says:** the easiest routine: mark off midnight ET to 7:00 AM ET and take the lowest low (and the highest high) of that window. If those lows are relative equal lows, "that's a loaded deal", it is where sell-side liquidity rests and price will want to seek it if the day is bearish. It does not always happen that day, "but that's how I classify it".
- **How to use:** it is the draw you cast the vision toward. Hold the vision (see Casting a vision) while the opening-range FVG, macros and small FVGs play out beneath it.
- **Example in this video:** overnight low was a relative equal low and a clear standout. Price took it later in the session after the 10:50–11:10 macro displacement, where the first run lower goes through the nearby sell side and then the overnight sell side.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:40](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1060) mark midnight to 7:00 ET lowest low · [0:19:14](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1154) "that's the draw" · [0:34:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2064) price dives through the overnight low
- **Nuance / caveats:** "Not all the time, not that very day." It is a classification of where liquidity is, not a guarantee.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Relative equal lows (and highs): the "slightly higher low to the right" rule  (aliases: equal lows, RELs)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** two lows are relative equal when the one on the right is slightly higher than the one on the left. That is the pattern that makes a strong candidate for an algorithmic sell-side raid. If the right-hand low is instead lower than the left (not relative equal), the raid is less likely to be immediate; price can eventually trade through, but first retraces for an inefficiency above or a short-term high (an "efficiency premium" or buy-side pool) to the left.
- **How to identify:** compare successive swing lows; right low marginally higher than the left = relative equal. He says "that's how your eye is supposed to identify it".
- **How to use:** treat as a high-probability target when the plot is bearish. If you see the non-equal version, expect a deeper retracement before the run.
- **Example in this video:** (1) zoomed in during the opening-range consolidation: two lows, the right one slightly higher, flagged as a strong candidate for a sell-side raid; price later takes them. (2) PM session: minor sell side with relative equal lows (lows to the right slightly higher) just above an old AM-session RTH low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:59](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1439) what makes them relative equal · [0:24:46](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1486) the non-equal version needs a deeper retracement · [0:40:48](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2448) PM relative equal lows
- **Nuance / caveats:** he has taught this "for years", so it is a restatement.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: FVG as premium/discount array: behavior inside the gap  (aliases: consequent encroachment (CE), lower quadrant, upper half)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - In a bearish plot a SIBI is a premium array: it should repel price or stop it from entering the upper half. A move that only "breezes" to the low of the gap and says "no thanks" confirms the plot.
  - A later FVG formed in that rally (a leading candle) is then tested by a supporting candle that reaches its CE (50%) and no further; then price dives.
  - Body versus wick signature: when wicks poke almost to the top of the FVG but the candle bodies stay in the lower half (lower quadrant), "that's the signature that you know it's getting ready to start falling".
  - When bodies cannot reach the high of the gap, only the wicks respect it, then price drops from the CE on that wick.
  - Using the same logic on a higher timeframe: how far into an inefficiency above price a bearish market trades tells you the strength. Only reaching the lower half signals weakness (bearish bias intact); slicing through the upper quadrant has different implications (see Suspension block). (caption unclear in this passage)
- **How to use:** watch where bodies close relative to the gap's midpoint and top, not just wicks. Cut through candles (use mid-ranges) rather than painting whole supply/demand zones: "I'm cutting through candles." He insists this is not supply and demand renamed.
- **Example in this video:** mid-morning 1-minute: price comes up into an old SIBI, wicks nearly to the top, bodies stay in the lower quadrant, then it sells off to a new minor sell side. Again later, a small gap left after that low: price comes up, bodies do not reach its high, wicks respect it, CE on the wick, then price moves lower (sideways first until the 10:50 macro).
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:11](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1391) SIBI leading candle, CE test by supporting candle · [0:30:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1824) "cutting through candles", not supply/demand · [0:31:59](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1919) wicks to the top but bodies in the lower half = signature of falling · [0:33:37](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2017) bodies don't reach the high, wick respects, CE
- **Nuance / caveats:** the "bodies in the lower quadrant" signature is stated for a bearish case; the bullish mirror is implied but not shown.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Leading vs supporting candles ("leading man / extras")  (aliases: candle as actor, narrative candles)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage (analogy for the narrative method)
- **What ICT says:** every candle has a role in the plot, but not every candle is a lead. Leading candles are the ones that carry the story at the right time (e.g. the SIBI-forming candle in the 9:50–10:10 macro). Supporting actors are the later candles that "use" the leading candle (reach its CE, fail at its high). "Extras" are candles and gaps that do not matter to the plot. During a consolidation, hunt for the candles that deliver the performance at the right time, not the noise.
- **How to identify / use:** ask whether a given gap or candle is on the path to the draw. Example of an extra: a tiny FVG that forms before the swing low has even been broken ("a common gap") is unimportant. It would become salient only if price had broken below that low.
- **Example in this video:** leading candle = the macro-time candle that creates a SIBI after price returns to the first FVG; supporting = the next candle reaching the CE of that SIBI; extras = the small FVG inside the consolidation before the low is taken.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:25](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1345) leading man/woman candlestick · [0:26:20](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1580) why the tiny FVG is an extra · [0:34:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2064) supporting actors that use earlier leads
- **Nuance / caveats:** an analogy, not a formal concept, but it answers "why did he pick that FVG?" (because it was a leading candle in the plot, tied to the draw and to time).

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Dealing range defined by PD array and liquidity, with equilibrium inefficiency  (aliases: the range, equilibrium inside the range, "plot twist")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - After price sells from the first presented FVG into a new (minor) sell-side low, you define the range from that PD array (the high) to the new low that was just taken. "Defined simply by time and my PD arrays": no volume profile, point of control or value area involved.
  - The retracement after the minor sell-side raid has an upper limit: the equilibrium (midpoint) of that range, and there should be an inefficiency (a SIBI) sitting around that midpoint. Extend that gap through, and price comes back to it, then "the story is still the same". Retracements people read as a short-term low and reversal are only plot twists that reach to the equilibrium.
  - Later, that same equilibrium SIBI is revisited at a time period and used as resistance (price comes up to it, then sells off to new minor sell side).
- **How to use:** after a shallow run on minor sell side, project how high the retracement can go by the midpoint of the range and the FVG there; use this to avoid being tricked into a long.
- **Example in this video:** range from the high of the first presented FVG (the premium array it sold off) down to the minor sell-side low; mid-range holds a SIBI; price retraces to it then sells to a new minor low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:07](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1627) range defined from the PDA to the new sell-side low · [0:28:46](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1726) midpoint inefficiency and "no overlap with volume profile" · [0:29:34](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1774) retracement only goes to the equilibrium FVG · [0:30:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1824) why that gap was chosen: middle of the range defined by liquidity and PDAs
- **Nuance / caveats:** "time distortion" (grinding consolidation) is mentioned as the context where the market stalls before delivering. This reinforces earlier teaching of equilibrium as the retracement limit.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Reclaimed FVG
body:
- **Kind:** example only / light coinage
- **What ICT says:** an old SIBI that price returned to and used (i.e. an FVG already used earlier as a reaction point) is described as a "reclaimed fair value gap" and is being utilized again in a range consolidation, with price displacing lower only once the macro time arrives.
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:12](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2112) old SIBI = reclaimed FVG
- **Nuance / caveats:** only one sentence; no further definition given.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Macros used in this review  (aliases: 9:50–10:10 macro, 10:50–11:10 macro, lunch macro)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** he points at specific algorithmic time windows. 9:50 to 10:10 ET: price returns to the first presented FVG and creates the leading SIBI. 10:50 to 11:10 ET: after sideways grinding, price displaces lower (the first run is at the nearby sell side, then it carries on to the overnight lows); he teases people who say that macro "supposedly doesn't exist". 11:30 to 1:30 ET is a lunch window with a "sneaky" lunch macro. Moves tend to start on macro time.
- **How to use:** time first, then price: wait until time agrees with the price level before expecting delivery.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:25](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1345) 9:50–10:10 macro · [0:33:37](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2017) 10:50–11:10 macro, displacement · [0:35:12](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2112) displacement only starts once the macro arrives
- **Nuance / caveats:** the 10:50–11:10 window is not highlighted on his chart ("you do it on your chart"), but he gives the times explicitly.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Lunch avoidance and PM session  (aliases: 11:30–1:30 no-trade for beginners)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** if you are brand new, do not trade between 11:30 AM and 1:30 PM ET, because you will get chopped up and the lunch macro is sneaky. Do nothing, come back at 1:30 PM ET, and watch how price sets up the PM session.
- **Example in this video:** PM, approximately 1:30 ET: market rallies up and approaches the first presented FVG again (also, as he explains later, the top of a daily PD array: see Suspension block), then sells off. Minor sell side with relative equal lows forms, and an old RTH AM-session low sits below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:40:00](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2400) don't trade 11:30–1:30 if new · [0:40:48](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2448) wait until 1:30 PM, PM setup begins
- **Nuance / caveats:** the rule is explicitly for beginners ("if you're brand new"); he does not say he himself avoids it.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Partials  (aliases: taking partials at liquidity)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** he defends taking partials against people who say not to. The relative equal lows in the PM session are "perfect candidates" to take a partial if you are short from up above. After the speed develops (elongated candles below those lows), price then reaches for the next sell side (the old AM-session RTH low).
- **How to use:** take a partial at nearby, obvious liquidity (relative equal lows), then watch for acceleration (elongated candles through them) as confirmation that the further pool is the target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:41:36](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2496) speed below the lows = reach for the next sell side · [0:42:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2544) partials defended
- **Nuance / caveats:** no percentage for the partial is given.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Inversion FVG as a small-timeframe Model 2022 entry  (aliases: iFVG, "model 22")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (example only; restates old teaching)
- **What ICT says:** in the PM drop, an inversion FVG is the last major upside displacement (an FVG) before price hits a premium array and folds over. That sequence, he says, is his Model 2022 "on a very small time frame", and it is the first FVG after the rotation over. Afterward, price uses the iFVG's CE, sells off, uses another FVG, sells off again, consolidates (a bearish pennant), breaks lower and fizzles into the low into the close.
- **How to identify:** rally into a premium array (first presented FVG / daily PD array), last up-displacement FVG becomes the one price trades back through (inversion), and the first FVG after the reversal is the entry zone.
- **How to use:** short from the iFVG (CE used as the reaction point); partials at the relative equal lows; target the AM-session low and then the rest of the day's delivery.
- **Example in this video:** PM session, 1-minute: price rallies into the first presented FVG, a small iFVG forms as price folds over, price retraces to its CE then drops, takes the low, clears the RTH AM-session low, dives, consolidates in a bearish pennant, breaks, and fizzles into the close.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:24](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2544) "this is an inversion fair value gap"; "model 2022 on a very small time frame" · [0:43:12](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2592) drops, clears the AM-session low · [0:43:59](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2639) bearish pennant, breaks lower, fizzles into the close
- **Nuance / caveats:** he stresses nothing here is new teaching: "It's my old stuff being presented in a way where it helps you build a narrative."

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Suspension block  (aliases: ICT suspension block; daily-chart PD array released in 2025)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage (new PD array)
- **What ICT says:**
  - A PD array he released in 2025, an inefficiency that sits between candles. The usual view is to take one candle's low to another candle's high as the inefficiency. That is an inefficiency, but he says the real inefficiency is framed by the volume imbalance on each side (volume imbalance and volume imbalance), i.e. from one candle's open to another candle's close. The candle in between is what is highlighted as the suspension block. (caption is unclear on exactly which candles' open and close; this is the best reading.)
  - It is "another form of buy-side / sell-side inefficiency" (BISI/SIBI).
  - It is explicitly not a liquidity void. A liquidity void is where there was no trading at all, an actual gap with no buying or selling. That is the only void that exists in price.
  - A bearish daily suspension block's high acts as a premium array on the daily chart: price rallies into it and is sent lower.
- **How to identify:** on the daily chart, find a bearish-delivery inefficiency in which the body-to-body imbalances (volume imbalances) frame a candle. The block's high is that candle's open (as stated when he points at the top of the block on the day).
- **How to use:** put the daily suspension block on the chart as a premium array. Watch how deeply an intraday rally into it gets: if price reaches only the lower portion, the market is weak and it will go lower; he notes that on this day price ran into the upper quadrant, then sliced down, and the implication is a reach for the half of the daily range below (see Daily context).
- **Example in this video:** the reviewed day: price (after dropping) retraces up against the high of the daily suspension block and the first presented FVG, then sells off. At around 1:30 PM ET price makes a small run up to the top of the daily suspension block (that candle's open), "going up to go down", then falls, which he says many people were caught off guard by because they only watch 1-second to 15-minute charts.
- **Timestamps:** [0:44:48](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2688) released in 2025, introduces it on the daily chart · [0:45:38](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2738) framed by volume imbalances; not a liquidity void · [0:46:29](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2789) retrace to the high of the daily SB = premium array · [0:48:05](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2885) 1:30 run up to the top of the SB
- **Nuance / caveats:** several lines in this section are caption-garbled ("lower upper quadrant", "slices through it", "respecting only the lower half... indicating bearishness is weak"). Treat the quadrant-by-quadrant reading rules as provisional; the secure content is the definition, the not-a-void statement, and the premium-array use.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Liquidity void (strict definition)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** a liquidity void is only a real gap where there is no trading at all, "no buying and selling in there". A suspension block, FVG or volume imbalance is not a void; each is an inefficiency with trading on both sides.
- **Timestamps:** [0:45:38](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2738)
- **Nuance / caveats:** tightens how the term "void" should be used in the playbook ("the only void that exists in price").

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Top-down: always check the daily chart  (aliases: higher-timeframe narrative, daily half-range target, NWOG)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** a one-, five-, 15-minute or one-hour chart alone will not tell you why price rallied and sold. You must do proper top-down analysis and at least consult the daily chart. Without it "you are trading blind" no matter how hot your recent results. On the day, the daily chart showed the suspension block (premium array) and a range whose half (blue line) was the lower reference; price fell just short of it. A new week opening gap (NWOG) was present that week and price dropped off nearby.
- **How to use:** look at what the daily chart is offering (premium or discount array nearby, midpoint of the daily range, opening gap) before engaging intraday.
- **Timestamps:** [0:43:59](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2639) why it ran up then sold: need top-down · [0:44:48](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2688) "trading blind" without the daily · [0:48:52](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2932) half of the daily range as the next reach; NWOG present
- **Nuance / caveats:** exact NWOG price, date and relation to the move are not clearly stated.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Pre-market read (7:00 to 9:30 ET)  (aliases: pre-market session, "the 7 o'clock hour")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (process)
- **What ICT says:** he uses 7:00 to 9:30 ET as a diagnostic. If he can call every candle's fluctuation in pre-market and feels in rhythm, he expects to "destroy the opening range" and often catch the low or high of the day. If he cannot, he waits until about 10:00 ET and lets the first 30 minutes trade. Pre-market behavior sets the tone for how the market should deliver after the 9:30 bell; there is "no better resource".
- **Example in this video:** price ran straight up in pre-market just to reach the old Dec 23 displacement FVG formed after a turtle soup, which then supplied the narrative for the day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:51:18](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=3078) pre-market 7:00–9:30; if dialed in → opening range; otherwise wait till 10:00 · [0:52:06](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=3126) pre-market sets the tone · [0:52:55](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=3175) ran to the old Dec 23 FVG
- **Nuance / caveats:** the overnight lows rule uses midnight–7:00 ET; this uses 7:00–9:30 ET. Two different windows for two different jobs.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Narrative trumps market structure; time distortion  (aliases: "time then price")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / philosophy
- **What ICT says:** "Narrative trumps market structure." Time distortion (the algorithm holding price in consolidation or delaying delivery until the right time) can break the current market structure, so moves "jump out of nowhere" for people who only use structure and who then complain that the chop is real. His summary: "it's all a derivative of time first, then price", and price is always drawing to one of the four targets (see Casting a vision).
- **Timestamps:** [0:39:11](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2351) narrative > structure; time distortion · [0:40:00](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=2400) time then price
- **Nuance / caveats:** frames structure as secondary to the draw and the clock. It does not say structure is useless.

title: From Vision To Execution
head: Tools are unnecessary: everything is in OHLC candles
body:
- **Kind:** rule / philosophy
- **What ICT says:** footprint, depth of market, level 2, volume profile, order-book heat maps are not needed: "everything is available in these open, high, low, and close candlesticks". What you wait for is the time for the candles to perform. The range was defined purely by time and PD arrays, with no overlap with POC/value area/volume profile.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:46](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1486) gimmick tools vs candles · [0:25:34](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1534) everything is in OHLC · [0:28:46](https://youtu.be/rXgEMIJ1fQg?t=1726) no overlap with volume profile

title: ICT Mentorship 2022 Introduction
head: 2022 Mentorship model (framing)  (aliases ICT uses: "stripped down version", "stripping it down to its chrome", "a model my daughter could look at")
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The 2022 YouTube mentorship will teach one simple model with few moving parts, no "bells and whistles" or advanced theories, keeping everything germane to that model. His advanced private-mentorship concepts create exceptional traders but most students get bogged down and suffer analysis paralysis ("kid in the candy store"). The model is meant to show both what to do and when NOT to do something.
- **How to identify:** n/a (course framing).
- **How to use:** Learn one model and its setups; setups repeat with common characteristics but are never carbon copies.
- **Example in this video:** None beyond the ES live-account trades below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:38](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=158) — built for his daughter, minimal moving parts; [0:03:26](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=206) — advanced content causes analysis paralysis; [0:04:12](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=252) — stripped-down version, mentorship style, traded with index futures.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicitly narrower than his private mentorship content; he says he will also show how to scale the concepts to any timeframe and that forex traders can still use them.

title: ICT Mentorship 2022 Introduction
head: Three stages: yearner → learner → earner
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage
- **What ICT says:** Everyone is treated as a "green horn" yearning to learn. The mentorship moves students from yearning to structured learning and, at their own discretion and timing, to earning. He will not take suggestions on how to teach differently. Many who start will not complete it out of frustration.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Treat the mentorship as a structured learning process; do the drills/homework he assigns.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:33](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=393) — three stages, treated as green horns; [0:08:08](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=488) — yearning to learning to earning.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Planned length about 3–4 months (including March 2022, when he uploads nothing), not a full year.

title: ICT Mentorship 2022 Introduction
head: Draw on liquidity — study prompts, not trade setups  (aliases ICT uses: "where price will likely draw to next")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He will draw on charts beforehand where he expects price to draw to next; this is for study, not a trade setup and not an enticement to take a live trade. Students must not grow dependent on him calling moves; independent decision-making is the goal so results (good or bad) are owned by the student.
- **How to identify:** Levels he marks before the fact.
- **How to use:** Anticipate on your own, then check yourself against what he reveals or reviews.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:22](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=442) — not setups, study where price will draw; [0:09:43](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=583) — avoid codependency.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: ICT Mentorship 2022 Introduction
head: Buy-side / sell-side liquidity (liquidity matrix)  (aliases ICT uses: "buy stops", "liquidity matrix")
body:
- **Kind:** definition (brief)
- **What ICT says:** Markets work within a liquidity matrix: buy side and sell side. His charts stay simple: a line for a level he wants to see breached, and a line for a level he wants price to reach up into. Buy stops sit above a high.
- **How to identify:** Highs (buy stops above) and lows (sell stops below) marked with simple lines; avoid "chart graffiti".
- **How to use:** Target the resting liquidity (e.g. buy stops above a high for a long).
- **Example in this video:** ES 2m long targeting buy stops above a prior high (see OTE concept).
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:11](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1451) — above this high is buy stops, targeting into that; [0:26:33](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1593) — simple lines; liquidity matrix of buy side and sell side.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** To be taught in detail later in the series.

title: ICT Mentorship 2022 Introduction
head: Optimal Trade Entry (OTE) — "forgiving entries"
body:
- **Kind:** example only / rule
- **What ICT says:** He calls the long shown a "very very simple strategy, optimal trade entry". You do not need to be highly precise about entries; you need to be precise about directional bias and where price is reaching for. He will teach "forgiving entries".
- **How to identify:** Not defined in this video.
- **How to use:** Prioritize bias and draw on liquidity over pinpoint entry price.
- **Example in this video:** ES (E-mini S&P 500, March 2022 contract), 2-minute chart, live TD Ameritrade account: two shorts the previous session (entry and cover shown, plus a small scalp), no further trades after; then a long entry later, exit into buy stops above a high. Only a few handles captured. Account shown at about $23,694.11.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:33](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1353) — ES March 2022, 2m chart, short entries/covers; [0:23:22](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1402) — long setup "one of the setups you're going to learn"; [0:24:11](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1451) — OTE, forgiving entries, precise bias.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Entry/exit prices are not stated in the transcript (only pointed at on chart).

title: ICT Mentorship 2022 Introduction
head: Micro vs mini / futures vs CFDs (contract specs)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** ES handle = 4 ticks (e.g. 4567 to 4568); $50 per handle, $12.50 per tick on the E-mini S&P. Margin for one ES contract roughly $12,000–13,000 (his estimate). Micros (MES, also micro Nasdaq) pay $5 per handle with much lower margin, so you can graduate up over time. Outside the US you could trade a CFD (e.g. US500 via MT4), but for US traders this is illegal because it does not go through a regulated exchange; US traders must use futures.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** If margin prevents trading ES, trade micros; scale up later.
- **Example in this video:** ES tick/handle math.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:11](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1451) — handle = 4 ticks, $50/handle, $12.50/tick; [0:24:58](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1498) — 25 handles; micros $5/handle; [0:25:46](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1546) — CFDs, illegal for US traders.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Margin figure is approximate ("12 13,000 or whatever it is").

title: ICT Mentorship 2022 Introduction
head: Weekly objective: one good setup / 25 handles a week
body:
- **Kind:** rule (target framing)
- **What ICT says:** If you can find at least one good setup a week and take about 25 handles a week out of ES you can do very well; no need to hit home runs. Framing goal: an "income-based" hypothetical strategy, e.g. cover a $1,500 rent/mortgage or a car payment over time, not right away.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Set modest, repeatable weekly goals.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:58](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1498) — 25 handles out of ES; [0:27:21](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1641) — one good setup a week, 25 handles a week; [0:28:08](https://youtu.be/kt6V4ai60fI?t=1688) — cover bills over time.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He does not promise perfection or every-day consistency; aim is consistency over a week.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Weekly bias — "will the weekly candle expand higher or lower?"
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Before each new trading week (preferably on the weekend), decide whether the next weekly candle is more likely to go higher or lower. You are NOT trying to predict the weekly close; only which side the weekly range expands toward. This sets your initial bias for the week.
- **How to identify:** Look at the weekly chart and the prior weekly candle; consider where price is drawing (an old low/high not yet broken) plus context: seasonality, macro news (Fed rate hikes), earnings season, and the "underlying tone" seen on the daily chart.
- **How to use:** If expecting lower, look only for setups that sell (buy stops run first). The move may happen in the first half of the week or a single day; if you get your setup in that, "you're done" for the week.
- **Example in this video:** NQ March 2022 contract (TradingView symbol NQH2022), weekly chart: bearish expectation for reasons of seasonal tendency to decline at that time of year, Fed expected to raise rates, earnings-season volatility, and a heavy tone; drawing toward an unbroken old weekly/daily low expected to be targeted on Sunday's open into Monday.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:22](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=742) — read the next weekly candle before the week; [0:13:11](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=791) — reasons: seasonality, Fed, earnings; [0:15:32](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=932) — the weekly expansion may be one day; don't trade every session; [0:16:20](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=980) — weekly candle sets the initial bias.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He did not expect the whole range delivered in one week; what matters is the direction of expansion.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Draw on liquidity (DOL)  (aliases ICT uses: "where it's drawing to", "paperclip and magnet")
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Price is like a paperclip; price levels and seasonality act like a magnet pulling it toward certain levels. Price draws to one of two things: stops (liquidity) or an imbalance. Above old highs = buy stops; below old lows = sell stops. Speed and magnitude of the move to a level is learned by experience ("a feel"), not transferable.
- **How to identify:** On the daily chart, mark swing highs/lows (where liquidity sits) and imbalances. Most of the draw on liquidity "is predominantly found on" the daily timeframe, so most analysis should be linked to it.
- **How to use:** Define the weekly direction, then use the daily chart to see where you are within the weekly range expansion and which short-term lows/highs (stops) are the next draw.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily: in a weak market, each short-term low has sell stops beneath it; the old daily low is the larger objective.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:45](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=885) — paperclip/magnet analogy; [0:16:20](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=980) — daily chart: swing highs/lows, draw on liquidity found mostly on daily; [0:17:08](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1028) — draws to stops or an imbalance.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He explicitly says this is not auction theory and his boxes are not supply and demand.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Buy-side / sell-side liquidity and the stop hunt before a big move  (aliases ICT uses: "buy stops", "sell stops", "sucker play", "engineered liquidity", "inducing shorts")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Before any significant price move lower, always anticipate some measure of a stop hunt on buy stops / a short-term high taken out; when expecting higher prices, generally a short-term low and its sell stops get taken before a pronounced rally. Says this occurs almost daily. When buy stops are run, they become market orders flooding in, giving smart money (who want to sell high) willing buyers as counterparty.
- **How to identify:** Consolidation forming a short-term high and short-term low; relative equal highs (retail "resistance" with stops above); traders who were short trail stops just above the recent high.
- **How to use:** In a bearish week, wait for the run above the old high (buy stops), then look for the entry signature on lower timeframes. Do not sell simply because highs were taken.
- **Example in this video:** NQ hourly/15m, Friday (last day of the week): bearish all week, sell-off Thursday, overnight consolidation. Friday: price first trades down below the consolidation low (sell stops), inducing breakout shorts ("sucker play"), then runs up through relative equal highs/old highs (buy stops above where shorts trailed their stops). That run is the setup context.
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:19](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1219) — consolidation; sell stops taken first to induce shorts; [0:22:01](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1321) — buy stops as counterparty for smart money; note: anticipate a stop hunt before a significant move; [0:23:39](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1419) — relative equal highs, retail resistance; [0:25:18](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1518) — larger pool above in sync with downtrend.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says "algorithms" attack the buy-stop pool; he rejects the buying/selling pressure explanation in favor of liquidity.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Relative equal highs/lows  (aliases ICT uses: "cleanly delivered", "relative equal highs")
body:
- **Kind:** definition (applied)
- **What ICT says:** Two highs at basically the same level are seen by retail as resistance; textbooks say place a buy stop just above clear resistance when short. These levels hold briefly, but most of the time the market runs them before a meaningful move.
- **How to identify:** Two or more highs (or lows) at nearly the same price.
- **How to use:** Treat as an engineered liquidity pool and a likely target before the real move.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15m Friday: high right before the drop matches an earlier high; price runs through them.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:39](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1419); [0:24:29](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1469).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Market Structure Shift / break in market structure  (aliases ICT uses: "break in market structure", "market structure break", "short-term low being broken")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** After the buy stops are run, look for a short-term swing low to be broken. A swing low = a candle with a higher low on its left and a higher low on its right (three-candle swing low). A break below it is "key" and is the specific signature that tips the market's hand. Says it forms almost every day, many times per week, in one direction or the other.
- **How to identify:** On the lower timeframe (1–3m for indices), after the stop run, mark the short-term low that formed on the way up; wait for price to break below it.
- **How to use:** Only after the MSS do you look for the imbalance (FVG) to sell into.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2m, Friday: after running the old/relative equal highs, price creates short-term lows then breaks below them with a large down candle.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:43](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1663) — break in market structure; [0:28:31](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1711) — don't rush in after the high is taken, wait for the signature; [0:42:59](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2579) — swing low definition.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He points to other YouTube lessons on market structure breaks.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Fair Value Gap (FVG) / imbalance  (aliases ICT uses: "imbalance", "buy-side imbalance", "fair value gap")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / entry model
- **What ICT says:** An imbalance is where one candle moves in one direction only and the candle before's high and candle after's low don't overlap (for an up candle); price only went one way there and nothing offset it, so it has to be "efficiently delivered" on the opposite side (the algorithm must deliver equal price in the other direction to book it). He introduced "fair value gap" in 2016. Mark the first candle's low and third candle's high (for a bearish gap) as the FVG.
- **How to identify:** Three candles; the middle candle's range is not overlapped by candle 1's wick and candle 3's wick. Bearish FVG: candle 1 low above candle 3 high.
- **How to use:** After the MSS, when price trades back up into the FVG, sell short. If you can't get it on that timeframe, drop to a lower one (e.g., from 3m to 1m, or from 5m to 1m) and find an FVG there. A bullish (buy-side) imbalance below in discount is also a target, because price wants to rebalance it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2m, Friday: the big displacement candle breaking the short-term low leaves an FVG between that candle sequence; the next candle opens, trades higher and stops right in the gap: sell entry. The downside target was a buy-side imbalance (one up candle, prior candle high vs next candle low) located just below the 50% of the day's range near old lows; price traded down into it and "completely closed" it with down-closing price.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:56](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1076) — imbalance defined; [0:29:18](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1758) — price goes up into the area: sell; scale down timeframes; [0:30:04](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1804) — "fair value gap", introduced 2016; [0:38:04](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2284) — buy-side imbalance as target, closed in.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says 1m, 2m, 3m charts are best for finding imbalances in indices because HFT algorithms operate at timeframes up to about 3 minutes (often 15s/30s/45s/60s intervals).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Displacement entry, stop placement, and chasing  (aliases ICT uses: "sell into the gap", "don't chase")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Enter as price trades up into the FVG; it feels scary to sell while price is rising, but that is what you want (retail wants "confirmation" and comes in late). If price has started moving lower you can still get in near the FVG, but once a short-term low is taken out you are chasing; market orders there risk slippage and larger risk. Stop: above the swing high (the stop-run high) or above the FVG-forming candle's high, whichever fits your risk parameters. Alternative: a sell stop order in the gap candle to trip you in, with stop above that candle's high (may be too wide).
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Use micros while learning: full contract leverage on NQ can "burn you" if price moves 100 points quickly.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2m short "at 14,800" (he abbreviates "798"), covered at "675" (about 14,675) as price hit the top of the target imbalance range, about 120-130 handles.
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:26](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1946) — entry and stop options; [0:33:13](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1993) — can still get in near the area; [0:34:02](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2042) — chasing, slippage; sell when the candle is going up; [0:43:47](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2627) — sell stop entry alternative.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Premium / discount / equilibrium (dealing range split at 50%)  (aliases ICT uses: "split the range", "50 level", "liquidity matrix")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Take the current range (low of day to high of day so far) and split it with a Fibonacci 50% level. Above 50% is a premium (expensive, "algorithmic stance"); below 50% is a discount. Markets can stay in premium a while. When short, check where you are in the range: selling an FVG in premium, the algorithm will seek discount; it reprices lower regardless of buyers (buyers get "squeezed"; "bear squeeze/bull squeeze" are excuses for not understanding the algorithm).
- **How to identify:** Fib from high to low (or low to high) of the day's range; 50% level.
- **How to use:** Sell in premium, target liquidity/imbalance in discount (below 50%) — sell stops below an old low and nearby imbalances.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2m Friday: FVG short formed in the premium of the day's range; price drove below the 50% level, raided sell stops under a low and filled the buy-side imbalance there.
- **Timestamps:** [0:34:49](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2089) — liquidity matrix; range low/high of day; [0:35:36](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2136) — 50% Fib, premium vs discount; [0:36:26](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2186) — algorithm in a sell program reprices lower; [0:37:17](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2237) — sell stops below 50% as counterparty to cover.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The day's range here is "low of the day and high of the day thus far".

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Targets: low-hanging fruit  (aliases ICT uses: "closest target", "opposing high or low")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Aim for the closest target: an old low or an imbalance (when short). Don't get fancy targeting the lowest low; the market can deny it. Take the easiest target and let the market go further without you. When covering a short you need willing sellers at a low price — they sit with sell stops below lows.
- **How to identify:** Nearest old low / imbalance in discount.
- **How to use:** Exit at the first logical draw; he exited as price hit the top of the target imbalance.
- **Example in this video:** He held the old daily low as a bigger objective but didn't expect it that day, so he stopped trading after the first target; in hindsight wishes he had left a small runner.
- **Timestamps:** [0:38:54](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2334) — efficient delivery, didn't participate rest of day; [0:47:49](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=2869) — low-hanging fruit.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Accept leaving money on the table.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Time window: 8:30–11:00 ET  (aliases ICT uses: "sweet little spot in the morning")

- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He likes watching index futures around 8:30 AM to 11:00 AM New York time; usually there's a setup he can find in there.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 2
head: Top-down timeframe sequence (this episode's version)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Weekly (bias) → daily (liquidity/draw; transpose daily levels down) → hourly (week framed from Monday midnight NY to Friday) → 15m (stop run levels marked with short line segments) → 2m (1–3m) for MSS and FVG entry. Intraday = anything below daily (4H, 1H, 5m, 3m, 2m, 1m).
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** While developing, draw liquidity levels on your chart to keep your bearings; he himself watches a naked chart.
- **Example in this video:** The NQ walk-through above.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:43](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1123) — hourly framework, week from Monday midnight NY; [0:22:51](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1371) — 15m line segments; draw levels while learning; [0:26:05](https://youtu.be/tmeCWULSTHc?t=1565) — why 2m chart.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Market Structure Shift (MSS) vs market structure break  (aliases ICT uses: "intraday market structure shift", "shift in market structure", "break in market structure")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** For intraday use he says "shift", not "break". An intraday MSS signals a likely intraday draw up or down; it may produce just an intraday leg and the opposing high can still be taken the same day. "Market structure break" means more in context (can lead to prolonged multi-day movement). You do not force or anticipate ahead of the shift; you wait for the evidence. He says this is the complete, algorithmic definition — nothing else is needed.
- **How to identify:** (1) Price runs liquidity first: trades below an old low (sell stops under retail "support": a double bottom or single low) or above old highs/relative equal highs. (2) The short-term swing high (for bullish) formed right before the low is taken out — a swing high = a candle with lower highs on both sides. (3) The candle that trades through that short-term high: it does NOT need to close above it. The break is significant ONLY if liquidity was taken first.
- **How to use:** After the MSS candle closes, watch the next candle: when it closes, has an FVG been created? That FVG is the earliest place to trade. Bearish mirror: after buy stops are taken, a short-term swing low is broken and an FVG forms; sell the retrace into it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ March 2022 15m (homework chart): old low ~14,600 with sell stops below it; relative equal highs ~14,820–14,860 (caption gives both) with buy stops above. 2m chart same day: price dives under ~14,600 into sell stops, then rallies through the short-term swing high formed before that low ("light bulb" candle) — bullish MSS; the next candles leave an FVG, price trades down into it and "takes off" to run buy stops above the highs and through the relative equal highs. Then above the equal highs, a swing low forms and is broken — bearish MSS (because buy stops were taken); rally into the FVG = short, targeting sell stops below lows and an imbalance below the 50% of the range.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:50](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=110) — anticipate MSS at the liquidity points, don't force it; [0:02:39](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=159) — shift vs break; [0:06:35](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=395) — short-term high taken is significant only if price ran sell stops; [0:13:45](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=825) — need not close above; watch next candle for FVG.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He notes there are ways to sell right above the highs (or buy at the low) without waiting for the MSS, but says students won't have that skill yet. HFT algorithms use market structure on 3m/2m/1m and sub-minute (45s/30s/15s) charts.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Buy-side / sell-side liquidity (marking the pools)  (aliases ICT uses: "buy stops", "sell stops", "relative equal highs", "retail support/resistance")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Old low → sell stops below. Relative equal highs → buy stops above. If equal highs exist and they are higher than an older single high, he uses the equal highs as the reference. Liquidity location is pure logic: retail places stops beyond obvious support/resistance. Buying/selling "pressure" has no bearing on where price goes. Highs left just below a level "building up more interest" engineer liquidity for a later run.
- **How to identify:** Mark the 15m buy-side and sell-side liquidity pools, then drop to 3m/2m/1m.
- **How to use:** The run into these pools is the precondition for the MSS. When the market runs buy stops, smart money that bought lower sells to "high-seeking buyers".
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15m: shaded sell-stop area below ~14,600; relative equal highs above.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:04](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=64) — old low and relative equal highs; [0:12:56](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=776) — sell-stop zone below 14,600; [0:28:03](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1683) — highs building interest = engineering liquidity.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Fair Value Gap (FVG) as MSS entry; stacked FVGs rule
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:** FVG = a candle with one single pass up, and the next candle's low doesn't fully overlap the prior candle's high (gap remains). The candle after the MSS that forms an FVG is "at the earliest" where you'd trade. When there are two FVGs, one above the other (for a long), he lets price trade down into the lower one, sacrificing that better entry; if it trades into the lower one and comes back up into the higher (first) FVG, he enters there and expects the lower one won't be retraded. If price runs up into the target zone first, before retracing to the entry FVG, he nixes the trade and sits out.
- **How to identify:** After an MSS, the gap left by the displacement candle.
- **How to use:** Enter on the retrace into the FVG (limit or market). During the trade, a dip back into the lower FVG is permissible; if price overlaps the entire lower FVG and goes lower, close the trade (save the stop). Watch whether candle bodies stay inside the FVG (sign of accumulation).
- **Example in this video:** Live NQ 1m, Jan 25, 2022: bullish MSS, green-box FVG with a smaller FVG just below it. Price dips into the lower FVG, leaving wicks, comes back into the green FVG; he buys at market. Price stabs down once more into the wicks (he says they took it down to accumulate more longs, not selling pressure); max drawdown about $455. Then rallies to the bottom of the pink rectangle (an imbalance in premium) where he flattens: +$1,190, account $27,915.11.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:45](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=825) — FVG after MSS, earliest entry; [0:41:38](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2498) — two FVGs rule; [0:43:12](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2592) — nix trade if target hit first; [0:45:36](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2736) — permissible dip into lower FVG; close if it overlaps fully.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says he only draws these on the chart for teaching; trades a naked chart.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Order block = change in the state of delivery  (aliases ICT uses: "one continuous order block", "consecutive bearish order block", "change in the state of delivery")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** He invented the order block (first mentioned on BabyPips in 2010; taught one-on-one since 1996). Not every down-close candle is a bullish OB (or up-close a bearish OB). A series of consecutive down-close candles is "all one continuous order block"; the reference is the opening price of the first candle of that series, extended out in time. The order block "is just a change in the state of delivery": while price is delivered higher via a run of up-close candles, that run began at the first candle's open; when price trades below that open, the state of delivery changes (from offering buy side to offering sell side, i.e., now seeking sell stops), and the algorithm "remembers" that level, making it sensitive. Mirror for down-close candles: when their opening price is violated upward, it changes to offering buy side and seeks buy stops.
- **How to identify:** A high-probability OB: (1) it sits inside a liquidity pool (e.g., the down-close series inside the sell-stop zone), (2) has an FVG/gap, (3) there was a market structure shift. "Takes liquidity + gap + MSS."
- **How to use:** Bullish: buy limit at the opening price of the down-close candle series, located inside the FVG, plus about 3 pips "or whatever for spread". Bearish: mirror with up-close candles.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2m: series of down-close candles inside the sell-stop pool below 14,600; their opening price lies inside the FVG = buy limit; price runs to buy stops above highs. NQ 1m: two up-close candles before a drop form one consecutive bearish OB (open extended out), with gap, liquidity taken and MSS: "high probability" bearish OB.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:32](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=872) — down-close series = one order block; [0:15:20](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=920) — open of series inside FVG = buy limit; [0:23:16](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1396) — bearish OB with gap, liquidity and MSS; [0:24:06](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1446) — OB = change in state of delivery.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the root of the later "CISD" concept. He says that's all he'll give at the free level. He criticizes others for treating every opposite-colored candle as an OB.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Price delivery by algorithm (not buying/selling pressure)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** When price rallies, the HFT orders hitting the market are volume, not the cause; the price-delivery algorithm keeps offering price higher. Explains slippage: market buy expected at 14,662 filled at 14,664 = negative slippage; filled better = positive slippage. "Bull squeeze/bear squeeze" are cop-outs.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Don't interpret price via pressure/volume; read liquidity and delivery state.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m rally after MSS.
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:55](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1255); [0:21:43](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1303).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Belief statement; he challenges students to verify in charts.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Premium / discount; targets & partials (low-hanging fruit)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** Bearish leg: price goes from premium to below the 50% (equilibrium) of the range into discount, into the gap there. Partials can be taken below each short-term low (sell stops), but don't take them where there's too little movement; reach for the next one. First objective = the high end of the target FVG (the closest candle's low/high), the easiest target; over time grow into holding to see it fill the whole gap.
- **How to identify:** 50% of the leg's high and low; FVG/imbalance below.
- **How to use:** Multiple contracts: scale out at successive sell-stop pools and the FVG in discount. Live trade: exit at the low end of the target rectangle; the ideal is the top, but while learning take the low end.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2m bearish leg to FVG below 50%; live long target = bottom of pink imbalance in premium.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:43](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1063) — targets below; partials; [0:19:20](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1160) — 50% level, first objective in gap, low-hanging fruit; [0:27:16](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1636) — premium to equilibrium to discount; [0:49:07](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2947) — target low end of rectangle.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Timeframe progression 3m → 2m → 1m
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The same MSS/FVG logic appears on 1m with more execution points; a single gap on 2m may appear as two candles on 1m. Progress from 3m to 2m to 1m to find structure and imbalances.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Mark 15m liquidity pools; execute on 3m/2m/1m.
- **Example in this video:** Same NQ day shown on 2m and 1m.
