title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Session highs/lows to mark (killzone-like windows)  (aliases ICT uses: "London session", "New York session", "Asia")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Always use New York local time. London session 2:00–5:00 AM; New York session 7:00–10:00 AM; Asia 7:00–9:00 PM (caption). Mark each session's high and low: the market will probably sweep above those highs or below those lows and create MSS setups. Also mark any intraday high/low forming right before the 9:30 equities open.
- **How to identify:** Session high/low in each window.
- **How to use:** These are the "key highs and lows" whose sweep precedes the MSS.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:52](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=1972); [0:33:40](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2020).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The Asia window as captioned (7–9 PM) is narrower than his usual Asian killzone; treat as stated.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Trading hours, lunch, and afternoon session
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Hours of operation generally 8:30–11:00 AM NY, can extend to noon. He does not tend to trade after noon; the noon hour (lunch) is problematic — don't even look for setups. Wait until 1:00 PM, preferably 1:30–4:00 PM for the afternoon trend; a setup usually forms between 2:00 and 3:00 PM. The afternoon session is outside this mentorship's scope.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Backtest/stalk 8:30–noon ET.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.
- **Timestamps:** [0:33:40](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2020); [0:34:28](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2068).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 3
head: Internal range liquidity (IRL)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** IRL = short-term lows or highs inside a price leg that price is retracing back into; i.e., a short-term high or low with stops above/below it, or an imbalance in that same range.
- **How to identify:** Within the current leg, swing points and FVGs.
- **How to use:** Targets/partials when retracing within a leg.
- **Example in this video:** Sell stops below internal short-term lows in the bearish NQ leg.
- **Timestamps:** [0:34:28](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2068); [0:35:15](https://youtu.be/nQfHZ2DEJ8c?t=2115).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** External range liquidity not defined here.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 4
head: Range, Fibonacci equilibrium and target selection  (aliases ICT uses: "equilibrium", "50 level", "discount")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** Define the range from a chosen low to the high of the run; drop a Fib on it; the 50% is equilibrium. When the run pushes price into premium (expensive), wait for the bearish shift; target a low or an imbalance below equilibrium.
- **How to identify:** Low of the range to high of the range; 50% level.
- **How to use:** Short targets: swing low or imbalance below the 50%; multiple targets can be taken in sequence.
- **Example in this video:** ES March 2022, Wed Jan 26 2022, 2m: range from a marked low to the high; after the run up into premium, a swing low and an imbalance below the 50% serve as targets; price hits the imbalance, bounces, then draws down into the more pronounced low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:56](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=56) — range low to high, Fib, equilibrium; [0:02:35](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=155) — low or imbalance below 50% as target.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 4
head: Market Structure Shift requires an FVG to qualify  (aliases ICT uses: "break in market structure", "bearish market structure shift")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** After the old high is run, wait for a break below a short-term swing low. If that break does NOT create a fair value gap, it doesn't meet the criteria — no trade; wait for the next break. "It's there or it's not"; you can't force it. Waiting forces the market to show its hand.
- **How to identify:** Old high violated (buy stops) → swing low broken by a displacement candle → FVG present between the high and the breaking candle's low.
- **How to use:** Only once the FVG exists, sell when price trades back up into it.
- **Example in this video:** ES 2m Jan 26: first break below the old high's structure had no FVG (skip); price rallied again, then broke down with an MSS and FVG, retraced into it, and sold off into the old low below equilibrium. NQ 5m Jan 27: an initial drop from relative equal highs gave no FVG (no trade); price then ran above an old high (buy-side liquidity), then a swing low was traded through; "soon as this candle trades through it" you have an opportunity; FVG from the high to that candle's low; price rallied back into it (short), broke down, retraced into it again, and reached below equilibrium hitting all targets (lows and the imbalance) and a bit further.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:44](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=104) — breaks down but no FVG; [0:06:34](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=394) — no FVG = doesn't meet criteria; wait; [0:07:22](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=442) — swing low broken, FVG, short.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Consistent with Ep. 3: the opportunity starts as soon as the candle trades through the swing low (no close required).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 4
head: 8:30 AM — start of the hunt  (aliases ICT uses: "8:30 in the morning starts the hunt")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** 8:30 AM (NY time) "starts the hunt" for him: from then he looks for an old/short-term high (or low) to be violated.
- **How to identify:** Previous short-term high/low prior to 8:30.
- **How to use:** After 8:30, watch for the raid on the nearby old high/low, then the MSS + FVG.
- **Example in this video:** ES 2m Jan 26: previous short-term high violated after 8:30, then the swing low break (MSS), FVG retrace short around 4419 covered around 4382 (he rounds "to be not perfect"; about 37 points of opportunity).
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:35](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=155) — 8:30 starts the hunt; [0:03:23](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=203) — MSS, FVG short, target old low; [0:04:11](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=251) — ~4419 to ~4382.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 4
head: Fair Value Gap entry (ideal entry candle)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (applied)
- **What ICT says:** The FVG after the MSS is the ideal entry; the target is the discount old low. Using the FVG candle's high as an entry you technically could have been filled, but he wants you to study the total range available in hindsight.
- **How to identify:** As above.
- **How to use:** Short the retrace into the FVG; cover at old low / imbalance in discount.
- **Example in this video:** ES Jan 26 and NQ Jan 27 (above).
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:11](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=251); [0:04:59](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=299).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 4
head: Top-down: start on 5m and work down
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** For the NQ example, the 5-minute chart is "the timeframe you start with and you work down".
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Identify the range, relative equal highs/old highs on 5m; refine on lower timeframes.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5m, Thu Jan 27 2022.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:46](https://youtu.be/L-ReMHiavPM?t=346).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Earlier episodes used 15m for liquidity pools; here 5m is the start.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Index futures contract months, expiration and rollover  (aliases ICT uses: "front month", "nearby contract", "next month out")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Index futures (ES, NQ, YM) trade only four delivery months: H = March, M = June, U = September, Z = December. TradingView symbol example ESH2022 (TD Ameritrade uses "22"). Expiration is the third Friday of the delivery month; do not trade after expiration. Around the first or second day of the week before expiration, he monitors open interest (e.g., on barchart.com) and trades whichever contract month has the larger open interest (the larger liquidity pool).
- **How to identify:** Compare open interest of front month vs next month out.
- **How to use:** Roll to the next month once its open interest exceeds the front month's.
- **Example in this video:** At recording, March ES was the front month; June open interest only ~57,124 (caption says "million"; caption unclear) so March remains the contract to trade.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:49](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=109) — month codes; [0:02:38](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=158) — third Friday expiration; [0:04:15](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=255) — roll by open interest.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says Asian-range ideas (from his forex teaching) are not applicable to these index markets.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Intraday daily-range template (NY time)  (aliases ICT uses: "frame your day", "daily range on an intraday basis", "boundaries")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Set the chart to New York local time (otherwise calibrations break). Vertical lines at 8:30 AM, noon and 1:00 PM: a morning session, a one-hour New York lunch, and an equal amount of time after lunch. Morning trade: 8:30 (news releases come out at 8:30) to noon, preferably done around 11:00 — he generally avoids new trades after 11:00, wants to be positioned before 11:00 and ride into lunch, then square or take some off if holding through lunch toward the close.
- **How to identify:** Vertical lines 8:30 / 12:00 / 13:00.
- **How to use:** Only look for setups in the morning and afternoon windows.
- **Example in this video:** ES March 2022, day of recording (date not stated).
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:36](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=456) — 8:30 vertical line; [0:08:23](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=503) — morning, lunch hour, afternoon; NY time; [0:10:50](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=650) — morning trade 8:30–noon, preferably before 11.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He had said in Ep. 3 the afternoon was out of scope; here he decides to teach it because of "nonsense on YouTube".

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: New York lunch: no-trade hour  (aliases ICT uses: "lunch hour", "New York lunch")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Noon to 1:00 PM NY is a no-trade period — not even in demo. It can do weird things or simply go sideways; it is usually not clean price action. Swing lows/highs formed during lunch should be ignored for the afternoon structure. "The algorithm reserved the price run until later in the day."
- **How to identify:** 12:00–13:00 ET.
- **How to use:** Stand aside; re-engage after 1:00 (preferably 1:30).
- **Example in this video:** ES: right before lunch price went slightly above highs, traded down, then lunch.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:11](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=551) — noon–1:00 no trade; [0:22:03](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1323) — don't trade it; [0:25:21](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1521) — ignore lunch swing lows.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Pre-8:30 swing high/low as the stop-hunt reference  (aliases ICT uses: "most significant or obvious swing high and swing low prior to 8:30")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** On the 15m chart, find the most significant/obvious swing high and swing low before 8:30. Swing high = three-candle pattern with a lower high on each side; swing low = higher low on each side; candle close direction doesn't matter. Above the swing high = buy-side liquidity; below the swing low = sell-side liquidity. You only need the first one; no need to go back days. Then drop to the 5m chart (first lower timeframe for entry).
- **How to identify:** As above.
- **How to use:** These are the levels a stop run is framed on, the catalyst for the morning setup; the opposite one is the target.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m: pre-8:30 high and low marked with horizontal rays; transposed to 5m.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:16](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=796) — what highs/lows a stop run is framed on; [0:14:05](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=845) — swing high/low three-candle definition; [0:14:53](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=893) — drop to 5m.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** 15m called the "bellwether" timeframe for key highs/lows and FVGs.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: 15m as bellwether timeframe; avoid order blocks in this mentorship
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The 15m is the bellwether timeframe: key highs and lows, imbalances like FVGs. He'll look at order blocks but will try to stay away from them in this mentorship; he has models that don't rely on order blocks. FVG is the main focus because it repeats and is an easy pattern.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Build the framework on 15m, execute on 5m/1m.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:47](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=407).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Ep. 3 explained order blocks; from here the model is FVG-centric.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Three drives pattern into an old high  (aliases ICT uses: "three drives", "three little Indians" from Raschke & Connors' Street Smarts — caption reads "three little endings")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** A swing high, then a higher swing high, then a higher swing high — price pressing up three times — into an old high, on any timeframe. You don't need the third high to take out the old high: each swing high that fails gets sold by bears who put buy stops above the previous high, which keep getting taken, so liquidity is already being run and smart money is establishing shorts. He credits Linda Raschke and Larry Connors' book (Street Smarts) for helping him understand stop hunts.
- **How to identify:** Three ascending swing highs approaching or around an old high/relative equal highs.
- **How to use:** Treat as liquidity being run; then wait for displacement lower and an FVG to sell.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m: old high at about 4514.50 (caption unclear: "45145 / 4514 A5") matched by a later candle's high exactly (relative equal highs) with multiple successively higher short-term highs = three drives.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:42](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=942) — relative equal highs and three drives; [0:16:31](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=991) — three little Indians pattern; [0:17:19](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1039) — third high need not take the old high.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** If there are no stair-stepping higher highs and just one steady run up, anticipate the old high to be taken out (doesn't need to be by much), then look for the energetic move lower.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Displacement  (aliases ICT uses: "elephant in a children's swimming pool", "energetic/animated move", "obvious displacement")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** After price goes above an old high and trades back down, you want an obvious displacement — like an elephant falling into a kiddie pool — not a lethargic or anemic move. Only when displacement occurs do you look for the FVG (the low and high) and sell the retrace into it. Used to answer viewer criticism of a prior example where a swing low "looked violated" but he didn't use it: the break lacked displacement.
- **How to identify:** A pronounced, energetic candle (or candles) breaking the swing low, leaving an FVG; weak drifting breaks don't count.
- **How to use:** Displacement + FVG = trade; anemic break without FVG = wait.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m morning: first poke above the swing high with a weak anemic move lower (no); a wick that snapped back without an FVG (no); a matching high, a slight anemic dip below (no); then it trades up and "smashes down", next candle closes leaving an FVG = short; target the sell-side liquidity below the pre-8:30 swing low; price hits it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:06](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1086) — displacement analogy; [0:18:52](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1132) — then FVG and short; [0:20:25](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1225) — anemic vs energetic; [0:21:15](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1275) — smash down, FVG, target SSL.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Patterns sometimes fail (news events, market rolls over); hence the stop loss and money management.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Afternoon session: 1:30 PM macro, swing high/low stop hunt  (aliases ICT uses: "afternoon trend", "algorithm macro at 1:30")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** 1:30 PM is the earliest he wants to trade the afternoon, because "an algorithm macro" starts running at 1:30 in equities (details beyond this mentorship's scope). After 1:30, look for the first swing high and swing low and apply the same stop-hunt logic as the morning. If your daily bias says the daily candle expands higher, look for an afternoon trade in that direction using the morning logic. Levels that are "too clean" (straight-line edges) tend to be disrupted.
- **How to identify:** First swing high/low forming at/after 1:30 ET.
- **How to use:** Bullish afternoon: wait for a swing low to be violated (a small stop hunt is all that's needed), buy the sell stops, target buy stops above (e.g., the day's high/relative equal highs), and hold for the close.
- **Example in this video:** ES afternoon: the high of day with buy stops above it intact, daily context bullish (an important low formed last week, so the daily is retracing up and shorts are getting squeezed). After 1:30 a swing low is violated (small stop hunt), starting a buy program; buy-side liquidity runs aggressively and price trends into the close with only small retracements. NQ: at 1:30 a swing low almost equal to an earlier low (relative equal lows = retail support) is traded below, with an FVG to the left and relative equal highs (BSL) above; on the 1m the sudden drop below the equal lows ("floor dropped out") is where you buy. His demo entry was near the lowest candle and it rallied.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:47](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1907) — 1:30 swing highs/lows; [0:32:35](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1955) — algorithm macro at 1:30; too-clean levels; [0:33:22](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=2002) — swing low violated starts a buy program; [0:37:25](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=2245) — NQ at 1:30, relative equal lows; [0:39:01](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=2341) — buy the sudden drop.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First mention of "macro" in this series.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Buy program / spooling  (aliases ICT uses: "buy program", "sell program", "spooling")
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A buy program is when the algorithms continuously offer higher prices (spooling), regardless of volume; sometimes volume is good, sometimes not — that inconsistency is the signature of manipulation.
- **How to identify:** After a stop hunt, persistent repricing in one direction with small retracements.
- **How to use:** Get long after the stop hunt and hold rather than scalping small moves.
- **Example in this video:** ES afternoon rally after the 1:30-area swing-low raid.
- **Timestamps:** [0:33:22](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=2002); [0:34:10](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=2050).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Market-on-close acceleration (3:40 / 3:50 / 4:00)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The afternoon has built-in mechanisms that make the market accelerate into the close. A repeating phenomenon typically around 20 minutes to 4 (3:40), 10 minutes to 4 (3:50) and 4:00 PM, based on market-on-close orders; algorithms produce very aggressive pricing, forcing traders to cover/exit; if going up it ramps and accelerates.
- **How to identify:** Lower-timeframe price action in the last 20 minutes.
- **How to use:** Hold afternoon positions in the daily-bias direction into the close.
- **Example in this video:** ES ran aggressively into the close.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:42](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1422) — runs into the close; [0:26:09](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1569) — 3:40, 3:50, 4:00 MOC.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: Daily bias / daily range expansion; daily profiles  (aliases ICT uses: "market profiles", "daily profiles", "morning trend vs afternoon")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Like the weekly candle, ask whether the daily candle (today's or tomorrow's) is more likely to expand higher or lower — not predicting the close. The day is designed with a morning move, the lunch hour, and an afternoon move. Analogy to forex: the morning's low of the day acts like the "London low" in a buy day, then consolidation, then a New York continuation in the same direction — but here all in NY session time. Afternoon possibilities: reversal of the morning; continuation higher; a measured move (afternoon duplicates the morning move, e.g., 200 points morning + 200 afternoon = 400-point range); or morning consolidation then afternoon trend. Consecutive higher swing lows ("every one higher") show accumulation/underpinning.
- **How to identify:** Classify each day's morning (bullish/bearish/consolidation), what preceded it on prior days, and what the afternoon did.
- **How to use:** If expecting expansion higher, take the afternoon setup in that direction; relative equal highs forming in a bullish context = retail resistance building buy-side liquidity to be run.
- **Example in this video:** ES: bullish context (important low last week on the daily, daily retracing higher; crowd expects a crash and keeps shorting); afternoon ran buy stops into the close.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:42](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1422) — morning move, lunch, afternoon design; [0:27:46](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1666) — daily candle expansion; London-low analogy; [0:29:20](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=1760) — afternoon profiles incl. measured move.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Bias and entry techniques to be taught "next week"; not volume profile.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 5
head: The only two patterns you need
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** (1) A swing low (high) is violated in a stop hunt, then price rallies (drops): buy the sell stops. (2) If no swing low is raided, look for a sudden displacement higher, then an FVG; buy when price trades back down into the FVG. No breakers, no order blocks, no "15 gimmicky names" needed; the logic has to be there for either.
- **How to identify:** As described.
- **How to use:** Applies in both morning and afternoon sessions.
- **Example in this video:** ES/NQ afternoon (pattern 1); ES morning short (displacement + FVG).
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:47](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=2147) — buy sell stops; [0:36:34](https://youtu.be/N29ZJ-o31xs?t=2194) — two patterns.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Market efficiency paradigm (smart money vs uninformed retail)  (aliases ICT uses: "market efficiency paradigm", "informed/smart money", "speculative uninformed money")
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Two camps: a small circle of informed/smart money and a large collective of speculative uninformed money, with constant inflow of new money and outflow as accounts blow up. Smart money uses no secret indicators (no stochastics/RSI); it looks at time and price, and time is the most crucial element (time of day builds the likelihood of volatility and of short-term reversals). Smart money "cannibalizes" retail, which is typically wrong on bias and on stop placement. Smart money's question is the narrative: is the daily range going higher, and how — e.g., lower first to sucker shorts and run sell stops so they can acquire longs, then rally into the afternoon/close. Using retail liquidity this way is the market efficiency paradigm.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** "We look to enter longs where retail sells; shorts where retail buys." "We anticipate price seeking opposing liquidity." Don't trade patterns for their own sake, indicator readings, or momentum.
- **Example in this video:** He notes the e-mini markets' 4:00 PM algorithmic run "today" was relentless (one of the times he gave earlier).
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:02](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2) — enter longs where retail sells; [0:01:40](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=100) — price seeks opposing liquidity; two camps; [0:03:16](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=196) — time and price, time most important; [0:06:24](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=384) — narrative: lower first to sucker shorts, then rally.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Trend is your friend" fails at the end of a trend; every rule has an exception — that's experience.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Retail stop-placement conundrum
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Retail shorts either use no stop or don't know where to put it above an old high: too shallow and it's hit prematurely; too high and price spikes through to reach it, then reverses in their direction after a big loss. This is the trap smart money exploits.
- **How to identify:** Old highs/lows with obvious stops just beyond.
- **How to use:** Anticipate runs on those stops before the real move.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.

- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Time-based charts vs DOM / volume profile
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Algorithms operate first under time, so time-based charts are what he uses; depth of market and volume profile are data but the interpretation is private ("a religion").
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** Read institutional order flow via FVGs on time-based charts.
- **Example in this video:** n/a.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Bearish ICT Fair Value Gap (SIBI) — exact definition  (aliases ICT uses: "bearish ICT fair value gap", "institutional order flow pattern")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / entry model
- **What ICT says:** Three-candle formation, preferably after a run above an old high. Candle 1's low is traded below by candle 2; candle 3 makes an extended low below candle 2 but its high does NOT trade back up to candle 1's low. The space between candle 1's low and candle 3's high was traded only by candle 2 — only sell side was offered there, buy side was not efficiently offered. Paint roller analogy: rolling down leaves porous pockets; you roll back up over the same area to fix it — the algorithm returns to the area for efficient delivery. When price trades back into it and you're bearish, that's a short signal. Optimal formations come after a run into buy-side liquidity (above a single high or multiple highs such as a double top); nothing before that candle matters except that an old high was run. The FVG is smart money's "saving grace" if they missed selling above the high.
- **How to identify:** Label candles 1, 2, 3. Gap resides in candle 2. Upper boundary = low of candle 1. Lower boundary = high of candle 3.
- **How to use:** Easiest entry: sell limit just above candle 3's high (one tick, or one to two ticks/handle, "whatever you believe is ideal"; one tick removes guesswork). Stop above candle 1's high or above candle 2's high (whichever you can afford); while learning, use the wider stop. If the risk is too much, don't take the trade.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Feb 3 2022 1m (see worked example).
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:12](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=672) — three-candle rules; [0:12:47](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=767) — paint roller analogy; [0:15:12](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=912) — optimal after run into BSL; [0:16:46](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1006) — boundaries, limit entry, stop.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Experienced students know how to reduce the stop; he deliberately teaches the wide stop to protect beginners. He insists it not be renamed or repackaged.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Bullish ICT Fair Value Gap (BISI)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Mirror image: three candles; low of the FVG = candle 1's high; high of the FVG = candle 3's low; gap formed by candle 2. Expected after a run below an old low or multiple lows (sell-side liquidity), then a break above a short-term high closing above it with energetic displacement.
- **How to identify:** As above.
- **How to use:** Buy the retrace into it (limit just below candle 3's low); stop below candle 1/2.
- **Example in this video:** Used as the first target in the NQ short (a bullish FVG in discount).
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:18](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1338); [0:23:06](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1386).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Market Structure Shift with displacement; displacement high/low range  (aliases ICT uses: "displacement high", "displacement low", "trade idea being birthed")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Bearish MSS: price trades higher, retraces a little, runs above an old high (or the initial short-term high), then breaks below the short-term low — the "new trade idea is born" (still no entry). "Quick" = displacement: energetic, a real willingness to go lower, preferably a big beefy candle that closes below the low; a wick through and back is not convincing (it might go higher and make another high). The high that ran liquidity = displacement high; the low/close beyond the short-term low = displacement low. The FVG to trade must form in between these. No FVG in that range → no trade: wait or check another market (one of them will have it every trading day). Applies on all timeframes. Bullish is reversed.
- **How to identify:** Liquidity run → energetic close beyond short-term swing → look for FVG within displacement high-to-low range.
- **How to use:** Entry at the FVG per the rules above.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Feb 3 1m (below).
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:21](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1101) — bearish MSS concept; [0:19:08](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1148) — quick = displacement, prefer close below; [0:19:55](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1195) — displacement high/low; FVG hunted between; [0:21:29](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1289) — no FVG = no trade; forms every trading day.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines Ep. 3 (where the MSS candle didn't need to close beyond the high): here a close beyond with displacement is preferred/more significant.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: 9:30 open: first run often opposite the real move
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If nothing happened by 9:30, don't assume you missed it: equities open at 9:30 and get busy/volatile; usually (not always) the first run at 9:30 is opposite to the real move.
- **How to identify:** Initial 9:30 move against your daily bias, often building relative equal lows/highs and inducing traders.
- **How to use:** Wait for that move to run its liquidity and for the MSS in your bias direction.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Feb 3: 9:30 volatility creates a low then another low (sell stops building), inducing longs, while the highs above (his interest) stay intact; then the real setup forms.
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:36](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1956); [0:33:23](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2003).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Top-down execution: 15m → 5/4/3/2/1m
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Start on the 15m bellwether naked chart; at 8:30 (news; employment data that day) look left for the first swing high (bearish day) and draw it out in time. Then step down 5m, 4m, 3m, 2m, 1m looking for the MSS + FVG; he has all these charts open across his desk at once. Lower timeframes give tighter entries and more chances.
- **How to identify:** n/a.
- **How to use:** The same FVG may show on 4m, 2m and 1m with the same entry concept.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Feb 3: 4m shows the FVG after the swing low break (entry at candle high, stop above candle 1/swing high); 2m similar; 1m gives three entry chances into the FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:25:31](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1531) — 15m, 8:30, first swing high to the left; [0:26:19](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1579) — step down timeframes; [0:27:54](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1674) — all charts open; [0:28:42](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1722) — 1m three entries.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Worked example: NQ short, Feb 3, 2022
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says / what price did:** NQ March 2022 (NQH2022). Bias bearish for the day because price had already gone up a lot on the daily chart. 15m: line at the first swing high left of 8:30. On replay from 8:30: an early run above a short-term high left an FVG that sold off — a scalper could take that, but for the daily range he wanted the 15m high. 9:30: volatile, a low and another low (sell stops building), highs intact. A shallow initial poke above the 15m high line: candles overlap, no FVG, no swing low taken — nothing. Then a higher high above the 15m line; price breaks below the nearest swing low; candles 1-2-3 between the highest high and that break leave a bearish FVG. Entry: limit one tick above candle 3's high; stop above candle 2 or candle 1 (swing high). Price returns into the FVG three times (third nearly fills it), each feeling like it will keep rising (a bold green candle). Targets: the 50% of the move (entry-swing range) with a bullish FVG below in discount = first partial; relative equal lows with sell stops below = next target. About 60 handles in roughly 11 one-minute candles (over $1,000 per mini). A retracement then shakes out traders who trailed stops too tightly before the lows are taken; target around 14,680. From ~14,800 to ~14,680 ≈ 120 handles. His paper trade: short 2 NQ minis at 14,792.50, first partial at 14,675, limit exit at 14,647.
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:36](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1956) — early FVG vs the 15m high; [0:34:18](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2058) — initial poke has no FVG; [0:35:06](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2106) — swing low broken, candles 1-2-3; [0:38:14](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2294) — targets: FVG in discount, equal lows; [0:43:24](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2604) — fills 14,792.50 / 14,675 / 14,647.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First time he publicly uses TradingView bar replay (for students who can't watch live).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Trailing stops: don't move stop until an intermediate-term low is taken
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** After the first partial, leave the stop where it is (use the partial to quench the desire to roll the stop); beginners trailing aggressively get stopped right before the big move. Only once a significant intermediate-term low (on the 1m) is taken out — which is also a full target — may you roll the stop down if holding on.
- **How to identify:** Intermediate-term swing low on the execution timeframe.
- **How to use:** Partial at the first target; hold stop at original until intermediate-term low taken.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Feb 3: pullback after the first partial, then lows taken.
- **Timestamps:** [0:40:15](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2415) — move designed to shake out tight trailers; [0:41:01](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2461) — don't roll stop until intermediate-term low taken.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First mention in the series of intermediate-term swings for stop management.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 6
head: Internal vs external range liquidity (IRL / ERL) for partials
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Take the price run (low to high) and put a Fib on it: 50% is equilibrium; below is discount. An FVG in the discount, inside the range, is internal range liquidity — first target for partials. The stops below the range's lows are external range liquidity — the final target. "Partials internal range, external range your trade."
- **How to identify:** Range low to range high; FVG inside below 50%; old lows beyond the range.
- **How to use:** Scale out at IRL, take the rest at ERL.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Feb 3: bullish FVG below 50% = IRL partial at 14,675; sell stops under equal lows = ERL exit at 14,647.
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:29](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=1769) — exit strategy using external range liquidity; [0:45:00](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2700) — FVG in discount = IRL; [0:45:49](https://youtu.be/Bkt8B3kLATQ?t=2749) — stops below lows = ERL.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Extends Ep. 3's IRL definition with its counterpart ERL.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Daily bias (reading the draw from the daily chart)  (aliases ICT uses: bias, "where is price going to draw")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Daily bias means using the daily chart to judge whether the next daily candle is likely bullish or bearish. Ask where price will draw next: up to an old high or down to an old low. Keep that bias until the target is reached.
  - Bearish bias means expecting down-close candles each day and hunting intraday shorts. You can still take a long, but with far less leverage.
  - A bearish bias doesn't mean every day closes down. In his NQ example the bearish leg from the high to the old low had only 2 up-close daily candles. When the algorithm is "spooling" (expanding directionally), some days will still close up, and you may lose trying to short them. That's no big deal.
  - What people "really" want when they ask about daily bias is to catch the exact high and low of every day and never take a loss. He calls that impossible. Bias is a "quick down and dirty" way to frame the day, not a perfect forecast.
  - "Daily bias is not an everyday bias that's going to work in your favor." Some days the expected direction doesn't deliver and you have to adjust.
- **How to identify:** daily market structure shift, then a retracement into a daily FVG, then expect delivery to the next old low (or old high when bullish).
- **How to use:** Trade with the bias at your maximum (non-overleveraged) size. Trade against it, if at all, with reduced size. Hold the bias until the draw is reached; after that, expect a reversal, retracement or consolidation.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily (continuous contract on TradingView). Price ran BSL above relative equal highs, then broke below a swing low (MSS). It traded back up into a FVG, then delivered down to the old lows. ICT notes a gap near the low-to-high midpoint. With the bias bearish, each day from that high to the low was approached expecting shorts.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:09](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=9) — NQ daily: BSL run, MSS, FVG · [0:03:25](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=205) — teaching bias: expect down candles until the low · [0:05:47](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=347) — count up-close candles in a bearish run (2) · [0:07:25](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=445) — bias = where will price draw next
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He openly says that even he sometimes has no clear read on bias, and then has to "demand more price action" from the 9:30 open.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Dealing range, premium/discount and consolidation at equilibrium ("consolidation hurdles")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Once sell-side liquidity below the range low has been taken, price is likely to retrace back inside the range (the swing high to the swing low).
  - In the example price went back up into premium (above equilibrium), then down into discount (bounced off the old low), then consolidated around equilibrium.
  - When price hangs around equilibrium of the daily range, bias is very hard to read, even for him. That doesn't mean no trading. It means:
    - relying on intraday charts,
    - looking for liquidity pools,
    - trading intraday volatility (runs on old highs and old lows),
    - being nimble, a "surgical strike": take your handles and get out, don't overstay.
- **How to identify:** On the daily chart, mark the high to the low of the most recent swing after the liquidity raid and use a Fib only for the midpoint (equilibrium). If price is oscillating around 50%, you're in a consolidation hurdle.
- **How to use:** Lower your expectations, take intraday liquidity targets only, and use smaller objectives.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily after the sell-side raid. Price retraced into premium, then discount, then chopped around equilibrium. ICT preferred a move lower for Tuesday 8 Feb 2022 (a sweep of the lows) but it didn't deliver.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:50](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=110) — premium, discount, then consolidation around equilibrium · [0:10:37](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=637) — what to do when bias is unclear
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He uses the Fib only to find the midpoint, saying "no OTE, no indicators" in this mentorship.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Leverage scaled to bias (risk per trade)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Trading with the bias means using your maximum allowed leverage without over-leveraging. His example: an account that allows at most 10 contracts. He uses a fixed % risk; he likes 3.5% and his maximum is 4.5%.
  - Trading counter to the bias means dialing leverage back.
  - Students should risk less than 1%, about 0.5% or 0.25%. Don't put high risk behind a move you don't understand: it creates "toxic thinking", bad habits and fear of executing.
  - Beginners should be "indifferent to the results". Use a demo with very low leverage, or reduce leverage further.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:11](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=251) — 10-contract example, 3.5% · [0:04:58](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=298) — students: 0.5% or 0.25% · [0:09:50](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=590) — max 4.5%, prefers 3.5%

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: 8:30 a.m. reference line ("crosshairs") and looking left for liquidity
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Draw a vertical line at 8:30 a.m. New York time. That's the point you start looking back to the left from.
  - Mark the first low and the first high to the left of 8:30. If a swing point sits inside another candle's range, use the extreme (the candle that holds the outermost price), because that's where the liquidity rests.
  - Relative equal highs further left are buy-side liquidity. Retail traders see them as "strong resistance" because price failed there twice, and the market then runs right through it.
  - Use a first target (the nearest liquidity) and a longer-term intraday target further left.
  - "Algorithms run on time and price, not price and time." Refer to time first (8:30), then find the first low to its left.
- **How to identify:** Use the 15m chart. Draw the 8:30 vertical, find the first swing low and high to the left, then look further left for relative equal highs and lows.
- **How to use:** Expect a raid on the liquidity on one side, then a run to the opposing pool.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15m on 8 Feb 2022. Price traded below the first low to the left of 8:30, reversed, and took out the short-term high (relative equal highs further left). ICT took that trade and exited at that high instead of holding for the longer-term target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:24](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=684) — 8:30 crosshairs, first low, use the extreme · [0:12:14](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=734) — relative equal highs as "resistance" retail sees · [0:28:20](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1700) — time first, then price

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Targeting: range midpoint plus liquidity
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He exited at the short-term high rather than holding for the longer-term one. The midpoint of the larger range (high down to the low) was just above that short-term high, and there was a small imbalance there. In this mentorship he looks for "about the midpoint and some kind of liquidity" (buy stops above it) as the objective.
- **How to use:** Take profit where the range midpoint lines up with resting liquidity. Don't hold for the extended target just to show off a perfect trade.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:02](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=782) — why he didn't hold: midpoint plus imbalance plus buy stops
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He deliberately doesn't hold for big runs on the public account, so he doesn't present unrealistic results.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Narrative over pattern-matching
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Seeing a low taken out and expecting higher prices (or the reverse) isn't enough. There has to be greater context: why should the market do it? Students coming from "SMC" lack narrative, which leads to analysis paralysis or false confidence. Educators who only talk about the left side of the chart and can't trade the hard right edge give false security.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:38](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=878) — narrative missing in SMC

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: 2022 Mentorship entry model (raid, MSS, FVG), timed on a correlated index
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Sequence: price trades below an old low (SSL taken), then displacement and a bullish market structure shift (breaks a swing high). Look back through the up-leg for a FVG and enter on the retrace into it.
  - If price instead keeps going lower after your entry, "that's what your stop is for."
  - For homework, check the 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 minute charts. He used the 2-minute chart that day.
- **How to identify:** old low, then a run below it, then a displacement up through a swing high, then the FVG in that leg.
- **How to use:** Stop just below the low candle of the move (about 1 tick below). Target the short-term high or BSL.
- **Example in this video:**
  - NQ 2m:
    - Price trades below the old low formed before 8:30. The 10:04 candle is the low and the stop goes about 1 tick under it.
    - It rallies but doesn't break the short-term high, dips below the old low again but not below the 10:04 low, then turns higher.
    - NQ showed no FVG at entry time. ICT went long at 14,505.5, inside/near a bullish order block.
    - He exited at 14,622.75, above the 14,620 high: about 117 handles on 1 NQ mini.
  - ES 2m:
    - Price traded below the old low (SSL taken) with displacement down, then displacement up.
    - It broke a swing high (bullish MSS) and left a FVG.
    - The 10:36 candle traded down into that FVG, which was the long signal in ES.
    - ES then ran to the short-term high around 4495/4496 ("44.95 level"), swept it, accumulated more, and ran higher through the longer-term old high.
  - He used the timing of the ES FVG entry (10:36) to buy NQ: "trading what's not in the chart."
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:25](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=925) — 2m chart, 10:04 low candle, stop · [0:18:34](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1114) — ES displacement, MSS, FVG, 10:36 long · [0:20:07](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1207) — NQ long at 14,505 near an order block · [0:37:58](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=2278) — exit 14,622.75, 117 handles
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says he "promised not to teach order blocks much" in this mentorship but still references one for the NQ fill. The ES/NQ FVG timing trick is the point: you don't need the FVG in your own instrument if a correlated one prints it.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: SMT divergence ("cracks in correlation"), confirmation only  (aliases ICT uses: cracks in correlation, divergence, fingerprint of the algorithm)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Stack the Dow (top), NASDAQ (middle) and S&P (bottom) futures. They normally move in tandem.
  - When NQ and ES trade below their old low but the Dow refuses to make the lower low, at a key time and level, that crack in correlation confirms accumulation of longs. The bearish version is the mirror: the Dow fails to make a higher high while ES and NQ do.
  - It must confirm an idea you already have. "You're already looking for a reason to go higher" (old low, raid, MSS). By itself it means nothing.
  - He blew accounts in the 1990s trading these divergences alone, without narrative.
  - The Dow holding up is not "buyers coming in". It's an unwillingness to deliver lower, and ICT calls this a macro: something inside the algorithm that prevents or enables delivery of price.
  - Experienced traders may not need it. For developing students, these intermarket signals are "the best indicators you're ever going to have": no moving averages, stochastics or Fibonacci needed.
- **How to identify:** At a known liquidity level (old low) and time window, one index fails to take the level that the other two take.
- **How to use:** Use it to confirm a long (or short) setup that's already anticipated at a liquidity raid. Then execute with the FVG/MSS logic in your chosen instrument.
- **Example in this video:** 8 Feb 2022. During the decline NQ and ES both traded below the old low; YM did not make the lower low. ICT used this, plus the ES FVG, to go long NQ around 10:36.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:34](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1354) — Dow/NQ/ES stacked, Dow refuses the lower low · [0:23:26](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1406) — it confirms an already-anticipated idea · [0:25:57](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1557) — blew accounts trading divergence alone · [0:28:20](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1700) — "this is a macro": algorithm prevents/enables delivery
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The term "SMT" isn't used here. "Macro" here means an algorithmic mechanism that withholds or allows delivery. That's a different, earlier usage from the later meaning of a macro as a specific clock-time window (e.g. 9:50–10:10).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Turtle soup (ICT's version)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A fake break below an old low that then rallies, or a fake break above an old high that then drops. ICT calls this turtle soup. It's his own simplified interpretation, not the pattern from Linda Raschke and Larry Connors' *Street Smarts* (which he recommends as a book). He looks for runs above old highs to set up shorts, and the mirror for longs.
- **Timestamps:** [0:25:09](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1509)

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Intermarket relationships among the indices
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** ES, NQ and YM "generally move in the same direction". He trades NQ for its volatility but watches ES and YM on multiple monitors. The setup forms every day, but it may not be in your asset. "All boats rise in high tide." Read the environment as a whole, not just your own instrument.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 7
head: Leader orders / test contracts at the open  (aliases ICT uses: "leaders", "tossing a contract in", "premium for Intel")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (execution technique)
- **What ICT says:**
  - When he has no read (e.g. a sloppy 9:30 open, price in mid-range on the daily), he puts in a single contract, long or short, just to feel how price delivers around it.
  - Watch whether price moves easily away from the order, moves lethargically, or runs straight against it. If the test order is "ran over", your bias probably isn't aligned.
  - Small losses on these are "premium payments" for information. They aren't skill errors.
  - He learned this from a floor trader and George Angell (S&P floor traders). He also does it in Forex.
  - A demo account can't give this feedback loop because nothing is at risk.
  - He's not trying to pick a spot when he tosses these in, and he doesn't do it every day.
  - The 9:30 open is characteristically sloppy. Many people say don't trade it; he doesn't mind it.
- **Example in this video:** 8 Feb 2022. Two leader orders plus a short around the open lost money (one cost about $750). The 10:36 long, 14,505.5 to 14,622.75, made $2,345 on 1 NQ mini, which covered the leaders and netted about $1,100 for the day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:47](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1847) — sloppy 9:30 open, putting orders in to get a feel · [0:31:33](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=1893) — George Angell / floor-trader origin · [0:33:54](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=2034) — reading price against the order · [0:54:05](https://youtu.be/G8-z91acgG4?t=3245) — trade P&L breakdown
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says many of his students don't do this and don't think it's worth it. It's a trade-off tied to his goal of capturing 100+ handle moves rather than scalping.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 8
head: Daily bias on a Forex daily chart (HTF application of the model)
body:
- **Kind:** example only / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The model applies to "higher time frame" daily charts too.
  - On the daily chart: relative equal lows get run (SSL taken), then price rallies.
  - Two points of market structure break to the upside: a first swing high taken, a drop back, then a second swing high taken.
  - In the up-leg, find the FVG(s). Price trades down into one and is sent higher.
  - The old high above is buy-side liquidity, a likely draw on liquidity "whether it trades there or not".
  - Horseshoes analogy: you aim at the post every throw even though you don't hit it every time.
  - Even a failure swing short of the old high is tradeable if there's enough range from the open to the high to "take a stab at it".
- **How to identify:** SSL raid (relative equal lows) on the daily, then a bullish MSS (sequential swing highs broken), then a retrace into the daily FVG, with an old high as the target.
- **How to use:** Expect the next daily candle (here 10 Feb 2022) to trade higher, then go intraday to execute.
- **Example in this video:** EURJPY daily (Forex.com data feed on TradingView; he avoids another feed). Relative equal lows raided, rally, two bullish structure breaks, retrace into a daily FVG, then higher toward the old highs. The 10 Feb 2022 candle was expected to be bullish after the consolidation.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:45](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=105) — relative equal lows run, rally · [0:02:32](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=152) — two structure breaks, daily FVG, BSL draw · [0:03:20](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=200) — horseshoes analogy; a failure swing is still tradeable
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** ICT dislikes the yen pairs. He says they tend to make a "double return" to a level (a second retest) (caption partly unclear) and prefers other Forex markets.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 8
head: Entry model: SSL raid, MSS, FVG with top-down drill (5m to 3m to 1m)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - On the 5m chart within the killzone, price trades down, takes out a swing low, then punches above a swing high.
  - Isolate the leg from that low to that high and study it on each lower timeframe (5m, 3m, 1m).
  - On the 3m: did it take a swing low? Yes. Did it take a swing high? Yes. That makes it a "valid condition" to look for a trade.
  - Go back through the price leg for FVG(s). There were two. Price "could stab down" into the lower one, so be mindful, but try to get the entry in on the first one.
- **How to identify:** Inside 7–10 a.m. NY: sell-side swing low taken, then a displacement through a swing high, then FVG(s) in that leg.
- **How to use:** Enter on the retrace into the FVG. Be aware a deeper FVG may get tagged instead.
- **Example in this video:** EURJPY 5m/3m, 10 Feb 2022 NY session: the low was swept, the swing high broken, the 3m FVG(s) retested, then the rally.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:41](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=341) — 5m: swing low taken, punch above swing high · [0:06:27](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=387) — top-down 5m to 1m, 3m conditions · [0:07:13](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=433) — valid condition, two FVGs, entry

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 8
head: Fib standard deviation (−1) projection for targets in expansion  (aliases ICT uses: standard deviation negative one)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - When the setup forms in the middle of a range, with no nearby old high or low to target ("if we don't have a range to trade inside of"), project how far an expansion can go.
  - Anchor a Fibonacci on the previous swing: the low to the high of the price leg right after price leaves the consolidation (before the discount retracement). Then use the −1 standard deviation as the target.
  - His Fib settings are in the "OTE primer" video on the channel.
- **How to identify:** The swing that broke structure before the consolidation and pullback. The pullback creates the discount, and then the retracement rally.
- **How to use:** The −1 extension of that swing is the expansion target. Here it was hit "right to the point".
- **Example in this video:** EURJPY. The −1 SD projection landed at about 133.15/133.153, which matched the high of the move (133.153), and price reacted from there.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:00](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=480) — no range to target, use the swing leg · [0:08:46](https://youtu.be/7rbV8aWkcqY?t=526) — anchor Fib, −1 SD, 133.153
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** A harder-timeframe old high exists further left, but the SD projection is the "real easy way" when nothing is close.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 9
head: Daily dealing range: discount plus an indecisive daily candle means expect a retracement
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Choose the daily range: the most recent swing low (which took out a short-term low, digging into SSL) and the swing high. Fib it only for the 50% (equilibrium). Below 50% is discount.
  - On Monday 14 Feb 2022 NQ traded into a deep discount but didn't take the lows further left. Monday closed with an indecisive candle, the body "basically absent" (open ≈ close).
  - In discount with an indecisive close, a retracement may be needed first, even if a lower low is the eventual target.
  - Monday's close left a daily imbalance (FVG). Overnight into Tuesday, price ran up into it. The FVG's lower and upper edges became reference levels on the lower timeframes.
- **Example in this video:** NQ continuous (TradingView). Mon 14 Feb: deep discount, doji-like close, daily FVG. Tue 15 Feb: overnight run into the FVG; the upper end of the FVG was the draw.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:53](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=53) — range selection, premium/discount · [0:01:41](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=101) — indecisive Monday close means a retracement; daily FVG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The daily FVG's top isn't known until Monday's close. Don't look back and think he "knew" the level in advance.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 9
head: Power of Three (AMD)  (aliases ICT uses: Power 3, accumulation manipulation distribution)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Bullish day: the opening price is near the low of the day or session. Price trades lower to make an important low (manipulation), then rallies to create the high and closes near the high.
  - You don't need to predict the close. The aim is to anticipate the fake move at the start.
  - If bullish, the small move lower after the open is what you hunt for a long. If you miss it, try to get long as close to the opening price as possible.
  - Which opening price? He likes 8:30 a.m. ET. Draw it forward in time.
- **How to identify (bullish, checklist he runs at the 8:30 open):** Did price go below the 8:30 opening price? Did it trade into the imbalance? Did it take a short-term low? Did it hit an order block? Was it an optimal trade entry? Each yes adds confluence.
- **How to use:** Buy below the opening price during the manipulation leg, with a target toward the day's draw (e.g. the high end of the daily FVG or relative equal highs).
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Mon 14 Feb 2022. Price was below the 8:30 open, inside the pre-8:30 imbalance, took a short-term low, hit an order block, at OTE: a long. In the afternoon price traded below the opening price again, then rallied and took the relative equal highs toward the upper end of the daily FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:34](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=154) — Power 3 bullish profile · [0:05:46](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=346) — hunt the small move lower; use the 8:30 opening price · [0:06:34](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=394) — 8:30 confluence checklist

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 9
head: Order block (precise definition)  (aliases ICT uses: bullish order block, complete order block)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - "Consecutive down-close candles right before a price surge that has an imbalance": that's how you find order blocks.
  - A high-probability order block: your narrative or bias is bullish, you see displacement (price runs quickly higher), and you mark the down-close candles before it and anticipate a return to them.
  - In the 5m example, the imbalance's lowest portion contained 4 consecutive down-close candles, a "complete order block on this time frame", anchored to the daily bullish order block.
  - The best entry combines all three: FVG plus order block plus OTE.
- **How to identify:** a run of consecutive down-close candles, then displacement up leaving a FVG. Mark the down-close candles' range.
- **How to use:** In a bullish narrative, wait for the retracement back into the order block (ideally overlapping the FVG and OTE) and buy.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5m, 14 Feb 2022. After the high formed, price broke down and retraced into the imbalance (the FVG between one candle's low and another's high) that had the 4 down-close candles of the order block. It rallied, sloppily but continuously higher, into the close.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:00](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=300) — down-close candles left of the imbalance = bullish OB · [0:07:23](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=443) — 4 down-close candles, definition, high-probability OB · [0:08:10](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=490) — FVG plus OB plus OTE
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Earlier episodes said he wouldn't teach order blocks much. Here he gives a compact definition.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 9
head: Don't chase overnight runs; after a big overnight run, avoid the NY AM and trade after lunch
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - When there's a big overnight move (he cites London, 2:00–5:00 a.m.) before New York, don't chase it at 8:30 just because it went up overnight. Wait for more information.
  - A consolidation typically follows a big run. Not always: sometimes it keeps running and you'll miss it.
  - With a big overnight range, don't expect much in-and-out precision. Wait for a significant move or you'll get chopped up.
  - **Equity index futures only (NQ, YM, ES), not Forex:** if there's a big overnight run, avoid the New York AM session entirely. Wait for the other side of lunch (after 1:00 p.m. NY time) and anticipate a raid on the New York lunch lows or the New York morning-session lows.
  - New York lunch = noon to 1:00 p.m. NY local time.
  - Everyone wakes up wanting to chase. That leads to losing trades and a chase cycle, and in choppy sideways conditions it's "like a blowtorch on your account".
- **How to use:** After the overnight expansion, mark the AM consolidation lows (especially relative equal lows). In the PM, wait for them to be run into a FVG, then a bullish MSS and FVG entry.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Tue 15 Feb 2022. A huge overnight (London) rally ran into the daily FVG. ICT says he would have missed it and it surprised him. The AM was sloppy and back-and-forth, leaving relative equal lows. Relative equal highs formed before 7:00 a.m. weren't taken. BSL sat around 14,575 and the draw was the upper boundary of the daily FVG. In the PM, NQ dropped, took the sell side and dug into a FVG, with candle bodies respecting the level, then rallied.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:35](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=635) — 15 Feb overnight run, wouldn't have caught it · [0:12:08](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=728) — don't chase; consolidation follows; big overnight range means don't trade much · [0:15:22](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=922) — the rule: avoid the NY session, wait until after 1:00 p.m. · [0:24:16](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=1456) — why: everyone chases in the morning

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 9
head: Engineering liquidity (relative equal lows as stop pools)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Back-and-forth AM price action builds "suspect" relative equal lows with sell stops below them. Anyone long overnight will "jam their stop loss right underneath" once price starts rising.
  - It's even better when the high above hasn't been taken yet.
  - Price runs up, consolidates, creates a low, starts rallying; retail moves stops under that low. That's the setup he wants, the liquidity he expects to be run.
  - After the overnight stops have been run, the market doesn't need to go back down there. It gets "sneakier" and won't give stopped-out traders another chance at the same price.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:33](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=873) — relative equal lows, overnight longs' stops · [0:17:45](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=1065) — "that's engineering liquidity" · [0:19:21](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=1161) — post-lunch, they won't let stopped traders back in

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 9
head: PM entry model: lunch/AM lows raided, MSS, FVG (with missed-entry limit at the short-term low)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - From 2:00 p.m. NY time, price trades down into an imbalance and takes the liquidity below relative equal lows (post-lunch), then rallies.
  - Checklist: a swing high is broken. Was it energetic? Yes. Did it leave a FVG? Yes. Price trades back down into the FVG and creates a short-term low. You can buy there.
  - If you missed it and price runs off, you may get a second chance when price comes back to that short-term low, which has sell-side liquidity resting below it. Buy at that low or 1 tick below it on a limit.
  - Stop: at the short-term low below, formed after the FVG (exact reference caption unclear). "That's the rules."
- **How to identify:** PM session (after lunch), a raid on SSL (relative equal lows), an energetic break of a swing high with a FVG, a retrace into the FVG.
- **How to use:** Limit buy at the FVG, or at the short-term low or 1 tick below. Stop below the swing low. Target the BSL or daily FVG high above.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, 15 Feb 2022:
  - The short-term low formed at 2:34 p.m. with a low of 14,528.5. The suggested limit was 14,528.25 (or 14,528 even).
  - Risk about 14.25 handles. With 6 micros he says about $85 risked to make about $300, roughly 3.5:1.
  - Heat after entry: about 9 points (he says $54 on 6 micros). The stop was not hit, with about 5 handles to spare.
  - One mini = $20 per handle.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:33](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=1113) — PM narrative: stops raided into FVG, rally · [0:20:09](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=1209) — swing high broken, energetic, FVG, missed-entry case · [0:20:59](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=1259) — limit at the short-term low or −1 tick; 2:34 p.m.; 14,528.5 · [0:21:49](https://youtu.be/iZLXnNiZm_s?t=1309) — stop rule, 14.25 handles risk, 6 micros, about 3.5R
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** His micro dollar figures ($85 for 14.25 points on 6 micros; $54 for 9 points) work out to $1 per point per micro. Editorial note: MNQ is actually $2/point, so verify the contract math yourself. He says he's "roughing" it without a calculator.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 9
head: A FVG is not invalidated by a wick through it (permit imperfection in volatile conditions)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price traded below the short-term low (the sell stops) and into the FVG further. Commenters asked whether that invalidates the FVG. It doesn't. The candle bodies respected the FVG.
  - In volatile markets he permits "a greater level of imperfection in price delivery": use the FVG logic for the entry and the stop premise for protection.
  - Trust the setups and let the stops do their job. A stop-out is "just one trade you got wrong, not your career".

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 10
head: Economic calendar and the 8:30 a.m. news embargo
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Check the economic calendar every day you trade, or you may be surprised by volatility. He uses forexfactory.com (any calendar works). Red = high impact, orange = medium, yellow = low.
  - 8:30 a.m. ET is the crosshair time because the news embargo lifts then and many releases hit the market.
  - Releases can be a smoke screen or a catalyst. Often price builds up (or drops) right before the report, then the real move follows.
  - If price pumps higher ahead of the 8:30 release on a bearish-bias day, it's "tipping its hand". Price is being driven into a premium before the news so the news can be used to sink it. Shorts have already been accumulated above the opening price.
- **Example in this video:** Thu 17 Feb 2022 calendar (several medium-impact events). NQ rallied ahead of 8:30, then sold off with the bearish daily bias.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:54](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=54) — ForexFactory, colour codes · [0:01:42](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=102) — 8:30 embargo; buildup before the report, then the real move · [0:36:11](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=2171) — pricing in a premium ahead of the news to sink it

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 10
head: Daily bias = will the daily range expand above or below the open  (aliases ICT uses: the key to bias)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The most-requested question over the years is how to find daily bias. He says this is "really all I teach my students", with nothing more secret than this.
  - You only need to know whether the daily range is more likely to expand higher or lower than the opening price. Predicting the close is "more advanced" and not needed to be profitable.
  - Bearish day: open, a rally (small, or even a large wick), down, close near the low. Bullish day: the reverse.
  - Not every candle in a swing conforms. In sustained HTF swings there are few opposite candles. Don't let one counter day knock you out of your bias.
  - Once bias is set (e.g. bearish after a daily MSS and a retrace into a FVG), "any rally or up-close candle should be viewed as a potential shorting candidate".
  - Stay with the bias until the draw (e.g. relative equal highs, BSL) is reached. Then study whether it wants to continue.
- **How to identify:** daily structure (swing points), daily FVG and premium/discount, the draw on liquidity.
- **How to use:** Each day, expect a Power-of-Three candle in the bias direction. Losses on counter days are expected. Keep the bias until the target liquidity is taken.
- **Example in this video:**
  - NQ daily (1992-style OHLC bars, then candles). Bullish sequence:
    - A 3-bar swing low forms. The next day washes out below the open and closes on its high.
    - The following day is expected to rally into the FVG above (bullish bias).
    - Price then retraces below equilibrium of the swing into discount, followed by a series of open-near-low, close-near-high days.
    - It keeps reaching for relative equal highs (BSL). Bias stays bullish until above them.
  - Bearish sequence: the rally into a daily FVG, then open-rally-close-on-low days toward sell-side lows, then a potential key reversal and chop.
  - Current context: NQ traded up to the top of the daily FVG (from Ep. 9), the bias is bearish, and the targets are the lows below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:18](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=198) — "number one question": daily bias · [0:06:31](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=391) — rallies are shorting candidates · [0:17:44](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=1064) — expand higher or lower than the open is "the key to bias" · [0:20:57](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=1257) — daily bullish Power-3 sequence to relative equal highs
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Simplifies the "draw on liquidity" framing from Ep. 7 into the open-relative expansion question.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 10
head: Power of Three on the daily candle (AMD components, precise)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says (bearish day):**
  - **Accumulation:** the open and anything above it is where shorts are accumulated (smart money, and ICT and his students, aim to enter there).
  - **Manipulation:** the initial rally above the open, the "sucker play" for breakout traders. It only goes up to go down. This is the Judas swing.
  - **Distribution:** from the low of the day to the close, where the short positions are distributed (closed).
  - The low of the day often forms late. If price has been beaten down all day, around 3:30–3:45 p.m. ET it's probably close to the low. Not always: sometimes there's a sudden continuation.
  - Bullish is mirrored: open near the low, a false move down, a rally, distribution of longs near the close.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:56](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=776) — components defined; open and above = accumulation of shorts · [0:16:09](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=969) — manipulation = sucker play; distribution · [0:16:56](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=1016) — low of day near 3:30–3:45 p.m.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 10
head: Opening range (open-to-manipulation-extreme, projected through the open) and close-proximity entries
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule (new framing)
- **What ICT says:**
  - On a bearish day, measure the range from the opening price up to the high (the Judas swing). Subtract that range from the opening price: project it below the open. That projected zone is what he calls the **opening range**.
  - "Every premium array" (every FVG, stop raid and OTE short setup in any approach he teaches, including the paid mentorship) will form between the open and its high, and within that projection below the open.
  - This tells you how much leeway to give the market once it trades below the open while still taking a favorable short. These are **close-proximity entries**: there are many opportunities just below the opening price.
  - If price leaves that zone without you, don't chase. "I don't care how good it looks later in the day."
- **How to identify:** Opening price (intraday, the midnight NY open) and the manipulation high. Distance = high minus open. Zone = open plus or minus that distance.
- **How to use:** Write down intentions before the session: "bearish; look for shorts in the open-to-high range, or just below the open within the projected range." Only take setups inside it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15m, 17 Feb 2022. From the midnight opening price, price rallied above it into a FVG (a sell above the open). The open-to-high distance was projected below the open, and a further short formed there at the equities open. He describes the projection as "multiply that by two": from the high, double the high-to-open distance downward.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:56](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=776) — open-to-high range subtracted from the open · [0:13:45](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=825) — every premium array forms in that range · [0:14:34](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=874) — close-proximity entries below the open; don't chase · [1:00:18](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=3618) — write intentions; outside the range, no trade
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is ICT's specific 2022-Ep.10 meaning of "opening range". It differs from the RTH 9:30 opening range and gap concepts taught elsewhere.

head: Paint-roller analogy for imbalance and rebalancing (FVG logic)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The chart background is the wall and each candle is a paint roller. A big, long candle leaves "porous" places where price wasn't efficiently offered to the other side (not enough time or back-and-forth for buyers to participate). There's a strong (not universal) tendency for price to go back and overlap the whole range, repainting it evenly. Once a range is "completely balanced" there's no reason for price to hang around there.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:06](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=726) — range fully balanced, no reason to stay · [0:27:22](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=1642) — paint roller: long candles get overlapped

head: Bearish market structure shift (energetic break) and the two-FVG rule
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Framework: a swing high is broken to the upside, taking buy stops (BSL), then a swing low is broken.
  - Was the decline lethargic? No: sudden, with momentum, obvious down-close candles. That's how you know you have a shift in market structure.
  - When there are two FVGs, try to trade the first one, but your money management must allow your stop to weather a run up into the second. "That's part of the rules."
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5m, 17 Feb 2022. At 7:00 a.m. price rallied above relative equal highs and cleaned up an imbalance, then broke down energetically.

body:

- **What ICT says:**
  - If the 5m leg has no FVG, step down through the 4m, 3m, 2m and 1m.
  - The first timeframe where you find a FVG is your trading timeframe. Don't go lower once you've found one.
  - If there's no FVG even on the 1m, you have no trade.
  - On the 4m the candles looked "beefier" and cleaner than on the 5m. You want clean price action where the FVG (the break in even distribution) stands out.

head: Bearish breaker (stop placement)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The breaker pattern (taught in his free YouTube lessons): a high, a low, then a higher high (the run above BSL), followed by a return into it.
  - Bearish breaker candle = the down-close candle right before the big move up that took out the short-term high.
  - The market will "mostly stay in the lower half" of the breaker candle. So use the breaker candle and just above it for the stop, not the higher imbalance further up.
- **How to use:** Short the FVG inside or below the breaker. Stop just above the breaker candle.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 4m, 17 Feb 2022. BSL was run after rebalancing, then the breakdown. A FVG and a small imbalance were above. The stop was placed just above the breaker candle.
- **Timestamps:** [0:40:07](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=2407) — breaker = high, low, higher high; stop just above the breaker candle · [0:40:56](https://youtu.be/S9ORTYmXwdE?t=2456) — price mostly stays in the lower half of the breaker candle
