head: Margin, leverage and volatility risk (discount brokers)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Discount brokers that let you trade a NQ mini for a couple of thousand dollars, or a micro for under $100, are "absolutely stupid". You're asking to blow the account.
  - He saw a 100-point NQ move in a single 1m candle. Slippage example: 50 points against 8 minis is $1,000 per contract, times 8 (the caption's "$88,000" is a mis-hearing). One candle can roast an account.
  - He wants at least $10,000 per NQ mini, and $15,000 is fair given current volatility. That day alone NQ moved about $8,000 per contract top to bottom.
  - TD Ameritrade required about $22,000 per NQ mini (exchange-based initial margin; a figure of about $17,604 is also mentioned, caption unclear).
  - When the exchange raises margins, it's "tipping their hand" that big moves are coming.

head: Daily narrative: dealing range, a premium retracement to fill a gap, then a sell-side raid
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - On the NQ daily, measure the dealing range high to low. 50% = equilibrium.
  - Price went from the lows up into premium, tried to rally above the high and failed, broke back below 50% and left a gap. It came back up into premium to fill the gap.
  - That kind of retracement "lulls traders" into thinking higher. But the target is the sell-side liquidity below the old daily low (his "green line"). All the consolidation just sets up another selling opportunity.
  - It spent three days in the range rebalancing, then "released" downward and attacked the sell side.
- **Example in this video:** NQ March futures daily: a daily FVG (from the previous episodes) traded into, three days of rebalancing, then a sell-off into the SSL below the old low.

- **How to use:** Short inside the FVG, above the open. Target the SSL below the old daily low.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 11
head: Short-, intermediate- and long-term highs/lows (market structure nesting)  (aliases ICT uses: halos, long-term intraday high)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Swing high: a candle with a lower-high candle on its left and a lower-high candle on its right (3 candles).
  - Short-term high (STH): any swing high.
  - Intermediate-term high (ITH): a swing high with lower short-term swing highs on both sides of it.
  - Long-term high (LTH): a high with lower intermediate-term highs on both sides. On a 3m chart this is a "long-term intraday high", which he admits sounds like an oxymoron.
  - Lows are mirrored.
  - Old chart-book habit: one circle (halo) over a short-term high, two for an intermediate-term high, three for a long-term high. This classifies "the nesting effect of the highs and lows".
  - It's "far more than just lower lows and lower highs", and it's not supply and demand or support/resistance.
  - Source: Larry Williams, from his early-90s VHS course (*Future Millionaires Confidential*, title approximate) and the market-structure chapters of *How I Made One Million Dollars Last Year Trading Commodities*. ICT says it's still essential reading (minus the "moon phases" fluff), and he rereads it yearly.
- **How to identify:** Mark every 3-candle swing high. Then promote a swing high to intermediate-term when the swing highs on either side are lower. Then promote to long-term when the intermediate-term highs on either side are lower.
- **How to use:** In a bearish leg with the draw below, short close to the current intermediate-term high. It's a lower high relative to the long-term high, so it's unlikely to be exceeded and is "likely to break" lower. Backtest by classifying swing highs and lows to build trust in the model.
- **Example in this video:**
  - NQ 3m, 21 Feb 2022. An earlier long-term intraday high had lower swing highs on either side, making the next high an intermediate-term high.
  - At 10:33, one candle back showed a high with a lower high on either side: a swing high lower than the ITH, which was lower than the LTH.
  - That nested structure (with the SSL draw below acting as a "magnet") is why he trusted the short.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:28](https://youtu.be/Sqw2bww93Zo?t=628) — long-term, intermediate and short-term highs on a 3m chart · [0:11:17](https://youtu.be/Sqw2bww93Zo?t=677) — the draw below as a magnet; short near the ITH · [0:13:42](https://youtu.be/Sqw2bww93Zo?t=822) — swing high definition; chart-book halos (1/2/3) · [0:14:29](https://youtu.be/Sqw2bww93Zo?t=869) — nesting; Larry Williams book
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Expanded in the next episode's market structure lesson.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 11
head: Displacement as confirmation and optimal entry near the session high
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - After entering he wants to see displacement. When it comes, it's confirmation: "sit back and relax and let it do its thing."
  - He enters up near the session high (the 8:30 run-up). He doesn't wait for a breakout below the low, because that's the optimal entry. You don't need the highest high, but you must understand why price should trade away from your entry level.
  - Missed entry: after the swing high is broken and the displacement comes, if price returns to touch the FVG (the candle high) again, you can short there using the FVG entry technique.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:52](https://youtu.be/Sqw2bww93Zo?t=1012) — wants displacement · [0:17:40](https://youtu.be/Sqw2bww93Zo?t=1060) — missed-entry return into the FVG · [0:18:31](https://youtu.be/Sqw2bww93Zo?t=1111) — near the session high; don't wait for the breakdown; displacement = confirmation

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 11
head: Exit management: market vs limit order; take profits into the raid and step aside for the gap fill
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - He was watching 13,590/13,586 as an objective but didn't use a limit order. If price ran fast and far lower he didn't want a limit capping his exit, so he left it open and closed manually at 13,612.25.
  - Once price runs into the low (the liquidity), take profits and move to the sidelines. A big gap is likely to come back and rebalance (fill), and it did.
- **Example in this video:** Short 13,858.25, exit 13,612.25 = 246 handles (×4 ticks per handle for tick counters). That's $4,920 on 1 NQ mini.

  - You must know when enough is enough. Social-media talk of "push your edge" is wrong: pushing it dulls it. You sharpen your edge by knowing when to get in and when to get out. People who say that are gamblers, likely unprofitable.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: The two narrative questions (the only things price does)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Before sitting down at the charts, ask: is price likely to go **up for buy stops (BSL) or to rebalance an imbalance (FVG) above**? Or **down for sell stops (SSL) or to rebalance an imbalance below**? That's the current market narrative.
  - He ignores patterns, harmonics, Elliott waves, ratio ideas and anything "retail".
  - The market only books and prints candles on two principles: **liquidity** (above old highs for buy stops, below old lows for sell stops) and **imbalance** (creating or rebalancing it). "Imbalance, rebalance, run for liquidity. That's it."
  - The riddle: if harmonics, Elliott, supply/demand, volume profile, Wyckoff, Ichimoku and the rest were real, how would the market choose which conflicting discipline to follow on a given day? Believing them is "faith-based".
  - Bank traders only look at imbalance, rebalance and liquidity (in Forex they add interest-rate differentials). They don't care about S/R, trend lines or MA crosses.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:43](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=343) — up for stops or rebalance vs down for stops or rebalance · [0:06:33](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=393) — the number one question; no harmonics or Elliott · [0:38:43](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2323) — bank traders: imbalance, rebalance, liquidity · [1:11:48](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=4308) — the market only does these two things

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Higher-timeframe parent / lower-timeframe child structure
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The daily chart is the parent. All minor lower-timeframe swings are subordinate to it. The daily has the bulk of the volume and order flow; institutions and banks work off it. It "makes or breaks your trend continuation."
  - You can still navigate on a 1m chart within that context.
  - A retail "trend change" (a failed higher high, then a break of the swing low before it) is often just a deep discount buy for ICT when the HTF is bullish. You need the HTF hierarchy to know which.
  - The daily FVG high he outlined is a higher-timeframe level. The high that forms there on the 1h is a **long-term high** that shouldn't be broken. If it breaks, his daily analysis is probably wrong. Then he demands more information and sits on his hands, or, if in a trade, takes the stop as a cost of business (not a flawed model, not a failed trader).
  - Developing students should keep forecasts to about a 5-day horizon and not worry about forecasting the whole weekly range. It took ICT six years.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:36](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=636) — daily is the parent; this is a long-term high · [0:11:25](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=685) — if broken, the analysis is wrong; the stop is a cost of business · [0:20:08](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1208) — retail trend change vs deep discount; parent/child · [0:29:45](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1785) — link everything to the daily; 5-day horizon

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Short-, intermediate- and long-term swing classification (ICT's version)  (aliases ICT uses: STH/STL, ITH/ITL, LTH/LTL)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / new coinage (extends Larry Williams)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Base classification (from Larry Williams; the source book shown is *Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading*): an ITH is the highest high between two short-term highs, i.e. a STH with a lower STH on its left and a lower STH on its right. Lows mirror this.
  - **ICT's addition, "the main one":** any time price trades back to **rebalance an imbalance** (fill a FVG), the swing high formed at that rebalance is **immediately** an **intermediate-term high**. If price drops back down to fill a bullish imbalance, that low is an **intermediate-term low**.
  - So there are two ways to classify an ITH: (a) a STH with lower STHs either side, or (b) a high formed by rebalancing an imbalance.
  - He labels these in his mind, not on the chart, to avoid distraction. Annotations are "lipstick" for teaching only.
  - Don't mark every swing on the lower timeframes; that's overkill. Establish structure on the framing timeframe (1h here).
- **How to identify:** Find FVGs (single-candle "one-pass" moves). When price returns and fills one, the turning point at that fill is an ITH or ITL.
- **How to use:** In a bearish idea, the ITH formed by rebalancing must not be exceeded. The next short-term high should be lower than it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ March 2022, 1h, inside the daily FVG. A down candle left an imbalance; price rallied back up to fill it. The swing high formed there was labeled an ITH. On the way down, a fill of a bullish imbalance made an ITL.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:00](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=780) — every rebalance of an old imbalance becomes an ITH or ITL · [0:16:56](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1016) — ITH between two STHs; "main takeaway for your notes" · [0:41:08](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2468) — the two classifications of an ITH stated explicitly
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** It extends the Ep. 11 halo hierarchy. ICT stresses he doesn't "teach Larry Williams market structure". Williams was only the starting point.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Weak intermediate-term high (ITH below its neighbouring short-term highs)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Ideally an ITH should be above both STHs beside it. When the ITH formed by rebalancing is **not higher** than the STH to its left or right, it's "only rebalancing". The market is **exceedingly weak**, and "the algorithm is tipping its hand".
  - ICT says he pioneered this idea; no one taught it to him.
  - This answers the retail question of which way a pennant or triangle will break. Retail sees low, high, higher low, failed higher high: a pennant. The weak ITH says it breaks down.
  - Retail traders see the consolidation as a bull flag. ICT likes to fade those ("false bull flag").
- **How to use:** With a bearish HTF premise, a weak ITH justifies anticipating the failure. Treat the up-close candles forming there as a bearish order block and look for an aggressive short.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:14](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=734) — false bull flag; fade it · [0:14:35](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=875) — pennant: which side breaks? · [0:22:31](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1351) — ITH not above the STHs either side; "it's going lower" · [0:37:56](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2276) — not higher than two STHs means very weak; algorithm tipping its hand

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Invalidation rule: an ITH/ITL must not be violated
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - If bearish and an imbalance is rebalanced, the next short-term high should be lower than that ITH. If price trades higher than the ITH, "your trade idea's probably flawed".
  - Don't force the trade again. Wait for market structure to get back in sync with your expectation. That's how you avoid blowing the account or forcing your will on the market.
  - If the ITH or ITL breaks after your idea became possible, go to the sidelines and don't re-enter. The next setup may be the same session, the same day, or the following week.
  - While the key high holds, trust the move and keep holding.
- **Timestamps:** [0:41:55](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2515) — next STH should be lower; if broken, the idea is flawed, don't force it · [0:50:47](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3047) — key high/low; violated means cancel the idea · [0:52:26](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3146) — move to the sidelines; can't force it

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Order block, ICT's actual definition (consecutive candles, not "the last candle")
body:
- **Kind:** definition (correction of common usage)
- **What ICT says:**
  - A bearish order block is the **consecutive series of up-close candles** before the down move, not "the last up-close candle before the down move". "That is not my order block... stop teaching that... call it something else."
  - On the 1h it was the last two up-close candles. On the 15m the same zone was five up-close candles.
  - Inside the order block's range you can hunt FVGs. You **don't need** price to trade below the last up-close candle first.
  - The "classic ICT bearish order block" entry: price trades down below the OB, then comes back up and bumps the bottom of the OB rectangle.
  - The "advanced interpretation" uses market structure: you're already expecting the sell-off at the weak ITH, so you see the imbalances forming inside the OB while it's still building.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1h, two up-close candles at the weak ITH make the bearish OB (shaded pink). On the lower timeframe, the last two candles inside the OB with a gap delivered "exactly to the quarter point" of a candle's high (check it on your own chart).
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:07](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1447) — the last two up-close candles = OB; "that is not my order block" · [0:25:44](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1544) — hunt FVGs inside the OB range; no need to trade below it · [0:39:32](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2372) — classic vs advanced OB interpretation · [0:43:31](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2611) — OB = one consecutive series; quarter-point precision

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Aggressive short inside the order block (no short-term low break required)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Standard model: a short-term low is broken (MSS), then price returns into the FVG to short.
  - Aggressive variant: with the HTF premise and a weak ITH, if a FVG forms with a breakdown inside the up-close OB candles, short the return into it. "Notice I don't need a swing low broken."
  - Stop right above the high.
  - It's a fractal: a small single-candle imbalance on the 15m mirrors the hourly imbalance. If price trades back to that candle's high, that's the aggressive entry.
  - The 15m is the bellwether for the actual in-and-out. If you don't like the risk parameters there, drop lower.
- **How to identify:** Daily premise (bearish), a 1h weak ITH at the rebalanced imbalance, 1h up-close candles (OB), then on 15m (or lower) a breakdown leaving a FVG inside the OB.
- **How to use:** Short the FVG or the OB bottom. Stop above the high. Target the HTF objective (daily low/SSL), often many times the risk.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15m. Five up-close candles inside the hourly OB, then a breakdown with a FVG. Price rebalanced it and the aggressive short followed. Heat was limited to one candle, the stop above the high, and the downside objective many times the risk.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:19](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1639) — fractal small imbalance; entry at the candle high · [0:28:58](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1738) — 15m bellwether; 1h frames the trade · [0:36:18](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2178) — 15m zoom: 5 up-close candles, FVG, no swing low needed · [0:42:43](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2563) — aggressive sell; stop above the high

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Classic low-risk / high-confirmation return-to-OB short
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price trades down below the order block, leaves a small gap, then trades back up into it: the short.
  - Stop above that candle's high.
  - Refine with the 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 minute charts.
  - A limit order at the bottom of the hourly bearish OB is the fill: heat limited to one candle's move, stop above the OB, large downside objective.
  - 4m view: price hits the 5m OB "perfectly", trades lower, comes back into the top of the HTF FVG with a little overshoot. That's fine in volatile markets. Expect "a measure of imperfection"; going slightly above a level doesn't mean it broke.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:43](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2563) — classic return-to-OB; stop above the candle high · [0:45:08](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2708) — limit at the OB bottom; heat one candle · [0:46:44](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2804) — 4m: overshoot is OK

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Institutional order flow: up-close candles are resistance in bearish swings, down-close candles are support in bullish swings
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - When bearish, all up-close candles should keep price from going higher than them. Price may come back and touch them (acting as a bearish OB, a "speed bump") but shouldn't trade above them. If price doesn't overtake the nearest up-close candles, it doesn't need to reach the ones above. Price "remains heavy".
  - When bullish, the swing has few down-close candles. Those should support price, without being overlapped below. It's permissible only if there's a short-term low in close proximity whose sell stops get taken before reaccumulation and continuation higher. If there's no nearby swing low (no SSL), there's nothing to worry about.
  - "Bullish swings: down-close candles are support. Bearish swings: up-close candles are resistance."
  - Use this to know the move is still good (hold without fear) and when it's likely flawed.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 4m/5m. After the OB short, rallies traded back into up-close candles but never overtook them. Later up-close clusters were never re-reached, and price kept falling.
- **Timestamps:** [0:48:22](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2902) — institutional order flow defined · [0:49:10](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=2950) — doesn't overtake the up-close candle; real resistance · [0:51:35](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3095) — speed bumps; bullish mirror · [0:53:13](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3193) — down-close overlap only OK if a short-term low with SSL is nearby

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Significant break in market structure and targeting projections
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - If price breaks a short-term low **and** an intermediate-term low (or just the ITL), that's a **significant break in market structure**, more meaningful than merely taking out a short-term low.
  - The long-term high to long-term low range is then used for targeting. Measure it and replicate it downward for generic price targets.
  - Alternative: anchor the Fibonacci from the **ITH** (the failed retracement where the decline begins) down to the long-term low that breaks. The **−1.5 standard deviation** projection marked the eventual low.
  - Why the ITH and not the earlier high? Because that's where the swing (the decline) actually begins; it's the framework. This answers years of "why did you anchor your Fib to that swing?" questions.
  - The long-term high/low range is generally linked to a higher-timeframe (daily) range, here the daily FVG framing.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1h. The ITH at the rebalanced imbalance, then a decline below the STL and ITL. Fib from the ITH to the LT low: −1.5 SD = the low of the move.
- **Timestamps:** [0:25:44](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1544) — LT high to LT low range used for targeting · [0:28:58](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1738) — STL and ITL taken means use the LT range · [0:30:34](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1834) — significant break; replicate the range · [0:32:11](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=1931) — Fib ITH to LT low, −1.5 SD; why that anchor
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Compare Ep. 8's −1 SD projection from the prior swing. Here the anchor rule (from the ITH where the decline starts) and −1.5 SD are explicit.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: How the algorithm "knows" where stops are
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The algorithm can't see any individual's stop. It knows where people will have stops based on short-, intermediate- and long-term highs and lows, and where the imbalances are. His terminology is a "language" built to describe visually what the algorithm does: "not exactly like the algorithm does, but very close".

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Why a daily FVG gets revisited (efficiency)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A one-sided single-candle (one-day) drop leaves too little time for buyers to participate. The algorithm allows efficient price delivery by going back up to offer those prices again, with an up candle balancing the move. It doesn't matter whether those buyers are right. Once rebalanced, price spends a little time, then displaces again toward the objective. This is "likely", not "must", and not necessarily immediate.
- **Timestamps:** [1:07:43](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=4063) · [1:08:32](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=4112) · [1:09:21](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=4161)

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Trade with the daily chart (salmon analogy); counter moves are traps
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Trading against what the daily chart is likely doing is "asking for failure". You can go long when the daily is going lower, but why swim against the tide like the salmon that spawns and dies? Quick counter-trend pops on the 15m or 5m are traps that create fresh selling opportunities when the daily continues lower. When the daily reaches its objective, stop and get your bearings again.
- **Timestamps:** [0:56:29](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3389) · [0:58:05](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3485)

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Neutral / no-trade condition and the "one-sided framing" test for high probability
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - After the daily objective (the old low) was hit during an overnight war-news drop, NQ came back above that old low. ICT's stance: **neutral, do nothing**. You can still be bearish, or bullish against the daily, but with greater risk.
  - He isn't trading anything (Forex, futures, stocks, bonds) for the rest of February because of global uncertainty ("money is running scared"). He openly says "I don't know." Knowing when not to trade is the greater lesson.
  - **High-probability test:** if you can easily frame a bullish idea and it's a hard stretch to frame a bearish one, the bullish side is high probability, and vice versa. If it "could go either way", don't take it. Those are the regret trades; he blew accounts in the 1990s that way.
  - He isn't in the business of picking tops and bottoms, and he teaches his paid group not to either.
- **Example in this video:** NQ March 2022 daily, late Feb 2022. The run below the lows was delivered, the rebalance into the daily FVG was delivered, the break lower came overnight on war headlines, and price is now back above the short-term/old low: neutral.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:30](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=150) — not convinced a low is in; no top/bottom picking · [0:58:54](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3534) — back above the old low means neutral · [0:59:40](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3580) — "I don't know"; no trades · [1:01:17](https://youtu.be/8GkQfdAXZP0?t=3677) — one-sided framing test

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 12
head: Technical science, not technical analysis
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He read John Murphy's *Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets* ("the retail trader's bible") in 1992–93. It's useful for knowing what NOT to do, since the 90% crowd follows it. Trend lines are subjective (which swing low do you anchor?). Reduce price to measurable relationships: "we don't do technical analysis, we do technical science."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Order block (high-probability bullish order block)  (aliases: bullish order block, down-closed candle, "higher time frame order block")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - In a bullish move, down-close candles should not be violated; they act as support. In a bearish move, up-close candles should not be breached.
  - A high-probability bullish order block = (1) the down-close candle, (2) an imbalance (fair value gap) left when price moves away from / above it, and (3) the underlying narrative that price is likely to go higher to reach buy-side liquidity. "That's it."
  - No engulfing-candle requirement — "forget all that, you don't need that."
  - An hourly down-close candle can be made up of two down-close candles on the 5-minute chart; consecutive down-close candles together are treated as one order block.
  - The "mean threshold" of the order block = the middle of the candle (body/range) — used as the line below which price should not trade once entered.
- **How to identify:** Down-close candle after (or during) a bullish run; price displaces away and leaves an FVG; higher-timeframe narrative points to a BSL target above (e.g. relative equal highs).
- **How to use:** Wait for price to trade back down into the down-close candle, ideally overlapping with the FVG, at a meaningful time (after the 9:30 equities open). Buy there; stop below the order block; target the buy stops above relative equal highs. A lower-timeframe order block + FVG nested inside a higher-timeframe order block gives the entry ("hierarchy higher time frame to a lower time frame").
- **Example in this video:** MNQ, 1-hour chart then 5m / 1m / 30-second, morning session of a Friday in early March 2022. After a run up, a down-close hourly candle formed; price rallied away leaving an imbalance. Relative equal highs above held buy stops, which he marked as roughly 14,110 (red line). After the 9:30 open, price retraced down into the hourly down-close candle (and its gap), in a discount of the low-to-high range (below 50%). On the 5m, price hit the order block, rallied, and traded back down into the gap between one candle's high and another's low, overlapping a lower-timeframe order block = his first long entry. Price went above the next down-close candle's high, retraced into an imbalance without eating through those down-close candles, he bought again; a third, shallower retracement only into an FVG (not back to the order block) was the final add. Price ran to the target above the relative equal highs.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:51](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=771) — rally leaves down-close candle; BSL above relative equal highs (~14,110). [0:13:39](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=819) — rule: in bullish moves down-close candles should not be violated. [0:17:38](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1058) — definition: gap + down-close candle + BSL narrative, no engulfing. [0:20:00](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1200) — 5m order block + FVG overlap entry.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicitly rejects the "engulfing candle" retail version of order blocks (and mocks a $7 order-block indicator). Simplified "public" language for the advanced structure taught in Ep. 12.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Fair Value Gap (FVG) — entry inside the gap; shallow retracement near the objective  (aliases: imbalance, gap)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Retracements in a bullish leg go down into an imbalance "so smart money can buy again."
  - When price is close to the profit objective, the algorithm generally does not retrace all the way back into the order block to rebalance; it only makes a small retracement into the FVG — buy at that candle's low.
- **How to identify:** The gap between one candle's high and a later candle's low (3-candle FVG) left during the rally.
- **How to use:** Enter on the retracement into the FVG, especially when it overlaps an order block; near the target expect only a partial fill of the gap.
- **Example in this video:** Third add on MNQ: retracement didn't reach the order block, only dipped into the FVG, then ran to target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:24](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1344) — retracement into imbalance without breaking the down-close candles. [0:23:12](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1392) — "classic": small retracement inside the FVG near the objective.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none stated.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Intermediate-term low  (aliases: "intermediate term low")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** A low with a higher low to its left and a higher low to its right (a short-term low flanked by higher short-term lows) is an intermediate-term low. Once price fills the gap and starts rallying from it, that intermediate-term low should not be taken out until the objective is reached.
- **How to identify:** Swing low flanked on both sides by higher lows (short-term lows), forming at the retracement into the imbalance/order block.
- **How to use:** Its integrity confirms the bullish leg; the whole leg is trusted while it holds.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ hourly/5m: the retracement low into the hourly order block was the intermediate-term low; "should never be overtaken until the objective's reached."
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:01](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=961) — higher low left and right = intermediate-term low. [0:21:35](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1295) — once the gap is filled it becomes an intermediate-term low that should not be taken out.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He admits classifying short/intermediate/long-term highs is the hard part from Ep. 12 and that this simplified language is meant to sidestep it.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Entries & stops — trailing stops below down-close candles
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Initial stop below the middle (mean threshold) of the bullish order block candle.
  - When price trades above a new down-close candle's high, your stop must remain below that candle's low — not inside it — because price can "dig into" that candle (it acts as an order block). Putting the stop inside it gets you stopped prematurely.
  - Once price rallies and takes out (goes above) a cluster of down-close candles, the stop can be raised to below that down-close candle (cluster), treating the consecutive down-close candles as one order block.
  - If price breaks the low of those down-close candles, being stopped out was correct — the move may be failing.
- **How to identify / use:** Each new bullish leg has its supporting down-close candle(s); trail the stop below their lows.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ: two consecutive down-close candles; price got very close to them on a retracement but did not eat through their range; he held.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:49](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1489) — stop below mean threshold; stop must stay below the candle's low. [0:25:37](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1537) — raise stop once the down-close candles are taken out.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Getting stopped early often leaves beginners afraid to re-enter — he calls that "infancy."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Judas swing / 9:30 opening retracement
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:** In a bullish context, price retracing lower into the 9:30 a.m. NY equities open is the "initial incorrect move" — like a Judas swing. Don't chase this down move, and don't chase price higher right before the 9:30 open either. The public reads the prior bounce area as resistance/support; the algorithm keeps pressing higher toward buy-side.
- **How to identify:** Bullish narrative + price dropping into the open into a discount PD array (order block/FVG).
- **How to use:** Time of day matters — he takes the opening price, extends it out in time, and wants the order-block retracement to occur after the 9:30 open; then look for the long.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ dropped after 9:30 into the hourly down-close candle/imbalance, below 50% of the range, then rallied.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:14](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=914) — time of day; opening price extended out. [0:18:24](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1104) — retracement after 9:30 = Judas-like fake move. [0:19:11](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1151) — checklist: discount, inside order block, equities open has happened, bullish.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Premium / discount (discount entry)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** For a long, look for a discount of the low-to-high range — below 50%.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ entry was below 50% of the range and inside the order block.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:11](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1151) — "I'm below 50, yes; I'm inside the order block, yes."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Buy-side liquidity (BSL) at relative equal highs / draw on liquidity
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** Relative equal highs look like "resistance / a ceiling" to retail traders; buy stops rest above them. The algorithm, unwilling to let price go lower, goes after profitable shorts' stops. The ideal exit for longs is where willing buyers (buy stops of shorts) are — when price trades above the level, buy stops become market buy orders, flooding liquidity so longs can sell at a higher price. Don't exit 6 or 10 points higher arbitrarily.
- **How to identify:** Two highs at roughly the same level; mark the level just above them.
- **How to use:** That level is the profit objective of the trade.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ, ~14,110 above the relative equal highs (red level).
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:51](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=771) — "just going to call it 14,110." [0:16:49](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1009) — retail sees ceiling; price should go over. [0:20:49](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1249) — why exits sit at buy stops.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Intermarket: index correlation (ES leading NQ)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** NQ and ES generally move in tandem. If ES has energy to the upside while NQ is lethargic, NQ tends to be drawn higher "in sympathy" — "all boats rise in a high tide."
- **Example in this video:** The morning of the trade, ES had a lot of upside energy; NQ lagged; he expected NQ to follow.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:29](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=629) — markets move in tandem.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a "laggard catches up" use, not an SMT divergence signal.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Higher-timeframe draw before a counter-trend move (bearish macro, bullish retracement target)
body:
- **Kind:** example
- **What ICT says:** He is technically bearish on equities, but price already ran below the lows (his weekly objective), so he would not sell short. Instead he asks what price could reach up into: the open (or low) of a prior up-close candle and/or an FVG above, then could resume lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:41](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=581) — possible retracement targets above.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Risk management — pyramiding (largest position first)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Build the biggest position at the initial entry, then each add is smaller (3 micros, then 2, then 1) — a stable pyramid. Buying 1, then 2, then 3 is an "inverted pyramid" — unstable. The earlier, larger position's equity supports the adds so you can weather a deeper retracement. Adds only while price is still below the objective. He counts the whole thing as one trade.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ demo: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 micro contracts; $10,000 hypothetical account → $12,111 (≈21% on one trade). 6 micros required about $1,200 margin (hypothetical AMP Futures discount broker). MNQ = $2 per point (4 ticks).
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:59](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1919) — pyramid: 3 then 2. [0:32:47](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=1967) — inverted pyramid unstable. [0:33:34](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=2014) — one trade, 3 scalings, $10,000 → $12,111. [0:34:21](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=2061) — 6 micros ≈ $1,200 margin.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Says this gearing was "optimal" for $10k; more would have been too much leverage. "Stop thinking you need a lot to make a lot."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 13
head: Micro vs mini futures
body:
- **Kind:** example
- **What ICT says:** Micro E-mini Nasdaq: 1 point = 4 ticks = $2. Micros are enough to grow an account if you compound.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:16](https://youtu.be/tpPtItWqmlg?t=676) — MNQ point value.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 14
head: 2022 Mentorship model (MSS → FVG limit entry → BSL target)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (applied)
- **What ICT says:** Market structure shift to the upside, then wait for price to drop back into the fair value gap; enter with a limit order there; aim for a run above the buy-side level.
- **How to identify:** Bullish MSS (short-term high taken) with displacement leaving an FVG; an obvious BSL level above; an opening gap above to fill.
- **How to use:** Limit buy in the FVG; first target at/above the BSL level; scale out; final target at the gap-fill/limit level.
- **Example in this video:** Micro Nasdaq (MNQ), morning session (the session after Friday's close — likely a Monday; date not stated). Bullish MSS; long 12 micros on a limit order inside the FVG — the fill was at the low candle. Targets: run above 14,160 (BSL), initial interest 14,180, 14,220 "possible today". Price ran above the short-term high made prior to 10:00 a.m. and made a new equity-session high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:01](https://youtu.be/NUdu1n-ML98?t=1) — MSS up, gap fill from Friday's close, long 12 micros, targets 14,160/14,180/14,220. [0:00:48](https://youtu.be/NUdu1n-ML98?t=48) — limit entry; FVG closed. [0:03:56](https://youtu.be/NUdu1n-ML98?t=236) — final limit fill; entry was at the low candle.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** none.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 14
head: Opening gap fill (gap from Friday's close)
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** He looks for a "gap fill from Friday's close" as the draw; when price got very close to closing that gap he took partial profits.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ — took 6 contracts off as price neared the closure of the gap; 14,220 seen as the full fill/objective.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 14
head: Fair Value Gap as reaccumulation zone (bull-flag behaviour)
body:

- **What ICT says:** While long, he watches whether price keeps driving toward and through a small FVG above (~14,122–14,138). Price may consolidate in that area and "reaccumulate for new longs", like a pause / bull flag, roughly 14,120–14,140.
- **How to use:** Consolidation at an FVG during an expansion is not a reason to exit; expect continuation.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ consolidated around the FVG level "reaching into an order block" before continuing up.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:48](https://youtu.be/NUdu1n-ML98?t=48) — small FVG ~14,122–14,138. [0:01:34](https://youtu.be/NUdu1n-ML98?t=94) — bull-flag-style reaccumulation 14,120–14,140.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 14
head: Buy-side liquidity vs retail "resistance"
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** Buy-side liquidity sits around 14,160. Price will often consolidate there with a small retracement that gets people thinking it's time to short; retail sees 14,160 as resistance because price fell from there before. He expects it to "bust through the door" and run to 14,180.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:22](https://youtu.be/NUdu1n-ML98?t=142).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 14
head: Targets & partials / trade management
body:

- **What ICT says:** Plan: take 6 of 12 contracts off above 14,180 "to fund the position," roll the stop to break-even, then leave a limit order at 14,220 for the rest. While in the trade, watch candles (expansion), not the P&L number.
- **Example in this video:** He took 6 off slightly early as price got near the gap closure ("change my mind and close it here"); the remaining limit order then filled.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 15
head: Market structure shift (bullish) + FVG completion
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (applied)
- **What ICT says:** He wants to see the swing high broken — that makes market structure bullish. Then he waits for the candle to close to "complete the imbalance" and marks the low end of the fair value gap.
- **How to identify:** Swing high taken with displacement; the third candle's close defines the FVG.
- **How to use:** Buy when price returns into the FVG.
- **Example in this video:** NQ (live account), morning: swing high broken → bullish; FVG formed; entry in the FVG around the 9:30 open.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:06](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=6) — wants the swing high broken. [0:01:45](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=105) — waiting for the candle close to complete the imbalance.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 15
head: 9:30 open volatility / stop-run below the FVG (narrative over mechanics)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - At the 9:30 equities open, volatility can overshoot the FVG low; if price comes back up into the FVG he will buy it.
  - Buying blindly at the open is risky — "you don't know how far it's going to whip below that low."
  - Price going below the just-formed short-term low (which is outside and below the FVG) does not negate the FVG, because he uses narrative: traders see the bullish move, buy, and place stops below that swing low; those sell stops (13,612) get taken.
  - Entering long right there is a "high-risk entry."
- **How to identify:** Bullish structure + FVG + a short-term low just below it holding obvious sell stops; the open sweeps them.
- **How to use:** After the sweep, buy as price re-enters the FVG; expect energetic expansion afterwards.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: sell stops at 13,612 were taken at the open, then price re-entered the FVG and he went long.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:35](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=155) — open can overshoot; don't know how far it whips. [0:03:23](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=203) — narrative; sell stops at 13,612 taken.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines a strict "FVG invalid if its low is broken" reading — a sweep of the adjacent short-term low can be part of the setup.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 15
head: Premium / discount — target an FVG in premium
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** There's an FVG at the "680" level, above equilibrium, so it's in a premium; that's why he targets it ("the 80 level"). About 50 handles away → roughly $1,000+.
- **Example in this video:** NQ target ≈ 13,680 (stated as "680"/"80 level" — full price inferred from the 13,612 level).
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:00](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=300).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He believes price goes much higher (daily could reach ~14,000, "a bit of a stretch") but takes the nearer premium FVG because he's on vacation and wants the round equity figure.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 15
head: Displacement / expansion after entry
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** After entering at the open he wants price to "expand aggressively," an "energetic run" above the swing high just to the left — no dilly-dallying.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:00](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=300), [0:05:48](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=348).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 15
head: Fair Value Gap as support during the run
body:

- **What ICT says:** A small FVG formed in the last three candles up; it doesn't need to be filled or revisited, but if revisited, price should be supported by it — i.e. not trade below the "630" level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:48](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=348).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 15
head: Entries & stops — mental stop at the open
body:
- **Kind:** rule / caveat
- **What ICT says:** He normally uses a stop loss, but when trading the open stops "can be taken really easily and then reverse." He allows price to go slightly below the low and would close at market. He explicitly does not encourage trading without a stop; he is at the screen ready to close. Once in profit he could put the stop at entry.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:13](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=253), [0:05:00](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=300), [0:06:45](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=405).
