title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 15
head: News drivers — high-impact event day (FOMC, caption unclear)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If stopped at break-even he would move to the sidelines and take no more trades that day because of the event (caption reads "F1 see"; likely FOMC). On such days "you can trade in the morning but you got to be done early"; equity traders must be aware of the economic calendar because volatility comes later in the day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:45](https://youtu.be/tGxuitjtO88?t=405).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Swing high / swing low (3-candle definition)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A swing high is a candle with a lower high on the candle before and the candle after. Not to be confused with an MT4 fractal — that takes more candles (five), and "five candles later... you've already missed the move."
- **How to use:** Once the swing-high candle's following candle closes (on the daily, "this candle closes the next day"), start looking for a short opportunity.
- **Example in this video:** ES M2022 daily: price ran above relative equal highs (BSL), then printed a 3-candle swing high; next day (Friday) he looks for shorts.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:00](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=60) — run above relative equal highs, swing high. [0:01:50](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=110) — not an MT4 fractal.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Power of 3 / AMD with opening prices (midnight and 8:30)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Anticipate an open, a rally (manipulation), then distribution — accumulation, manipulation, distribution — combined with premium/discount analysis.
  - For index futures there are two opening prices: **midnight New York** and **8:30 a.m.** (the open of whatever candle begins at 8:30 — 1m, 3m, 15m, hourly; "it doesn't matter what candle you use").
  - If bearish, ideally price trades **above** the opening price — that's the manipulation, a Judas swing ("market protraction"): price going opposite to where it will go later in the day.
- **How to identify:** Bearish daily bias; mark midnight and 8:30 opens; look for the rally above them into a premium PD array.
- **How to use:** Sell after the run above the opening price once structure breaks and a FVG retrace occurs.
- **Example in this video:** ES Friday: price traded higher in the morning above the opening price, then broke lower attacking sell-side liquidity and ran into the daily bullish order block.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:50](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=110) — Power of 3. [0:04:58](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=298) — two opening prices: midnight and 8:30. [0:05:45](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=345) — bearish: trade above the opening price = manipulation / Judas.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Clarifies student confusion: any timeframe's 8:30 candle open is fine.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Order block (daily bullish order block as draw / discount array)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** In a premium after a run above old highs, the down-close candle below is the bullish order block — a likely target if price goes lower. Its level is the **opening price of the down-close candle**, extended out in time onto lower timeframes. Relative equal lows above it add sell-side liquidity: SSL "by itself... is likely, but it's further likely if we have a discount array."
- **Example in this video:** ES daily bullish order block at **4504** (open of the down-close candle). Relative equal lows on the hourly sat above it. Price ran the lows and tapped the OB; the reaction was strong.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:36](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=156) — down-close candle as bullish OB. [0:03:24](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=204) — level 4504; relative equal lows. [0:07:19](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=439) — OB level extended onto the hourly; reaction.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Fibonacci swing projection on candle bodies ("fulcrum point" targeting)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement (targeting)
- **What ICT says:**
  - When structure has shown a willingness to go lower — swing low "decisively broken," then a retrace into the FVG — the broken low is a **fulcrum point**. Measure from the swing high down to that low and project the same distance lower ("this is my swing trading model and I'm applying it to targeting").
  - Anchor the Fibonacci on the **highest body** (open or close, doesn't matter which) of the swing high and the **lowest body** (open or close) of the swing low — not the wicks. "The wicks and the tails are all distractions"; this is how the algorithm reads price. He learned it in forex and says it carries over to index futures; it was less pure in the open-outcry era.
  - Using wick high to wick low will not give the measurement — "that's why everybody that uses Fibonacci struggles."
  - Precision only helps when the narrative is already in place (liquidity + discount array); otherwise "a thousand lines on your chart" will hit something.
- **How to identify:** Displacement breaks a swing low; retrace into FVG; measure the bodies of that high-to-low swing.
- **How to use:** Use the projections as targets; choose the one that confluences with the HTF draw (OB / below relative equal lows).
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m, Friday morning: projection levels **4514.50** (first) and **4501.25** (next). 4501.25 sits just below the daily OB at 4504 — and the actual daily low was exactly **4501.25**. Exact Fibonacci extension settings were shown on screen, not spoken.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:06](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=486) — swing low broken, retrace into FVG, fulcrum point. [0:08:53](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=533) — anchor on highest/lowest bodies. [0:10:29](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=629) — targets 4514.5 and 4501.25. [0:12:05](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=725) — daily low 4501.25 exactly.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicitly contrasts with standard wick-anchored Fibonacci use. "You can't predict daily highs and lows" — he says you can, if you understand the algorithm's elements.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Daily bias framed on the daily chart
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** "The majority of your analysis should be framed on your daily chart" — where is the expansion likely to take price, higher or lower? That carves out your bias. The daily draw (OB at 4501.25/4504) doesn't need to be hit yet; you know it's the draw.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:32](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=872).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Bearish setup checklist (15m) — displacement, MSS, FVG, above opening price
body:
- **Kind:** rule / checklist
- **What ICT says:** Build-up into premium; market breaks aggressively (displacement down); did it take out the swing low? yes; did it trade back up into the imbalance? yes; did it trade above the opening price? yes — "probabilities are now going through the roof." Then price traded to the old swing low (SSL), through it, aggressively rebalanced the down move back into a bearish order block, sold off again, into and past lunch to the daily bullish OB.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m Friday; the 9:30 retrace into the 15m FVG was the main entry.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:19](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=919), [0:16:06](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=966).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Higher-timeframe FVG as framework for lower-timeframe entries
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** On the 5m, the return into the 15m FVG at 9:30 "does not look clean"; you might not see it as a sell because it wasn't filled on the 5m. The 15m provides the framework/context — "we don't need it to trade up into that [fully]." On the 1m, a small FVG right above a short-term high was the setup.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:41](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1061) — 5m vs 15m. [0:19:17](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1157) — 1m view of the same retrace.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Multiple setups per session (morning session)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Split day: morning session 8:30 a.m.–noon; NY lunch noon–1:00 p.m.; PM session after.
  - Max four trades: two in the morning, two in the afternoon (from his "real money, real results" series).
  - Morning typically offers **2–3 setups** because volatility comes in at the 9:30 open; the open is tricky — you can get caught offside. He prefers students wait for the initial move to "qualify" the expected direction.
  - Repeating pattern: short-term low broken with displacement → FVG → return into FVG → short → target the broken short-term low (fulcrum) / next SSL.
- **Example in this video (ES 1m, Friday morning, bearish):**
  1. First FVG after a short-term low broken with energetic displacement; short on the return; first objective the fulcrum short-term low. E.g. 2 contracts: take 1 off there, let the other ride toward the lower-timeframe objective (daily OB) later in the day.
  2. Another short-term low taken, FVG, retrace into it → short; target the run below the next low.
  3. Another imbalance after an aggressive move lower; retrace came close to the stop of the earlier short.
  4. A shallow run below an old low → anticipate a deeper run; take a partial below that low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:10](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=10) — sessions and lunch. [0:16:54](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1014) — max four trades, 2 AM / 2 PM. [0:18:28](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1108) — 2–3 setups in morning; qualify the initial move. [0:22:33](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1353) — walkthrough of setups 1–2. [0:26:29](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1589) — setup 4, re-entry after missed entries.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Some days have only one or two retracements, or the move happens right at the open and you miss it — be happy your analysis was right.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Lunch hour rule & partials
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He doesn't take entries during lunch (noon–1:00 p.m. NY) but profits can be taken then. A limit order at the order-block level "plus a couple points" can fill during lunch; no need to babysit once the position is funded (one contract off, stop to break-even).
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:33](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1353), [0:23:21](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1401).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Index futures vs forex delivery
body:
- **Kind:** rule / opinion
- **What ICT says:** Index futures are more precise and uniform — everyone works with the same price; many of his trades came within a quarter point of his stop without hitting it. In forex you trade in your broker's in-house liquidity pool and they can widen spreads. Forex is "quiet" now; he tells students (private and YouTube) to follow index futures until currencies loosen up.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:55](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1495), [0:25:42](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1542).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: PM session buy-side liquidity pool (Friday reversal / position squaring)  (new coinage: "PM session buy-side liquidity pool")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The pink-box zone above the **most energetic high of the morning session** — the high that launched price down to the daily target.
  - Because it's Friday, the daily objective has been hit, price is in a discount and has traded to the lower end of the week, expect a retracement back into the weekly range: position squaring / short covering by smart money that sold all morning. Shorts holding over the weekend put stops above that high → liquidity.
  - Retail sees relative equal lows broken ("support broken") and sells when price returns to them; smart money buys from those sellers — "engineering buy-side liquidity on the basis of sell-side flow."
  - Premium for the PM: take the morning high (the 8:30/9:30 rotation high — either works) down to the low; above 50% = premium; the PM draw is into that premium.
- **How to use:** Look for longs in the PM targeting the buy stops above the morning's energetic high.
- **Example in this video:** ES Friday PM: after tagging the daily OB, price repriced from discount to premium into the pink buy-side pool.
- **Timestamps:** [0:28:05](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1685) — defines the pink rectangle. [0:28:52](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1732) — Friday, weekly range retracement, weekend-hold stops. [0:29:42](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1782) — 50% of the morning high-to-low = premium. [0:32:49](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1969) — short covering; engineering BSL on sell-side flow.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He personally won't hold index positions over the weekend (gap risk).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Algorithm summary: discount ↔ premium, liquidity, imbalance, time then price
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The algorithm seeks discount to premium and premium to discount; within that it reaches for liquidity (buy stops / sell stops) and/or imbalances (creating FVGs or returning to them) — on the basis of **time, then price**. He calls it a gross oversimplification but "by and large that's all these things do." All you need: liquidity, imbalances, time of day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:28](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1828), [0:42:19](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2539).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Mitigation block (PM long)
body:
- **Kind:** example
- **What ICT says:** Market structure breaks (to the upside), price comes back down into the mitigation block which also has an imbalance/FVG → be a buyer, aim for the buy stops in the PM pool. He references levels 4532 and 4540 as the price ranges to think about (relation to the earlier chart).
- **Timestamps:** [0:34:23](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2063), [0:35:09](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2109).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Old high as support (old highs become a discount array)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If price trades above an old high, that old high becomes a discount array — broken old highs can act as support ("not all the time"). What makes them real support/resistance is the narrative: when you know price is drawing up to buy stops, a retest of a broken old high that also fills an imbalance is a buy.
- **Example in this video:** ES PM: price traded back down, hit an old high to the left and filled an imbalance, then ran up to the pink BSL area.
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:09](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2109), [0:35:58](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2158) — "something for your notes."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Market structure shift + stacked FVGs (confirmation entry)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model
- **What ICT says:** After filling buy-side liquidity in the pink area, price breaks a swing low (MSS); short on the retrace into the FVG aiming for the low or the order block. Or wait for a confirmation entry: after hitting the FVG it breaks lower again, another 1m structure break with an imbalance. Rule restated: **if you have an FVG with a small FVG right above it, anticipate price trading up into the upper one** — use it as the entry; target the order block.
- **Timestamps:** [0:36:47](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2207), [0:37:34](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2254).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: "Buying and selling pressure" myth / DOM
body:
- **Kind:** rule / opinion
- **What ICT says:** He doesn't trade with the DOM — spoofing means resting orders may not be there; he sees no advantage in it (but won't argue if it works for you). Price doesn't need volume to move: a candle can be created with two transactions — price reprices/gaps to a level and one market order trades there.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:14](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=1874), [0:43:54](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2634).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Unique model / fractal setups
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Your unique model is a setup so similar every time it repeats the same idea on a different chart, day, or timeframe. Traders using the same concepts can take opposite trades on the same day. Everything is fractal — 30-second and 15-second charts show even more setups; staying on a 15m chart and trading the daily range is fine.
- **Timestamps:** [0:47:05](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2825), [0:47:54](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2874).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 16
head: Risk management — pyramiding
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Biggest position first, then smaller adds (e.g. 5, then 3, then 2), roll into the objective — gives equity velocity. Buying 1, 2, 4, 8 is reckless; he has "roasted accounts" doing it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:48:41](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2921), [0:49:28](https://youtu.be/EpGQnhjXBq8?t=2968).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Daily bias from liquidity (BSL taken → SSL next; "unfinished business")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** Once price runs above relative equal highs (buy stops taken) and turns lower, the next draw is the sell stops below. Two areas of SSL: relative equal lows ("two little devils") to the left, and a further low. Monday's candle low had not yet taken out the prior low → "unfinished business" below. After three consecutive down-close daily candles, the bias for the next candle is bearish.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD daily: run above relative equal highs, three down-close days, Monday's low not yet below the relative equal lows; Tuesday expected lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:03](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=63) — run above relative equal highs. [0:01:51](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=111) — relative equal lows; unfinished business; bearish bias. [0:03:28](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=208) — why buy stops above highs feed smart-money shorts.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Institutional price levels / big figure
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Big-figure (00) levels are very influential because a lot of commerce/liquidity transacts around them. Institutional price levels: the 00, 20, 50 and 80 levels.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD 1.0900 big figure as the downside objective, sitting at the daily relative equal lows.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:16](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=256), [0:05:03](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=303).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Fibonacci swing projection on bodies (standard deviation / fulcrum point)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (targeting) — revisits Ep. 16
- **What ICT says:** Anchor on the highest up-close/open body in the retracement and the lowest open or close of the swing (not wicks). The projected levels are valid **only if the swing low (fulcrum point) is broken**. Choose the target where the projection converges with liquidity/big figure: the lowest projection level that doesn't go through 1.09.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD: projection levels 1.0919, 1.0900 and 1.0901 ("essentially the big figure"); converging with relative equal lows at 1.09 → target 1.0901. The day's low was (he recalls) 1.0901; price reached the Fib standard deviation and the daily relative equal lows (blue line), with candle bodies respecting the level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:03](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=303) — revisits swing projection. [0:05:51](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=351) — 1.0919 / 1.0900 / 1.0901; only true if the low breaks. [0:06:41](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=401) — which level to aim for. [0:17:48](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1068) — reached projection and daily lows.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Buy-side liquidity pool (hourly) absorbed before the decline
body:
- **Kind:** example
- **What ICT says:** On the hourly, price traded up into the buy-side liquidity pool level, "absorbing all of that liquidity," broke down taking several short-term lows, retraced, broke lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:41](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=401).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Power of 3 / Judas swing (midnight opening price, protraction)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** At midnight New York the day begins; if bearish, you want a rally first — "market protraction," against the expected intraday direction — the Judas swing / manipulation leg of accumulation-manipulation-distribution. It trades up into a HTF imbalance, which tends to form the daily high; then look for distribution lower the rest of the day. Preferably price trades **above** the midnight opening price — that's where smart money accumulates shorts. The algorithm repeatedly offers price above the opening price; that's "not buying and selling pressure."
- **How to use:** Hunt shorts at or just above the midnight opening price, combined with time of day (killzone) and a PD array.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD 15m: midnight open extended; price went above it several times ("higher once more... and again") before beginning its descent into the daily range low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:29](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=449) — want a rally from midnight = Judas swing. [0:08:18](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=498) — rally into imbalance forms the daily high. [0:09:05](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=545) — trade above the midnight opening price. [0:09:52](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=592) — not buying/selling pressure; add time and price.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Killzones — FX New York open killzone vs index futures
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - **FX New York open killzone: 7:00–10:00 a.m. ET** — specific to FX pairs; hunt your setup within that block.
  - **Index futures: 8:30–11:00 a.m.** (he says "your local time" meaning NY); he can take index trades up to 10:40–10:45 and still be OK.
  - FX: generally no new trades after 10:00 a.m. unless there's a news driver. A 10:00 a.m. high-impact release extends the NY killzone into the 11:00–11:30 window.
  - Other post-10:00 drivers: e.g. CAD traders must allow for crude oil inventories, usually around 10:30 a.m.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:52](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=592) — 7–10 for FX; 8:30–11 for indices. [0:11:28](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=688) — killzone annotation on 5m. [0:24:07](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1447) — trade until 10:40–10:45 in indices; no new FX trades after 10 unless news. [0:24:54](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1494) — 10:00 news extends killzone to 11–11:30; oil at 10:30.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Order block (bearish) — defined by FVG + displacement + last up-close candle; use the body
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Price ran up, overshot the imbalance a little, and reached the last up-close candle = bearish order block. How you know it's an order block: the imbalance after a nice move lower (displacement + FVG), and price trading back up to the last up-close candle. He prefers to annotate/expect returns to the **body** of the order block candle, not the long wicks.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD 15m/5m: OB hit early in the NY open killzone around the 7:00 hour; later the 10:00 news spike ran back into the body of the same bearish OB.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:39](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=639) — overshoots imbalance to last up-close candle. [0:15:25](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=925) — return to the OB body, not wicks.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Opening price selection — midnight vs 8:30 (FX)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** NY-session FX traders use the 8:30 a.m. opening price but also refer to the midnight open ("recalibrate at 8:30"). If bearish and the 8:30 opening price is **lower** than the midnight opening price, use the lower one — it sets the minimum threshold for the Judas swing/protraction up. Reverse for bullish: look for a move below the opening price to go long.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:28](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=688) — recalibrate at 8:30. [0:18:35](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1115) — use the lower of the two when bearish.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: News drivers (ISM Services PMI) as volatility injection / stop raid
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He doesn't care about the data, expectation, or what the number means — only that the algorithm uses the injection of volatility at or around that time to reprice and facilitate trades ("it's a rigged game" for those not in the know). High-impact news is the "wild card": it's designed to stop out traders trailing stops above recent swing highs, jamming price above the opening price so their buy stops become counterparty to smart-money shorts. You may avoid news if you don't know what you're doing, "but don't be afraid of them."
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD: 10:00 a.m. ET ISM Services PMI; price dropped after the 7:00-hour OB tap, then retraced up into the 10:00 release, back above the midnight open and into the bearish OB body, then fell.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:15](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=735) — ISM Services PMI at 10; volatility only. [0:16:13](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=973) — news as stop-raid wild card. [0:24:54](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1494) — don't be afraid of news.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Intermediate-term high (protected by an imbalance)
body:
- **Kind:** rule — refers back to Ep. 12
- **What ICT says:** After a swing low took out a prior low, price rallied once more above the midnight open but did **not** take out the earlier high, because there's an imbalance (FVG) below/associated with that high. That makes it an intermediate-term high — if bearish, it shouldn't be taken out. Not merely because there's an imbalance, but because the narrative is lower prices + it went above the midnight open + the imbalance.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:50](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=830), [0:14:38](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=878).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Swing high + displacement + FVG entry (5m/4m)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (applied)
- **What ICT says:** Return into the OB forms a 3-candle swing high (lower high either side) → look for displacement lower → market structure shift → retrace into FVG → short. On the 4m chart, a clean FVG in the down leg: price runs right up into it, closes it, "then and only then" aggressively runs below the short-term low toward the objective.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD 4m: FVG between one candle's low and another's high; price filled it, displaced lower to ~1.0901 (low of day per his memory).
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:25](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=925) — three-candle swing high. [0:17:00](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1020) — find the FVG on the 4m (pause and look). [0:20:11](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1211) — FVG hit, displacement to 1.09.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 17
head: Entries, stops & targets in FX (fluffing exits for spread)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Don't aim for the exact level — "fluff up" exits by **3–5 pips**; beginners use **10 pips**. E.g. target 1.0900 → limit to cover shorts at 1.0905.
  - Spreads: every broker can widen the spread when it suits them; overzealous limits have cost him many "amazing exits."
  - Stop above the entry candle's high (or above the swing high if you want more room).
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD hypothetical: entry ~1.096 (as captioned), stop 1.09728 — he'd round the risk to ~10 pips; target just above 1.0900. Risk-to-reward better than 8:1; on a hypothetical $100,000 demo / funded-challenge account this one trade "gives you basically what you're looking for."
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:11](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1211) — fluff exits 3–5 pips. [0:21:00](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1260) — 1.0905 limit for a 1.0900 target. [0:21:46](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1306) — spreads; 10 pips for new traders. [0:22:33](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1353) — entry/stop numbers. [0:23:20](https://youtu.be/5WIqHJDQ_p4?t=1400) — >8:1 R:R.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Entry/stop figures are as heard in captions; the gap between them (~12.8 pips if entry is 1.0960) doesn't exactly match his "round to 10" comment (caption unclear).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Daily bias & commit to one direction
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Start bias analysis on the daily chart. A bias is "just an idea that you want to work within": you take shorts when bearish and filter out the other side unless clearly proven wrong. Flip-flopping intraday (going long, then short, back and forth) draws down or blows the account. Your bias won't be perfect and neither is his. Know what you're looking for ahead of time so you're not chasing impulsive swings.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD bearish bias carried from the Ep. 17 (Tuesday) lesson; draw = the old daily low below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:01](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=481) — bias bearish, FX-specific discussion. [0:11:12](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=672) — commit to one direction. [0:11:59](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=719) — bias isn't perfect; filter out the other side.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Fair Value Gap (daily) — retracement target in discount; only need a touch
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** After 5 consecutive down days, with price deep in the range (discount), a retracement is likely. As soon as the daily FVG forms, expect a short-term bounce up into it. Price only needs to trade to the FVG's edge (that candle's high) — "you can be greedy" and wait for the midpoint, deep fill, or full closure, but "I don't need that." Time of day then decides the entry; you don't need to catch the high of the day.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD daily: big drop toward an old low, next day's candle traded up creating the FVG; Thursday's rally touched it (slightly above the marked premium level).
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:47](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=527) — only need it to trade into the FVG. [0:15:57](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=957) — five down days, discount, bounce into FVG.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says a pattern of high → low → higher high around the daily FVG might look like his "bearish breaker" but is not, because the discount (lower) edge of the FVG — the candle's high — is lower than the swing low (caption reasoning brief; see [0:02:26](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=146)).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Previous day's high & low as intraday framework (old highs/lows, last 3 days)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The daily draw on liquidity (the old low) is not your intraday trade target — it may not happen in one day. Instead frame each day with the previous day's high (premium level) and low (target). There's lots of liquidity around daily highs and lows; "institutional mindset traders" use them and high-frequency algorithms attack them. His first lesson on BabyPips (2009–2010): mark the previous day's highs and lows for the last 3 days — "you're never going to run out of trades."
- **How to use:** Bearish day: expect the open to rally just above the previous day's high (Judas swing) back into the FVG, then sell targeting the previous day's low.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD: Wednesday's high marked red (premium), Wednesday's low marked as target. Thursday opened, rallied, popped just above the short-term high into the daily FVG, then sold off toward Wednesday's low. Range of opportunity roughly 60 pips (he reads it as from ~…935 to ~…874 — figures caption unclear).
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:45](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1005) — targets; mark the FVG-day low. [0:17:32](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1052) — daily DOL isn't the intraday target. [0:18:20](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1100) — Thursday Judas into FVG; HFT attacks previous day highs/lows. [0:19:08](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1148) — last 3 days' highs/lows.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Chart layout & multi-timeframe workflow (daily → hourly → 15m → 5m)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / process
- **What ICT says:**
  - Layout: upper-left = daily, lower-left = hourly, right (biggest) = 15m. The **15m is his "bellwether" chart** — referenced throughout the day for managing positions, stalking new setups, and trusting intraday bias.
  - TradingView link button: drawings on one timeframe appear on all timeframes of that symbol. With one laptop/screen, just switch timeframes — annotations carry over.
  - Set the chart time zone to **New York** wherever you live, so time-of-day elements match his teaching.
  - Hourly: mark only the frame of reference (daily FVG, liquidity pool, relative equal highs, previous lows), then move to 15m.
  - 15m: vertical daily divider at midnight NY; midnight opening price (15m candle; if scalping use the 5m) drawn out in time to **11:00 a.m. NY**.
  - Don't enter new positions from a phone (too compressed, can't see the lay of the land); managing a trade on a phone is OK.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:39](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=99) — daily top-left. [0:23:08](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1388) — layout and 15m bellwether. [0:21:33](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1293) — no new entries on a phone. [0:28:43](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1723) — midnight open extended to 11:00; set chart to New York.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Relative equal highs (hourly) + midnight open — higher first, then lower
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied)
- **What ICT says:** On the hourly, the daily FVG also shows, with relative equal highs below/at it (buy-side liquidity pool). On a bearish day, the market wants to "go higher first to go lower": after the midnight open, rally above the relative equal highs into the FVG, then displacement down breaking a swing low and creating an FVG.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD: 6 April low mapped; new day 7 April at midnight NY. At ~5:25 a.m. NY (London) price swept the previous day's (6 April) low first; he ignored London because it didn't give the rally into his level. The rally into the premium level/daily FVG came at **9:30 a.m. NY**, above the relative equal highs, then displacement lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:44](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1484) — hourly relative equal highs. [0:30:20](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1820) — rallied above them; displacement; swing low broken; FVG. [0:45:21](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2721) — 5:25 a.m. sweep of 6 April low; rally at 9:30.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Killzones — FX New York session and order placement
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - FX NY session/killzone: **7:00–10:00 a.m. NY**; look for the setup to form inside it.
  - Killzones are when you **determine your entry and place your orders**, then walk away — the fill doesn't need to happen inside the killzone. If you can't derive an order placement by then, you have nothing to do that day.
  - If the limit isn't filled by **11:30 a.m.**, pull it — no good-till-cancel. Otherwise it may fill at a bad time of day, keep running through the relative equal highs and stop you out.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD: setup identified ~10:00 a.m.; limit sell placed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:55](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1915) — FX killzone 7–10. [0:32:43](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1963) — order placed at 10:00. [0:47:42](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2862) — pull unfilled order by 11:30. [0:48:29](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2909) — killzones are for order placement.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: FVG entry — 15m minimum expectation, refined on 5m (parent/subordinate imbalances)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - 15m: after the displacement, put a limit sell at the FVG "or plus one pip"; stop above the high. If the imbalance is very stretched you can use it for the stop; if worried, put the stop above the swing high. This is the "minimum expectation" entry.
  - Then split the 15m down into 5m and look for FVGs inside that 15m down-leg for a fine-tuned entry (5, 4, 3, 2, 1-minute).
  - **Higher-timeframe imbalances are the parent; lower-timeframe imbalances are subordinate.** He rejects a viewer's claim that the smaller-timeframe FVG must form before the HTF one — "it never works like that."
  - You can choose any price within the 5m FVG range — that's where your unique style comes in; the more greedy, the more likely you don't get filled.
  - "Low threshold entry" (first touch) has the most pips of risk, but money risk is controlled by leverage/position size.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD 5m inside the 15m leg: one small FVG, one stretched FVG, another small FVG; the entry used was in the 5m FVG with a secondary small FVG above it, which price traded up into.
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:43](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=1963) — 15m limit and stop. [0:33:30](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2010) — drop to 5m. [0:34:17](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2057) — HTF imbalance is parent. [0:35:54](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2154) — pick any price in range; low-threshold entry.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Stacked FVG rule (small FVG above your FVG)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If you settle on an FVG and there's a small FVG right above it, expect price may trade up into the upper one — but place your limit in the lower one (it might not reach the upper), and your risk/stop must incorporate the upper one. Overzealous limit prices are "fleeting" — he's teaching how to avoid missing trades and operate consistently.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:15](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2535), [0:43:02](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2582), [0:43:49](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2629).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Order block — must have an imbalance; consecutive candles; change in state of delivery
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement (corrects popular misuse)
- **What ICT says:**
  - "What makes an order block valid? It has to have an imbalance. Without the imbalance, there is no order block." That's why it's not supply and demand (he doesn't require "fresh" zones; he'll trade through candles/fractals).
  - Three consecutive up-close candles = **one consecutive bearish order block**; "the order block begins with this candle's low" (the lowest candle of the run).
  - Price does **not** need to reach the last up-close candle (the highest one, before the down move) — the common "last up-close candle" definition is wrong here. The reason it's not reached: the higher-timeframe parent imbalance (15m FVG range) stops price there. Trading into the bottom candle of the three is enough.
  - "What is an order block? It's a change in the state of delivery." As soon as price trades below the order-block candle's open, the algorithm starts delivering sell-side; then it breaks the swing low — "changed gears internally."
  - Many YouTubers parrot his order block buzzword without understanding it; learn it from the source.
- **How to identify:** Run of consecutive up-close candles into the premium/HTF array → displacement below the lowest candle's open → swing low broken → FVG present.
- **How to use:** Enter in the FVG that overlaps the lower portion of the OB; disqualify the upper candles (don't expect price to reach the top one).
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD 5m: the run into the daily FVG and above the hourly relative equal highs = 3-candle bearish OB; price traded into the lowest candle and the FVG, not to the last up-close candle; then sold off.
- **Timestamps:** [0:38:17](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2297) — three candles = one bearish OB. [0:40:39](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2439) — must have an imbalance; not supply & demand. [0:41:26](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2486) — why the last up-close candle isn't reached (parent 15m imbalance). [0:46:07](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2767) — "it's a change in the state of delivery."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines/contradicts the simplified "last up-close candle before the down move" OB used in earlier YouTube teaching; also echoes Ep. 13's requirement of an imbalance. Early statement of the Change in State of Delivery (CISD) idea.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Market structure shift (internal) & intermediate-term high as stop location
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Breaking the swing low = an internal bearish shift in market structure. Any rally after that is a "suspect rally" setting up another run lower. The high that has the imbalance is an intermediate-term swing high — it should not be exceeded — so the stop goes above it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:43:49](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2629) — internal shift. [0:46:56](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2816) — suspect rally; intermediate-term high; stop placement.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Targets — previous day's low; trade result
body:
- **Kind:** example
- **What ICT says:** Target = the 6 April low (previous day's low). The limit sell filled, price broke lower and reached the target at 2:45 (afternoon): ~**40 pips**. Not the highest high and price went a little lower afterwards — "who cares?"

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Entries & stops — no ultra-tight stops
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Stops of 1 pip or half a pip might work occasionally, but not once you put on size; you'll sweat every tick. Wider (structure-based) stops let you walk away from the chart; he cares where price is going, not whether it touches his stop.
- **Timestamps:** [0:44:35](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2675).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Risk management — leverage, not pips, is the real risk
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** A larger stop in pips is not more risk in money — you control the amount via leverage/position size. Leverage is what traders abuse because they ask "how can I make the most?" — the axe that hits the target can come back and hit you in the head.
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:54](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2154), [0:36:41](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=2201).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Model simplicity (what to ignore)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If starting over, he'd use only this 2022 model — not the central bank dealer's range, not the Asian range, nothing not mentioned in this model. "This literally is the simplest way to work with intraday and daily order flow." Applicable to forex, bonds, (with caveats) gold.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:37](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=337), [0:06:25](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=385).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 18
head: Market selection — gold is event-driven
body:
- **Kind:** rule / opinion
- **What ICT says:** Gold usually needs a geopolitical or "something crazy" event to move; otherwise it's highly manipulated with stop hunts and consolidations — frustrating, not ideal for aggressive short-term trading for new traders (he doesn't deny some people profit in it).
- **Timestamps:** [0:51:39](https://youtu.be/eai0nHhAC8w?t=3099).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Fair Value Gap — fractal "signature" of the 2022 model  (aliases: imbalance, fair value gap, "the gap")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / example
- **What ICT says:** The repeating signature he wants students to look for is: price creates a FVG, breaks a low (or high), comes back and fills the gap. It may partially fill, go halfway, or completely close it; you do not need pinpoint precision, an "average" entry with sound money management is enough. The same pattern he teaches on 1m–5m exists on the hourly chart; it applies to forex, bonds and futures, not just index futures.
- **How to identify:** Break in structure, then a FVG made by one candle (the gap between the candle before's low and candle after's high); look at candle *bodies*, allow wicks/tails to poke through ("the volume of the move is inside the bodies").
- **How to use:** The retrace into the gap typically lands near 50% of the "parent" price swing (the whole swing from the low to the high that produced the gap).
- **Example in this video:** DXY hourly at the 101 level: market drops, takes a swing low, leaves a FVG; price comes back up and the candle bodies respect the gap while wicks go slightly above it. Then it "breaks aggressively," runs stops below several lows, fills the gap and goes right below the low, which was ~50% (equilibrium) of the parent swing.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:29](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=389) — the signature described; [0:10:27](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=627) — DXY hourly, bodies respecting the FVG = algorithmic delivery; [0:13:38](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=818) — hourly fractal of the YouTube model, 50% of parent swing; [0:15:14](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=914) — single-candle imbalance, bodies vs wicks.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He stresses this is "algorithm delivering price," not supply/demand, harmonics or indicators.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Order Block (bearish and bullish)  (aliases: OB, "up close candle", "down close candles", "bookmark")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** A bearish order block is the up-close candle(s) right before displacement lower; a bullish order block is the down-close candle(s) right before displacement higher. It is a *change in the state of delivery*: price was dropping, pauses with up-close candles, then resumes. The algorithm "bookmarks" that spot and refers back to it, like a bookmark in a book you return to and pick up the storyline. The displacement "qualifies" the order block because it creates a fair value gap. He says the order-block material sold by others (books on Amazon) is "completely wrong" and that he is withholding more order block theory for his book trilogy (volume 2).
- **How to identify:** Bearish: lowest up-close candle in the cluster before the down-move; use its *low* and its *opening price*, extend them forward in time. Multiple consecutive same-direction candles together form the block (two up-close candles on DXY 15m; three consecutive down-close candles on ES 1m). Must be followed by displacement that leaves a FVG.
- **How to use:** Levels within the block: candle low (easiest to reach for a bearish OB above price), the open/body, the **mean threshold** (50% / midpoint of the order block), and the high (least likely). As a target, pick the "lowest hanging fruit" (for a bearish OB above price, its low).
- **Example in this video:** DXY 15m: hourly FVG with an additional 15m imbalance inside; price comes up deeper, closes it in; two up-close candles before the drop = bearish OB; low of lowest up-close candle + its open, projected forward, "hammered it." ES 5m and 1m: down-close candles + FVG at the low of the day act as bullish OB entries (see ES case study).
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:47](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1247) — DXY 15m bearish OB, low and open of lowest up-close candle; [0:23:08](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1388) — OB = change in state of delivery, bookmark analogy; [0:25:29](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1529) — displacement qualifies OB by creating FVG; [1:20:58](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=4858) — target levels inside the OB (low, open, mean threshold, high).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says the algorithm does not know where *your* stop is; it works off the common logic of stops placed/trailed just above recent short-term highs.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Mean Threshold  (aliases: half of the order block, median of the order block)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** The mean threshold is the halfway point (median) of an order block. On the ES daily he draws it as the midpoint of the bearish OB candle and uses it on lower timeframes as one of the possible targets.
- **How to identify:** 50% of the order-block candle's range (he draws it from the daily up-close candle).
- **How to use:** Intermediate target between the OB's low/open and its high.
- **Timestamps:** [1:18:37](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=4717) — mean threshold defined on the ES daily OB.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Trailing-stop liquidity above short-term highs  (aliases: buy stops above short-term high, trailing stop loss mentality)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In a decline, shorts trail their stop to just above the most recent short-term high (because books teach it). So above the short-term high in a down-move there are buy stops; in an up-move, longs trail stops under recent lows. He is "not a big fan" of rushing his own stop for this reason.
- **How to use:** Treat those trailed-stop levels as liquidity targets. In the ES afternoon he points to a run down into sell stops of traders who trailed stops up before the final PM push.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:41](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1481) — trailing stops above short-term highs; [1:23:21](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5001) — buy stops above the high of a down-move.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Higher-timeframe bias vs. contrarian (counter-trend) trading  (aliases: institutional order flow, contrarian setups)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Institutional order flow is rooted in higher-timeframe bias. Short-term counter-bias moves are part of natural retracements; you "can and will absolutely lose money" trading them as a new student, swinging buy/sell/buy/sell. Some of his students are naturally contrarian and pick spots where retail sees a reversal of the HTF bias (e.g., he is long-term bullish DXY; they short where retail thinks DXY has topped). That's fine because it matches their personality, but new students should learn to trust HTF bias first; if you are contrarian it will show over time.
- **How to use:** Don't try to pick tops/bottoms; there is plenty of opportunity between intermediate-term highs and lows. He doesn't mind missing the long-term high/low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:50](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1010) — staying on right side of institutional order flow; [0:18:26](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1106) — don't pick tops and bottoms; [0:25:29](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1529) — counter-trend warning; [0:26:16](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=1576) — contrarian students.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "I'm not teaching the trend is your friend": his frame is discount→premium / premium→discount within market structure, not trend-following indicators.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Optimal Trade Entry (OTE) in a counter-trend retracement  (aliases: 62–79 retracement, short-term premium)
body:
- **Kind:** example / refinement
- **What ICT says:** 62% and 79% retracement levels are the OTE range he teaches. In a contrarian long against a bearish bias, you can buy the low and simply target the 62% retracement level (or "above the bodies" of the candles in the prior down-move), keeping it easy. That's a "bread and butter" ~30–40 pip move.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD hourly: daily low at 1.0806 + one pipette (1.08061) gets run on a slam lower (during Passover week); price rallies, creates a FVG, runs back toward old highs into the 62% retracement of the high-to-low (short-term premium). EURUSD 15m: displacement off the old daily low leaves a clean FVG; buy the retrace into it, sell at the hourly 62% retracement, ~30 pips.
- **Timestamps:** [0:47:41](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=2861) — EURUSD hourly, daily low 1.08061 swept; [0:48:28](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=2908) — OTE into short-term premium, contrarian; [0:49:15](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=2955) — 62 and 79 = OTE range, target 62%; [0:54:49](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=3289) — 15m version, ~30 pips, not recommended for new students.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicitly "against the order flow"; something to backtest, not for developing students to trade live.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Narrative after a liquidity run (sell-side taken → seek buy-side)  (aliases: draw on liquidity, short-term oversold)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Once an old daily low is taken, the market is "short-term oversold on the daily"; sell stops/sell-side liquidity have been removed, so the market now looks for buy-side liquidity. An energetic displacement off that low that leaves a FVG is the algorithmic tell; a trade back down into the gap is a buy even though newer traders fear "it'll go below these equal lows."
- **How to use:** Buy the retrace into the displacement FVG; target the short-term high / above the bodies / 62% retracement.
- **Timestamps:** [0:53:15](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=3195) — EURUSD 15m clean FVG off old daily low; [0:54:02](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=3242) — narrative: SSL taken, now BSL.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Consolidation → wait for displacement  (aliases: sideways consolidation, congestion, sloppy price action)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** When a market goes back into sideways congestion, he has no bias and waits for displacement in either direction to define a new range. After displacement, use the range: if it breaks lower, look for a retrace above 50% into the 62–79% premium; vice versa if it breaks higher. When charts are sloppy/back-and-forth (GBPUSD hourly and 15m in this video), there is "nothing" to trade; close the charts.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD: price went below short-term lows, short-term break in structure, came back to fill the FVG, spent a lot of time there (holiday + new week, slow volume) and popped back into the range. GBPUSD: bearish below the FVG (invalidated if it trades above it), but hourly/15m have nothing worth trading; he hasn't traded cable for months.
- **Timestamps:** [0:50:52](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=3052) — no bias, wait for displacement; [0:51:41](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=3101) — 50% of range, 62–79 objective; [0:59:36](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=3576) — GBPUSD "nothing on this chart"; [1:09:54](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=4194) — manipulated market = rattlesnake, back away.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Messy price means "heavily manipulated," not that the algorithm stopped working. Holiday weeks (Passover/Easter) leave money on the sidelines; give it a few days to a week to clean up.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Swing low (3-candle definition) & Dealing range  (aliases: daily dealing range, range high/low)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A swing low has a candle to its left with a higher low and a candle to its right with a higher low. The daily dealing range is drawn from the most recent swing low to the swing high of the move (he skips older relatively-equal lows and uses the swing where "this move started"). On the 15m he picks "the most energetic, most recent" low and the higher high above relative equal highs as the dealing range.
- **How to use:** Measure equilibrium (50%) of the dealing range; a retrace to ~50% = short-term discount (bullish bias for next day) or premium.
- **Timestamps:** [1:17:04](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=4624) — swing low definition, daily dealing range; [1:32:52](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5572) — 15m dealing range choice.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Daily bias from equilibrium of the dealing range  (aliases: daily bias, short-term discount)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If the daily chart retraces to ~50% (equilibrium / short-term discount) of its dealing range, there's a likelihood the next day (or the day after) will be bullish. You go into the next day expecting higher prices; if the next day is down or flat you still expect higher. Then identify the premium array the market will draw to (e.g., a daily bearish order block above) and pick the easiest target.
- **How to identify:** Daily dealing range → 50% hit → look above for the premium PD array (OB low / open / mean threshold / high) and for old highs / relative equal highs.
- **How to use:** You're not predicting the daily close; you want to participate in the *morning-session* move in the bias direction into the target, not the whole leg.
- **Example in this video:** ES June 2022 daily: market traded into a deep discount, retraced to ~50% of the dealing range from the most recent swing low; next-day bias bullish; premium array = last up-close daily candle before the down-displacement (bearish OB), targets its low, body, mean threshold, high. Buying below the opening price on the bullish day could reach the candle's low (easiest), body, and the mean threshold.

head: Purge and Revert  (aliases: purge and revert, run on sell stops then revert to 3-day high)

The high of a three-day decline has buy stops resting above it (shorts' trailed stops). He tells viewers to search his channel for the original "purge and revert" video.
- **How to use:** After the purge of the short-term low, expect a draw back to the 3-day high (combined here with the daily OB target and the 15m relative equal highs).
- **Example in this video:** ES: on the 18th price took out a short-term low below old lows (≈50% of the daily range); counting day 1, 2, 3, the high three days back is the revert target, which coincides with the relative equal highs on 15m.

body:

- **What ICT says:** Two level highs = relative equal highs; they "engineer" buy stops because retail sees double-top resistance, shorts there with stops above, and treats the sideways drift as a bear flag (projecting a measured move lower). When it "looks too perfect, too pristine, too classic support/resistance," expect it to be run. Old highs/lows and relative equal highs/lows are the easiest, most visual targeting method; that logic will never change because stops always rest above old highs and below old lows.
- **Example in this video:** ES hourly/15m: two level highs above the consolidation = BSL; this became the day's target.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Smart-money order pairing  (aliases: offset, pairing orders, counterparty)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (narrative logic)
- **What ICT says:** When price purges sell stops below old lows, smart money pairs their buy orders with those sell stops and is now net long. To get out they must sell to willing buyers at higher prices: the buy stops resting above old highs. So after sell-side is taken, the draw is to buy-side. Continuum: smart-money buys ↔ retail sells, smart-money sells ↔ retail buys. If you don't think about how orders are paired before you click "enter," you are gambling.
- **Timestamps:** [1:28:07](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5287) — narrative: purge sell stops, net long, need buy-side; [1:28:54](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5334) — "think algorithmically how you pair your orders"; [1:31:17](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5477) — point of origin / terminus, SM vs retail order continuum.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: New York Midnight Opening Price vs. 8:30 Opening Price  (aliases: midnight open, midnight candle opening price, 8:30 open, "last ditch for Power of 3")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement (answers viewer confusion)
- **What ICT says:** Set TradingView to the New York time zone regardless of where you live. The New York midnight candle's opening price, extended forward, is the price he preferably wants to buy *below* when bullish (sell above when bearish). 8:30 ET is when the news embargo lifts; the 8:30 candle's opening price is the "last ditch" Power-of-3 reference. Rule: if bullish and the midnight opening price is *lower* than where price trades around/after 8:30 (price never comes back below midnight open), midnight isn't a factor, so use the 8:30 opening price. If price is below the midnight open and, after 8:30, also below the 8:30 open, the market is "really in a discount" and that is the "dandy," silver-platter setup.
- **How to identify:** Use the actual opening price of the 00:00 ET candle and the actual opening price of the 8:30 ET candle (wait for 8:30 exactly). He does *not* use the daily candle's opening price on TradingView (nothing inherently wrong with it, but for clarity and continuity he doesn't).
- **How to use:** Bullish day: buy below midnight open; best when price also drops below the 8:30 open into a FVG/OB taking short-term sell-side. Bearish day: mirror. No indicators, divergence or Fibonacci are needed to see the "oversold" condition.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m/5m, April 19, 2022: price below the midnight open; at 8:30 price drops below the 8:30 open too, runs short-term swing lows into a bullish FVG + two down-close candles (OB), finds support at the 8:30 opening price, springs aggressively above short-term highs. Daily low ~4377 (caption "43.77"); the daily bar open on TradingView (~4404.5, caption unclear) differs from his midnight open.
- **Timestamps:** [1:25:43](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5143) — introduces midnight and 8:30 opening prices; [1:34:28](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5668) — set chart to New York, buy below midnight open, 8:30 = news embargo lifts; [1:36:52](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5812) — the midnight-vs-8:30 decision rule; [1:44:52](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=6292) — doesn't use TradingView daily open, uses actual midnight and 8:30 candle opens.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Clarifies earlier 2022 mentions of "opening price at midnight / 8:30" that confused viewers. You don't need the low of the day.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 19
head: Judas Swing & Power of 3 (daily and session level)  (aliases: Judas swing, micro Judas swing, AMD, accumulation-manipulation-distribution)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** The Judas swing is the move opposite to what you expect the daily range to be; if bullish, you "love" the move down after midnight. You don't have to buy the London/overnight lows; you can wait for 8:30. A drop below the 8:30 opening price (after already being below midnight open) is a *micro* Judas swing for the New York session; the move below midnight open builds the low of the daily candle. Both are Power of 3 (accumulation, manipulation, distribution): each move below an opening price is "the trap / snare" catching traders who think it's going down.
- **How to use:** On a bullish day, look for that *specific* drop (below opens, into short-term sell stops and a FVG/OB) then expect displacement higher into liquidity; then offset, sell to buyers, move to the sidelines.
- **Example in this video:** ES: price moves from the range down after midnight (Judas swing of the day); then 8:30 drop below the 8:30 open (micro Judas), rally.
- **Timestamps:** [1:32:05](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5525) — narrative steps: daily delivery, Judas swing, buy below opening, displacement, run into liquidity, offset; [1:38:29](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5909) — Judas swing definition, don't need London lows; [1:39:15](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=5955) — micro Judas swing for NY session, Power of 3 AMD; [1:40:02](https://youtu.be/IEa1N0rTtbc?t=6002) — each move below opening price is the trap.

head: ES case study, April 18–19, 2022 (full intraday sequence)  (aliases: "dandy of a setup")
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says / what price did:**
  1. Daily: ES traded into deep discount, retraced ~50% of dealing range, purged short-term sell-side on the 18th. Monday evening (18th) he told the private group ES should go higher to the 15m relative equal highs.
  2. Hourly/15m: brutal back-and-forth consolidation; relative equal highs above = BSL target; dealing range = most recent swing low to the higher high above the REH.
  3. 5m: after midnight, price drops (Judas). At 8:30 price drops below the 8:30 open into a bullish FVG + two down-close candles (OB), taking short-term swing lows; rallies, returns to the 8:30 opening price for support, then springs above short-term highs ("by itself that's enough").
  4. Holding for the daily range: price reaches the target area; consolidates at lunch; around 2:00–3:00 pm runs down into sell stops of traders who trailed stops up; then pumps into the PM session up into the 15m relative equal highs.
  5. 1m "YouTube model" overlay: run above a short-term high = bullish market structure shift; FVG; trades down into it, three consecutive down-close 1m candles = OB + FVG → buy; retests; retraces up into the NY midnight opening price, back into another gap and its midpoint; rallies, consolidates, expands into the 15m REH.
  6. At the 9:30 equities open another opportunity forms: OTE retrace, then rally up the daily range to the candle high that equals the 15m REH. Low of day ≈4377.

head: Intermarket analysis: DXY as barometer / false breakout  (aliases: inverse relationship, teeter-totter effect, trading market vs barometer)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In forex your trading market (e.g., EURUSD) needs a barometer to measure its movement: the dollar index. Their relationship is inverted. If DXY is going down to a level you've identified as a bullish/buying point, then EURUSD rallying at that moment is likely a *false breakout* and becomes a shorting opportunity at the exact moment DXY hits its level.
- **How to use:** Mark the DXY level where you expect a dollar low; watch the EURUSD high at the same moment (here, taking out the previous week's high = buy stops). Once DXY reaches its level, look for a short in EURUSD.
- **Example in this video:** As DXY hit the ~99.92 area, EURUSD ran above the previous week's high (cleared buy stops) — same instant — then reversed lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:44](https://youtu.be/Q6GFu8-Z4rY?t=524) — EURUSD runs previous week's high, why it's a false breakout; [0:09:30](https://youtu.be/Q6GFu8-Z4rY?t=570) — barometer and inverted relationship; [0:10:17](https://youtu.be/Q6GFu8-Z4rY?t=617) — same moment DXY hit the buy level; [0:15:50](https://youtu.be/Q6GFu8-Z4rY?t=950) — teeter-totter: dollar higher puts weight on euro.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He didn't take either trade (asleep, and not trading forex now) — he doesn't need every move.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 20
head: Displacement requirement for the FVG entry (which low to use)  (aliases: energetic move away, displacement, parabolic gap)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** He uses the short-term low that the *displacement* breaks, not a nearer low, because the FVG needs price to move energetically *away* from it. If after the FVG candle closes the next candle opens right at the low and hasn't moved away, there's no displacement yet. A limit order is not placed while price is still inside/near the gap area; it's placed only after price has displaced away from the FVG.
- **How to identify:** Run on buy stops (here, above old weekly high) → price drops through a short-term low (market structure shift) with an energetic candle leaving a FVG → price moves away from the gap.
- **How to use:** Then put a limit order at the FVG (for a short, at the top edge / the high of the candle that defines it). Don't chase if it goes deeper first; wait for the retracement while the killzone is open.
- **Example in this video:** EURUSD 2m, London session (day after Ep. 19, ~April 21, 2022): after running above the old weekly high, price trades lower and takes the short-term low with a FVG; MSS; price goes a bit lower without retracing, then rallies back into the FVG = entry.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:39](https://youtu.be/Q6GFu8-Z4rY?t=759) — why that low: next candle opened right at it, no displacement yet; [0:13:27](https://youtu.be/Q6GFu8-Z4rY?t=807) — limit order only after price moves away from the FVG.

- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** The NY midnight opening price is used to trade the London session (2:00–5:00 a.m. NY) and to frame the daily range Power of 3. If bearish, the ideal is a rally *above* the midnight opening price (the daily Judas swing) then decline; if bullish, a decline below it. He sleeps through London ~90% of the time; at ~7:00 a.m. he checks: if bearish and price made a Judas rally above midnight open and is now below it, he has an edge on daily bias and expects another short-term rally, ideally above the 8:30 opening price.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m: only two tiny moves above the midnight open — an anemic Judas swing (he wanted ~15–20 handles); a viewer said Power of 3 wasn't in effect, he says it was, just very small. London (3:00 a.m.) broke down.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:27](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=627) — midnight open, anemic Judas, expected 15–20 handles; [0:12:50](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=770) — midnight open used for London session and daily Power of 3; [0:15:12](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=912) — bearish want rally above, bullish want decline below; [0:29:34](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1774) — recap + 7 a.m. check routine.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Clarifies Ep. 19's teaching from the bearish side; tiny Power-of-3 moves can still count but may not be useful.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 21
head: 8:30 Opening Price = New York session opening price  (aliases: 8:30 open, NY session open, Power of 3 for NY session)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition
- **What ICT says:** The 8:30 opening price is the New York *session* opening price (the NY session in his model is 8:30–11:00 a.m. NY local time), not to be confused with the NY midnight open. He uses it for the Power of 3 of the New York session with the same logic as midnight: if bearish, he wants a rally above the 8:30 open — a Judas swing / "false rally" / "suspect rally" — and he fades it (sells into it).
- **How to identify:** Extend the 8:30 candle's opening price forward. (On a 4-minute chart the candle shows as 8:28; don't let that confuse you.)
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:00](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=960) — 8:30 open = NY session Power of 3; Judas swing = false/suspect rally to fade; [0:24:00](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1440) — NY session = 8:30–11:00; [0:25:37](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1537) — 4m chart shows 8:28, open never traded above.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 21

body:
- **Kind:** entry model (restated)
- **What ICT says:** Normally: look to the left, before 8:30, for a short-term high; after 8:30 price rallies above the 8:30 opening price and runs those stops, then breaks down with displacement and an imbalance (FVG); price rallies back into the imbalance and sells off (entry there).
- **Example in this video:** On this day on the 5m the model did *not* form: price never rallied above the 8:30 open.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 21
head: Extremely heavy (one-sided) market: trading without the Judas rally  (aliases: "too heavy," wilting market, no short-term premium)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** If you're bearish and price fails to rally above *both* the midnight open and the 8:30 open, it's extremely bearish — it can't even reach a short-term premium above the key opening prices at key times. Such a market won't give "stunning little short-term rallies" to fade; either you get in where you can on small pockets of imbalance (FVGs) in the direction of the move, or you miss it. This doesn't mean the algorithm/concepts changed; it happens in futures, commodities (corn, soybeans, gold, oil) and stocks. Leaving out the "rally above the 8:30 open" element takes courage and isn't scalable with the public model; otherwise just tape read.
- **Example in this video:** ES: below midnight open and 8:30 open all day; 15m retrace into a bearish OB + imbalance, rolled over just before 9:30; 3m imbalance and bearish OB re-entries; 2m and 1m FVGs refining entries; a FVG rallies up to a bearish OB and sells off with stop above; price drives into the noon low; lunch retrace; aggressive selling into the PM session/close.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:47](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1007) — no rally above either open while bearish = extremely bearish; [0:17:34](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1054) — small pockets of imbalance or miss it; [0:19:10](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1150) — heavy markets must be traded differently; [0:36:43](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=2203) — 1m/2m imbalances without needing the 8:30 rally.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Modifies the standard model's requirement of a run above the 8:30 open; ICT presents it as coaching, not part of the YouTube model.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 21
head: Two-FVG rule: enter at the lower gap, size stop for the upper gap  (aliases: stacked FVGs, signature in price action)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In the London open setup on ES: displacement lower with a FVG, rally up into a bearish OB and FVG, then a micro structure shift below a short-term low with another imbalance. With two FVGs stacked above price in a short, the upper one *can* be traded to on a spike, but your entry is on the lower FVG and your stop must allow for price trading up into the upper one. Don't assume you'll get the better (upper) entry — here price never went there. He calls this kind of thing a "signature" that repeats algorithmically.
- **How to use:** Short: limit at lower FVG; stop above the upper FVG. If the risk is too large, trade a micro contract or skip.
- **Example in this video:** ES London open (~3:00 a.m. NY) — "the only real sound entry" of the day in his view.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:56](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1196) — London setup, micro structure shift, two FVGs; [0:20:45](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1245) — "this as the entry and this as the risk."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 21
head: 9:30 Equity Open  (aliases: 9:30 opening, stock market open, RTH open)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** 9:30 is when stocks begin trading their NY session; it brings initial volatility. It can whipsaw in a small range, or in a large range clear both buy-side and sell-side, and then the real move for the day unfolds; wait for it. On this day 9:30 simply accelerated the move already in motion since 3:00 a.m. London.
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:24](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1584) — what to expect at 9:30; [0:27:12](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1632) — today it accelerated the London move.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 21
head: Power of 3 (AMD) explained for a bearish day  (aliases: accumulation-manipulation-distribution, fractal Power of 3)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Power of 3 is fractal. Bearish: smart money *accumulates* short positions; then *manipulation* above the opening price, where they add more shorts; then price goes the other way and they *distribute* (cover) at an important low that can be forecast — daily relative equal lows, old daily lows, Fibonacci projections — in agreement with time of day.
- **Example in this video:** ES moved down into the lunch hour beginning at noon, made an important low, retraced during lunch (punched above a high once), broke down, consolidated, then continued into the afternoon.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:48](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1488) — AMD explained, distribution at forecastable low with time of day; [0:25:37](https://youtu.be/kmVXVJE08eQ?t=1537) — lunch retracement then afternoon continuation.
