title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Draw on liquidity first, order block second  (aliases: DOL, magnet, bullseye)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** New students always want to know which order block / entry candle to pick — that's the *easiest* part. What matters is what the market is likely to do and where it's going to draw to and why; spend most of your study on that and on reading the tape. Picture a magnet at the target level pulling price (TradingView's magnet/bullseye icon used to mark it).
- **Example in this video:** ES June 2022 daily: daily bearish OB + seasonal tendency + risk-off dollar → draw to the daily relative equal lows, which were tapped on April 29, 2022.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:04](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=4) — recap: bearish OB, seasonal, REL; [0:01:40](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=100) — picking the order block is the easiest thing; [0:06:25](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=385) — magnet analogy for the DOL.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Imbalance + gap respected by candle bodies  (aliases: permissible price action, bodies vs wicks)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** Wicks poking slightly beyond an imbalance is "permissible price action" you must get used to; what matters is that candle bodies stay inside the imbalance — the wicks reach for liquidity/stops but the bulk of the volume is held inside.
- **Example in this video:** ES hourly: previous day pumped higher, fell just short of a high, declined, paused, then gapped down and rallied back; between one candle's low and the next candle's open there's an imbalance coupled with an actual gap; five or so candles wick just above it while bodies stay inside; then price releases lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:01](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=481) — imbalance coupled with a gap; [0:08:49](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=529) — bodies inside, wicks reach for liquidity.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Premium/discount relative to old highs/lows  (aliases: short-term premium, short-term discount)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Any time the market trades *above an old high* it is in a short-term premium (it's going into liquidity); any time it trades *below an old low* it's in a discount. Trading above the 8:30 opening price also puts it in a premium on a bearish day. Like overbought/oversold, premium can still go higher and discount can keep going lower — so it must be read through the narrative.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:25](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=625) — 8:30 open traded above = premium, above old high = premium; [0:11:16](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=676) — definition, viewer question answered.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Narrative vs. market structure  (aliases: narrative, present narrative)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Market structure "is not the answer"; it frames an idea, but the idea must align with the present *narrative*: why the market should go where you think on that particular day, based on the climate, economic calendar events, and the volatility being offered for that session/day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:04](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=724) — narrative defined.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Power of 3 on a bearish day / breakout traders as counterparty  (aliases: open-rally-distribute, AMD)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Bearish day Power of 3: the open, a rally up (manipulation) creating the high, then the move lower; smart money sells short into buy stops above highs, then offloads (covers) their shorts into sell stops below relative equal lows. Daily REL attract long-term trend-following/breakout traders who sell at market when they break — the perfect counterparty for smart money buying back shorts. Smart money enters near the high above the opening price, exits at an important low, and the market closes near the low of the day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:51](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=771) — Power of 3 described; [0:13:40](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=820) — trend followers' breakout sells pair with smart money; [0:14:26](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=866) — enter near high above opening, close near low.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: 9:30 open stop run → displacement → FVG (15m checklist)  (aliases: equity open, 2022 model checklist)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example
- **What ICT says:** At 9:30 the stock market opens (the bell). Checklist on the 15m: Did it take a high out? Did it break below a low? Was it displacement (energetic)? Did it trade back up into the imbalance? If all yes, you can be a seller to get in sync and, as a swing/short-term trader, aim for the old daily relative equal lows.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m, April 29, 2022: 9:30 runs a short-term high, breaks lower leaving an imbalance; retrace into it = sell; target = daily REL (blue line), which was reached.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:38](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=578) — 9:30 open, four-question checklist; [0:10:25](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=625) — aim for daily REL.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: ES 1m short: FVG entry and stop placement  (aliases: stop above FVG candle)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** On the 5m, relative equal highs sat above the opening price (buy-side liquidity), with other nearby highs too ("too rich" to expect the farther ones). Price punched up through them, broke down, came back once more above the opening price, then "gave up the ghost" and ran for sell-side. On the 1m: run above REH → break of a swing low with displacement → back up into the FVG, above the opening price → short. Stop must be *at minimum* above the candle that creates the FVG (conservative: higher). A big stop reflects volatility; worrying only about max profit while dismissing risk is what gamblers do.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:16](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=916) — 5m REH above opening price; [0:16:03](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=963) — runs them, breaks, aggressive sell-side run; [0:16:59](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1019) — 1m checklist; [0:17:46](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1066) — stop above FVG-creating candle.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Afternoon session re-entry after 1:30 p.m.  (aliases: PM session, post-lunch retracement)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He likes to go back in at ~1:30 p.m. (has traded earlier). After 1:30 the lunch hour has smoothed out and there's usually a retracement higher when the day is bearish (lower when bullish) — that retracement into an imbalance / relative equal highs is a short (or long) entry.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m afternoon: retrace runs up into an imbalance / REH → short; another small FVG retrace → short, aiming for the daily REL line.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:34](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1114) — 1:30 re-entry rule; [0:19:21](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1161) — afternoon shorts into daily REL.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Stacked FVGs: where to enter and where the stop goes  (aliases: two fair value gaps rule)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (restated, reinforcing Ep. 21)
- **What ICT says:** If there is only one FVG, place your entry there and don't expect a deeper retracement. If there is another FVG beyond it, expect price to "stab up into" that one, so your stop must be positioned to weather it — either have deep pockets or use micros. Trying to sell the highest candle / buy the lowest (being "ICT junior") makes you miss moves.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5m: after displacement below relative equal lows, a FVG right above, and another one above that; price did extend into the upper one.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:33](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1353) — two FVGs, expect stab into the upper one, micros vs $20/point; [0:23:20](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1400) — rule: one FVG vs two FVGs; [0:24:07](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1447) — don't hunt the exact top/bottom.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Swing-point hierarchy: long-, intermediate-, short-term highs  (aliases: market structure nesting, fractal)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** A swing high followed by a break lower *with an imbalance* qualifies as an intermediate-term high. When two such highs nest (the later one lower than the earlier), the earlier one is a long-term high and the later one an intermediate-term high. A retracement inside that bearish structure forms a short-term high, which should respect the underlying bearish order flow and go lower toward sell stops below the lows. The same pattern (REL → high taken → break with displacement → FVG → retrace with bodies respecting it) repeats smaller and smaller: it's a fractal.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5m/1m, April 29, 2022: high run (buy stops taken, breakout longs trapped), REL broken = MSS on 5m during a bearish period; a smaller copy of the move forms below it: REL, high taken, two candles broken, FVG, bodies respecting it, aggressive break lower; then retracement = short-term high under the LTH and ITH.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:46](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1306) — buy stops taken, REL broken, MSS; [0:24:54](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1494) — fractal repeat; [0:25:41](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1541) — two narratives, LTH vs ITH via imbalance; [0:26:27](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1587) — STH inside bearish structure should respect order flow.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Order block refinement ("calibrate") and midpoint entry  (aliases: top-down OB refinement, mean threshold entry)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:** He uses the up-close candle in the retracement as a bearish order block — "I'm telling you how to read the tape," not the YouTube model. "Calibrate" = top-down: take the 5m order block, go to the 1m, refine it, and enter as price retraces and hits the *midpoint* of the block. A small counter-signal on the 1m (e.g., an opposing OB/FVG) is subordinate to the higher-timeframe bearish structure. Wicks above the OB are fine as long as candle bodies (the bulk of the volume) stay inside it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: price retraces up into the 5m up-close candle area (shaded zone); on the 1m he enters around the midpoint; price wicks above the OB but bodies stay inside, then breaks lower with displacement → REL → displacement → FVG; price comes back into the FVG and exactly to the bottom of the bearish order block (he notes he says "bullish order block" for the green candle at one point; context = up-close candle acting as bearish OB, caption/misspeak unclear).
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:16](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1636) — up-close candle = bearish OB, tape reading; [0:28:13](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1693) — calibrate 5m OB down to 1m; [0:29:00](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1740) — midpoint entry, subordinate to HTF; [0:32:11](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1931) — wick above OB, bodies inside, displacement.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Pyramiding: largest size first (NQ trade, April 29, 2022)  (aliases: scaling in, building a position, close proximity entry)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / live trade
- **What ICT says:** He builds positions with the maximum size first, then smaller adds at logical, precise areas (3 → 2 → 1 contracts); he never keeps adding one more contract. Built-in equity on the earlier contracts makes heat on the last small add insignificant. A "close proximity entry" = entering right after a level filled when price is still near it (he wasn't watching when the FVG filled).
- **Example in this video:** NQ June 2022: sold 3 contracts at the 1m OB midpoint; sold 2 at the FVG (close-proximity, just after it filled); sold 1 when price retraced back into the bearish OB — the candle low there was 13,334.75 and his entry 13,335.00 (a quarter point into it); heat on that contract up to 13,339.50 (4.5 handles). Covered all 6 at 13,285.00 — set just above the target level in case shallow runs didn't fill. He calls the whole thing a market maker sell model (selling where distribution takes place).
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:58](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1978) — the three entries; [0:33:44](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2024) — entry 13335 vs candle low 13334.75; [0:34:33](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2073) — max size first, 4.5 handles heat; [0:36:07](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2167) — exit all six at 13285; [0:36:59](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2219) — market maker sell model.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Many trades in his TD Ameritrade statements use close-proximity entries and other methods not taught publicly (e.g., showing students how to weather drawdown); don't judge his precision from them.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Later scalp: 9:30 whipsaw long  (aliases: 9:30 volatility)

- **Kind:** example only

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: SMT divergence (ES vs NQ)  (aliases: SMT, smart money technique, correlation crack)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** ES and NQ (S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 composites) are closely correlated and generally move in tandem, not always. If you're bearish and one makes a higher high while the other fails to, that shows a willingness to break the correlation: the higher one's move is a stop run and the lagging one is really weak — distribution. It's confirmation without an indicator; an "x-ray view" of real accumulation and distribution.
- **How to identify:** Compare the same swing points on both. On TradingView: compare/add symbol in a new pane below, and set the price source to High to compare high-to-high.
- **Example in this video:** Friday April 29, 2022: ES high at ~2:30 a.m.; after 8:30 ES rallies but makes a *lower* high than the 2:30 high, while NQ makes a *higher* high (vs its ~2:35 high) → bearish SMT, confirming the short.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:35](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2555) — ES 2:30 a.m. high vs post-8:30 high, NQ higher; [0:43:24](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2604) — SMT definition, stop run, ES weak; [0:44:12](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2652) — TradingView compare pane with high source; [0:45:00](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2700) — x-ray of accumulation/distribution.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Fibonacci setup: equilibrium, OTE on bodies, standard-deviation projections  (aliases: OTE, 62/79, standard deviations, calibrate to daily range)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Fib settings (he types his own levels into the style tab): 0.5 = equilibrium (discount vs premium). OTE levels = 62% and 79%. Negative extensions act as standard deviations used to project how far a move will run; calibrated to the daily range they give a good idea of where the low should form. Standard deviation projections mentioned: one, two, and one-half standard deviations. For premium/discount use the range high to low; but for OTE he anchors on candle *bodies* — the lowest open or close and the highest open or close in the swing — because wicks are stop runs; using bodies "gets to the heart of the matter" (he says critics who claim he misuses Fibs don't get this). OTE + FVG together is "what makes it optimal."
- **How to use:** Entry where the 62–79 OTE overlaps a FVG; take profit at a standard-deviation projection; to know "how far below the low can it go," look at the standard deviation.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: OTE high-to-low; price trades up into OTE and the FVG = entry; body-anchored OTE puts the retrace right up almost to the 79% level. A one-standard-deviation projection lower is hit precisely, then a retracement — good profit-taking area, also below the low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:46:39](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2799) — fib style settings, 0.5 equilibrium, standard deviations, calibrate to daily range; [0:47:30](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2850) — OTE 62 and 79; [0:48:17](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2897) — OTE + FVG = optimal; [0:49:05](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=2945) — 1/2/0.5 SD projections, bodies (lowest open or close) for OTE; [0:50:39](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=3039) — 1 SD target hit, take profits.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Exact on-screen settings list isn't read out in full; only 0.5, 62, 79 and the 0.5/1/2 SD projections are spoken.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 22
head: Algorithm won't change from teaching  (aliases: saturation, "a sucker born every minute")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (belief)
- **What ICT says:** Most people won't be disciplined/rule-based, so wide knowledge won't break the concepts; new liquidity (new speculators) keeps arriving. If he thought teaching would make it stop working, he wouldn't teach it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:48](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1788) — discipline makes it rare; [0:31:24](https://youtu.be/QKc_i90chVg?t=1884) — new liquidity always arrives.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: FOMC / news-event delivery pattern  (aliases: FOMC, knee-jerk reaction, NFP-style legs, 2:00 / 2:30 FOMC)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model
- **What ICT says:** FOMC behaves like non-farm payroll: a knee-jerk initial leg, then another leg, then a fake-out leg, *then* the real setup comes. He waits a few minutes for the "initial shakeout" before outlining anything. The announcement is at 2:00 p.m.; price drops into the level, and usually by around 2:30 the initial leg that "prices in" the event (high or low) is finished and the real move starts. A trade taken ahead of the FOMC announcement is a "gambler's setup" and he doesn't count it.
- **How to use:** Mark where the initial leg should terminate (a discount FVG below 50% of the range, near sell-side liquidity), wait for price to deliver into it after 2:00, then look for the reversal and the run on the opposite liquidity (here Tuesday's high).
- **Example in this video:** MNQ: after 2:00 the market drops; ICT marks the blue zone as the end of the bears' race; price drops into it shortly after 2:30, turns, and runs Tuesday's high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:06](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=6) — waiting for FOMC initial shakeout, "end of the road" zone; [0:01:40](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=100) — FOMC like NFP: leg, leg, fake-out leg, then real setup; [0:11:10](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=670) — 2:00 drop, initial leg finished ~2:30, then rally; [0:14:23](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=863) — pre-FOMC trade = gambler's setup.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "This isn't an invitation" to trade FOMC or NFP — extremely risky; great to study in hindsight or watch live as a case study of liquidity runs.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: Stacked FVGs — expect the stab into the second  (aliases: initial imbalance, second imbalance)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (applied again)
- **What ICT says:** With an initial imbalance and a second one beyond it, always imagine price could stab into the second. He'd rather see price come down into the target first; a move too far back up would "upset" the higher-timeframe FVG not yet traded into.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:06](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=6) — initial imbalance, could stab into the second; [0:02:27](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=147) — doesn't want to upset the untraded FVG.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: Short entries into the drop: FVG as resistance, stop above last up-close candle  (aliases: bearish order block, stop above most recent green candle)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example
- **What ICT says:** With sell-side resting below a recent low, you could short with the stop right above the most recent green (up-close) candle to the left. If price revisits the bottom of a FVG and bumps it like support-turned-resistance, that's a short; stop again at the high of the most recent green candle. A bearish order block above can be hit and price resumes lower. An order block (blue line) in the path can cause a bounce first.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ during the post-2:00 drop: shorts aim at the "bullseye" just below a short-term low (sell-side pool), then the blue shaded zone. Sequence: liquidity run, drop, hits an order block (blue line), bounces into the FVG, which sets up the decline into the highlighted zone.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:27](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=147) — short with stop above most recent green candle; [0:03:16](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=196) — FVG bottom bumped like resistance = short; [0:13:35](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=815) — recap of the drop sequence.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: "Running" vs "Sweeping" liquidity  (aliases: run on liquidity, sweep, expansion vs reversal)
body:
- **Kind:** definition (vocabulary)
- **What ICT says:** He picks these words deliberately. *Sweeping* a high (or low) = price goes just a little above (below) it — a shallow run — and reverses back into the range. *Running* a high (old high or relative equal highs) = price goes right over the top of it and continues without looking back (expansion).
- **Example in this video:** Before/at FOMC price made a shallow move above Tuesday's high (red line) = a sweep, then came down. After the drop into the blue zone, price ran Tuesday's high "much more meaningfully" — straight through and higher.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:03](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=243) — "running the Tuesday high, not sweeping"; [0:04:50](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=290) — sweep = shallow run and reverse, run = right over top and doesn't look back; [0:05:38](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=338) — sweep and reverse into range vs expansion move.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: Discount FVG below 50% of the range as the turn point ("checkered flag")  (aliases: end of the road for bears, blue shaded area, bullseye)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** Measure the range from the high formed at 2:00 p.m. (14:00 on chart) down to the low; below 50% (discount) sits the turquoise/blue FVG — that's where the drop should end before the real move higher. Candle bodies respecting that zone is "really handsome price delivery." A slight dip below it is fine; he's not worried about that much accuracy. If wrong, price might only reach the smaller "bullseye" below a short-term low and rally from there.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ: price trades down into the blue zone, bodies respect it, dips slightly below, then turns higher; after it takes out the swing high around 13,150 and crosses back above the larger FVG, the reversal is confirmed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:50](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=290) — "checkered flag" = end of race for bears; [0:07:16](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=436) — bodies respecting the blue shaded area; [0:08:02](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=482) — turn, swing high ~13,150 taken, back above the larger FVG; [0:09:37](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=577) — 50% of the range, FVG below it is the target.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: Fibonacci expansion target — wicks vs bodies  (aliases: Fib projection, extreme of range, body-to-body)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Normally he anchors Fibs on the highest open/close and lowest open/close in the swing (bodies) when not much volatility is expected. On FOMC, volatility is high, so the extremes of the range must be considered: use the wicks. For upside objectives draw from the low up to the high (he first drew it backwards). The wick-based expansion gives objective one and objective two (the "extreme target for today"); the body-to-body version "makes more sense" for the target he had outlined earlier.
- **How to use:** After the reversal (swing high taken and price back above the FVG), project the range from the 2:00 p.m. high to the post-2:30 low upward to get the target.
- **Example in this video:** MNQ target 13,437.00 — hit ("there she is") after ~2:30; price then pulled back into imbalances and continued higher even after the target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:02](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=482) — 2:00 high to post-2:30 low expanded to 13,437.00; [0:11:58](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=718) — bodies normally, wicks on FOMC because of volatility; [0:12:47](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=767) — low-to-high objectives 1 and 2, body-to-body comparison.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Answers the recurring "why does ICT use wicks sometimes and bodies other times" question: volatility expectation decides it. Refines Ep. 22, where he anchored OTE on bodies.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: Bullish order block on the reversal & continuation imbalances  (aliases: down-close candles, institutional order flow)
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:** After the turn, a retrace into an order block made of two down-close candles is a buy; as price runs Tuesday's high, retracements into small imbalances are buys. In a bullish delivery of institutional order flow, down-close candles should support price as it goes up.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:10](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=910) — buy at OB of two down-close candles, imbalance buys; [0:15:59](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=959) — down-close candles supporting price in institutional order flow.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 23
head: Eight setups in one move — choose the one that fits your model  (aliases: unique setup selection)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (teaching philosophy)
- **What ICT says:** He counts eight tradeable setups in the whole sequence (excluding the pre-FOMC gamble): (1) the drop's FVG short, (2) the return to the FVG short, closing the short below the low, a long scalp up into resting liquidity above a high, a short from the FVG into the outlined objective, a buy at the order block after the turn, buys on retracements into small imbalances during the run of Tuesday's high, and continuation after the target. You aren't meant to take all eight; each could be the specific setup that fits a student's unique model. The highest form of analysis is knowing where price will draw *before* it turns.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:37](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=577) — eight trades in this move; [0:10:23](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=623) — you don't all need the same setup; [0:14:23](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=863) — enumerating the trades; [0:15:10](https://youtu.be/TV9TfwHXuqs?t=910) — later buys.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The exact count/order of the eight is narrated loosely over the chart; listing above is reconstructed from his narration.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 24
head: 2022 Mentorship model — where setups form (bearish version via relative equal highs)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / rule
- **What ICT says:** Setup forms after price runs above an old high or relative equal highs. As soon as price trades above the relative equal highs, scan back through the run-up and find the **nearest short-term low** — that is the trigger. It is not enough that price goes above the highs and simply drifts back down below them; price must go below that short-term low **with displacement** ("energetic move"). That displacement leg is "the foundation of the setup." Only then go into that leg and look for a fair value gap to short into.
- **How to identify:** (1) relative equal highs / old high level; (2) price runs through it; (3) identify the nearest short-term low formed during the run-up; (4) displacement takes out that short-term low = market structure shift; (5) FVG inside the displacement leg.
- **How to use:** Sell when price retraces up into the FVG in the displacement leg. Until the short-term low is taken out, "there's no trade there, there's no setup there." Reverse everything for longs (run below relative equal lows/old low, displacement above nearest short-term high, buy the FVG).
- **Example in this video:** Diagram drawn: green line = relative equal highs; price approaches, small correction, approaches again, then runs through; trigger = nearest short-term low in that run; displacement through it; FVG in the leg.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:41](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1901) — "where do setups form" journal subtitle; [0:33:16](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1996) — nearest short-term low is the trigger; [0:34:03](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=2043) — no displacement through the low = no setup.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He calls this the filter that removes low-probability trades — the displacement requirement is what separates a real shift from a simple dip back below the highs.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 24
head: 2022 Mentorship model — second entry framing: raid into an old FVG
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Same logic as relative equal highs, but the "level" being raided is an old fair value gap above price (bearish case). Price trades up into the old FVG; it does **not** have to completely close the gap — trading anywhere between its low and high is good. Simplify it: treat the **low of the fair value gap** exactly like the relative equal highs. Once price trades above the FVG's low into it, go back through that up-leg, find the trigger (short-term low); when it is taken out = the market structure shift; the move down is the displacement leg; then look for a (new) FVG in that leg to sell.
- **How to identify:** old opposing FVG overhead; price trades into it (partial fill OK); nearest short-term low of the run-up taken out with displacement; new FVG formed.
- **How to use:** Short the new FVG in the displacement leg. For longs: old FVG below price, price trades down into it, treat the FVG's high as the "relative equal lows," wait for displacement above the nearest short-term high, buy the new FVG.
- **Example in this video:** The bullish version is what he hoped for at the 9:30 open: drop into the small gap he marked with a blue arrow, then displacement up, then buy an FVG targeting a run to 4303 (level quoted; likely ES — caption context unclear which index).
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:37](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=2137) — old FVG version, doesn't have to fully close; [0:36:24](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=2184) — FVG low treated as the relative-equal-highs line; "those are the two entry strategies for this model".
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He states these are "the two entry strategies for this model" — i.e., the model's sweep can be of liquidity (equal highs/lows) or of an opposing PD array (old FVG).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 24
head: Model as a filter (no setup = no trade)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** A model with sound logic should keep you out of bad trades — not always, but sometimes when a big move goes the other way that you didn't expect. If the structure doesn't form, nothing is lost; it's a missed move, not a losing trade. "It doesn't mean that the model's broke."
- **How to identify:** Missing ingredient (e.g., no displacement after the stop run) = no entry.
- **How to use:** Don't buy just because price reached your point of interest. Wait for all elements.
- **Example in this video:** May 5, 2022. 15m chart: price traded down into the shaded FVG, the candle stopped right at an old candle high, and the next candle "gave up the ghost." Initial criteria met (traded below an old low → sell stops run), but on 15m and 5m there was **no displacement back above the old low** — price consolidated, returned to the low and "melted" through it, and through the FVG. Anyone who bought "is not using what I'm teaching." Market then made a large move lower (the post-FOMC selloff) — a missed move, not a loss.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:33](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1053) — model validity keeps you out of bad trades; [0:22:14](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1334) — 15m: traded below old low (initial criteria); [0:23:01](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1381) — 5m: no displacement → no trade; [0:37:11](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=2231) — "market did not provide the structure."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 24
head: FVG as "where the trade might form" + time element (9:30 Judas swing)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** The FVG he flagged is only the place in price where the pattern *might* form — "by itself it's just price." You must first incorporate time, algorithmically: at the 9:30 equity open you expect volatility. With price focused on highs overhead and the market already dropping into a discount ahead of 9:30, he expected a drop (to get traders thinking lower) then a rally — a Judas swing at 9:30 — "not just go down indiscriminately"; it has to do something specific (drop into that FVG, then displace).
- **How to identify:** HTF draw above; price in discount pre-9:30; a nearby FVG below; 9:30 volatility.
- **How to use:** Wait for the drop into the FVG at 9:30, then require displacement and a new FVG before buying.
- **Example in this video:** Blue arrow in the community post marking the small gap below price; he expected a 9:30 drop into it, displacement, FVG long, run to 4303. Never formed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:38](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=338) — waiting for the 9:30 Judas swing into the gap; [0:19:53](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1193) — dropped into a discount, want manipulation around 9:30; [0:21:27](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1287) — FVG is just price; first element is time.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 24
head: Relative equal highs ("smooth criminal highs") as draw / setup location
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** Community post told viewers to drop a horizontal line across the "smooth criminal highs" (relative equal highs) on NQ and ES 15m charts and study how they're treated ahead of NFP Friday. Bearish framework on NQ 1h: look for a run above those relative equal highs, then a washout lower that creates the model.
- **How to identify:** Relative equal highs on 15m/1h index charts.
- **How to use:** As a liquidity target to be run before a reversal (setup location).
- **Example in this video:** E-mini NQ June 2022 contract, daily and 1h chart; he felt price could stab above the relative equal highs and then run lower. Price never ran them; both scenarios (drop into FVG then run the highs; run the highs then reverse) failed to develop.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:50](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=290) — the community post; [0:16:46](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1006) — NQ daily relative equal highs; [0:34:50](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=2090) — neither scenario panned out.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says he'll "explain what [smooth criminal] is in a moment" but in this video only treats them as relative equal highs (caption unclear on any further definition).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 24
head: Day-of-week / news context: Thursday before NFP
body:
- **Kind:** rule (context)
- **What ICT says:** Thursday ahead of non-farm payroll Friday was part of his reasoning for expecting the relative equal highs to be targeted. NFP Friday is usually volatile — can be messy, sloppy, sometimes a dud, sometimes as volatile as FOMC. Because FOMC (the day before) had already done what it did, he didn't expect NFP to have that much impact.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:06](https://youtu.be/nv0ey5UyOmY?t=1146) — Thursday before NFP reasoning.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Bearish order block — high is the "most unlikely" level
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** On the ES daily, the bearish order block he flagged earlier was a catalyst for a future move down; the high of that candle "shouldn't be pierced" — it is the most unlikely level to be traded to and through. Order blocks were introduced in his free "Scout Sniper" series; the OB is "not the secret sauce" of this model — the FVG is the focus.
- **Example in this video:** ES June 2022 daily: relative equal highs were run (buy stops), price broke down, traded into the bearish order block region without exceeding its high, then fell toward relative equal lows (sell-side liquidity) and lower targets he had outlined.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:15](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=435) — daily chart recap; [0:08:02](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=482) — OB high most unlikely to be traded through.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Seasonal tendencies (May weakness in indices)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** Seasonal tendencies are times of year when markets or asset classes historically produce price swings in a certain direction — usually, not always (analogy: in Maryland you expect heat, not snow, on July 4th). From about the last week of April into May, S&P, Nasdaq, Dow and Russell tend to be weak. By itself it means little; combined with his model it's "a road map to consistency." Study it every year in old data, then forward-test it.
- **How to use:** As HTF bias filter — bearish seasonal + BSL run at highs = framework for shorts.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:12](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=672) — definition/analogy; [0:11:58](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=718) — late April into May weakness.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Smart money liquidity cycle (sell to buy stops, buy back from sell stops)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Smart money sells short to buy stops resting above old/relative equal highs, leaving them net short; to get out they must buy back cheaper, from sell stops resting below old lows (sell-side liquidity). Large fund traders place stops in similar places to retail — the difference is only size. This is the "market efficiency paradigm": liquidity resting or engineered where it's wanted — not support/resistance, not supply/demand. The algorithm goes to the liquidity "whether there is sufficient volume or not" — not because of buying pressure.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:19](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=859) — net short, buy back from sell stops; [0:15:06](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=906) — funds and retail stops in same areas; [0:49:58](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2998) — algorithm goes there regardless of volume.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Rebalancing a large daily range (previous-day low as retracement target)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / new framing
- **What ICT says:** After a large range down day (Monday, closed near its low), go back to the *previous day's* low (Friday's low). The next day's retracement up to that level "rebalances" Monday's entire range/sell-off. It tricks people into thinking the low is in, when price has only gone up to a logical level on the daily that rebalances the drop. On the 15m the move doesn't look like an imbalance, but on the daily it's a large distribution candle.
- **How to identify:** Large down day closing near low → mark prior day's low → expect the next session's Judas rally to reach it (when bias is bearish).
- **How to use:** Use the prior day's low as the "how far can it go" upper limit for the Judas swing; look for the short setup there.
- **Example in this video:** ES, Tue May 10 2022: price ran up from 8:30 and hit Friday's (May 6) low right at the 9:30 candle, rebalancing Monday (May 9)'s drop, then sold off.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:24](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1284) — go back to previous day's low; [0:31:48](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1908) — rebalances Monday's range; [0:32:36](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1956) — "how far can it go — that's the Friday low."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Links to his 2010 BabyPips advice: study the open, high, low, close of the last three days — that's where he first found the FVG (no one else discovered it from that prompt).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Order of liquidity runs defines bias (buy-side first = bearish)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** With a bearish bias, the market goes up to a premium for one of two reasons: run old high(s) for buy-side liquidity so smart money can sell to them, then seek sell-side liquidity below to offset. Running buy-side (relative equal highs) at 9:30 *without* first taking the previous low is bearish. If price had first taken the previous low and then rallied, "that to me is not bearish."
- **Example in this video:** ES 1h/15m: relative equal highs above, old low (Friday's low) above that; at 9:30 price runs the relative equal highs and hits the old low (red line), purging buy-side; then sells to take partials below a short-term low and run Monday's low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:01](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1621) — BSL purged at 9:30; [0:28:38](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1718) — buy side run first is the bearish tell.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Midnight New York = start of the algorithmic day
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Break daily ranges up by day starting at midnight New York time — "this is how the algorithm works." Wellington/New Zealand does not start the 24‑hour cycle; anyone teaching that "doesn't know what they're talking about."
- **Example in this video:** Tuesday's 1h chart from midnight: price went up, down, and closed near the midnight open — matching the indecisive daily candle (long upper wick, small body).
- **Timestamps:** [0:25:25](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1525) — midnight NY start; [0:46:47](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2807) — Wellington myth.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: 8:30 news embargo lift and the 8:30–9:30 Judas swing window
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** At 8:30 ET the news embargo is lifted and the algorithm starts seeking liquidity (even on light-news days); it may wait until 9:30. When bearish, the 8:30–9:30 hour is expected to produce a run higher to set up shorts. The short may form inside that hour, or the hour may just provide the leg that frames the later setup. 9:30 equity open = manipulation time; it looks like a breakout to retail, who buy and get run.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m/5m: run starts at 8:30 from relative equal highs, 9:30 candle tags Friday's low; the shaded rally is the Judas swing.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:01](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1861) — 8:30 embargo lifted; [0:34:11](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2051) — the hour-long interval; [0:34:57](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2097) — 9:30 manipulation, retail chases.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Power of Three inside an "indecisive" daily candle
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** A daily candle with a big upper wick and small body looks indecisive, but through power of three: accumulation around the 8:30 opening price (draw it out in time), the rally above it (manipulation), then the mentorship pattern (FVG, market structure shift), displacement and distribution down into a discount array. Lower-timeframe framing with time and price removes the confusion.
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:36](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1956) — power of three with 8:30 open; [0:33:23](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2003) — open, rally, high, trade down.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Displacement leg + Fibonacci equilibrium filter (sell only in premium)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (he calls it a "hard line rule")
- **What ICT says:** Shade the displacement price swing (on the 5m here). Put a Fib on its high and low; 50% = equilibrium. For a short, the FVG entry must be at equilibrium or higher (premium) — "we don't want to sell in a discount." Following this alone keeps you out of many ill-fated trades (not 100%).
- **How to identify:** Displacement leg = the drop from the Judas high that breaks short-term lows (here it broke several short-term lows, so the leg extends to the final low).
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m leg from the 9:30 high down; equilibrium = 4044.50. An FVG visible on the 4m sat below 4044.50 (discount) → not valid for a short.
- **Timestamps:** [0:36:29](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2189) — fib, equilibrium 4044.50; [0:38:02](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2282) — FVG in discount rejected; [0:38:52](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2332) — hard-line rule.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Stepping down timeframes to find the FVG (5→4→3→2→1)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry procedure
- **What ICT says:** Keep the shaded displacement leg and step down 5m → 4m → 3m → 2m → 1m until you find a fair value gap inside it (in premium).
- **Example in this video:** ES: 5m leg shaded. 4m — one FVG but in discount (invalid). 3m — no FVG in the leg. 2m — a small FVG ("the unicorn," jokingly) formed with a short-term low taken out → the entry.
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:43](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2143) — strip down 5,4,3,2,1; [0:40:26](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2426) — 3m none; [0:41:15](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2475) — 2m FVG found.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Unicorn" here is a joke about rarity, not the later named Unicorn model.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Stop placement and trailing
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Initial stop: 1–2 ticks above the high of the candle that creates the FVG. Wider alternative: above the swing high (Judas high) — if that is too much risk, trade micros (ES micro $5/point vs mini $50/handle). If you can't weather that on a micro, you're underfunded (e.g., a $100 account is asking to fail). Don't trail tight right away — positions need room to breathe; move the stop only after a larger shift in structure (a lower low taken out), then to above the corresponding lower swing high. If it then stops you, you were probably wrong or price is consolidating (ugly conditions anyway).
- **Example in this video:** 2m FVG short: stop above the FVG-creating candle was not hit, though price retraced after moving in favor.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:04](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2524) — stop above FVG candle; [0:43:39](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2619) — 1–2 ticks, swing high, micros; [0:44:25](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2665) — when to move stop.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Targets: short-term low partial, then sell-side (previous day low); lunch-hour delivery
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:** Offset shorts at a nearby short-term low (partial) and then the sell-side below the previous day's low. Smart money "sells short here and then adds to it." A limit order would have filled during the lunch hour. He expected the final punch through the low just ahead of or right at 12:00; it came ~27 minutes later — the only thing that didn't line up.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:48](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1668) — partial below short-term low; [0:48:25](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2905) — model recap, lunch-hour fill; [0:49:11](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2951) — expected at 12:00, came ~27 min later.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Sessions: London works, Asia rarely
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The pattern forms somewhere every day — London (overnight highs/lows) or New York. He teaches NY because you know what London did. Works in London "absolutely"; Asia "not that often" (most illiquid for him). Asian-session traders should use yen pairs, NZD and AUD on 1–5m charts. Everything taught works in forex, not just index futures.
- **Timestamps:** [0:45:12](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2712) — forms daily, London; [0:45:59](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=2759) — Asia, yen/NZD/AUD 1–5m.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Don't pick tops/bottoms; trade the middle of the move
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In a bearish market, don't try to call the long-term low (he has lost more money doing that than anything else). Oversold indicators/bullish divergence tempt bottom-picking. "There's a lot of meat in between the major turning points"; you can afford to be wrong at the end, it'll be obvious, then switch.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:13](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1333); [0:23:01](https://youtu.be/CnTXwAuDi9Y?t=1381).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 25
head: Fractal (ICT usage)
body:

- **What ICT says:** A fractal is simply a small segment of price action you're studying that's doing something specific (e.g., the old daily low viewed on the 1h).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 26 - Example Of Tape Reading Practice
head: Intraday order flow against the daily bias (after sell-side is taken)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** He is trading against the daily bias on the basis that sell-side liquidity has already been taken and price has traded into a fair value gap (~4000). Price traded down three times intraday and took out yesterday's low; the lack of follow-through bolsters a counter-trend long. Retail sees the consolidation as a bear flag and expects lower prices.
- **How to identify:** Relative equal lows / previous day low swept; price reached into a discount FVG; repeated failure to continue lower.
- **How to use:** Target the nearest buy-side liquidity (short-term high), not a full reversal. The best case (high of day) is optional — "it doesn't need to do that to be profitable."
- **Example in this video:** Likely ES (levels ~4000; instrument not named in captions), date not stated. Sell-side below relative equal lows run; entry long around the FVG near 4000 (fill read as ~4006.25/4006.50, caption unclear); draw = buy-side above a short-term high (≈4036 area); stretch = 4051.25 (high of day, buy stops).
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:05](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=5) — against daily bias, sell stops taken, FVG near 4000; [0:01:44](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=104) — SSL taken, 4051 stretch; [0:04:06](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=246) — three drives down, yesterday's low taken, lack of follow-through.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 26 - Example Of Tape Reading Practice
head: Bullish order block (drawn in real time) — higher of two down-close candles
body:
- **Kind:** definition / entry refinement
- **What ICT says:** With two consecutive down-close candles, draw the order block on the *higher* of the two; use its uppermost opening price as the level. Price may drop into it, pick up momentum, and the algorithm reprices higher to buy-side liquidity (≈4036). It might only touch the small wick high of that candle, or not touch it at all. Once working, "the down-close candles are supporting price."
- **How to use:** Add to the position (pyramid) when price trades back to the OB. He added two contracts on the first OB (to 6 contracts), then saw price touch the second OB's wick.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:06](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=246) — adds two on order block, now six long; [0:08:45](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=525) — higher of two down-close candles, uppermost open; [0:10:20](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=620) — touches the wick.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 26 - Example Of Tape Reading Practice
head: Stop placement inside FVG / below old short-term high
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Stop moved up just under a low that "should not trade back down into" — it sits inside the lower end of the fair value gap and below the old short-term high around 9:30. Market structure supports the idea, sell-side is already taken, and price is back inside the range between the stop and the buy-side target. "Notice I'm not in a hurry to rush my stop-loss up." After expansion, stop to breakeven, then a bit higher.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:52](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=292) — why the stop placement is confident; [0:11:07](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=667) — stop to breakeven and higher.

head: Fading the "imbalance" crowd after the 8:30 drop is rebalanced
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** Traders who follow imbalances (popular lately) saw the quick sudden drop at 8:30; the market came back and rebalanced it and is now drifting lower, so they try to sell short — he goes against that and targets their stops (buy-side).
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:32](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=572).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 26 - Example Of Tape Reading Practice
head: Scaling out & pyramiding (trade management)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** Bulk of the position (4 of 6 contracts) comes off at market once price runs above the buy-side liquidity; then consider moving the stop up on the remainder and "see if I can get lucky." He wants delivery "in big candles, speed delivery" toward the target.
- **Example in this video:** Executions: bought the FVG after sell stops taken, added at the order block, sold 4 above the buy-side high, moved stop up and the final 2 were stopped out. ~$5,000+ hypothetical profit.

head: Tape reading practice (no position required)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** To practice reading order flow you don't need a demo position; mark the liquidity pools and PD arrays before price gets there and state exactly what you expect — "nothing ambiguous." Dim levels already used (e.g., sell-side once taken) so focus stays on active levels. Ignore the P&L — "that's the distraction, pay attention to the price."
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:19](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=199) — P&L is a distraction; [0:07:58](https://youtu.be/k26euOG6zAk?t=478) — no demo position needed, be specific; dim used levels.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Draw on liquidity doesn't need to be reached
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If you believe price will draw toward an objective (today or into next week), look for a setup that lets you participate in the expansion toward it; the DOL "does not need to be traded to" to have a profitable framework. Think of it as a magnet.
- **Example in this video:** NQ daily/1h: relative equal highs at 12,547 and 12,553.25 (he uses the higher, 12,553.25, flagged in his community post as "too clean"). Price never reached it on the day, yet the long was profitable.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:17](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=17) — 12,553 too clean; [0:01:54](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=114) — DOL needn't be traded to; [0:03:27](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=207) — magnet.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Sell-side taken → buy-side becomes the draw (hourly framework)
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:** On the 1h, a shift in market structure, then relative equal lows were swept (below and back above), one more attempt lower was rejected. With the large sell-side pool taken and price back above the relative equal lows, the clear draw is buy-side above the relative equal highs. Little imbalance remained in between because that area was already rebalanced, so he expected price to "punch through" and take the buy stops.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:41](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=161) — 1h sweep of relative equal lows; [0:03:27](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=207) — buy-side is the draw.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Power of Three at the 9:30 open (London low raid)
body:
- **Kind:** example only

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Lunch high and the 1:30 PM afternoon liquidity search
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The high formed at the 12:10 candle — lunchtime "usually creates a retracement of some sort or consolidation." Around 1:30 PM the algorithm starts seeking liquidity again; if it's going to continue higher, it first seeks sell-side. Relative equal lows existed, but they weren't in a discount yet — the afternoon retracement must reach equilibrium of the day's range (low of day to high of day; purple dashed line = Fib 50%) or below.
- **How to use:** On a bullish day, wait for the afternoon retracement to drop to/below the day's equilibrium into an FVG, then buy for continuation.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5m: price dropped through equilibrium into an FVG at ~2:00 PM (2:05–2:25 candles), then displaced higher — an MSS within a likely bullish day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:49](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=349) — buy discount FVG at/below equilibrium; 12:10 lunch high; [0:06:37](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=397) — 1:30 liquidity search, equilibrium; [0:07:24](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=444) — drop into FVG at 2 PM, displacement.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Counter-trend (HTF) retracement logic — Friday position squaring
body:
- **Kind:** rule / context
- **What ICT says:** This was counter-trend to the higher timeframe; the logic is that after being down a long time, a retracement is likely, and on Friday most participants want to get out before the weekend, so the algorithm squeezes them to square positions before the Friday close. You *can* frame his FVG model inside a counter-trend idea (if you're a contrarian by nature), but for the highest probability, trade in sync with the early-session move using the 8:30–9:30 window principles.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:24](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=444) — counter-trend to HTF; [0:08:10](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=490) — Friday squeeze; [0:13:43](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=823) — counter-trend vs 8:30–9:30 highest probability.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Timeframe step-down to the entry (4m → 3m → 2m) and OB + FVG confluence
body:
- **Kind:** entry model application
- **What ICT says:** 4m: only a small FVG, not used. 3m: a gap visible — "fine if that's what you were looking for." 2m: down-close candles (order block) plus an FVG; price traded down into it — that's where he bought.
- **How to use:** Scale in at the beginning (top) of the FVG and around its middle; he tried for the lower portion but price didn't get there.
- **Example in this video:** 36 contracts bought (paper; assumes a low-margin discount broker such as AMP Futures). Took 10 off on the rally; intended to close 20 with a limit above 12,430 but it closed at market (phone/TradingView error); closed more, final contract late in day. None of the exits were above 12,430.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:10](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=490) — 4m/3m; [0:08:58](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=538) — 2m OB + FVG, 36 contracts; [0:10:33](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=633) — buying beginning and middle of FVG; [0:11:19](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=679) — exits and error.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Backtesting with first-person annotations (pseudo-experience)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (study method)
- **What ICT says:** Backtesting = going back and marking up old moves (bar replay or hindsight). Fill empty chart space with commentary written as if you saw it coming ("I saw this setting up… I wanted to see this displacement… I expected it to move aggressively toward the short-term highs and took partials above halfway high to low"). Screenshot/print into your journal and reread weekly. This "tricks" the subconscious into forming pseudo-memories and activates the reticular activating system (like noticing your new car everywhere), so live setups feel familiar. Time to full understanding varies — weeks to a year+.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:30](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=870) — what backtesting is; [0:15:16](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=916) — annotate with self-talk; [0:17:39](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=1059) — reticular activating system; [0:18:26](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=1106) — pseudo-memories.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He borrowed this from coping techniques he learned for anxiety; frames it as positive self-talk.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 27 - Counter Trend Ideas
head: Profit scaling at premium of the swing
body:
- **Kind:** rule (mentioned in the annotation example)
- **What ICT says:** Take something off once price is above halfway between the swing high and low — "premium profit scaling."
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:39](https://youtu.be/gLK4Qm6jte8?t=1059).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 29
head: SMT divergence (Smart Money Technique / Tool)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:** Using intermarket relationships, not indicators: when one correlated index makes a lower low and the other refuses to, that divergence (he "dubs" it SMT — smart money technique or smart money tool) supports the bullish bias. Used here only as confirmation within an existing bullish bias.
- **How to identify:** Compare ES and NQ swing lows at the same time; one breaks the prior low (e.g., the 10:00 AM low), the other holds it.
- **How to use:** Favors longs in the index that held (here he traded ES, the more "structured" one); confirms the low is unlikely to be taken.
- **Example in this video:** ES 1m: drop to relative equal lows, retrace, then later decline fails to go below the 10:00 AM low; NQ meanwhile made a lower low below its 10:00 AM low → bullish SMT.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:18](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=198) — ES vs NQ comparison; [0:04:07](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=247) — "this is what I dub SMT."

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 29
head: Displacement-leg 50% rule invalidates a counter-bias short
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** A rally, break of a short-term low, FVG, price trades up into it and breaks down — "big deal," it doesn't fit: the displacement leg requires the FVG to be above 50% of the leg's high-to-low (premium) for a short. Also bias was bullish, so no interest in shorts.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:57](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=297).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same premium/discount filter as Ep 25 (sell only above equilibrium of the displacement leg).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 29
head: Long setup: sell-stop run → short-term MSS → FVG (1m ES)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model application
- **What ICT says:** At 9:30 the market took a short-term high and declined — no short pattern (no FVG revisited). Price formed relative equal lows; later it ran sell stops, rallied (short-term shift in market structure), and retraced into a fair value gap — the long. A second bullish structure shift (highs taken) left another small FVG, where he added via limit order. Target: liquidity above the highs.
- **Example in this video:** ES 1m, May 16 2022: entries 3994.50 and 3996.25 (first had under two handles of heat, low ~3994.50; second about one handle, caption unclear); added position filled by limit with ~1.75 handles (7 ticks) of heat; full exit at 4022.50 (missed the very high). No NQ trades.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:27](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=147) — 9:30 takes short-term high, no short; [0:08:08](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=488) — MSS, FVG, second FVG add; [0:09:44](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=584) — executions; [0:11:17](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=677) — exit 4022.50.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 29
head: Close proximity entries
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** If you miss the ideal fill inside the FVG (fumbled order entry, software delays), getting in very close to the FVG without letting price run too far away is acceptable — "I don't think there's anything wrong with it." The point is to enter where the model suggests. In this example the FVG zone gave about eight candles of opportunity to get in inside or near it.
- **Example in this video:** His entry candle only wicked down toward the FVG; his fill was near, not in, the gap; less than ~2 handles of heat.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:32](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=392) — close proximity entries introduced; [0:07:19](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=439) — missed ideal entry; [0:08:08](https://youtu.be/QkokVv0owSE?t=488) — eight candles of opportunity.

Know when volatility is likely to occur and when it shrinks. Next day (Tue May 17): 8:30 retail sales and 2:00 PM Fed chair speaking — "all kinds of volatility"; don't try to trade it ("you'll probably hurt yourself").

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 30
head: PM session continuation: lunch lows get swept
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** When there is an afternoon continuation to the upside, the lows made during the New York lunch hour (12:00–1:00) will often be swept first. "If you're bullish and it consolidates in lunch, find the lunch lows, wait for it to run that out, and then they'll resume."
- **How to identify:** Bullish daily bias; lunch-hour range with relative equal lows; afternoon drop below them (often into an imbalance below).
- **How to use:** Look for longs after the lunch lows are run; target the HTF draw (here 12,553.25).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: lunch (noon–1 PM) relative equal lows run in the afternoon, price digs into an imbalance below them, then rallies to 12,553.25.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:53](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=53) — lunch lows swept on afternoon continuation; [0:11:23](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=683) — restated rule.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 30

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 30
head: Stop-run manipulation narrative (longs raked, shorts squeezed)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:** The run up triggered buy stops / breakout and bull-flag buyers, who were then taken into drawdown and stopped out (or squeezed out) below the relative equal lows; morning longs who trailed stops below the lunch lows were also taken out — so they can't profit on the real move to 12,553.25. Then shorts (e.g., from ~12,530) who feel safe get squeezed as price rips higher. The FVG overhead that looks like "resistance" isn't — "it's going to lift off from here."
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:31](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=151) — buy stops triggered, longs squeezed out; [0:04:08](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=248) — not resistance; shorts' internal dialogue.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 30
head: Order block support + 3:00 PM algorithmic spool to liquidity
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** After the drop, price went down to an order block and rallied; it traded back into the order block multiple times. He allowed for a fill in the FVG but it didn't get there. At 3:00 PM "the algorithms will start to spool price in the direction of the liquidity" — 12,553.25 — which it hammered. Sequence: OB → rally → OB → higher → consolidate right below the target → pump through.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: long entry ~12,417.75 (just below the 20 level; poor entry — missed the imbalance fill); stop below the relative equal lows; exit at/above 12,553.25. ~$5,000 hypothetical.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:55](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=295) — OB, 3 PM spool; [0:05:42](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=342) — entry 12,417.75, missed FVG; delivery sequence.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 30
head: No setup = market not likely to deliver that way
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** On the 5m, the afternoon sell-off produced no model setup (even without running buy-side). When the market is "in sync," these algorithmic principles will not appear in moves that are not likely to deliver — not always, but often; the market can sell off without giving a setup and then create the real move the other way where the setups do form.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:19](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=439); [0:08:08](https://youtu.be/CL94EnGqB4Q?t=488).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 31
head: Pointing to liquidity (scout / sniper framing)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He never calls entries/stops/targets; he points to where price is likely to go. When price is above and he draws attention to an old low (the May 16 low), he means it's the target for sell-side liquidity — "we're aiming for liquidity." He's the scout; students are snipers who must do the scoping (entry, stop, limit orders), which he has already taught.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 31
head: Using FVGs to join a move after the open
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Don't fixate only on the setup at the opening. If you don't get a trade at the open, you can still use a fair value gap to get involved with the move toward the draw.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:52](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=292).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 31
head: Bearish order block (15m) → FVG (5m) → swing high entry
body:
- **Kind:** entry model application
- **What ICT says:** 15m: the up-close candle right before price went lower is a bearish order block; extend it in time — price came back and hit it. 5m: an FVG that isn't visible until you zoom in; price overshoots it (high volatility). Stop goes above that candle's high. Fine-tuning: after hitting the FVG, a three-candle swing high formed; as soon as that third candle closed, he entered short on the next candle — trusting that the FVG was reached, a swing high formed, and bias is bearish, with the May 16 low as the target.
- **How to identify:** Bearish bias + identified SSL target below; 15m last up-close candle (OB) tapped; 5m FVG traded into; 3‑candle swing high confirms.
- **How to use:** Enter after swing high completes; stop above the high; target old low (SSL); partials along the way.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m: 4 contracts short at 4007.75, stop above the swing high, target below the May 16 low. First partial on the initial drop, another by limit order; final exit around 3910 near the low of the day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:40](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=340) — 15m bearish OB; [0:06:29](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=389) — 5m FVG overshot, stop above; swing high; [0:07:16](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=436) — entry logic.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 31
head: Trailing stops in high volatility
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Once price broke lower and moved aggressively in his favor, he moved the stop down — only because volatility was so high that a retracement could knock him out. "That's not fear, that's just sound money management." He also lacked time to babysit the trade.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:52](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=292) — couldn't babysit; [0:07:16](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=436) — moved stop due to volatility.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 31

body:
- **Kind:** example only
