title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 31
head: Forex vs index futures (volatility rotation)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (context)
- **What ICT says:** Indices are where the volatility is now; "price is price" — it works the same in forex. He expects currencies to have "pretty wild movement" within ~12 months, at which point indices will look slow. He was long USD/CAD on the 8:30 impact news that morning; it was a "snooze fest."
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:56](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=56); [0:01:43](https://youtu.be/OYNpIeu9czw?t=103).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 32
head: Outside day (down close) → choppy next day if old low isn't reached
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** An outside day trades above the previous day's high and below the previous day's low (the whole prior range is inside it); here it closed down. The following day, if price trades down toward an old low but falls short of it (the "double bottom" that feels safe), it tends to be choppy — especially after a down-close outside day.
- **Example in this video:** Old daily low at 3855; day's low 3856 (one handle short), day low area 3872.25; old highs at 3933.25. Price then chopped.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:54](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=54) — outside day defined; [0:01:40](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=100) — falling short of old low → choppy; [0:03:17](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=197) — levels 3872.25, 3855, 3856.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 32
head: Setups that look like they'll form but don't (50/50 in the middle of the range)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The market often presents what looks like a setup that never comes to fruition. Price traded up into an FVG, worked lower, created a small FVG, bumped into it — "nothing really in here to work with in terms of the model." Probability is statistically 50/50 when price trades back into the middle of the range — no edge there. The FVG "should have offered more movement lower" but didn't take out the short-term low properly before rallying.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:14](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=254) — no model short; 50/50 in middle of range; [0:05:02](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=302) — FVG should have offered more.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 32
head: Dealing range (trade ideas framed by the current range)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Even with a longer-term bias (he still favored the 3855 sell-side), every trade idea must be taken based on its *current dealing range* — e.g., from this high down to that low — and measured.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:02](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=302).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 32
head: Consolidation day 3:00–4:00 PM model (run outside range → back to midpoint)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / rule
- **What ICT says:** On a consolidation day the market creates an initial range and stays in it until 3:00 PM. Between 3:00 and 4:00 PM the algorithm often trades outside the bounds of the day's range, then rams back to the middle of the range. It "used to be the bond close" that started this; now 3 PM to the 4 PM equities closing bell sets the tone for on-close orders. Before 3 PM the rally aims at buy-side liquidity; traders see a breakout and buy, and smart money pairs with them to go short. Mark vertical lines at 3 PM and 4 PM; study the middle of the daily range (midpoint of the day's high and low, e.g., from the ~9:30 low to the high).
- **How to identify:** Range-bound session; relative equal highs (buy-side) above the range from shorts trailing stops; 3–4 PM window.
- **How to use:** After price runs the buy-side in 3–4 PM, look on the 1m for a swing low broken, an FVG, and a retrace back up into it → short; target the midpoint of the day's range (partial), runners to a further level.
- **Example in this video:** Shorts from the prior day trailed stops above the old highs; price bumped them shallowly, then rammed through the relative equal highs to above 3933.25. 1m: swing low broken, FVG, retrace into it, sell-off to mid-range. Short 3940.75, four contracts off at 3908.75 (mid-range), runner with limit at 3855.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:49](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=349) — vertical lines at 3 PM/4 PM; [0:06:39](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=399) — middle of the daily range; [0:08:14](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=494) — 1m swing low, FVG, retrace; [0:09:07](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=547) — fills 3940.75 / 3908.75 / limit 3855; [0:10:43](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=643) — consolidation day defined; [0:11:32](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=692) — bond close, on-close orders.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Choppy days: "wait until three o'clock." Most traders are too afraid to short after a breakout run in the last hour — that's the edge.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 32
head: Protective buy stops as a "rushing liquidity wave"
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Buy orders resting above relative equal highs are short sellers' protective stops. When price trades above, those stops become "a rushing liquidity wave" of willing buyers at the market — which smart money sells into. The run also induces breakout longs, building sell-side liquidity below (their stops) for later.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:26](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=446) — run to squeeze shorts and induce longs; [0:16:20](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=980) — rushing liquidity wave.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 32
head: Gravitation to the midpoint of the daily range
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** On a range-bound day, split the low and high of the day; the midpoint is where price "wants to gravitate back to" after the late-day excursion outside the range.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:06](https://youtu.be/hzoMJQlEv5M?t=1026).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 33
head: Waiting for the key short-term low (not ultra-aggressive in high volatility)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He wasn't interested in anything until the 3915.25 short-term low (15m) broke. You could short smaller short-term low breaks "if you want to be ultra aggressive," but with high volatility he wants to "know that I know": he doesn't want to catch a break below a minor short-term low and then see price run relative equal highs above. He was giving price a chance to run those highs first.
- **How to identify:** Pick the short-term low whose break on the 15m clearly confirms the shift out of consolidation.
- **Example in this video:** Consolidation; his prior paper position's final balance stopped out on a run up into a deeper FVG which made the high of day; then the break of 3915.25 around the 10:00 hour.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:01](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=61) — 3915.25 was the turning point; [0:04:15](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=255) — wanted that low broken; [0:10:37](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=637) — why not ultra aggressive; [0:13:00](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=780) — off air at 10:00 anticipating the low being taken.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 33
head: FVG after an old low breaks — not "support turned resistance"
body:
- **Kind:** rule (important distinction)
- **What ICT says:** After a run below an old low, he shorts the retrace into the fair value gap — not a retest of the old low as resistance. "If the fair value gap doesn't exist, I don't trust that level as an old support broken turned resistance." His levels are pre-classified by liquidity logic (where orders are), and the market creates patterns around them. The level shows where liquidity rests; the imbalance is what he keys off.
- **How to identify:** Old low (sell-side) taken with displacement; FVG left in the move; retrace into FVG.
- **Example in this video:** After 3915.25 breaks: FVG (visible on 5m, not 15m) → short; then a further FVG after breaking 3872.25 → another short; price didn't stop at the 3872.25 level on the retrace because it went up into the imbalance above it, then delivered lower to and through 3855.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:00](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=540) — not break-and-retest; [0:09:48](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=588) — why not stop at 3872.25; [0:11:25](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=685) — levels built on liquidity; confluence.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 33
head: Premium requirement vs. "in a hurry" delivery — use the short-term dealing range
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Measuring the 15m displacement leg, the FVG didn't retrace to a premium — he didn't expect it to, because price was "in a hurry" to get below the 3855 level for the week. Drop to the 1m and use the short-term dealing range (swing high to swing low): there the FVG retrace *was* at equilibrium or above (premium), confluent with the 3915.25 level. "You just don't have the experience to see it yet."
- **How to use:** If the HTF leg FVG is not in premium, check the smaller dealing range on the lower timeframe before rejecting the setup.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:02](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=302) — "some will say it didn't go to a premium"; [0:13:00](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=780) — in a hurry to 3855; [0:14:36](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=876) — 1m short-term dealing range premium.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines Ep 25's "hard line" premium rule: premium is relative to the dealing range you measure; under urgency, the lower-timeframe dealing range applies.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 33
head: Confluence (not a single factor)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Pushing the button requires several things together: the liquidity level (e.g., 3855 targeted only if 3915.25 breaks), an FVG, a further level break, another FVG, then delivery.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:25](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=685); [0:12:13](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=733).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 33
head: PM session: 1:30 low, last-hour rally into premium FVG, spool into the close
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:** At 1:30 PM watch the afternoon session; a short-term low formed and price rallied. In the last hour it rallied into a fair value gap in the premium of the range (target = above 50% of the swing). After 3:00 PM a small drop into an FVG, then an "algorithmic spool" running aggressively into the close up to a level seen on the hourly — a Friday reversal into an old imbalance, then consolidation into the close.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:40](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=400) — 1:30 PM, last hour into premium FVG; [0:07:26](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=446) — 5m equilibrium/premium; post-3 PM spool.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 33
head: Not a one-model trader
body:
- **Kind:** rule (context)
- **What ICT says:** He isn't a "one-trick pony" limited to the mentorship model; he won't spoon-feed a daily example of the model — finding them yourself in back-testing builds confidence and pattern recognition.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:49](https://youtu.be/8z6My18WZqA?t=349).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 34
head: Sunday opening gap as a weekly dynamic level (precursor to NWOG)
body:
- **Kind:** new framing / rule
- **What ICT says:** Plot the Sunday opening gap (the gap between Friday close and the Sunday evening reopen, ~6 PM ET) and extend it across the entire week. Many times there's "a lot of valuation around that gap" — it acts as a dynamic price level: if price is above it, look for it to act as support; if below, resistance. Some weeks run away from it and never return, but in consolidation weeks (e.g., an FOMC week) the choppy range-bound action keeps revisiting it. If price is going to trade down into the Sunday gap, look for it to first run above nearby swing highs / relative equal highs (buy-side).
- **How to identify:** Mark Friday's close and Sunday's open; shade the gap; extend right.
- **How to use:** Expect reactions at the gap's edges (he watched its lower end); combine with FVG/OB entries; in consolidation weeks use it as the range's pivot.
- **Example in this video:** ES: price traded below sell-side and into/through the Sunday gap down to an FVG, rallied to the opening range; at lunch retraced back up into the Sunday gap which acted as resistance; dropped to an order block (big down candle), accumulated, rallied back above the gap; retraced back into it as support (discount low); then FVG → 15m OB → run to 3952.75/3954.50.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:48](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=288) — lower end of Sunday gap to watch, resistance from below; [0:05:35](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=335) — lunch retracement into gap as resistance; [0:08:48](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=528) — "dynamic support/resistance" (and "blasphemy" joke); [0:09:36](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=576) — rule above = support, below = resistance; run highs before trading down into it; [0:10:25](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=625) — FOMC-week consolidation.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He knowingly uses retail language ("support/resistance") only for this gap, to make it understandable. Contrast with Ep 33, where old lows are not trusted as S/R without an FVG.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 34
head: Precise price delivery into an FVG (to the tick)
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** A 5m FVG he gave live: the low of one candle was 3926.75 and a later candle traded back up to exactly 3926.75 as its high — "perfect price delivery." These tools originated with index futures and bonds in the 1990s, not forex.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:27](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=147); [0:03:14](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=194).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 34
head: Sloppy vs clean sessions
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** "Sloppy" means the market gives very few options — you must know exactly what you're looking for. The morning was sloppy (even with a nice delivery, it lacked all the mechanics of entry); the afternoon had multiple clean entry mechanics (FVG, OB, OB) and a run to the objective, so it was his preferred session.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:10](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=430); [0:07:59](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=479).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 34
head: Target calling (3953) and order-block delivery
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** He called 3953 (rounded one quarter point above the 3952.75 old high); high printed 3954.50 (1.5 handles beyond). He preferred the run to that level over trading down to the Sunday gap or old London-open lows. 15m order block → rally "hammers" 3952.75.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:10](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=430) — 15m OB to 3952.75; [0:07:59](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=479) — 3953 vs 3954.50; [0:08:48](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=528) — preference for the run up.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 34
head: Unfilled gap ("missing data") as a draw
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** On the 15m there's a gap above ("missing data — an actual gap") which he believes won't be left open; price will want to draw up into it. Perfect delivery would reach the low of that candle (not expected to be perfect). If price goes above that area, it likely means a deeper run on the daily — running the high and reaching an order block whose low is at 4000.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:40](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=820); [0:14:29](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=869).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 34
head: Fibonacci on the impulse swing in the trade direction (premium/discount correction)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (correction of a common error)
- **What ICT says:** Many new students measure a range in the wrong direction (e.g., a high-to-low leg) and use its 50% as a discount for a long. Wrong. For a long, draw the Fib from the low up to the high of the *impulsive (expansion) swing in the direction you want to trade*; the anticipated retracement to and below 50% is the discount — hunt longs at that level or lower, ideally in an FVG. For a short, measure the down leg (high→low) and sell at/above 50%. "You don't want to use a price leg from high to low measuring something you're trying to go long on."
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m: low to high of the rally toward the relative equal highs/3953 target; retrace below 50% into an FVG = long. Same on a second dealing range (anchor high, run to low that hadn't been taken).
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:18](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=918) — the error (from a student's forex video); [0:16:04](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=964) — low→high for longs; [0:16:52](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=1012) — use impulsive swings in trade direction.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 34
head: 2m FVG — should not be revisited once price moves away
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** On the 2m, once price moved away from the FVG, he didn't want to see it come back into it (a sign of strength/validity).
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:15](https://youtu.be/t8flQP5jy-Q?t=675).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 35
head: Order block sensitive levels and the Mean Threshold
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:** For a candle used as an order block, the three sensitive areas are its low, its open, and the middle of its range. The midpoint (50%, Fib across the candle) is what he calls the **mean threshold**. When price trades up into the mean threshold of a daily bearish order block (up-close candle), that "bodes well for a continuation" to take out the short-term high beyond it.
- **How to identify:** Fib the OB candle high-to-low; 50% = mean threshold.
- **How to use:** Watch price reaction at low → open → mean threshold; reaching the mean threshold without rejection signals continuation through.
- **Example in this video:** ES daily: price consolidated right below the low of the up-close candle forming the daily bearish OB, then dug up into it during the session, reaching its mean threshold.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:05](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=5) — low, open, middle of the range; [0:00:54](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=54) — mean threshold defined; [0:08:47](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=527) — watching for mean threshold.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same idea as CE for FVGs, but applied to an order block candle's full range.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 35
head: Choosing the dealing range: use the most recent stage of the leg
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** A 5m price leg can deliver in stages. If one leg had a single pass and another has two stages (low → high → small retracement → second run), use the most recent stage — short-term low to short-term high — as the dealing range. Fib it; 50% is equilibrium; wait for a drop into discount, ideally into an FVG.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m: most recent stage measured; discount FVG below 50% traded into; long (also showed on Twitter).
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:14](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=194) — two-stage delivery, use most recent; [0:04:00](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=240) — equilibrium, discount FVG.

The opening (~4002, "check your own chart") was a little higher.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 35
head: SMT divergence — setup and timing
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule / how-to
- **What ICT says:** On TradingView, click the "+" compare button, add NQM2022 (NQ June 2022); it plots a line on closes by default — change the settings to plot on the **low** when comparing lows (highs for highs). If NQ makes a lower low while ES fails to, that's SMT (smart money technique): ES is accumulating while NQ takes liquidity — a "crack in correlation." They usually move in tandem; divergence tends to appear at 8:30, 9:30 and news releases. Without a bias you'll often see an apparent SMT that then disappears as they re-sync — so know what price is reaching for first.
- **How to use:** With bullish bias, a higher low in ES vs. a lower low in NQ (especially vs. the 8:30 low) is the "telltale sign" price goes higher; buy the stronger index's FVG/OB.
- **Example in this video:** ES drop back into the FVG made a higher low than the 8:30 low; NQ made a lower low → stop-out/accumulation; ES "compressed like a spring," then exploded at 9:30. He missed the ideal entry and used a close-proximity entry on a 15m order block.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:26](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=386) — TradingView compare setup, plot on low; [0:07:13](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=433) — times of divergence; need bias; [0:07:59](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=479) — ES higher low vs 8:30, NQ lower low.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 35
head: Early run before 7:00 AM → deep retracement → SMT near 9:30
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If there's a nice early run before (or at) 7:00 AM, expect a deep retracement, and look for the ideal scenario with SMT divergence around 9:30 — it will probably need a "cracking correlation" to set up the next leg (if there is one). Seeing an early run before 7 AM gives insight into what the 9:30 open will be like.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:34](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=814); [0:15:08](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=908).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 35
head: Staircase delivery (repeated discount FVG retracements) & not picking tops
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** On the 1h: dealing range low → high → retrace into discount FVG → rally; repeat (discount FVG, order block, rally, consolidate) — the algorithm picks up accumulated longs at each discount, pressing toward buy-side. With a bullish bias, don't try to sell/pick tops.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:34](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=574) — hourly structure; [0:10:21](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=621) — the repeated sequence; [0:11:09](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=669) — did you try to short?

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 35
head: High resistance liquidity run (why not short here)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition
- **What ICT says:** With many supporting ranges below (down-close candles supporting price, underlying bullish order flow), a reversal would have to pierce and break all those ranges — a high resistance liquidity run that's "likely to not form or pan out" (not impossible). So price is likely to "go up just to keep going higher, not go up to go down." Know narrative and bias, and what would constitute a short.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:59](https://youtu.be/MdYrslpUezU?t=719).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 36
head: Premium/discount on the hourly as "overbought/oversold" (no indicator needed)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Take the hourly swing low to swing high; equilibrium is the 50% level; anything above is premium, below is discount. Price dropping into a fair value gap below equilibrium = an "oversold condition" — "do we need an indicator to plot that? Absolutely not."
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:59](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=59).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 36
head: Sell-side clearing with no model entry = "tipping its hand"
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Before 9:30 price ran up into a premium; then it sank rapidly around the 9:30 opening, taking relative equal lows (sell-side), bounced briefly, then took another low — knocking out longs who tried to pick the bottom. There was no model short entry on that drop: "that's telling, it's tipping its hand" — it was a rush to clear sell-side liquidity, not a genuine bearish move. Retail rarely re-enters after being stopped like that.
- **How to identify:** Fast drop through obvious lows without a displacement/FVG setup that your model would short.
- **How to use:** Treat it as a liquidity sweep in a bullish context; look for the subsequent MSS + FVG long.
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:47](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=107) — run to premium then slide through relative equal lows; [0:05:42](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=342) — no model entry, tipping its hand.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 36
head: 8:30 failure to take the lows → deep retracement, not reversal
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He didn't believe certain lows would be taken because, if they were going to be, it should have happened at the 8:30 news — it didn't, so the pullback was just a deep retracement before price was sent higher into a premium before 9:30.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:42](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=342).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 36
head: Which market structure shift counts? (depends on your range)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Students see multiple short-term structure breaks and ask which is "the" MSS. Answer: it depends on the range you're working within. He was playing the run up to a premium (as tweeted), so in that range the MSS occurs when price takes out *that* range's relevant high, then drops into the FVG — which is what he bought.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:55](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=295); [0:05:42](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=342).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 36
head: Long after sell stops are cleared (5m/1m execution)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model application
- **What ICT says:** Sequence: MSS → rally (rebalancing the drop) → 5m FVG → draw on the morning high (short-term highs) → overshoot into a deep-premium FVG → pullback inside the range → FVG, MSS, relative equal highs → drop into a very good order block → rally into imbalance → consolidation, bump above short-term high → final drop clearing sell-side → his long. "I'm buying those sell stops."
- **Example in this video:** ES 1m: long 5 contracts @ 4120 at a discount; ~5 handles of heat; stop below the swing low (not hit). Tweet: "sell-side liquidity taken, free to run to 4143.50." 3 contracts sold at 4139.25 (first partial, when tweeted); final 2 filled by limit at 4143.75; price later went a bit higher. Earlier small morning trade with partials and a limit fill also shown.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:34](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=154) — MSS, 5m FVG, morning high as DOL; [0:04:07](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=247) — long at discount, 5 handles heat, stop below swing low; [0:06:30](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=390) — entry 4120, tweet; [0:07:17](https://youtu.be/pWnMpdN_g98?t=437) — partials 4139.25 / 4143.75.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 36
head: Weekly trading discipline (NFP week / month transition)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In the first week of the month (non-farm payroll week, transition between months) he typically likes to have all trading done by Wednesday. Having made his trade, he's satisfied for the week. Without a clear definitive objective on the daily (could go either way), he sits on his hands. Consistency comes from rules of engagement.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: Breaker (definition) + daily FVG confluence
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** A breaker (bullish) forms from a low, a high, then a lower low — find the high in between and extend it out in time; when price trades back down into that area, it's the breaker. Here it overlapped a daily fair value gap; price came down, filled the FVG, and began to rally.
- **How to identify:** Low → high → lower low (sell-side taken) → price rallies above; the in-between high's zone becomes support on retest.
- **Example in this video:** ES daily: price worked down into the FVG/breaker zone, filled the FVG, tested it again and rallied; next buy-side = short-term high above; with acceleration, relative equal highs and an FVG higher up.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:02](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=2) — breaker defined; FVG fill; [0:00:48](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=48) — next targets.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: Daily bias "meat on the bone" — consecutive bullish days until the high is taken
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** When the market moves up from a swing low, it's easy to assume it will come back up to the prior high. If each day is bullish (with maybe one exception), the bias is expected to stay bullish until that high is taken. After it's taken, a day or two of retracement is logical (here back into the FVG it created), then it tests and rallies again.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:48](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=48); [0:01:35](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=95).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: NFP Friday — conditional expectation and why not to trade it
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Do not speculate on non-farm payroll Friday — it can be very volatile, choppy, or a dud; students lack the experience to weather it. Instead study it: determine what side of liquidity it will reach for before the 8:30 release and watch the 1m/5m when volatility hits. His bias expectation: the short-term high could be run overnight; if not, and at 8:30 price is above the daily FVG's high (the relevant candle's low), expect an attempt toward that high (not necessarily through it).
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:35](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=95) — don't trade NFP; [0:03:11](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=191) — 8:30 conditional; [0:03:58](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=238) — study liquidity sides around the release.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: Stop trading by Wednesday's NY session in NFP weeks
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He teaches students to stop trading by the New York session on Wednesday: if you haven't "bagged anything" from Sunday's weekly open until Wednesday's NY session begins, don't trade; if you've profited, stop for the week and only observe. Thursday and Friday of NFP weeks are choppy, sporadic, come back against you and "lose a lot of their precision" (not always, most of the time). Avoid arenas where your proven walk-forward results are diminished; it forges discipline and patience.
- **Example in this video:** He forced himself to short on Thursday (covered as price dipped below a short-term low) specifically to show his precision drops on such days.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:47](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=287) — stop by Wednesday NY session; [0:05:34](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=334) — Thu/Fri lose precision; [0:10:18](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=618) — avoid built-in disadvantages; [0:11:08](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=668) — Sunday open to Wednesday NY.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: HTF levels transposed to lower timeframes (not S/R)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Lines on the hourly are not drawn as hourly support/resistance — they're the daily FVG boundaries (two blue lines) and the daily short-term high (red line), transposed down. Losing that context makes LTF price look like noise.
- **Example in this video:** ES 1h: Wednesday hit the daily FVG low, consolidated, dropped to it again, then a mad dash took the short-term high (bullish MSS) and relative equal highs; next draw = buy-side above; a small FVG below might be revisited first.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:21](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=381); [0:07:07](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=427).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: Power of Three on the intraday chart (not noise)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** The day opened (NY midnight opening price), consolidated, rallied, dropped into the daily FVG low (below the midnight open — the manipulation), bounced, took the short-term high, and closed near the high: accumulation, manipulation, distribution. Easy to see on a daily candle; on 1m/5m people call it noise, but it's the same thing on a smaller interval.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:54](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=474) — dropping below the NY midnight open; [0:08:42](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=522) — power of three; [0:09:29](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=569) — not noise.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: Spotter call: 5m FVG above market price as the draw
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:** At 11:37 AM ET June 2 he tweeted asking followers to locate the 5m FVG above market price — the draw. It was reached shortly after. He acts as a "spotter": points to a level at the current market price and asks you to study how and *when* price gets there — not a trade signal. Above the NY midnight opening price, after a drop to a discount creating the low of day, heading into lunch: delivery could come before 12:00 or in the PM session (~1:00–1:30).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: Journaling chart template (2m example) with timing observations
body:
- **Kind:** rule (study method)
- **What ICT says:** Mark up the chart after the fact: order block (the down-close candle before the up move), consolidation, drop into the FVG, then the delivery to the target. Record observations — e.g., price started delivering ~6 minutes (3 × 2m candles) after hitting the FVG and took roughly 20 minutes to reach the target. Phrase every annotation as if you saw it beforehand (self-talk) to build pseudo-experience; keep it factual and positive — never "I wish I'd seen it" or "I'm never going to get this." Review each weekend (previous week/month). Weeks to months; "certainly by the first year." "You will do this or you will fail."
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:33](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=1053) — arrows are illustration, not trades; OB + FVG; [0:18:20](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=1100) — 6 min to start, ~20 min to deliver; [0:19:54](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=1194) — self-talk; [0:20:41](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=1241) — never negative.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Repeats and extends Ep 27's backtesting-annotation method with timing measurements.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 37
head: PM session: lunch low stop run then old high taken
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** During NY lunch a short-term low formed; price dropped and took it (stop run), then drifted up and took the old high ("unfinished business"). After the low, no 2022-model entry, but the FVG continuation he pointed out live was the only other setup (not traded).
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:15](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=1335); [0:23:02](https://youtu.be/HuZurY0ghDI?t=1382).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Narrative / Draw on liquidity  (aliases: where the market is likely to go next)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Narrative is knowing what price should do, why, and what it will run into along the way that proves the assumed narrative is actually underway.
  - He says he is not teaching entry patterns where a precise entry price is what matters most. He is teaching how to work out where the market is likely to go next (the DOL).
  - The DOL is set algorithmically, not by "buying/selling pressure". Read price and the logic behind it instead of basing trades on indicators (overbought/oversold, line crossovers).
  - Once you can read price, entries are "the easiest thing to do".
- **How to identify:** First mark the higher-timeframe objective (here the daily FVG, prior-day high, relative equal highs/lows). Then watch for events at key times that confirm or reject it.
- **How to use:** The narrative alone is not an entry. Even after he believed price would run to the prior-day high, he says buying right away could have stopped him out by being early. He waited for displacement, measured premium/discount, and only bought in a discount.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m. Price traded down into the 15m FVG and rallied from it. That told him the algorithm was "priming itself" for an afternoon run toward the previous day's high (4168.25). At 10:35 ET he tweeted "note previous day's high".
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:18](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=378) — what he teaches: where price goes, not entry patterns; [0:07:54](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=474) — definition of narrative; [0:28:22](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1702) — 15m FVG retrace leads to the afternoon narrative; [0:29:09](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1749) — narrative alone is not a buy signal.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He stresses he does not need to be right. Being wrong about 4070 cost nothing because there was no setup and no trade.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Abandoning / changing bias  (aliases: changing gears, managing your bias)

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Fair Value Gap vs liquidity void "fill" (Chris Lori comparison)  (aliases: imbalance, fair value)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Chris Lori teaches that the market comes back to fill liquidity voids completely. ICT does not teach that. Full fills can happen, but because he understands the algorithm, it is not likely most of the time.
  - What makes an imbalance a fair value gap is that price comes back down into it (into part of it). It is "a fair value to buy it if you're bullish." He does not insist imbalances completely rebalance.
  - His precision comes from knowing where the market is reaching, then using the imbalances along the way.
- **How to use:** Treat FVGs as places to buy (in a bullish narrative) on a partial return, not as zones that must fully fill.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m. After a short-term MSS higher, price created an FVG and traded back into it. Several imbalances along the leg were each partially revisited.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:43](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=283) — Chris Lori liquidity voids vs ICT; [0:05:31](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=331) — "fair value to buy it if you're bullish".
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He calls Chris Lori the only technical analysis educator he recommends, while stressing the "stark contrast" in approach.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Market Structure Shift + FVG retrace (not support/resistance)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - After the run took out the short-term high on the daily/15m, he calls it an "absolute market structure shift bullish".
  - Price came back and rebalanced the FVG and dug slightly past the broken high. That is why he is not trading "resistance broken turns support".
  - His logic: price went through a short-term high, created an imbalance, then traded back into the imbalance.
- **How to identify:** A short-term high is taken with displacement and an FVG is left behind. Watch for the retrace into that FVG, not into the broken high.
- **How to use:** The FVG is the area to watch. If price digs into it, repels higher, and takes out the short-term high, that sets the stage for the afternoon move.
- **Example in this video:** ES 15m: price ran higher, left an FVG, and traded back into it after the 9:30 open. On 5m it "doesn't look like" an FVG unless you carry the 15m zone down.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:43](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=523) — 15m FVG is the area to watch for the afternoon; [0:09:30](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=570) — MSS; digs past the high into the FVG.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Multi-timeframe workflow: 15m bellwether into 5m
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The 15m chart is the "bellwether chart".
  - Shade the 15m FVG on your chart, then drop to the 5m and watch price trade into the shaded area.
  - If you stay on one timeframe and do not carry HTF analysis down, "you're gonna be trading blind".
  - Same with the daily FVG: shade it, and on the 5m you will see price dip into its lower end and rally.
- **How to use:** Mark the daily PD array, then the 15m FVG, then time entries on the 5m.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:04](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=664) — shade the 15m FVG, drop to 5m; [0:28:22](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1702) — daily FVG shaded, seen from 5m.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** A Twitter follower asked whether the logic works outside the 1–5m charts. Yes: it scales to whatever timeframe and chart you want, as long as you know where price is drawing.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Scalping model vs trading the daily range
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The model on the YouTube channel is a scalping model.
  - Day-trading the daily range uses the 15m and 5m charts.
  - You can use the scalping model as your entry criteria while trading with daily-range logic and narrative.
  - His goal in daily-range trading is "the lion's portion" of the daily range, not the exact high or low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:21](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1041) — model = scalping; daily range = 15m and 5m; [0:26:00](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1560) — why he teaches reading price when the model gives nothing.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He openly did not trade the YouTube model this day. "When the model speaks I'm going to show you", but not every market or session gives the model setup.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Power of 3 / classic buy day with the midnight opening price
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - If bullish, buy at or close to the midnight opening price.
  - Power of 3 when bullish: from the midnight opening price, price drops to create the low of the day, then rallies.
  - "Advanced ICT": if you know price will go down to go up, you can wait for the drop, an MSS, and a return into the 15m FVG.
  - A "classic buy day": open at midnight, trade down to create the low of day, rally, then form an OTE / FVG, or buy the short-term low during SMT divergence.
- **Example in this video:** ES: the low of day formed at about 9:10 ET (he first said 9:05, then corrected it), below the midnight open, and rallied into the 9:30 open.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:34](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=994) — midnight opening price; buy at or near it when bullish; [0:18:08](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1088) — low of day at 9:10 ET; [0:41:57](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2517) — "classic buy day" description.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: NY lunch hour / PM session: consolidation vs retracement into lunch
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Bullish PM rule (from earlier notes): price runs higher in the morning, consolidates into lunch, then after lunch drops to sweep sell stops below a short-term low or below the lunch lows, then rallies.
  - If price is consolidating into lunch: mark the swing lows during the lunch hour, wait for price to sweep them, then rally.
  - If price is retracing (not consolidating) into lunch, that signals "they're going to work through lunch". It is a fast market.
  - Floor-trader origin: in the open-outcry days, floor traders stayed on the floor through lunch in a fast market. The algorithm keeps that same behaviour.
  - The NY lunch hour is noon–1:00 PM NY time.
- **How to identify:** Ask whether price is going sideways (consolidation) or making a directional pullback (retracement) going into lunch.
- **How to use:** In a fast-market retracement, look for a short-term low forming ahead of lunch. Then look for the sweep of that low into a discount FVG during lunch.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m. After failing at 4140, price dropped into an FVG and rallied, leaving smooth relative equal highs. It created a short-term low ahead of noon. During the lunch hour it dropped below that low into the discount FVG, then rallied through 4140 and the old high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:01](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=901) — PM session and lunch introduced; [0:19:44](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1184) — bullish PM liquidity rule; [0:20:30](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1230) — retracement, not consolidation; [0:22:05](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1325) — "work through lunch", floor-trader origin.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This extends the earlier PM-session rules by adding the fast-market/retracement case.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Dealing range, premium/discount, and choosing the swing to measure
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - When trading the daily range, factor in the midnight opening price. Price had already gone above it, and he did not expect it to go back below the earlier low. So measuring from the earlier low is "pointless".
  - He used the market-structure swing low (the one that started the displacement) to the swing high as the dealing range.
  - He wanted a retracement to a discount (below 50%) and the FVG there. "The algorithm reprices to a discount."
  - Checklist: Was there displacement? Was it an energetic run? Measure low to high, wait for a discount, find the FVG below 50%.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m. Fib from the swing low to the swing high: 50% was below, with an FVG under it. Price traded into it, made a short-term low, then dipped again into the FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:16](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1276) — why that swing low (midnight open factor); [0:23:38](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1418) — algorithm reprices to a discount; [0:45:10](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2710) — dealing range low/high, fib, 50%, FVG.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Buying sell stops below a short-term low (stop run inside the FVG)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Smooth relative equal highs are seen as resistance. Shorts trail their stops just above them, and sell stops sit below the nearby short-term low.
  - Think like smart money: buy sell-side liquidity, with the order resting under the short-term low inside the FVG.
  - He prefers buying the sell stops because "it really fortifies the setup" and gets him in where smart money buys. Had price rallied without the sweep, he would simply have missed the move.
- **How to use:** Place a buy limit just below the short-term low that sits inside the discount FVG. Stop goes below the FVG / lower low.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m, NY lunch hour. Short-term low at 4110.50. His fill was at 4110.25, one tick below it, on the candle whose low was 4108.25. Price rallied, consolidated, pushed through the old high and the 4140 level, and later returned to the FVG once more (an OTE) and rallied again. It still did not reach the prior-day high of 4168.25.
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:58](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1798) — buying sell stops, entry candle; [0:36:21](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2181) — execution details (4110.50 low, 4110.25 fill); [0:46:00](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2760) — "I'm buying that very candle".

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: SMT divergence (ES vs NQ) and the TradingView setup  (aliases: smart money tool / technique)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - SMT is "smart money tool or smart money technique" (he never settled on what the T stands for). It is his way of measuring real accumulation and distribution.
  - When bullish, compare lows: for example, ES makes a higher low while NQ makes a lower low. The stronger index is under accumulation, and the weaker index's lower low is "just a stop hunt" below a short-term low.
  - Use it when price retraces into a discount FVG and you expect a move up.
  - TradingView setup: click the "+" compare tab, add NQM2022 (later NQU2022), open its gear settings, and set it to plot the low, because you are comparing lows when bullish.
- **Example in this video:** ES vs NQ. (1) At the morning low near 9:10 ET, ES made a higher low while NQ made a lower low, which set the stage for the run up. (2) At the lunch-hour retracement into the FVG, a further SMT appeared on the low compare.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:48](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=948) — ES higher low vs NQ lower low; [0:39:33](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2373) — TradingView compare setup; [0:41:09](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2469) — compare lows inside the FVG after a discount retrace; [0:46:48](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2808) — recap.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says this is how you are supposed to talk to yourself in your journal: "this low versus this low".

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Entry variations on the same bullish setup  (aliases: OTE, turtle soup, FVG entry, buy stop above swing high)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** In answer to "which FVG do I use", he gives several ways to enter the same idea:
  1. **OTE:** fib from the low to the high and buy the 62–79% retracement.
  2. **Turtle soup:** a low, then a lower low violating it, with the OTE on top of that.
  3. **FVG in discount:** low to high, find the FVG below the 50% level, and buy when price trades to the top of it. Stop below the lower low.
  4. **Buy stop above the swing high:** wait for price to trade into the FVG, then put a buy stop above the swing high formed just before price entered the FVG. Stop just below the lowest low after it hits. This is "buying strength". It is not his preferred strategy.
- **How to use:** All of these depend on a bias that has been "corrected and calibrated" by what price did at key times (9:30).
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:46](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2566) — OTE, turtle soup, FVG below 50%; [0:43:33](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2613) — buy stop above swing high (not preferred).

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Order block (down-closed candle) as a management reference
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** After the run through 4140, he drew a line at a down-closed candle (an order block) to see whether price would be supported there. Price traded through it, and once it did he closed out the trade. He was still inside a multi-day daily range, so the prior-day high might not trade that day and might need Wednesday.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:47](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1847) — order block traded through, trade closed.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Trade management: partials at old imbalances / old buy-side liquidity, stop raising
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - He took half off where an old area of buy-side liquidity and an old imbalance sat to the left. That area could be "just a stop run" or a failure swing, and he could be wrong.
  - He did not need price above the short-term high to take that partial.
  - He raised his stop as price moved up, because price had already used the FVG once and twice and "should never come back down" into it. If it did, he would be wrong and would close any remaining position.
  - He would rather take his own exit than be stopped out.
- **Example in this video:** About half off (the caption is unclear on the contract count; it mentions "10 contracts"). Then 3 contracts at 4134.50, 1 contract at 4141.50 through the old high and the 4140 level (he says he was "three seconds late"), then the last contract closed manually. The stop was never threatened.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:40](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=760) — rectangle zone for half off; [0:13:27](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=807) — old BSL and imbalance to the left; [0:25:13](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=1513) — raising stop, kill the trade if the FVG fails; [0:37:10](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2230) — partials detail.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 38
head: Futures contract rollover rule
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** He monitors barchart.com and rolls to the next contract (June to September, for example) when open interest in the next contract becomes larger than in the current one. He notes this differs from how others roll.
- **Timestamps:** [0:39:33](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2373) — NQM2022 → NQU2022 / ESU2022; [0:40:22](https://youtu.be/36184dDAqtM?t=2422) — open-interest rollover rule.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 39
head: HTF levels transposed to LTF; keep annotations simple
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Start your annotations on the higher timeframe and keep them simple: the level price will draw to, and the key levels that would change or confirm a bias. Then carry exactly those levels to the lower timeframe. Lower-timeframe price is "subordinate" to HTF levels. Many new students get lost in the timeframes.
- **Example in this video:** ES daily (left) and 1h (right). The daily relative equal lows and the daily FVG below them were drawn on the hourly.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:09](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=9) — daily and 1h side by side, LTF subordinate to HTF; [0:04:58](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=298) — start annotations on HTF, keep it simple.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 39
head: Conditional narrative, not "always sweep equal lows and reverse"
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The forecast was conditional. If price went below the daily relative equal lows, it would not "go down to go up". It would keep drawing into the daily FVG below.
  - That implies the volatility would be large enough for a large-range day.
  - Others teaching his concepts (or their own twists on them) claim price always hits relative equal lows and then reverses. "That's not the case." Narrative must be understood, and narrative requires experience, which he is lending.
- **How to use:** When he names an objective (4070), study what sits at that level yourself (old lows, relative equal lows, FVG). He will not spoon-feed it.
- **Example in this video:** ES. Pre-market (before 9:30) DOL was 4070, below the daily relative equal lows. Beyond that, the target was the daily FVG. Price ran through 4070, then to about 4040 (caption says "440"), and closed inside the larger daily FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:58](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=58) — 4070 DOL below relative equal lows; [0:02:35](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=155) — below the lows means draw into the FVG, large range day; [0:05:45](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=345) — "not always equal lows then reverse".

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 39
head: FVG and order block on the hourly: candle bodies stay inside the FVG
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - FVG restated as three candles where the middle candle has an exposed area not overlapped by the candle before or the candle after.
  - On the 1h, price rallied into an FVG and up into a bearish order block. "You can take that trade" at the order block.
  - He points out that the candle bodies stayed mostly between the FVG's two levels. Wicks poked out, but "largely the volume is encapsulated" inside the gap.
- **Example in this video:** ES 1h. A swing low with displacement, consolidation into midnight NY, then a rally into the FVG and the bearish order block above. An old low back to the left was a natural target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:18](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=438) — 1h FVG and consolidation into midnight; [0:08:06](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=486) — three-candle definition, bodies inside the FVG.

title: 2022 ICT Mentorship Episode 39
head: Power of 3 (bearish) with the midnight opening price; Judas swing
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - On a down day, short at or above the NY midnight opening price, as close to it as you can.
  - Bearish Power of 3: accumulate shorts, then manipulate the traders already short (the Judas swing) by running up to a short-term premium in the dealing range, then distribute lower.
  - Hold shorts for the daily range to fulfil. "Submit yourself to time": wait until the last hour, 3:00–4:00 PM, for delivery into the target.
  - In London, price rallied and built a premium ahead of the 8:30 window.
- **Example in this video:** ES 5m. Price hovered around the midnight open, and London rallied to build a premium before 8:30. A high formed, short-term SSL was taken, and price retraced up and consolidated (11:00–noon). It took buy-side again during lunch, then broke lower and attacked the SSL below 4070, then ran to about 4040 and closed inside the daily FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:29](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=629) — midnight open plus Power of 3, Judas swing; [0:11:17](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=677) — partial at 4070, wait until 3–4 PM; [0:13:45](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=825) — short at or above midnight open; [0:14:37](https://youtu.be/yFpHbBnsK_c?t=877) — whole daily range on 5m.
