title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Power of three / daily range framing
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** If the AM action were the whole day closing at 4:00 PM, you'd see the daily range. It has a Judas swing (fake rally), then a drop and a close near the low: power of three. Every AM session you're essentially looking for that to form. The fake manipulation "does the harmful work": it stops people out of good trades or traps them in the wrong direction (here, trapped long), then drops. Retail ("street money") looks for support and resistance. ICT looks for liquidity and inefficiencies.
- **Timestamps:** [1:01:38](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=3698), [1:02:25](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=3745)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: FVG classification & annotation (SIBI / BISI)  (aliases: inefficiencies, imbalances)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The middle candle's close names the gap. A **down-close** middle candle = **SIBI** (sell-side imbalance, buy-side inefficiency): it offered delivery only on the downside and is inefficient for any move back up. An **up-close** middle candle = **BISI** (buy-side imbalance, sell-side inefficiency).
  - SIBI definition: a down-close candle where the previous candle's low and the next candle's high don't connect. The only bridge between them is the down-close candle.
  - Everything from the first candle's low to the third candle's high is inefficient and "invites" price to trade back into it. That doesn't mean now, or even this session.
  - **Keep the original FVG levels** (low, consequent encroachment/midpoint, high) even after partial fills, because they're used again. Mentally note the **remaining unfilled portion**. Tiny remaining slivers matter: ICT has placed limit orders just beyond such slivers and had them run with no significant drawdown.
  - If price later revisits, it may just tap the high of the gap. If it goes above and comes back down, he uses the candle's wick and its halfway point as the retracement limit, and the gap becomes an inversion FVG (caption somewhat unclear here).
  - "These inefficiencies are the real support and resistance": price kisses them, turns on a dime, and bodies stop at them.
  - Color scheme is up to you. He won't share his exact colors, so copycats can't pass his charts off as theirs.
- **How to identify:** After checking for relative equal highs/lows on 15m, 5m and 1m (or finding none), annotate all inefficiencies, starting on the 1m and working back up.
- **Timestamps:** [1:03:11](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=3791) annotate inefficiencies once the relative equal highs/lows check is done; down-close = SIBI. [1:04:49](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=3889) small remaining gaps used for limit orders. [1:05:39](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=3939) keep original levels, note the remaining portion. [1:23:16](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4996) keep low/CE/high; inefficiencies are the real S/R.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Volume imbalance inside an FVG: draw to the body, ignore the wick
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (he calls it new and his own)
- **What ICT says:**
  - A volume imbalance is the separation between one candle's **body** and the next candle's body. If the bodies don't overlap or at least touch, there's a volume imbalance.
  - When an FVG has a volume imbalance in it, the FVG's boundary should incorporate the volume imbalance, which means taking it to the **body** rather than the wick. "The wicks are not the true narrative." A wick is like a child coloring outside the lines.
  - Wicks inside such an FVG that reach only up to the CE (halfway) or less are disregarded. Use the candle body.
- **How to identify:** Zoom in. Check whether adjacent candle bodies leave a gap. If they do, re-draw the FVG edge at the body.
- **Example:** Aug 6, 1m: he corrects one of his own SIBI drawings because its edge should include a volume imbalance between bodies.
- **Timestamps:** [1:06:28](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=3988) "look closely, what's wrong". [1:07:16](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4036) VI definition. [1:08:53](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4133) VI means ignore the wick. [1:09:40](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4180) wicks up to CE or less are ignored; take it to the body.
- **Nuance:** He says you won't find this in books or among "five-minute trainer" copies. The exact wording on which wicks are ignored is a little loose in the captions.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Overshoot past CE = the spread
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** When price trades into an FVG up to consequent encroachment "plus a little bit more", the small bump past the level is the algorithm giving the spread to anyone who used that level for entry, so they get filled. It isn't "buying pressure".
- **Example:** Aug 6, 1m: price rallies right into a SIBI's CE plus a tick or so, then folds.
- **Timestamps:** [1:10:29](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4229)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Inversion FVG — the highest-precision form  (aliases: iFVG, role reversal)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - **All** of his PD arrays have an inversion aspect: every one can reverse its role. He introduced iFVGs on Twitter Spaces "last year" and will detail them in his book.
  - The highest-precision, most trustworthy iFVGs depend on this context: after 7:00 there's a smooth area (relative equal highs), price runs it (a stop hunt), and an FVG **inside the range that creates the bearish breaker** fails.
  - In the bearish case, the inverting gap is the **BISI** in the up-leg that ran the relative equal highs. Without the time and narrative context, a beginner would treat that BISI as a buy and get collapsed on.
  - Required behavior: price runs above the gap, comes back below it, then redelivers up into it (it acts as resistance) before a deeper protraction lower. That's what his old tweets meant by "want to see this FVG act as an inversion FVG".
  - Once it inverts, the BISI is the only buy-side gap of interest. After a valid return it "sells off", and your focus shifts to SIBIs.
- **How to use:** Sell the return into the iFVG. Respect its CE. For stops, see the breaker section.
- **Example:** Aug 6, 1m, just after 7:00: relative equal highs form and are run. The up-leg's BISI then fails. Price breaks down, returns into it, respects CE, and breaks lower. Later another return gives an OTE as well.
- **Timestamps:** [1:13:39](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4419) all PD arrays invert. [1:14:27](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4467) highest-precision iFVGs need the post-7:00 relative equal highs context. [1:16:54](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4614) the BISI in the breaker range; beginners would buy it. [1:43:32](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6212) must go above, then below, then redeliver.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: First FVG prior to the stop run (change in state of delivery)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Always note the very first FVG *prior to* a stop run. He colors it red or pink. It marks a change in direction and "acts just like an order block": it is the change in the state of delivery. The narrative: price goes up after 7:00, stop hunt, breaks lower, comes back up into an inefficiency, and specifically the first FVG prior to the stop hunt.
- **If it doesn't form:** use the breaker instead (below).
- **Timestamps:** [1:27:20](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5240), [1:28:07](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5287)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Breaker vs. FVG in the stop-hunt leg (premium entry) + breaker stop rules  (aliases: bearish breaker)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - The breaker, as first taught on BabyPips around 2011–2012: a high, a low, a stop run above the high, then a reversal back into the range. The most sensitivity is in the **lowest down-close candle prior to the run-up**. The bearish breaker can be the consecutive down-close candles.
  - The refinement: look at the leg from the breaker up to the high where stops were taken. **If that leg has an FVG, navigate away from the breaker and use that premium gap.** Others will trade the breaker or the low point and won't be comfortable selling near the high. The gap created by the drop off the iFVG is "the sweet spot": your OTE, "your 2022 model".
  - **Breaker stop:** above the **highest high of the consecutive down-close candles**, plus maybe one or two ticks. Many times he uses the exact high, because a good breaker won't want to go back into its full range.
  - **But** if there's a gap inside the stop-hunt leg, price can return all the way up into it, maybe with a small "mohawk" wick spike outside while the body stays inside or below the gap. The breaker-based stop isn't safe in that case.
- **How to use:** Use the stop-hunt-leg FVG as the primary short entry. Use the breaker only when no such gap exists.
- **Timestamps:** [1:15:16](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4516) breaker history. [1:16:06](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4566) sensitivity in the lowest down-close candle. [1:20:04](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4804) the FVG in the stop-hunt leg beats the breaker. [1:28:53](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5333) breaker stop rules and the mohawk caveat.
- **Nuance:** He suggests going back over your old breaker studies or losing trades. This signature (the gap in the stop-hunt leg) is often the factor you missed.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: One-sided delivery focus: extend every same-side FVG
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Once the state of delivery turns bearish, focus **only on SIBIs** ("every single SIBI") and every short-term high, even single ones, because stops sit above them. Extend each SIBI to the right. This is what "extend it to the right" meant on Twitter.
  - **Ignore BISIs** while bearish. Don't highlight or extend them. The exception: if price does something violent and starts to reverse, attention moves to the BISI as a potential inversion FVG.
  - Even inefficiencies that have already been used get extended in time. Price will push up into them, resist, and continue toward the draw.
  - Don't expect a simple "price enters gap, sell it". Anticipate some manipulation. Example: a return into an old SIBI that first takes the stops of shorts who sat just above the energetic drop, then breaks down off CE. Bodies respect the gap. Wicks may do a little damage, but not to random locations.
  - This removes the ambiguity of "which FVG do I pick". The rest comes with experience.
- **Example:** Aug 6, 1m, roughly 8:00–9:00: price bumps back into an old SIBI, works around its CE, drops, and leaves a new inefficiency. Bodies stop exactly at the levels while wicks bump the bottom of the SIBI. Price breaks lower.
- **Timestamps:** [1:25:42](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5142) only SIBIs until the narrative changes. [1:29:41](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5381) key off every SIBI and every short-term high. [1:31:18](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5478) ignore the BISI unless there's a violent reversal. [1:39:26](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5966) extend right; expect manipulation.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: How far can it go: ranges & draw
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - After a reversal pattern, measure the potential run using the range **prior to that reversal pattern** that formed after the relative equal highs were taken. Price "gravitates to that low".
  - For this beginner model, the target is the opposing relative equal high or low.
  - For holding longer (advanced, not for Caleb), use the **previous day's low or high** as the next logical draw.
  - Other ranges that can anchor your own model: the 7:00–8:00 hour range, the highest high and lowest low since 9:00, and the 9:30 opening. When price trades to them, you're out. You don't need 100 handles a day.
- **Timestamps:** [1:21:40](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4900) range prior to the reversal. [1:35:25](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5725) the pre-7:00 low and the extended inefficiencies. [1:41:55](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6115) previous day's high/low for longer holds. [2:22:49](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=8569) hourly and opening ranges as model anchors.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Optimal Trade Entry (OTE)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / example
- **What ICT says:** OTE has been his flagship pattern on the channel since 2012. After a market structure shift, measure high to low. The OTE is the **62–72% retracement** (he first misspeaks "60") plus the **70.5** level. Aug 6's stop hunt and breakdown was a classic OTE that the old free lessons would have caught. The new signatures (iFVG, the stop-hunt-leg FVG) add precision and help you trust holding the trade.
- **Timestamps:** [1:36:14](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5774) shift in market structure. [1:37:01](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=5821) 62–72%, 70.5.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Consolidation & over-used gaps: when NOT to engage
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Long, protracted consolidations with both relative equal highs and lows: sit still. Otherwise you're "playing the breakout game", and he is "not a breakout artist".
  - Once one side is run, it usually attacks the other.
  - If price is back inside a SIBI that has already been overlapped and respected **twice**, that's low probability. Even if it then crashes 1,000 points, it isn't a trade he'd take. The day is complete.
  - If the day isn't obvious, sit on your hands and turn off the charts. "I don't know" is an acceptable and respectable answer. A choppy, range-bound day ("unfulfilled delivery of price") is to be avoided.
- **Example:** Aug 6: both relative equal lows and highs form. Price runs higher, then down below the lows. Then it sits back in a twice-used SIBI: no trade, day done (morning).
- **Timestamps:** [1:43:32](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6212) sit still, not a breakout artist. [1:45:56](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6356) one side taken, then the other. [1:46:45](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6405) twice-overlapped SIBI is low probability. [2:12:30](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=7950) if it's not obvious, don't trade.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Hourly Fibonacci standard-deviation range finding
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (homework exercise)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Done **after the fact** only. For each hour, anchor the Fib from the hour's high to the lowest low: 7:00, then 8:00, then 9:00 (the highest high and lowest low up to 9:00).
  - His settings project standard deviations: one SD, two SD, and **2.5 SD**, which is usually the extreme for wicks. The caption is unclear on exact level labels ("two, which is one standard deviation").
  - Projections from different hours that cluster close together give a ballpark of how far price can reach, without needing ADR.
  - **By itself it's "useless".** It only matters when it converges with a real old low or old high (a liquidity pool). He doesn't demand the exact extreme. He exits at the highest-probability convergence and doesn't care if price runs 200 handles beyond.
- **Example:** Aug 6: the 7:00, 8:00 and 9:00 projections clustered. Price went below an old low and came close to the deepest projection but fell short. "That's fine."
- **Timestamps:** [1:53:30](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6810) start measuring swings after the fact. [1:54:16](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6856) 1, 2 and 2.5 SD, done each hour. [1:55:03](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6903) clustering; useless alone. [1:56:38](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6998) convergence with an old high/low as the exit logic.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Immediate rebalance (+ breakaway gap, order block)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - **Immediate rebalance:** an extended-range candle goes up. Price drops back and **just touches that candle's high**, rather than filling a gap, then runs to an objective (liquidity or an inefficiency).
  - He also wanted a nearby FVG to **stay open** (not traded fully down into the candle high). An FVG that stays open acts as a **breakaway gap**.
  - These "drills and exercises" teach anticipatory price reading and lead later to entries, stops and management.
- **Example:** Aug 6, after the AM selloff: there's a disruption at the lows (sell side taken), and relative equal highs sit above. He expects a poke above the day's high, which is the initial high near 7:00 (the "blue level"). Price does an immediate rebalance (touches the candle), rallies, trades back down into a down-close candle (an **order block**), closes the inefficiency once more, then expands up through the 7:00 high. That's a 40+ handle run. After touching the high of day he'd be done: no afternoon trading.
- **Timestamps:** [2:27:41](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=8861) definition and the breakaway gap wish. [2:34:55](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=9295) it played out: immediate rebalance, then OB. [2:35:43](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=9343) breakaway gap and OB detail; done for the day.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: 15-second chart & Price Delivery Continuum Theory
body:
- **Kind:** refinement ("extra credit", explicitly not for beginners)
- **What ICT says:**
  - **Price Delivery Continuum Theory:** with an expected draw, the fractal market offers continuous participation. Once a timeframe has used up its entry opportunities, go to a lower timeframe (down to 15s or 5s) instead of chasing.
  - The 15s chart is "very forgiving". It lets you get into a move you missed on the 1m/5m/15m, or cut stop size (handles or pips). It is **not** a shortcut. If you can't read 1m/5m/15m price, you'll get chopped up on 15s.
  - **Limit orders:** don't demand perfection. Place the limit **just above** the level (for longs), e.g. just above a wick's midpoint, not at the exact extreme. That's the "low-hanging fruit" where volume is. Expect occasional non-fills even when price touches or slightly exceeds your price: "don't be a dick for a tick". Constant extreme fills invite B-book broker slippage and requotes.
  - **Adding:** when the run is already "long in the tooth", an add-on partial can't be larger than one contract. Pyramiding is hard to teach. Don't start yet; be consistent with small size first.
  - Tighter stops via 15s are for later, once you're managing real risk.
- **Example:** Aug 6 rally leg on 15s: the 1m immediate rebalance shows up as price returning to rebalance the "quick sudden run from this close to that close". Then relative equal highs, an FVG, price trading outside it, and back in with a 1m immediate rebalance to a deeper discount. That's the first return after taking buy side and a 15s long or add-on. Later, a down-close candle inside an FVG that returned into an old inefficiency is another buy, with the limit just above the wick's midpoint.
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:39](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=1959) why 15s; unfilled limits. [0:37:28](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=2248) re-entry and stop reduction, not a golden ticket. [2:38:13](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=9493) PDCT defined. [2:48:36](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=10116) 15s long, add of at most one contract, limit just above the level. [2:51:47](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=10307) down-close-candle-in-FVG buy.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Algorithmic delivery vs. buying/selling pressure
body:
- **Kind:** definition (worldview)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price is scripted by time and price, not buying and selling pressure. The algorithm refers to salient prior price points at given times.
  - HFT-style algos don't buy while price expands up. They wait for price to reach the inefficiency threshold, then fire long entries on the **first downtick** after it's met.
  - Time & sales show few contracts move price. One contract books a price.
  - "Volume precedes price" really means volume is larger where stops are taken (below lows, sell stops). Further beyond a level, volume thins, which is why gaps appear as price presses higher.
  - Limit-up analogy: one contract can open a market limit up.
- **Timestamps:** [2:42:14](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=9734) the algorithm refers to salient points. [2:43:49](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=9829) first downtick after the inefficiency. [2:44:37](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=9877) volume precedes price, reinterpreted. [2:47:00](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=10020) limit-up analogy.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: What an entry model is
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** An entry model is the **catalyst** that puts you in the trade given your directional expectation, "the thing you're betting on panning out". Relative to the stop, you need a multiple **greater than one** of what you risk. You do *not* need 2:1, 3:1, 4:1 or 5:1, just reasonable, anticipatable fluctuations. Through journaling, your eye will gravitate to one entry model (breakers, FVGs, iFVGs, institutional order flow entry drills, mitigation blocks, and so on). He lets you pick what resonates rather than forcing one PD array.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:34](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=994) let your personal interest choose. [2:02:59](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=7379) your eye resonates with one model. [2:03:46](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=7426) entry model = catalyst, R greater than 1.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #2   August 6, 2024
head: Aug 6, 2024 AM session walkthrough
body:
- **Kind:** example only (no prices are read out; index futures, measured in "handles")
- **Step by step (1m unless noted):**
  1. Pre-7:00: London (2–5 AM) sold off. Its lows are ignored for relative equal lows purposes but define the London range.
  2. After 7:00: relative equal highs form (right one slightly lower) and are run. Smooth made jagged; buy-side engaged.
  3. The BISI in the leg that ran them (the first FVG prior to the stop run, in the bearish breaker's range) fails and becomes an iFVG. Price returns, respects CE, and breaks down. The drop's SIBI in the stop-hunt leg is the "sweet spot" (OTE / 2022 model).
  4. Around 8:00, relative equal lows form while price rallies against the bearish bias. Price bumps back into an old SIBI (taking shorts' stops), works its CE, breaks lower. Every SIBI is extended right and the BISIs are ignored.
  5. Protracted consolidation with relative equal highs and lows. A run up into SIBIs "falls out of bed", then a deeper protraction toward the London low. One side is taken, then the other.
  6. Price is back inside a twice-used SIBI: low probability, morning done. Hourly Fib SDs cluster near the low reached, which fell just short of the deepest projection.
  7. Later: a disruption at the lows (jagged) points to buy side. Immediate rebalance, then an order block, then a 40+ handle expansion to the initial 7:00 high (high of day). Done for the day.
- **Timestamps:** [0:58:25](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=3505), [1:20:51](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=4851), [1:44:19](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=6259), [2:36:31](https://youtu.be/pkI4AgC4OPI?t=9391)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: New Day Opening Gap (NDOG)  (aliases: new day opening gap, NDOG; label "ND" + date)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Applies to the **index futures** in this teaching. Every day except Friday, the market stops at **5:00 PM ET**, pauses for one hour and reopens at **6:00 PM ET**.
  - On a **1-minute chart**, take the close of the **4:59 PM candle** (the last print before the stop) and the **opening price of the first 6:00 PM 1m candle**. The space between those two prices is the NDOG. You do not need live data for this, and the effect on price lasts for weeks.
  - **Three levels:** the gap high (whichever is higher of the 5 PM close and the 6 PM open), the gap low (whichever is lower), and **consequent encroachment (CE)**, the midpoint. He also adds the **0.25 and 0.75 levels** with a Fib, which splits the gap into equal quarters ("quadrants").
  - Draw each level with a **horizontal ray** that extends right forever. Put the label in the middle/right and **always include the date**, because the date tells you how old (and how important) the level is.
  - **Dating convention:** a gap that forms Tuesday evening at 6 PM is **Wednesday's** NDOG, because it is the reference for Wednesday's trading.
  - **Life cycle: 5 trading days** (not calendar days). If there is a holiday, skip it and add a day. Example: a gap formed Tuesday for Wednesday is valid Wed (day 1), Thu (2), Fri (3), Mon (4), Tue (5), so it is good "until Wednesday next week". Keep **five** NDOGs on the chart. This is a starting rule, not a hard cutoff: he still uses gaps that are **9 months old** when they fit the narrative.
  - Filling the gap does **not** make it stale. He contrasts this with retail "gap fill, done" thinking and with supply/demand "fresh zone" logic. Price keeps coming back to these levels.
  - Price is especially sensitive to an NDOG it has **touched only once**. It is still "hot" and price will very likely be drawn back to it ("just a guarantee", one of the very few guarantees in trading, he says).
- **How to identify:** 1m chart → 4:59 PM close vs. 6:00 PM first open → mark high, low, CE (and quarters) → label with date → keep the last 5.
- **How to use:**
  - It is the **underlying narrative / draw on liquidity** behind the intraday REH/REL objectives. An intraday target is "linked to" an NDOG and/or NWOG.
  - **Clustering filter:** look only at the last 5. If most of them sit above the current price (maybe one at or below), expect price to gravitate up, and the reverse when they cluster below. If you are anticipating a short but the gaps cluster above, give the first 30 minutes after 7:00/8:00/9:00 a chance to spike up into them in a thin price run. Then wait for a market structure shift or breaker and/or an **inversion FVG** before shorting.
  - Clustering is a **filter, not a hard rule**. A cluster below doesn't mean "short only". If he wants a long, he first waits to see whether they drop price toward the gaps.
  - The trade does not need to reach the NDOG that day to be profitable. If it hadn't traded there during the day, he would have looked for it to happen in **London that night**.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m. On Tue Aug 6, the 5 PM close was **above** the 6 PM open, so it was a **down gap**. That made it Wednesday Aug 7's NDOG. After the open, price traded up into the gap and stopped exactly at a quadrant level, **18,049.50** (caption "18, 04950"), which he calls perfect. It hovered around the **upper quadrant**, dropped to CE, then to the **lower quadrant**, and took a low there. It did not touch the actual gap low before rallying away. At 7:00, 8:00 and 9:00, price was far above the gap. In the afternoon (during the stream), price fell back and closed into it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:21](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1041) definition starts · [0:18:58](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1138) the 4:59 close and 6:00 first print · [0:27:53](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1673) dated for the next day, 5 trading days · [0:31:52](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1912) quarters, stop at 18,049.50
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He first introduced NDOGs in Twitter Spaces. He says "it's 2024" and that he is now showing his hand: the journal routine, the clustering filter, the 150-handle proximity rule and "touched once = hot". If the exchange ever went to 24-hour trading and the NDOG disappeared, he says you would still have NWOGs and REH/REL.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG)  (aliases: new week opening gap, NWOG; label "NW" + date)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule
- **What ICT says:** The NWOG is the range between **Friday's 5:00 PM close** and **Sunday's 6:00 PM open**. Mark it the same way as the NDOG (high, low, CE) but label it NW. **Life cycle: 5 weeks**, so keep five of them. Like NDOGs, they work 6–9 months later because they are real places where the market didn't trade efficiently. There is only one NWOG per week against five NDOGs. **For a swing trade the NWOG has more impact**, because the market makers have had the whole weekend to digest information before setting that opening price.
- **How to identify:** 1m chart, Fri 4:59 PM close vs. Sun 6:00 PM first print.
- **How to use:** It is the higher-tier "black hole" draw. Use it together with NDOG clusters for the directional filter and as targets for holding longer.
- **Example in this video:** none specific. He points to price dipping into a gap and calls that the first and second time it passed into it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:28:41](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1721) definition and 5-week cycle · [0:45:19](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=2719) NWOG vs NDOG for swing trades
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Keep the full history on a separate TradingView layout if you want to track older gaps. You must also keep count of how many times each has been referred to.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Opening-gap housekeeping (journal + layouts)
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:** He keeps a **spiral notebook** with one column per market (usually S&P, Nasdaq, sometimes the bond market). For every NDOG he writes the high, low, CE and the date/week it formed. He personally looks at any of them when price is **within 150 handles**. On TradingView, build separate **layouts**: one with only NWOGs and one with only NDOGs for your market. You pull them up at session start and keep your execution chart clean (he teaches as if from one laptop).
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:16](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1576) journal, 150 handles · [0:29:30](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1770) layouts

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE) vs. Equilibrium; gap quadrants  (aliases: midpoint, "consequent encroachment")
body:
- **Kind:** definition + refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - **CE is the midpoint of any gap or inefficiency.** It is not called equilibrium. **Equilibrium** belongs to a *range* that has been delivered up and down (a trading range). A gap is not a range: no trades printed between the 5 PM stop and the 6 PM restart.
  - Grade the gap with 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 to get equal quarters. Price respects the upper and lower quadrants to the tick.
  - **SIBI (down-close FVG):** the best shorts form in the **lower half**, and you want the upper half left open. **BISI (up-close FVG):** the best longs fill in the **upper half**, leaving the lower half open. When price can't fill that half and runs, it is a **breakaway gap**. That tells you the algorithm will move quickly, so anticipate large range expansion.
- **How to use:** CE serves as an entry level and as a **strength/weakness gauge** (see the order block concept below).
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:04](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1864) CE vs equilibrium · [0:33:25](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=2005) CE rules for SIBI/BISI, breakaway gap

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Sell-side / buy-side delivery vs. liquidity; inefficiency vs. BPR  (aliases: one-sided delivery, "liquidity void" critique)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - **Liquidity** means real resting orders, the buy stops above highs and sell stops below lows. He calls it the "lifeblood"/"heartbeat" of the market.
  - An **inefficiency** (FVG, gap) has had **one-sided delivery**. A down move is *sell-side delivery*, and what it lacks is *buy-side delivery*, and vice versa. So "sell-side delivery" and "sell-side liquidity" are not the same thing.
  - Chris Lori's "liquidity void" is a misnomer, ICT says: there was buying (or selling) in it, and what's missing is the opposite side of delivery.
  - Price merely trading back into an FVG does not balance it. It must trade there **and leave**, and then it becomes a **balanced price range**.
  - **Hierarchy of draws:** NDOG/NWOG and relative equal highs/lows rank above inefficiencies (FVGs). Inefficiencies are "subordinate and less important" because the algorithm places more weight on the former. Real opening gaps outrank everything because no trades took place there.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:10](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=1330) what the gap lacks (sell-side delivery) · [1:53:37](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6817) hierarchy of draws · [1:55:15](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6915) delivery vs liquidity · [1:57:39](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=7059) BPR and the Lori critique

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Engineering liquidity (predicting REH/REL before they form)  (aliases: engineered liquidity, design of liquidity)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Midnight NY is the start of the "true day". The algorithm refers back to midnight and everything after it for liquidity and inefficiencies, and beyond that to NDOG/NWOG.
  - Starting at **7:00 AM** (then 8:00, 9:00), look for relative equal highs/lows or "smooth" price that forms after the session changeover. In the **30 minutes after each top of hour**, anticipate a move in the opposing direction (this continues from Lecture 2).
  - Because a known NDOG/NWOG draw gives you a "magnetized reference point", you can predict **where relative equal highs/lows will be built before they form**. That, he says, is exactly what engineering liquidity means.
  - Example rule: with an NDOG below and REH forming after 7:00, **never short right away** on the first drop. Let price run those highs first (a **Judas swing**), and don't chase.
- **How to identify / REH-REL quality filter:** Two swings close together, and the right-hand swing must sit inside the left one. For relative equal **lows**, the right low has to be **higher** than the previous low. Then it is a high-probability REL to draw to. The NDOG below acts as "rocket fuel" on top of that.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 7 2024. In the 7:00 and 8:00 hours, price built REH and REL. The NDOG sat far south, so he expected the highs to run first. Price dropped, and retail chased it short. After 9:00, it rallied and pumped above the highs (one, two, three relative equal highs), made another REH, then broke down. He calls that a Judas swing into 9:00 that chops traders up all morning.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:57](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=897) NDOG as underlying narrative; 7/8/9 intervals · [0:50:57](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=3057) predict REH/REL before they form · [0:52:31](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=3151) don't chase; Judas swing · [1:28:40](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=5320) REL right-side rule
- **Nuance:** Once the real draw is lower, the REH above can simply be left alone ("they can stay in play"). He doesn't need them taken before shorting the afternoon.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Afternoon session protocol on no-news mornings (bond auction setup)  (aliases: PM session, 1:00 bond auction)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / narrative filter
- **What ICT says:**
  - Check the economic calendar (ForexFactory, Econoday). When the **morning has no medium- or high-impact news**, the morning tends to be lackluster and rangy: false breakouts, pulls back into the previous day's range, or reverses an attempt higher. It "demands a lot more experience" because you get caught offside.
  - Morning drivers usually come at **8:30 ET**, sometimes 10:00, with crude oil inventories at 10:30. Today had none, which is why he booked his eye appointment for the morning.
  - **Rule (write it down):** no medium/high-impact data in the morning → trade the afternoon, because the cleaner price action comes after New York lunch.
  - On such a day, a **bond auction at 1:00 PM ET** (a medium-impact driver, not very volatile) is the afternoon catalyst. He says he has never taught this before. **Condition:** it only counts as this clean setup when there is **no morning news**. With morning drivers, it doesn't hold.
  - Afternoon timing: he wants to be at the charts by **1:30 PM**. Moves can start a bit before 1:30, which is fine. The **1:30–2:30** window usually holds a "sweet spot". If nothing forms 1:30–2:00, use the **2:00–3:00 Silver Bullet**. If that is missed or sideways, use the **3:00 hour to the close**.
  - If you miss the move, use Lecture 2's technique: a **sub-1-minute chart** to get in sync with a run already unfolding on the 1m/5m.
- **How to use:** Set the narrative before 1:00. The draw is below (SSL plus NDOG), so you are looking to short into the auction release and treat the release as fuel for the run.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:29](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=269) no-news mornings are rangy · [1:09:22](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=4162) bond-auction condition · [1:19:49](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=4789) rule: trade the afternoon, 1:30–2:30 · [1:26:15](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=5175) 1:30, 2:00 Silver Bullet, 3:00 hour
- **Nuance:** Caleb's own focus is the **7:00–11:00 AM NY** window: start at 7 or 8, or just wait for the 9:30 bell and use **9:00–11:00**. The afternoon rules are given "for completeness". He says he will also show London later.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Trading ahead of a news release (pre-1:00 logic)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:** People ask how he knows direction before news. His answer: if price has already rounded over, left an FVG whose **candle bodies respect it**, and started **displacing lower** before the release, the likelihood is that it will explore below the nearby lows, because that's where liquidity is. Buying and selling after the release does not cause the move. The market is already running before the number comes out.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m. At **12:42 ET**, price trades up and rolls over, leaving an FVG ("one of the 81 PD arrays") with bodies respecting it, then displaces lower going into the 1:00 auction. He lists the draws below:
  - (1) a short-term low, the day-session low since 7:00, with minor SSL
  - (2) the London session low, a relative equal low that passes the right-side-higher rule
  - (3) the NDOG further down as the "black hole"
- **Timestamps:** [1:34:20](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=5660) 12:42 FVG roll-over · [1:36:44](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=5804) the logic before news · [1:39:12](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=5952) three draws below

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Bearish order block from an FVG that failed to reach CE (strength/weakness signature)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - When a retracement runs up into a SIBI and **can't even touch its CE** (it comes close and falls short), that is an "algorithmic signature" of weakness. He then treats that up candle as a **bearish order block**. Once the candle closes, he needs price to move away and come back up into the **bottom of that candle**, and he sells there.
  - **Conditional rule:** if the retrace *had* touched the CE, he would not take the trade. He would wait for another attempt a little above CE and short in the upper part of the gap.
  - PD arrays are fixed levels to enter and exit on, but he also uses them to **measure strength and weakness**.
  - **Two stacked SIBIs:** expect price might go up into the higher one. If it fails at the **lower one's CE** and a news driver is coming, he is happy to be short. If it had touched the lower one's CE, he would expect a run into the higher gap, and the stop would then have to go above that (higher) gap's CE. Which gap he means is slightly unclear in the caption.
- **How to identify:** a SIBI in a bearish narrative → a retrace whose wick stays below CE → treat that candle as a bearish OB → the next candle trades up into its body/low without passing CE or the candle high → enter short.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Aug 7, shortly before 1:00 PM. A candle runs into the SIBI, misses CE and closes. The market displaces below that bearish OB. The next candle opens, trades up, touches it, and he shorts. The candle low was **18,320.25** and his fill was **18,321.25** (6 contracts).
- **Timestamps:** [1:43:59](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6239) fails to touch CE · [1:44:47](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6287) bearish OB rule, what he'd do otherwise · [1:45:37](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6337) PD arrays as a strength gauge · [1:47:12](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6432) fill price, two FVGs

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Live/demo trade recap: NQ 1m, Aug 7 2024 bond-auction short  (example only)
body:
- **Kind:** example (demo account, shown to his youngest son, not Caleb)
- **Sequence (diagrammable):**
  1. Narrative: the morning had no news, and the 1:00 PM bond auction was the driver. The NDOG was below, SSL sat at the day-session low and the London REL, and the morning REH were already engineered and run.
  2. 12:42: price rolls over, leaving an FVG and displacing lower.
  3. Price retraces into a SIBI, falls short of CE, and that candle becomes a bearish OB. He shorts **6 contracts at 18,321.25**.
  4. A big down-close candle is followed by an **immediate rebalance** (price trades back up into it). He adds **4 contracts at 18,291.25** (a pyramid). There is some heat on the add, but because the 6 larger contracts are at the better price, the combined position stays about **$1,700** in profit.
  5. The retrace goes up to an FVG level but **does not touch its CE** before the swing high. He **moves the stop to the first entry minus 2 ticks** and "just relaxes".
  6. **1:00 PM:** the auction candle pumps up (an up-close 1m candle) and then dumps. A small SIBI forms, and there is a slight **mohawk** overshoot of its boundary that doesn't take the high. The next retrace stops right at the FVG's edge: candle high **18,283.75** vs. FVG candle low **18,283.50**.
  7. After that retracement he points out a **2022 model** and an **OTE** on the chart.
  8. Price trades through the London lows. His **limit order just below the London low** fills. He takes off all **10 contracts** at about 18,2xx (caption "18,23…", unclear). That is **over 100 handles** on the 6-contract portion.
  9. Later in the session, price continues down and closes into the NDOG.
- **Lesson he draws:** 1-minute traders saw the 1:00 pump as a failure swing or iFVG going for the REH. They "lost the plot", because the draw was the London lows and the NDOG.
- **Timestamps:** [1:46:24](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6384) executions shown · [1:50:23](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6623) six-and-four, heat explained · [1:51:12](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6672) stop to entry minus 2 ticks; 1:00 pump and dump · [1:59:17](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=7157) fills, over 100 handles

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Immediate rebalance & Mohawk  (example only / refinement)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (both referenced from Lecture 2)
- **What ICT says:** **Immediate rebalance:** after a big displacement candle, price trades right back up into it and then continues. He used it as the add-on area here. **Mohawk:** price overshoots an FVG boundary by a little ("coloring outside the lines"). It doesn't change the read as long as the swing high isn't taken. In a bearish narrative, judge how price treats **every SIBI** on the way down.
- **Timestamps:** [1:49:36](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6576) immediate rebalance · [1:52:01](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6721) mohawk, how price treats each SIBI

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Six-and-four position building / pyramiding  (aliases: "my model six and four")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (trade management)
- **What ICT says:** He puts the larger piece (**6 contracts**) on at the best price and adds a smaller piece (**4 contracts**) later. The bigger, better-priced first entry absorbs heat on the add, so a retrace above the second entry can't put the whole position underwater. Building larger positions this way comes from years of experience, he says. How much you can take out of a run depends on how high in its range (premium vs equilibrium) you get in.
- **Timestamps:** [1:50:23](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6623) · [2:17:30](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=8250) "how much you can yield" depends on where in the range you enter

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Holding trades longer / price-run sizes  (aliases: scout trade, intermediate-term run)
body:
- **Kind:** rule + process
- **What ICT says:**
  - **Prerequisite:** you must first be able to consistently get **5 handles in ES or 10 handles in NQ**. Holding longer does not fix an inability to do that.
  - **NQ price-run grades:** under **50 handles** is a "scout" (small intraday). **50+** is an intermediate-term run (what he means by swinging intraday volatility). **100+** is a larger swing. He has no grades beyond that. Most of his content aims for roughly 20 pips / 25 handles / 50 handles.
  - **Rule of excess range:** to take 10 handles, the setup must offer **15–20**. To hold longer, there must be a draw outside your normal range, such as an NDOG/NWOG, that justifies more than a 1m chart's range.
  - **Graduation drill:** aim the trade at the near target (the short-term low or REL), take a partial or close there, then **tape-read the rest**. Screenshot and note every impulse or doubt ("I have doubts it drops here") and review it afterwards. This exposure desensitizes you to needing to be right. Use demo or tape-reading for the extended part until you trust it.
  - Holding for longer runs increases the chance of being stopped out prematurely, because early on every retracement feels like the bottom. Watching price gravitate to NDOG/NWOG over weeks and months is what builds that patience. You can't fast-track it.
- **Timestamps:** [1:10:58](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=4258) 5 ES / 10 NQ prerequisite · [1:11:47](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=4307) 50/100-handle grades · [1:25:26](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=5126) 15–20 to get 10 · [1:40:48](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=6048) partial + tape-read the rest + journal doubts

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Algorithmic reference points (why gaps repeat)  (IPDA framing)
body:
- **Kind:** definition (narrative)
- **What ICT says:** The algorithm works like a recipe. It must refer back to old information: the **date, day of week, week of month, month, quarter, the price, and the time** it was trading there. Levels hold because of these time-and-price references, not because buyers or sellers ran out or because of how many times a level was hit. This is why gaps that filled weeks ago still matter.
- **Timestamps:** [0:49:17](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=2957) why would it care about an old gap · [1:06:57](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=4017) recipe and reference points

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: 81 PD arrays; iFVG mention
body:
- **Kind:** definition (claim)
- **What ICT says:** He has **81** specific PD arrays (not 84), and each one works as an entry, partial and take-profit mechanism. Counting inversions would technically double that. You need **only one**, plus the patience to wait for it inside a narrative. All of them appear every day on some timeframe. An **inversion FVG** is distinct from an FVG and is "one of the bangers". If you wait patiently for it, it gives excellent runners. No trend analysis, moving averages or daily chart were used today. He used only time of day, time and price, liquidity, and the calendar narrative.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:59](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=659) 81 PD arrays · [0:42:57](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=2577) iFVG as a "banger" · [1:17:23](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=4643) you only need one · [1:18:12](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=4692) no trend analysis or daily chart

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #3   August 7, 2024
head: Street money vs. smart money (sentiment)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (context)
- **What ICT says:** "Street money" means people who openly share their ideas online, or uninformed people suddenly interested in a market. His example is his wife asking about Bitcoin near $20k, after which he called the top. When the social-media herd is loudly bearish ("crash") against what these principles show, he leans the other way, because the odds favor the opposite side.
- **Timestamps:** [1:00:36](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=3636) · [1:01:25](https://youtu.be/ZkLc4-adodg?t=3685)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: New Day Opening Gap (NDOG) — derivation & labeling  (aliases: new day opening gap, NDOG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The NDOG for a trading day is formed the evening before: the gap between the 5:00 PM ET close (start of the one-hour break) and the 6:00 PM ET open. E.g. Tuesday's NDOG is created Monday at 6 PM; Wednesday's NDOG is created Tuesday at 6 PM.
  - If the 6 PM open is above the 5 PM close it is an up gap: the 6 PM open is the NDOG high and the 5 PM close is the low (and vice versa for a gap down).
  - Put a Fibonacci on the gap's high and low; the 0.5 level is the consequent encroachment (CE / midpoint).
  - Add 0.25 and 0.75 to your Fib settings to get the quadrant levels.
  - Quadrants are only worth plotting when the range is large. If the NDOG is small (he gives "10 or 15 handles, something less than 20 handles" on NQ) just eyeball the midpoint — the difference between entry and stop is too small to matter.
  - Example of a "significant" range: ~66 handles (caption reads "18,99 to 18,33"; exact prices unclear) — he would plot quadrants.
- **How to identify:** 5 PM ET close vs 6 PM ET open of the prior evening.
- **How to use:** reference levels (high, low, CE, quadrants) for where price gravitates, where bodies stop, where wicks overshoot. See "Opening-gap clustering bias" below.
- **Example in this video:** Before 8:30 on Aug 8, NQ was trading just below Wednesday's NDOG low and above today's (Thursday's) NDOG high — "in between", i.e. no-man's land.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:27](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=507) — price sitting between Wednesday's NDOG low and today's NDOG high; [0:13:17](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=797) — 5 PM close / 6 PM open derivation; [0:14:06](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=846) — CE via Fib, quadrants only for ranges > ~20 handles; [0:15:40](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=940) — add 0.25/0.75 to Fib settings.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Continues Lecture #3 (Aug 7) teaching — he tells viewers to go back and watch that one.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG) — labeling  (aliases: new week opening gap, NWOG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Measure from Friday's close to Sunday's 6 PM ET open; 50% = CE. For a significant NWOG, also plot the quadrants. To keep the chart clean, he measures with a Fib, then replaces it with a single horizontal line typed at the exact price (e.g. NWOG CE ~18,451.75 — caption also says "441.75", unclear) and removes the Fib.
- **How to identify:** Friday close vs Sunday 6 PM open.
- **How to use:** Same as NDOG — one of the clustered reference points that tells you where price will reach.
- **Example in this video:** Early in the week price spiked into the NWOG with wicks ("wicks do the damage"), hit the bottom of the NWOG and accelerated lower into Tuesday's NDOG CE, then Wednesday's NDOG with bodies respecting it, then CE again. On Aug 8 the NWOG was far above price — "it's going to take a real move to get up there".
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:30](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=990) — NWOG measured from Friday close to Sunday open, quadrants; [0:18:54](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=1134) — review of price respecting NWOG / NDOG levels earlier in the week.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Keep the **last five NDOGs** and the **last five NWOGs** on your reference layout.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Opening-gap clustering bias (which side will price press into at 8:30)  (aliases: stacking / clustering of new day opening gaps)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - At 8:00 ET look for relative equal highs and relative equal lows into 8:30.
  - At 8:30 (with or without news) ask: where is the stacking/clustering of the NDOGs and the NWOG — above or below the current price? Price is most likely to press into the side that has the inefficiencies, **even if they have already been traded to / "filled"**.
  - Gaps are not "used up" once touched — "the algorithm ... calls back to these points of reference based on time and price." They have a "life cycle" of sensitivity.
  - He estimates the direction is right "80% or higher" initially (explicitly "not 100%").
  - Retail breakout traders will try to buy above / sell below the nearby highs/lows — you wait, because between two gaps neither direction is more likely until the 8:30 move.
- **How to identify:** (1) Price location just before 8:30; (2) count NDOGs/NWOG above vs below; (3) context: has price already dropped into a deep discount of the recent range? (4) where have the profitable positions been (the side that has been winning recently is the side that will be squeezed).
- **How to use:** Defines the draw for the 8:30 run and subsequent scalps. If price had dropped into a clean FVG just before 8:30 (e.g. at 8:25), you could have bought into the news anticipating the run; without such a PD array, don't gamble — wait and drop to a 15-second chart to trade the inefficiencies/first order block that support the idea.
- **Example in this video:** Aug 8, NQ: just before 8:30 price was below Wednesday's NDOG and above Thursday's NDOG; Tuesday's NDOG, Wednesday's NDOG and the NWOG all sat above. Price had already dropped into a deep discount of the range from the low up to Wednesday's high, taken relative equal lows inside a BISI, and bounced off the upper quadrant of that BISI. At 8:30 it rallied up into Wednesday's NDOG low, CE, and high, then Tuesday's NDOG — as forecast the day before.
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:33](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=1233) — clustering is above, so bias is up; [0:26:23](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=1583) — 8:00 relative equal highs/lows, 8:30 clustering; [0:27:10](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=1630) — gaps already traded through still matter; [0:33:38](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=2018) — same signature without news, ~80%+.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Direct application of Lecture #3. Contrasts with the "gap is filled, forget it" view of everyone else in the industry.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: 8:30 spooling / algorithmic repricing  (aliases: spooling, the market spools, buy program / sell program)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - At 8:30 ET the algorithm starts "spooling" (running) regardless of news; he never looks at the actual report numbers (CPI, PMI, NFP) — "it's all baked in."
  - Medium/high-impact news "loosens it up" so price can reach further outside the normal band of volatility; the magnitude and speed are bigger. No news → price still moves toward the same levels, just less energetically.
  - Spooling analogy: like fishing line shooting off a reel when cast. When the algorithm enters a buy program it spools higher; a sell program, lower.
  - The big 8:30 run is repricing, not buying pressure — check time & sales / volume: few contracts traded during the run. Historical analogy: open-outcry floor traders "pairing orders" (one contract needed to book a price) to stair-step price.
  - Other scheduled times where price spools: 8:30, 10:00, sometimes 9:45, 10:30 (crude oil inventories), plus macros.
- **How to identify:** Economic calendar (Forex Factory is cleaner; he prefers Econoday — more information, free). The calendar is your "TV guide" for when to watch.
- **How to use:** The 8:30 initial run is essentially untradeable unless already positioned before it; the draw is determined by where price is relative to the gap clusters right before the release.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15-second chart at 8:30: from 17,986.75 to roughly 18,08x (caption unclear) — "100 handles in just like 15 seconds". On the 1-second chart, the first one-second candle went from 17,986.75 to ~18,037.75 (caption unclear).
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:16](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=556) — algorithm spools at 8:30 even without news; [0:36:13](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=2173) — 15-sec chart ~100 handles in 15 seconds; [1:19:56](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4796) — fishing reel analogy, buy/sell programs; [1:56:04](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=6964) — 1-second chart of the 8:30 candle.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Warns funded-account traders using 5–15 contracts on a ~$3,000 max loss that gambling these runs guarantees blowing out.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Macros (algorithmic time windows)  (aliases: macro)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (restated)
- **What ICT says:** A macro is the last 10 minutes before the top of the hour and the first 10 minutes after the top of the hour (i.e. xx:50–xx:10). The market spools there too, running for liquidity or rushing into an inefficiency. He prefers to trade a bullish MSS setup inside a macro.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:04](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=1384) — trade inside a macro; [1:21:32](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4892) — macros spool like news times.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Silver Bullet (10:00 window) as fallback  (aliases: 10 o'clock Silver Bullet)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / filter
- **What ICT says:** If price expands strongly up into the NWOG before the 9:30 open, he would stand aside and wait for the 10:00 Silver Bullet, and only trade around that premise. Late in the stream he expected a possible Silver Bullet at/into 10:00 because price was "heavy".
- **Example in this video:** At ~10:00 price traded down into the area he pointed to, then ran up for the relative equal highs — he calls it "a pretty good read on a 15-second chart". His expectation (as "if I was making the market") was a drop to upset the relative equal lows/area below, then a run above the relative equal highs, possibly into the afternoon.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Breaker with an FVG inside (and the potential inversion FVG)  (aliases: breaker, bearish breaker, inversion fair value gap)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** A (bearish) breaker = high, low, then a higher high that blows out the buy-side liquidity. If there is a fair value gap inside the breaker's leg, focus on that FVG rather than only the down-close candles that formed the last turn. That FVG becomes a potential inversion FVG — highlight it and extend it to the right as a PD array price may draw up to.
- **How to identify:** High → low → higher high (BSL run) → FVG within that structure.
- **How to use:** Upside target/draw; area where price can engage/reverse.
- **Example in this video:** Above the FVG he chose (which sat above equilibrium of the range), there was an FVG inside a breaker; he flagged it as the next upside target if price went higher. Later, price did reach it ("there's that Gap I told you about, high, low, higher high").
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:02](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=1922) — breaker + FVG rule; [1:21:32](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4892) — inversion FVG above breaker as upside target; [2:06:34](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=7594) — reached.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He marks FVGs he views as inversions in orange. A BISI that price has displaced back down through is NOT a buy when retested — "that's not a buy" — just because it was originally a bullish gap.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Fibonacci = equilibrium only; premium/discount of the most recent range  (aliases: equilibrium, 50%, premium, discount)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** His only use of the Fibonacci is to find the midpoint — that tells him overbought (premium) vs oversold (discount); no indicator needed, and divergence on any indicator is "useless". Measure the most recent large directional range (here the high down to the low right at 8:30). Ask who is holding profit — in a protracted down move it's the shorts, so the pain will go to the shorts. At or below 50% = discount; at or above 50% = premium.
- **How to use:** Choose the FVG target that is above equilibrium (for a bullish draw) as the objective.
- **Example in this video:** He measured the high (Wednesday area) to the low before 8:30; price at 8:30 was in deep discount; the FVG he chose as target sat above equilibrium and inside the breaker.
- **Timestamps:** [1:15:55](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4555) — Fib only for midpoint; [1:16:43](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4603) — who is profitable in the recent range; [1:17:30](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4650) — premium/discount.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Fair Value Gap — definition, bodies vs wicks, CE  (aliases: SIBI, BISI, sell-side imbalance buy-side inefficiency, buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - FVG = the space between candle 1's low and candle 3's high (bearish case) on a single pass of price; with sell-side delivery the inefficiency is on the buy side (SIBI). It remains an inefficiency until price trades back into it.
  - "Consequent encroachment" = the midpoint; it's "consequential" that price encroaches into it when it returns.
  - Bodies respect the levels; "the wicks do the damage".
  - The extreme of how far a wick may go against you: look left — a volume imbalance or short-term high nearby; expect at most a tick or so beyond it.
- **How to use:** Bearish example: price returns into a SIBI, wicks up into a nearby volume imbalance (one tick above), fails to reach CE, next candle dives → that's your "institutional order flow entry drill" (sell). Stop above the FVG/wick extreme. Partial at the next level (e.g. Tuesday's NDOG low). If the gap is left open (not refilled) it is a breakaway gap; price likely stays heavy and could offer 15–20+ handles.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15-sec chart, after the run up to the FVG CE target (~…250): price couldn't hold at CE (resistance), broke below a low = market structure shift, retraced up into a short-term premium SIBI with bodies respecting it and wicks reaching a small volume imbalance, then traded down to the low of Tuesday's NDOG.
- **Timestamps:** [1:15:06](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4506) — FVG definition; [1:27:12](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=5232) — CE as resistance, MSS, retrace to short-term premium; [1:31:15](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=5475) — CE meaning, bodies; [1:32:03](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=5523) — wick extreme, entry drill, breakaway gap, partial.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Reclaimed fair value gap  (aliases: reclaimed FVG)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** If you miss the first move away from an FVG, you can trade it when price returns into it again — the market is "offering that again", reclaiming the FVG. A small volume imbalance next to/inside the FVG tells you how far the wick can go. If bodies stay inside the FVG and the wick only reaches the volume imbalance, the setup is still viable.
- **Timestamps:** [1:29:36](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=5376) — takeaway on FVG + volume imbalance + reclaimed FVG; [1:30:26](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=5426) — bodies staying inside the FVG.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Volume imbalance & overlapping bodies as PD arrays on the 15-second chart  (aliases: volume imbalance, "one of the PD arrays I supposedly don't have")
body:
- **Kind:** example / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Where two consecutive candle bodies overlap/agree (top of one, low of the next), that level is a PD array. After the 8:30 run, a volume imbalance inside a BISI should hold: price should form support or be unable to trade to the BISI midpoint — or if it does, it must repel immediately. Every little down-close candle must then support price (acting as a bullish order block) until price takes out the next level.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15-sec chart after 8:30: price pulled back to Wednesday's NDOG CE; the open of one candle and the low of the next matched exactly (caption "18,81.5", unclear), then a rally leaving a BISI with a small volume imbalance; price traded only to "some random quadrant level", left the volume imbalance open, rallied to the high of Tuesday's NDOG, then pulled back into down-close candles just outside Tuesday's NDOG low. He said if that fails below the candle's low, stand aside until the 9:30 open.
- **Timestamps:** [0:38:37](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=2317) — overlapping bodies PD array; [0:39:28](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=2368) — volume imbalance inside BISI, must hold; [0:40:19](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=2419) — down-close candles must support; stand aside if it fails.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Order block + volume imbalance + NDOG confluence entry (hypothetical long)  (aliases: bullish order block, rejection block)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (example)
- **What ICT says:** On a 15-second chart you can use order blocks, small FVGs and volume imbalances as entries as long as the direction is still in play. Any convergence of an NDOG high/low/CE with a down-close candle while bullish → use it as the catalyst to study whether price runs to your objective.
- **How to use:**
  - Entry: the opening price of the order block (down-close candle) / the volume imbalance inside it ("worst case" fill).
  - Stop: at the rejection block — the close of that candle; he expected at most a one-tick wick below because the bodies had already filled the volume imbalance. This is the logic behind his tight stops.
  - Target: CE of the FVG above equilibrium.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15-sec, after ~9:00 ET: price came down, touched the top of Tuesday's NDOG high (two PD arrays — volume imbalance + NDOG high — inside a down-close order block). Hypothetical entry ~…173, target CE ~…250, high reached ~…252 → roughly 70–80 handles.
- **Timestamps:** [1:03:04](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=3784) — volume imbalance + Tuesday NDOG high inside order block; [1:08:37](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4117) — entry and stop logic (rejection block); [1:12:37](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4357) — 173 → 250/252; [1:23:59](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=5039) — convergence of NDOG level + down-close candle as catalyst.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Done after the "major damage" of 8:30 was over; price had already pressed one-sided, so he said he'd wait rather than chase a ~100-handle run. Don't read stalling as reversal/bearish divergence — it is drawing to inefficiencies.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Balanced Price Range (BPR)  (aliases: balanced price range, balanced price delivery)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:** When price has been offered both up and down through the same range (e.g. between one candle's low and another's high), it is balanced. Analogy: painting a wall with a roller — once an area is painted (balanced), you don't need to go deep into it again; price only returns to the edge. Use quadrants of the BPR to study reactions.
- **Example in this video:** 15-sec chart: a BPR formed from a low that was also Wednesday's NDOG CE up to a high; price later traded back to the up-close closing price/open and rallied. On the 1-second chart, price dropped into a BPR around Wednesday's NDOG CE and didn't go deeper.
- **Timestamps:** [1:23:10](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=4990) — BPR on 15-sec chart; [1:56:54](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=7014) — FVG at Wednesday NDOG CE and BPR; [1:57:50](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=7070) — paint-roller analogy, quadrants.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Support & resistance critique / old highs as targets  (aliases: liquidity above old highs)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / mindset
- **What ICT says:** Classical S/R (John Murphy etc.) shows what retail will try to do, which is useful only because it tells you where their stops are. If an old high is resistance, why does price go back to it? To go above it, because shorts' stops are there. Treat old highs/lows as levels "to be attacked". The real S/R is the opening gaps and inefficiencies (NDOG, NWOG, "Event Horizon" — things outside the candles "like dark pools").
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:43](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=1483) — S/R too myopic; [0:55:04](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=3304) — "we're trading old reference points ... to engage and liquidate traders"; [1:26:25](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=5185) — outside-the-candles levels; [2:01:48](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=7308) — attack the levels where orders sit.

head: Chart layouts: reference layout vs operating layout
body:

- **What ICT says:** Keep NDOG/NWOG levels on a separate reference layout (e.g. "new day opening gap template") outside your live trading layout; you don't need every level on the chart you operate on. Only bring the ones in close proximity onto the trading chart. Ideally have a second monitor; with one screen you'll juggle more.
