title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #4    August 8, 2024
head: Walking forward / observation drills (no demo)  (aliases: forward testing, tape reading)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / process
- **What ICT says:** Lectures 1–3 covered back-testing; this lecture and Friday's are about walking forward. In the initial stage you do not demo trade, pick entries, or set stops — you annotate the chart, watch, screenshot interesting moments and write notes with pen and paper (e.g. "screenshot at 8:57 on the 1m chart — concern was..."). Ask questions like: will it go into this FVG and propel up before 9:30? Will it first clean up relative equal lows? Log how fast price moves away from/to a level, what it looked like before a failure, how much it runs against you before delivering. Do this daily for weeks and months.
- **Timestamps:** [0:46:59](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=2819); [0:51:02](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=3062) — back-testing vs walking forward; [0:54:16](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=3256); [1:05:30](https://youtu.be/hdSscxZgE58?t=3930).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Turtle Soup (name origin & premise)  (aliases: turtle soup, fake out, fade)
body:
- **Kind:** definition (introduction only)
- **What ICT says:** The name comes from Linda Raschke & Larry Connors' book *Street Smarts* (he paid $175 for it in the mid-90s; the book most influenced his understanding of stop hunts). It snubs Richard Dennis's "Turtles" trend-following system, which bought breakouts of the 20-day high (sold below 20-day low) and had a very low strike rate but caught big trends. Turtle soup does the opposite: when price breaks above a 20-day high and fails back into the range, trade the reversal. ICT says he does not just use a 20-day high/low — "there's other things" — and promised to show those characteristics at the end, but the stream ended before he got to it. He calls turtle soup "my version of a reversal pattern": retail resistance gets pegged, then reverses toward the opposite side (discount, and vice versa).
- **How to identify (as applied in this video):** Price trades above a high and immediately goes right back in — "that's your turtle soup, it's a fake out" — as opposed to a strong "nitrous oxide" push through the level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:20](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=320) — announces turtle soup lecture; [0:06:09](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=369) — Richard Dennis, 20-day breakout; [0:07:49](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=469) — Raschke's turtle soup; [0:51:33](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3093) — failure back inside = turtle soup.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Full turtle soup characteristics not delivered in this lecture (stream cut short). He also teased talking about "wicks" — also not delivered.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: NDOG at the 6 PM restart (Asia application)  (aliases: new day opening gap, NDOG)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** At 5 PM ET indices take a one-hour break and reopen at 6 PM. NDOG = 5 PM close vs 6 PM open; 6 PM open above the close → it's the NDOG high; below → NDOG low. CE = midpoint. If the gap is over 20 handles, he always has the CE annotated; under 20, he eyeballs the CE and the quadrants.
- **Example in this video:** Thursday Aug 8 evening (for Friday's trading), NQ: the 4:59 PM candle closed at 18,558; 6 PM opened at ~18,550.25 (caption "18550 point2") — a gap lower of less than 10 handles, so just eyeball the middle.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:52](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=1192) — 6 PM derivation; [0:20:40](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=1240) — 20-handle rule; [0:31:22](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=1882) — 18,558 close / 18,550 open; [0:32:12](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=1932) — less than 10 handles, eyeball.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Do not trade as soon as the gap is noted — time must be the trigger first.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Initial buy-side / initial sell-side liquidity (the 6 PM / NDOG protocol)  (aliases: initial BSL, initial SSL, minor buy-side/sell-side liquidity pool, "initial range for building and engineering liquidity")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / entry model framework
- **What ICT says:**
  - After the 6 PM open, you want to see price do two things: (1) move away from the NDOG and take a short-term high (a minor buy-side liquidity pool), then (2) cross back over the NDOG and take a short-term low (a minor sell-side liquidity pool) — or the reverse order. Simply trading below the NDOG isn't enough; a short-term low must be taken.
  - Once both happen, that new high and new low after 6 PM are the **initial buy-side liquidity** and **initial sell-side liquidity** for the day — "the initial high and low that every trader that trades at that moment is going to refer to for where their stop loss is going to be." This visually represents how the algorithm "calibrates" and engineers liquidity.
  - Price "coloring outside the lines" of the NDOG (crossing through it) is expected — it is not a failure of the level.
  - If after 6 PM price "dilly-dallies" and doesn't bump above or below into 7 PM, Asia will likely be dull — don't trade; go to bed.
  - These initial levels later act as the real support/resistance the algorithm refers back to (overnight, London, and even the NY open).
- **How to identify:** Mark NDOG → raid of short-term high → cross back through NDOG → raid of short-term low (or mirror). Label initial BSL small at top-left of the line, initial SSL bottom-left; keep them muted. Then look left for larger pools of liquidity (e.g. relative equal highs).
- **How to use:** At the key time (7 PM for Asia), look for price to retrace into the NDOG while not going back to the opposite initial liquidity; then trade toward the initial liquidity on the other side (and the larger pools beyond it).
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Thursday Aug 8 evening: after the 6 PM open price ran above a short-term high (initial BSL), dropped back below the NDOG to take a short-term low (initial SSL), crossed back above the NDOG with displacement before 7 PM. On the 7:00 PM candle it dipped back and touched the NDOG high — did not go near the initial SSL. Relative equal highs and the initial BSL sat above.
- **Timestamps:** [0:36:16](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=2176) — the two things to see; [0:41:06](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=2466) — why they're labeled "initial"; [0:41:56](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=2516) — algorithm calibrating; stops reference; [0:43:32](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=2612) — dull Asia if no bump either side.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says the same "initial BSL/SSL" logic applies to the 9:30–10:00 opening range and (with the 12:00–12:30 range) to London.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Asian session window & the 7 PM trigger  (aliases: Asia killzone, Asian session)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Asia key times are 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM New York time — a small window. The algorithm "comes online" at 7 PM; buy/sell programs begin at or just after 7. Markets don't move until it's time — time first, price second. Asia is the least enticing session for him personally, but valid for people who work 9–5 in the US. Same concepts apply to forex. He does not trade crypto.
- **How to use:** Do the 6 PM protocol, then trade the 7 PM reaction; if it isn't there, don't push a button but still study it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:50](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=710) — Asia least enticing for him; [0:33:50](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=2030) — markets won't move until time; 7–9; [0:46:46](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=2806) — 7:00 candle retraces into NDOG; [0:49:09](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=2949) — 7–9 PM window.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Asia long — order block entry, stop, management (his live trade)  (aliases: bullish order block, breakaway gap, BISI)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (worked example)
- **What ICT says:**
  - After the displacement above the NDOG leaves a BISI, he does not want price to return into it — that makes it a **breakaway gap**. Then he wants momentum/speed through the relative equal highs and initial BSL ("nitrous oxide"), not a push above and right back in.
  - Order block entry: buy in the discount of the down-close candle — **below its body** (here its close), anywhere in the wick. People who just "buy down-close candles" only heard his first introduction to order blocks.
  - Stop: below the consequent encroachment of the NDOG.
  - Once price takes out the short-term high, move the stop to break-even, or at minimum to the top of the NDOG. Don't rush the stop.
  - Additional entries: a gap-up retraced on the next candle, and a classic volume-imbalance retrace.
  - "Every displacement does not have to see it trade back down into" — it's better when the BISI is never revisited; a return into it means the move is deferred, with uncomfortable waiting, drawdown or chop.
  - Two qualifiers that build confidence: (1) displacement ahead of 7 PM after working above and below the NDOG, keeping the initial SSL intact; (2) taking out the short-term high.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 8 ~7 PM ET: down-close candle closed at 18,560; his entry 18,559.75; price rallied through relative equal highs, consolidated around the level, then ran into the initial BSL and beyond. Exit 18,607.5 (limit order).
- **Timestamps:** [0:50:46](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3046) — breakaway gap, relative equal high run; [0:53:07](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3187) — buy below the order block body; [0:53:57](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3237) — entry 59.75, stop below NDOG CE; [0:55:33](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3333) — break-even / top of NDOG; displacement shouldn't be revisited.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Measured-move targeting with standard deviations (-1 / -1.5)  (aliases: range finding, measured move, standard deviation projection)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Take the price leg prior to the run (the "slingshot/catapult" wind-back) — here a high down to a low — and project it with a Fib.
  - -1 = a perfect measured move (the leg added to the high): the "low-hanging fruit", no-brainer exit, especially if it reaches into an old high / relative equal highs where real stops rest. Partial there with a limit order if you have more than one contract.
  - -1.5 = where price can extrapolate and "get ahead of itself".
  - He aims for the "gray area" between -1 and -1.5 (roughly the midpoint; caption says "like 1.05 something" — unclear, likely ~1.25), and exits at or above the midpoint because trying to be too precise often means the limit isn't filled.
- **How to use:** Simplest rule for beginners: for a long, measure the price leg before your run and project -1; if it reaches an old high or relative equal highs, that's the draw.
- **Example in this video:** Asia long: measured from the high to the low of the leg before the 7 PM run; exit 18,607.5, "just above halfway" between -1 and -1.5. Price later traded up to the projection.
- **Timestamps:** [0:57:57](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3477) — prior leg as the range to measure; [0:59:32](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3572) — -1 and -1.5; [1:01:09](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3669) — exit 607.5; [1:03:34](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3814) — gray area vs low-hanging fruit.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He admits he wants to nail highs but accepts that perfect exits aren't a "steady diet".

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Weakness signature: failure to reach CE of an FVG  (aliases: consequent encroachment, PD array failing)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** When bearish, if price trades up into an FVG and fails even to touch its CE (midpoint), it is "decidedly weak". Then the next bearish order block or a 15-second FVG entry will "probably be a winner", moving one-sided lower; target the inefficiency below, a single low, or relative equal lows (SSL). (Mirror for bullish.)
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:37](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=997); [0:17:23](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=1043).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Initial liquidity levels as real support/resistance overnight; previous day high/low
body:
- **Kind:** example / rule
- **What ICT says:** The initial BSL/SSL levels are what the algorithm keeps referring back to — this is the "real" support/resistance, not lines drawn at random swing points. Retail sees a quick run up and consolidation as a "bull flag" — "that's fake". Most big setups form around the previous day's high and low (what he taught on BabyPips in 2010).
- **Example in this video:** NQ overnight Aug 8–9: the bull-flag-looking consolidation broke down to the old initial BSL level; swept below the NDOG to the NWOG high (next level below); gyrated around the initial SSL; rallied back to the NDOG, then to the previous day high and gyrated around the initial BSL; another bull-flag look at midnight ran down to the NWOG CE; then gyrated in the 12:00–12:30 range, popped through, consolidated around the old initial BSL, hit it, pumped, and at ~6 AM dropped back into the NDOG, bumped the previous day high again; ~7:58 AM it traded up to the initial SSL level and dropped.
- **Timestamps:** [1:09:07](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4147) — bull flag is fake; [1:11:31](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4291) — to NWOG high; [1:12:19](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4339) — previous day high, initial BSL; [1:15:30](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4530) — PDH/PDL setups, initial SSL test.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Volume-imbalance short into relative equal lows (7:58 AM example)  (aliases: volume imbalance, relative equal lows, SSL)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (example)
- **What ICT says:** If you missed the reaction at the level, wait for an FVG or volume imbalance; price opened, traded up into a volume imbalance → short, targeting the relative equal lows (and the relative equal low further left).
- **Example in this video:** NQ, 7:58 AM ET Aug 9: price hit the initial SSL reference and dropped; retrace up into a volume imbalance = short; delivered through relative equal lows into the NWOG low, then reacted. From inside the NWOG, a reaction off the NWOG low makes the NWOG midpoint the reasonable draw. Then price dropped into an FVG after taking a short-term low and rallied back to the initial SSL reference.
- **Timestamps:** [1:16:17](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4577) — 7:58 setup; [1:17:07](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4627) — NWOG low; [1:18:44](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4724) — FVG precision, back to initial SSL.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: RTH opening range gap & the 9:30–10:00 opening range  (aliases: regular trading hours gap, opening range, midgap)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Switch the chart from electronic trading hours (ETH) to regular trading hours (RTH) to see the RTH gap: the difference between the previous day's 4:15 PM ET settlement close and the 9:30 AM open. (4:00 bell, 15 minutes settling, 4:15 day session done; electronic trading continues to 5 PM, restarts at 6 PM.)
  - The opening range is algorithmically 30 minutes, 9:30–10:00 — "there is no 15-minute opening range." Within it the market establishes initial buy-side and sell-side, like the 6 PM NDOG protocol. Sometimes there's no opening-range impact and price just runs.
  - Highlight the whole gap range and watch. With a large gap, price will normally trade a bit against the open, then work back, often taking/approaching the low formed.
  - After a big gap lower, there is about a **70% chance** price returns to **midgap** (the gap's midpoint) — even if bearish overall; "not 100%".
  - Whether the gap closes fully is judged using the initial BSL/SSL levels and other factors.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Aug 9: gapped down on RTH; first candle green (open = low); price ran up because it had already taken a low, reached midgap, bumped the low again, then ran up to the initial SSL reference level from the 6 PM protocol — not a full gap closure (it could have reached the 4:15 close or half the wick).
- **Timestamps:** [1:21:06](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4866) — ETH vs RTH; [1:22:41](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=4961) — 30-minute opening range; [1:24:19](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5059) — highlight the gap; [1:25:09](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5109) — 70% midgap.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: No-news morning behavior
body:
- **Kind:** rule (restated)
- **What ICT says:** With no medium/high-impact news in the morning session, the market can be aimless and choppy from 8:30, though external events (Middle East tensions, US election) can still cause big runs. In that environment he doesn't hold overnight and doesn't take more trades than he should.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 8:36 AM Aug 9: traded down to the NWOG low, rallied, retraced into an FVG and its CE, traded above, back to CE, up to at least the NWOG high and to the initial SSL reference, then "fell out of bed".
- **Timestamps:** [1:34:50](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5690); [1:35:38](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5738).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Time & price defined
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** "Time" = the specific times taught (6 PM, 7 PM, 8:30, 9:30, macros, etc.). "Price" at that time is always either an **inefficiency** or **liquidity** (above an old high, below an old low, relative equal highs/lows). The market operates on time first, then price; his tools applied at the wrong time won't work.
- **Timestamps:** [0:56:22](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=3382) — time first; [1:30:05](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5405) — price = inefficiency or liquidity.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: TGIF (Friday weekly-range retracement)  (aliases: TGIF setup, Thank God It's Friday)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** When the week has been strongly one-sided, Friday is inclined to retrace back into the week's range (Sunday open through the week) by 20–30% of the weekly high-to-low range; in some cases up to 40% (he has rules for that he won't teach). Shorts on Friday after a bullish week can target ~30% down from the weekly high. Sometimes it's a straight shot then dies sideways; sometimes it meanders and breaks down in steps. Not a prediction of Friday's close. Driven by nobody wanting to hold risk into the weekend; a 30% pullback doesn't break a long-term bullish picture.
- **Example in this video:** Week of Aug 5–9, 2024 NQ moved strongly up; no news Friday → he expected possible meandering lower.
- **Timestamps:** [1:36:24](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5784); [1:37:15](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5835); [1:38:03](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5883).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: SMT divergence between NQ, ES, YM (how he weighs it)  (aliases: SMT, smart money technique)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** He doesn't trade the Dow (YM, "dirty 30") — only uses it to confirm market breadth and continuity. A divergence involving the Dow is taken "with a grain of salt": he'll be cautious and may consider a partial, but won't close the whole trade because of it. A divergence between NQ and ES (e.g. long NQ, NQ makes a higher high and ES doesn't) is more valid — he'll likely take a partial because it signals weakening momentum.
- **Example in this video:** Aug 9: ES "looks even worse than NASDAQ"; both ES and YM have relative equal highs that are "too clean" — he'd expect them to be disrupted (smoothness taken out) before any move lower; he wouldn't trade ES there.
- **Timestamps:** [1:40:24](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=6024) — ES/YM too clean; [1:41:14](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=6074) — Dow divergence grain of salt; [1:42:01](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=6121) — NQ vs ES divergence → partial.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #5    August 9, 2024
head: Clean charts / levels on a notepad ("trading naked")
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:** He keeps key levels written on a notepad/tablet next to him, not on the chart; annotations on his charts are only for teaching. Lines clutter the chart, draw the eye, and in his own development made him hold losing ideas stubbornly ("it's going to happen because I have these lines"). Removing annotations made him flexible to see when price was in trouble. Beginners should keep annotations at first and not rush to go naked — it takes weeks/months of experience.
- **Example in this video:** NQ at 18,482.5 with his notes saying NWOG high 18,513.25 — in close proximity, so price could gyrate back up there; relative equal highs above still "too clean".
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:12](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=852); [0:15:50](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=950); [1:27:34](https://youtu.be/ul6x6BwOg6M?t=5254).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Session start-time delineation (7:00 ET) and "wait for the first sweep before annotating"  (aliases: "7 o'clock rule", the initial run, last week's rules)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement (re-statement of Lecture #5 framework, applied live)
- **What ICT says:**
  - If your trading day starts at 7:00 a.m. ET (New York local time), you start watching price at 7:00 and mark the first short-term high/low formed by the 7:00 candle area. The chart clock must be ICT time (New York local). "7 o'clock isn't changing"; the rules are never optimized or "morphed".
  - He does NOT annotate the 7:00-candle high as the initial buy-side liquidity just because it is a high. He waits for the initial run to take the high out (gives it "some allowance"), then waits for a short-term high to form and price to trade lower and take out the low. Only then does he highlight both the high and the low.
  - The first 30 minutes after 7:00 (7:00–7:30) is used to form the initial high and low he delineates.
  - Start time variants: if you start at 8:00, use any relative equal highs/lows formed after 7:00 that have not been pierced; if they were already taken, sit and wait for your own relative equal highs/lows to form after 8:00. If you use the 9:00 hour you have additional factors, e.g. the regular-trading-hours opening range (he had shown Caleb that on Friday).
  - He frames the whole approach as: where is it going, why should it go there, how do I know when it will start, what is the beginning of that move.
- **How to identify:** a defined start time; a marked high/low pair after that time; the first run takes one side; then the other side is raided (see Relative equal highs/lows below).
- **How to use:** it defines which liquidity is "initial" for your session and tells you where to be patient. "Waiting" is the entry condition.
- **Example in this video:** Mon Aug 12, 2024. A high exists to the left of 7:00 and the 7:00 candle also makes a high. Price ran above those (relative equal highs, plus the London-session high), sold off, then broke lower leaving a fair value gap and displacement; the lows below (5:00 a.m. low, 7:00 range low) became the targets.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:55](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=595) — "I'm not trying to annotate that high" until the run happens and the low is taken; [0:35:27](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=2127) — recap of why the 7:00 candle high is not labeled initial BSL; [0:36:17](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=2177) — what to do if you start at 8:00; [0:48:22](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=2902) — first 30 minutes post-7:00.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Teaching is explicitly a recap of "last week" (Lecture #5). He repeats that the rules do not change and no settings are tuned.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Relative equal highs / lows as the first liquidity after the start time  (aliases: REH/REL, "layered sell-side pool", initial buy side)
body:
- **Kind:** rule + example
- **What ICT says:**
  - At 7:00 you wait for relative equal highs (or lows) to form after the time marker, then wait for price to pierce them. The pierce is the raid; the reaction after it is what you trade. "They cannot hide 7 o'clock."
  - A "literal" relative equal high is needed: a lower high next to a high to the left counts (he checks: is this high higher or lower than the one to its left; lower, so it meets the criteria).
  - The run only has to trade above the relative equal highs that formed after 7:00; it does not need to reach the London high or any other level.
  - Highs formed earlier (London) are lower priority ("the level of least importance to me"); the ones that form after the start time are the interest.
  - Lows: he sees a layered sell-side pool: relative equal lows, a slightly higher low, and the 5:00 a.m. low (end of the London session) that price "stopped short of". The small low inside the range from 7:00 (and inside the London-run range) is the minor sell-side liquidity.
  - At 9:00 the same logic applies: relative equal highs at 9:00 are "your 9:00 setup"; and at the 9:30 open there are fresh relative equal highs plus a gap just under them.
- **How to identify:** two or more highs (or lows) within a small tolerance, formed after the start time and not yet breached; for sell-side, the low inside the session range is "minor" sell-side liquidity.
- **How to use:** when bias is down (see NWOG/NDOG bias), wait for relative equal highs to be pierced, then look for a bearish PD array to short. Mirror for longs implied but not walked through in this video.
- **Example in this video:** Highs at the 6:xx/7:00 candles and London highs are run; price then trades below the 7:00 range; the relative equal highs after 7:00 are what the bearish order block sits on.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:46](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=646) — relative equal highs taken, leaves minor sell-side low inside the 7:00 and London range; [0:11:39](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=699) — layered sell-side pool; [1:45:34](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=6334) — 9:00 relative equal highs "your 9:00 setup"; [2:24:22](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=8662) — at 7:00 with NWOG/NDOG below price you know you are waiting for a relative equal high.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Minor sell-side" means a low inside the range between the 7:00 start and the high, not an external swing.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG) and New Day Opening Gap (NDOG) as the draw and as bias inputs  (aliases: "old inefficiencies", "clustering of new day opening gaps", "black hole")
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule (re-stated from Lecture #5)
- **What ICT says:**
  - NWOG for this week: Friday's 5:00 p.m. closing/settlement price to Sunday's 6:00 p.m. opening price (Sunday Aug 11 here). NDOG: the prior day's 5:00 p.m. close to the 6:00 p.m. open one hour later. Example: the Friday Aug 9 NDOG was formed from Thursday evening's 5:00 p.m. close and the 6:00 p.m. open. A new NDOG forms each evening.
  - NDOGs have a shelf life / life cycle; he suggests working with them as if about five days, "not that it's limited to five days". The market gravitates back and forth to these inefficiencies, like a magnet; they are the "first central tenets" of bias.
  - A gap under 20 handles is not subdivided into quadrants (he does not annotate quadrants or the midpoint on it). He eyeballs it (roughly upper/lower half). Implication: quadrants matter for larger gaps.
  - The algorithm "has to refer back" to old inefficiencies at the opening bell, so you gravitate toward them rather than watching order-book heat maps.
  - Price on Monday morning was above the NWOG and above the Friday NDOG and the cluster of earlier NDOGs and last week's NWOG; therefore the weight of the market is down, to discount arrays below.
- **How to identify:** compare price at your start time to the NWOG and NDOG cluster. Above them = expect sell-side delivery toward them.
- **How to use:** primary draw on liquidity for the session; targets are the NWOG (bodies stopped at it), then the next NDOG (Fri Aug 9), and the midpoint (CE) of the NDOG as the end of the morning's interest.
- **Example in this video:** Price traded lower from the bearish order block, through layered sell-side and the upper quadrant region, and the candle bodies stopped right at the NWOG; it then continued to last Friday's NDOG and traded to the NDOG's midpoint (consequent encroachment), where he said "that ends my interest in the morning session". Price then showed willingness to go higher and traded back over the area.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:14](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1634) — NWOG as the draw; [0:28:19](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1699) — NDOG life cycle and the <20 handles quadrant rule; [0:29:16](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1756) — how the Friday NDOG is calibrated; [0:32:49](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1969) — trading to the NDOG midpoint ends the morning's interest.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says he introduced NWOG/NDOG publicly in spring/summer 2023 on Twitter Spaces and deliberately let public interest fade because it is "too good" to be in everyone's hands.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Session-bias checklist at 7:00 (price vs NWOG/NDOG cluster)  (aliases: "first elements of bias", session bias, "weight of the market")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry framework
- **What ICT says:**
  - If at 7:00 price is above the new week opening gap and the NDOGs are clustered below price (all of last week's NDOGs, Friday's NDOG, last week's NWOG), the market is likely to enter a sell program: sell-side delivery, a sustained run lower. He then does not look to go long even if price springs higher; he expects that rally to fizzle above old highs formed after 7:00.
  - Bias here is a session bias; it need not be the daily bias (predicting close above/below the open). Focus on the morning session: a run that is measurable, one-sided, that you can participate in.
  - When the weight is down, the market "discovers / probes into discount arrays" below: inefficiencies, deep retracements into the previous week's range, or short-term lows that can be identified on the 15-minute chart.
  - The run has to be "definitely a protraction", one-directional, going to a level that can be predetermined, "not random".
  - He is not trying to predict the day's close, only one session run.
- **How to identify:** (1) price vs NWOG; (2) where the NDOG cluster sits; (3) TGIF/weekly-range retracement status (below); (4) time of day (7:00+).
- **How to use:** with bias down: wait for relative equal highs after 7:00, wait for the pierce, then enter a bearish PD array (list below) and aim for sell-side liquidity, NWOG, and NDOG.
- **Example in this video:** exactly the Aug 12 morning described above.
- **Timestamps:** [1:09:55](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4195) — session bias vs daily bias, probing discount arrays; [1:35:09](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=5709) — "if we're above NWOG and the clustering of NDOGs"; [1:38:13](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=5893) — above NWOG is a checkbox for sell-side delivery; [2:16:16](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=8176) — strip it down to the chrome.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He calls this "bland, not sexy, rule-based". He says the mirror for longs (price below NWOG with NDOGs above) follows the same logic but does not walk through it here (inference, not stated).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: TGIF: Friday retracement of 20–30% of the weekly range, deferred to Monday  (aliases: "Thank God It's Friday", weekly-range retracement)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** In an up-close week he looks for a retracement of about 20–30% of the weekly range into Friday ("TGIF"). If it does not happen on Friday, it is deferred; the likelihood of that 20–30% retracement of the previous week's range shifts to the next week's Monday. It is not required to be profitable; it is "one more little box to check" that puts probability on shorts over longs. He had told Caleb on Friday the retracement could happen; instead price pressed into Friday's close.
- **How to identify:** prior week closed up; Friday did not retrace 20–30% of the weekly range.
- **How to use:** use as a supporting factor for short bias on Monday (with NWOG/NDOG below price). It applies even with CPI/PPI later in the week.
- **Example in this video:** Last week rallied; no TGIF on Fri Aug 9; Monday Aug 12 morning sold off, consistent with the deferred retracement.
- **Timestamps:** [1:07:05](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4025) — TGIF 20–30% not formed Friday; [1:07:57](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4077) — deferred to Monday; [1:32:29](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=5549) — restated.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Treated as a probability tilt, not a trigger.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Bearish Order Block: opening price as the change in state of delivery  (aliases: "my order block", up-close candle order block, CISD)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + entry model + refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Bearish OB = an up-closed candle that is followed by price trading below (a close below) that candle's opening price on the time frame you are using. The opening price on an order block is the "change in state of delivery". Validation: a later candle closes below the OB candle's opening price.
  - It does NOT require trading below the OB candle's wick/low. "My order block does not require the trade below the wick" when the narrative is understood.
  - It is only meaningful if narrative and time agree. He mocks the old "down-close candle gets touched, market goes up" approach (baby pips), and says there is no such thing as an "institutional candle". Candles alone fail without narrative.
  - It is a premium array in a sell program: up-close candles are used to stave off advances higher, but not every up-close candle works; price may go back up into inefficiencies and touch them again because time is afforded for it.
  - Each candle's opening price: he explicitly labels the change-in-state-of-delivery level on every order block.
- **How to identify (as stated):** (1) a run above relative equal highs or buy-side liquidity (the sweep), (2) an up-closed candle at the top, (3) a subsequent candle opens below the OB's opening price and (4) the OB candle's body is displaced away from, leaving an inefficiency (FVG) behind.
- **How to use:**
  - Entry: sell as price trades back up to the OB's opening price, on an uptick, after the next candle has opened below that open. The sweet spot is the opening price, or between the opening price and the candle's low. "Hammer that as a short"; trade it the first time it returns. He does not worry about slippage near the low of the gap.
  - Stop: he says "rejection block, which is the close on the order block" (stop just beyond the close of the OB candle; caption slightly unclear). Risk can be defined as far as the midpoint (mean threshold) of the OB; "it doesn't need to be up here" at the high.
  - Target: the layered sell-side below, then NWOG, then NDOG.
  - Heat: price traded only about one tick above the entry area; accept some heat since the algorithm returns to the area first.
- **Example in this video:** 1-minute chart, morning of Aug 12. An up-closed 1m candle went above the relative equal highs (formed after 7:00 / London). The next candle opened below its opening price. Price traded up, filling the short at the OB opening price on the uptick. A second 1m green candle (also validated by closing below its open) is another bearish order block. Price then dropped through the inefficiency to sell-side liquidity.
- **Timestamps:** [1:07:05](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4025) — OB needs no trade below the wick; [1:10:53](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4253) — validation mechanics on the 1m chart; [1:11:48](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4308) — entry on the opening price, stop at the close/rejection block; [1:19:53](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4793) — second bearish OB labeled the same way; [1:39:07](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=5947) — validation not because it traded above London's high but because it ran stops and then went below the open.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a more specific statement than earlier "OB = last up/down candle" teaching: validated by close below the open, no wick/low trade required, entry at the open price, stop at the close of the OB body. ICT acknowledges the opening-price entry may not always fill.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Mean threshold vs. Consequent Encroachment (CE)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Consequent encroachment is the midpoint of any gap/inefficiency (FVG, volume imbalance). Mean threshold is the midpoint of a specific range formed by a single candle, such as an order block candle. Some students call both "consequent encroachment" and he corrects that.
- **How to identify:** gap or inefficiency → CE; single-candle range (the OB) → mean threshold.
- **How to use:** CE and mean threshold are where the bodies are held; entries/stops are placed against them. Stop can be as far as the OB's mean threshold. He wants candle bodies to respect the upper half of the gap.
- **Example in this video:** The bodies on the retrace "stay at the high of that fair value gap and essentially the midpoint of this order block, which is mean threshold".
- **Timestamps:** [1:21:45](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4905) — the definitional correction; [1:42:53](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=6173) — bodies held at the gap high / OB mean threshold.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The midpoint of a gap being "CE" (not "mean threshold") is the key naming rule here.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: FVG measurement with volume imbalance, and "upper half stays open" as the algorithmic signature  (aliases: respecting half of a gap, SIBI/BISI, "bid/sell efficiency")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement + rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - When measuring the gap, do not use only the wick of the candle: the body close vs. the next candle's open leaves a separation (a volume imbalance), and you need to combine that with the gap measurement to get the true consequent encroachment level.
  - In a sell program, for a bearish gap/inversion gap/reclaimed FVG (a premium array), you want the upper half of the inefficiency left open: price should respect only the lower half. That is "how you know the algorithm is respecting the PD array" and a measurable displacement in your favor should follow. Wicks poked above the gap by only one tick; bodies respected the lower half.
  - If price trades up to the top of the gap, he needs an immediate rejection there and then a displacement. If it does not give him that, he will not touch it again until a new FVG forms on a lower time frame.
  - He admits there are times where the inefficiency closes entirely and price still goes lower, and he does not like it in a trade.
  - Signatures are "things not printing in the candlesticks".
- **How to identify:** gap forms during displacement, price retraces, bodies stall at the CE/upper half while wicks poke slightly past it.
- **How to use:** short only on the retrace into the lower part of the gap (see lowest-threshold entry below); invalidation: bodies trade through the upper half.
- **Example in this video:** After the bearish OB, the 1m FVG formed; price returned and only the lower half was respected; wicks went above by one tick, bodies stayed under.
- **Timestamps:** [1:12:42](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4362) — measuring with the body close and the volume imbalance; [1:14:27](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4467) — only the lower half respected; [1:17:09](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4629) — upper half should act as resistance / stay open; [1:18:58](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4738) — need immediate rejection and displacement at the top.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The captions garble "SIBI/BISI" as "cellid balance bid efficiency" (caption unclear). The "half the gap respected" idea was previously taught elsewhere as CE; here he uses the upper half as the algorithm's tell.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Inversion FVG and Reclaimed FVG as premium arrays  (aliases: iFVG, reclaimed fair value gap, orange-shaded box)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - An orange-shaded area on his chart means: he wants to see price go below it, spend time below, then come back up and treat it as an inversion FVG, a barrier price does not want to get back above. If candles promote that idea and then displacement appears, he can short using a FVG, an institutional order flow entry drill (IOFED), or a bearish order block.
  - A "reclaimed FVG" is when the narrative and time are not in agreement with the simple read of the gap: even though price trades back up into the inefficiency, it is not a buy; it is a premium array. Beginners think "gap = it will sell off when touched" or "gap = it will go up".
  - He lists the bearish arrays to use once price rejects the pierce: FVG IOFED, bearish breaker, bearish order block, bearish mitigation block, inversion FVG ("used to be viewed as bullish but once it trades below it and returns, it becomes usable").
- **How to identify:** a (formerly bullish) gap that price has broken below and then returns to from beneath.
- **How to use:** short on the return into it with narrative aligned (above NWOG/NDOG, sweep of REH complete); the lowest part of the gap is the lowest-threshold entry.
- **Example in this video:** Early in the stream: the live trade at 0:30 "touches the bottom of the inversion fair value gap — that's a trade" before the market rips lower through layered liquidity. Later he describes price trading up into the gap and the bodies respecting the lower half.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:47](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1307) — orange-shading convention for an inversion FVG; [0:53:45](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=3225) — reclaimed FVG explanation; [0:30:07](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1807) — touch of bottom of iFVG as the trade; [2:17:10](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=8230) — list of bearish arrays.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Reclaimed fair value gap" is used here as a premium array descriptor (caption partly unclear).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Entering at the lowest threshold of a gap; limit orders that do not fill; Price Delivery Continuum (drop to a lower time frame)  (aliases: lowest probable resistance entry, IOFED-style entry)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / execution rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - For a short, he uses the "lowest probable resistance": the lowest level of a FVG that he thinks will hold price down (the low of the gap). It is the "easy" entry, the one he knows he will get, so he does not have to fear a limit not filling. Reference: the high of the up-close candle defining the BISI (gap).
  - Even with precision he has seen limit orders where price prints the level and still does not fill. The fix: if price trades to the top of the gap and rejects and he misses it, he waits for the displacement and a new fair value gap on a lower time frame (on a 1m chart that means 15-second/30-second) and enters there. "That's the price delivery continuum theory" from last week. He does not need to enter on the time frame he is studying.
  - After a stop-out or missed fill the entry is forgiving when you know what you are looking for.
  - Entry zone for the OB: between its opening price and its low; take it the first time price returns, and do not worry about heat.
  - Scaling in: when a new FVG forms on the way back and he adds, he does NOT roll the stop aggressively just because he has another entry. He waits for the market to roll out of the area after proving it (bodies kept at the gap high / OB mean threshold) before tightening.
- **How to identify / use:** as above.
- **Example in this video:** Adds into a second gap on the retrace; stop kept; trade stopped out with a gain later (trailed).
- **Timestamps:** [0:51:56](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=3116) — lowest probable resistance/lowest threshold entry; [1:18:58](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4738) — lower-time-frame fallback, price delivery continuum; [1:41:57](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=6117) — use the lowest-threshold entry; [1:42:53](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=6173) — don't roll stop just because you added.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Contrasts with the common instinct to chase the best price (top of gap).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Seek and Destroy (Monday/pre-news chop)  (aliases: S&D, jagged, "made jagged")
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** Seek and Destroy is where the market goes just above a short-term high, then goes back lower to take an old short-term low, then back up to take the short-term high just formed, and so on. It runs you over even when you are right on direction. It is typical on a Monday morning ahead of big news days (here PPI/CPI), because large pools are not positioned and everyone is "chomping at the bit". Price action is "skittish" and "sloppy". He talks about waiting for the market to be "made jagged" (liquidity engineered) versus smooth areas.
- **How to identify:** repeated rotation above a fresh short-term high and below a fresh short-term low.
- **How to use:** be conservative: take partials, protect quickly, do not hunt home runs, and give yourself one shot.
- **Example in this video:** The opening stretch of the stream: his limit short filled, stop was brought down to protect, price rotated back and stopped him out in profit.
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:21](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1581) — definition; [0:19:56](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1196) — limit order filled, stop brought down, price came back into the entry area; [0:44:33](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=2673) — back-and-forth before PPI/CPI days.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Describes day-type, not a model.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Trading around high-impact news; Mondays; early-session timing  (aliases: PPI/CPI, NFP Monday, Silver Bullet, morning session)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - He does not care what CPI/PPI/NFP numbers say; he looks at the time when price is likely to run. These reports (8:30 a.m. ET) tend to give protracted one-directional moves (sometimes an aggressive reversal) and are "face rippers"; he sits out and waits for information after the manipulation.
  - Mondays: generally not interested, because he wants other traders to put their neck out and see consensus first. Exception: every Monday of a week where non-farm payroll falls on Friday, he trades.
  - Do not trade Monday morning ahead of PPI/CPI as a rule for his son; if you do, give yourself one chance early.
  - Why trade before 9:30 or before the 10:00 Silver Bullet window: when a big event is on the following day, take trades early, because by the open everyone is trying to do something and it gets volatile; he wants to be in "when the market's cleanest" (the 7:00–8:00 / first 30 minutes after 7:00 framework).
  - Without news data in the morning, sustained runs are less likely: know where you take partials, move quickly to protect, do not look for home runs. Having an economic calendar event behind the technical idea is better.
  - After the report, he would wait for information (he also remarks it is probably better to trade the afternoon on a no-data morning; wording ambiguous).
  - Next sessions: he starts at 9:15 ET Tue–Fri with pre-drawn levels.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:39](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1419) — Mondays and NFP exception; [0:17:20](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1040) — mornings without data are harder; [0:47:24](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=2844) — why trade early before 9:30/10:00; [2:14:25](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=8065) — not trading ahead of CPI/PPI.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The "Silver Bullet" reference is only a time marker (10:00); no Silver Bullet teaching.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Targets, draw on liquidity, and where he expects the end of the move
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** Targets in order: the minor sell-side liquidity inside the 7:00/London range; the layered sell-side pool (relative equal lows, the 5:00 a.m. low at the end of London's session); then the NWOG (price bodies stop at it) and next NDOG (Fri Aug 9). His interest in a short ends at the midpoint (CE) of the Friday NDOG. He says he would not have held through the minor low because the jagged action there is bait for more shorts; he would not buy and would not try a 200-handle short.
- **Timestamps:** [1:22:42](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4962) — minor sell-side, NWOG, then the Aug 9 NDOG; [1:23:35](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=5015) — price trades down to Friday's NDOG then shows willingness to go higher; [0:32:49](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1969).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Partials, stop trailing and "pay yourself"  (aliases: Terminus, trade management)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Take a partial before the main objective ("Terminus"); once the first partial is taken and the stop is moved to cover costs "you cannot lose", barring a gap, and the need to be right disappears. "Partials always pay you."
  - Do not punish yourself if it does not run. In volatile markets price can return many times to the entry area; if you lack a plan, take the win.
  - He shows a limit order, expand it beyond the initial level when price really moves, and take single partials at levels he likes.
  - Once the stop has been reduced (moved to a gain), do not widen it back. "If I moved it too prematurely I'm going to eat it."
  - If a trade can be closed prematurely by a failing narrative, move the stop to an advantageous location so a reversal still leaves you with something. He asks you to know why the trade is still viable, why hold, and what lets you re-enter after a stop.
  - If you realize you made a mistake entry (accidental fill), close the trade and see how you would manage it; this removes the "it has to be right" weight. Do not partially pyramid into a mistake.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:09](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1089) — partials always pay; [0:19:03](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=1143) — if you do not take partials; [0:45:30](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=2730) — breakeven stop is "closest thing to Nirvana"; [1:17:09](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=4629) — close accidental trades; [1:58:54](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=7134) — expand limit orders, take single partials.
- **Example in this video:** At the stream start a limit short was filled, stop lowered, trade stopped at gain (not a loss), then price dropped to the target he had drawn. An accidental fill at the gap CE happened when his laptop touchpad was bumped; he used it as a teaching moment, not a signal.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Walk-forward (tape-reading) learning path, demo and journaling
body:
- **Kind:** process rule
- **What ICT says:** First goal: learn where price is going and why (the draw), "your first mutant power". Do walk-forward testing: no trades, just watching price form and anticipate the FVG, and the upper half staying open, every day for months. Only when it is boring and you can anticipate formation do you start demo; "you shouldn't even have a demo available" before that. Demo for a minimum of 6 months before any real account, so you learn yourself and the tools in your own hands. Journal old moves to build pseudo-experience, then walk forward with the hard right edge. In demo/live a stop just outside the "should not trade past this" boundary desensitizes you to fluctuations.
- **Timestamps:** [0:58:09](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=3489) — demo a minimum of 6 months; [1:59:48](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=7188) — if not obvious, do not hold an opinion; [2:22:32](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=8552) — forward walk testing definition; [2:23:28](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=8608) — stop outside the boundary.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #6   August 12, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Sentiment indicator via other streamers' chat
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / process
- **What ICT says:** He watches emotional, emoji-heavy live-stream chats; when people proclaim long (e.g. 15 contracts on an unpassed funded account) right as price trades into a fair value gap or just above a short-term high, that is the best scenario to take the opposite side if his own technical criteria are present. He never joins another streamer's trade; he uses their chat as a contrarian sentiment gauge and posts levels (buy side/sell side) in chats. He cautions that being contrarian just by temperament is a trap; do it only when the technical criteria are there.
- **Timestamps:** [1:29:46](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=5386) — chat as perfect sentiment indicator; [1:30:39](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=5439) — 15-contract example; [1:59:48](https://youtu.be/woAQ1XJeD7Y?t=7188) — contrarian caution.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: News-day protocol (8:30 ET reports: NFP, CPI, PPI)  (aliases: post-news framing; "don't trade the storm")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - On days with an 8:30 ET high-impact driver (NFP, PPI, CPI, and by implication FOMC) you "shouldn't be trading that day". Wait for the 9:30 opening bell and, if you insist on engaging for practice, usually trade the **10:00 Silver Bullet**. For NFP specifically, waiting for the Silver Bullet is "the easiest way in", though it does not guarantee a win.
  - Do not mark an "initial high / initial low" for liquidity before these reports. The release is heavily manipulated, usually produces one-sided runs, and any directional bias or target given before it is more likely wrong than right. Let it run "like a hurricane" and look for setups only after the storm: what did the run leave behind?
  - Frame the day from the opening-bell range. Building the framework inside roughly 7:00–9:30 ET is fine; do not look at anything before 7:00, because that pulls in London-session price action and makes the daily profile more complex. Relative equal highs/lows that form after the open count as the initial BSL/SSL.
  - For a new trader these are days to watch and log, not to trade. He is explicitly telling his son not to feel he has to be successful navigating them yet.
  - He believes CPI/PPI are especially manipulated in an election year, and that the Fed is "in the market". These are his stated opinions.
- **How to identify:** a scheduled 8:30 ET report. Price before and during it is a one-sided run.
- **How to use:** stand aside until 9:30. Look for relative equal highs/lows after the open, then a 10:00 hour (Silver Bullet / 9:50–10:10 macro) idea. Study the 8:30 run's origin afterwards (see "Higher-timeframe draw on liquidity").
- **Example in this video:** PPI 8:30. NQ rallied off the 6 pm new-day opening gap, challenged the London high, and pushed through it. By 9:30 it had delivered straight to the weekly/daily objective he gave at the start of the stream. He called the 9:30 open "one-sided, one-shot delivery". He took no trade.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:47](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=407) — no trading news days; Silver Bullet for NFP · [0:14:06](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=846) — no initial high/low before CPI/PPI-type reports · [0:30:58](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=1858) — frame from 7:00–9:30, nothing before 7:00
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** consistent with earlier "avoid the news candle, trade the aftermath" teaching. The new detail is "no initial BSL/SSL before the report" and "do not use pre-7:00 price".

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Higher-timeframe draw on liquidity first (weekly → daily → intraday)  (aliases: where is price going to be drawn; "the first thing you're trying to do")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / process
- **What ICT says:**
  - The first and only initial job is to get a feel for where the market could genuinely end up without much back-and-forth, i.e. the draw on liquidity. You are not trying to find patterns, the best stop location or where to move your stop. "If you don't have [the draw], everything else is going to put you offside."
  - He builds it from the weekly chart down to the daily, then the intraday charts. If the market is going to move, it moves to something on the daily chart.
  - A tradable idea needs range. He wants at least ~20 NQ handles of simple, timeable run, because from 20 handles he can take 10–15.
- **How to identify:** weekly and daily imbalances (SIBI/BISI), candle lows/highs, consequent encroachment of wicks and old highs/lows that price has not yet reached.
- **How to use:** mark the weekly and daily levels on your chart or notepad before the session. Then watch price either reach them or fail. Do not chase once price is already there.
- **Example in this video:**
  - Weekly: the low of the weekly candle of 22 July 2024 at 18883.25 (as captioned). A weekly sell-side imbalance / buy-side inefficiency (SIBI) sits there, and he also notes the consequent encroachment (CE) of that candle's wick. He asks for stiff opposition at the level ("I like to see some kind of stiff opposition to any forward run higher at the 18883¼ level"), meaning he does not expect a clean run through it.
  - Daily: the butt end of a daily candle low about 10 handles away, ~18854 (as captioned).
  - Result: NQ ran about 50 handles up off the Monday-evening/overnight gap area and hit both levels. Weekly and daily objectives were met early, so he saw nothing left to buy.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:34](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=454) — weekly low 18883.25 and its CE · [0:10:03](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=603) — daily ~854 and weekly ~883/884 written on the notepad · [0:33:32](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=2012) — the draw is the first thing, "almost like meditation" · [3:09:24](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=11364) — if you do not know where the market is likely to draw to, everything else puts you offside
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** prices are as auto-captioned and may be off (e.g. thousands digits). He says "forget the PPI label" and just study the whole run from its origin (the new-day opening gap) to the target to see the PD arrays along the way.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: New Day Opening Gap (NDOG): CE rule and as a level  (aliases: new day opening gap; 5 pm close → 6 pm reopen)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - The NDOG is the difference between the 5:00 pm ET close and the 6:00 pm ET reopen. "Sticking with the rules", if it is **over 20 handles** (NQ) he annotates its consequent encroachment. Price traded back to the CE level, then rallied.
  - Friday's NDOG and the new week opening gap are also downside targets: if price goes below the NWOG it can run to Friday's NDOG.
- **How to identify:** 5 pm close vs 6 pm open gap on NQ, larger than 20 handles → draw high, low and CE.
- **How to use:** CE of a large NDOG is a retracement/support level on the next session (here, the 8:30 run's origin). The NDOG high was also noted as a level that was formed "last evening".
- **Example in this video:** The NDOG high formed 5→6 pm Monday. Early Tuesday, price traded back down to the NDOG CE, then rallied aggressively (an order block and a breaker block with the CE and a sell-side imbalance/buy-side inefficiency converging). Price then pushed above the London high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:38](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=698) — NDOG high, over-20-handle CE rule · [0:18:59](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=1139) — walk-through of the rally from the NDOG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** the explicit "over 20 handles → mark CE" threshold is the number to keep. NDOG origin was used as the start of the measuring leg for the whole day's study.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: TGIF / Monday weekly-range retracement (20–30%)  (aliases: TGIF (Thank God It's Friday); weekly range retracement)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - He expects a **20–30% retracement of the present or previous week's range**. If that retracement does not happen by Friday (he dubbed it "TGIF"; the candle is one-sided), it can instead show up on Monday.
  - To use it: if the last week was predominantly one-sided and Friday did not retrace, use the **highest high Monday forms**. Measure a fib from last week's low to that high and anticipate the retracement.
  - Look for confluence between the 20% level and gaps. On Monday 12 Aug, the 20% level of (last week's low → Monday's high) sat on **Friday's NDOG**. His call was "if it goes below the new week opening gap it can go down to Friday's NDOG", and it did.
- **How to identify:** weekly fib (low → high including Monday's high) plus Friday's NDOG and the NWOG.
- **How to use:** a Monday/Tuesday retracement target for longs after a one-sided up week. He also says early-week action is where you do it "early" on days like this.
- **Example in this video:** Monday 12 Aug: price traded below the NWOG to Friday's NDOG, which coincided with the 20% fib. ICT says he was stopped out on his own Monday trade ("I did not lose on purpose") before it ran to all the levels he outlined.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:31](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=1471) — the 20–30% / TGIF explanation · [0:25:17](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=1517) — fib from week low to Monday high + Friday NDOG confluence · [0:26:57](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=1617) — what happened to his stop on Monday
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** refers to Monday's live stream (12 Aug) and Friday's stream (9 Aug). The 20–30% weekly retracement idea is an expectation, not a certainty.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Relative equal highs/lows (initial BSL/SSL) — smooth vs jagged  (aliases: initial relative equal lows/highs)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - He is teaching Caleb to focus on **relative equal lows and highs** as the initial liquidity, and to wait for a relative equal high to form rather than predicting it.
  - He prefers the **smooth** level (clean equal lows or highs) to a jagged one. "I don't like this one because it went slightly lower than that one."
  - Pre-8:30 lows had been run on the news, so he did not use them. He marked the post-open relative equal lows (SSL) and later equal highs (BSL) instead.
  - Sequence he observed: post-open relative equal highs ran (BSL taken), and no SSL run yet. Later the sell-side run came, then price was too far up to want to buy.
- **How to identify:** two or more highs/lows at nearly identical price, formed after the opening bell (7:00–9:30 window), with smooth, not overlapping, price action.
- **How to use:** mark them and see which side the market wants. A higher high after a sweep of relative equal lows means he has no interest in shorting; he is "done for the morning".
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m/5m before and after 9:30. Equal lows were swept at the 8:30 news, then equal highs formed post-open and were raided at ~9:50 into the 10:00 hour.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:44](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=944) — initial relative equal lows annotated · [0:23:44](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=1424) — rejects a slightly lower low · [0:30:09](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=1809) — relative equal highs form after the open · [1:24:25](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=5065) — "where is it smooth here"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he repeatedly contrasts smooth levels (good) with jagged action (muddy, avoid).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Inversion expectation (shading a gap to fail)  (aliases: iFVG expectation, orange shading)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - When he wants a gap to **fail**, he colors it differently (orange rather than his usual color) to signal "I expect inversion characteristics". A gap that trades down through becomes a buy-side imbalance/sell-side inefficiency (BISI) that now acts as resistance.
  - He wanted to see price trade below a gap, come back up, and find stiff resistance on it, then retrace into the daily range lower. Price did not oblige, and that kept him out.
  - He says he actually wants to see PD arrays fail, because it gives confidence that the directional expectation is still on.
  - Small wicks beyond an array do not invalidate it ("coloring outside the lines"); but too much of that is what makes a day muddy.
- **Example in this video:** the small 9:30-area gap on the 1-minute chart. Plan: price breaks below it, returns, rejects, retraces to discount. Instead price pushed up, and he said anything above the short-term high would "kill it" for the morning.
- **Timestamps:** [0:59:27](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=3567) — shading the gap orange · [1:00:17](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=3617) — inversion color convention · [1:20:27](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=4827) — he wants to see PD arrays fail
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** only a statement of expectation and annotation practice; no rule numbers.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Invalidation by candle close (exit before the stop)  (aliases: save the stop)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - If he were short with the stop placed at a given area and a candle **closes** above it, he would kill the trade rather than wait for the stop to be hit ("save the stop"). A close up there means price will likely come back and treat the area as support.
- **How to use:** define the invalidation area for a short idea at a gap/high. A closed candle (not just a wick) beyond it ends the idea.
- **Timestamps:** [1:52:58](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=6778)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he did this on a hypothetical short idea; wicks are allowed, bodies/closes are what count (same logic as "wicks do the damage, bodies tell the narrative").

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Three-drives pattern (his measured-move target)  (aliases: three Indians — Street Smarts, Connors/Raschke)
body:
- **Kind:** example only / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price pierced the weekly objective three times, which he calls a "three drives" pattern, from the book *Street Smarts* ("three Indians"). He likes classic patterns that pre-date him.
  - Classic use: he used to look for it, usually with a stochastic bearish divergence on the third high, as a reversal setup.
  - His own measured-move twist, which he says is not in the book: measure from the **low before the first high to the third swing high**. First target is **half of that range**, then the low itself.
  - He does not rely on it. Three higher highs do not guarantee a reversal; on a manipulated day the market can "grind you to dust". Some people see it as a long-term top; he has seen it also mark just an intermediate retracement before continuation.
  - He prefers to wait for the logic he teaches (next easy draw on liquidity) over predicting where the weekly closes.
- **Also:** he likes selling inside a bull flag when probabilities favor lower, i.e. he likes seeing "obvious" patterns when he is on the opposite side. He credits Nick Van Nice (not George Lane) with the trend-following stochastic divergence, which he calls a type-two divergence.
- **Timestamps:** [0:40:58](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=2458) — three drives / Street Smarts · [0:45:01](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=2701) — half-range measured-move target · [0:46:36](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=2796) — prefers the "next easy thing" logic
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** an aside, not a model he is teaching in this mentorship.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Day-type filter: when to stand aside (grinding / choppy / jagged days)  (aliases: environment filter; "fish out of water"; "swim upstream")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / psychology
- **What ICT says:**
  - He skips days where price just **grinds one way** with no meaningful retracement, or is **muddy, lethargic and jagged**: small candles, back-and-forth, coloring outside the lines, constantly overlapping. On such days PD arrays are not cleanly respected and he cannot reliably say where it will go.
  - He wants an environment with **gyration**: clean runs, obvious gaps, pullbacks into those gaps, and room to be a buyer and a seller in the same day or even hour ("Spider-Man web swinging"). He calls a day where he can buy and sell both sides a "playground".
  - Conditions that make him back off: right after a high-impact news driver, one-sided from the open, and any session where he cannot paint a simple 20-handle run.
  - Pre-set kill criteria: for the morning he said if price made a **higher high above the short-term high after sweeping the relative equal lows**, he was done and would close the stream. Otherwise by about 10:20 ET with no displacement below the low, he was done.
  - If he is in a trade on such a day he takes many more partials, because he cannot hold comfortably. On unpleasant days he may take one contract off and see how he feels, then another.
  - "High probability" is defined here as: it is very difficult to frame the other side of the market going against the trade idea. If both scenarios can be painted, it is not high probability.
- **How to identify:** one-sided grind with no real retracements; overlapping candles and tiny ranges; long consolidation; many small wick violations of arrays; heavy-news day.
- **How to use:** write down the conditions that make you not trade, and a stop-for-the-day trigger, before the session. Log these days and study them afterwards.
- **Timestamps:** [0:49:03](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=2943) — grinding days · [0:55:26](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=3326) — coping by scaling out one contract at a time · [1:25:13](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=5113) — definition of high probability · [1:29:14](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=5354) — lethargic, "swim upstream" days · [3:19:05](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=11945) — wants intraday swing-trader environment
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he stresses this is personal fit. Some students may thrive on these days. The line he adds: "you have to know your own Kryptonite."

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Breakaway gap: FVG left after a consolidation + stop hunt  (aliases: breakaway gap; "this gap should stay open")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - When price leaves a **consolidation after a stop hunt** (the stops below the range are taken, then price breaks above the range high) and leaves an FVG on the way, that gap is a **breakaway gap**. They "tend to stay open" — not always but most of the time, so it acts like real support (or resistance for the mirror case).
  - It acts as support even though price may not return to it for a long time. In this video price came back down to it only one tick short in places, and later dipped just into it.
  - **Why expect that:** the gap formed leaving the consolidation. It is not "support and resistance" (price did not need to retest a wick) and not "supply and demand" (he calls S&D a myth outside commodities); it is algorithmic delivery.
  - Contrast: other times he **wants** a gap to close, i.e. wants it to fail so it can invert (see inversion expectation). Say which you expect before the trade.
- **How to identify:** (1) a multi-bar consolidation, (2) a sweep of its low (for a long idea), (3) displacement above the consolidation high leaving an FVG, (4) a higher-timeframe target above.
- **How to use:** it is the setup for the IOFED entry (next concept). Go back through old charts: look for gaps left open after leaving a consolidation after a stop hunt and see how often they hold.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, ~10:47–10:52 ET. A 9:30-onward consolidation with a sweep of the stops below it, then a break above the range high. That left an FVG whose candle-3 low (top of the gap) was 18931.00 (as captioned). Price dropped back into the top of the gap at 10:52 without filling the lower portion, then rallied to the daily volume imbalance.
- **Timestamps:** [2:04:55](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=7495) — why he expects it to stay open · [2:08:10](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=7690) — left the consolidation after a stop hunt, gap tends to stay open · [2:25:58](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=8758) — "breakaway gap … breaking away from this consolidation" · [2:50:54](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=10254) — not classic support/resistance because price never touched the wick
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** an old idea made explicit. He says whenever he says "I want to see this one stay open / remain unfilled" in streams, this is the logic. He calls the stream remarks repeatable proof it is not cherry-picked.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Institutional Orderflow Entry Drill (IOFED)  (aliases: institutional order flow entry drill)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (re-taught; the detail is the valuable part)
- **What ICT says:**
  - IOFED is a **partial entry into a fair value gap that you believe will not fill completely**. Use it only when he (or you) says a gap should stay open/unfilled. "Unless I say that this gap should stay open … you're never looking at IOFED" — it is not the go-to for every FVG. You can still adopt it as a personal entry model.
  - **Where to fill:** the upper half of the gap. In the bullish case the gap spans candle-1 high (bottom) to candle-3 low (top). The best fills are from the **CE to the top of the gap**. The lower half is the least probable fill. If you are wrong and price trades down to the low, it usually still matters not, because the CE-to-top fill has already happened.
  - **Limit order placement:** put the limit at the candle-3 low (top of the gap) — it only takes one tick below that to fill a long — or even one tick above it. Never aim for the low end: he has had real limit orders where price traded 2 ticks past and did not fill (spread, queue), then ran without him. He asks the viewer to choose between the top of the gap and one tick above, and to accept the extra drawdown. (Exact wording on the tick offset is garbled in captions.)
  - **Stop:** below the candle-1 high (bottom of the FVG). In his example the span was about nine ticks (~2.25 NQ handles; 4 ticks = 1 handle, as captioned).
  - **Philosophy:** "low resistance barriers to entry" and "low-hanging fruit" for targets. He is "never trying to get a fill at the low end"; he does not demand precision; the spread must not be a factor.
  - **Scaling variant (his own):** first entry 6 contracts at the top of a wider gap; add 4 more when price goes into the CE/upper quadrant; add 5 more one tick below CE if it trades there (same assumption: the lower portion stays open). In his timed example: 10:47 first entry, 10:49 into CE, 10:51 one tick below CE. That is averaging into a losing position, which at least one funded-account firm (he names Topstep, Caleb's choice) does not allow. Workaround: use IOFED as the only entry and pyramid with later, higher PD arrays (order blocks and FVGs above), which that firm allows.
  - **Mirror:** he says the same applies when the array is a premium array (price trading up into it), but the sensitive area flips accordingly (mirror by implication; he does not walk it through).
- **How to identify:** a gap you expect to remain open (breakaway gap, left after a consolidation/stop hunt), a higher-timeframe target above, and price returning toward the gap.
- **How to use:** place a limit at/near the top of the gap, stop below the gap's candle-1 high, target the next array/liquidity (here the 18951.50 candle high ~20 handles, then the daily volume imbalance).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Tue 13 Aug 2024, call made around 10:47–10:50 ET: "I want this gap to stay open". 10:52 ET (inside the 10:50–11:10 macro): price dips into the top of the gap — a drop of roughly one tick — without touching the lower portion, then displaces up. Target: the high at 18951.50 (about 20 handles away) and then the daily volume imbalance whose low he ballparked near 18956 with CE near 18960 (about 30 handles total from the 18931 entry). ICT said he would only expect Caleb to aim at the CE of that daily volume imbalance. He did not trade it himself.
- **Timestamps:** [2:02:32](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=7352) — "screenshot this": any trade one tick below that low is an IOFED · [2:18:35](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=8315) — CE-to-high is the sensitive zone · [2:20:57](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=8457) — limit placement and the unfilled-limit experience · [2:29:09](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=8949) — 6 + 4 + 5 scaling and funded-account averaging rule · [2:43:41](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=9821) — targets: ~20 handles, then daily VI CE ~30 handles
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** this restates the older IOFED as a "gap should stay open" tool rather than a general OTE-style entry into any FVG. Prices as captioned are noisy. All figures in the example are approximate.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Price delivery continuum (dropping timeframes inside one run)  (aliases: "price delivery Continuum Theory" (caption unclear))
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A run that starts on one timeframe (here the 1-minute) can be dropped to the **30s / 15s / 5s** chart to find multiple entries inside that same delivery, so you are not chasing price. There is a threshold where you must stop adding — the same premise as his pyramiding lesson.
  - If price had retraced into the gap and broken down, he would have dropped to the 15-second chart and used its FVG into the target.
- **Timestamps:** [2:06:33](https://youtu.be/-WItxLARGpE?t=7593)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** only a brief mention; he says he will teach it more.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #7   August 13, 2024
head: Order block with consecutive down-closed candles; the open = change in the state of delivery  (aliases: bullish order block; CISD; "first time I taught this")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement / new teaching (he states his private-mentorship students never saw it)
- **What ICT says:**
  - An order block is **not only the last down-closed candle** before the run. When several down-closed candles are consecutive, the series is **one order block**. Count down-closed candles leftward: is there one immediately to the left? One before that? One before that? Stop when there is not.
  - The key price is the **opening price of the first (leftmost, highest) candle in the series**. That open is the **change in the state of delivery**: "the algorithm sees these three candles and goes right to that opening price". The algorithm is called back to it.
