TGIF can start forming at **1:00 pm ET Thursday** (give noon–1 pm the chance to do its thing first) and runs through Friday's close; he expects this particularly when the weekly range is elongated (larger than the last few weeks). Measured from the highest high formed by Thursday 1 pm going into Friday. If price has made the 20% retracement, and he has no trade on, he is done for the week (weekly Power of 3 has "done its work"). If a 20% retrace happens on Thursday before the close, he doesn't trade Friday at all. If TGIF doesn't form on Friday, carry it to Monday: look for the 20–30% on Monday's trading (it did that this week).
- **How to identify:** Weekly chart (September NQ contract): draw the fib from the low up to the high of the week (an up week; for down weeks reverse), toggle the 0.5 level off so only the 0.2 and 0.3 show. Quadrants are 0.25/0.75.
- **How to use:** After the 20% retracement the rest of the week/Friday becomes lackluster/"fickle": price overlaps back and forth with no sustained runs. A higher high after 20–30% retracement requires "manual intervention" (FOMC or something un-scheduled), which tends to appear at low volume. Take most of an upside trade (75–80%) off at upper levels, because you can't know when the Thursday-1 pm retracement will arrive. A 30% retracement would not change the weekly bullish bias; he says it'd be healthy.
- **Example in this video:** NQ week of Aug 12–16, 2024: two big relief rallies (Middle East de-escalation) after a two-week up move; Friday morning price retraced to the weekly 20% level (also overlapping the Thursday OR upper quadrant), then chopped back and forth for the rest of the morning; he would not engage the afternoon.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:43](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=223) 20% of weekly range plus OR upper quadrant · [0:04:31](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=271) how to draw the fib · [0:05:20](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=320) carry to Monday if not formed Friday · [1:58:09](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=7089) 20% on Thursday means avoid Friday · [2:00:39](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=7239) TGIF can form 1 pm Thursday; 20–30% from Thursday-1 pm high · [2:09:40](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=7780) take 75–80% off
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Related day-of-week notes: he doesn't trade Mondays (demands the market show him information for Tuesday's directional bias/draws), and often avoids Fridays after a big run-up; if no morning money was made on a Friday he does not go in during the afternoon.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Power of 3 applied to daily and weekly candles (retracement of 20–30%, close in upper third)  (aliases: "daily Power of Three", "weekly candlestick has done its job")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / rule (he flags it as "new information")
- **What ICT says:** On a bullish daily candle, after the objective is met, price typically retraces 20–30% of that day's range and the close tends to be in the **upper third** of the candle (not on the high). If a day does close on its high, expect a retracement or short opportunity the next day. Once the 20–30% retracement has happened, it is less likely to revisit the high; price tends to settle within the upper third. Apply the same logic to the weekly candle (this is the TGIF idea): once the retracement has occurred, the weekly candle has completed its role.
- **How to identify:** Draw a hypothetical candle: low, open, high, and close in the upper third; measure the high-to-low range for 20–30%.
- **How to use:** Don't try to extract a new high after the retracement; late-day action is small-range "not trying to make new ground".
- **Example in this video:** A crude candle diagram he drew by hand (not a real chart), mapping daily to weekly.
- **Timestamps:** [2:04:50](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=7490) hypothetical daily range · [2:05:41](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=7541) close in upper third; 20–30% retrace · [2:07:16](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=7636) same logic for weekly candle
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Not always" is his own caveat.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Lunch macro — 11:30 am to 1:30 pm ET retracement rule  (aliases: "lunch hour", "midday retrace/reversal")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The lunch hour is a two-hour window, **11:30 am–1:30 pm ET**. Whenever price has run in one direction into 11:30 (one big move or staggered), anticipate a retracement. Find the easiest relative equal low or single low in the run up **after 10:00 am** (it must be after 10:00; he is "not always looking for something before 10"); the lunch macro will retrace to that low, even if price later goes higher. Reverse logic for a down run: from 11:30 hunt setups up to the short-term high or relative equal highs formed after 10:00. Retracement is the minimum; other subtleties/macros capturing larger reversals or pyramids will be in his book. Rationale: whatever has been in motion since the start of the day (he frames the day from 7:00 am ET to 11:30) is the longest-held winning ticket, so the lunch hour runs against it; sometimes the midday retracement becomes a whole-day or weekly reversal.
- **How to identify:** Mark the relative equal lows (or the singular low) that formed between 10:00 and 11:30.
- **How to use:** Fade the morning trend toward that low/high; his Thursday short (Turtle Soup, below) was taken in this window.
- **Example in this video:** Thursday 8/15: one-sided up run; he took a short about 1.5 handles from the high in the lunch window. Friday: choppy; at 11:15 he said the morning session was about to end and the lunch macro to begin; he identified the day's low area (a "high-resistance" zone) and the longs being the longest winners as the target group for the lunch run.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:39](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=1839) lunch hour is 11:30–1:30, not 60 minutes · [0:31:27](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=1887) retrace to the easiest REL/single low after 10:00 · [0:32:17](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=1937) reverse for down runs · [1:50:48](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=6648) first part of day vs lunch hour; longs hold the longest winner
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** In lecture 9 he used the lunch macro as an 11:00–11:30 fade; here the window is formally 11:30–1:30 ET. "Don't take my word for it; go back through your charts, it's there every day."

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Macro windows around the top of the hour  (aliases: "macro 9:50–10:10", "inside the macro")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The macro is the window from 10 minutes before the top of the hour to 10 minutes after it (e.g., 9:50–10:10). When a confluence of key levels (two-day-old opening range/ORG level plus one or two other elements) and a PD array form inside this window, a good reaction is likely. Price in the first part of the morning (before 10:00) was "unorganized"; he expected cleaner delivery starting about 15 minutes before 10:00 and into the macro.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:00](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=420) inside the macro; medium-impact news at 10:00 · [0:49:23](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=2963) macro described as ±10 minutes around the top of the hour
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** 10:00 consumer sentiment was a medium-impact driver on Friday.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Observations / price-delivery measurements (tape reading journal)  (aliases: "baseline", "tally", "heat on the move", "study not trade")
body:
- **Kind:** process / refinement
- **What ICT says:** While watching price live, state what you expect it to do, then write down: the time you observed it, the time it took to reach the level or to close over (count 1m candles), how much heat (adverse movement) there was, and whether it ever came back to take the low/high before delivering. Do it after the fact on recordings too if you can't watch live. Keep a daily tally of how many opportunities you saw in real time with no help; early on it will be near zero, weeks later 3–4 a session, by year-end many; the ratio of correct to incorrect will drift to about half and half, and after that the failures diminish. Record failures honestly and study them; do not "pretend it never happened" because no button was pushed. Do not attempt this on live money.
- **How to identify:** An observation = an FVG/PD array that, if it holds, suggests a draw to a specific level (e.g., a new day opening gap), plus an explicit target.
- **How to use:** Minimum thresholds: **ES 5 handles**; **NQ at least 10 handles, he prefers 15**; and in framing a trade he wants a **range of at least 20 handles** from where it could begin to where it could draw (a "minimum range for targeting purposes"); if 20 handles are available, 10–15 is reasonable to capture. Don't demand a trade pan out to the full target.
- **Example in this video:** Friday NQ 1m: an FVG formed 10:22, price moved in favor for 9 minutes (until 10:31), could not get above the high, and a stop would have been hit at 10:37; he logs this as a failed first data point. Second example: a gap that became an inversion FVG and rallied toward the NDOG; count the candles on the 1m chart and note whether heat occurred, and whether price returned to take the low before the run.
- **Timestamps:** [0:57:01](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=3421) record the time observed and time to deliver · [0:58:37](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=3517) daily tally and baseline · [1:09:04](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=4144) worked example: 10:22 FVG, 9 minutes, stopped 10:37 · [1:14:36](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=4476) ES 5 handles, NQ 10 to 15 · [2:26:41](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=8801) 20-handle minimum NQ range
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He frames this as what a student should do for weeks before pressing a demo button; the numbers are thresholds for study, not signals.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Fair Value Gap entry framework for beginners  (aliases: "Caleb's model", "BISI/SIBI", "volume imbalance", "institutional order flow entry drill")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:** Caleb's entry model is a fair value gap used **only when there is an obvious draw on liquidity**: buy **one tick below the high of a discount (bullish) FVG**; sell short **one tick above the low of a bearish FVG**. He chose the FVG because it's the easiest to see, not because it is the best. He calls a candle that trades into a gap without closing it an "institutional order flow entry drill" (the marker to start). In another example he used the **high of the gap plus one tick** as the limit because it is the easiest to get filled (using the CE or low of the gap would never have filled), with the stop below the candle's open/low of the volume imbalance. He prefers the gap to stay partly open.
- **How to identify:** Clear displacement leaving a single FVG/volume imbalance, with a candle that wicks or trades into it without closing it.
- **How to use:** Entry at the gap's near edge ±1 tick; stop just beyond the gap-forming candle; first partial at the first threshold (10 handles in his example); define the Terminus (see below).
- **Example in this video:** Friday NQ 1m: "that candle would be institutional order flow entry drill because it goes below these candles but doesn't close that gap in"; a 10-handle run to a prior high would be taken; the larger target (relative equal highs) is optional.
- **Timestamps:** [0:54:36](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=3276) institutional order flow entry drill, wick over NDOG · [1:16:12](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=4572) marker to start; 10 handles then out · [2:28:21](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=8901) fill at gap high plus one tick; stop below the candle · [3:17:18](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=11838) the stated Caleb entry rule
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicit about not wanting anyone to think the FVG is the only/best entry; next week's lectures will build "elements of entry", tape-reading what price should and should not do.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Inversion Fair Value Gap (iFVG) mechanics  (aliases: "reclaim", "treat it as an inversion gap")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** A bearish FVG becomes an inversion FVG when a candle **closes above** it; then a **new candle** must come back down and touch it (the high, CE, or low of the gap); a single candle cannot do both. A wick spiking above does not count as the close. Once touched, price can use it as support and rally ("treat it as an inversion FVG as it did here, then sent it higher"). Reverse for bearish. He wants it to "stay open", i.e., not be completely closed.
- **How to identify:** Close beyond the gap, then a retest by a following candle; the touch can be as deep as the low of the gap.
- **How to use:** In a bearish context he lists a very nice confluence: iFVG + a bearish FVG + bearish order block, where the order block is the candle with the highest up-close inside the FVG and the iFVG (not the more obvious-looking one). Test the wick: if price trades up but does not touch the midpoint of the gap/wick, that is weak (bearish); if it trades up and prints a volume imbalance, that could be an entry.
- **Example in this video:** Friday NQ 1m: an orange FVG: "see it go above it, close above it, open a new candle" then touch it; a second gap with a body inside and a tail down was acceptable; a wick-up into a gap that fails to reach the midpoint was called weak.
- **Timestamps:** [1:17:02](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=4622) iFVG: gap taken, comes back, touches · [1:20:29](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=4829) bearish order block inside both gaps; wick must not touch the midpoint · [2:24:44](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=8684) must close a candle beyond, start a new candle, then touch · [2:38:00](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=9480) close above, new candle, then touch
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Consistent with lecture 9's "wick may enter but body must stay inside" but here the requirement is the close-beyond/new-candle-retest sequence.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Terminus, partials and the 50% rule  (aliases: "running down equity" (caption unclear), "first threshold")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** **Terminus** is where you think the trade will draw to; frame the start and the Terminus before taking anything. Inside a range, look for short-term lows/highs (single or relative equal) and any inefficiency (as in market maker buy/sell models); choose the easiest to get to (top, CE, or low of a gap) and don't demand the halfway point or the low. For partials: in a long, if there is a short-term high **at least 50% of the way** to your target and price takes it out even once, take a partial there (he presents this as a rule his private students know); the stop on the balance stays beyond. Don't take a partial just because you are up $500 and afraid (emotional); define the first threshold that must be breached first. His own scaling: 15 contracts, peel 5 at the first target and trail the stop; get 10 to 15 handles as the typical second partial; move the stop to cover costs/commissions if the full 20 doesn't come.
- **How to identify:** First short-term high (or low) located beyond halfway to the target.
- **How to use:** Log the time at entry (candle 1), partial (e.g., minute 5), stopped on the balance (minute 9), and the distance (about 10 handles including spread in and out).
- **Example in this video:** Friday NQ 1m, a hypothetical (not a live trade) logging exercise on the 10:22 FVG: the earlier high sat beyond the halfway point; price passed it once, so the partial is taken there; the balance is stopped about 9 minutes into the setup.
- **Timestamps:** [1:24:29](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=5069) Terminus; easiest short-term low/inefficiency · [2:34:00](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=9240) the 50% short-term high rule · [2:35:38](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=9338) distance and time data · [2:36:25](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=9385) rules vs emotional partials
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says private students know the "running down equity" name and he is unsure he'd said it publicly; the phrase is caption-unclear.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: High-resistance liquidity run and the "maximum carnage" low-of-day sweep
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** An area that price has traded in many times (multiple legs straight down, then reversal) is hard to trade through; a sell-off through it is a **high-resistance liquidity run**. But if price takes the day's low aggressively with speed, taking out everybody, that is "maximum carnage" and not a high-resistance run, especially on a Friday after a huge up week where even a 30% weekly retracement would not alter the bullish backdrop.
- **How to use:** Identify the lows where the day's longs (the longest winners) hold stops; if the lunch macro takes the low with speed, expect continuation lower into the close.
- **Example in this video:** Friday NQ 1m: price was drifting around a prior low area in the late morning (about 11:15–11:20 ET by his clock comments); he wanted any move below it to be quick, not drifting; the relative equal highs above were the alternative.
- **Timestamps:** [1:49:57](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=6597) high-resistance run defined · [1:52:25](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=6745) maximum carnage; speed or not · [1:53:12](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=6792) 30% weekly retrace would be healthy
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Applies the High/Low Resistance Liquidity Run concept to a chop day (previously taught for trending conditions).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Draw on liquidity: which relative equal high is valid, and how he'd engineer the sweep
body:
- **Kind:** example / refinement
- **What ICT says:** He walks through which highs count as valid relative equal highs (each high he points at is higher than the one to its right; audio is hard to follow, caption unclear) and compares the nearby relative equal lows (one is lower than its neighbour, so less clean); he concludes the buy-side is the more probable draw. His hypothetical "if I were running it": push through the "590" level, sweep the "601" level (later "601.50") with a wick only (no body), then slam below and take the low of day, keeping the weekly high in play and sweeping the day-session high. The drop would be fast and furious, not fuzzy, trapping shorts who are profitable and anyone with stops at the low. At the end of the session he again said he would sink it to the low of the day into the close (not a prediction).
- **How to identify:** (levels as captioned: "590", "601", "592", "60150"; leading digits not captioned)
- **How to use:** Treat clean, smooth levels as magnets; spikes through them can be quick.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Fri 8/16, about 11:45 ET (by stream clock): price near the NDOG and the relative equal highs; he asked which is easier, the liquidity above the REH or all the way back down.
- **Timestamps:** [2:19:14](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=8354) which is easier, REH or lows · [2:20:02](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=8402) which REH is valid · [2:21:07](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=8467) how he would run it · [2:46:09](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=9969) sink it to the low of the day into the close

head: Don't use ICT's publicly drawn levels as your stop or liquidity  (aliases: "easy target", "pair of orders")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Do not put your stop where he said "this is where the stop would be" — with tens of thousands following live, you create an easy target that can be run (open the spreads, push a button). Learn to read it yourself. A level that is too smooth can be run: he imagines paired orders at the smooth level to engage stops just above it.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #10  August 16, 2024
head: Clean vs. unorganized ("sloppy", "fickle/thickle", "picket fence") price action  (aliases: "choppy day", "one-sided train day")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / filter
- **What ICT says:** A day or session is *clean* if you see impulsive legs leaving a singular FVG, a singular short-term low, a run to an obvious level, a retracement with a single FVG, and a quick move to another obvious level. If not, don't push hard and demand more conviction. *Unorganized/sloppy*: overlapping candles ("picket fence"), balanced price range with no speed, many little gaps and highs/lows but no obvious side; it's usually the day when people "get chopped up". Wait for displacement; once an inefficiency exists, watch how price reacts when it returns into it. A **one-sided "train"** day (like Thursday and Tuesday) is the other bad environment: don't chase; get in before it starts or stay out; hold and be out of the way. Explanatory apple analogy: with one green apple among reds your eye finds it; with many reds you get distracted — clean = only one obvious draw.
- **How to use:** Screenshot examples of both and label them; avoid 8:30 news for beginners (he told Caleb to wait until after). On a choppy Friday: do your one setup and be done.
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:51](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=1791) one-sided train day (Thursday) · [0:46:11](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=2771) apples analogy · [1:38:31](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=5911) criteria for a clean day · [1:54:02](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=6842) picket fence · [1:44:12](https://youtu.be/qoNQfVzVXZQ?t=6252) balanced price range, no speed
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Fickle = overlapping, sputtering; occurs after the weekly 20% retracement.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Caleb's model (the beginner framework / learning ladder)  (aliases: "Caleb's entry mechanism", "Caleb's model", "session draw on liquidity first")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model + curriculum (new coinage)
- **What ICT says:** He is deliberately forcing his son (a beginner who cannot yet determine the draw on liquidity) to use ONE entry mechanism, the fair value gap, inside order-flow context (price, not level 2 / DOM / volume profile). The aim is a baseline understanding of price action. The FVG may later lead him to see order blocks, breakers and inversion FVGs. It "should not necessarily be yours", and ICT says it does not matter which PD array you start with (order block, OTE, etc.) as long as you start and watch price daily.
- **How to identify / the steps as taught:**
  1. Outline liquidity above and below: relative equal highs and lows. Caleb only looks to the right of 7:00 ET, i.e. the last two hours before 9:00-9:30. Advanced students may also use the London range and Power-of-3 context from earlier teaching.
  2. Mark gap references: RTH opening range gap, new week opening gap, the nearest new day opening gap(s).
  3. Do not trade the first 30 minutes (opening range, 9:30-10:00). Watch which side of the liquidity is taken first. ("Water disturbed, jagged" = the taken side; smooth = the untouched side.)
  4. The side taken FIRST is the trap (Judas swing). The second side is the draw. ICT frames it with the Bible line "the first shall be last".
  5. After the first side is taken, wait for price to reclaim a reference (e.g. back above an old NDOG), then enter on a fair value gap using IOFED (see below).
  6. Take partials at an easy, low-threshold target (e.g. lower quadrant of the NWOG).
  7. Graduated later steps: hold through lunch and close at about 1:30 if in profit; eventually frame the full day (open-to-low zone) and then daily bias from weekly/monthly. He says you cannot derive daily bias until you can read the session draw.
- **How to use:** Session draws on liquidity are "dynamic" (exist above and below). Learn session bias first, then daily bias.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Aug 19: relative equal highs sit above, relative equal lows below. Price takes the sell side first after 9:30, sweeps below old lows and an old NDOG, then reclaims and runs to the buy side and NWOG.
- **Timestamps:** [1:32:04](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=5524) session draws are dynamic, learn this before daily bias · [1:46:27](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=6387) only look back two hours from 9:00 to 7:00 · [2:08:13](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=7693) take first side, second comes later · [2:29:47](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=8987) graduated steps: lunch hold, close at 1:30
- **Nuance / caveats:** He says repeatedly that he is not calling a bias in advance ("I'm not calling that, I'm looking for reasons to hunt a setup"). He lays out what he'd want to see and what would invalidate it. He also notes that experienced students can fold in London and pre-7:00 data. Caleb should not.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Opening range (first 30 minutes, 9:30-10:00 ET)  (aliases: initial opening range)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule
- **What ICT says:** The opening range is 30 minutes (9:30-10:00 ET), not 15 minutes. Anything that says a 15-minute opening range is "a gimmick to look different". Beginners are best served taking NO entries in this window. Sitting still teaches discipline and patience and filters out the fake setups you would chase impulsively.
- **How to identify:** Vertical line at 10:00 ET. Mark the high/low of 9:30-10:00 as liquidity on both extremes (buy side above, sell side below).
- **How to use:** Watch which extreme is taken first; the other becomes the draw. Observation at 1:47:20: price found responsiveness at the midpoint of the opening range (gap) and could not get into its upper half, so he sent viewers back to the 7:00 liquidity.
- **Example in this video:** Early in the session price respected the opening range, failed to reach the 3/4 (upper quadrant) of the RTH opening range gap, then swept down.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:39](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=1179) 30-minute opening range, no 15-minute version · [1:41:39](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=6099) wait the first 30 minutes for the damage to be done, "you're going to see it at 10 o'clock"
- **Nuance / caveats:** The 10:00 fair value gap in the example is described as a Silver Bullet-type gap (1:20:06), i.e. the 10:00-11:00 window.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: RTH Opening Range Gap (and RTH vs ETH awareness)  (aliases: opening range gap, ORG)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + refinement
- **What ICT says:** The opening range gap is the difference between the regular-session settlement (4:15 pm ET on the prior day; the last tick is the "close") and the 9:30 ET regular-trading-hours opening price. He explains the session mechanics: electronic trading continues until 5:00 pm ET, stops, and resumes at 6:00 pm ET on a normal day. On Friday (or a holiday) it does not resume until Sunday 6:00 pm ET. On an RTH chart there is no candle at 4:15, so the next candle is Monday 9:30.
- **How to identify:** Anchor one edge at the prior-day 4:15 pm settlement (Friday Aug 16 here) and the other at the 9:30 open. Draw a fib on the low and high to get quadrants (lower quadrant, consequent encroachment, upper quadrant). Shade it.
- **How to use:** Price uses the gap's quadrants as reaction levels: "found footing" off the lower quadrant, support at the midpoint, "bodies staying inside" while it grinds. Spending too long inside the gap means they are "not in a hurry" to pierce the high. What he wants to see for upside: a close above the gap's CE, then a next candle that comes down and fails to touch the CE, then a spring toward the upper quadrant (0:25:58).
- **Example in this video:** Price came back up about three-quarters of the gap early (just short of the upper quadrant), later respected the CE and the high repeatedly. Bodies stayed inside, wicks overshot. Candle pokes above the high did not close above it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:13](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=1033) what makes it the opening range gap · [0:18:02](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=1082) 4:15 pm settlement, 5:00/6:00 restart rules · [0:55:11](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=3311) RTH vs ETH toggle warning
- **Nuance / caveats:** (My inference from his remarks) The ORG's high edge is Friday's 4:15 pm settlement (19,604), which is also the NWOG's low edge, so the pink ORG sat just below the NWOG; price had to climb through it to reach the NWOG low/lower quadrant. ICT warns he has mis-weighted a level before because ETH vs RTH was toggled on the chart. His habit is to say aloud "I'm back in electronic trading hours" and then confirm the chart label reads ETH.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG)  (aliases: new week opening gap, NWOG high/low/CE)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + refinement
- **What ICT says:** NWOG = Friday's settlement price (the last tick/close) vs. Sunday's 6:00 pm ET opening tick. Whichever is higher is the NWOG high, whichever is lower is the NWOG low. Annotate it as "New Week Opening Gap August 18 2024". A viewer asked why the gap isn't measured lower; he answers that the last tick is the close and that is what you anchor to. In this video Friday's settlement is 19,604 (NQ) and the gap is just under 20 handles (exact edges garbled, caption unclear).
- **How to identify:** Use the 1-minute chart to calibrate the exact settlement and open prints. Drop a fib on the gap low and high for CE, lower quadrant (25%) and upper quadrant (75%). Extend it forward.
- **How to use:** The NWOG is "highly influential ... like a black hole", and price gravitates to it. "If you don't extend the new week opening gaps on your chart and keep them on there for a few weeks you're trading blind." It is a PD array that can serve as a draw once you have identified the nearest liquidity. See *Target selection* below.
- **Example in this video:** Early: price comes back up to the NWOG low and reacts off the lower quadrant of the opening range gap (0:11:28). Later: price runs from the IOFED entry to the NWOG low, then CE and the NWOG high, with bodies respecting each level. The pre-7:00 exit target was the NWOG's lower quadrant (see Target selection).
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:22](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=442) calibrate Friday close and Sunday open on the 1-minute chart · [3:08:50](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=11330) how to define the NWOG high/low · [3:40:25](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=13225) keep NWOGs on the chart for weeks
- **Nuance / caveats:** "Nothing gets stale around here": older gaps (NDOG/NWOG) remain relevant.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: New Day Opening Gap (NDOG) as a sell-side reach  (aliases: new day opening gap, NDOG, old NDOG)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / example
- **What ICT says:** When you ask "how far below the sell-side liquidity can price reach?", look for an old NDOG below. Here the Friday Aug 16 NDOG is the outer limit. Price can trade through an old NDOG; ICT says he is not demanding a precision stop-and-turn there. What matters is how price behaves after it trades through (it can go through the low and wick). He teaches to use the specific NDOG whose bodies show respect: "I'm going to refer to this one" over a lower one that did not respond.
- **How to use:** Mark both the NDOG high and low on the chart and the mid-level; expect a retrace to its high at least after a reclaim. Specifically he wanted price to get back above the NDOG, drop to the NDOG high (touch or fail to touch), then run, and not to see a close below the CE of the low-wick on the closing basis.
- **Example in this video:** After the first sweep below the equal lows, price trades down into the Aug 16 NDOG, rallies back, reclaims it and trades down only to the NDOG high, then runs up. Reaction at the NDOG high, then the IOFED gap forms.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:19](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=739) NDOG as the reach on the sell side · [0:50:27](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=3027) price can trade through old gaps, see how it behaves · [2:00:06](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=7206) which low/NDOG the algorithm refers back to
- **Nuance / caveats:** Referred to as an "old, stale" gap by viewers. ICT rejects that framing.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Quadrants, consequent encroachment and wicks treated as gaps  (aliases: CE, upper/lower quadrant, "wicks are gaps")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Any range or gap (NWOG, opening range gap, a candle wick, a fair value gap) is measured in quadrants: low, lower quadrant (25%), CE (50%), upper quadrant (75%), high. A wick can be "treated like a gap": half of the wick is its consequent encroachment. Price often stops at the quadrant rather than the CE. Example: the sweep low stopped exactly (to the tick) at the upper quadrant of the first wick and never touched the midpoint of that wick or of the lesser wick.
- **How to use:**
  - Not touching CE is a strength tell: if you are long and price cannot even dip into a level that "could" support it, it is immediate feedback that price wants to go higher. ICT calls this a paradigm shift. Support does not "push" price; the failure to reach it is the information.
  - Bodies versus wicks: bodies closing at a level matter; wicks are "allowed to do the damage".
  - Conditions he states: "no close below the midpoint of the wick", "I'd like to see this stay open", "OK for the candle to touch while open as long as it doesn't close below".
- **Example in this video:** Wick CE of a 1-minute candle watched from the 15-second chart; price came down toward it and did not touch it, then rallied (3:15:10). His recorded pre-7:00 market-order entry went in as price dropped into the CE of a 1-minute wick treated as a gap (2:55:12), coinciding with the 15-second gap plus order block (3:14:22).
- **Timestamps:** [0:52:03](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=3123) sweep low stops at the upper quadrant of the wick, not its CE · [2:55:12](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=10512) wicks are gaps, CE of the wick · [3:02:30](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=10950) why not touching a support level is the signal
- **Nuance / caveats:** He contrasts this with support/resistance thinking ("support ain't pushing anything").

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Candles are still forming: let wicks happen  (aliases: wicks outside the lines)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / psychology
- **What ICT says:** A wick can only form because a candle is first a full-bodied candle at the extreme of the wick. While a candle is open and forming, price can trade outside a gap's boundary or level. That is normal. Do not demand price stay inside the lines. When ICT first showed Caleb an FVG, Caleb assumed price would fill exactly to the middle and never go outside, and was alarmed by a candle coloring outside the gap's low. ICT compares it to a child coloring outside the lines: not a failure.
- **How to use:** Judge the level on the close, not on intra-candle excursions. Give the candle room to form its wick or you will be "humbled fast" and lose trust in reading price.
- **Timestamps:** [0:47:14](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=2834) Caleb's fair value gap story · [0:48:48](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=2928) "no close below it, can touch it" · [1:43:14](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=6194) coloring outside the lines analogy (approx.)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Institutional Order Flow Entry Drill (IOFED)  (aliases: "institutional order flow entry drill", "entry drill", Caleb's entry mechanism)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (this lecture's core)
- **What ICT says:**
  - A fair value gap is formed during a displacement move. While the displacement candle is still forming you anticipate the FVG. Once the next candle opens, you drop a buy limit at the gap's high edge (the top of a bullish FVG, i.e. the low of the third candle) plus ONE tick. That assures a fill. You do not try to buy the low end of the gap or its midpoint.
  - The expectation: price retraces into the gap and goes a tick or so below the reference candle's low, "leaving a portion of the gap open" (does not close the whole FVG), then displaces higher. Each FVG used "as a propellant" should stay at least partly open; the failure to fill completely is the signature of strength ("cracks in order flow").
  - The gap can fill completely and still be a valid trade; you just take more drawdown. From the candle high ~19,576.75 to low ~19,580.50 he quotes "five handles or so" (his figure; captions unclear) as the extra risk, plus commissions.
  - Sizing the fill logic: he has had limit orders not filled even when price traded to the level, with real brokers too, so always include the +1 tick.
- **How to identify:** 1) Displacement after the first side of liquidity is taken. 2) A fresh FVG forming on the candle that is still open. 3) Price first reclaimed a reference (NDOG, a prior low/wick) so you are on the right side. 4) You want to see it NOT close the gap and NOT close below the CE of the relevant wick.
- **How to use:** Entry: limit at gap high + 1 tick. Stop: below the swing/wick lows where price has been "traveling back and forth" (he does not give a fixed number of ticks; e.g. below the wick-low area and the lower low). Targets: first threshold = NWOG low (he calls it the first threshold), then CE, then upper quadrant, and he expects a pierce through the NWOG high because there are stops resting at the smooth highs. Take partials at the low-threshold target. Preplacing limit orders "100-some handles away" and dragging them in when you expect a Silver Bullet-type FVG is a practical tip (1:19:19).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Mon Aug 19, about 10:20-10:25 ET (derived from the video clock; he calls it a 10:00-window/Silver Bullet-type FVG): price sweeps equal lows, runs into the Aug 16 NDOG low area, reclaims and closes above, drops to the NDOG high, then a displacement candle forms. While it is forming ICT says the FVG will form and that price will dip about one tick below the candle low. Result: dip of two ticks to about 19,580.00, then a second dip to about 19,578.50. Net drawdown versus the 19,580.50 reference = 2 handles = 8 ticks = $40 per NQ contract. The gap's lower portion stayed open (low did not reach the candle high 19,576.75). Price then rallies to the NWOG low, CE and upper area and pushes through the NWOG high with energy. Later he wicks through the buy-side highs but admits surprise that they were not cleanly taken (he had thought the first punch was the real run). He admits he was off on the dip ("expected one tick, got two" and, by the $40 figure, two handles).
- **Timestamps:** [1:04:46](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=3886) FVG below the wick, leave a portion open · [1:09:38](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=4178) limit price and drawdown math (8 ticks, $40) · [1:22:31](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=4951) buy the high of the gap plus one tick · [1:32:52](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=5572) what if it closes the gap · [2:00:54](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=7254) called before it formed, not closed, "off to the races"
- **Gaps as a strength gauge (1:28:07):** whenever a PD array such as a gap is not traded to, or is not completely overlapped, that tells you about the strength of the underlying move.
- **Nuance / caveats:** ICT notes he is not forcing every student to use it. He says people "prematurely teaching" his concepts say to buy the low end of the gap for a tiny stop. He says that precision is not needed; where the market will draw matters more. He admits he cannot always get fills at the exact tick and treats the tick buffer as essential. Quote-worthy: "I want to see these little cracks in orderflow." Price quotes in this section come from garbled captions.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Order block, rejection block, breaker and "actual gap" as used here
body:
- **Kind:** example only / light refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Order block: the down-closed candle ("means absolutely nothing" to others) before the up-move; its high (~19,591.25) is traded above by the next candle. He notes that a pyramid add at the low of the candle above it would have missed its fill by one tick.
  - Rejection block: "the lowest down-close candle in the swing"; the sweep cleared it and stopped.
  - Bullish breaker: the last up-close candle in a range after a retracement breaks to the upside. Price trades down into it and then shifts structure.
  - "Actual gap" with an order block: an actual open/close gap (no overlap) following a down-close candle while you are bullish is a strong PD array: as soon as price trades into it, it is a buy. Even without the order block it is still an FVG. Gaps are also classed as breakaway vs common (common gaps can fill in; he labels a green level a breakaway because price never retraced into it).
- **Example in this video:** The pre-7:00 trade: a gap with an order block after a down-close candle; he bought at market as price slammed into it (3:14:22-3:15:10). The 15-second sequence showed MSS, breaker, FVG and CE together (3:25:43-3:26:31).
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:13](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=2533) rejection block cleared · [1:08:51](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=4131) order block high 19,591.25 · [3:14:22](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=11662) actual gap plus order block is a strong PD array · [2:51:15](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=10275) every retracement that breaks upward gives a bullish breaker

head: Immediate rebalance
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule (on-side indicator)
- **What ICT says:** A big down-close candle followed immediately by a candle that opens and goes right back up to the previous candle (before the down close, or the larger-range candle). He calls it one of the best on-side indicators you could get, provided liquidity has not already been taken. He adds that if he were short he would pyramid on a retest of that candle's low and look for speed through it, then treat that as the first partial (captions ambiguous about direction).
- **Example in this video:** 15-second chart, second drop inside the opening range: institutional order flow entry drill, then an almost immediate rebalance up to the pre-drop candle.
- **Timestamps:** [3:24:05](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=12245)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Balanced Price Range on the 15-second chart ("brick wall")  (aliases: BPR)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:** Where one candle's range and an adjacent candle's range are passed through in both directions (down once, back up once), that overlap box is a balanced price range. Price is expected to respect its far edge like a brick wall. In the example a single 15-second candle passed down through the previous candle's range and a single candle passed back up, so the region was offered in both directions. A trading-range analogy: price that has traversed a defined range in both directions needs something significant to go beyond it.
- **How to use:** Do not expect price to trade below the BPR low when you are long. A BPR that gives way = "manual intervention" ("the hand in the mix is the market maker"). The Matrix "black cat deja vu" analogy: change in the pattern means something changed behind the scenes, so step aside.
- **Example in this video:** 15-sec chart: price drops from the 1-minute inefficiency into the BPR, does not take out the BPR low, then rallies; later retracements into the BPR leave it intact. (His geometric explanation is hard to follow in the captions.)
- **Timestamps:** [3:29:38](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=12578) BPR defined on the 15-second chart · [3:34:02](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=12842) failing BPR means intervention · [3:36:25](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=12985) tracking: price goes into it but not past it
- **Nuance / caveats:** He says he does not know a book term for this and "had to come up with a way to describe it". He also notes that a BPR on 15s can look like a plain wick on the 1-minute.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Price delivery continuum (time-frame hierarchy, sub-minute charts)  (aliases: "price delivery Continuum theory", matrix of time frames)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / concept
- **What ICT says:** Identify the PD array on a higher time frame, then use the lower time frame to execute. A 1-minute chart is the "higher time frame" for 5s/15s/30s/45s charts, but only a mild one; it is itself subordinate to the 5-minute and 15-minute. Do your initial study on 15m, 5m and 1m for a solid base. He watches a continuum from weekly, daily, 4H, 3H, 2H, 1H, 30m, 15m, down to 5/4/3/2/1 minute and sub-minute, because the algorithm "cycles down and then right back up through the time frames".
- **How to use:**
  - Measure each PD array on the time frame it exists on (a 15-second imbalance may not exist on the 1-minute).
  - The higher time frame PD arrays supporting the trade keep confidence up; as price moves away from a 15m/5m PD array, your focus drops to lower frames; the 1-minute PD arrays stay "hawkish" in focus while you work on sub-minute.
  - Speed is a perception: a 15-second chart moves no faster than an hourly chart. Magnitude of a move is set by the time of day it begins, not by the chart time frame. 15-second charts only give more opportunities to engage.
  - Do not always expect the same gaps on a 15-second chart as on the 1-minute.
- **Example in this video:** The 1-minute wick CE + displacement shown on the 15-second chart: the 15-second FVG (a different shade) sits inside the 1-minute gap and must stay open; the 15-second breaker, MSS and BPR line up with the 1-minute logic.
- **Timestamps:** [2:46:47](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=10007) anchor sub-minute charts to a higher time frame · [2:53:38](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=10418) the continuum from weekly to sub-minute · [3:00:51](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=10851) moving away from HTF PD arrays · [3:22:28](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=12148) magnitude is set by time, not time frame

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Relative equal highs/lows: validity rule and the 7:00-9:00 look-back  (aliases: relative equal highs, relative equal lows, REH/REL)
body:
- **Kind:** rule + refinement ("from this 2024 mentorship")
- **What ICT says:**
  - A valid relative equal high is a high that has a slightly LOWER high to the right of it. That is where liquidity is most likely tapped. A high slightly higher to the right can still be traded through; if it only wicks above and the bodies stay below, the earlier high is still a valid relative equal high and price will go into the wick. You then need to see price trade above and close with speed and magnitude.
  - Look-back window for Caleb: only from 7:00 ET onward. If you start watching at 9:00, look back just the last two hours (7:00-9:00).
  - Buy stops rest above those highs (shorts protect with buy stops); sell stops below lows. You don't need a book map/DOM to know that.
- **How to use:** Mark the equal highs and lows, wait for one side to be taken; note which was taken first. In this video the early run took the sell side first; the buy side was left intact and was the draw. Equal-lows sweep went to the left-most/lowest of the cluster (use the lowest swing low as the reference).
- **Example in this video:** Equal highs sit above (the 9:00 high is "lower than that one" so it qualifies). After 9:30 price takes the sell side first.
- **Timestamps:** [1:46:27](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=6387) 7:00 start, two-hour look-back · [2:56:01](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=10561) validation rule for equal highs · [3:04:54](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=11094) buy stops above highs

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: First side taken = the Judas swing; engineering liquidity
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:** The side offered first (the "wrong" side, the "primrose path") is the trap. Retail sells the drop; their stops sit above; then price runs the stops. Who made money so far (shorts) is who gets squeezed. Longs from a low are "unseated" by a sweep of the low. After the sell-side is taken, the move up is predominantly the draw. Smooth means resting liquidity; jagged is where it has been run.
- **How to use:** Do not trade the first side. After sell-side is taken, look for a reclaim of a reference (e.g. old NDOG) and a pullback that holds above a wick CE; enter via IOFED.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Aug 19: shorts profit early, price drops to take lows (down to ~19,544.5, caption unclear), reclaims the Aug 16 NDOG, runs to take buy stops over the equal highs and into the NWOG.
- **Timestamps:** [1:44:03](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=6243) engineering liquidity · [1:53:43](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=6823) Judas swing = the wrong side first · [2:28:12](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=8892) Judas goat analogy

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Target selection: draw, then the easiest low-threshold exit  (aliases: low-hanging objective, lowest quadrant exit)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Steps for "where is price drawing to": (1) find the relative equal highs/lows; (2) ask how far beyond them price can reach; (3) find a NDOG/NWOG beyond them, because that is where it gravitates; (4) if it is in close proximity use it and, if the range permits, break the gap into quadrants; (5) the lowest quadrant (lower quadrant of the gap you reach into) is the easiest threshold to exit profitably. He wants a barrier that is the lowest possible to profit from, not a "lofty" target.
  - You cannot use the NWOG low as the target when the buy stops (equal highs) sit above it. Price must go through the equal highs, so the exit is just above the highs, i.e. the NWOG's lower quadrant.
  - Fills: a limit exit at a level needs price to trade one tick through, and sometimes does not fill even when price touches. He sets the exit one tick beyond where he wants price to reach and takes "a steady diet" of easy targets.
- **Example in this video:** Pre-7:00 NQ trade: entry at market into the gap/order block, rally to the lower quadrant of the NWOG (~19,610.25, caption unclear; another quoted level "19,618" is garbled). Stated ordering from low: NWOG low (19,604), the buy-side/equal-high "blue line" slightly above it, then the lower quadrant, then CE. He exits one tick through the quadrant and says he raised the target to it as price approached.
- **Timestamps:** [3:06:28](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=11188) NWOG low is not usable because the buy stops sit above · [3:08:50](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=11330) how far beyond equal highs? look for NWOG/NDOG · [3:12:01](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=11521) why he picks the easiest barrier · [3:19:12](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=11952) logic restated with the exit price

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Power of 3 open-to-low zone for a bullish day  (aliases: Judas swing range, open to low range, classic buy day)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / teaching diagram
- **What ICT says:** He sketches a daily open-high-low-close bar (open at 9:30, close at about 4:15 pm). On a bullish day the initial drop from the opening price to the day's low is the fake move/Judas swing where smart money buys. Caleb is not expected to buy the exact low; he hunts for a long anywhere inside the range between the open and the low (e.g. IOFED inside that zone), then holds toward lunch. Measure where a lunch-macro retracement could go and do not keep the stop within reach of it. Eventually, if you are bullish from monthly/weekly, you buy at the open or below it.
  - Days that close near the high: the last hour makes the extreme and comes off a little before the close. The classic buy day just closes up near high, not necessarily one way.
  - He built the lesson in response to paid students who said they can't participate in a classic buy day if the low forms before 9:30 (an 8:30 entry he cannot teach from a 9:30 stream).
- **Story:** Larry Williams said he could not find how to buy below the opening price, so he bought strength above the open; ICT's Power-of-3 work is the answer to that. (Used as motivation, not a rule.)
- **Example in this video:** The 1-minute IOFED gap sits inside the open-to-low zone (box shaded blue on the chart at 3:25:43).
- **Timestamps:** [2:09:52](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=7792) daily bar diagram · [2:12:18](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=7938) open to low = Judas swing, where smart money buys · [2:14:37](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=8077) hold toward lunch, measure the retrace · [2:21:02](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=8462) the gap lives inside open-to-low · [2:24:12](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=8652) buying at or below the open when bullish
- **Nuance / caveats:** He says he is not predicting the close; this is practice for holding trades. The same logic is fractal (weekly, monthly, 5-second).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Old highs and old lows as PD arrays (after they are broken)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** After price trades above an old high and retraces back down to it, the old high is a discount array: he says "old highs are the highest discount array; old lows are the lowest premium array" (he first misspoke and corrected himself). Every time price breaches a PD array, look back at the range just traveled, map every PD array in it, and check whether any were left untouched ("did you miss a PD array not traded to? did it disregard it? That's a good thing, it means you're on side").
- **Example in this video:** The old relative equal high, after being traded above, was used as a discount array on the retracement.
- **Timestamps:** [3:38:47](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=13127) old highs vs old lows as arrays · [3:39:37](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=13177) un-traded PD arrays mean you are on the right side

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Partials, stops and holding trades  (aliases: partial profits, trade management)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / psychology
- **What ICT says:** Take partials at the first easy threshold. Do not trail to flatten or "lock in" prematurely during a choppy week. Giving back 60% of open profit with no partial off is uncomfortable. How to hold: you grow confident when gaps stay partly open, CE is not touched, and PD arrays you expected are not traded to. He still takes stops ("it's not a panacea"). Holding through lunch is a later skill; in profit, plan to close at about 1:30.
- **Example in this video:** After the IOFED entry, partials at the NWOG low then CE then upper quadrant; he would pyramid (add) on an immediate rebalance only if short and liquidity untouched.
- **Timestamps:** [0:23:36](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=1416) 60% giveback without partials · [1:05:34](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=3934) how to hold trades and confidence · [2:24:12](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=8652) why partials: you don't know when it will turn

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Jackson Hole week characteristics  (aliases: Jackson Hole Symposium behavior)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / day-of-week-style seasonal tendency
- **What ICT says:** During Jackson Hole week (Aug 19-23 here; Powell expected to speak several times, Wed-Fri volatile) price delivers with a lot of overlapping back-and-forth: it re-delivers over ranges it normally would not retrace so often. This is a "seek and destroy" climate; if you roll your stop to cover costs or breakeven it generally comes back and hits it. ICT says he has noticed this only for this event, no other economic event.
- **How to use:**
  - Decide where your first line of partials is before entering and keep it easy/low-threshold; do not try to outsmart the market with a greedy hold.
  - If long and price trades into a premium inefficiency (sell-side imbalance, buy-side efficiency) or clears a short-term high, take something off.
  - Do not over-trade. Expect one-directional runs to frustrate.
  - Check it yourself: on the weekend, review the 1-minute charts for the overlapping delivery.
  - ICT says moves attributed to Powell's words are really intervention; he prefers to be out of the way before the speech.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:45](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=1845) overlapping delivery in Jackson Hole week · [0:34:43](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=2083) where to place first partials · [0:39:50](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=2390) rolling the stop gets hit · [0:41:26](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=2486) don't over-trade
- **Nuance / caveats:** He says "it is not every single week", it is predominantly Jackson Hole.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: FOMC rate decision: two-stage delivery and the 3:15 last-hour macro
body:
- **Kind:** rule (news driver) + macro
- **What ICT says:** On a rate announcement/policy statement at 2:00 pm ET there is an initial move into 2:00 and a move from 2:00 to 2:30 (press conference). About 70% of the time (caption says "70%", later "7%" is a garble) whatever direction you see going into 2:30 reverses and the biggest move of the day goes the other way and is more exaggerated. Hold the reversal until about 3:15 pm and get out early, since that starts the last-hour macro. He notes this is one of four macros in the 3:00-4:00 window and the only hour with multiple macros. No "20-40 minute" or "30-40 minute" macros exist; those are gimmicks. FOMC minutes (that week) are less impactful than a rate announcement.
