title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Lunch-hour retracement behavior
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** In lunch, price retraces against whatever has been profitable: it seeks sell stops after an up move and buy stops after a down move. Therefore measure the possible lunch retrace and keep your stop beyond it.
- **Example in this video:** After the run to the NWOG, the lunch-time 15-second drop sweeps relative equal lows and does not touch the NWOG high again.
- **Timestamps:** [3:40:25](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=13225) · [2:14:37](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=8077)

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #11  August 19, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Reaper Fair Value Gap  (aliases: "Reaper", month-anchored FVG)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage (introduced in an earlier lecture; clarified here)
- **What ICT says:** A fair value gap anchored to a meaningful day: the first fair value gap that forms after 9:30 on a Monday (first day of the week) or on the first trading day of the month. Draw it out through the whole week/month. The algorithm goes back to specific dates as frames of reference (he lists: first trading day of the month, first day of the week, Wednesday, previous Friday; "not all of them"). "Reaper" is a scythe that cuts through the whole month and makes it tradable. Use it when it also matches the time of day the market should deliver.
- **How to use:** In a new month (August here) go back to the first day of the month, take the first pertinent PD array, and carry it through the chart. Treat each FVG as unique: if it shares space with another PD array it changes its character, so do not rename or re-teach it.
- **Example in this video:** The Reaper FVG he showed the previous week from August 1 was referenced repeatedly through the month.
- **Timestamps:** [3:48:26](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=13706) every FVG is not the same · [3:50:03](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=13803) algorithm goes back to specific days · [3:51:38](https://youtu.be/aONkyy-HTqE?t=13898) first FVG after 9:30 Monday, draw through week and month
- **Nuance / caveats:** He says more is in "the book". He admits slips (calling a market maker sell model when it was a buy model, or "distribution" when it was reaccumulation) and says if it is going up it is reaccumulation, not distribution. The Aug 1 date is as spoken: "August 1st first day of the week" is caption-unclear (Aug 1, 2024 was a Thursday).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Power of 3 / Daily range schematic  (aliases: PO3, AMD (not named in this video), "classic buy day", Judas swing)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition (applied to the day)
- **What ICT says:**
  - He sketched one daily range before the live stream: the 9:30 opening price is the reference. Any move down away from the 9:30 open on a bullish day is "the Judas swing" or fake move, meant to get people thinking it will keep dropping.
  - After that comes the "trend following" portion, which is directional and one-sided up. At the close, price comes off the highest high and settles off the high (so the daily candle has open near low, close near high).
  - Larry Williams (1995 video course, "confidential trading course" caption unclear) said it was hard for him to buy below the opening price when bullish, so he bought strength. ICT says this was his opening: Power of 3 is his answer to that problem, with a systematic way to be a buyer at or below the open.
  - Buying at the opening price or lower when bullish gives many more handles/points than buying strength; he says this was solidified last Tuesday (Aug 13).
- **How to identify:** requires a bullish daily/weekly bias first. Then watch for price trading below the 9:30 open (Judas) toward relative equal lows / sell-side liquidity, then an entry drill (see below) at or below the open.
- **How to use:** be a buyer at/below the 9:30 open when expecting higher prices on the daily chart; the low of the day is expected to hold ("low-risk buy"); then hold through time (see hold rules).
- **Example in this video:** ES, Aug 19, 2024, 15m/1m. Price opens at 9:30, drops a little, pops slightly above the open, drops again, then takes out relative equal lows below the open. That is the buy zone. Price then rallies above the new week opening gap and continues up all day to close near the high; daily candle open near low, close near high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:30](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=810) Larry Williams problem and PO3 as the answer · [0:14:19](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=859) the 9:30 open, Judas swing, trend-following leg, close off the high · [0:17:35](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1055) buying at/below the open for longer targets
- **Nuance / caveats:** he says shorts intraday are still possible against the daily bullish bias but with much smaller size. He tells viewers to search the channel for "power three" for the full teaching.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Institutional Orderflow Entry Drill (IOFED)  (aliases: "the drill", "institutional orderflow entry drill", "low-risk buy")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (applied example only; mechanics not re-taught here)
- **What ICT says:** the entry on the day was the institutional order flow entry drill at or below the 9:30 open. He calls it the low-risk buy: price "should not come back below" that entry and should keep pressing higher. He says you only appreciate where these setups form relative to the 9:30 open after doing the drills for months, not days or weeks.
- **How to identify (as applied):** price sweeps through the new week opening gap, clears inefficiency into an order block (there were two), and then there is a change in the state of delivery. Price comes back to engage the order block, which "upsets" a perfect delivery to the NWOG, and then runs.
- **How to use:** after the entry, do not run the stop up repeatedly (see hold rules). Wicks that poke outside the PD array ("coloring outside the lines") are expected and welcome.
- **Example in this video:** ES 1m, Aug 19. Price drops below the 9:30 open, trades through the new day opening gap ("on the 16th" per captions) and comes back up. ICT says he wanted to see it get above that new day opening gap, then see it trade down again (it does), and that second dip is the entry. A breaker on a 15-second chart was also used (he says he was long ES while a DOM-ladder streamer said it would not make a higher high).
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:44](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1484) 1m chart, new day opening gap and the low run out · [0:25:33](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1533) institutional orderflow entry drill called · [0:28:43](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1723) order block, CISD, "coloring book" explanation
- **Nuance / caveats:** captions are rough here; the exact candle and price of entry are not stated. He refers viewers to the same-day live stream for the real-time call.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG)  (aliases: new week opening gap, "coloring book")
body:
- **Kind:** definition + example
- **What ICT says:** NWOG = Sunday 6 PM open compared with Friday's settlement price. Price was above it all day, and the gap was used as support for the buy. Price is likened to children coloring inside a coloring book: it can color outside the lines and he wants to see that, because it gives the opportunity. "Let the wicks do the damage."
- **How to use:** treat the NWOG as a magnet and support on a bullish day; the retracement into it (and the order block nearby) is the buy zone; the lunch macro sell-off also engaged the NWOG.
- **Example in this video:** ES, week of Aug 19. Price swept through the NWOG, cleared inefficiency into the order block (two stacked), CISD, rally; at 11:30-ish the lunch-macro drop came back to the NWOG and the 11:17 low, then rallied.
- **Timestamps:** [0:18:21](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1101) NWOG defined (Sunday 6 PM vs Friday settlement) · [0:28:43](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1723) coloring inside the lines · [0:31:06](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1866) lunch macro engages NWOG
- **Nuance / caveats:** also mentions a new day opening gap and an opening range gap, but does not define them here.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Lunch macro (11:30-1:30) and the "first low after 10:00" rule  (aliases: lunch macro, 11:30 macro)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - At 11:30 the lunch macro starts and can run to 1:30 (he notes it could also keep going higher with no retracement). It tends to go against the morning's direction to take liquidity from whoever has been profiting.
  - Method: at 11:30, ask who made money from 9:30 to now. If longs (market rallied), the algorithm seeks the stops of traders who trailed their stops under a low. To find that low, go backwards from 11:30 and take the first low you come to, but it must have formed after 10:00 (it factors in any Silver Bullet run and protraction). Lows before 10:00 do not count.
  - After the macro closes at 1:30, there is no more time element for taking those stops, so price is free to continue in the direction of the early session (open near low, close near high).
- **How to identify:** (1) mark 11:30; (2) scan left for the first swing low; (3) confirm it formed after 10:00; (4) expect a raid below it during 11:30-1:30 if the morning move was up.
- **How to use:** expect a pullback/raid and do not be shaken out; he says he told viewers this ahead of time so they would hold. If the sell side has been taken and 1:30 passes, the continuation is free.
- **Example in this video:** ES 1m, Aug 19. The relevant low was at 11:17 (after 10:00). At 11:30 price dropped, took out that low (stops of anyone trailing below) and engaged the NWOG, then consolidated and rallied after 1:30.
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:31](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1771) 11:30 starts the lunch macro, who is making money · [0:30:17](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1817) go backwards to first low after 10:00 (11:17 low) · [0:33:34](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2014) why after 10:00 (Silver Bullet run) · [0:34:23](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2063) 1:30 closes the macro, free to continue
- **Nuance / caveats:** the captions have him saying "11:00 for the folks that don't know my macro for lunch" before correcting to 11:30; the macro start is 11:30 per the rest of the passage. He also says the lunch macro explains the sell-side move without any need to look at depth of market.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Last-hour macros: 3:15-3:45 and 3:45-4:00 (market on close)  (aliases: last hour macro, MOC macro)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / new detail
- **What ICT says:**
  - 3:00 starts the last hour of the day. He told his community "after 3 o'clock, if you have not taken anything, pay the trader" (take something off), and to hold a minimum until 3:15.
  - A macro runs 3:15 to 3:45. Then the 3:45 to 4:00 window is the market on close; he stresses it is 15 minutes (not 10), 3:45 to 4:00 ET.
  - He says there are four macros in the last hour (caption unclear: "four of four macros"); he names the one starting 3:15 and the one starting 3:45.
  - In earnings season, an algorithm fires at 4:01 and produces a run into 4:15; after the regular session closes, electronic trading can go "bonkers."
  - From 3:45 the algorithm refers back to daily and weekly levels, cycling from higher timeframes down to seconds and back up; all inefficiencies and liquidity are incorporated. He calls this "casting your lure" toward the HTF level.
- **How to use:** in a daily trend day, hold into 3:15 at minimum; the 3:15-3:45 retracement can be disregarded as noise; the 3:45 run is aimed at the HTF target.
- **Example in this video:** ES/NQ, Aug 19. Price rallied through the 2:00 hour, had a small retracement into 3:00 (low sitting inside a fair value gap), then from 3:30 a candle spooled up into the blue line (close of the daily SIBI) and traded into the daily volume imbalance and the pink shaded target area, closing near the high.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:08](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=908) 3 o'clock pay the trader, last hour · [0:35:10](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2110) hold minimum to 3:15 · [0:42:19](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2539) 3:15-3:45 then market on close 3:45-4:00, 4:01 earnings algorithm · [0:39:09](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2349) 3:45 algorithm references HTF levels
- **Nuance / caveats:** he says he made a little under $20,000 on a live account with this information; he also says do not take trades because of what he says.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Holding trades longer (time-based management)  (aliases: holding for the daily range, "submit to time")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Start from higher-timeframe bias, then enter an intraday setup that is in sync with it. To hold for bigger runs, the first and foremost thing is to submit to the time the daily candle needs to form and close.
  - Having bought at/below the open on a bullish day, "you do not strangle it by running your stop loss up"; do not keep moving it higher and higher.
  - Expect the 11:30 lunch macro raid against the move (so do not trail tight), then hold to at least 3:15, ideally through the last hour.
  - "Just let one contract go": leave one contract as a runner using these rules and you will have bigger runs.
  - These are skills built through months of drills; you cannot force it.
- **How to use:** define the plan by time before entry: low-risk buy at/below the open, expect the lunch raid, then hold to 3:15-4:00.
- **Example in this video:** ES long from the opening drill held through the 11:30 raid to the afternoon run; he says he drew roughly two handles of draw down for a run of over 200 handles (he states "over 200 and some handles").
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:30](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=570) how to hold trades that keep moving without being stopped out · [0:28:43](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1723) do not strangle it by raising the stop · [0:35:10](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2110) let one contract go · [0:38:21](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2301) submit to the time required for the daily candle to close
- **Nuance / caveats:** a mention of "Tanja" (a student) making over 100 handles; his remarks on hold-time apply to bullish-daily context, and shorts against that bias are small size.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Higher-timeframe narrative and daily-chart targets  (aliases: HTF levels, daily/weekly objectives, "magnets")
body:
- **Kind:** rule + example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Method he used in the mentorship: give HTF levels where price is likely to reach, then the student only watches lower timeframes for the completion of a run on opposing liquidity and then gets in sync with order flow. He claims high-90% accuracy on this for students.
  - He gave all levels on Tuesday Aug 13; HTF levels act like magnets pulling institutional order flow. Keep them on the chart and on a notepad and check whether price is marching to them.
  - Levels on the daily chart (ES/NQ-scale prices in caption look like NQ, ~19,868): the mean threshold of an up-close candle, a rejection block, buy-side liquidity above, the low of a candle (SIBI: "sell side imbalance buy side inefficiency"; that candle's low 19,868.2 vs the day's high 19,871.7, so it was cleared at the close), and a volume imbalance between two candle bodies (pink shaded area).
  - Retracements intraday against that HTF bias are just retracements and do not change the premise; the opposite side's liquidity gets taken first and the market usually goes for the opposite.
- **How to identify:** he lists them in order going up: mean threshold of the up-close candle, rejection block, BSL, the candle low (SIBI), and the volume imbalance between two candle bodies.
- **How to use:** frame buy side and sell side, anticipate the run on opposing liquidity, and enter when it completes. Trade size is the largest in the direction of daily orderflow.
- **Example in this video:** daily chart, Aug 19. Last week he said he was reaching higher (not picking a top); price hit the mean threshold, then the liquidity above, then the SIBI, and traded to its upper level into the pink area; after that, he is content with the weekly objective and unsure whether there is a higher high, range, or drop.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:13](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=133) recap of last Tuesday's levels · [0:10:16](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=616) how the mentorship framed buy side/sell side and HTF · [0:45:32](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2732) daily chart walkthrough: MT, rejection block, BSL, candle low, volume imbalance
- **Nuance / caveats:** a daily chart price like "19,868" does not match ES; the chart shown is probably NQ while he says he traded ES (caption/unclear). The "last Tuesday" stream is not in this batch.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Volume imbalance  (aliases: volume imbalance on the daily)
body:
- **Kind:** definition (brief)
- **What ICT says:** the space between one candle's close and the next candle's open where there is no body, only a wick, and the bodies of the two candles do not overlap. He calls this a volume imbalance and says he talked about it at the end of the previous Tuesday's stream. It is used as a daily target (pink area).
- **How to identify:** two consecutive candles whose bodies do not overlap, leaving a gap between close and next open that is wick-only on one side.
- **Timestamps:** [0:03:50](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=230) definition at the daily chart · [0:45:32](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2732) as a target
- **Nuance / caveats:** description is loose in captions; treat as "bodies do not overlap".

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Algorithmic price delivery (vs. depth of market)  (aliases: "the algorithm", price engine, IPDA (not named))
body:
- **Kind:** definition / argument
- **What ICT says:**
  - The algorithm is the price engine: it offers price, and buyers and sellers agree to it. The "commodity" is price action itself. Price is first piped to top-tier institutions and retail gets the scraps.
  - It needs only to know what time and where, not how many contracts are trading. Order books can be spoofed (big banks have been fined), so ladders are bait and do not drive the market.
  - Price cycles through time frames (less than daily down to seconds and back up) so inefficiencies and liquidity get incorporated. Moves are not buying and selling pressure.
  - His example was a streamer calling ICT a scam while saying ES would not make a higher high; ICT went long ES off a breaker on a 15-second chart and it accelerated higher.
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:45](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1245) breaker on 15s chart vs DOM claims · [0:21:33](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1293) algorithm offers price · [0:31:57](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1917) algorithm needs time and where, spoofing
- **Nuance / caveats:** mainly argument, not a setup. Skip the personal back-and-forth.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #12  August 19, 2024
head: Position sizing by bias and event risk
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The heaviest position size is in the direction of daily bullish order flow ("not overleveraging"); shorts against it are small. For himself he would trade 1, 3 or 4 contracts, not 10, 15 or 20, because most of the expected daily move is already done.
  - Jackson Hole Symposium (Wed/Thu/Fri that week): treat it like a non-farm payroll week, i.e. trade Monday staying with the setups and expect volatility late in the week.
  - Scenario: if the Middle East escalates (Iran/Israel), expect large-range daily down candles, perhaps one big one, then a pause a day or two, and the market would struggle to print green candles.
  - He notes no down daily close in over two weeks is unsustainable and speculates that a run into the inefficiency may be where a rug-pull comes if the news breaks.
- **Timestamps:** [0:27:08](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=1628) Jackson Hole like an NFP week · [0:46:18](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2778) contract size 1-4, not 10-20 · [0:48:41](https://youtu.be/EQfTD6ntB4A?t=2921) larger size long, small size short, Middle East scenario
- **Nuance / caveats:** the geopolitical talk is his speculation; he says he does not know whether a higher high, range, or drop follows.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: New Day Opening Gap (NDOG)  (aliases: new day opening gap, "the gap carried forward")
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - NDOG = the difference between the 5:00 PM ET settlement and the 6:00 PM ET reopen (one-hour pause in trading). It is labeled for the next trading day (Aug 19 settle to 6 PM open is "the 20th"), and you carry it forward into the day you are watching.
  - Once price trades through it, do not discard it. He says the common error is to disregard a gap as soon as it fills ("throwing the baby out with the bathwater"); the algorithm refers back to the high, low and quadrant levels again and again whenever price trades through and back to them.
  - Bodies of candles tell you the gap is respected; wicks are allowed to do the damage.
  - Caleb's model: the NDOG or NWOG is the draw. Lookback he gives for Caleb: NDOGs up to about 5 days back, NWOGs up to about 5 weeks back. He adds that older NWOGs do not get stale for sentiment and can still produce reactions.
- **How to identify:** compare the 5:00 PM settlement candle with the 6:00 PM open on a one-minute chart, mark the high and low, optionally add quadrants.
- **How to use:** (bullish case) look for relative equal highs just below or at the NDOG/NWOG so there is liquidity to run on the way to the magnet; (bearish case) relative equal lows just above the NDOG/NWOG. Treat the gap as support after price goes through it and returns (like an old FVG).
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 20 open. Price opens below the NDOG; ICT watches the NDOG high as the draw. A small 15-second gap forms, the wick stops it and price rallies into the NDOG. He highlights a 15-second BISI overlapped with the NDOG as "a very very easy bread and butter setup." Later price drops back to the NDOG low, the candle bodies hold it, and price rallies (see the entry drill concept).
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:49](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=49) opens below the NDOG, watching it as a draw · [0:05:48](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=348) "that is my son's model," the draw is the NDOG/NWOG · [0:06:34](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=394) REH/REL placement and 5-day / 5-week lookback · [0:09:53](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=593) how the NDOG is built and labeled · [0:10:43](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=643) don't discard it once filled
- **Nuance / caveats:** the opening range and the NDOG are different things; he reminds viewers of that when he mixes terms. "Five days / five weeks" is the criteria he gives Caleb, not a hard rule for everyone.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Opening Range Gap (RTH opening gap) and its midpoint  (aliases: opening range gap, ORG, "the gap from yesterday's settlement to today's 9:30")
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule (with a high-probability tendency)
- **What ICT says:**
  - The opening range gap is the difference between the previous session's settlement (the RTH close candle at 4:15 PM ET per his description) and the 9:30 AM open. Use the candle close to open as the edges, break it into quadrants (he stresses this is not "quarters theory"), keep it on the chart and extend it through the day.
  - Price will use the high, low and quadrants repeatedly whenever it trades through it and back.
  - Gap lower is a lure to get traders short; you then expect a gap fill. At the very minimum, expect price to go to the 50% (midpoint, consequent encroachment) of the gap; he calls this "one of the strongest things in trading." Use a Fibonacci to mark the midpoint.
  - The gap does not always close completely: it can go halfway and then rocket in the direction of the gap. If it will go lower it goes halfway (or a little more) and fails to close, then drops.
  - You do not even need to be right on bias for this retracement trade.
  - He also uses the "opening range" as 9:30 to 10:00 (30 minutes) for the beginning of the session; later he corrects himself for using "opening range" for the 9:31 moment.
- **How to use:** if the open gaps lower, drop the fib on the first tick; if there is range between current price and the gap midpoint, he will go long right there (he says he has done it many times) and target the midpoint. If bullish with a higher-timeframe target, expect price to go above the gap and then use the gap as support.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 20. Price gapped lower from Monday's settlement, took the ORG, went above it, came back and used it as support. A consequent encroachment of about "834" (caption; likely 19,834) is cited as the midpoint; the ORG high is around 19,850.25 (he places it "on the close of that candle").
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:14](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1034) ORG on the 1m chart · [0:37:21](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=2241) ORG high at 19,850.25, extend through the day · [0:38:09](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=2289) gap lower, mark 50%, no bias needed · [0:49:29](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=2969) go long on the first tick if there is range to the midpoint
- **Nuance / caveats:** he says people disregard gaps because "everybody knows about gaps," which is why the setup is ignored; the half-fill is the minimum expectation, not a guarantee.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Consequent Encroachment, Mean Threshold and quadrants  (aliases: CE, MT, quadrants, "lower/upper quadrant")
body:
- **Kind:** definition (clarification)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Consequent encroachment (CE) = the midpoint of a gap: FVG (up- or down-close), BISI/SIBI, volume imbalance, opening gap, even a wick treated as a gap.
  - Mean threshold (MT) is different: it is the equilibrium or midpoint of an order block.
  - Wicks are classified like gaps ("I internalize them as the same thing as a gap"), so a wick can be divided into quadrants and its CE used as a limit for how far price may overshoot.
  - Lower quadrant, midpoint (CE) and upper quadrant are the levels he uses to measure what is still unfilled in a gap.
- **How to use:** mark quadrants on every gap you track; measure whether price reaches the next quadrant, how fast, and how it behaves there (stalls or slices through "like a hot knife through butter").
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:45](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=885) CE vs MT, wicks as gaps · [0:15:35](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=935) quadrants, not quarters theory
- **Nuance / caveats:** corrects a common mix-up between MT (order block) and CE (gap).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Daily volume imbalance as a higher-timeframe draw  (aliases: volume imbalance, "the yellow area", daily SIBI target)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + example (target given on the Aug 13 stream)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Volume imbalance: the space between one candle's close and the next candle's open where the bodies do not overlap and only a wick bridges the two candles. He teaches to look at the wick as a gap and measure between the bodies.
  - Divide it into quadrants; the portion not yet traded is the objective. On the daily chart, price had already traded into the daily SIBI (the blue line is that candle's low at 19,868.25; the pink area is the SIBI); the yellow shaded volume imbalance sits just above and is the remaining target.
  - He wants to see whether price can reach the lower quadrant, then the midpoint (CE), of the yellow area. "Not saying it has to go right there right now; technicals have to support the idea."
  - He says his interest for the rest of the week is whether price trades into that area; it need not reach it today.
- **Example in this video:** Daily NQ, levels flagged Aug 13. In Monday's last hour and London on Aug 20 price rallied into the SIBI up to roughly the upper quadrant of its first part (caption unclear on exactly which quadrant), then reversed down into the NDOG. On Aug 20 price reaches the lower quadrant of the yellow area and then its CE (perfect delivery, he says), pulls back, then makes a short-term high after the target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:12](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=492) levels from the Aug 13 stream and Monday's last hour · [0:11:33](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=693) high of the daily SIBI and the remaining open portion · [0:13:57](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=837) volume imbalance defined between the two bodies · [0:16:25](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=985) candle low 19,868.25, SIBI between this candle's high and that candle's low
- **Nuance / caveats:** captions blur which quadrant was tagged on Aug 19 versus Aug 20; the safest reading is that the yellow area above the SIBI is the unfilled draw and the lower quadrant, then CE, are the stepwise objectives.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Price Delivery Continuum Theory (reading real order flow from price)  (aliases: "price delivery continuing theory", "my way of reading real order flow", the algorithm)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / method
- **What ICT says:**
  - Read order flow from what has actually traded: the open, high, low and close of each interval, not from depth of market, ladders, level-2 or Bookmap. Resting orders can be pulled (spoofing); you cannot spoof the OHLC of a candle. Volume booked is seen with time and sales only after price engages the level.
  - Frame it as a question: does price support the algorithm repricing back to these reference points? Can price reach the next level, how fast, and what does it do on arrival (stop short or go through)? Then did it show willingness to trade to the next CE?
  - Because price is algorithmic it follows "scripts"; contract counts have no bearing. The market is drawn to inefficiency ("a big magnet"), it needs only to touch the low end of an inefficiency first, then you watch whether it aggressively runs to the midpoint.
  - He says he does not use Bookmap-type tools, and that students who understand his method do not need them; he admits it might have helped him early on.
- **How to use:** screenshot your own chart and watch price hit levels; do not rely on his charts.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:44](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1364) no DOM or ladders, just price · [0:25:09](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1509) price delivery continuum theory, spoofing · [0:25:58](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1558) lowest quadrant yes, CE yes · [0:29:10](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1750) inefficiency, delivery of price vs contracts
- **Nuance / caveats:** this restates his recurring argument against order-book tools, now under a named theory; the name in captions is "price delivery continuum / continuing theory."

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Fair Value Gap overshoot and nested timeframes  (aliases: coloring outside the lines, "mohawk", wick CE)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement + example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Ideal FVG behavior (bullish): price only goes into the upper half of the gap, not the bottom half. If it leaves the gap open it is "extremely strong" and should keep pressing higher. It can still overlap the gap completely and remain valid ("completely permissible").
  - How far can a wick overshoot? Take the highest wick to the left and use its consequent encroachment; that is where the overshoot should stop. On Aug 20, the 1-minute FVG was measured from one candle's high to another candle's low, and the wick ran to the CE of that wick ("perfect delivery").
  - Nested timeframes: on the 15-second chart the candle bodies stay inside the FVG and respect it; only the wick reaches as low as the 1-minute FVG's low / the CE of the wick.
  - "Mohawk" (caption unclear; spelling as heard): a bearish candle that goes just outside an FVG. It looks scary but is permissible price action; knowing it can be measured is what keeps you in the trade.
- **How to use:** measure the allowable overshoot beforehand so a scary bearish candle does not shake you out; keep the lower-timeframe levels alongside the 1-minute levels.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:05](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1265) upper half of an FVG ideal, leaving it open is strong · [0:22:44](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1364) wick CE perfect delivery · [0:24:20](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1460) 15s bodies respect the 1m FVG · [0:40:33](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=2433) "mohawk" and measuring overshoot
- **Nuance / caveats:** this builds on the "how far can it color outside the lines" idea from earlier lectures (he references yesterday's session).

body:

- **What ICT says:** the entry on Aug 20: price drops back after a displacement, delivers perfectly to the NDOG, then rallies leaving a fair value gap. He says the entry is the candle plus one tick, which gets filled on the retrace. The first objective is the high-water mark of the daily SIBI, then the volume imbalance (pink/yellow area).
- **How to use:** entry at the FVG (candle high + one tick for a buy); first target = daily SIBI high, then the lower quadrant, then the CE of the volume imbalance; take partials as short-term highs break.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m/15s, Aug 20 around 9:30-10:00 ET. Price takes the NDOG low, rallies (displacement), pulls back, the FVG forms, the entry triggers, price rallies to the SIBI high; it then digs back into an order block and rebounds almost immediately; it did not fill the lower part so a portion was left open; price then reaches the lower quadrant with speed and goes straight to CE. Short-term high made above after the target; he says he would have taken a partial.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Partial profits at short-term highs ("running down equity")  (aliases: "run down equity", scaling out, "dollar menu men")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - When long in a buy program, every short-term high that gets broken is a candidate to take a partial. He says this is important and to put it in your notes. Do it above the broken short-term high because that is premium-level pricing.
  - Take a partial rather than move the stop. In the early stages of development, tightening the stop to "lock in profit" only increases uncertainty and anxiety, and you end up watching the stop rather than whether price still supports the idea.
  - After a partial is banked, moving the stop to cover cost means "theoretically you don't have any chance of losing money," a huge paradigm shift for a developing trader.
  - The purpose: you do not know if it is going to continue, so distribute; even if your target does not get hit, the trade has paid. If you skip the partial and price turns, you watch a winner become a loser.
  - The initial stop is not meant to remain; he has protocols for moving it. When trading back and forth all day he is more aggressive moving the stop because he will take other trades.
  - He says partials are "a professional mindset," not weakness; claims that you must be right or hit your target are social-media nonsense. What matters is constantly making money.
- **How to use:** (1) define minor targets in advance; (2) at each broken short-term high, take something off; (3) only then think about the stop (cover cost after a profitable partial); (4) do not require the final target.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 20: after reaching the daily volume-imbalance lower quadrant and CE, price made another short-term high; he says if you did not take a partial there you should be taking something off. Price then slipped lower, and he points out the long trader already distributed near the highs and is comfortable if price drops.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:44](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1844) partial above a short-term high · [0:32:19](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=1939) partial before moving the stop; don't move early · [0:46:18](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=2778) distributing at premium levels · [0:52:37](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=3157) partials as professional mindset · [0:55:01](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=3301) partial, then cover cost
- **Nuance / caveats:** this seems to sit alongside last lecture's "let one contract go" advice (M24-012): partial profits plus a runner. It is aimed at early development; he says discretion on stops loosens with experience.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #13  August 20, 2024 Begins 9:15am ET
head: Framework and "bias-less" progression  (aliases: graduating, trading without a bias, "liquid" trader)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / mindset
- **What ICT says:**
  - Beginners need a framework or structure (one bias, a named model with a draw) in order to measure progress; he says Caleb's model is gaps plus the higher-timeframe target.
  - Eventually you trade price by time of day and what it is reaching for, with no fixed bias: buy and sell back and forth for 10-20 handles each way, 100-200 handles in a day, and survive two or three stopped trades, breakevens or commission-only losses.
  - He says this takes a decade or more, not six months or two years; anyone claiming faster is using his vocabulary without having been taught.
  - The market must have enough volatility for that; on aimless days take one trade (or one morning, one afternoon, or a lunch-macro reversal) and be done.
  - Different traders can trade long and short on the same day with different models and both be profitable, because the tools are meant to be made your own.
  - Success is measured by being able to frame a setup from a beginning point to a "terminus" worth 15-20 handles; the draw on liquidity need not be reached. A 15-20 handle frame is, in his definition, a high-probability trade that Caleb may take, but it is a green light, not a guarantee.
- **Timestamps:** [0:48:42](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=2922) make it your own; long and short traders both profitable · [0:57:22](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=3442) bias-less trading by time of day and what price reaches for · [0:58:08](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=3488) one or two trades on slow days · [1:00:32](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=3632) DOL need not be reached; frame the move · [1:01:21](https://youtu.be/LMi_mO3AP08?t=3681) 15-20 handles = green light
- **Nuance / caveats:** the "terminus" language is used loosely here for the end of the framed move.

head: Session logging / chart annotation routine  (aliases: "daily meditation", journaling charts)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (process)
- **What ICT says:**
  - For each session, capture screenshots of your own charts (not his, though viewers who cannot watch live may use his to catch up) in PowerPoint or a notes tool, and type annotations in the open areas of the chart.
  - Record what levels mattered, how price traded to them, the highest high and lowest low, and how price worked with the levels given in advance. Do it every single day, not only on good technical days.
  - Expect it to feel monotonous and useless early; he says it is the routine that taught him to anticipate and repeat setups. Journals get more specific over time and drop the unimportant items.
  - What to log (his "number one, go-to" list): time of day; new day opening gaps and new week opening gaps; the opening range gap; the first-presentation fair value gap; plus other order blocks and FVGs you notice. Don't be afraid to annotate things that later prove unimportant.
  - His focus for Caleb: "what creates the high and low of the day."

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #16  August 24, 2024
head: Volume imbalance (precise definition)  (aliases: VI)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** a volume imbalance is any pair of adjacent candles whose bodies do not touch or overlap; you measure the separation between the previous candle's body (open or close) and the next candle's body. There is no difference whether the candles are up- or down-closed. The wicks may travel and even open above the previous candle's low; that does not negate it. He adds that even a single tick of separation counts (captions on that last sentence are garbled).
- **How to use:** measure the gap, take its consequent encroachment, divide into halves/quadrants. When bearish, the upper (premium) half should not be traded back into if the algorithm "respects" the array.
- **Timestamps:** [0:09:11](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=551) definition
- **Nuance / caveats:** consistent with M24-013 (where he treats the wick bridge as a gap and measures between bodies).

body:

They were worked one level at a time: a small remaining portion of a daily SIBI; the daily SIBI high of Jul 23 (caption "CBI"); the big down-close candle of Jul 24 as a SIBI; the rejection block; the wick's consequent encroachment; the volume imbalance; and the bearish order block (the Jul 22 up-close candle) with its mean threshold.

  - Rule: if you expect weakness and the HTF PD array is a volume imbalance that price already traded through, the best sign of algorithm respect is that price does not trade into its upper half. The upper (premium) half was shaded pink, and the NDOG of Aug 22 plus the daily SIBI high sat there; price had already gone through it three times and broke through.
  - The up-close candle at that area, once broken, becomes a bearish order block to use for intraday shorts.
  - Levels quoted: CE of the daily volume imbalance high = 19,943 (he thinks it respected the Friday high); mean threshold of the bearish order block = 19,881.75.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #16  August 24, 2024
head: Balanced Price Range (BPR) and high resistance liquidity  (aliases: balanced price range, "guarded by the algorithm", manual intervention)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement (his usage differs from the common overlapping-FVG BPR definition)
- **What ICT says:**
  - On the 1-minute chart he labels a segment a balanced price range: a small SIBI exists between one candle's low and another's high; price trades up into it (a small wick above is fine), breaks lower to a low, comes back up and overlaps the whole prior run, breaks lower again, retraces to the "propulsion block" again, then finally leaves the range below the low.
  - Why "balanced": price delivered both ways, back and forth (down, up, down, up), offering efficient delivery both higher and lower inside a clear trading range, and then leaves it. It is not enough to go up, down and leave.
  - Balanced price ranges are very difficult to get through. Buy-side stops above the high are "high resistance liquidity": it takes something very significant to reach them, in this case manual intervention (the algorithm is overridden), as around Fed, payroll, CPI and PPI.
  - Therefore if price does return to the BPR low and reaches into it, nothing is wrong with the logic; but if price reaches the high it signals manual intervention; he would not chase long and would "cut the interest in the day and be done."
  - Always trade after those news drivers; you do not know what they will do at the time of delivery.
  - Extend the BPR through the day. He kept the levels on a notepad (the chart gets busy); he recommends putting them on the chart while learning.
- **How to identify:** (1) a mapped range with a small SIBI inside; (2) price trades both directions inside it; (3) price leaves it with displacement; (4) the range's high holds as resistance.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Aug 23 before the open: the range sits above, price displaces below its low; ICT says he is not interested in longs "because of the factors on the daily chart." The shaded BPR high-low extended through 9:30.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:11](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=791) BPR introduced · [0:14:47](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=887) back and forth then leaves · [0:16:28](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=988) high resistance liquidity and manual intervention · [0:18:03](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1083) displacement leaves, return to BPR is guarded
- **Nuance / caveats:** this does not mention the usual "two opposing FVGs overlapping" definition. Record this as ICT's wording here.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #16  August 24, 2024
head: First-Presentation Fair Value Gap (9:31-10:00 ET)  (aliases: first presented FVG, first presentation FVG, "your real first fair value gap")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The first FVG that forms inside the 9:30-10:00 opening range. The candle that creates the imbalance (the middle candle) cannot be earlier than 9:31: toggle TradingView from electronic trading hours (ETH) to regular trading hours (RTH) and a 9:30-created gap disappears. A real first-presentation gap must exist in both ETH and RTH views.
  - Do not use gaps that start at 9:30, or 9:30 to 9:32 (caption wording), for this purpose; the earliest valid imbalance candle is 9:31.
  - Project it forward through the whole day and log how it behaves later. He calls this a school of thought he taught in Twitter Spaces in 2023, not in older books, and says it is the "number one go-to."
  - Carry it until 3:45 ET (end of the 3:15-3:45 macro), because the final-hour algorithm can reference it.
  - All times are New York time.
- **How to identify:** (1) set the chart to RTH; (2) find the first 3-candle FVG after the open whose middle candle is 9:31 or later; (3) check it also appears on ETH; (4) the gap must form between 9:31 and 10:00.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 23. The first presented FVG formed on the early rally; during the lunch hour price worked below it and sold off to fill the undelivered part of the opening range gap; later price rallied, rolled through and overlapped it; then in the last hour the day's low formed at 3:45 right at the bottom of that gap, and price rallied back to a previous NDOG, swiped above a short-term high, and closed.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:40](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1180) opening range 9:30-10:00 and the first FVG · [0:20:29](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1229) RTH vs ETH toggle · [0:38:16](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=2296) imbalance candle cannot form before 9:31 · [0:42:14](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=2534) carry it through 3:45 · [0:43:05](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=2585) low of day at 3:45 at the bottom of the FVG
- **Nuance / caveats:** likely reason (my reading, not stated): a gap whose middle candle is 9:30 needs a pre-9:30 candle that RTH does not show. He says viewers' comments asking why he did not use an earlier gap are answered in the live stream.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #16  August 24, 2024
head: Opening Range and the "first one taken" rule  (aliases: opening range, 9:30 high, buy side vs sell side clean equals)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** the opening range is the 30 minutes from 9:30 to 10:00. If both the buy side (relative equal highs, including the 9:30 high) and the sell side (relative equal lows) are obvious and clean, wait for the first one to be taken; the side that is taken first is the fake run. On Aug 23 the buy side was taken, so "all of this is a fake run"; had price gone down first and then reversed, he would have treated that FVG as an inversion FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:19](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1279) opening range, REH and REL, wait for the first one to be taken

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #16  August 24, 2024
head: Aug 23 top-down short walkthrough (turtle soup, CISD, pyramid, accumulation test, iFVG)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (example); contains several rules
- **What ICT says:**
  - Accumulation test: after a run, a small BISI/SIBI forms; if price does not build multiple candles at its consequent encroachment ("I don't want to see it accumulate"), it will quickly run again, so expect another drive above the high. It drops, reverses out, and pumps higher; no accumulation at the CE means a higher high.
  - Sequence on Aug 23 (NQ 1m): opening buy-side raid creating relative equal highs; price hits the daily SIBI high from Jul 23, sweeps above the NDOG, runs to the mean threshold of the bearish order block (daily, Jul 22) and leaves relative equal highs; then drops without accumulating at the CE; a higher low forms; it rallies; a small gap forms, price rallies above and treats it as support; it runs just above the relative equal highs (turtle soup) and falls back through the bearish order block.
  - Failure signal: price could not reach the NDOG of Aug 22; he calls that weakness. When a candle swept below the opening price, that is the change in the state of delivery.
  - Short zone: any price between the opening price and the mean threshold of the Jul 22 bearish OB is a short; he calls the turtle soup the validation of the bearish order block, and says you can add/pyramid anywhere between those levels.
  - Price then breaks down through the Aug 20 NDOG, rallies one candle to touch the daily SIBI high (Jul 23) again, and breaks lower; he wanted it to go below the gap, come back into the lower half, and not trade the upper half; it drops to the next NDOG and rejects sharply, leaving the upper half unfilled.
  - Targets: relative equal lows (minor sell side), then the opening-range sell side that had not been tagged; the 10:00 move while Powell spoke was Judas swing / manual intervention knocking out shorts.
  - Inversion FVG: price makes relative equal highs again, does not accumulate in the BISI, runs a new high; the gap formed after the run is passed and becomes an inversion FVG. With buy side swept, the market should be in a sell model: consolidation, rally (manipulation), break lower (smart money reversal) = a low-risk sell. Price breaks below the old NDOG and below the FVG, acts as an iFVG, upper half stays open.
  - Final target: the NDOG of Aug 23 sitting inside the old NWOG of Aug 18 (see Event Horizon).
- **How to use:** he did it live ("I'm expecting this before it even happens"); shorts were between the open and the order-block MT; add as it works; hold for the nested-gap draw.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Fri Aug 23, 2024, 9:30 to the afternoon; moved over 200 handles. Prices not stated in captions beyond the daily levels above.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:08](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1328) no accumulation at CE, drop-reverse-pump · [0:23:47](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1427) turtle soup, back below bearish OB · [0:24:34](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1474) CISD, short zone, add/pyramid · [0:27:46](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1666) iFVG and sell model, low-risk sell
- **Nuance / caveats:** the captions in this stretch are rough; the order of touches (daily SIBI, NDOGs) is approximate. A passing line says every FVG should not be viewed as a future iFVG; first presentation is its own idea.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #16  August 24, 2024
head: Event Horizon  (aliases: "my event horizon", gray pool / dark pool / "black hole")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage (PD array)
- **What ICT says:**
  - When there is a new day or new week opening gap above and another below where price is expected to draw, measure from one to the other with a fib and put quadrants on it: upper quadrant, midpoint, lower quadrant. That zone is the Event Horizon. The algorithm will reprice into it "like a black hole" and draw price in.
  - It can be NDOG with NDOG, NDOG with NWOG, or NWOG with NWOG; there is no preference or added strength for one pairing; what matters is that they are close to one another.
  - Look-back: use the IPDA data range, no older than 60 days (about three months) for the gaps; if a NWOG is older than 60 days he is not generally interested, especially for the Event Horizon (the algorithm can use any of them; this is his maximum).
  - He calls this kind of PD array a gray pool (dark pool) and says retail cannot see it in the candles; he has others similar, will not teach all of them, and may share one more in the mentorship (no promises). He shares the Event Horizon with private students and mentioned it in passing in a Twitter Space.
  - Nesting: the Aug 23 NDOG sat inside the high-low of the NWOG of Aug 18; "when they nest like that" it is a huge black hole, easy to anticipate where it will be drawn.
- **How to identify:** two nearby NDOG/NWOG ranges (each within 60 days), measure between them, mark quadrants, and watch whether the candle bodies stay inside the zone and fail to go above the upper quadrant.
- **How to use:** treat the zone as a place price is drawn into; judge it by the candle bodies, which should stay inside it (not above the upper quadrant) when it caps a move. He also asks how far price can go below sell-side liquidity even without the extra opening gaps.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 23: the pink Event Horizon zone (between two NDOGs, per the captions) sat where price built relative equal highs and pumped one more time; the bodies stayed inside it and never went above the upper quadrant. Price then dropped through sell-side liquidity toward the NDOG of Aug 23 nested inside the NWOG of Aug 18 (his stated destination from the start of the stream). Which exact gaps bound the zone is not fully clear in captions.
- **Timestamps:** [0:28:36](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1716) NDOG nested in NWOG · [0:29:24](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1764) "my event horizon" · [0:30:14](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1814) fib and quadrants, bodies stay inside · [0:31:50](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=1910) combinations allowed, 60-day cap
- **Nuance / caveats:** earlier in M24-013 he used a 5-week lookback for Caleb's NWOGs and said older ones don't go stale; here the stated hard maximum is 60 days. He says it is "outside the spectrum of a candlestick."

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #16  August 24, 2024
head: Opening Range Gap (RTH) and its 70% midpoint tendency  (aliases: ORG, premium/discount opening range gap)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - ORG = previous regular-trading-hours close (4:15 PM ET close; he cites the 4:14 candle) to the 9:30 open the next trading day. If it opens above, that is a premium ORG; below is a discount ORG.
  - He says he taught this year that 70% of the time the midpoint (CE) of that gap gets traded to. Measure it on the first tick, then add quadrants; the midpoint matters most.
  - Track the undelivered portion (from previous settlement to the day's low, if it hasn't fully closed) and project it forward.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Aug 23: he wanted to see price drop to the ORG CE but would only act at premium levels. Price dropped into the undelivered portion during the lunch hour; the candle bodies respected the Aug 18 NWOG, and the gap delivered.
- **Timestamps:** [0:34:12](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=2052) ORG definition and 70% CE · [0:34:59](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=2099) undelivered portion · [0:35:46](https://youtu.be/kuURDD1ajdQ?t=2146) lunch-hour delivery respects the NWOG

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Opening Range Gap (RTH) — small / "anemic" gap protocol  (aliases ICT uses: opening range gap high/low, "previous settlement", "little unchanged", discount gap / lower gap opening)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - On the RTH chart, the opening range gap (ORG) is the space between the previous day's regular-hours settlement and the 9:30 ET open. The previous settlement (Friday's 4:14 pm ET RTH price here) is the ORG high when the open is lower, and the 9:30 opening price is the ORG low. On Friday the market keeps trading electronically after the RTH close for another 46 minutes. On other days it closes and reopens an hour later at 6:00 pm ET.
  - Before 9:30 he labels the ORG low "opening range gap low / settlement" and fixes the label when the real open prints. Toggling between RTH and electronic (ETH) hours lets you see the gap.
  - "Little unchanged" means the 9:30 open is less than about 30–40 handles from the previous settlement. If the market cannot muster a bigger difference at the opening bell, he sits on his hands until 10:00.
  - The first question for a morning session is whether the market is opening significantly higher or lower than the previous settlement. Larger gaps "invite larger volatility and a lot more protraction". A very small gap signals a market reluctant to run.
  - Scale reference: a 20-handle move is 19,732 to about 19,752 on the chart (the caption says "7,52", so 19,752 is inferred). The ORG that day was not much bigger than that.
- **How to identify:** compare the previous RTH settlement price (4:14 pm ET candle) with the 9:30 open on the RTH chart. If the difference is under about 30–40 handles, it is a weak gap.
- **How to use:**
  - Protocol for a weak gap: sit still, wait until 10:00, wait for the Silver Bullet or something more obvious, and give the algorithm the full first 30 minutes (9:30–10:00). "I don't care if there's a fair value gap." Ignore anything that shows up before then.
  - Don't elect a liquidity target or take a trade early. He says that over about 25 years of using ORGs he has been wrong when he forced it.
  - Conditional he gave: had the open been a higher gap, at or above the 8/21 NDOG, he would have looked for a drop into the 8/25 NWOG (using its consequent encroachment) and then a long up into the buy side above.
  - Do not treat the ORG high as the CE. The CE is the midpoint between the ORG low and high, which is a different price.
- **Example in this video:** Mon 8/26/2024 (stream starts about 9:31 ET). Pre-open, price had a higher-gap setup but erased it. On the 2-minute chart it hammered the CE of the 8/25 NWOG and Friday's settlement, then dropped and displaced below relative equal lows (sell side disturbed). It had already taken a buy-side level and was seeking minor short-term buy side above. At 9:30 it opened with a small discount (lower) gap just under settlement. Price traded back above the ORG high (settlement), stayed inside the 8/25 NWOG, failed hard near the 8/21 NDOG, and returned to the southern end of the ORG. He sat out all of 9:30–10:00.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:01:41](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=101) — RTH vs ETH, labelling ORG low/settlement.
  - [0:08:55](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=535) — "little unchanged" = under 30–40 handles, so wait until 10:00.
  - [0:11:21](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=681) — rules of engagement, 4:14 pm settlement mechanics.
  - [0:16:58](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1018) — "sit still, wait till 10:00, wait for Silver Bullet", the 25-years remark.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** this is a "don't engage" filter, not an entry. He teaches Caleb to treat a weak ORG as a cue for patience (he also uses the ORG in the coin-flip challenge below). The 10:00 wait is framed as the protocol he elected for Caleb. He says other traders may be positioned early and that is fine.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers

body:

  - The first element of any rule set is time: when you are allowed to act. "The market is going to deliver based on time."
  - You execute only inside a defined time envelope, such as a macro or the first 30 minutes.
  - Disorganized or "spotty" price delivery in the first 30 minutes is a condition to journal. Compare the first 30 minutes of every day: clean and pretty days versus sloppy ones.
  - The AM session is everything before noon ET. His homework note asks for the noon closing price.
- **How to use:** mark the 9:30–10:00 range, wait for it to complete, and only then look for a model entry. Log the 9:30–10:00 character each day.
- **Example in this video:** the 1-minute chart 9:30–10:00 was "disorganized, sloppy", with volume imbalances tapped twice and wicks but no clean FVG. He called it poor price action.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: New Day / New Week Opening Gaps (NDOG / NWOG) as nested magnets — "Caleb's model" draw  (aliases ICT uses: "black hole", draw on liquidity, layered/nested gaps)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model (draw only; entry is an FVG or iFVG)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Caleb's draw on liquidity is NDOGs and NWOGs. When several are layered or nested together they act "like a big black hole" and a very large magnet that "sucks price in". Retail tools (support/resistance lines, pitchforks) will not show this.
  - The model chain he lays out: OTE (his long-running flagship), then the 2022 model (his daughter's), then the Silver Bullet (Cameron's), and now NDOG/NWOG plus an FVG, "first presentation", as Caleb's model.
  - Gap CE and individual levels matter. Price hammering the CE of the 8/25 NWOG was part of pre-market reading.
- **How to identify:** mark each NDOG/NWOG on the chart and extend it right. Look for clusters where two or more overlap or sit close together below (or above) price.
- **How to use:** target the nested cluster as the draw once a valid entry appears. A "real nice setup": price trades up into an FVG or iFVG, rejects, and then runs down into the nested gaps. Use the CE of a gap as the reaction level.
- **Example in this video:** the 8/23 NDOG and the 8/18 NWOG were nested below price, with the 8/21 NDOG and 8/25 NWOG above. After the 10:00 hour price dropped into the nested 8/23 NDOG / 8/18 NWOG. He pointed to bodies sitting right on the high of the 8/23 NDOG and then accelerating down. "Last Friday" he had said the same cluster would draw price.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:04:04](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=244) — working inside the 8/25 NWOG.
  - [0:38:08](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=2288) — layered 8/23 NDOG and 8/18 NWOG as a big draw.
  - [0:51:04](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=3064) — "huge black hole... Caleb needs to target NDOGs and NWOGs for his draw".
  - [1:17:40](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=4660) — model progression, including this as Caleb's model.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he stresses the model must not be swapped for another PD array just because this one has no trade today. Silver Bullet "is there every day… nothing's changed", and he rebuts creators claiming it stopped working.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Immediate Rebalance  (aliases ICT uses: "one directional and an immediate rebalance")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - It is a single candle with a large range lower and a lower close, clearly bigger than the surrounding ranges, followed by a candle that opens and trades all the way back up to touch the prior candle's low. That low is the level that would have bounded a bearish FVG. The down candle's whole range is re-delivered with buy side, so the gap never forms.
  - The rebalance must happen on the candle immediately after the big down candle. If the first candle does not do it, the next one still counts. After that it is not valid.
  - It works on all timeframes.
  - In a bearish context it is a strong continuation tell, "tipping its hand" like a poker player flashing a full house. It promotes speed and large range, and it is not a reversal.
  - He describes only the bearish case, and says "it matters not if it goes higher or lower" (caption unclear, probably meaning the mirror image is equivalent).
- **How to identify (checklist):**
  1. A low forms.
  2. One candle prints a large down-close range, larger than recent candles.
  3. The next candle (at most the following one) opens and trades back up to the prior candle's low.
- **How to use:** if you are short from higher, or want to short or add (pyramid), anticipate this when the large down candle closes. Watch where the next candle opens and expect it to run back to the prior candle's low, then expect speed to the downside. He says it "might be your model" in itself. Retail chat reads it as a reversal (candlestick logic, "Steve Nison") and gets it backwards.
- **Example in this video:** 1-minute chart just before and around 10:00 ET (video about 0:26–0:31). Price made a low, printed a big down-close candle below the prior candle's low, and the next candle opened and ran back up to that low. Price then took out the low, "boom". He used it as the example of an observation to screenshot and annotate.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:27:38](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1658) — walk-through of the candle sequence.
  - [0:28:25](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1705) — "fair value gaps are not a renaming of imbalance": the superior form is the gap that does not fill in.
  - [0:32:30](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1950) — definition: single big candle, lower close, must be larger than prior ranges.
  - [0:33:18](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1998) — one-or-two-candle window and how to use it.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** the candle-count window is stated slightly inconsistently. At 0:31:40 it is "valid if it does it on the next candle, but after that it's not", and at 0:33:18 he allows the candle after the first. Treat it as one or two candles. The one example is only partly clear in the captions, so the diagram should be redrawn from the description above.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Fair Value Gap — context matters; the "not filling in" form  (aliases ICT uses: inefficiency, BISI/SIBI, volume imbalance)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - "Every gap with three candles" is not an FVG in the sense that matters. You need the surrounding narrative and price action.
  - He criticizes a YouTuber who calls FVGs a renaming of an imbalance. The FVG he cares about is a specific signature where price does not fill in. "The highest order of trading them" is to see them not close in, which he says he proved with real money in live sessions.
  - On Friday he gray-shaded a gap because he wanted to see whether price displaced down from it. It then traded down and went through the gap, so he treated it as an inversion FVG.
  - Viewers who said he was wrong were incorrect, in his account. His usage: the bottom of the gap acts as resistance (premium) and the upper half is left open. (The captions of this explanation are partly garbled.)
- **How to use:** don't trade every three-candle gap. Ask what price is doing around it and whether price respects it or only wicks into it.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:21:06](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1266) — defends the Friday gap and iFVG call.
  - [0:22:42](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1362) — "go back and watch Friday's live stream".
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** this contrasts with the immediate rebalance, where the gap is closed at once and that is read as bullish for continuation. Both are "signatures": a respected un-filled gap, versus a gap redelivered instantly as the algorithm showing its hand.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Inversion FVG (iFVG) on a 15-minute BISI + lower-timeframe entry  (aliases ICT uses: "inversion fair value", BISI / "buy side imbalance sell side inefficiency", "institutional order flow entry drill")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A 15-minute BISI (a big up-close 15-minute candle's gap) sits below price as a discount array. When price finally "snaps through" it (closes through), it becomes an inversion FVG.
  - Use the CE (midpoint) as the key level. The setup is bearish as long as price does not return above that midpoint. It may wick to or through it, but it is better if price only trades back up into the lower half and falls from there. You never want to see price go back into the upper half.
  - Ideal path: price leaves, comes back up, bumps a wick just below the CE, and leaves.
  - Entry on the lower timeframe: on a 15/30/45-second chart (he is on 1-minute), after price leaves the iFVG and displaces away, take the very next FVG that forms on those charts, which he calls the "institutional orderflow entry drill". Then target the next sell-side liquidity or inefficiency.
  - A sell-side target in this case was the nested NDOG/NWOG cluster.
- **How to identify:**
  1. A larger discount array (15-minute BISI) exists below.
  2. Price closes through it (bodies, not just a wick).
  3. Price returns to the high or the CE of the shaded area.
  4. Price stays below the midpoint.
- **How to use:** short from the lower half or CE of the iFVG after a lower-timeframe FVG forms. Stop and size are not given here beyond his general rules. The target is the next sell-side liquidity or a nested NDOG/NWOG.
- **Example in this video:** about 10:05–10:15 ET. Price traded down through two relative equal lows but had not closed through the whole 15-minute BISI. Bounces back up to the high of that gap had bodies not closing in it ("did not close out of it"), so it was "nothing yet". Then price closed through the BISI and he watched it return to the gap for a rejection (iFVG behavior). It later fell toward the nested 8/23 NDOG / 8/18 NWOG and the old low 19,591.75, and accelerated lower. There was no 1-minute FVG at 10:00 to enter from, so there was no trade for Caleb. He said a better setup would have been a rally into a small 1-minute FVG and a drop from it.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:34:05](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=2045) — the 15-minute BISI not fully closed, bodies still show nothing.
  - [0:37:19](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=2239) — price "snapped through"; the CE (half) rule.
  - [0:38:56](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=2336) — return to the high of the gap without a close in it; "neon sign".
  - [0:50:14](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=3014) — iFVG rules and the 15/30/45-second entry drill.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he repeatedly says not to try to pick the bottom ("stinky fingers") while the bodies still say lower. He also says that if price fails even to retrace to the halfway point of a small SIBI, it never reaches the iFVG and likely runs down aggressively with large, quick ranges (0:39:44).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Bodies versus wicks — what the candle closes say
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Wicks into a level prove little. The candle bodies (closes) show whether the narrative has changed. "Look where the bodies are."
  - A wick into the 15-minute BISI or iFVG without a body closing in it means nothing has changed, so don't try to catch the turn.
  - Momentum and delivery being lower means any bounce is only a return to premium. A bullish body or wick alone is not a reversal.
- **How to use:** require closes (bodies) through a level to change your read. Otherwise treat wicks as noise, and sit still.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:34:55](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=2095) — "look where the bodies are… hasn't proven anything yet".
  - [0:43:51](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=2631) — bodies tell the narrative: nothing has changed.
  - [1:14:29](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=4469) — bodies not leaving the 50-minute FVG bullishly.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** this is not a formal ICT rule with a stated number. It is applied repeatedly on 15- and 50-minute arrays in this video.

head: Consequent encroachment (wick CE and ORG CE)  (aliases ICT uses: CE, "rejection block" (usage unclear))
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The CE of a long wick can be used like a gap's CE. If price can overtake the CE of that wick and come back down and show support, that is interesting. If it can't even go up to the premium half, or breaks lower, it is very weak. (Applied on the 1-minute chart in the opening range.)
  - A wick CE example is 19,701 on the 15-minute chart.
  - The ORG high is not a CE. The CE is the midpoint of the gap.
  - He also says "we're only working with the rejection block, which is the lowest down close candle... closing price" (caption unclear). He seems to refer to the lowest down-close candle's close as the reference.
- **Timestamps:**

head: Retail logic that misleads: three drives, divergence, hidden divergence
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example only
- **What ICT says:**
  - Three consecutive lows (three drives, "three Indians" in Street Smarts) look like a reversal pattern to retail traders. The bodies said nothing had changed.
  - Standard momentum divergence (RSI/CCI/MACD/stochastic) would have shown bullish divergence at the lows. He lost money on it in 1992–94 and says price doesn't respect it.
  - Trend-following (type 2) divergence, a higher indicator high against a lower price high, is a "hidden divergence". He credits Nick Vanise for it (name as captioned, unclear) and says it is the useful form.
  - "My stuff makes your retail stuff work."
- **Timestamps:** [0:49:27](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=2967) — three drives read; [1:23:12](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=4992) — divergence.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Model selection and not model-hopping  (aliases: Enigma, "right-now model")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Pick one model and don't swap it because another would have worked today. "I'm only interested in price if it shows me what I'm looking for."
  - ICT himself has different models for different conditions: choppy/listless markets, trending markets (three or four), reversals, MMBM/MMSM, and intraday volatility. The last is Enigma, which needs no bias, no long-term draws and no PD arrays.
  - A model that gives no setup today is not worse than one that did. Wanting your model in every day, session or instant is the problem.
  - The "right-now model" is whatever you grab to justify getting in, and it is the one that blows accounts.
  - Don't reach for OBs or OTE just because the assigned model has no setup.
  - A model that doesn't fire gives a win: no commission, no loss, practiced patience.
  - He notes it would be easy to show off setups outside Caleb's model and collect praise, but that would not teach Caleb anything (1:13:41).
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:55:55](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=3355) — "not better than Kayla's model" (the caption says Kayla; he means Caleb's model).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Stop-loss philosophy and Caleb's risk rules  (aliases: risk management, one contract, one trade a day)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Never trade without a stop-loss. The stop is a real structural stop (not "a two-handle stop-loss"), placed where you are definitely wrong.
  - A stop defines the moment you are wrong and pays for the lesson. Size so the stop does not hurt: a loss must not shake trust in the model or stop you from taking another trade.
  - People who avoid stops keep blowing funded accounts.
  - Caleb's rules: one contract only, micro first. At most one trade a day. One winning trade for the day, you're done. One losing trade, you're done. Turn the charts off.
  - Funded-account plan: take roughly $5,000 out of the funded account, then move to a live account at AMP Global (the broker he names). Trade a micro and build slowly toward one standard lot, only when trading at 1.5x the full exchange margin. A standard lot on a $300 account is reckless.
  - Fees: commissions are "piranha". Example: $1,000 made on $1,200 of commissions is a loss. Fewer trades means lower costs. One good trade a week puts you ahead of 99% of retail. Four trades a month keeps commissions minimal.
  - The "shield first" idea: learn to survive with small risk before using the sword.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [1:35:05](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=5705) — a real stop; you are wrong if it hits.
  - [1:36:39](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=5799) — never trade without a stop.
  - [1:39:04](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=5944) — one contract, micro first.
  - [1:48:39](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=6519) — commissions math.
  - [1:55:57](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=6957) — $5,000 payout, then AMP Global, margin rule.
  - [1:57:34](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=7054) — one win or one loss and done.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** these are Caleb's personal rules, but ICT says they are why you "cannot blow the account". For general viewers he stresses that overleveraging and a standard lot versus a micro is the early mistake.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Coin-flip opening range gap system (a mechanical challenge)
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** flip a coin (heads buy, tails sell) at the first return to the opening range gap, and use the other end of the opening range as the stop. If you risk no more than a quarter of 1%, he says it is profitable by the end of the year. He challenges viewers to test it in a system tester. The point is that a mechanical, bias-free rule beats most discretion, and following rules is the hard part.
- **Timestamps:** [1:42:18](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=6138); [1:43:06](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=6186).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Journaling and observation protocol (screenshot prompts)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Whenever ICT makes a special reference ("watch this wick/FVG"), screenshot it, annotate your observation, and later record what happened. These are his prompts for review at the end of the session (about 11:00 ET).
  - Watch old recordings with the sound off, pause when price does something notable, and annotate it on your own charts. Keep a running log from a template, and revisit it on weekends and again 3–6 months later.
  - Write down what you thought at the time (for example "it can't drop more") and what signatures showed nothing had changed.
  - Homework that day: go through every delivery on the 1-minute, 5-minute and 15-minute charts. Match each retracement and each up-close candle on the 1-minute/5-minute to its reference point on the 15-minute. Note every inefficiency that stayed open, and note the noon close price (everything before noon is the AM run).
  - The "green apple" analogy: five red apples and one green. Train your attention on your single PD array so you don't chase every movement.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:26:50](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=1610) — screenshot prompts.
  - [0:55:07](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=3307) — green apple, reticular activating system.
  - [0:55:55](https://youtu.be/iLe_4m84_yw?t=3355) — watch recordings, annotate, keep a template.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #17  August 26, 2024  Impeding Barriers
head: Retail sentiment as a contrarian indicator
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** other live streamers' chats and social posts are a retail indicator. The more people are excited about a direction, or opinionated the other way from his read, the better he feels about his own idea. If crowds aren't excited he weights it less. The urge to join in is strongest when others say "I'm long / I'm short".
