title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: First-presented FVG: 3-day life cycle and reuse  (aliases: first presentation FVG, first FVG 9:30-10:00)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:** Carry each day's first-presented FVG (the first FVG that forms in the opening range 9:30–10:00 ET) forward on your chart for a 3-day life cycle. After the third day its importance wanes in his view, though it can still be used. He shows yesterday's (Thursday Aug 29) first-presented FVG in green and describes today's price reacting to it. Opening range = 9:30 to 10:00.
- **How to use:** Price tapping beneath relative equal lows, touching the 9:30 opening price, then popping off the consequent encroachment (CE) of yesterday's first-presented FVG is, to him, a possible single narrow "model": one small, repeatable thing to look for, then sit still the rest of the day.
- **Example in this video:** After the open (NQ with a big premium gap) price dropped into yesterday's first-presented FVG, took the relative equal lows beneath, tagged the 9:30 opening price, popped off the CE of yesterday's FVG, and rallied to pump above the initial/minor buy-side liquidity, forming today's first FVG in the 9:30–10:00 window. Price then came back into the opening range and into that new FVG. Later in the morning price traded down into yesterday's first-presented FVG again ([0:59:15](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=3555)).
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:33](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=393) — 3-day life cycle and the pop off the CE; [0:11:06](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=666) — "that could be your model"; [0:20:58](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1258) — recap of the opening sequence; [0:55:05](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=3305) — watching whether price gets back above today's first FVG.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** A new, specific number (3 days) for how long the first-presented FVG stays relevant. He stresses that students should note the setups they can reliably recognise.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Immediate rebalance (immediate rebound) rule  (aliases: immediate rebounds)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (caption partly unclear)
- **What ICT says:** After an expansion candle, a bullish PD array will usually see the very next candle trade back to the level (the high of the candle prior to the expansion, i.e. the edge of the gap) and then run immediately — sometimes within the same candle, sometimes the very next. If it returns once more and closes with its body into the area, price has to show quick "go go go" strength, otherwise it is "problematic".
- **Example in this video:** Candle runs up into the opening price, next candle trades down into the level (immediate rebalance), then another dip closes on the body; he says it now must expand to make a higher high of the day or the idea fails.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:45](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=765) — rules for immediate rebounds; [0:14:57](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=897) — after leaving the ORG, does it keep going or come back in?
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First time this term appears in these three lectures; precise candle definition is uncertain from captions.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Naked chart with raw price levels (notepad method)  (aliases: levels in raw form, naked chart)
body:
- **Kind:** process / refinement
- **What ICT says:** He keeps his chart naked and keeps the levels he is watching in a notepad in raw price form, so he gets a clean measurement between what price is doing and what it can do by reading the price axis against his notes. He anticipates price running to those levels; they only appear on the chart when price presents and "books" there. He draws levels on charts in these lectures only for teaching. Having all levels drawn without an outlined narrative is confusing and lets trolls say "it will hit one of them".
- **How to use:** For each level ask: if it is a premium level, does it repel price lower or stop it going higher? If a discount level, does it hold price up or is it smashed through easily? Couple that with an easy narrative (time of day, draw on liquidity); let setups that go against your bias pass.
- **Timestamps:** [0:19:05](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1145) — what next level is it reaching for; [0:21:56](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1316) — too many levels without a narrative; [0:23:31](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1411) — notepad and naked chart.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** In the same stretch he mentions an "event horizon" — roughly the midpoint region between the Aug 18 NWOG above and the nearest NDOG below, used as a raw-number reference zone (caption unclear on the exact definition).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Layered NDOG/NWOG clusters as speed bumps  (aliases: nested opening gaps, high-resistance run conditions, "congestion")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / condition filter
- **What ICT says:** When new day and new week opening gaps are nested close together near price (here the Aug 27 NDOG, the Aug 18 NWOG and the Aug 16 NDOG), price needs a real, significant move to slice through, and the algorithm "constantly refers back" to them while they are within the time frame he specifies. A cluster acts as an initial draw. If price fails to even reach the lowest threshold of the cluster (here the Aug 18 NWOG low) and drops below its low, it is tipping its hand that it does not want to go higher. This is not a lack of buyers or a sellers' imbalance (he calls that nonsensical): you are measuring the efficiency of price reaching premium arrays and whether it has the "pursuit" to reach the next one. If instead price slices aggressively through (one or two candles), ignoring them, it signals it is in a hurry, usually because of an imbalance or liquidity pool it is targeting.
- **How to identify:** Plot the last few NDOG/NWOG ranges; check proximity to current price. With few of them near price, runs are cleaner and more elongated ("interstate highway early in the morning"); clustered close together they impede flow and produce short-lived moves ("speed bumps").
- **How to use:** If bearish, you want discount arrays "demolished" with no respect, for a fast run; if price struggles at each one, the market is not fast, do not push. Test: does a premium level repel price, does a discount level hold it?
- **Example in this video:** NQ Aug 30: opens with a huge premium opening gap above, runs up, falls about one tick short of the Aug 18 NWOG high (about 19,629 vs a 19,628.75 high), rolls back into the 9:30 opening price / Aug 27 NDOG high, and chops for the rest of the morning with repeated short-term highs taken and little follow-through.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:20](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1460) — nested gaps, what slicing through means; [0:25:08](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1508) — failing to reach the NWOG low = tipping its hand; [0:31:15](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1875) — cleaner when gaps are far apart; [0:32:49](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1969) — disrespect of the array shows urgency; [0:38:38](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2318) — one tick short of the NWOG high.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Builds directly on lecture 19/20 (layered gaps, high-resistance runs). New here: the "tipping its hand" test and the explicit proximity/clean-run comparison. He also calls the resulting chop "time distortion" (caption unclear).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Fridays and holidays: when not to push your edge  (aliases: day of week tendency, Friday into a long weekend, holiday volume)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / day-of-week tendency
- **What ICT says:** This is the Friday before Labor Day weekend. He is not saying "never trade Fridays": people take his words out of context. Generally he likes to make money before Friday because Friday is the last bit of a daily/weekly candle: in a bullish week the daily candle opens near its low and closes near its high, so Friday usually will not make a much higher high or have a deep retracement and mostly works inside Thursday's range. On a holiday Friday, deep-pocketed institutions are largely not participating, so you do not get clean institutional order flow; they roll stops to a manageable level and leave. Treat the week as non-farm-payroll-like: the easier price action comes early in the week. Also be wary of the first day after a holiday (Tuesday) while volume irons out.
- **How to use:** He only trades such a day if he can identify a daily/4h/1h pool of liquidity or inefficiency target; otherwise he does nothing. His son Caleb is told not to trade Fridays going into holiday weekends. Never push (dull) a sharpened, tested edge on days like these ("don't push, push, push"); the market is fickle.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This clarifies, not contradicts, earlier "Friday" advice. He explicitly rejects the shorthand "ICT says never trade Mondays/Fridays". He also says light volume does not mean price runs because of buy/sell pressure: it means fewer participants for the algorithm to mark to market against; you need the stage set (participants, clean runs) for efficient trading.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:26](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=266) — holiday weekend, no stream Monday/Tuesday; [0:28:01](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=1681) — don't trade Fridays into holidays, treat week like NFP week; [0:48:41](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2921) — only trade with a daily/4h/1h target; [0:49:27](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2967) — Friday is the last of the daily candle; [0:56:46](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=3406) — don't push your edge.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Economic calendar planning and news days  (aliases: news drivers, NFP, FOMC, fake first run)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** On the weekend, look at the whole next month of the calendar for heavy, medium and high-impact news drivers. The days before high-impact events (e.g. before FOMC) can be quiet; the public thinks "the casino is open" on days like NFP Friday. Students can trade those days only after the initial shock wave, and hold no opinion going into them. The first run on a high-impact news driver is the fake one (the "first mouse" gets caught; you pick up the cheese afterwards). News events like FOMC and NFP are, in his words, heavily manually intervened.
- **Timestamps:** [1:08:12](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4092) — look at next month's calendar; [1:08:59](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4139) — trade after the initial shock wave; [1:09:47](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4187) — first run is fake; [0:34:26](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2066) — manual intervention on FOMC/NFP.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He also says brokers may lift/limit execution around news; this is aside commentary, not a trading rule.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Back-testing price at known levels and the "hunter" model  (aliases: backtesting, model building, hunter analogy)
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:** Over the weekend go through the charts and study how many times and at what time of day price traded into a given area (here the Aug 18 NWOG with the Aug 27 NDOG inside): how it behaved, what formations appeared, whether there were frameable runs, what it aimed for, how long it took from a first FVG or a low being taken until the opposite-direction run, and how much range it moved. Framing that is "the first beginning point of a limitless supply of setups". Hunter analogy: tracks in the snow are the evidence, a hide (tree stand) is your trade location, and you hunt the one thing (deer, elk) you prefer; likewise each trader picks the specific repeating phenomenon that appeals to them. He says he can make a new model every day because they are built on how the algorithm behaves around certain events, and that he will teach next week how to use higher-timeframe charts in a top-down approach and anticipate setups in advance.
- **How to use:** Start with whatever jumps out at you; it need not be your model for life. Journal the examples, screenshot them.
- **Timestamps:** [0:39:41](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2381) — study old price action, start with what jumps out; [1:00:07](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=3607) — checklist of what to review; [1:01:41](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=3701) — hunter analogy; [1:04:54](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=3894) — next week plan.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Homework: watch the 2016 month four core content (about eight short videos) where he introduced the PD matrix, and choose which PD arrays make sense to you ([1:11:25](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4285)).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Journaling, positive self-talk and not announcing predictions  (aliases: reticular activating system, tape reading, scar tissue)
body:
- **Kind:** psychology / process
- **What ICT says:** Journal the examples you could not see live, with positive self-talk, to "trick" your subconscious into expecting those conditions (activating the reticular activating system) so you spot them while tape reading. Do not share predictions on social media: it raises the need to be right and to save face, and being wrong then costs you emotionally (scar tissue). Journaling the call and feeding the journal positive recognition avoids chasing significance, being liked, or respected.
- **Timestamps:** [0:40:29](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2429) — journal with positive self-talk; [0:41:18](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2478) — don't tell people what you think will happen; [0:42:06](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=2526).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Liquidity is the lifeblood; algorithm "patches" inefficiency; inducement and smart-money traps are not real  (aliases: algorithm doctrine, engineering liquidity, one contract marks price)
body:
- **Kind:** doctrine / definition
- **What ICT says:** The market moves on liquidity. Where a price range has none (an inefficiency), price is "deficient" and goes there to provide liquidity/efficiency ("patchwork"), then decides whether to continue its current program (e.g. sell program, reprice lower) or reach to liquidity above the inefficiency. It can "engineer" liquidity: encourage traders to use obvious levels (relative equal highs as resistance, stops above/below old lows) — that engineering is real. Price moves because only one contract needs to trade between one buyer and one seller (mark to market); candles do not measure how many contracts traded; volume is a red herring. The algorithm does not see your stops or know how many contracts sit under an old low; it goes to levels defined by reference points. He states that "inducement" (as taught by some who got leaked content) and "smart money traps" are not real concepts.
- **Timestamps:** [1:15:27](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4527) — liquidity as lifeblood, engineering liquidity; [1:16:16](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4576) — "inducement" and smart-money traps not real; [1:17:52](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4672) — one contract is enough, volume a red herring; [1:19:27](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4767) — patching inefficiency, then next program.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Directly contradicts the usual "inducement" framing in ICT-derived retail content; also repeats and sharpens lecture 19's statement that the algorithm does not know how many orders are resting.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Dealers vs traders; floor traders and yesterday's high/low  (aliases: market makers are dealers, floor pivots)
body:
- **Kind:** aside / definition
- **What ICT says:** Market makers/desk traders are dealers who handle price piped to them; they do not originate it and often cannot call where price is going. Ex-pit floor traders had a "pulse of the market" edge and used yesterday's high/low plus floor pivot numbers (e.g. R1 just above yesterday's high suggests a run to yesterday's high); on charts today they struggle, and he says VWAP and volume profile are excuses for entries, not edges. The bridge from pit activity to chart is the PD array/liquidity framework he teaches.
- **Timestamps:** [1:20:14](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4814) — dealers not traders; [1:22:34](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=4954) — floor traders, pivots and yesterday's high/low; [1:28:11](https://youtu.be/eYYyonGwTRs?t=5291) — VWAP/volume profile.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Lecture #21  August 30, 2024
head: Late-morning short: institutional order entry drill into Tuesday's low  (aliases: bearish order block with CISD, minor sell-side, Tuesday's low)
body:
- **Kind:** example
- **What ICT says:** Around 11:00 AM, after the jagged upside (lots of sell-side resting underneath), he points to a bearish order block whose opening price is the change in the state of delivery; the roll-over from there, aiming at Tuesday's (Aug 27) low, "might be your model" for a quick 25 handles and done. Mid-gap (CE) of an FVG was hit before 10:00 and a 3/4 closure of the gap was in play. Tuesday's low had been used a lot that week and sits in the lower end of the opening range gap. For a beginner like Caleb he prefers these short-term strikes with immediate feedback: get in, get out, be done for the day.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: RTH Opening Range Gap (ORG) and its 70% midpoint rule  (aliases ICT uses: opening range gap, "regular trading hours gap", "midgap", "half the gap", "the gap" between settlement and open)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (statistical tendency) / definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Toggle TradingView to regular trading hours (RTH) to see it: the gap runs from the previous day's closing/settlement price to the first traded price at the 9:30 open. He toggles the chart between RTH and ETH (electronic trading hours) to show it.
  - If price opens below the prior settlement it is a **discount ORG**; if it opens above it is a **premium ORG** (he only walks through the discount case in detail, so the premium side is the implied mirror).
  - The midpoint of the gap is the key level: "70% of the time" price will trade to that midpoint ("half the gap") **between 9:30 and 10:00 ET**. He says he derived the figure going back to 1987 using pre-electronic/Globex numbers, and tells students to journal it daily to verify it themselves.
  - Because the open was lower than settlement, price is more likely to trade **up** first, seeking buy-side liquidity. As a student you are not trying to call full gap closure, just the move into the midpoint.
  - 70% is not 100%: the previous day (Tue 9/3) opened lower, only a tiny wick got into the gap, never reached even a quarter of it, and the market "fell out of bed" — he uses this as the proof it is a probability, not a guarantee.
- **How to identify:** Switch to RTH; draw the box from prior RTH close to 9:30 open; mark its midpoint (50%). Note the size — on 9/4 NQ was "over 100 handles" below prior settlement, which he calls a very large discount gap. Log in your journal whether the midpoint traded between 9:30 and 10:00.
- **How to use:** Treat the midpoint as a first target (partial) for longs taken after a discount open, or as an area where a trade is "done" for the learner — "you don't care what it does after that." Combine with the first-presentation FVG as an entry and a New Day/Week Opening Gap above the midpoint as the next objective (see below).
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Wed 9/4/2024. Large discount ORG (>100 handles below Tue's settlement). At the 9:30 open price makes a small drop, then rallies, creating the first 1-min FVG (shaded white). Price then trades up to the ORG midpoint inside 9:30–10:00 — ICT: "there's the 70% strike rate." The prior day (Tue 9/3) is the counterexample (gap opened lower, midpoint never tagged).
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:48](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=888) — "70% of the time between 9:30 and 10:00" the midgap is traded to · [0:31:55](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=1915) — premium vs discount ORG and the midpoint · [0:32:47](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=1967) — Tuesday's failure case · [0:33:35](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2015) — origin of the 70% figure (back to 1987)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He frames this as a "low-hanging fruit" model, not the best-of-the-best setup. Wicks may exceed levels; the probability is for trading *to* the midpoint, not holding it.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: Opening Range (9:30–10:00 ET) and "first presentation" FVG  (aliases ICT uses: first Fair Value Gap, first presentation of the fair value gap, "the real opening range")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The opening range is **9:30 to 10:00 ET, the first 30 minutes**. He says any other definition of opening range is "a gimmick"; this is what the algorithm references.
  - The first FVG that forms in that window is the "first presentation" FVG. Sometimes the trade sets up inside the window, sometimes after it, but you always get to study/seek that first FVG.
  - On **trending days** you only get one chance at it before price keeps going; on **non-trending days** price returns to it several times, offering a trade or a target.
  - On normal days candle **bodies stay inside** the first FVG's range (wicks may poke out). After a large-range day the bodies spill outside the FVG ("colors outside the lines") and the setup looks muddy.
- **How to identify:** From the 9:30 open, find the first 3-candle FVG (he uses the 1-min chart live); shade it; note its high, low and midpoint (CE). Track whether candle bodies respect it.
- **How to use:** Enter on the retrace into the first FVG in the direction of the gap-implied draw; partial at the ORG midpoint; extend to the New Day Opening Gap (see model below). A contrarian trader can instead fade it once it has been violated (see iFVG concept).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 9/4/2024: small drop after 9:30, rally creating the white-shaded first FVG at ~9:31; price trades through it, bodies close outside it (the distortion he highlights at 0:13:06), later comes back, hits it, then rallies again to the relative equal highs and lays a candle body over the NDOG (he teases Twitter critics who said the FVG "failed" — he expected it to be reclaimed).
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:31](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=691) — opening range defined 9:30–10:00 · [0:12:17](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=737) — trending vs non-trending days and the first FVG · [0:13:06](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=786) — body outside the FVG = post-large-range distortion · [1:01:28](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=3688) — price returns to the "reclaimed" first FVG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says the FVG is "not the best PD array I have" — he leans on it because it is obvious to new students ("deer in headlights") — and that "the best ones you'll never learn" ([0:18:15](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=1095)). Use of the 9:30–10:00 window as the single definition of opening range is stated as a firm rule here.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: NDOG / NWOG inside the ORG as the extension target  (aliases ICT uses: new day opening gap, new week opening gap, "Terminus" for the final target)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - If a New Day Opening Gap (or New Week Opening Gap) sits **inside the ORG and above its midpoint** on a discount-gap day, the odds improve that price keeps going from the midpoint up to that gap — "a very strong 70%."
  - It does not need to be both an NDOG and an NWOG, and you do not need the whole gap: "it could be just the low" of the gap — the first level reached is the target ("low-hanging fruit"). Do not hunt "the best of the best."
  - The model as he states it at 0:59:51: **buy the first fair value gap → partial at the midgap → Terminus at the NDOG low.**
  - After that, expect price to possibly sweep around both sides of the NDOG and reach for a full gap closure (the ORG high) — treated as a bonus, not the plan.
- **How to identify:** On RTH, draw the ORG; mark its midpoint; plot the NDOG and check whether it lies in the upper half of the ORG. NDOG on 9/4 was around 18993.75 and 18999.75 (caption unclear: "18993 and three quarters, 18,999 and three quarters").
- **How to use:** Long entry in the first FVG, take a partial at ORG midpoint, run the remainder to the NDOG low. Longs that did not take profit at the NDOG got run over fast — he stresses taking something off there.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 9/4/2024: after the rally to the ORG midpoint, price continues to the NDOG (upper quadrant of the ORG), then sells off sharply around the 10:00 ET news print (see liquidity concept) toward Tuesday's daily low. Later in the session price pushes slightly above the relative equal highs and the NDOG top — "went just a little above it" — and he leaves open a further attempt to the full gap closure.
- **Timestamps:** [0:33:35](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2015) — NDOG/NWOG inside the ORG above midpoint · [0:36:47](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2207) — the whole sequence recapped as a model that "will hit, will stick" · [0:37:35](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2255) — only one level needed, low-hanging fruit · [0:59:51](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=3591) — FVG → partial midgap → Terminus NDOG low
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Terminus" is used loosely here as the final target of the trade (he also says "wait for my partials and wait for my Terminus to be hit," [0:56:43](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=3403)); he does not define it as a named model in this video.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: Post-large-range-day / post-holiday morning rule  (aliases ICT uses: "sit on your hands," "sit still," fickle morning session)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - After a very large range day (up or down), or the day after a holiday, **do not trade the AM session while you are learning** — price tends to be "fickle," chopping back and forth with unclear, muddy setups.
  - The higher-probability setups come in the **afternoon (PM) session, which begins at 1:30 PM ET**, and he also points to the **2:00 macro, 1:50–2:10 ET**.
  - Experienced traders can trade the morning, but only if they know what is most likely to happen; beginners who force trades "go into tilt," buying and selling back and forth.
  - He says this advice appears in the 2016/2017 mentorship content, so it is not form-fitting after the fact.
  - Context for 9/4: Tue 9/3 was a very large-range down day (post-Labor Day), closing on the low; the daily chart shows a big down-close candle. That is what made Wed AM "wonky."
  - Why: everyone saw yesterday's down day, so the late-to-market crowd wants to short at the open; that tends to engineer buy-side liquidity to be run (he adds "not always but generally").
- **How to identify:** Daily chart shows an unusually large-range candle the day before (or the day follows a market holiday). Check that price opened with a large gap.
- **How to use:** Skip or heavily limit AM trades; mark your levels; journal what happens; focus on PM 1:30 onward and the 2:00 macro.
- **Example in this video:** On Tue 9/3 he says he waited and traded the PM session (he refers to yesterday's PM trade, shown on Caleb's channel). He says that, in hindsight, a short AM entry would have been at the CE of the daily imbalance and he would have held 2–3 contracts into 1:30.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:20](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=440) — sit on your hands after large-range days · [0:13:54](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=834) — why retail shorts the open · [0:19:02](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=1142) — "it's in the 2016/2017 content" · [0:27:02](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=1622) — PM begins 1:30 ET, 2:00 macro 1:50–2:10 · [0:27:51](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=1671) — where the AM short entry would have been
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** It is a protocol to protect learners, not a claim that no AM trade exists. The "2:00 macro 1:50–2:10" here is stated as a time window to learn the PM, not as a standalone entry model.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: Consequent Encroachment (CE) of the Aug 13, 2024 daily FVG  (aliases ICT uses: midpoint, "mid gap," BISI = buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - An FVG is bounded by the low of one candle and the high of another (the gap between candles 1 and 3); its midpoint is the consequent encroachment. He describes the Aug 13 daily FVG as a BISI.
  - He draws the CE as "the middle of the range defined by this candle's low and that candle's high" and uses the same midpoint idea on the daily FVG, the ORG and the 1-min first FVG.
  - If price intends to rise from a lower level, it is better if it does **not** come back down to touch a midpoint below (which gap's midpoint is not clear from the captions).
  - He notes a small volume imbalance in the Aug 13 FVG area that "gets worked out" naturally by the candle's high.
- **How to identify:** Mark the gap between the two outer candles' wicks; add a line at 50%.
- **How to use:** Use the Aug 13 daily FVG high / CE / low as the daily-timeframe draw for the pre-open plan: price ranging between the FVG's high and CE before the open; if price rolls over and takes the opening-range low, the next draw is into that daily FVG below.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15-min pre-open: price ranges between the Aug 13 daily FVG high and its CE; ICT's stated plan ([0:09:45](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=585)) is to see price trade to the ORG midgap, possibly reach the upper part of the ORG, then roll over and, if it takes the low formed in the new opening range, drop into the Aug 13 FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:33](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=393) — Aug 13 daily FVG definition and midpoint · [0:10:34](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=634) — plan: midgap then maybe the Aug 13 FVG below · [0:22:08](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=1328) — "here is consequent encroachment"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He explicitly says he is "not trying to push a narrative" pre-open — exploring both sides.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: Buy-side / sell-side liquidity, relative equal highs and the "news smokescreen"  (aliases ICT uses: opposing liquidity, SSL below Tuesday's low, REH)
body:
- **Kind:** example / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Tuesday (9/3) daily low and the lows formed in the new opening range are the sell-side liquidity below; relative equal highs plus the top of the NDOG are the buy-side liquidity above ("that's the liquidity" — take a screenshot).
  - Stops for traders who shorted the open sit above; the market runs them first, then forms the first FVG.
  - He says that **high or medium-impact news** on the economic calendar is used as a "smoke screen" so a drop looks like selling pressure. The 10:00 reaction after NDOG was an example: longs who stayed in past the NDOG were hit quickly and price went down to Tuesday's daily low, where sell-side liquidity rested.
  - After a large down day, "street money" (retail) wants to repeat yesterday's profitable direction (short). Smart money buys into the lows and rallies to the NDOG in the upper quadrant of the ORG. (His narration of who is being drawn in is loose; paraphrase with care.)
- **How to identify:** Mark prior day low/high, REH/REL, and the NDOG edges; note scheduled news times.
- **How to use:** Expect price to run the nearest obvious liquidity first and reverse into the PD array; avoid holding longs through a stop-run at the target level without a partial.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 9/4/2024: price drops/runs lows first, forms first FVG, rallies to ORG midpoint and NDOG, reverses sharply around 10:00 ET into the Tuesday daily low, later returns and pokes through the REH/NDOG top.
- **Timestamps:** [0:35:12](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2112) — "invisible barrier" at the NDOG · [0:36:00](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2160) — news as smokescreen · [0:43:58](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2638) — REH + top of NDOG as the liquidity · [0:47:07](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2827) — street money vs smart money positioning
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The event is not named (he does not say which 10:00 release); do not assume one.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: Inversion FVG (iFVG) contrarian short  (aliases ICT uses: inversion fair value gap, reclaimed fair value gap)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (contrarian alternative) / example
- **What ICT says:** A trader who is bearish can fade the move by shorting an **inversion FVG** — "extend it over here, you can see the body respecting it" — and targeting the sell-side liquidity he had outlined. He says several of his students took exactly this trade, as well as the long from the first FVG to the 70% midpoint.
- **How to identify:** An FVG that price has closed through, which then acts as resistance on retest (bodies respect it from the other side).
- **How to use:** Short on the retest of the inverted gap; target the sell-side below (the Tuesday low / opening-range low).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1-min, after the first FVG was violated, the gap flips to resistance; price retests it and falls toward the sell-side he outlined. Later he calls the original first FVG a "reclaimed" FVG as price comes back, hits it, and rallies again to the REH.
- **Timestamps:** [1:00:39](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=3639) — short at an iFVG, target sell side · [1:01:28](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=3688) — "reclaimed fair value gap" (caption unclear on exact term)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He offers this only as a contrarian option while his preferred read was the long to the midgap/NDOG. No stop or size is given.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 04, 2024
head: Entries, partials and "one setup is enough"  (aliases ICT uses: low-hanging fruit, early-onset maturity)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (execution mindset)
- **What ICT says:** All you need is one repeatable piece — e.g. buy the FVG, get to the halfway point of the gap — "and you don't care what it does after that." Beginners want the full swing and expect to capture the whole move; that is unrealistic. If you can only frame a trade one way and you are in it, you have no anxiety, wait for partials/Terminus, and accept being stopped out in profit on a trail.
- **How to use:** As he frames it: pick one clear objective (midpoint, NDOG low), take partials there, trail any remainder with a stop, and do not second-guess a trade framed in one way.
- **Example in this video:** The long from the first FVG to the ORG midpoint was his "model"; the NDOG low is the extension.
- **Timestamps:** [0:49:30](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=2970) — one setup to the midpoint · [0:56:43](https://youtu.be/Ipjk9S8HTbA?t=3403) — partials, Terminus, trailing stop
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** No stop-loss rule, size or R multiple is stated in this video.

head: Turtle Soup short ("the real turtle soup") / One Shot One Kill  (aliases ICT uses: OSOK, "one shot one kill", fading a retail bull flag)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - This is "a turtle soup short, one shot one kill": he sells short by fading a retail bull flag into old highs, willing to let price run up and sweep those highs first.
  - "The real turtle soup" = knowing how to operate inside the daily candlestick: understanding what the range will do, where it will go and how it forms, so that the stop is in the right place.
  - He worked a **bearish order block** and annotated the **sell-side liquidity** below as the objective.
  - The whole position was one trade (single entry sequence at/near the high of the day), not a series of separate trades; he jokes about people claiming $100,000 in four days — "what took you so long?"
- **How to identify:** Price sweeps old/relative equal highs (retail sees a bull flag / breakout), reaches a bearish order block, and the higher-timeframe draw is down into a daily FVG / sell-side liquidity.
- **How to use:** Short into the sweep of the highs from the bearish order block; hold for the daily-range delivery rather than scalping; target the sell side below and the daily FVG midpoint.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Thursday 9/5 to Friday 9/6/2024. He enters near the high of the day (his fills are shown at 8:05: an initial fill near the high, then adds of 4 and 4 more contracts — initial size not stated clearly in the captions), holds through the day, and covers on a limit order at the $100,000 profit level after price reaches the CE of the Aug 13, 2024 daily FVG in the London session.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:01](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=1) — turtle soup short, OSOK, bearish OB, SSL annotated · [0:03:12](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=192) — "the real turtle soup … how you operate inside of the daily candlesticks" · [0:07:18](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=438) — one single trade at the highs attacking the $100,000 level · [0:08:05](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=485) — fills shown: adds of 4 and 4, then the exit
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He does not give the stop distance or the initial size. "Turtle soup" here is defined by the context (sweep of highs, daily range logic), not by a lookback count.

body:
- **Kind:** example / definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - "What you're looking at here was a market maker sell model that delivered down to the August 13th, 2024 daily fair value gap consequent encroachment" — the midpoint of that daily gap was the objective.
  - He had signalled that level in advance through commentary on the live streams and reviews; the price delivery matches those annotations.
  - He frames the question "if there's a smart money entity, how would they trade?" and answers with this trade: sell the highs, hold, deliver to the daily PD array.
  - If he had wanted the full daily range, the CE of the Aug 13 FVG at the close of Thursday's day would have been that point.
- **How to identify:** Daily FVG below (Aug 13 BISI), highs above swept first, then price delivers down to the gap's midpoint.
- **How to use:** Use the daily FVG CE as the profit objective for a short taken at the high of the range; anticipate the delivery from earlier annotated levels.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: entries near the high of the day on Thursday 9/5, price then delivers down to the Aug 13 daily FVG CE (the sequence of intermediate levels is only partly clear from the captions, including a sweep of Wednesday 9/4's first FVG level, which he says he was willing to see swept); the Friday London session is shown pushing again into that CE with sell side just below it.

title: ICT NQ Live Execution September 6, 2024 100k [OSOK]
head: Adding to the position / pyramiding  (aliases ICT uses: adding, pyramiding opportunity, "orange level")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Places where he could have added: sweeps of relative equal highs, retraces back up into the NDOG ("anytime it touches that you add more"), the first-FVG levels from earlier days (e.g., the first FVG of Wednesday 9/4), and an "orange level" he calls a pyramiding opportunity at the start of the new trading day.
  - **Condition for adding on retraces into the NDOG:** only "as long as it doesn't take out the high" between **2:30 PM and 3:00 PM** — if that window's high is exceeded the add is invalid.
  - He says he would be interested in adding, but an add in that spot would come "after midnight on the following day" (caption unclear on exactly which add this refers to).
  - He is not interested in adding in the final hour of the daily range on that day; he prefers to hold what he has and not watch the chart the whole time ("I knew what I was looking for").
- **How to identify:** Mark the prior days' first-FVG levels, relative equal highs, the NDOG, and the 2:30–3:00 PM high; adds happen on retraces up into these while the reference high holds.
- **How to use:** Add on each tag of the NDOG / first-FVG level while the 2:30–3:00 PM high remains intact; avoid adding after that high is taken out.
- **Example in this video:** Fills at 8:05 show the initial entry near the high, then adds of 4 and then 4 more contracts (he says "right there," near the high); the retraces up to the NDOG and relative equal highs are the add areas he points out on the 1-min chart.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:26](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=146) — REH and the final-hour add, but he declines it · [0:03:12](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=192) — add into the NDOG if the 2:30–3:00 high is not taken out · [0:05:39](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=339) — orange level as pyramiding opportunity · [0:08:05](https://youtu.be/N9RW9v2kOoY?t=485) — the actual adds

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: News drivers: NFP / FOMC / CPI / PPI handling  (aliases ICT uses: "manual intervention", high/medium-impact news driver)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - NFP is "not algorithmic": like FOMC (and CPI, PPI) it is a manual intervention, where "they literally pick where they want it to go abruptly". The same logic (run to liquidity / inefficiency) still applies, it is just delivered abruptly and farther outside the normal range.
  - Do not try to position ahead of it (he would have terrible stats; he does not know where they will run it first). Do not trade the release itself. Earliest anyone should trade NFP is about 15 minutes after the 8:30 release (8:45 ET); 20-30 minutes after is better. If already in a trade you can leave a small runner.
  - After the initial shock, look at what is "left behind" (smooth edges / inefficiencies / untouched pools); that is what price goes for next.
  - Why you cannot trade the first minutes: slippage (his example: aiming to buy 18,845 and getting filled 18,862 or worse, which blows up your risk), requotes, or no fill at all. Brokers "pull their engagement" because retail over-leverages funded accounts into these events; this is the illusion of "illiquidity" (liquidity exists, brokers withhold execution). A limit at the opening price of the run +1 tick can fill about 20 minutes after, not in the first ~3 minutes.
  - Use NFP as a clue only: framing the 15-min pools beforehand tells you which pool is more likely to be run (see next concept). He is "not always right"; on CPI/PPI he says his anticipated direction of the initial delivery is right only ~2% of the time (98% wrong) (as stated).
  - Medium/high impact only: he uses Econoday (since the 1990s) and Forex Factory; ignores low-impact; cares about US data, Fed-related events (caption unclear) and bond auctions; speeches matter less. Fundamentals/raw numbers (jobs created or lost) are irrelevant ("the chart's going to tell you everything"); the data is "meant to stimulate" investors into risking money.
- **How to use:** Pre-frame buy-side/sell-side on the 15-min before 8:30, note which is favored, do NOT enter, wait for the shock, then re-read.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Fri Sept 6, 2024. Before 8:30 price had already traded down to the Aug 13 daily FVG low (~18,765, his target; he had covered his short there). NFP then ran up: first to a minor 5-min buy-side level, jammed down taking a short-term low without breaking the main 15-min low, then ripped through the buy side (a single 5m candle; wicking around on the 1m) and into the New Day Opening Gap before 9:30.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:01](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=481) NFP not algorithmic, wait 15-30 min; [0:09:38](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=578) wait for the shock, see what is left behind; [0:13:47](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=827) brokers pull liquidity / illiquidity illusion; [0:55:22](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=3322) slippage and requotes
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Consistent with his earlier "don't trade news" line; the new angle is using NFP as a liquidity-selection clue and the explicit 15-minute earliest-entry rule.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: 15-minute "bellwether" liquidity framing  (aliases: primary vs minor buy-side/sell-side, "dealing range" for the day)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The 15-minute chart is the bellwether time frame for where the obvious, clear pools of liquidity the algorithm refers to for that day's range are resting. Frame 15-minute relative equal highs (buy side) and relative equal lows / key lows (sell side) as the primary buy-side and sell-side pools. These give the first parameters for a narrative for the session or daily range.
  - Drop to the 5-minute: levels there are "minor" buy-side/sell-side pools inside the 15-min range. The 5m breaks the primary dealing range into smaller pools.
  - Do this every day, and put the 15-minute pools annotated at the start of 9:30 in every journal entry. No order-book/heatmap tool needed ("I've never been ambiguous about where it is").
  - He told his son Caleb to expect to mark the wrong pools at first and that is fine; do it on your own chart before watching the review.
- **How to identify:** 15m relative equal highs above / relative equal lows below; the pool of the 5m shows as a smaller equal-high/low inside that range.
- **How to use:** After framing, ask: stay inside the range, run just outside the low, just outside the high, or run both sides (and which first)? That frames the morning narrative.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15m on Sept 6: relative equal highs above (buy side) and lows below; the sell-side low had been taken slightly lower than a second adjacent low, which he said "tipped its hand" (see next concept). On 5m he annotated a minor buy side at slightly-unequal highs (copying the line with Ctrl-drag, labeling "minor buy side liquidity pool").
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:53](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=1073) 15m is the bellwether; [0:21:47](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=1307) journal every day with 15m pools at 9:30; [0:36:58](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=2218) 5m = minor pools; [0:51:24](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=3084) primary vs minor
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is a beginner-level starting point he is giving Caleb; "primary" = defined on the 15-minute chart.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Choosing which liquidity pool is more likely to be run  (aliases: "high probability" pool, jagged vs blocky, tipped its hand)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Pre-NFP read: the sell-side relative equal lows had been undercut (a lower low was taken slightly below the adjacent low), and the move down also spent time below a wick (accumulation). He took this as sell side already "acted on / hand tipped", and the blocky, relatively-equal buy-side highs above as the more likely draw for the news.
  - Signature of a real stop hunt: price traded through a wick (piercing, jagged look, spent time below it = accumulating). A blocky, smooth-edged structure is less "disturbed". The disturbed side is treated as already satisfied; the untouched blocky side is the next candidate. (He also says the lower-high / undercut structure matters: a high that is lower than the adjacent one is already "disturbed", per his 2024 earlier teaching.)
  - Add context: day of week (Friday), what the week has done (down all week, big Tuesday drop), and whether the weekly/daily objective has already been achieved. Here the Aug 13 daily FVG low objective was already hit so a Friday NFP should not be a "prolonged move lower".
  - If it is a medium-impact driver instead of NFP/FOMC/CPI, he expects the same draw but gradually rather than in a flash.
- **How to identify:** (1) which pool has been taken or "softened" by a wick-through; (2) which side is blocky/untouched; (3) weekly direction and day of week; (4) HTF objective reached.
- **Example in this video:** 15m NQ Sept 6 pre-NFP: sell-side lows undercut, buy-side equal highs intact; price ran up to the buy side at the release. He notes the alternative (could have run the other low then up) and that he was not trading it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:23](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=923) why one pool is more likely; [0:40:11](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=2411) lower-than-adjacent highs/lows and wick vs blocky; [0:47:27](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=2847) real stop hunt vs blockiness + Friday + week direction
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The narration on this is partly garbled (he points at "this one/that one" on the chart). Treat the exact wording as (caption unclear); the principle (prefer the pool whose structure is already disturbed/undercut or the untouched blocky counterpart, plus day-of-week and weekly-direction context) is what is stated. He explicitly warns it is a lean, not a certainty ("it could just as easily gone down, wiped this one, then went up").

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Wicks as PD arrays  (aliases: discount wick / premium wick, wick quadrants, midpoint of a wick)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - He treats wicks with quadrants and the halfway point. If price is above a wick, he wants to see it trade down into the upper half of the wick but not below its midpoint (consequent encroachment of the wick). If a leg passes through easily and spends time below it, that was accumulation.
  - Wicks below price are "discount wicks" worth annotating and writing on the notepad as key levels; a wick that price trades below becomes a "premium wick" (resistance from above).
  - A volume imbalance sitting under the wick range is the next draw below the wick's CE.
- **How to use:** Mark discount wicks and their 50% as levels; expect support at the upper half; a break of the midpoint with time spent = accumulation/transition.
- **Example in this video:** Daily NQ: he marked the discount wicks below the Aug 13 FVG and the volume imbalance beneath them as "next draw" levels if price kept going lower; on 1m Thursday, a discount wick became a premium wick once price was below it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:40:57](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=2457) wick halfway point; [1:28:24](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=5304) wick CE and volume imbalance below; [3:08:17](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=11297) discount wick becomes premium wick
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says he will "break that down in the quadrants" in later teaching; here it is only introduced.

head: Pre-9:30 range scenarios (both sides run before the open)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (conditional narrative)
- **What ICT says:** If price runs sell side first then buy side before 9:30 and the range that defines stays intact into 9:30 (no higher high, no lower low), there is about a 50-50 chance it stays inside that range rather than running the low again. If it takes the buy side but does not rip (just hangs and retraces into the first FVG of the prior day), expect a failed attempt at the lows, then a push lower after 9:30 into about 10:00–11:30, closing around the upper part of the Aug 13 daily FVG.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Sept 6 around the 8:30–9:30 window, framed with the New Day Opening Gap and the first FVG of Thursday ("blue line").
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:38](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=1838) scenarios; [0:32:14](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=1934) retrace into Thursday's first FVG

head: Retail sentiment as a contrarian read ("watering hole")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / refinement
- **What ICT says:** He watches other YouTubers' chats as a sentiment gauge; those channels form a "watering hole" where followers' stops/entries pool. If most chatters are aiming at a level that his technicals say will not be taken (e.g., "I want 18,686") he reads that as dumb money opposed to the algorithm and expects them to "fall on the sword". He sometimes seeds a chat to provoke an opinion ("acting like a Judas"). The algorithm delivers price; smart money engages it with their own algos/discretion; banks do not trade with this framework.
- **How to use:** Treat crowd conviction at an obvious level as a sign of resting liquidity, not confirmation.
- **Timestamps:** [0:37:47](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=2267) watering-hole sentiment; [0:43:21](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=2601) smart vs dumb money

body:

For the RTH opening gap he anchors on the 1m chart: previous close/settlement to the first print at 9:30 (he turned off electronic trading hours for the settlement line). title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Fair Value Gap (FVG; BISI / SIBI) — definition, mechanics and tolerance
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Definition: the range between candle 1 and candle 3 not overlapped by any other candle's range. A bullish one (buy-side imbalance, sell-side inefficiency) means the market has not offered efficient sell-side delivery through that range; for every range that goes up, efficient delivery means price must be offered back down through the same range. "Anybody tells you anything other than that... making stuff up." (He mis-says SIBI as "CBI" in the captions: "sell-side imbalance, buy-side inefficiency" = bearish gap.)
  - Draw only the real gap: low of one candle to the high of another, shade only that. Every small separation between three candles is not a tradeable FVG; you need other PD-array context. His example of a bearish FVG that is not tradeable is the intraday inefficiencies inside the larger bearish structure above the CISD price.
  - Preferred behavior: you do NOT want a bearish FVG to fully close in; you want price to go into it a little and reverse. Trading just because "an imbalance completely closes in" is "the lowest form of trading with imbalances".
  - Tolerance: wicks may color outside the FVG, but only about one "standard deviation" of the FVG, meaning roughly its own width, and generally less; bodies should not close beyond it. Small stray pokes are "mohawks". It will not go "five times" the width.
  - Paint-roller analogy: the daily is the roller, the 15m a 2-inch brush, the 5m a 1-inch brush, the 1m a fine brush; price runs out of "paint" in porous pockets which an FVG marks.
- **How to identify:** 3-candle pattern; gap between candle 1's high (or low) and candle 3's low (or high); bodies of lower-TF candles respecting it.
- **How to use:** Premium/discount and CE rules; for shorts enter inside the gap (see Order Block entry); stops beyond the OB; FVGs from the HTF are projected to the LTF as boxes.
- **Example in this video:** Daily NQ Aug 12 (Mon) high to Aug 14 (Wed) low, with Aug 13 (Tue) the displacement candle in the middle, is the bullish FVG he used as his weekly downside objective (low of the gap about 18,765.25, hit Thursday into Friday).
- **Timestamps:** [1:26:49](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=5209) textbook definition; [2:12:08](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=7928) do not want gaps to fill; [2:30:41](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=9041) draw only the real gap; [2:47:31](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=10051) one-standard-deviation wick tolerance
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The wick tolerance rule (~one FVG width) is new; he says it was "supposed to be in the book". He also says there is "no one-trick-pony explanation" of an FVG: other PD arrays must be recognized even if you do not trade them.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: What moves price: only two mechanisms  (aliases: draw on liquidity)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition
- **What ICT says:** Price only goes up to (a) go into inefficiencies above market price or (b) take buy-side liquidity (buy stops: either breakout longs' entries or stops protecting shorts). Price only goes down to (a) go into inefficiencies below (FVG, opening range gap) or (b) take sell stops below old lows (breakout shorts or stops protecting longs). "Nothing else"; manual interventions use the same levels, just farther and quicker. It does not need many contracts (he claims one contract can move price a tick when the next price is offered), so "buying and selling pressure" is not the driver; price skips creating small gaps when it is delivered to a level.
- **How to use:** Always ask which inefficiency or which pool price is reaching for.
- **Timestamps:** [1:29:59](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=5399) the two mechanisms; [1:31:33](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=5493) volume/contracts study; [3:12:17](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=11537) house-price analogy
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Stated as an absolute; he is demystifying the "algorithm" language.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: One Shot One Kill (sniper model)  (aliases: OSOK, sniper mentality)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / mindset
- **What ICT says:**
  - Take very few, surgical trades: "one or two, maybe three a week", not an everyday setup. Do not spray a magazine (machine gun) hoping to hit something.
  - The PD array (FVG) is the "scope": the target is the moment price steps into the FVG; as price hits its consequent encroachment or approaches it, it is in the crosshairs. Then "exhale", enter as price enters the FVG. Stop placed beyond the imbalance candle: below it for a bullish FVG, above its high for a bearish FVG (which candle he means by "imbalance candle" is caption unclear; in the OB entry below he uses the order block high +1 tick). After entering, do nothing extra and sit still; do not announce trades on social media.
  - Aim at the largest magnitude: sell the highest premium array available and target the extreme (his example: ~360 NQ handles from the Thursday short to the Friday FVG low). Be prepared to absorb fluctuations between entry and the target.
  - Start with humble goals: consistently 5 handles in ES, 10-15 handles in NQ.
- **How to use:** Define target first (HTF FVG low), then find the highest-timeframe premium array to enter from, place the stop once with logical price points, never chase it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:59:19](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=3559) one to three setups a week; [1:00:07](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=3607) sniper analogy; [1:01:43](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=3703) enter on FVG, stop placement; [2:36:15](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=9375) "above this price, aim for that one"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Also the title of his posted video ("OSOK"). He says the stop for pyramided adds is not trailed up.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Exits: limit order realism and "moral victory"  (aliases: marrying the vein)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / psychology
- **What ICT says:**
  - He covered 14 NQ contracts short with a limit near the Aug 13 FVG low and consciously set the limit a bit above the exact level (~18,770 rather than the high of 18,765.25) so the order would fill given the spread; his original profit objective would have paid "a couple hundred dollars more" but he prioritized getting off all 14.
  - With larger size (e.g., 100 contracts) a limit exactly at the level may not fill fully; "touching the level is not enough". Accept the "low hanging fruit" exit; keep the expectation of perfection for the journal ("moral victory"), not for the order ticket.
  - Do not hold for the perfect tick or you can "marry the vein" (staying in a played-out trade) and turn a winner into a loser.
- **Example in this video:** NQ short from the Thursday daily-FVG setup; limit exit adjusted from 18,765.25 to roughly 18,770; ~360 handles captured (stated as "almost 360 handles").
- **Timestamps:** [1:34:44](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=5684) adjusting limit for spread; [1:37:53](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=5873) moral victory in the journal; [1:41:50](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=6110) marrying the vein

head: Lunch macro (11:30–1:30 ET) and afternoon session first 30 minutes
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The New York lunch macro is the two hours 11:30–1:30 ET. Whatever the morning session did, there is always some retracement against it in those two hours (orders get trailed up/down, stops are used). Draw vertical lines at 11:30 and 1:30 every day and study what price does; it happens so often it could be your model.
  - Always keep charts on New York time; any local-time chart means you are "not following the logic".
  - 1:30 starts the afternoon session; in the first 30 minutes (to 2:00) fair value gaps and other PD arrays (breakers, vacuum blocks, propulsion blocks, volume imbalances) form and are tradeable; the FVG is not limited to 9:30–10:00 (a "one-trick pony" misconception).
- **Timestamps:** [1:44:15](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=6255) lunch macro defined; [1:45:51](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=6351) afternoon first 30 minutes
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Stated in 11:30–1:30 terms here; he slips once and says "11:30 to 12:30" then corrects to 1:30. He also reported entering Tuesday's short in the afternoon after 1:30.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Change in State of Delivery (CISD) and the bearish Order Block
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule / entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price was offered up (buy-side delivery) through a run of up-close daily candles; then a displacement lower (the Tuesday Sept 3 drop) overtakes that candle's low. The reference point is the opening price of the (lowest/first) up-close candle in that run; that open is the change in the state of delivery and the algorithm refers back to it. Here: the opening price of Thursday Aug 29's daily candle (exact candles are pointed at, caption unclear).
  - The up-close candle(s) before the displacement form "all one singular bearish order block". He says it is not simply "the last up-close candle" as he first taught it; the rule definitions will be in his book. Because the displacement overtakes the low, you cannot use just that candle's high and low; use the truest beginning of the run-up as the order-block reference (the opening price).
  - Validation: the order block is only confirmed when price crosses below that opening price. It does not need to close below; no engulfing candle or "FU candle" requirement. On the 15-minute chart price had wicked above the open/high a couple of times and then a candle traded below the opening price, which validates it. Lower-TF bodies respecting the level adds confidence.
  - Mean threshold: for the up-close bearish OB, shorts belong from the candle's open up to the halfway point (mean threshold); the upper half should ideally never be traded through. Staying away from it signaled strength; he added a pyramided entry once and let it ride.
  - Entry/stop (the 15m example): after validation the next candle created a bearish FVG (the "first presentation", not limited to 9:30-10:00). Entry = the FVG's candle-3 high (lower edge, which is the lowest threshold entry) minus 1 tick to ensure a fill (a sell limit placed one tick below the edge; the price quoted is about 19,183.25, caption unclear). Stop = high of the bearish order block candle plus 1 tick. Risk is defined, "it never goes there". You can also add on the open of that candle or deeper into the FVG.
  - FVGs that sit above the CISD price inside the bearish structure should stay open and are not to be traded up into ("real heavy").
- **How to use:** Mark the open of the run-up candle on the HTF chart; track when LTF price wicks above and bodies respect it; once price trades below the open, the OB is valid; short retests between the open and the 50% (mean threshold); stop = OB high +1 tick; target = next draw (HTF FVG low/old low).
- **Example in this video:** Daily NQ (Aug 29 open as reference), Tue Sept 3 displacement lower, Wed Sept 4 candle high (he describes the low-of-one-candle to Wednesday's-high range as the "real" daily bearish FVG; my reading is Wednesday's high is its lower edge), then Thursday Sept 5 the 15m/5m/1m trade (below). Exact candles are pointed at on screen, so treat the candle identification as approximate.
- **Timestamps:** [2:05:43](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=7543) bearish OB from two up-close candles; [2:12:56](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=7976) CISD is the opening price; [2:25:49](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=8749) validation on lower time frame; [2:28:15](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=8895) entry minus 1 tick, stop OB high +1 tick; [3:00:17](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=10817) mean threshold
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicit update: the order block is not "the last up-close candle before the drop" in every case; the opening price of the start of the run-up matters. He also states validation needs only a cross (wick/body trade) below the open, not a close.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Price Delivery Continuum Theory (top-down PD array transposition)  (aliases: higher time frame PD array respected by lower time frame)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Whatever PD arrays exist on a higher-timeframe chart, the lower time frames should respect them: draw the HTF FVG as a rectangle and carry it to lower charts. Wicks may color outside the lines; judge whether the bodies go beyond the array. If bodies respect it, you are getting closer to the entry.
  - Standard ladder only: monthly, weekly, daily, 4H, 1H, 15m, 5m, 1m (nothing in between like a 6m or 7m); sub-1m is excessive.
  - Time is the most important factor: "if it ain't the right time, price ain't going nowhere".
  - At the end he contrasts this with the retail claim that the higher timeframe must be confirmed by the lower one: he says the HTF array is what the LTF reacts to because algorithmic delivery is high-frequency. (Wording here is garbled; read as: LTF behavior confirms HTF array.)
  - Bodies on a 1-minute chart may sit in the zone if the 5m/15m/1h show only wicks there; going to a 5s/15s chart would show bodies on a wick too.
- **Example in this video:** Daily bearish FVG/OB zone transposed to 1h (wall of wick overlap = balanced price range plus a small bearish FVG left exposed above an old high), to 15m (price running into the FVG, wicks beyond), to 5m (bodies respecting the box), to 1m (market maker sell model).
- **Timestamps:** [2:24:14](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=8654) opening price drawn from daily down to hourly/15m; [2:42:45](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=9765) 5m bodies respect; [2:43:33](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=9813) time-frame ladder; [3:43:40](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=13420) contrast with retail
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Name in the captions is "price delivery Continuum Theory" (caption unclear on exact name).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Turtle Soup (ICT version)  (aliases: stop hunt reversal and continuation)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Turtle soup is both a reversal and a continuation pattern: a short-term high is run (pierced) at the right time of day, then price reverses. You can use an FVG to enter the turtle soup. His use: price wicks above a short-term high / above the lower edge of a HTF bearish FVG into the premium of that FVG, you short, targeting the opposite extreme.
  - The idea comes from Linda Raschke's and Larry Connors' book (the turtle traders used a 20-day-high breakout); he took the name and the stop-hunt-then-return-into-range concept only; nothing of the rules. He claims his application is "the highest tier" of the idea. "Candle range theory" (the Twitter version of turtle soup) he calls worthless.
  - Rule for this trade: entry to be above the Wednesday daily high (the lower edge of the daily bearish FVG) and below the FVG's upper edge, and only after a short-term high forms at the intended time of day and is pierced; target the low of the Aug 13 daily FVG ("black line").
- **How to use:** Define the HTF FVG zone (entry window) and the target; wait for a short-term high to form at the right time; enter on the piercing and retrace; sit still.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Thursday Sept 5 (video recorded and executed live, with market-order hot buttons shown on chart): above the Wednesday daily high (about 18,552.5 as captioned, caption unclear), inside the daily bearish FVG; after the 9:30–10:00 opening range, price traded up into the 1h/15m FVG, wicked above the high and he sold, adding again on the wick (pyramid) and held to the Aug 13 daily FVG low.
- **Timestamps:** [2:33:05](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=9185) turtle soup reversal/continuation, CRT dismissed; [2:35:27](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=9327) run above Wednesday high = turtle soup; [2:44:19](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=9859) real turtle soup vs Raschke/Connors; [3:05:06](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=11106) executions shown
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Consistent with his earlier Turtle Soup teaching; new is the explicit pairing with an FVG entry and HTF target.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Market Maker Sell Model (1-minute read) and second-stage distribution
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - On the 1m: look for the original consolidation (a clean box of price, not the impulsive sharp stretches); a stop run below its lows (relative equal lows, sell side) then rally back to touch the original consolidation high (first stage accumulation/reaccumulation), then rally and take a high (the "smart money reversal") inside the HTF premium. You do not need the smart money reversal itself; wait for the break of market structure at the low, then trade the retrace back up into the order block (CISD price).
  - First stage distribution then second-stage distribution: the second stage is the "unicorn", the fastest, most powerful and easiest hold. If you can spot it, sell the second-stage redistribution (or buy second-stage reaccumulation for the buy model).
  - He says this is a market truism (markup then sell-off), nothing to do with Wyckoff or ICT. Targets are the pools: sell side below, then below the original consolidation.
  - "Second mouse gets the cheese": do not sell the first touch of the premium just because price is high; wait for the run and the re-test after the opening range.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Thursday after 10:00: consolidation, run of the lows under relative equal lows, rally back to the consolidation high, accumulation, then a rally taking the high (outside the FVG box, coloring above it). Break of structure at the low, retrace up into the bearish OB (opening price), pyramided adds in the lower half of the OB candle, then expansion down through first stage distribution then second stage distribution into the sell-side pools.
- **Timestamps:** [2:49:51](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=10191) original consolidation; [2:55:29](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=10529) second mouse gets the cheese; [3:07:28](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=11248) first and second stage distribution; [3:08:17](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=11297) unicorn
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Points to his 2017 mentorship playlist for the full model; captions on stage labels are partly garbled ("reaccumulation" used in the sell model).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Premium arrays: lower-half usage, stop discipline and pyramiding
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** For a premium array (bearish OB/FVG) you want to see the lower half used and the upper half ideally untouched. Sell outside the FVG (above it, e.g., after the sweep) for "premium pricing". Place the stop once at logical price points and do not chase it through the range; add (pyramid) into the premium only while risk stays defined, and do not trail the stop up to the high. Funded-account rules forbid adding to a losing position; he did not (and used fewer than 15 contracts).
- **Timestamps:** [2:57:07](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=10627) premium pricing, terminus, sit still; [3:01:52](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=10912) one more pyramid then let it ride; [3:37:08](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=13028) no adding to losers

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Liquidity engineering / late-day run to unseat trailed stops  (aliases: building liquidity, fake bull flags, time distortion)
body:
- **Kind:** example / new coinage
- **What ICT says:** In the last hour of Thursday, price wicked up into the daily FVG high / balanced range area to unseat trailed stop losses of shorts; then it "marked time" and dripped down, leaving old NDOGs and fake bull flags in the upper quadrant of the daily FVG so buyers would place long entries with sell stops beneath ("engineering liquidity"). As price neared the low it was delivered quickly so longs would not pull orders; the sell stops needed to be there to be taken. He calls the holding pattern in the middle "time distortion": the market held in place while entities accumulate or distribute. He says this is scripted, a macro or "short list of orders and directives for the price engine" and denies it is buying/selling pressure.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m/5m, Thursday last hour into Friday early session: wick up, slow grind, fake flags, then quick drive into the Aug 13 FVG low at ~18,765.
- **Timestamps:** [3:18:44](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=11924) wick up in last hour, previous NDOGs; [3:20:22](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=12022) engineering sell stops; [3:13:53](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=11633) denying harmonic/S&R traders; [3:00:17](https://youtu.be/MxaJD1WIzos?t=10817) time distortion defined
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He had planned to close at the consequent encroachment of the daily FVG on Thursday (it only reached CE); he held for the low.

head: Futures versus forex/CFD execution
body:

In futures everyone has the same high tick, low tick, open and close and a reputable broker; in forex each broker has its own prices and discretion to widen spreads, requote or not fill, so stops get hit and then price runs. title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NonFarm Payroll September 06, 2024
head: Time horizon, holding trades and weekend risk
body:
- **Kind:** rule / psychology
- **What ICT says:** You will stagnate if you only take 5 handles in ES or 10-15 in NQ; you need periods of holding, and holding a trade for the whole daily range or into the next day toward algorithmic targets is the progression. His comfortable time frame: working inside the weekly range; he does not hold over the weekend (risk of gaps/geopolitical events; the market is only closed 5:00–6:00 PM daily). A winner or a loser should be judged on proficiency and precision, not windfalls: remove your top two or three windfall wins and see how you do.
