title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Opening range gap — half-gap and full-gap closure at the open (RTH)  (aliases: opening gap, previous settlement to opening price, gap closure)
body:
- **Kind:** example only (applies earlier teaching) + RTH/ETH nuance
- **What ICT says:**
  - The opening range gap is previous settlement (RTH close) to the open price. Today's reference: previous settlement 18,846 and an open in the high 18,920s, "a large gap". He shows it on RTH data.
  - Price immediately traded half the gap (opening bell, ~9:30 ET) and then did an almost full gap closure; a deep retracement back inside the opening range gap followed. He marks the midpoint (CE) of the gap and the "full gap closure" level, and notes that after the closure price kept "wicking" and printing bodies at a key level near the previous-settlement area.
  - For regular-trading-hours versus electronic-trading-hours: he deliberately switches the 1-minute chart to ETH (electronic trading hours) data when he wants to use a particular wick (the wick consequent-encroachment idea below), because those candles' highs/lows differ from RTH-only candles. At the end (1:17:33) he again notes the pocket he's studying shows on ETH data.
  - After the full gap closure it is "retracement back into the open range" in the first 30 minutes, and then "new day opening gap" levels (Sept 11 and Sept 10) act as draw on liquidity targets.
- **How to identify:** Mark prior settlement (4:15 PM ET close) and the first 9:30 print; mark the midpoint.
- **How to use:** Treat the gap's midpoint and far edge as targets from a premium; after closure, watch whether bodies respect the gap's prior-settlement level (deliver below = decidedly weak).
- **Example in this video:** NQ Wed 2024-09-11: settlement 18,846, opens ~18,920s; half gap traded in the first minute after the opening bell (video 0:06:50), near-full gap closure by 0:07:38, then deep retracement and a long back-and-forth.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:02:11](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=131) — previous settlement 18,846, huge premium opening on 15m
  - [0:06:50](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=410) — opening bell: half the gap already traded
  - [0:07:38](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=458) — almost full gap closure, retracement inside the gap
  - [0:11:51](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=711) — new day opening gap as draw on liquidity; full gap closure then bodies at a key level
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same opening range gap framework as 09-09 (M24-025) but the gap here closed within minutes. He does not state the 70% / 30-minute rule again in this video.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Daily / weekly inefficiency (FVG) as reference levels; volume imbalance under it  (aliases: "inefficiency" = FVG, dash lines, high of the inefficiency, volume imbalance)
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:**
  - He annotates a daily chart inefficiency (a larger weekly one above and another inside it). The dash line (high of the inefficiency, and its low) is watched by 1-minute and 15-second bodies: price opens, trades down to it, and also reprices a small volume imbalance between a candle's close and the next open (around 18,924.75 and 18,921; caption says "924 3/4" and "21 even"). Both are "accomplished" at once.
  - Bodies staying at the top of the inefficiency's dash line (not just wicks) is the evidence price is "respecting" it; it then likely explores the other side (the low of the inefficiency), and because sell-side liquidity rests just below that low, price accomplishes two things: uses the PD array and runs the sell-side.
  - A Thursday September 5 daily candle low (dash line) is also tracked as a key level; sell-side was resting around the 18,886–18,888 area on the 15-second chart (caption unclear on exact numbers).
- **How to identify:** Draw the daily inefficiency on lower time frames with a shaded box; note the dash line for the high and the low. Look for bodies (not wicks) holding the top.
- **How to use:** If bodies respect the top, expect an exploration of the bottom and the sell-side under it.
- **Example in this video:** 0:03:02–0:03:51: daily chart annotated, price opens above, trades down to the candle low and volume imbalance; later, at 0:30:59, bodies closing at the top of the inefficiency inside the opening range gap on the 1m predicts the rotation to its low.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:03:02](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=182) — daily inefficiency, weekly one, volume imbalance annotated
  - [0:26:09](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1569) — body lays right at the top dash line of the inefficiency; delivers lower
  - [0:31:46](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1906) — lower side: sell-side below the low plus new day opening gap
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He prefers numbers and a few lines on the chart rather than clutter, but shows boxes for teaching.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Balanced Price Range (BPR) and the "paint roller" test of efficiency  (aliases: balanced price range, porous price, bodies overlapping, "blue box")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / new coinage ("paint roller analogy")
- **What ICT says:**
  - Paint roller analogy: price is efficiently delivered where bodies have rolled "paint" over a range; ranges between two bodies with no body overlapping (only wicks) are thin paint, i.e. porous/inefficient. Example: between the previous day's settlement candle body and another body only one single body-pass down occurred, so there is "not a lot of paint" there.
  - A BPR formed (the blue box) in the 15m/1m; price trading below its top is "decidedly weak" and price needs to respect the top end of that area; if it goes below it, it was just a retracement into the opening range.
  - Minor buy side lies on the far side of the BPR and minor sell side on the other; "that's the cool liquidity that matters, not your book math".
  - Later (1:17:33) he asks Caleb to study the pocket on RTH data: it becomes a BPR once price leaves it, with bodies respecting it, and everything then goes lower.
- **How to identify:** An area where one move down and one move up overlap so that opposing FVGs share the same price zone (his blue box); porous = bodies not overlapping.
- **How to use:** Price below the BPR top = weak; if it respects the top, short with the BPR as premium array; watch the minor liquidity on each side.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:15:18](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=918) — BPR, respect of the top of the blue box
  - [0:19:40](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1180) — paint roller analogy
  - [0:26:09](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1569) — minor buy side / sell side around the BPR
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Uses BPR for micro scale on the 1m; the "paint roller" analogy is a new way to explain efficient vs inefficient delivery.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Micro liquidity and "bread-and-butter" scalps (high-frequency scalps, "Scout" (caption unclear))  (aliases: minor buy side / sell side, small structure)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - There is always liquidity, not only above old highs and below old lows: small micro structure (candle lows/highs, tiny BPRs, wick midpoints) also holds stops. If you have the higher-timeframe inefficiencies on the chart and watch price gravitate to short-term sell side / buy side, you don't need the full daily range to deliver; you get small repeating scalps.
  - On a 15-second or 30-second chart there are many examples inside one daily range; adding all the up/down fluctuations NQ could "move" 1,500 points in a day even if the daily range is smaller.
  - Quants/HFT algorithms don't need a daily directional bias; they frame specific reference points and need a confirming quality (bodies' opens/closes matching the reference level), then trade both directions all day.
  - Claim: finding 2–3 of these per day and making 1.5–3% a day is feasible even with a very small account and micro lots; he contrasts this with swinging for 10–15%.
  - Warning: don't instantly start trading every OTE/FVG/iFVG/order block on a 15-second chart without a model; complexity comes from not knowing what you're looking for.
  - The factor to look for: a discount array that stops price falling (but not sideways) to afford buy-side delivery, or a premium array that stops price rising (not sideways) to afford sell-side delivery.
- **How to identify:** Bodies at a higher-timeframe inefficiency high/low plus a nearby small liquidity pool (candle low, equal lows).
- **How to use:** Scalp from the micro premium/discount arrays; it works because it needs only a small run, not the full range.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:26:59](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1619) — wick CE hit and delivery is "enough for a scalp"
  - [0:28:35](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1715) — "always liquidity", micro structure
  - [0:32:36](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1956) — 2–3 setups/day, 1.5–3% a day claim; micro lots
  - [0:34:13](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2053) — the premise: premium array -> not higher, not sideways, so lower; discount array the reverse
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Extends "buy-side / sell-side liquidity" teaching down to micro scale; the % claim is his statement, not a backtested figure.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Consequent Encroachment of a wick (wick CE) — opposing premium and discount CEs  (aliases: "consequent encroachment of the wick", wick midpoint)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / new refinement (he says "this could be your model")
- **What ICT says:**
  - Take a 1-minute candle with a prominent wick (ETH data); mark the 50% point (consequent encroachment) of that wick. Price returns to it after taking a short-term/old high above (buy stops) and reverses to the tick: that is "turtle soup old high" behavior plus a hit on the wick CE.
  - It does two things at once: it takes the short-term high (liquidity) and goes to a price the algorithms refer back to.
  - Once price reaches it, bodies start building around the CE ("hanging around", blocky bodies). Spending a lot of time there with bodies at the CE means it will go lower. He says there are "very few absolutes" but "we do technical science" and that this is as close as it gets: bodies of candles built around the wick CE -> price goes lower.
  - He calls the pairing "opposing premium and discount consequent encroachments on the wicks": the upper wick CE at a premium acts as the sell, and a lower wick CE (the discount wick CE) acts as the target (price delivered "right to the tick", e.g. a low of about 18,741.75 — caption unclear).
  - Qualifier: wait for a qualifying signature that bodies are respecting the high of the inefficiency/range (see above).
  - You do not need price to trade down to the low of the daily inefficiency; since this is a wick, "the damage is probably done" (0:43:00).
- **How to identify:**
  1. Pick a 1m candle with a long wick; draw its midpoint (the wick CE).
  2. Wait for a short-term high to be run above, taking buy stops.
  3. Price trades up into the wick CE and bodies begin building at it; the bodies' opens/closes line up with the high of the daily inefficiency.
- **How to use:** Short at/around the wick CE (often with a small add on 15s), target the lower wick CE and the sell-side liquidity beyond; expansion past it goes into the new day opening gap (Sept 10 NDOG in this case).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m (ETH data), ~10:00 to 10:08 ET (video 0:36:39–0:44:36): price runs the short-term old high (about 18,875 — caption unclear) up into the CE of an earlier wick, hits it exactly, then sells; the bodies sit at the CE too long; then price delivers lower toward the lower CE and beyond.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:24:22](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=1462) — "wick's consequent encroachment" on 1m ETH data; relative equal lows
  - [0:36:39](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2199) — old high hits the wick CE (turtle soup old high)
  - [0:43:47](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2627) — "this could be your model": opposing premium and discount CEs on the wicks
  - [0:44:36](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2676) — two things at once: takes the short-term high and meets algo reference
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** A new, quite specific model ICT presents live; there are no prices stated cleanly in the captions so replication requires re-watching.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Algorithmic price delivery: the "price engine", HFT algorithms and the "handshake"  (aliases: price engine, high-frequency trading algorithm, handlers, map like a video game)
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / conceptual framing
- **What ICT says:**
  - HFT algorithms operate on a simple premise: above an old high and below an old low there is liquidity, regardless of whether it is one contract or 10,000. They harvest fluctuations in both directions all day long, adding and taking partials.
  - He compares price delivery to a video game map (Pac-Man, Call of Duty): the maze/map is predetermined; the "price engine" delivers price within it, calculated from prior range data (previous day, last three days, previous week, previous month). Each session window (morning, lunch, afternoon, London, Asia) is a "map". Neither retail nor large institutions control price; they only operate inside the map unless there is manual intervention.
  - "Handshake": when the algorithms trading on the price engine's logic and the price engine's delivery agree at a level, price hits it to the tick (e.g. the exact wick CE). Not random.
  - Days with news (he mentions NFP and similar) let the "handlers" stir price up so it looks disorganized; the setups are still there, but framing them takes understanding.
  - He says to ignore indicators and moving averages; none of them tells price what it will do. Also defends algorithms as adding liquidity.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:35:03](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2103) — HFT algorithms add liquidity; retail blames them
  - [0:40:37](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2437) — video-game map analogy
  - [0:41:25](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2485) — price pre-determined by time windows and prior ranges
  - [0:44:36](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2676) — "handshake" between algorithms and the price engine
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Conceptual; the practical content is the wick CE model and micro liquidity above. Strong claims (e.g. "nobody else teaches this") are marketing, not testable rules.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Volume Imbalance and porous price ("patchwork")  (aliases: volume imbalance, porous price action, inefficient delivery; "patchwork" (caption reads "Patrick"))
body:
- **Kind:** definition + refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A real volume imbalance: two broad candle bodies with an indecisive (small) candle in between; the bodies don't overlap each other across that area. He says the volume imbalance is defined by the range the body "encapsulates" (the range between those bodies), and you do not draw it on the indecisive candle's body (some viewers said he drew it wrong; he rejects that).
  - Porous price: a down-closed candle with a small wick, then the next candle, with no bodies touching/overlapping between them; "no rhyme or reason" from a retail perspective, but "in need of patchwork": price will come back up and redeliver into that area. When it does, HFT algorithms "fire in shorts" there, targeting the smooth lows (the lower wick CE).
  - He notes gaps/FVGs are not all the same; "they actually do certain things differently", to be learned later.
- **How to identify:** Adjacent candles whose bodies don't overlap, with wicks overlapping; a tiny pocket on 15s that sits inside a higher-level 1m wick area.
- **How to use:** Treat as a short entry area on the retrace; it is an additional PD array, along with the small inefficiency between two other candles.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:46:13](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2773) — porous price action described
  - [0:47:02](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2822) — "in need of patchwork"; algorithms short into it
  - [0:52:39](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3159) — how a real volume imbalance is drawn
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Clarifies how he draws volume imbalances (bodies, not wicks), consistent with the 09-09 note about a "tiny separation" between a candle's low and another's high (a related but different case).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Adding to a short (pyramiding) at a short-term premium array
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** When bodies build around a short-term premium array/wick CE and you are already short, you can add a small amount ("toss on one or two contracts" if holding 15–20 contracts, "kick it up a notch"); then take something off lower. HFT algos do the same: short, add more, take something off below.
- **How to use:** Add small, on confirmation; he says you shouldn't fear adds if you understand what price is telling you.
- **Timestamps:** [0:47:52](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=2872), [0:54:23](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3263), [0:57:33](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3453)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Pyramid only while not past the 50% threshold of the target (see risk section).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Stop placement for the wick-CE short: "how far can it color outside the lines"  (aliases: stop above the order block, CISD opening price)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model detail
- **What ICT says:**
  - The 15-second inefficiency (one candle's low to another's high) is the entry zone, but the 1m wick above it can trade up to its consequent encroachment, so price can color "outside the lines" of the small gap. Entry at the low end of the 15s rectangle (the 1m candle's high), but the stop must account for how far the wick can go.
  - Also: an up-closed candle among down-closed candles is a bearish order block; the stop must at least cover that candle's opening price, which marks the change in state of delivery (CISD) of the run lower.
  - Stop = one tick above that, which is above the inefficiency. That looks like a big stop, but it is only large relative to a size like 30 contracts; fix size, not the stop.
  - Confirmation: when a candle trades a little outside the inefficiency without closing a body at its high end, it validates; then the middle of the inefficiency should hold price at bay ("shouldn't go higher; it's done the work of going into the upper half").
  - If you missed the run, you can still use the premium array / wick CE and the order block as your stop.
  - Balance size: small enough that being stopped doesn't hurt, big enough that you care. If you panic on entry you're too large; start with micros.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:59:58](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3598) — 15s vs 1m inefficiency ranges; outside the lines
  - [1:07:07](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=4027) — entry at low end of the rectangle; stop considering CE of wick and the bearish order block
  - [1:07:56](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=4076) — stop one tick above the order block's open / inefficiency
  - [1:10:22](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=4222) — use the order block as stop; size balance
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explains why his stops look "wide" in his trade-execution videos. "Mohawk" (caption unclear) is his label for the price action when a candle trades slightly outside the inefficiency.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Dynamic risk management: stop reduces risk only after the trade develops  (aliases: stop to breakeven at 25%, pyramid threshold 50%)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Once in, the stop should reduce risk in a dynamic way, but not "jam to break even immediately"; you must accept the initial risk and give the trade time to develop.
  - After price has run 25% of your expected profit target, you may move the stop to breakeven (covering commissions). You'll still get stopped out sometimes and it may then run without you; that is the "paid premium education".
  - You can pyramid new entries if the trade is paying and price isn't past the 50% threshold of the target (example: a 100-handle target).
  - Never trade without a stop; posting a screenshot of an open profit with no stop is a sign of a clout chaser.
  - Resistance is normal even in low-resistance liquidity runs: price still pauses and creates add opportunities.
- **Timestamps:** [1:01:34](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3694), [1:02:21](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3741), [1:03:09](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3789), [1:04:45](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3885), [1:06:18](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=3978)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The 25% breakeven and 50% pyramid thresholds are specific numbers worth quoting.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 11, 2024
head: Standard-deviation / measured-move projection from a dealing range to external range liquidity  (aliases: measure move, 1 standard deviation, fib extension)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Take any inefficiency (any timeframe, not only daily) and project its range (high to low) lower: one "standard deviation" is where price is reasonable to reach.
  - To anticipate going beyond that, the simple Fibonacci change: a viewer said "1.25"; ICT said go to the 1.5 level and add a 2 (likely meaning a -2.5 extension; caption unclear). That is "a beautiful area to anticipate external range beyond a measured move"; being content there means "you're done".
  - In this session price went down to the wick low, which would have been a superstar move; but a limit at the wick CE would never have been filled, hence the need for flexibility.
- **Timestamps:** [1:12:47](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=4367), [1:13:34](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=4414), [1:15:11](https://youtu.be/A1mLNIoEsq0?t=4511)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Exact extension numbers unclear in captions; verify against other videos on fib/standard deviations.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Opening range (9:30–10:00 ET) as the algorithmic 30-minute window; standard deviations of it  (aliases: opening range, first 30 minutes, "algorithm's opening range")
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The opening range is a 30-minute algorithmic period, 9:30 to 10:00 ET. In it the algorithm sets up initial buy side and sell side and then operates off them. 15 minutes of trading is not enough information for the daily range.
  - What to look for in it: initial buy-side and sell-side liquidity, plus any initial PD array (a significant break, or any imbalance: BISI or SIBI, "either one"). That gives context for a possible Silver Bullet trade at 10 o'clock (stated briefly; caption gives no more detail).
  - You can run standard deviations on the opening range: take the first-30-minute highest high and lowest low and project them; he says those projections give intermediate-term and long-term daily/intersession highs and lows ("don't take my word for it, see it for yourself").
  - The first FVG that forms after the open (here on the 1m, with the 9:33 candle) is the first presentation FVG; "the opening range essentially is that first presentation fair value gap".
- **How to identify:** Mark the 9:30 and 10:00 verticals; take the high and low of that window; mark the first 1m FVG.
- **How to use:** Treat the window as information gathering, not a place to bet the farm ("you're not trying to secure the low or high of the day"); then project the range's standard deviations for targets; remove the 10:00 verticals once the method has been communicated.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2024-09-12: after 10:00 the 15s chart shows price inside the opening range gap touching the NDOG low; the range's own highs/lows are used as references.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:12:03](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=723) — first presentation FVG on the 1m (9:33 candle)
  - [0:14:48](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=888) — what to look for in the window; Silver Bullet context
  - [0:18:19](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1099) — 30-minute algorithmic window, standard deviations
  - [0:19:06](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1146) — projecting the range's high/low gives intermediate- and long-term highs/lows
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Adds a projection claim (standard deviations of the 9:30–10:00 range) that he says he normally "tucks deep inside" lectures.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Opening range gap size and pre-market behaviour  (aliases: ORG high/low, previous settlement 4:15 PM ET)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Previous settlement is 4:15 PM ET (shown with RTH data). The opening range gap high is the higher of previous settlement and today's open; by definition the other is the gap low.
  - "You guys know the protocol": in the first 30 minutes look for half the gap to fill. Today the gap was about 15 handles and essentially filled almost immediately, also sitting inside the new day opening gap, so it was lackluster.
  - A small opening range gap means a poor, muddy start; don't expect excitement from the opening range gap on those days. A big gap with obvious buy-side and sell-side pools away from the open is better.
  - Pre-market (anything before 9:30): watch whether the gap is being maintained or shrinking toward 9:30. If it shrinks, expect a very muddy morning or at least a muddy first 30 minutes.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2024-09-12: tiny premium gap above 4:15 PM settlement; price trades down below it at the open; the NDOG for Sept 12 and its CE are also in play.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:02:30](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=150) — opening range gap high; half gap "essentially done"; inside NDOG
  - [0:15:54](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=954) — small gap (about 15 handles); definition of gap high/low
  - [0:16:43](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1003) — pre-market: gap maintained or shrinking?
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Complements M24-025 (big gap: don't buy premium) with the small-gap case (don't expect much).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Morning-session protocol after a large-range day  (aliases: "keep your fingers out of the mashed potatoes", large range day rule, candlestick range theory)
body:
- **Kind:** rule (core lesson)
- **What ICT says:**
  - When the previous daily candle is a large-range candle (bullish or bearish), the next morning session through lunch is high resistance: price "marks time" (barcoding/painting) for the first 30 minutes, chops traders, and setups are "more prone to fail". He says he has followed this since 1995 and calls it one candlestick range theory; "I never deviate".
  - For beginners the protocol is: do not trade the morning session after a large-range day (that means all the way through lunch). Write it in your journal; "you have permission to sit still".
  - The crowd that watched yesterday's big move wants to be on the same side; smart money lays a "landmine field" in the morning to punish exactly that side (novices follow signals, chat rooms, news).
  - Advanced students may have trades available, but only if they know their model; students like his son should not.
  - The richest traders have written plans of inactivity (planned stillness); trade only when probability is in your favor; recognize the condition, turn charts off, walk away, and return for the next session.
  - If you did trade that morning (even demo) and got lucky, you will mistake luck for skill and repeat it with real money.
- **How to identify:** Daily chart shows a monster candle yesterday (here NQ's large up-close day of Sept 11).
- **How to use:** Skip the AM; come back at about 1:15–1:30 PM ET and use the PM routine below.
- **Example in this video:** The whole session: NQ opens near unchanged from yesterday's close, drops, rallies in small bull flags, then sweeps the low again, exactly the chop he predicts.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:20:44](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1244) — "how many of you remembered you're not supposed to do anything in the morning session"
  - [0:22:18](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1338) — "you have permission not to trade the morning session"
  - [0:35:26](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=2126) — post-large-range day setups more prone to fail
  - [0:49:57](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=2997) — first 30 minutes marks time (barcoding)
  - [1:12:30](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=4350) — a protocol from 1995; recognise high-resistance conditions
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Extends the M24-025 filter (no news = demand clean price) with a day-structure filter. He frames it as "when to push the pedal, when to brake, when to turn the ignition off".

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Initial low of the day as a trap (Judas swing as deferred market delivery)  (aliases: Judas swing, turtle soup, "breadcrumbs", engineered sentiment)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - On a large-range up day, after the open smart money lets early buyers in with little bull flags ("breadcrumbs"), then drops price below the initial low of the day. Longs have their stops below that low; supply/demand traders, Fibonacci retracement buyers, harmonic traders, moving-average crossovers and oversold indicators all buy or stop there. The initial low is "always a suspect low".
  - The drop takes out the sell stops, which lets smart money accumulate longs against that liquidity. It also discourages the crowd (they flip to short), which is the same as a sell stop being hit.
  - You can use it as a turtle soup or as a scalp: trade down into the low.
  - He calls the pattern "your Judas swing... a deferred market delivery": initial drop to a short-term low, rally taking out a short-term swing high (breakout traders buy; their only logical stop is the initial low), then the low is taken.
  - "Not buying and selling pressure, but buying and selling liquidity": what matters is where the orders sit.
  - Keep the bigger structure in view: if the high-timeframe narrative is bullish, the sweep is accumulation; the opposite (sweep highs, then lower) if bearish. When short-term highs are taken in a bearish narrative, it is smart money building shorts.
- **How to identify:** Initial low forms within first 30 minutes of a day after a big up-close daily candle; bull flags; stops obviously below.
- **How to use:** Do not buy the first bounce. Wait for the low to be swept, with price reaching into a PD array (see hourly BISI below).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2024-09-12: a drop to a short-term low after the open; rally to the upper end of the opening range gap; then price sweeps the initial low again into the lower quadrant of the 1-hour BISI, "anyone that's long just had their bread toasted"; the low-of-day sell side is taken at about 0:26 and again later.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:23:54](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1434) — breadcrumbs, bull flags, rolling over into the BISI and the initial low
  - [0:25:33](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1533) — retail methods all buy here; initial low always suspect
  - [0:26:21](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1581) — use as turtle soup / scalp; sweeps the sell side
  - [0:46:47](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=2807) — engineering sentiment so traders flip short (sell stop hit)
  - [0:56:20](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3380) — "this is your Judas swing... deferred market delivery"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The Judas swing is described as a multi-step deferred delivery rather than a single 9:30–10:00 fake move.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: The predator / watering-hole model of liquidity runs
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage (analogy)
- **What ICT says:** Retail rushes to the "watering hole" in the first 30 minutes, thirsty to do something. Smart money (the predator) visits at night (accumulates earlier) and the crowd comes after, so when price trades below the trap low, the zone below it is "your hunting zone". Price levels, not supply/demand zones: "we're trading very specific price levels". The algorithm (price engine) drops price down so smart money can accumulate longs at a time and place; retail's stops are the liquidity.
- **Timestamps:** [0:45:08](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=2708), [0:57:53](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3473), [0:59:34](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3574) (hunting zone), [1:01:11](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3671) (not supply and demand)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Analogy only; the mechanical content is in the BISI grading below.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Grading an hourly BISI by quadrants (25/50/75): trade to the CE or lower quadrant, not the full low  (aliases: BISI = "buy-side imbalance, sell-side inefficiency", blue box, consequent encroachment, lower quadrant)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement (central technical teaching)
- **What ICT says:**
  - He marks a 1-hour BISI (the blue shaded area) defined by one candle's high to another's low, with a big candle passing through it. He drops a fib on that gap at 25%, 50% and 75%: the "upper quadrant", the CE (50%) and the "lower quadrant". "The mechanism it's calculating on is this high, this low and these levels."
  - Core rule: you do not want to see an inefficiency fully filled. If price wants to go higher, it will not touch the low boundary. Smart money looks for the lower quadrant or halfway point; ideally you see sensitivity in the upper half; if price goes below the CE, it must respect the lower quadrant and leave the lower boundary intact.
  - He earlier (0:06:07) repeats his 2024 teaching: when an inefficiency is bullish, don't expect complete overlap of the single candle that makes the inefficiency; expect sensitivity in the upper half.
  - He says liquidity voids being filled completely is not what he teaches (he contrasts with other teachers); price can trade all the way to the low, but that is not what he looks for.
  - A swing low is only interesting to him if it forms at a meaningful level: here, the swing low forms at the high / upper quadrant of the hourly BISI, so the liquidity below it is the interest. Swing high at the top of the opening range gap similarly has sell side beneath it.
  - Narrative: a Twitter poll: drop at the open into the hourly BISI, then work toward a smooth relative-equal-highs level at about 19,695 (4–5 highs from last week that "just did not get through"; he doesn't require it be reached that day; a logical draw because everyone forgot it).
- **How to identify:** On the 1H chart: candle high vs candle low gap; fib 25/50/75 over it; mark where short-term lows/highs form relative to the quadrants.
- **How to use:** Entries/targets:
  - Levels of interest: the CE and the lower quadrant, and any smaller inefficiency between those two prices.
  - Scale in: one contract at the CE, one at the lower quadrant. Stop at least 2–3 ticks below the BISI's low (the full inefficiency low), because it can touch the low even if you don't want it to.
  - Don't buy just because price is cheap and at the level; wait until it "gives enough information" (not full confirmation, "just a little bit more"), because price could still drop to the low of the BISI.
  - Prop firms may forbid averaging in / adding to a losing trade; in that case wait for the signature described below instead of scaling.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 2024-09-12: hourly BISI and a 5-minute BISI below the opening range gap; price opens and drops into the 5m BISI's upper half (sensitivity), rallies to the opening range gap high, drops again into the 1H BISI lower quadrant (sweeping the initial low of day), then rallies; bodies respect the lower quadrant.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:04:17](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=257) — BISI on hourly, quadrants on it
  - [0:06:07](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=367) — 2024 teaching: sensitivity in the upper half, no complete overlap
  - [0:39:29](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=2369) — why this swing low matters (forms at the high of the BISI)
  - [0:54:45](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3285) — 25/50/75 fib; it won't touch the lower boundary
  - [1:02:46](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3766) — scale in at CE and lower quadrant; stop 2–3 ticks below
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines "trade to the CE" by making the lower quadrant the outer limit and the full low the invalidation area. Exact NQ price levels in the captions are garbled (19,28x levels for the ORG high), caption unclear.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Immediate rebalance, vacuum block and order block sequence (worked example)  (aliases: immediate rebalance, vacuum block, order block theory, opening price, change in state of delivery)
body:
- **Kind:** definition + example (several new/applied terms)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price in the lower half of the gap: when price trades to the CE and returns up into the old low without reaching the midpoint of that smaller imbalance, it is weak (the most sensitive points are in the lower half), so it should go on to the next level, the lower quadrant of the 1H BISI.
  - Immediate rebalance: a candle opens and trades straight to the prior candle's low (here a discount wick that rebalances the gap formed by the open); annotate it. He counts three things at once: immediate rebalance + discount wick CE + nearness to the BISI's CE, then price hits the lower quadrant and runs slightly past it.
  - After the lower quadrant is swept, price trades higher: the candle's opening price plus a volume imbalance are two PD arrays. The series of down-closed candles is an order block ("order block theory, there's a chapter coming out"); the opening price of the order block is the change in the state of delivery.
  - Vacuum block (as used here): a separation between one candle's close and the next candle's open; there is no price between the two except the wick. The wick trades down to the prior close — that's the immediate rebalance, because the wick is the gap.
  - Price then delivers up to the first (highest) of the down-closed candles, the high of the whole order block; the market opens, trades into the order block and sends price higher to a swing high at the high end of the opening range gap, taking buy side.
  - Rule on timing: because the lowest desired level (BISI's lower quadrant) had already been traded to and slightly breached, the bounce from there is the valid reaction.
- **How to identify:** Series of down-closed candles at the low; the first up move's opening price; a close-to-open separation (vacuum); wick filling the separation.
- **How to use:** Entry is the order block / opening price after the sweep of the lower quadrant, with the stop under the sweep low (his stop guidance above); target the ORG high / swing high above.
- **Example in this video:** NQ ~10:35–10:45 ET (video 1:05–1:09): price hits the lower quadrant of the 1H BISI, spikes slightly past it, rallies; a candle opens with a gap above the prior close, wicks back down to that close (immediate rebalance), then rallies to the top of the down-closed series (order block high) and on to the opening range gap high.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [1:05:07](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3907) — lower-half sensitivity; weak if it doesn't reach the midpoint
  - [1:05:55](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=3955) — immediate rebalance, wick CE, three confluences
  - [1:07:33](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=4053) — order block, opening price, change in state of delivery
  - [1:08:23](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=4103) — vacuum block definition
  - [1:09:11](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=4151) — delivery to the order block high, then up to ORG high
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First time in this series that "vacuum block" and "immediate rebalance" are named together with order block theory; the description of the candle structure is spoken, so the exact candle count is not stated (caption unclear).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Two-layer buy-side / sell-side routine for the PM session (starting 1:30 PM ET)  (aliases: PM session, afternoon session protocol)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry framework
- **What ICT says:**
  - Don't need to trade the morning session at all; the PM session is "always" the easiest session for index futures because the day's range is already printed. You won't get the lion's share, but it is ripe for consistent setups. After a large-range day expect the better trades from 1:30 PM ET into the last hour.
  - Routine: come back around 1:15–1:30 PM ET. On the 15-minute chart note the highest high and lowest low of the day; drop to 5m (or 1m) and mark the next lower high and next higher low inside that range. That gives two layers of buy side (day high and the lower high) and two layers of sell side (day low and the higher low).
  - Before 1:30, write down in the journal (with the time) which side you think price will gravitate to; then see what happens as the PM session unfolds into about 2:00 PM. Chances are it takes one of them, not both.
  - Same method for London: use the previous session; previous day's high/low and the high/low inside it formed up to 2:00 AM ET.
  - Last hour: ICT says price prices in the extreme high/low of the day with big expansion candles (an open near the low and a close at the high); then in the last ~45 minutes it comes off the high/low into settlement; four macros in the last hour (five if you count the 2:00 bleeding into 3:00). He pushes back on someone who said no new high/low gets made in the last hour (the caption's "that is absolute" is unclear).
  - If the AM kept the low of day intact and consolidated, it is "all positive for the afternoon". He also expects an eventual reach for the 19,695 relative equal highs.
- **How to identify:** 15m day high/low; 5m/1m nearest lower high / higher low inside.
- **How to use:** Predict side, journal it, trade once price shows structure toward it; he says the same process is what he does every afternoon ("never changes").
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:34:37](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=2077) — better trading from 1:30 PM after an anemic open
  - [1:21:22](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=4882) — mark highest high / lowest low plus inner high and low; journal the prediction
  - [1:22:12](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=4932) — same for London; previous session and 2:00 AM reference
  - [1:27:06](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=5226) — 15m then 5m then 1m layers; 1:30 and 2:00 PM
  - [1:30:15](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=5415) — last hour expansion, last 45 minutes into settlement; four macros
  - [1:31:02](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=5462) — PM session is the easiest for index futures
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** New explicit operational routine; he says it's "the same stuff in the book", so a reader can cross-check.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ September 12, 2024
head: Multi-timeframe monitoring and building the narrative from other traders' failure
body:
- **Kind:** process
- **What ICT says:**
  - He cycles his eyes through daily, 4H, 1H, 15m, 5m, plus a matrix of 5/4/3/2/1-minute charts and another matrix of 45s/30s/15s/5s charts.
  - For each timeframe he asks how traders on that timeframe would interpret it and where their stop would sit; the goal is to see where less-informed participants "fail today" and where he can see high-probability delivery to a specific level.
  - Don't over-read retail patterns (pennants, double/triple touches, trend lines); the question is why price should go up: buyers need a discount price, which the algorithm affords.
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:47](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1787), [0:30:34](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1834), [0:32:11](https://youtu.be/DRuEMX4RhMw?t=1931)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Process, not a trade model. He notes he has about 12 monitors but the principle is the multi-timeframe sweep.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Fair Value Gap — three-candle anatomy and candle roles  (aliases ICT uses: "inefficiency", "sell-side imbalance buy-side inefficiency (SIBI) / buy-side imbalance sell-side inefficiency (BISI)", "the framing candle")
body:
- **Kind:** definition + rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - A valid FVG is always three candles. Candle 2 (the middle one) is the displacement/"trigger" candle. It is the candle you watch to see whether the gap stays open.
  - Candle 1 and candle 3 are the outer candles. The gap is the space between candle 1's extreme and candle 3's extreme that candle 2 delivered through, with no overlap.
  - Candle 3 is the entry candle. Candle 2 "frames" the gap: it is the area price should come back and revisit.
  - A gap is not a zone. There are specific price levels: the high/low of the outer candles, the midpoint (CE), and the quadrants.
  - Once candle 4 opens, you have a valid reason to anticipate a return into the gap. It may never come back; if price keeps going, let it.
  - A valid gap shows certain "signatures." ICT looks for all of them; a gap with only a few can still be used for drills, but a bad result in a drill is not a failure (see Process).
- **How to identify:**
  - Bullish: candle 1 moves and delivers price, candle 2 delivers price higher ("that's key"), candle 3 trades higher than candle 2 and candle 3's low does not touch or overlap candle 1's high. The gap runs from candle 1's high to candle 3's low.
  - Bearish: mirror image. Candle 3's high is the bottom of the gap and candle 1's low is the top.
  - Draw the gap including any volume imbalance (see separate concept).
- **How to use:**
  - Stop loss (bearish): aggressive/max-leverage stop is one tick above candle 2's high. Conservative stop for a one-contract trader who does not want to be shaken out is candle 1's high (mirror for bullish: candle 2's low = aggressive, candle 1's low = conservative).
  - Entry (bearish): candle 3's high, or one tick below it if "100% certain." Entry (bullish): candle 3's low plus one tick.
  - See "FVG entry model" and "Quadrant grading" below.
- **Example in this video:** Hypothetical hand-drawn candles first (bearish, then reversed to bullish, ~0:18–0:45), then repeated on the live NQ 1m chart on 9/16/2024 (see live trade concept).
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:01](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1021) three candles make an FVG; [0:18:38](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1118) candle 2 vs candle 1 stop; [0:25:38](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1538) candle roles recap; [0:40:11](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2411) bullish version.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says "this is what we're covering this week"; the details (candle roles, exact stop, exact entry) are being made explicit and "removing all the confusion about where stop losses go and what candlestick is the trigger." He notes the 9:30 opening-candle mistake later (see FVG selection).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: FVG entry model — candle 3's edge ±1 tick, limit order, and not a "zone"  (aliases: "low-hanging fruit entry", "ICT entry")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Entry for a bearish FVG: candle 3's high, minus one tick (a limit sell just below it if you are very sure price will drop). Entry for a bullish FVG: candle 3's low plus one tick.
  - ICT often places entries just ahead of the level ("a little bit ahead of a fair value gap or a bearish order block") so he gets filled. He does not like missing entries but is not worried about missing a trade: "81 ways" into the same trade.
  - He insists this is why ICT is not "supply and demand": you do not "trade a zone," you trade specific levels (candle 3's edge, CE, quadrant, candle 1/2 extreme). Shading a gap on a chart is only a visual.
  - Learners should first practice the easy objective entry (candle 3's edge ±1 tick) with one contract. Practice with market orders first so you learn timing and anticipatory price reading. The professional and more efficient way is limit orders. Exits should be limits too; entries on limits, or on rare occasions buying/selling on a stop.
  - Market orders are really only for getting out of something to protect money.
- **How to identify:** n/a (see FVG anatomy).
- **How to use:** Put the limit one tick inside the gap edge on candle 3; stop per candle 2 / candle 1; add only at defined deeper levels (see pyramiding). Once price leaves the gap and runs, trail/reduce the stop; ICT says it "should not go back inside the fair value gap."
- **Example in this video:** Live bullish 1m FVG: ideal entry = candle 3's low 19,339.25 + 1 tick = 19,339.50; ICT's actual market fill was 19,342.00 (about 2.5 handles worse, about $50 per mini), see live trade concept.
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:32](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1232) entry on candle 3's high or one tick below; [0:28:47](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1727) get filled, not zones; [0:35:16](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2116) easiest objective entry, market orders first; [0:36:05](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2165) limits are more professional.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** His market-order advice is for the learning stage; he later says he himself market-orders in when he missed a limit (see missed entries). Slight tension with "market orders only to exit"; resolved as: market-in only to capture a level you intended to be filled at.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Quadrant grading / Consequent Encroachment of the FVG  (aliases: CE, midpoint, "upper/lower quadrant", "grading your inefficiencies")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Always grade an inefficiency: mark the midpoint (CE, the 50% level) plus the upper and lower quadrant levels (the 25%/75% marks). A Fibonacci or a rectangle with a midline gives the same thing.
  - Bullish gap: the ideal is that price only drops into the upper half (from candle 3's low down to CE) and leaves the lower half untouched. That indicates the gap is "extremely bullish" and you are on side; you shouldn't worry about the stop, it is just there to do its job.
  - Bearish gap: ideal entries form in the lower half (from candle 3's high up to CE) and the upper half (CE up to candle 1's low) stays open. It then means a very strong probability that you are right.
  - Price should spend little time in the entry half: ideally one candle, at most two, enters it, and then the run starts.
  - Wicks (not bodies) may poke through the far side of the gap; bodies should not close beyond it.
  - If candle 4 drops into the gap right after it forms and immediately starts running, that is a clue the other half will stay open and the move is on a fast track.
  - The more price moves away from the gap, the less trepidation about the stop below the gap low.
  - The CE level is "your most important level" once you have drawn the gap with its volume imbalance.
- **How to identify:** Draw FIB/rectangle from candle 1's extreme to candle 3's extreme; mark 25/50/75%.
- **How to use:** Buy in the upper half (bullish), sell in the lower half (bearish). Anything beyond CE is a weaker location: size down to one or two contracts. Use the state of the far half as the confidence gauge.
- **Example in this video:** Bullish FVG that morning on NQ 1m: price dropped only into the upper half (about 3.75 handles of draw down from a ~19,405–19,445 fill, caption figures garbled), reached just short of the upper-quadrant level and never touched CE, then rallied; ICT: "did it leave the lower half open? yes... that means it's bullish."
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:25](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1585) CE and the half you want left open; [0:43:27](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2607) bullish: buy midpoint-to-low, lower half untouched; [0:53:58](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3238) best buys are in the upper half; [2:02:42](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=7362) "you have to always grade your inefficiencies."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Mean threshold" is used for the 50% of an order-block candle; CE is used for the 50% of a gap/wick (see separate concept).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Volume imbalance included in the gap drawing  (aliases: "volume imbalance")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** When drawing the gap, do not use only the wick-to-wick range. If there is a volume imbalance (a separation between the bodies of consecutive candles, where the bodies do not touch) next to the gap, include it so that the drawn range, and therefore the CE, is correct. "You can't just use the wick... that's not valid."
- **How to identify:** Look for a body-to-body separation adjacent to the wick-defined gap; extend the drawn gap through it, back to candle 1.
- **How to use:** Compute the CE and quadrants from the full range including the volume imbalance; he says this gives a better determination of the CE level.
- **Example in this video:** Hypothetical diagrams at ~0:24 and ~0:42; also referenced as the "volume imbalance" the morning's low traded into at 0:14.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:00](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1440) wick-only drawing is invalid; [0:42:40](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2560) always include the small separation.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Captions are garbled here ("(caption unclear)" on exactly which two candles the body separation sits between); his statement is that the box must extend through any volume imbalance.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Balanced Price Range (BPR)
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** Two opposing gaps that share the same price space (one offering a sell, one offering a buy) form a balanced price range; he calls it that when a bearish and bullish gap overlap. If price has gone down into one and the other holds as support, price can rally ("treat it as a discount array").
- **Example in this video:** On the morning chart, a small gap and a gap right after it isolated the price action in a BPR; he preferred it not to fill ([0:24:00](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1440)). Later, while expecting a rally to the opening range gap CE, he says two candles "shared the same space," so it is a BPR and price should find support in it and attack the buy side ([1:18:14](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4694)).
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:00](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1440), [1:18:14](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4694).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Mentioned in passing, not defined formally in this video.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Scaling in / pyramiding into an FVG (demonstration only)  (aliases: adding at quadrants)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (advanced; explicitly not for beginners)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Illustrative bearish plan: sell 6 contracts at candle 3's high minus one tick; add 4 more when price tags the lower quadrant of the gap; if price reaches CE or goes into the upper half (deep premium), add about 2 more as long as it keeps tapping there and bodies stay inside candle 1's low.
  - Bullish mirror: add at the midpoint, at the lower quadrant, and again if price tags the low of the gap, because the stop sits below candle 2's low.
  - Wicks through the far edge of the gap are acceptable; closing bodies beyond it are not.
  - He repeatedly says: do not pyramid or build big positions when learning; "just try to trade one contract."
- **How to use:** Size down as price goes to less ideal levels (beyond CE); "anything less than that I'm going to do one or two contracts."
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:35](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1775) 6 / 4 / 2 contract illustration; [0:35:16](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2116) "do not try to pyramid" (when learning).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Contract counts are illustrative of what he does, not a recommendation.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Missed entries — market in at the better price  (aliases: "missing the limit")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If you miss the limit (distracted, stepped away) and price is now below your bullish entry (above your bearish entry), execute at market right away: price is offering a better price than the one you were willing to pay, so you are not "chasing." If it touches the upper quadrant or CE, buy more; anything beyond that, keep to one or two contracts, because you do not want to see price spend time in the lower (far) half.
- **How to use:** Treat the better price as a gift, but keep the same stop (below candle 2's low) and sizing discipline.
- **Timestamps:** [0:48:20](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2900) "I'm just Marketing in"; [0:49:06](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2946) why that is not chasing.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The next video (#29) is devoted to managing missed entries.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Failed FVG becomes an inversion FVG; taking the loss as "VIP information"  (aliases: iFVG, "orange hue", reclaimed FVG)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - If you are stopped out of an FVG trade, you are probably watching an inversion FVG form: a gap that fails and now acts in the opposite direction. You can then trade the opposite direction with half the size you lost on and make the loss back and more.
  - Losing is "paying a premium for information"; you get better view of the next price run ("VIP seating").
  - A failed bearish gap (price trades above it) can be retraced into its upper half only, then it acts as a discount array and sends price higher; a failed bullish gap that price trades down through becomes resistance (he colored it orange to show that it will "not be treated as a buying opportunity").
  - Reclaimed: when price later rallies back above an inverted gap, it can act as a support again, a "stepping stone" toward the minor buy side. He calls the gap-turned-resistance-then-reclaimed a "reclaimed fair value gap" ("easy bread and butter type setup" for his son).
- **How to identify:** The close (body) beyond the gap on the failing side; he warns that wicks into a gap are not rejection if the bodies are respecting the gap.
- **How to use:** Treat the failing-gap level as the next entry area. Do not fear stops, because a stop being hit tells you where the next trade is.
- **Example in this video:** On 9/16 NQ, a gap that had been bullish was traded down through and then served as resistance (price sold off from it); later price rallied back above it and he wanted it to act as support (inversion again) on a pullback into it ([1:22:29](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4949), [1:23:17](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4997)).
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:52](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=1972) stop-out = premium for information; [0:52:18](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3138) stop out means inversion FVG, trade back with half size; [1:07:01](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4021) orange colour = inversion; [1:22:29](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4949) reclaimed FVG.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Sequence of which specific gap flipped how many times is hard to follow from captions; the principle is clear.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Choosing the right FVG — context at the open, the first presented FVG, and why a short was not valid
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Which FVG to use among several is "trial and error in the beginning," and the question he gets most. The week is meant to supply the nuts and bolts.
  - He wants to "let them have" the first minutes of trading after 9:30: no prediction, watch for the first presented FVG, "let the market shake out its initial excitement."
  - Why the bearish gap at the open was not a short: (1) the market had already gapped lower from Friday's settlement (a deep discount to start with); (2) at 9:30 it sold straight down with no pullbacks (Judas swing: "you never want to chase something like that"); (3) the only gap formed was a single candle in the lower half of the range from the 9:30 open down to the swing low, with no other inefficiency, order block or short-term high above to sell from; (4) price rallied into it and printed little wicks/dojis that retail reads as rejection while the bodies respected the gap, i.e., accumulation. "Retail logic": inside an inefficiency wick = rejection, therefore short. ICT: bait.
  - The gap in the lower half of the drop is "fake"; he would rather see price trade higher out of it and pull back only into its upper half.
  - If price keeps going down through it, a bearish FVG that formed in the lower half of an already deep drop should not be sold. If instead an inefficiency was all overlapping candles and the last candle then created the gap with space above, it could be tradable ("examples later").
  - The first FVG on a 1m chart cannot include the 9:30 candle as its basis; it can appear from the 9:31 candle on. He realised mid-stream that a gap he had called the first was not (caption partly unclear). Video #29 clarifies: the earliest possible FVG has its middle candle (candle 2) at 9:31, since the 9:30 open candle can only be candle 1.
- **How to identify:** After the first swing low forms (a candle with a higher low to its left and right), at that candle's close go back through the swing for inefficiencies, order blocks, short-term highs where buy side would rest. If there is none (a single straight-line drop), the move is characteristic of a Judas swing.
- **How to use:** Do not chase. Frame a long for the draw to high of day / opening price / ORG CE; entry from the first FVG that forms after the swing low, per the entry model.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Mon 9/16/2024: opens below Friday's settlement (big opening gap down), 9:30 opens and drops in a straight line (Judas), forms a swing low, a lone bearish FVG sits in the lower half of that drop, price rallies into it and prints small wicks in it, then rallies to the minor buy side and lower quadrant of the ORG; later makes a new high (above initial HOD) and then a lower high near 19,463.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:37](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=877) first look; [1:01:19](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3679) why not a short; [1:03:42](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3822) FVG in lower half of the drop; [1:14:56](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4496) 9:30 candle can't be the first gap.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Contrasts with "retail logic" of selling every rejection wick; reiterates that a down-close imbalance after a Judas move is a bait.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Wicks and candle gaps graded like FVGs; premium vs discount array  (aliases: "wick = inefficiency", "PD arrays work with wicks")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / new coinage-ish
- **What ICT says:** Anything that acts like an inefficiency, including a long wick, is graded the same way. A wick above market price is a premium array; a wick below price is a discount array (he doesn't use the word "tail"). For a bullish wick, the upper half should keep price from trading into the lower half. The wick's midpoint is its CE.
- **How to use:** If the next candle trades down to a wick's CE and sends price higher, that is a discount array doing its job. If the wick-CE is traded through, the setup is weakened. He uses the wick on candle 1 as an "extra credit" layer: see the next concept.
- **Timestamps:** [0:55:35](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3335) wicks work the same as FVGs; [1:06:13](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3973) CE of a wick as a reason to expect higher prices.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Said he gets no benefit from renaming; it is the same PD-array logic.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Candle 1 wick as a second layer — tighter stop ("extra credit")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** If candle 1 has a wick adjacent to the gap, that wick is itself an inefficiency: two layers of gaps. The stop can be placed one tick below the wick's CE instead of below candle 2's low. After price runs, you can move the stop just below that, then once price has left the high, near the lower quadrant of the FVG. This takes months of observation to trust: "you can't trust it the first few times."
- **Example in this video:** The live 1m bullish FVG (~11:00 ET): ICT points at the wick on candle 1 of that gap as the "extra credit" layer (2:01:03 onward), with its CE as an alternative stop reference; his actual draw down was about 1.75 handles.
- **Timestamps:** [2:00:14](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=7214) extra credit; [2:01:53](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=7313) stop one tick below wick CE.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says this is an advanced refinement shown to private students first.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Opening range gap CE ("mid gap") — first draw of the day, 70% within 30 minutes  (aliases: RTH opening range gap, "consequent encroachment of the opening range gap", ORG midpoint)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Draw a Fibonacci from the previous day's settlement price to the first opening tick at 9:30 (RTH). The 50% is the ORG CE; mark the lower/upper quadrants too.
  - About 70% of the time the midpoint is touched by 10:00 (within the first 30 minutes). "Not 100%": in the mentorship it has failed "one or two times," and it gets hit eventually.
  - It is "my always first draw." Even when price doesn't reach it, the CE is the bias anchor: you expect price to try for it, and the targets before it are the high of day, the opening price (a static price level, not a zone), buy-side liquidity (smooth/equal highs), and the lower quadrant of the ORG.
- **How to use:** Use it as a draw, a first partial or a Terminus. Choosing the easiest first partial (e.g., the lower-quadrant or CE of the gap, or the first FVG) is fine.
- **Example in this video:** 9/16/2024 NQ: gap opening lower; price rallies to the lower quadrant of the ORG but not CE by 10:00; he says "that need not be filled today." The level stays a key level for the session.
- **Timestamps:** [0:45:53](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2753) 70% rule; [0:46:41](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=2801) half the gap hit by 10:00; [0:58:46](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3526) how to draw the FIB; [1:15:47](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4547) "my always first draw."
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Captions at 0:45 say "7%"; clearly 70%. Appears consistent with earlier mentorship teaching on opening range gaps.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Judas swing at the 9:30 open after a gap
body:
- **Kind:** example
- **What ICT says:** If the market opens at 9:30 and goes straight in the direction of the gap (here, lower), with no swing structure to trade, that is a Judas swing; do not chase it, "let it run out of steam." It will run back over the top of the move. Characteristic: a single straight shot with no inefficiencies/order blocks/short-term highs to trade from.
- **Timestamps:** [1:02:08](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3728); [1:03:42](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3822).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Primary vs minor buy-side/sell-side liquidity; swing low definition; bodied swing high
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A swing low is the lowest candle with a higher low to its left and a higher low to its right; the swing is confirmed at the close that completes it. At that point go back for inefficiencies, order blocks, short-term highs.
  - A minor sell-side is the initial low; once taken out, the new low is the primary sell-side ("a much more meaningful event"). Similarly, a high that takes out the initial high of the day is primary buy-side. Relative equal highs and old highs are targets.
  - He prefers to see a bodied swing high be run (a stop hunt) rather than a tiny wick high.
  - After price fails to get ORG CE and leaves a lower high, short stops rest above it: his note was 19,463 (to be carried as a key level into lunch and the afternoon). He writes raw numbers down on a notepad and plans how they might be used in the next session (lunch macro, afternoon).
- **Timestamps:** [1:02:56](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=3776) swing low defined; [1:19:04](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4744) primary buy side; [1:20:40](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=4840) minor vs primary; [1:24:59](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=5099) bodied swing high.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Minor" and "primary" are by reference to the day's initial range.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Mean threshold of an order block (down-close candle) and "reclaimed order block"  (aliases: OB mean threshold, MT)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** For a bullish down-close candle (order block), no candle should close below its mean threshold (midpoint); it can stab through or even wick to the candle's low in theory, "it's not the best." If the midpoint is traded to/through, that indicates weakness and a likely run lower. Used to frame the next displacement; if it fails, you sit still or reassess/go the other direction, "that's part of using the PD arrays." A bullish order block that is violated and then recovered can become a reclaimed (bullish) order block that runs for the buy side.
- **Timestamps:** [1:31:44](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=5504) no close below mean threshold; [1:40:43](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=6043) reclaimed order block.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says he is "trying to trade the fair value gap today" and only describes the order block logic for framing.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Immediate rebalance
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:** After a gap forms, an immediate rebalance is price coming straight back to the candle's low (the gap's edge); the very next candle then usually resumes the prior direction.
- **Timestamps:** [1:34:10](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=5650).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Trade ICT FVGs Correctly \ September 16, 2024
head: Minimum range rule — 15 to 20 handles from entry to first target; first partial and Terminus
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Only take a framed setup if the range from entry to the first objective is at least about 15 handles for his son, ideally 20 handles (80 ticks on NQ); if it cannot make 15, 20 should still be visible for the target. He dislikes 10-handle trades: 10 handles is static price movement, you can be right on direction and still get stopped, and the risk model in NQ does not work.
  - Start the clock at the time of entry. Targets: first partial = the easiest liquidity or inefficiency; Terminus = where you are done for the day.
  - Stage 1 of drilling: just one exit (first partial). After 2-3 weeks of daily drills with no anxiety, stage 2: first partial plus a Terminus, e.g., the next liquidity (CE of the ORG, old highs, relative equal highs). The trade need not reach the final target; the range needs to afford it.
- **Example in this video:** Entry candle low about 19,340; first partial = the minor buy side/equal highs about 19,360 → 20 handles = 80 ticks.
- **Timestamps:** [1:38:16](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=5896) 15-20 handle rule; [1:39:07](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=5947) why not 10 handles; [1:46:29](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=6389) first partial then Terminus; [2:09:07](https://youtu.be/HhgWGduQZQY?t=7747) 20 handles = 80 ticks.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He specifies 15-20 handles for his son's learning drills in NQ; not claimed to be universal for all instruments.

head: Live trade demonstration — NQ 1m bullish FVG (paper account), 9/16/2024
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says / does:**
  - Bias: price took the sell side, left clean equal highs (buy stops protecting retail shorts) and an undelivered ORG CE above. Everyone short has made money; the market tends to roll against those in profit.
  - Setup: a bullish 1m FVG whose candle 3's low is 19,339.25; candle 3's low is the same price as the next candle(s) so it is a single-delivery gap. Ideal entry 19,339.50. When candle 4 opened right at the gap and started dropping into it, he market-bought. Fill 19,342.00; lowest tick on a 1-second chart 19,340.25: draw down 1.75 handles within seconds. No pullback to CE. Stop planned below candle 2's low.

He said total cost was about $50 (draw down about $40 plus $10 fee per contract with AMP Global) for about $630 profit on his paper account (caption; contract count not clear).
