title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: Opening range gap CE ("mid gap") — the 70% first-30-minutes draw and its size filter  (aliases: ORG midpoint, "consequent encroachment of the opening range gap", "70% strike rate")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Opening range gap = difference between yesterday's RTH settlement (last print at 4:14 PM ET; "settles at 4:15") and the first opening tick at 9:30 ET. The "opening range" is the 30-minute interval to 10:00.
  - Drop a Fibonacci from the previous settlement to the 9:30 open; the 50% level (CE) is the bias. About 70% of the time (not 100%, not a guarantee) price trades to the midpoint within the first 30 minutes (before 10:00).
  - Size filter: the gap should be more than 40 handles ("minimum 40"); larger is better; roughly 100 handles is a sweet spot; above about 200 handles he defers the setup because "heavy manipulation" means price may keep running.
  - If the gap is above price it makes the bias for the first 30 minutes down (premium gap -> expect a return to mid gap); mirror for a gap lower.
  - Combine with the economic calendar to improve the hit rate. A gap open above previous day's settlement is also described as a "premium" gap.
  - Expectation: one trade a week from this alone (~50 handles ≈ $1,000 on one mini, per ICT) would already be meaningful; "you have an experiment laboratory for 30 minutes every single day."
- **How to identify:** Check the gap size (settlement to 9:30 open) in handles, plot the 50% and the 25%/75% quadrants.
- **How to use:** Direction of the first FVG trade is set by where mid gap sits relative to price; target = mid gap (or partials en route, lower quadrant, etc.).
- **Example in this video:** NQ Dec contract, Tue 9/17/2024: previous settlement about 19,661.5, open about 19,795 (over 100 handles up, caption figures partly garbled), mid gap 19,728.25, lower quadrant about 19,694.5. Price sweeps Friday's high, forms a 9:33 FVG, trades down and delivers mid gap before 10:00 ("70% strike rate true today"), then lower quadrant 19,694.5 is the next objective. ICT says the gap-down mirror is to go long off the first FVG for mid gap.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:39](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=819) how the gap is defined (4:14/4:15 settlement to 9:30 open); [0:24:45](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=1485) mid gap delivered; [0:33:04](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=1984) "gap open higher more than 40 handles... 70% strike rate"; [0:52:29](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=3149) larger gap = more opportunity; [1:09:21](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=4161) 40 minimum / ~100 sweet spot / over 200 defer.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Adds the explicit 40-handle minimum and 200-handle caution to the #28 teaching of the 70% rule. He says "50 handles" to mid gap although the quoted figures work out to roughly 67 handles; treat the numbers as approximate.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: First presented FVG after 9:31 as the entry mechanism to mid gap  (aliases: "first fair value gap", "first presented FVG", "ICT's blue ribbon recipe")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Use the very first FVG that forms after the open (between 9:31 and 10:00). The earliest possible one has candle 2 at 9:31, because it cannot be built on the 9:30 candle as its middle candle (he corrected himself on this).
  - Trade it in the direction of mid gap. For a short from a premium gap: entry anywhere inside the gap, with candle 3's high (or one tick below it if you are aggressive) as the most direct level, with CE or the lower quadrant as other levels (all in the lower part of the gap); stop above candle 2's high. For longs, stop below candle 2's low.
  - Wicks above the gap ("Mohawk") do not invalidate the trade as long as the stop is above candle 2.
  - Stay in the trade until it is stopped out or reaches the target, as long as price stays beyond the stop and has not yet reached mid gap.
  - Time-based, mechanical, finite parameters: "every day at 9:00 ET you sit down and open NQ (or ES)..."; he first automated this kind of logic years ago in TradeStation EasyLanguage ("ATM with a pin code"), because the setup is rule-based.
  - Do not modify the recipe or rename it; the failure modes are over-leveraging, trading before the FVG is offered, not taking the trade because you haven't desensitized, and adding your own "horseradish."
- **How to identify:** First 3-candle imbalance after 9:31 on the 1m chart (also usable on 15s). Candle 2 = the displacement candle, candle 1 = prior, candle 3 = entry.
- **How to use:** Short entry near the lower edge of the bearish gap, stop above candle 2, target mid gap; then manage via partials (see next concept).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m 9/17/2024: the gap formed at 9:33 after a run to about 19,794–19,795; candle 3's high about 19,795; ICT's referenced entry is a limit near 19,794.75 (one tick below). Price spikes slightly above the gap (Mohawk) without taking out candle 2's high, then falls to mid gap 19,728.25 by 10:00.
- **Timestamps:** [0:29:50](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=1790) first presented FVG and entry; [0:33:53](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=2033) "first FVG that forms at 9:31, the earliest"; [0:36:17](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=2177) stop above candle 2; [0:55:41](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=3341) why it cannot be the 9:30 candle; [1:11:46](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=4306) rules recap.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Clarifies the 9:30-candle slip from #28. He pairs this with the 9:50–10:10 macro and the "10:00 hour Silver Bullet" idea but chose to wait.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: Managing the first-FVG trade — partials, break-even, and holding for mid gap
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Once price breaks a short-term low after you are short, move the stop to cover costs (break-even); if you have more than one contract, take a partial below that short-term low.
  - At mid gap he suggests taking 75–80% off; if you want to try for the whole gap, put the stop above the short-term low and leave the balance ("if it stops you out on the balance, who cares, you had a free look").
  - If you don't know how to select partials: take two partials, keep the stop where it covers costs, and "let the market take you out" on the remainder; the target is only a reference. This "removes all the I have to be right stuff."
  - If trading one contract and the stop runs, accept it and record how you felt; don't think "I wish I had closed it at the maximum open profit."
  - After a loss do not "make up": next day, simply take the setup by the parameters on the smallest size.
- **How to use:** Stage 1: one exit at mid gap; later: partial -> stop to cost -> second partial at the next liquidity (e.g., relative equal lows) -> trail.
- **Example in this video:** In the hypothetical late-session short he walks through (2:00–2:07): short limit one tick above the CE of a wick (~19,745.25), stop above that wick's CE, first partial at the FVG, second partial at the relative equal lows, stop stays at cost, remainder runs to the rejection-block low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:57:15](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=3435) stop to cover costs, partial below short-term low; [0:58:04](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=3484) 75–80% off at mid gap; [2:04:31](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=7471) two partials booked; [2:07:28](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=7648) let the market take you out.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** First time in the series he states explicit % partial sizes for the mid-gap model.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: Mohawk (wick through a PD array) and being selective on "muddy" days  (aliases: "coloring outside the lines", "curveball", "feint")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage / refinement
- **What ICT says:** A Mohawk is price poking beyond a PD array (e.g., a wick above a bearish FVG) before honoring it; it is not a failure of the method. He compares it to a boxer's feint or a pitcher's curveball. Ideally price stays inside the gap, but on days before high-impact news the delivery is "muddier" and less crisp.
- **How to use:** On such days do not use the lowest entry threshold (candle 3's edge); be more selective: let price run to the extreme of the gap first, then sell inside the wick that creates the Mohawk, getting very good premium pricing with a stop above candle 2.
- **Timestamps:** [0:30:37](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=1837) Mohawk created; [0:31:28](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=1888) curveball analogy; [0:32:17](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=1937) entry selectivity on muddy days.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines #28's "specific price levels" teaching: on news-adjacent days the deepest part of the gap/wick is the better entry.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: FOMC-day behavior and avoiding it as a learner  (aliases: news driver, two-stage delivery)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / context
- **What ICT says:** FOMC day is heavily manipulated and delivered in two stages: at 2:00 PM price goes one direction (higher or lower; he doesn't know which), and at the 2:30 press conference there is a counter-run, "usually, not all the time," over the top of the earlier move. Like NFP but more exaggerated. The day before FOMC is ranging/choppy with consolidations and less crisp price, and large players don't position ahead of it. For his inexperienced son: avoid FOMC day entirely (so no regret/temptation), and if trading the day before, only the morning session. Don't position large or swing-trade into it; the afternoon on the day before is dead and difficult.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:52](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=772) 2:00 / 2:30 two-stage delivery; [0:15:16](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=916) why positioning ahead makes no sense; [1:14:14](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=4454) day-before afternoon is spotty.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "Usually" counter-run; he does not claim direction.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: Missed entries — getting into a move that has already started  (aliases: late entry, "regret", chase vs fade)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / process
- **What ICT says:**
  - Missed entries come from freezing, second-guessing, turning the charts on late, or not noticing the setup. The title topic is "how to get into a move that's already happened or started," a skill he calls very valuable.
  - Time-frame translation: treat your execution time frame as the "hourly" of a smaller one: for a higher-time-frame trader, use a 15m or 5m (or in the examples 1m/15s) chart to get into a move that you missed on the hour, e.g., you scan the hourly chart, see a setup that has already started to move, and then trade into the first presented/next FVG on the lower time frame.
  - You have two choices when you miss a move: (1) regret, get angry, chase it or, worse, fade it because you are mad at the market; or (2) accept that the setups repeat, find another one, and wait for the FVG to be offered. He pushes (2): "wrestling the marketplace" is never good.
  - If the FVG isn't offered (price runs without giving you a gap), log it and don't get angry.
  - Use the time frame above the executable time frame and the time frame you intend to trade to frame the move.
- **How to use:** After the move starts, wait for a lower-time-frame FVG/imbalance to form in the move's direction (or an inversion), enter per the entry model, and require at least 20 handles of room to the first target.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:36](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=276) topic stated; [0:07:53](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=473) hourly vs 15m/5m/1m translation; [0:09:29](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=569) "get into a move that's already happened"; [0:41:58](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=2518) two choices (regret/chase/fade); [1:16:37](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=4597) don't be mad, find another setup.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Builds on #28's "if you miss your limit, market in at the better price" with a lower-time-frame and psychology framing.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: "High frequency" no-bias drill: relative equal highs/lows on 1m/5m with a 15s FVG entry  (aliases: short-term liquidity runs, sub-one-minute model)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (drill)
- **What ICT says:** For FVG trading you can do high-frequency trading with no bias at all: map relative equal highs (or lows) on the 5m/1m chart near price, then use the 15-second FVG to enter a run to short-term buy-side/sell-side liquidity (take out short-term highs/lows). It works for any session (morning, afternoon, lunch). It gives a framework while learning but you will be stopped out more than with anything else he has taught, because you are chasing every small liquidity run. You get caught offside when you ignore time of day, day of week, week of the month, seasonal tendency and the daily/weekly order flow. 20–30 trades a day is possible and "wouldn't be overtrading" with the model, but in impulsive hands it blows accounts.
- **How to use:** Filter by the higher time frame draw: if the daily is drawing to a pool above, only take longs; do the unfiltered version only for baseline drills (non-monetized) to learn how you react.
- **Example in this video:** 15s chart drill with 1m/5m relative equal highs; HTF draw = hourly relative equal highs around 19,926 on the Dec contract (the Aug 27–29 highs: "four or five" smooth highs); also the Sept 13 daily high near 19,862.75 (caption unclear).
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:58](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=1018) the no-bias idea; [0:47:36](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=2856) risks and filters; [1:15:01](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=4501) drill described; [1:19:02](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=4742) filter longs only when monetized.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Explicitly a drill/baseline tool; he does not recommend monetized use without the HTF filter.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: SMT divergence read from candle bodies (NQ vs ES), with the Dow as an early warning  (aliases: SMT)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Compare NQ with ES (Dec contract). In the example, NQ made a higher high in both wick and bodies; ES's wick went higher but its bodies at the high were lower than the prior high: that is an SMT divergence ("wicks do the damage," but bodies hold the bulk of the volume).
  - Look at the bodies of the swing highs/lows, not just the wicks.
  - Prefer NQ vs ES; the Dow is only an early warning, not the deciding factor. ICT does not trade YM: only 30 stocks, spotty, more wicks, moves first. S&P = 500 stocks (smoother), NASDAQ = 100, Dow = 30.
  - Make sure you are comparing the same contract month (he mistakenly reached for the Sept contract).
- **Timestamps:** [0:38:44](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=2324) index composition; [0:39:31](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=2371) the comparison; [0:41:10](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=2470) bodies show the divergence.

The "gray area" of a cluster of overlapping wicks of different lengths is something nobody pays attention to, but the algorithm refers back to it; when looking lower, he looks for discount arrays and a clustering of wicks, not just FVGs, relative equal lows or a single low. He teases "x-ray view" of price and very precise, time-based new material for his book; he made a video on it the night before.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: Breaker block, mean threshold and "inverted" PD arrays  (aliases: low-high-lower-low breaker, MT)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A breaker here is the low-high-lower-low structure whose range he marks; he watches whether price gets above its mean threshold (the midpoint of the block).
  - Naming: for an order block (or breaker) the 50% is the mean threshold; for a gap or wick the 50% is consequent encroachment.
  - As long as price is below half of the breaker's range he has no interest in longs; a run below the breaker's low sets up a short.
  - "Everything I key off of... has an inverted aspect"; PD arrays can be treated the opposite way once violated. It looks like classic support/resistance but it is "very specific candles, very specific prices": the low, the lower quadrant and the halfway of the block.
  - Prefers to see price spike through a block or take liquidity then show inversion/displacement, and bodies staying inside a block are not displacement.
- **Example in this video:** 15s/1m NQ late morning: price rallies to the top of a breaker (Sept 13 daily high area), bodies stay inside it, no inversion, then drops to a lower low.
- **Timestamps:** [1:35:09](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=5709) PD arrays have inverted aspects; [1:49:41](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=6581) mean threshold vs CE naming; [1:52:10](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=6730) bodies inside = no displacement outside.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He holds off explaining why the names were chosen ("the books will explain").

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: Minimum range filter — 20 handles from entry to first target
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** If you can't frame at least about 20 handles from entry to the target, sit still: "we can see the moves coming but it's not framable" for his son's model. Later: finding a setup and getting 20–25 handles is "a nice little bread and butter setup."
- **Timestamps:** [1:32:44](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=5564) "that's the filter"; [2:08:16](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=7696) 20–25 handles.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: "Buy program" / one-sided delivery — where not to trade
body:
- **Kind:** example only / refinement
- **What ICT says:** When price keeps ticking higher with no FVG (only tiny volume imbalances that rebalance immediately), bodies stay inside the prior PD array, and no displacement forms, the market is in a buy program and will keep offering higher prices regardless of how many people are short or what liquidity tools show; it squeezes until it reaches an inefficiency or liquidity (here the 1m short-term high, the top of the breaker/Sept 13 high). Being offside is "extremely painful." He declined the short to illustrate this ("exactly where you do not want to trade").
- **How to use:** If no FVG is offered, do not force an entry. After a one-sided run, wait for an energetic run/displacement and an inefficiency.
- **Example in this video:** From about 1:44 to 1:52, NQ grinds up to the top of the breaker, he shows there is no FVG, then a sharp drop; "I want to see this small portion stay open" before shorting.
- **Timestamps:** [1:43:56](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=6236) screenshot this; [1:45:32](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=6332) buy program; [1:51:21](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=6681) classic; [2:09:04](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=7744) one-sided runs hide inefficiencies.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Contrasts with his trade-with-the-gap lecture: the gap must exist to take the trade.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Manage Missed Entries \ September 17, 2024
head: Why a candidate setup was rejected — shallow, justifiable both ways, too long inside the gap
body:
- **Kind:** example only
- **What ICT says:** He passed on a short because price spent too long inside the gap (a stop-out scenario), the setup was too easy/shallow, and he could justify both a rally and a sweep of equal lows, so it was not high probability; selling at the low end of the day's range after a big drop means selling a discount to people wanting to buy cheap. He also wanted price to take a higher short-term high first and then give an FVG and inversion before shorting. Capital preservation is the main thing; knowing how you can lose and saying "no, this isn't it" comes with experience.
- **Timestamps:** [1:38:31](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=5911), [1:39:21](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=5961), [1:56:00](https://youtu.be/fhBnnU44A6E?t=6960).
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** A balanced price range (single candle up/single candle down sharing the same range) is also mentioned at 1:41 and 1:56 as the area to wait for a trade-through before acting.

head: Swing low validation and minor buy side

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Opening Range Gap (RTH) — huge gap handling, quadrants and midpoint draw  (aliases ICT uses: opening range gap, "mid gap", upper quadrant level, ORG)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The opening range gap is the space between the prior day's settlement/last RTH print (he says "414", i.e. 4:14 PM ET close, caption) and the 9:30 ET opening print. Two data points, two "arrays".
  - If today opens ABOVE yesterday's settlement, the bias/initial draw is LOWER toward the midpoint of that gap (50%, "mid gap" = consequent encroachment of the gap). It does not need to get there that day or that morning; it is only the bias/framework.
  - He claims an approximately 70% tendency ("built-in 70% advantage", "70% strike rate") for price to gravitate to the middle of the opening range gap within the first 30 minutes of the session (he says "first 10... sorry, first 30 minutes").
  - He draws quadrants of the gap: the upper quadrant level (75% of the gap measured from the gap low to the opening high) is the first logical reaching point on a drop, then the mid gap (50%).
  - A very large gap (several hundred handles) changes the plan: it "gives the market a chance to give the public a reason to chase" — price is likely to make a drop first (initial high of day), then run above that initial high to hit buy stops, then drop for the deeper retracement. With a small gap (he says 40–60 handles) the first fair-value-gap short would already have been an entry for him; with this gap he waits.
- **How to identify:** compare the 9:30 open with the prior settlement; draw the gap box; mark 75% / 50% (and 25%); mark the initial high of the day made during the 9:30–10:00 opening range.
- **How to use:** use the gap midpoint as the first draw; do not demand that it trades there. Use the 75% level as the interim/partial level (he describes it as a logical place for a partial, "if you were in a day that didn't have this multiple-100-handle opening gap you could take this as a partial and then aim for the upper quadrant level").
- **Example in this video:** NQ December (micro and mini), 15-second and 1-minute charts, Sept 19, 2024. Open gapped up several hundred handles. Mid gap stated as 19844.5 on the micro and 19843.5 on the mini (about one full handle apart because of the two contracts). Price opened, dropped initially, then ran the initial high (he marks a 19926 level at one point), then retraced.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:26](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=26) midgap shown · [0:05:38](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=338) micro vs mini mid gap levels compared · [0:24:58](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=1498) "the draw is mid gap in the first 30 minutes" · [0:56:36](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3396) opening range (9:30–10:00) behavior after a very large gap higher · [1:08:44](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4124) the two-array logic (settlement vs 9:30 open)
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He explicitly distinguishes the "opening range gap" (prior close to open) from the "opening range" (9:30–10:00). The prior close time is given as "414" in captions (4:14 PM ET) — treat as caption-derived. He does not state the mirror case (open below settlement) but the logic is symmetrical.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Initial high of day trap / buy-stop run after a huge gap up  (aliases ICT uses: "amazing trap for retail", running the initial high, stop run of the initial high)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - After a huge gap higher, expect price to make an initial high, wind down (creating an oversold look to indicators/harmonic traders), then run up and take out that initial high. Breakout buyers who buy above it are "trapped long" and the move above the high is to gather the buy stops/orders so smart money can sell into them and drive price lower toward opposing liquidity (sell-side).
  - Retail likes breakouts and confirmation; buying the highest high gives no reasonable stop and no retracement room.
  - The patient alternative: wait for the initial high to be taken out; a 15-second chart still offers plenty of FVGs and micro-structure turtle soups; you do not have to rush.
  - The old high is "not resistance" — he does not sell at the high; he expects price to go up there, spend time, accumulate orders and then drop. "Targeting" a level is different from treating it as support/resistance.
- **How to identify:** huge opening gap, 9:30–10:00 first push to an initial high, a pullback, then a run through that high; buy stops above.
- **How to use:** do not buy the breakout; wait for the stop run, then use the first FVG / iFVG for shorts targeting the gap midpoint or the sell-side below.
- **Example in this video:** After the first drop, price traded above the initial high (twice made a higher high intraday), the area between the initial high and the new high is shaded as a balanced price range (see below). Buy-side liquidity was cleared and then price reverted toward the first presented FVG/sell-side lows.
- **Timestamps:** [0:10:02](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=602) retail breakout trap explained · [0:13:22](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=802) initial high taken, "we're not rushing" · [0:52:33](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3153) second higher high = stop run · [1:00:43](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3643) high is not resistance, it absorbs buy stops
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says that when it becomes a balanced price range the high "will absolutely be just like" a support/resistance book would say (resistance broken turns support), but only in the sense that the BPR pocket forms after the sweep; the remark is jokey and the exact meaning is caption-unclear.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: First presented Fair Value Gap of the day (1-minute) as focus  (aliases ICT uses: first FVG, "the first one that can't hide", initial fair value gap)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - To answer "which FVG do I use?" he removes the choice: use the very first FVG presented on the 1-minute chart after the 9:30 open. Candle-by-candle check from 9:30 (no gap, no gap, ...); the first one that is a true gap is "first presented FVG".
  - Mechanically: wait for the 9:31 candle to close; at 9:32, if the 9:30–9:31–9:32 three-candle pattern leaves a gap around the 9:31 candle, that is the first FVG of the day. That gives the zone where the first setup should form "at or near".
  - He later adds that other time-based FVGs matter too, but this first one is "the first that can't hide" and is enough to start.
  - Keep the FVG gray at first (so no bias is baked in), extend it to the right.
  - Bias off this FVG: the initial focus is middle of the gap (the opening range gap midpoint) — "I'm making it binary".
- **How to identify:** 1m chart from 9:30; three-candle pattern where candle 1's high and candle 3's low (for bullish) do not overlap; the first one after the open.
- **How to use:** use it as the frame for the setup; either a retrace into its lower half / CE (the "model 2022" style entry) or, once price trades back through and below it, as an inversion FVG for shorts.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m Sept 19, 2024: first FVG formed after the 9:30 open; price traded to its CE, rose to fill a smaller FVG above, then dropped below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:12:26](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=746) candle-by-candle search for the first gap · [1:07:08](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4028) why first FVG · [1:09:31](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4171) 9:31 candle / 9:32 first FVG rule
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Simplifies which FVG to pick. A candle that overlaps (e.g. a later candle's high touching the earlier candle's low) means NO FVG there; he says he cannot use that one.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Model 2022 two-FVG logic (stacked FVGs)  (aliases ICT uses: "model 2022", "initial fair value gap model 2022")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (brief application)
- **What ICT says:** if there is an FVG and another smaller FVG just above it, always expect price to go up into the second, higher one. He calls the first entry into the lower FVG followed by the stab into the higher FVG "the model 2022 entry". He tried to time the low of the first FVG and notes that the actual entry was even better because it was outside (below) the FVG, i.e. forgiving.
- **How to identify:** two FVGs stacked, a larger lower one and a smaller one above.
- **How to use:** buy the retrace into the lower FVG, target the upper FVG.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s/1m: price dipped to the lower of the two FVGs (mid / lower half), then "stabbed" into the upper FVG.
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:59](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=1259) two FVGs, "this is model 2022 stuff" · [0:35:19](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=2119) he recaps that he pre-called the trap and the 2022 entry
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** only referred to, not re-taught; the reader should cross-reference the 2022 mentorship notes.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Inversion FVG (iFVG) short after a trap  (aliases ICT uses: "treat it as an inversion fair value gap", work the lower half / CE)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - After price drops below the first FVG (the bullish one) it can be treated as an inversion FVG; shorts can be taken from the lower half / consequent encroachment of the iFVG, aiming at sell-side below.
  - Condition for the 15s entry: price must leave the iFVG and stop reaching for premium. Allow ONE candle to touch back into it. After that, the next displacement lower that creates an FVG is the one he would sell on, targeting the range/liquidity (here the minor sell-side low).
  - If the candle that touches back means no clean gap exists (candle 3's high overlaps candle 1's low), that FVG is unusable — "I can't use that one now"; wait for another displacement lower that does leave a gap. Without a clean one, no trade — "can I take a losing trade here? No".
  - Look for bodies staying below the CE of the iFVG; he watches that the bodies do not lay on top of the mid gap.
- **How to identify:** a bullish FVG that price has closed below; retrace into its lower half/CE; rejection.
- **How to use:** entry on a fresh FVG made by the displacement after the touch; target a minor sell-side liquidity at least 20 handles away; risk on a micro can be wider.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s: after the second run higher, price falls below the first FVG; one candle touches back; the next displacement lower leaves no gap because of an overlap so he stands aside; later another one forms.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:30](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=930) either CE of the first FVG then up, or work lower half as iFVG · [0:37:44](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=2264) reaction off iFVG CE · [0:38:32](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=2312) conditions for the short · [0:43:32](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=2612) cannot take it without a fresh FVG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The "touch once with one candle" language is a refinement of the iFVG entry; it is stated for 15s execution.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: 20-handle minimum run filter  (aliases ICT uses: "20 handle run potential", "frame a little box with 20 handles")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - For this NQ lesson, a setup is only valid if it offers at least 20 handles (points) to a logical target. First require a directional bias, then find a PD array (FVG, order block, any PD array) from which price can run at least 20 handles.
  - If the available range is 18 handles, he does not take it and the student should feel good about the discipline — "white glove approach".
  - Daily practice: after the session, frame a 20-handle box on the chart and look back to see where entries from an FVG would have yielded 20 handles and whether a logical target (e.g., filling a gap) was within reach.
- **How to identify:** measure entry-to-target; target examples: the low of the minor sell-side pool, upper quadrant of the opening range gap, the next FVG.
- **How to use:** a filter, not a target in itself; with a micro NQ, 20 handles is about $40 per contract at $2/point (arithmetic, not stated) — he instead frames the goal as $75–$100.
- **Example in this video:** the minor sell-side low was just about 20 handles from the proposed entry; the caption gives "20,10 even" as the 20-handle target level (caption unclear).
- **Timestamps:** [0:28:58](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=1738) 20 handle run introduced · [0:39:21](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=2361) if it doesn't afford 20 handles, pass · [0:46:50](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=2810) frame a 20-handle box after the fact
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This 20-handle threshold is specific to this beginner exercise on NQ ("if you watched what I was teaching on the other day").

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Fibonacci external projections (negative extensions) for the run beyond a dealing range  (aliases ICT uses: negative 0.25, negative 0.5, one standard deviation / measured move)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Anchor the Fibonacci on the swing high (highest candle) to the low of the dealing range. For external liquidity beyond the range, the first stepping stone is -0.25. If it makes a measured run, the target is -1 (one "standard deviation" = the range projected below the low). Half of that is -0.5.
  - "How far can we reasonably expect it to go below this low?" — use these levels.
  - He notes -1 here lines up with the upper quadrant of the opening range gap; confluence between Fibonacci and another PD array is what matters.
- **How to identify:** a clear high-to-low leg; project the same distance beyond the low.
- **How to use:** targets/partials beyond a low; with a huge gap, continuation beyond is possible.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s: fib from the highest high down to the low; price traded to -0.25 and bodies stayed around -0.5 area; measured move projected to near the upper quadrant level.
- **Timestamps:** [0:54:08](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3248) dealing range fib anchored high to low · [0:54:55](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3295) -0.25, -0.5, -1 · [0:55:46](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3346) half the run = $75–$100 open profit
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Matches his earlier "-0.25 / -0.5 / -1 (std dev)" projection teaching; here the level is linked to the opening gap quadrant.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Balanced Price Range from a run into real orders
body:
- **Kind:** example only / refinement
- **What ICT says:** the shaded area between the initial high and the stop-run high is treated as a balanced price range because price ran into real buy orders (breakout buyers) that smart money sold to. It is "not contrived", not a random area — it is where the orders were. Below it: sell-side pools and the first presented FVG.
- **How to identify:** overlapping up and down moves around a stop run (caption description loose).
- **How to use:** price should gravitate toward opposing liquidity (sell-side) because breakout buyers are trapped.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s: price swept the initial high, sold off from there; he highlights the pocket and extends it right.
- **Timestamps:** [0:53:21](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3201) BPR defined from the run · [1:02:17](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=3737) pocket becomes BPR
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** definition here is looser than the strict "overlapping bearish and bullish FVG" version — treat as his usage in this video.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Micro vs. Mini contracts (NQ) — execution forgiveness and size  (aliases ICT uses: MNQ, micro Nasdaq, one-contract experiment)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / execution
- **What ICT says:**
  - Traders without the capital for a mini can trade the micro and "do very well". He opens charts of both December contracts (micro and mini) side by side, 15-second and 1-minute.
  - The micro is "very, very forgiving": you can use wider stops and need less precision; with the mini you must be more precise.
  - Beginner objective: yield $75–$100 on ONE micro contract per day and stop. When it becomes a mini, the same setup pays about a weekly salary (his words).
  - In the beginning enter at market, not limit orders, to feel the entry (regret or accomplishment).
  - Contract roll: rolled from September to December on Tuesday; he failed to say what the catalyst for the roll was.
  - CFDs: US100/US500/US30 will be covered on another day; he notes Americans are not legally allowed to trade CFDs.
- **How to identify / use:** mid-gap on micro 19844.5 vs mini 19843.5, almost identical.
- **Example in this video:** long-side stab into the second FVG on the micro yielded $75–$100 within the first move down from the high (after a poor entry).
- **Timestamps:** [0:01:25](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=85) micro vs mini intro · [0:19:15](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=1155) micro is forgiving · [0:22:36](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=1356) $75–$100 goal · [0:33:43](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=2023) market in, no limit orders at first
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is an educational ladder for beginners, not his own sizing.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Binary if/then/else decision tree (algorithmic framework)  (aliases ICT uses: "arrays", "data points", "if then else")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / process
- **What ICT says:**
  - Build trading as programming: define where the data comes from (arrays) → where the first setup will form each day (the first 30 minutes after 9:30) → what the first data point is (settlement vs 9:30 open) → conditions that trigger an action.
  - If the open is above settlement: bias lower to the gap midpoint; wait for 9:31 to close; if at 9:32 an FVG exists, that's the focus; then wait for a setup that meets the 20-handle filter. If neither scenario is present, sit still.
  - "I'm making it binary."
- **How to identify / use:** a checklist before the open each morning.
- **Example in this video:** the whole session.
- **Timestamps:** [1:07:57](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4077) if/then/else · [1:08:44](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4124) two arrays · [1:09:31](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4171) 9:31 / 9:32 first FVG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he frames this explicitly as how to remove discretion for a beginner.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Micro Vs. Mini \ September 19, 2024
head: Macros / "time and price theory", Fibonacci OTE and PD-array confluence  (aliases ICT uses: macros, 20-minute intervals, "loaded deal", 62–79% retracement)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - His "time and price theory" is macros: 20-minute windows every hour — the last 10 minutes before the top of the hour and the first 10 minutes after it (i.e. xx:50–xx:10). Time when the market should start running for liquidity or inefficiency; he sets an expectation to look for a setup every hour.
  - A retracement into 62–79% of a leg is only a 3/4-probability thing by itself; combine it with a PD array agreeing and being inside a macro window and it becomes "a loaded deal" — it may not run 100 handles but will run back to the top of the framed range.
  - The same applies to indicators: bullish divergence on stochastics/RSI/MACD works only when it coincides with an order block or FVG inside a macro.
  - An order block is two specific price levels, not a zone: the first is the initial entry for smart money, the second is where they can add if offered.
  - Fibonacci only gives measurements of a range and of the area beyond; it matters when it agrees with another PD array.
- **How to identify / use:** check the clock (xx:50–xx:10), the OTE retracement (62–79%) and a PD array overlapping it.
- **Example in this video:** none (spoken principle).
- **Timestamps:** [1:13:32](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4412) macros = time and price theory · [1:16:48](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4608) order block = two price levels · [1:20:00](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4800) 62–79% + PD array + macro · [1:20:47](https://youtu.be/XiZHGOeVAOk?t=4847) indicator divergence in a macro
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Stated in the context of ridiculing Gann, Elliott, harmonics, trend lines and "zones". He says he does not trade classic supply/demand or support/resistance, but that his framework can pick the "right" ones.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Opening range gap — "discount" gap, size thresholds, and CFD bridging  (aliases ICT uses: opening range gap, ORG, settlement price (4:14 PM ET) to 9:30 open)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Futures: the gap is between the prior day's settlement price at 4:14 PM ET (he also says "4:15 or 4:14") and today's 9:30 AM ET opening price. Futures still trade 4:15–5:00 (he says another 45–46 min, "closes at 5:00") and overnight, but the RTH-chart view (regular trading hours) shows the clean gap.
  - If yesterday's 4:14 settlement is higher than today's 9:30 open, it is a DISCOUNT opening range gap (today opens below the prior close). The settlement line is the high of the ORG and the 9:30 open is the low.
  - A small ORG is about 20 handles and is "limp/anemic"; he does not like less than 40 handles. With under 40 handles he uses other tools for the morning or opts out until 10:00 and then trades a Silver Bullet (short mention).
  - You can anticipate the gap near 9:29 (electronic hours): see whether the open will be above or below settlement and guess whether it will be wide.
  - The opening range is the first 30 minutes (9:30–10:00 ET), an algorithmic interval ("anything less than this they're making up stuff"). He says he will teach more uses in the 2024 mentorship and the book, and won't reveal everything before then.
  - For CFD traders: CFDs trade around the clock with no settlement break and no 4:15–6:00 gap, so there is no gap function; bridge it by marking the 4:14 PM ET candle's close (that is the "settlement") and the 9:30 open on the CFD chart. The same two price points give the same information.
- **How to identify:** RTH chart; find the 4:14 PM ET close, the 9:30 open; draw two bold horizontal lines extended; label premium or discount.
- **How to use:** gap size determines morning approach (small gap = harder morning, pay attention to time and yesterday's levels); the previous day's gap and whether it was traded to its midpoint matter.
- **Example in this video:** NQ December micro, Thu Sep 19 settlement (caption reads "2,55", i.e. about 20,055) vs Fri Sep 20 open ("20,035 even", caption) = 20 handle discount gap. Yesterday's gap "barely made its way toward the upper quadrant" and never traded to its midpoint/CE, leaving a vacuum of price below.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:09](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=429) prior 4:14 settlement candle shown · [0:08:00](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=480) discount opening range gap · [0:09:38](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=578) opening range 9:30–10:00 · [0:20:11](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1211) under 40 handles → other tools or wait for 10:00 Silver Bullet · [1:04:26](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3866) CFD chart: mark 4:14 and 9:30
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** In M24-031 he put the small-gap level at 40–60 handles (a first-FVG entry would be fine); here he sets about 40 as the floor below which he changes approach. Prices are caption-derived, so verify.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: First presented FVG (9:30–10:00) from the PRIOR day, extended to the right  (aliases ICT uses: "yesterday's first presented fair value gap", orange box, extend right, life cycle about 3 days)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / new coinage-like refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - The first FVG that forms between 9:30 and 10:00 on the 1-minute chart must involve at least the 9:31 candle; the 9:30 candle cannot be used for the first FVG presentation. Today's formed at 9:34; Thursday's formed around the 9:38 candle (he points at a candle at 9:38).
  - Extend each day's first presented FVG forward (chart settings: "extend right"); its useful life cycle is about 3 days, sometimes weeks if not yet traded back into. The algorithm refers back to it, unless it is a trending day.
  - Journal them: for each of the last three days, did that day's first FVG influence price today?
  - Today's own first FVG may not matter yet: the market opened inside Thursday's FVG and so uses that larger gap first; today's small gap may be useful "next week instead".
  - Its levels are very specific prices (high, upper quadrant, middle/CE, lower quadrant, low), "not a zone". When bearish, he wants price not to go back into the upper half of the gap.
- **How to identify:** 1m chart after 9:30; first FVG that includes the 9:31 candle or later and is complete before 10:00.
- **How to use:** as a reference range for later days (opens inside it = it matters); short from its high or CE when bearish; used as an iFVG if price trades back up into it after going below.
- **Example in this video:** Thursday Sept 19's first FVG shown as an orange box extended into Friday; Friday opened inside it. Overnight London/Asia trades also worked around that box.
- **Timestamps:** [0:11:12](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=672) first FVG forms at 9:34, can't use the 9:30 candle · [0:17:48](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1068) extend yesterday's first FVG, life cycle ~3 days · [0:21:46](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1306) how to set "extend right" · [0:23:21](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1401) why you must extend it · [1:02:47](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3767) later in the day price returns to the first FVG
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** builds on M24-031's "first presented FVG" rule by adding the multi-day extension and the "open inside prior day's FVG" condition.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Time distortion and the 9:50–10:10 macro  (aliases ICT uses: time distortion, macro, "spool", algorithmic window)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Back-and-forth consolidation before a macro is NOT lack of buyers or sellers and not a balance between them; it is "time distortion" — price waiting for a specific time. Here 9:50–10:10 AM is the algorithmic window when the market "spools" (starts to run).
  - A macro is a short list of directives (a script) that the delivery algorithm runs: it looks back through the previous session (overnight, yesterday afternoon, London, Asia), finds liquidity pools not yet traded to, and then delivers price there. It does not know how many contracts rest there, only that the low/high has not been traded.
  - Macro times repeat: the last 10 minutes before the top of each hour for 20 minutes total (here 9:50 for 20 minutes).
  - He says he does not require macro times when volatility is high; but when factors stack against you (small gap, Friday, end of week), stick to time.
  - "First the time, then what price around that time."
- **How to identify:** clock 9:50–10:10 ET (and other hourly :50–:10 windows); preceding choppy consolidation.
- **How to use:** expect the move toward untraded opposing liquidity once the window opens; wait for it rather than breaking out early.
- **Example in this video:** Friday Sept 20: at 9:50 price began to move lower toward the relative equal lows on the micro NQ.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:41](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=821) time distortion waiting for 9:50 · [0:33:02](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1982) it's scripted; repeats 10 minutes before each hour, 20-minute duration · [0:37:52](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=2272) what a macro is · [0:45:07](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=2707) macro = short program script heading to the pools
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** this is a more mechanical description of macros (looking back through the prior session) than in earlier lectures.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Day-context stack: Friday (TGIF), small gap, big prior range, open inside yesterday's gap  (aliases ICT uses: TGIF, "things stacking against you", weekly range retracement)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / bias
- **What ICT says:**
  - TGIF: on Fridays, look for a pullback of about 20–30% of the weekly range (the highest high to lowest low of the week) — "not that it needs to do that", but he looks for it. He says he will explain how to measure it in Caleb's channel video.
  - Factors that made the morning hard for a newer trader: small 20-handle gap, a large-range day yesterday, Friday end of week, opening inside yesterday's first FVG, and yesterday's gap largely untraded (vacuum below). All combine to favor a lower move after the 9:50 macro and make a clean morning setup harder.
  - His morning tweet said "focus on two sell-side liquidity pools" (the relative equal lows below), so direction was known beforehand.
  - Beginner rules vs advanced: "don't trade Mondays" and "don't trade high-impact news" are guidance for new students; those who know what they are doing can trade news after the report prints and then look for the inefficiencies or liquidity left behind.
- **How to identify / use:** build a checklist of day-of-week, gap size, prior range, where the open sits relative to prior FVGs; combine into a narrative before 9:30.
- **Example in this video:** all of the above for Sep 20, 2024.
- **Timestamps:** [0:16:12](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=972) TGIF 20–30% of weekly range · [0:28:09](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1689) why the morning is hard for a new trader · [0:28:56](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1736) Monday / news advice is for new students · [0:31:26](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1886) vacuum below yesterday's gap + TGIF
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** a mild restatement of earlier day-of-week tendencies; the 20–30% figure is stated hedged.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Buy-side raid at the open → trap, then drop to the opening range gap low  (aliases ICT uses: knock out shorts, trap buyers above old high, rake them across the coals)
body:
- **Kind:** example / pattern
- **What ICT says:** at 9:30 the market rallied and took out short-term buy-side liquidity, stopping out anyone short and trapping buyers who bought the break above the old high; price then traded back toward sell-side (sell stops below). The pattern played out as: open → swing up to the high of the ORG (yesterday's 4:14 settlement) → trades through it for more liquidity → back down through the opening price (low of the ORG) → one more pass for buy-side → drops again toward the ORG low.
- **How to identify:** pre-session high wicked at the open, followed by failure to continue.
- **How to use:** do not buy breakouts; look to short from an uptick into a PD array after the raid.
- **Example in this video:** micro NQ 1m, 9:30–9:50 ET Sept 20.
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:23](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=923) the raid and trap · [0:26:35](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=1595) open → high → open low → buy side again
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** same theme as the 031 breakout-buyer trap.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Short entry from the high of yesterday's first FVG (sell on an uptick) with breakaway gap  (aliases ICT uses: breakaway gap, sell into strength, uptick)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (applied) / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - He wants price to trade down through today's own first FVG at the macro; he removed the volume imbalance (body-to-body gap) from today's FVG so it only shows candle low to candle high (wick-to-wick), because the volume imbalance is the "least impactful". Reading the volume imbalance as a breakaway gap: price leaving with a gap because the market is being re-priced lower at that time.
  - Once price is below, he waits for it to come back UP into yesterday's first presented FVG (orange box) and sells short on that rise: entry at the high of that gap (it looks random but is the high of the reference FVG), with time (macro) and the breakaway gap on his side. If it hits the CE of yesterday's FVG and leaves, that is the same story.
  - Rationale he gives: large funds and HFT cannot short on a down-tick; they must wait for an uptick (some have filters needing a percentage/time threshold) — so "selling short on an uptick" is smart money behavior (his claim; not verified).
  - Target: just below the relative equal lows (sell-side) he flagged on Twitter; he exits at a tick below them.
  - Entry was a market order only because he is using market replay/paper; with limit orders you can get very tight entries and meaningful stops, which he will teach in this mentorship.
- **How to identify:** bearish bias; yesterday's first FVG overhead; price makes a lower low then retraces up into the box.
- **How to use:** short at the box high or CE; stop above the box high (not stated numerically); target the equal lows.
- **Example in this video:** micro NQ 1m, Fri Sep 20: price drops through today's 9:34 FVG at 9:50, rallies into Thursday's first FVG (touching its CE), then he shorts at the top of that FVG and covers just under the relative equal lows. (Prices not clearly stated in captions.)
- **Timestamps:** [0:47:33](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=2853) levels of yesterday's FVG are specific prices · [0:50:01](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3001) sell on uptick, not downtick · [0:51:37](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3097) CE tag then entry at top of the gap · [0:55:37](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3337) exit under the relative equal lows
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** "breakaway gap" is a loose term; caption is partly garbled.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Consequent encroachment of a wick ("discount wick") as entry and target  (aliases ICT uses: CE of a wick, discount wick)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / new technique
- **What ICT says:**
  - Measure a candle's body to its low (the lower wick) — the midpoint of that wick is its consequent encroachment. If bearish, you can enter short at that price; the same kind of level can be used as the target. Anchor the measurement to something that makes sense (body end to wick extreme); a random line floating in space is meaningless.
  - He calls it "a discount wick" (the wick in the discount of the candle).
- **How to identify:** the long lowest wick candle in the consolidation before the drop.
- **How to use:** short at the wick's CE when bearish; take profit at another discount wick's CE.
- **Example in this video:** micro NQ 1m: CE of the long low wick = 19974.25 (caption "19974 point2"); entry short there; target the CE of a lower wick at 19930.50 or lower; exit filled at 19933.75 ("slipped a little"); then price rallied back up into yesterday's first FVG and cleared the high of the day later.
- **Timestamps:** [1:00:22](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3622) measuring body to low · [1:01:10](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3670) CE price 19974.25 · [1:01:59](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3719) target CE 19930.50, exit 19933.75
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he says the same wick-CE entry appeared in the CFD chart too (midpoint of the wick, get short, it drops). New refinement; verify the exact definition of "discount wick" in other videos.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Volume imbalance inside the FVG — include it on CFDs  (aliases ICT uses: volume imbalance, "separation between the bodies")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - A volume imbalance is the small separation between one candle's body (close) and the next candle's open — body to body — not wick to wick.
  - On futures he sometimes strips it out to focus on wicks (as above). On CFDs always include volume imbalances in the FVG, because broker pricing varies and without them you won't have a true depiction of the zone the algorithm refers to.
  - He says this idea of the volume imbalance is not in other books.
- **How to identify:** open of candle N+1 differs from close of candle N.
- **How to use:** CFD charts: draw FVG including the volume imbalance.
- **Example in this video:** US100 CFD 1m: first gap at 9:30–10:00 with volume imbalances at two places; mark 9:50 macro, 9:51 begin lower, target sell-side/relative equal lows; same wick-CE short.
- **Timestamps:** [1:06:05](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=3965) always include volume imbalance for CFDs · [1:06:52](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=4012) definition (body to body) and 9:50 macro marked · [1:07:40](https://youtu.be/Vo8WKYKtzIU?t=4060) "all you have to do is use the times"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** broker feeds differ, so the CFD "FVG" is not identical to futures.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ CFDs Vs. Futures \ September 20, 2024
head: Algorithmic price delivery vs order flow / DOM / level 2  (aliases ICT uses: scripted market, price engine, repricing, dealer vs market maker)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / mindset (concept framing)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price is delivered by an algorithm (a price engine) that offers prices according to a script; buying and selling pressure does not determine direction. Chop/consolidation is the algorithm cycling through its directives, not indecision.
  - Time and sales, volume profile, depth of market (level 2), the "book map" are used after the fact to justify moves; the ladders can be spoofed ("not all real orders"), a mirage. A large pool of orders on one side does not mean price goes there.
  - Support/resistance, old highs and indicators do not matter if the algorithm is repricing lower; it simply keeps offering lower prices until it reaches the liquidity pool (resting sell stops).
  - Opposing liquidity: if buy-side was taken, find the nearest obvious sell-side pool that has not been traded to.
  - The market is not free; because it is scripted it repeats at the same times each day.
  - Dealer vs market maker: a dealer trades the same price feed as everyone else; it doesn't make price. He says price is "way above you".
  - He uses the GameStop/AMC/Bitcoin runs as examples of price being delivered in big premium skips when it is time to trap participants (and mentions NFP/CPI/PPI as similar news drivers).
- **How to use:** don't use order-flow tools for direction; use time + liquidity + PD arrays. He adds that he wished he had such tools only in the beginning because he did not know liquidity.
- **Example in this video:** the Sept 20 drop through "supports" and old highs to the relative equal lows.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Avoid Seek & Destroy \ Tape Reading \ September 23, 2024
head: Time distortion — recognising a held / strangled market  (aliases ICT uses: time distortion, "held", "strangled", muddy, dirty, holding pattern)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Price spending too much time inside inefficiencies (any gap, FVG, wick, the unfilled part of an opening range gap) is the signature that the market is being held — it is not permitted to run yet.
  - He wants to see price spend time ABOVE old highs (accumulating new longs) or BELOW old lows (accumulating new shorts), but not inside inefficiencies.
  - Buying and selling pressure exists but price barely moves; it is kept "artificially" in a tight range; when the range is released the move is cleaner and more sustainable, so the afternoon session should be good.
  - Trading ahead of the release gets you beat up ("chopped up"); "the better you recognise when the market is being held, the better your trading".
  - Signs listed: too many wicks that are not adjacent, so he cannot draw a clean gray (precision) level; a PD array that is only touched with no displacement; the market that "looks like a technical day" turning into a holding pattern; a medium-impact news driver at 9:45 (Flash Manufacturing PMI) causing a flurry but no meaningful run to highs or lows followed by a rejection.
  - With muddy morning probabilities he elects to wait until 10:00 (Silver Bullet starts) and use the first presented FVG then.
- **How to identify:** price repeatedly re-entering the same gap; overlapping candles; small ranges; many equal-ish wicks; he says it can look like consolidation inside a range between two obvious highs/lows.
- **How to use:** do not press; stand aside; use 10:00 Silver Bullet; revisit in the afternoon. He tells viewers to screenshot the chart and label it "time distortion and very difficult morning session conditions".
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m/15s Monday Sept 23 9:30–10:35 ET: price chops inside last week's gaps and the unfilled lower part of a premium opening range gap; it clears the early highs, then consolidates under and around them; at 10:31 it is still ranging between the same high and low.
- **Timestamps:** [0:14:58](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=898) muddy = time distortion, wait till 10:00 · [0:40:04](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=2404) "the time distortion is real" · [0:41:14](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=2474) why he isn't pressing the button · [0:42:00](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=2520) above old highs / below old lows vs inside inefficiencies · [1:02:37](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=3757) held artificially, release gives a nice afternoon
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** follows the M24-032 definition (time distortion = waiting for a macro/time) and extends it to a practical "do not trade this" filter. He admits he cannot teach exactly when not to trade from a static chart: "you have to see it."

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Avoid Seek & Destroy \ Tape Reading \ September 23, 2024
head: Displacement as the confirmation signature at a PD array  (aliases ICT uses: "tips its hand", signature, "demanding" displacement)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** having a line or rectangle at a PD array is not enough; there has to be displacement off the level — a signature that "tips its hand". Typical order: a run on stops (liquidity) before price trades to the PD array, then trade at the PD, then drop hard or rally away. Then wait for the fair value gap or order block formed by that move to trade back. Demanding this keeps you out of choppy trades.
- **How to identify:** body closes away from the array with a gap; not just a wick or a touch.
- **How to use:** no entry until the displacement; he says that is why he is not in a trade while price touches arrays.
- **Example in this video:** the tiny first FVG of the day (about a quarter point, overlapping an old new-day opening gap) is not a trade unless price shows displacement off it, trading above it and treating it as a discount array.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:46](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=466) displacement off a level is the signature · [0:10:14](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=614) small first FVG overlapping an old NDOG needs displacement · [0:32:29](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=1949) demanding displacement after trade to the array saves you from chop
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** consistent with his earlier PD-array teaching; here framed as a no-trade filter.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Avoid Seek & Destroy \ Tape Reading \ September 23, 2024
head: Gap time-in-inefficiency rule: hit the CE once, then leave  (aliases ICT uses: consequent encroachment should not be violated, "second time to CE", repeating phenomenon)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement (possible mini-model)
- **What ICT says:**
  - After price reaches the consequent encroachment of a gap (here the first presented FVG of the day), it should leave it; a second trip back to the CE is a failure sign: "it should have hit it once and then left" and "you never want to see that."
  - For a bullish read: price can trade down into the upper half, touch the CE and even wick through it, but it is better if the lower portion stays open.
  - For the short he had framed (gray box): if price gets the CE and leaves, the upper half of that gap should not be traded to again, and the CE should not be retraded, until the low (sell-side) is taken. If it does come back, the trade is unreliable. He tells viewers to record this in the journal — "a repeating phenomenon that could be a model in and of itself".
  - Never want price staying inside any gap, inefficiency or wick.
  - An inverted gap (a line/rectangle over an FVG that price has closed through) should act as support when price is above it; price should get back above it and keep the CE intact.
- **How to identify:** count touches of the CE after the first reaction; track whether the target low got traded to before the second touch.
- **How to use:** a second CE visit before the target = skip or exit; it saved him from a short that failed.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m Sept 23: the gray short box in the first FVG traded down but failed when price made a second tag of the CE; he had said it would likely fail because it was spending too much time.
- **Timestamps:** [0:48:34](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=2914) second attempt at CE is unwelcome · [0:51:00](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=3060) CE should not be violated; lower portion open · [0:59:29](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=3569) upper half / CE shouldn't be traded to until the low is taken, journal this
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he does not formalize it as a named model; it is presented as an observation worth journaling.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Avoid Seek & Destroy \ Tape Reading \ September 23, 2024
head: Low-resistance liquidity run via volume imbalance after a premium retracement  (aliases ICT uses: "low resistance liquidity run", volume imbalance between bodies, purple premium box)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (framework described, not triggered)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Preferred sequence (before the low gets taken): price breaks below a level and leaves a small gap between candle bodies (volume imbalance); the next candle closes/opens, price trades back up into the volume imbalance and the bottom of the purple shaded premium array, then reprices lower into the low. That is "a very, very low resistance liquidity run setup".
  - He prefers it when the liquidity (the low) has not yet been taken, because it is then "coming back up into a premium"; it still delivered after the low was taken, but is less preferred.
  - Description: high-frequency trading setups you can study, tape read and demo-trade.
- **How to identify:** break of a low with a body-to-body gap, then a retrace into the gap/premium array.
- **How to use:** short from the premium array (volume imbalance + bottom of the purple box) targeting the untaken low.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m/15s Sept 23 morning: levels from last Thursday's data (a gray box = Thursday's first presented FVG, purple box = a premium array/gap from Thursday); price took the short-term low first, which removed the preferred setup.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:58](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=358) the framework described · [0:07:46](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=466) high-frequency setups to study · [0:08:35](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=515) premium gap already returned to midpoint
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** the term "high/low resistance liquidity run" appears in his canonical list; here he only mentions the low-resistance variant while explaining he did not get his setup.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How To Avoid Seek & Destroy \ Tape Reading \ September 23, 2024
head: Opening range gap — unfilled portion as the draw (premium gap)  (aliases ICT uses: unfilled portion of the opening range gap, mid gap, new day opening gap)
body:
- **Kind:** example / application
- **What ICT says:** Monday had a large premium opening range gap; price had already traded down past its midpoint (CE) — filled half and a little more — made the low of the day so far, then broke up. The part below (between a candle's low and a candle's close, shown in blue) remains unfilled and is "primed for a potential exploration down". He plans a daily buy-side target higher (the August 22, 2024 old daily high — caption reads "2251 and a quarter", likely 20,251.25, caption unclear). He says that later he would teach more on "new day opening gaps"; the first FVG of the morning overlapped an old new day opening gap (NDOG).

head: First presented FVG and Silver Bullet (10:00) on difficult mornings  (aliases ICT uses: first presented fair value gap, Silver Bullet, "wait till 10:00")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** on a muddy morning, "sit on my hands" until 10:00 and use the first presented FVG for the Silver Bullet — probabilities shift in your favor if you wait. The first FVG on the 1m chart formed at 9:32 (caption says "9 Minute chart" but he means the 1-minute chart). On apprehensive days he highlights it in gray rather than coloring a direction, and tracks whether the trade would pan out while deciding how comfortable he would be in it. He names the Silver Bullet entry as "a run on the buy side" off a candle that holds its low while the next candle trades below it (a possible Silver Bullet for a buy-side run).
- **How to identify / use:** gray FVG, wait for 10:00, require displacement (see above).
- **Example in this video:** at 9:32 first 1m FVG; he marks a gray box; at 0:33:37 he wants one 1m candle to hold its low and the next to trade below it as a Silver Bullet for a run on the buy side (not executed).

head: Buy side → sell side → FVG/iFVG rally sequence ("Caleb's strongest model") with wick CE entry  (aliases ICT uses: running short-term high then low then rally, inversion fair value gap, CE of the wick, extension)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (recap of an earlier trade/vignette)
- **What ICT says:**
  - The strongest version of the beginner's model: a short-term high is taken (buy side first), price then trades down and takes out a short-term low (sell side), then rallies using a fair value gap — which can be an inversion FVG.
  - His earlier entry used the consequent encroachment of a wick; entry slightly above that CE and the inversion FVG. He targeted the short-term buy side with a 0.25 extension of the old high (caption unclear: "load High 0.25 extension") and finessed the exit by factoring in the spread because price does not always reach the target.
  - Missed the best entry below the CE with a market order; a limit would have caught it but "it's not likely to always do that for you".
  - Chicken leg analogy: the meat is not at the tips of each bone; you do not need the highest high or the lowest low, just the bulk of the move in your directional bias.
- **How to identify / use:** sequence BSL taken → SSL taken → bullish displacement leaving an FVG/iFVG → long; target the next short-term high, optionally a −0.25 extension; account for spread.
- **Example in this video:** an earlier trade shown on his Twitter vignette (instrument NQ/micro; date not stated in this video; likely the Friday Sept 20 / prior session).
- **Timestamps:** [0:15:48](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=948) Caleb's strongest model sequence · [0:16:37](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=997) CE of wick entry, iFVG, 0.25 extension target · [0:17:27](https://youtu.be/Qg3O1GkJDeQ?t=1047) chicken leg analogy
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** the 0.25 extension here is the same −0.25 first stepping stone he taught in M24-031.

body:
