title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Premarket Concepts \ September 30, 2024
head: Turtle Soup (origin of his stop-hunt thinking)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / history
- **What ICT says:** Linda Raschke and Larry Connors' Turtle Soup (from "Street Smarts") fades the 20-day breakout used by Richard Dennis's turtles — buy the break below the 20-day low, sell the break above the 20-day high, a false-breakout pattern capitalizing on the turtles' low strike rate. He took from it the idea of looking at stop hunts and being on the other side of stopped-out traders, applied to intraday charts; he does not count 20 days, he counts candles/structure. He credits Larry Williams for other ideas (e.g. the currency-futures comparison that preceded SMT).
- **Timestamps:** [0:32:35](https://youtu.be/l7eu9yvUUtg?t=1955) — Turtle Soup explained; [0:34:11](https://youtu.be/l7eu9yvUUtg?t=2051) — how it became his intraday stop-hunt foundation; [0:30:13](https://youtu.be/l7eu9yvUUtg?t=1813) — 90s currency comparison
- **Nuance / caveats:** The 20-day-high/low rule is the book's, not his.

head: Time-based charts and tape reading (vs volume profile / Level 2)  (aliases: algorithm operates on time first)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** Use time-based candlesticks only; Renko/range bars hide what the algorithm does because it operates on time first. Volume profile, Level 2 and Bookmap are looking at what already happened; he is looking 15–20 minutes ahead. Watch the tape and the price axis; he watches price numbers more than candles because they correlate with his notepad levels.

body:
- **Kind:** process

Do it daily and read it on weekends. He plans two journal-style annotation days this week.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Premarket Concepts \ September 30, 2024
head: Floor pivots and the "no panacea" principle  (aliases: pivot numbers, draw on liquidity vs terminus)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:** Early on he used floor pivot numbers as support/resistance; he later saw price run to the liquidity beyond them. A pivot is only a suggestion of where price might reach, like a draw on liquidity, never a terminus; liquidity below old lows/relative equal lows can be the low of the day, above old highs the high of the day. Nothing in trading is a panacea; the game is time, price, liquidity, inefficiencies.
- **Timestamps:** [1:46:52](https://youtu.be/l7eu9yvUUtg?t=6412) — pivots and liquidity; [1:47:40](https://youtu.be/l7eu9yvUUtg?t=6460) — nothing is a panacea
- **Nuance / caveats:** None.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Limit Orders & Volatility Pinball Drills \ October 01, 2024
head: Volatility Pinball drill  (aliases ICT uses: "price action drill", "limit order drill", "pinball")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage (practice method, not an entry model)
- **What ICT says:**
  - A demo-account exercise to learn limit-order entries and to desensitise yourself to entering (and to selling short). He says he built it as a game in the 1990s, writing down hypothetical entry, stop and target on paper, using the candle's open as the hypothetical fill (e.g. for a bearish order block).
  - Chart: 15-second chart (more opportunity), 1-minute as the highest timeframe. Occasionally a 5-minute chart if it works there. No higher-timeframe bias or draw-on-liquidity is framed for the drill.
  - Size: exactly ONE contract. No two contracts, no pyramiding (he will teach pyramiding later for his son).
  - Orders: all entries are limit orders; stop and take-profit are placed at entry. You may not move or cancel the stop. The trade ends either at the stop or at the limit target, whichever trips first, and you wait before the next one. Market orders are not allowed in the drill. No partials in the platform, though you annotate hypothetical partials (see below).
  - Reason to enter: each time a fair value gap forms (for his son's practice) you engage it, aiming at the nearest pool of liquidity (old high/low, relative equal highs/lows, short-term highs/lows) or inefficiency (an FVG, the NWOG/NDOG). He says you can swap in order blocks or other PD arrays. Do not demand that it be "the right one".
  - Alternate buying and selling (he considered flipping a coin) and deliberately include counter-trend drills so you feel what that is like. Range-bound days are better for drilling than strongly directional days.
  - Volume: minimum 10, ideally 15–20 per day, which he says takes about an hour to an hour and a half. Do it in London, NY, the lunch hour and PM if you can. Do it for weeks, up to a few months; progress is visible in a couple of weeks and notable by 2–3 months.
  - Journal every drill (see Process). Over time your eye begins to jump to setups you have seen repeat in the drills, and you start to see setups you never noticed.
  - It is explicitly not Enigma, not a model, not a signal service, and he says you will lose if you copy it with a real or funded account.
- **How to identify:** n/a (practice method). A drill entry = a PD array that has just formed + a stop framed at the level that would prove you wrong + a target at the nearest liquidity or inefficiency.
- **How to use:** Frame stop and target first (entry is secondary; see Limit order mechanics). Log entry time, time to stop or target, how much unrealized profit it gave, and your emotional state. Review at the end of each weekend and note which drills lined up best with what delivered.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15-second chart, 10 drills after the 9:30 ET open, net about +$3,575 with 6 of the 10 losing (ICT's own count). Walk-through of the first few:
  - Drill 1: sell limit just below the high of a small gap with the stop at the high; stopped out.
  - Drill 2: a winner.
  - Drill 3: counter-trend long off a small 15s FVG aiming back up toward the NWOG; stopped out immediately.
  - Drill 4: entry inside a gap within the 60-minute discount (consequent encroachment of a wick), stop just beyond, target just above the wick's CE.
  - Later: the first FVG of the day at 9:31 on the 15s chart delivered quickly down to the 15-minute relative equal lows, which sat on September 23rd's weekly low. A sell at the inversion FVG (see below) and a final buy on a FVG aimed at relative equal highs closed the set at 10 drills.
  - The target-based exits (take profit) were all limit orders. The earlier market-order buttons were used only to show it was not Market Replay.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:02:40](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=160) — purpose: learn limit orders, why market orders are used only to prove live data.
  - [0:17:20](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=1040) — rules: no market orders, no moving the stop, one contract, journal your feelings.
  - [1:34:39](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=5679) — "volatility pinball" defined.
  - [3:03:42](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=11022) — result of 10 drills and recap of what it is.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He frames it as the opposite of trading selectively: "I'm forcing myself to take" whatever forms, including low-probability ones. His real trading would pyramid from the first FVG entry rather than do one-and-done. Do not treat the drill P&L as skill evidence in either direction.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Limit Orders & Volatility Pinball Drills \ October 01, 2024
head: Limit order mechanics (buy limit / sell limit, stop, target)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Selling short: place a SELL limit ABOVE market price; the market has to rise to your price. Buying: place a BUY limit BELOW market price; the market has to trade down to it.
  - Fill: the market must trade at least ONE TICK through your limit price to be sure of a fill. Just touching it may not fill you, and larger size may need more.
  - Frame the trade in this order: (1) the draw (where you think price goes), (2) the stop (where you are wrong), (3) the entry is the "secondary concern". For a bearish idea the entry is some premium array above market.
  - Example placement: for a short at a small gap, sell limit one contract just below the candle's high, stop dragged to the high, target one tick above the draw level.
  - A stop is mandatory every time ("your insurance policy"). It is the market telling you your idea was wrong and a "good time to be wrong"; do not treat it as an enemy.
  - The only permitted market order is to exit a trade you know you are offside on or that is about to turn on you.
  - Entering with a market order signals rushing, impulsiveness, emotion.
- **How to identify:** n/a
- **How to use:** Decide target (old high/low, inefficiency such as the NDOG) and stop first, then sit a limit at the PD array. Log how long a trade lasts, average profit, average risk; calculate these yourself manually rather than only trusting a platform.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s, near the open: market price around 20,241.5 (he says "241 a half"); he explains selling at a gap above and targeting the NDOG/inefficiency below.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [2:02:14](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=7334) — the stop as insurance.
  - [2:05:26](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=7526) — sell limit walkthrough.
  - [2:07:06](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=7626) — buy limit reversed.
  - [2:07:55](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=7675) — must trade one tick through to fill.
  - [3:15:04](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=11704) — "always limit orders".
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He admits he uses market orders on the live stream only to show the buy/sell hot buttons, which prove it is not Market Replay (Replay moves those buttons to the lower right and hides the live-session status timer).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Limit Orders & Volatility Pinball Drills \ October 01, 2024
head: Partials in drills (annotated, hypothetical)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Because the drill uses one contract, you ANNOTATE where a partial would have been taken and screenshot it. This trains you to hunt for places to "fund the trade", remove risk and reward yourself.
  - Candidate partial levels he names: below each prior low as price makes new lows, each time price makes a low and retraces and then goes below it again (even by one tick); the consequent encroachment (50%) of a large wick as price trades down into it; the midpoint of gaps price trades through; below relative equal lows; after a partial you can roll the stop to cover costs.
  - He says partials are how beginners avoid fear and greed, since a single contract still feels like risking the mortgage.
- **How to identify:** n/a
- **How to use:** In your journal write "partial here" at the closing price of the level broken. Ideal reading is speed straight into the next target (e.g. the 60-minute consequent encroachment).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s short, price falls and breaks successive lows; he annotates partial #1 beneath the first low, another as the move expands, and uses CE of a large wick as another. Actual price values he quotes are garbled in captions (caption unclear).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Limit Orders & Volatility Pinball Drills \ October 01, 2024
head: Volume imbalance — body-based definition and the "real" liquidity void
body:
- **Kind:** refinement (he says he is correcting an insufficient description from the previous day's stream)
- **What ICT says:**
  - A volume imbalance is the separation between the BODIES (open/close) of consecutive candles, not the wicks. Wicks can still "do the damage" and trade through the area.
  - If a candle has no body (open = close, a doji-type), the algorithm ignores that candle entirely. The reference is the separation between the bodies of the candles on either side of it. Drawn by the wrong rule (using the open/close of the doji) the imbalance would look different.
  - A "real common gap" (his phrase; i.e. a true liquidity void) is where no trading took place between one candle's high and another candle's low. Only this is a liquidity void by definition; a body separation where wicks overlap is not.
  - Paint roller analogy: price delivering down and back up over an area offers both sell-side and buy-side delivery, so that area becomes "balanced". Wicks can still print outside the box.
  - A candle that closes with a volume imbalance above it (down-close candle, then price up) — when the next candle trades up, expect price to return into that imbalance as a discount array. He wants the imbalance to be left intact as price rallies.
- **How to identify:** Draw the rectangle between the body of candle A and the body of candle C, skipping any bodiless candle between. The imbalance is "still in its true form" even when wicks have crossed it.
- **How to use:** Mark the box from the bodies, expect price to return into it after it is created, and read wick pokes outside it as stop-running rather than a failure as long as the bodies keep resting on the box (see Indigo).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Asian session, about 8:10 PM ET. The body of a candle stops at 20,229.5, the very next candle's low is 20,229.5 "to the tick"; later a candle's low and the low of another are both 20,231.50. He uses these to show the algorithm references candle bodies, and that the wick did the damage while bodies rested on top of the box.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:56:48](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=3408) — separation between bodies.
  - [0:59:13](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=3553) — doji with no body is ignored.
  - [1:00:48](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=3648) — real liquidity void defined.
  - [1:01:37](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=3697) — paint roller.
  - [1:05:41](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=3941) — 20,229.5 to the tick.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Updates the previous stream's simple "gap between candle 1's close and candle 3's open" description. He says it is not always only this; other things must be considered.

head: Dual volume imbalance on the daily chart (unnamed PD array) and grading with quadrants
body:
- **Kind:** definition / new coinage (he withholds the name)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Specific PD array on the daily chart (NQ December 2024): two volume imbalances stacked, one on each side of a middle candle. The middle candle's body sits inside the span between the two outer bodies. He says it must be a candle "surrounded by a volume imbalance on both sides".
  - Encompass the first imbalance to the second and draw the box out in time (the blue shaded rectangle).
  - He says he will not give the array's name because people will rush out books; the name will come once his books are in print.
  - "Grading": put a Fibonacci on the low-to-high of the box and add the quadrants: low, lower quadrant (25%), midpoint/equilibrium (50%), upper quadrant (75%), high. Then you anticipate PD arrays forming around the quadrant levels rather than reacting.
  - A price run into the upper quadrant of this box is the "qualifier" for entry: price should reach it, not necessarily the whole box.
- **How to identify:** Find a candle whose body is contained between two consecutive volume imbalances (one before, one after). Box from the low of the first imbalance to the high of the second; fib with quadrants. (Exact construction in captions is partly unclear.)
- **How to use:** Look for liquidity runs (stops below relative equal lows) that carry price into the upper quadrant, then take the order block there (see Indigo). As targets, the top of the box was reached on the rally.
- **Example in this video:** Daily NQ Dec 2024 box shown on 9/30–10/1; the Asian-session drop on 9/30 PM ET went below the relative equal lows and into the upper quadrant of this box; the rally then went to the top of the box. No exact box prices are given.

head: Indigo entry model  (also: "ICT's Indigo model entry")
body:
- **Kind:** new coinage (entry pattern)
- **What ICT says:**
  - A purge of liquidity followed by an order block that trades into that liquidity, with a volume imbalance on top of it (for a bullish setup) or below it (bearish). Simply: "order block inside of liquidity with a volume imbalance on top".
  - There are two possible reasons for a long entry: price goes to liquidity (sell stops below relative equal lows), or it goes to a discount inefficiency such as a real gap. The main one is liquidity.
  - Filters: the sweep must go beyond the lows into a higher-timeframe reference (here the upper quadrant of the daily dual imbalance); the smooth lows / the NDOG low alone are too insignificant to buy at; do not buy early into "too smooth" levels.
  - He says it is "a combination of several factors" and more will come later; it is not fully taught.
- **How to identify:** (1) Run on stops (sell side for longs); (2) reaches a higher-timeframe level (quadrant); (3) a down-close candle forms (order block) with a volume imbalance above it; (4) price crosses that candle's open (validation).
- **How to use:** Enter anywhere in the order block (open to high or wick, "the watering hole"); add as price touches the top of the volume imbalance; stop below the sweep; target the minor buy-side pools then the buy-side level (20,287) and the top of the daily box.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m, Asian session, Monday 9/30 evening into 10/1 (around 8:00–8:10 PM ET). Price made relative equal highs and then dropped aggressively. Breakout buyers had bought above and had stops below the equal lows and a wick; below sat a real gap and the NDOG. Price drove below the equal lows into the real gap and into the upper quadrant of the daily dual imbalance. A down-close candle formed with a volume imbalance on top; ICT went long inside the candle and added at the top of the imbalance. He did not buy early. Price rallied through the minor buy-side pools to the 20,287 buy-side level.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:51:15](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=3075) — the Indigo name and one-line definition.
  - [0:53:36](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=3216) — why he would not buy earlier; "if this low would have gone lower... it wouldn't be the Indigo entry".
  - [1:08:55](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=4135) — order block entry zone.
  - [1:29:48](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=5388) — recap.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says "Indigo" is not needed and that optimal trade entry, Silver Bullet and the 2022 model are each sufficient. He also refuses to call it supply/demand (see next concept).

head: Order block validation and anticipation (refinement)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - An order block is not merely a down-close candle, and does not need to be engulfed. It is validated by other factors around the idea that the market should turn.
  - Here: as soon as price crossed the candle's open to the upside (it need not close above) it validated as a bullish order block.
  - He anticipates and predicts WHERE the order block, FVG or imbalance will form, based on the liquidity and the higher-timeframe level; he is not reacting to it after it forms.
  - PD arrays are not designed to stop price in its tracks; they give intelligence on what to look for. Here price was expected to trade to and through the real gap "like a hot knife through butter".
- **How to identify:** Down-close candle (bullish OB) at a liquidity purge and a reference level, with a volume imbalance above it.
- **How to use:** Entry anywhere between the open and high (or wick) of that candle. Anything lower in the area is extra entry.
- **Example in this video:** Same Asian-session trade as above.
- **Timestamps:**

  - [1:18:32](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=4712) — "an order block is validated when you have other factors".
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He contrasts this with supply and demand: a demand zone needs an anchor of buying, but here price was below all the lows and there was no demand zone. He also says he does not trust diagonal trend-line support and resistance and does not look at classic S/R.

head: Retail breakout logic and why stops are the draw  (Buy-side/Sell-side liquidity, relative equal lows)
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Retail buys the breakout above a short-term high (buy stop) and places stops below "support" (relative equal lows, a smooth gap, a wick low) and trails stops under wicks.
  - When price creates relative equal highs and then drives down hard, it is going after those sell-side stops. Read price by looking at where retail already got long and where their stops are.
  - The macro window starts the move; the target is the inefficiency or liquidity pool above or below.
  - He wants to be "diametrically opposed" to John Murphy's technical analysis book, which he recommends only to learn what the retail mindset sees; he has "zero affinity" for its content.
- **How to identify:** Relative equal highs followed by a quick drop; breakout-buy high; smooth swing lows and a clean gap below as "support".
- **How to use:** Wait for the stop run, then use PD arrays at the HTF level.
- **Example in this video:** Same NQ 1m: relative equal highs, aggressive drop, buy stops above the little high are the retail longs, their stops below the lows/wick are the target.

head: Breakaway gap vs Measuring gap
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - When price leaves a higher-timeframe PD array (the daily box), he wants to see a buy-side imbalance / sell-side inefficiency created on the way out (bullish) or the reverse (bearish), and to see it STAY OPEN (unfilled).
  - A gap at the beginning of a move that does not get filled is a breakaway gap: a lot more move is coming.
  - A gap in the MIDDLE of the move is a measuring gap: the second leg should equal the first leg. Fib method: draw from the start of the move; the gap's 50% area marks the halfway point so the second leg mirrors the first.
  - Do not want to see price merely touch the top of the HTF box and fall back.
- **How to identify:** Imbalance left as price exits an HTF array; where it sits relative to the whole move decides which gap it is.
- **How to use:** Measuring gap gives a projected target; a breakaway gap means expect more.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m rally out of the top of the daily box left a volume imbalance; he says in this instance it is a breakaway gap, not a measuring gap, so more move is coming (and shows what a measuring projection would look like).
- **Timestamps:** [1:21:45](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=4905), [1:23:21](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=5001)

head: Inversion FVG — stop above the gap's midpoint, body in the lower half
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A short entered on an inversion FVG should NOT see price reach the halfway point of that gap. For a beginner (his son) he suggests a stop at the high of the gap, but adds you have to allow for delivery up into a higher FVG when the leg that displaced lower contains two FVGs (as in the 2022 model).
  - So the stop goes above the midpoint (consequent encroachment) of the higher gap, not necessarily the extreme.
  - A bearish iFVG has to trade away first and then come back up. The body should stay in the LOWER half; the wick can poke into the upper half. In the example the wick stabbed outside the orange box, which he calls normal here because two FVGs are stacked on the distribution side.
- **How to identify:** Former bullish FVG broken by displacement lower; price returns; two stacked FVGs inside the displacing leg.
- **How to use:** Stop above the CE of the higher gap; partials at consequent encroachment of wicks and gaps and at each new low.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s drill, short at the iFVG after a displacement lower; price Wick'd into the upper gap but stayed below its midpoint; partials noted at the CE of a wick, a low, a gap's CE, and a new low.
- **Timestamps:** [2:41:47](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=9707), [2:43:23](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=9803), [3:12:39](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=11559), [3:13:29](https://youtu.be/DnuCB5Stk-0?t=11609)

head: News-week protocol (NFP / CPI / PPI / FOMC weeks)  (aliases ICT uses: "nonfarm payroll protocol", "no touch day", "volatility injections", "high-impact news drivers")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - High-impact reports (NFP, CPI, PPI at 8:30 ET; FOMC in the afternoon, around 2:00/2:30, a two-stage delivery) are used as "volatility injections". They give the market maker a pretext for moves that are really manual.
  - The week of the report is hard to trade, and the difficulty starts days before the release, not only on the day.
  - For NFP week (report Friday 8:30): trade the Monday, which he calls easy, and possibly Tuesday. Tuesday is decent until the London session of Wednesday, which is "the last bit of good price action". Wednesday NY session onward (Wed/Thu/Fri) becomes messy and range-bound.
  - New students should not trade Wednesday, Thursday or Friday of NFP week. The pre-market session before 9:00 ET on Wednesday is acceptable. After 9:00, if you have not already had a trade, do nothing. (Early in the video the caption has him saying the difficulty starts "after 11 o'clock" Wednesday. Caption unclear. He later says 9:00.)
  - If the report is on Thursday or Friday, best trading is Monday and/or Tuesday. If the report is on Monday or Tuesday, do nothing at the start of the week and trade the easier "salad days" later in the week.
  - If you have no clear weekly/daily draw, do very little that week. Once the weekly draw has been satisfied (here the weekly BISI target delivered Monday), "it's already done enough" and he does not need another trade.
  - Never be in the market going into the 8:30 release. A single 1-minute candle can travel 250+ handles in NQ on NFP, and it is untradeable.
  - He ignores the raw data. It is "already baked in". What matters is the energy before the release, at the release, and where the market goes right after. Bullish data often produces a drop and the reverse.
  - Schedule it: check the economic calendar (forexfactory.com or an econ-day calendar, both free) a month ahead. Plan when to trade and when to sit still. Medium-impact (orange) events can be traded. The no-trade rule is for high-impact (red) events.
  - He frames "knowing when not to trade" as a skill worth more than a tight stop or a good entry.
- **How to identify:** Check the calendar for red-folder CPI, PPI, NFP, FOMC. Note the weekday of each release. Mark the week as "reduced activity" from the day the week turns choppy through the release.
- **How to use:** Trade Monday/Tuesday on NFP weeks, tape-read or paper trade the rest. Re-engage only after the post-news precision test (see below).
- **Example in this video:** NQ Wed 2024-10-02, NFP on Fri 10-04. An economic number came out at 8:15 ET. Price ranged around the top of a weekly BISI with minor liquidity above and below. ICT sat still, only annotated, and said any trade idea could be upset by manual moves.
- **Timestamps:** [0:02:36](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=156) news used as volatility injection · [0:16:17](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=977) why a newer student should skip Wed/Thu/Fri · [0:33:37](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=2017) which weeks he is least active · [1:49:55](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=6595) no-touch rule restated · [1:55:39](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=6939) NFP protocol: trade Monday
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He is not saying it cannot be traded. He says it is a drag on new students' accuracy and psychology. He admits he has blown accounts on NFP, and had his head ripped off by PPI/CPI, and no longer tries to predict the pre-release direction.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Tape Reading NQ \ October 02, 2024
head: Post-news re-entry test (precision returns)  (aliases: "manual intervention", "sharks in the water", "green light")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - After a high-impact report, wait a minimum of 15 minutes. Then study 1-minute and sub-1-minute (15s) price delivery.
  - While "manual intervention" is underway, PD arrays are not respected and price stops and turns for no reason. The market makers are manually pushing price. Moves overshoot highs/lows by a lot and do not lay the low or high onto anything precise.
  - A quick test is the consequent encroachment (CE) of fair value gaps. If price eats straight through the whole FVG with no respect for the midpoint, intervention is still on, so sit still.
  - When PD arrays start stopping price "on the tick" again and CE supports price, the algorithm is back in control and precision tools work again. That is the green light.
  - While intervention is underway, "opportunities are cleverly disguised impossibilities". The entry looks ready to pluck, but it bites.
- **How to identify:** Watch the 1m and 15s charts for whether FVG midpoints, order block edges and old levels are being respected to the tick.
- **How to use:** No respect means no entry. Wait until PD arrays are respected consistently, then trade normally.
- **Example in this video:** He tells viewers to watch the 1m and 15s charts around Thursday 8:30 (employment data) and Friday 8:30 (NFP) and see the absence of precision for themselves.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:30](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=2550) 15-minute minimum wait, watch 1m/sub-1m · [0:43:18](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=2598) CE test · [0:46:29](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=2789) "opportunities are disguised impossibilities" · [0:48:05](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=2885) intervention looks like big abrupt moves past levels
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** His "manual vs scripted" framing: normally price is algorithmic (scripted, precise). During news weeks the hand of the market maker moves it.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Tape Reading NQ \ October 02, 2024
head: Near-term liquidity first, then flip (range-bound week approach)  (aliases: "volatility pinball", "broken wing trick")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - In news weeks, expect range-bound, listless trading. Do not mindset a "trending day". Price bumps stops on one side, fakes a trend, and returns to the range.
  - Identify the nearest buy-side and sell-side pools (minor liquidity). Wait for one to be taken. Usually the first side taken can simply be flipped and traded to the other.
  - Significant price runs (30, 50+ handles, not 10-20) usually follow liquidity being taken first. Taking the sell-side first, especially with a bullish higher-timeframe bias, makes any discount array more trustworthy.
  - Why: the sell-side raid stops out profitable longs, traps breakout shorts, and gives smart money cheap fills (the sell stops become market sell orders that smart money buys into).
  - If neither side has been taken, he is "indifferent" and sits still.
- **How to identify:** Mark the closest clean highs/lows (minor BSL/SSL). Annotate whichever has been raided.
- **How to use:** After one side is taken, look for PD arrays (FVG, OB) in the direction away from the raid to ride to the other side. Without the raid, do nothing.
- **Example in this video:** Pre-market NQ 15m/5m: relative equal highs were disrupted early, price traded down into the weekly BISI. Minor sell-side sat below a down-close 5m candle and relative equal lows sat beneath. ICT preferred a sweep of the lows before a rally into the highs. He said an FVG forming after a drop below both lows, with price rallying, would have been a long. Price never did that, so no trade.
- **Timestamps:** [0:17:52](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=1072) identify pools, wait for one to be taken, flip · [0:19:29](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=1169) significant runs follow liquidity taken · [0:21:56](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=1316) volatility pinball · [0:29:20](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=1760) smart money buys the sell-stop liquidity
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Long bias was based on the election-year argument (markets propped up) and the bullish long-term trend. He says that is only his lean, not a requirement.

head: Minor vs primary BSL/SSL (annotation at 9:00 ET)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Before 9:00 ET, annotate the closest buy-side/sell-side pools as "minor". At 9:00 ET, re-annotate for the opening bell. The clean highs, clean lows or a singular high/low closest to price at that time are the "primary" buy-side and sell-side liquidity.
  - Do the same on 1m, 5m and 15m. Primary pools are not looked for until 9:00, because you wait for the opening bell and then expect a run to one of them.
  - The best trade circumstance is when the higher-timeframe (daily/weekly) draw is already clear.
- **How to identify:** At 9:00 ET find the nearest clean high and low relative to current price. Anything closer or smaller is minor.
- **How to use:** Treat the primary pools as the targets for the 9:30 opening bell and morning session.
- **Example in this video:** At 9:00, primary buy-side was a recent clean high, higher buy-side was farther away, and the lows below were primary sell-side. A minor sell-side sat at about 19924 (caption unclear).
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:46](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=1366) minor vs primary defined · [0:53:46](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=3226) annotating primary at 9:00
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** None.

head: Bullish order block, mean threshold and candle bodies
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - A down-closed candle on the 5m (order block) is bullish support while price stays above its mean threshold (50% of the candle).
  - If a candle body closes below the mean threshold, the order block is breached and "not a good area to expect price to stop". It does not always mean continuation lower, but lower becomes more likely.
  - The ideal case is a drop into the upper half of the OB with the mean threshold never touched. He never wants to see candle bodies deliver into the lower half of a bullish OB.
- **How to identify:** The mean threshold is the midpoint of the order block candle. Watch for a body close beyond it.
- **How to use:** A body close through the mean threshold invalidates the long idea. He then looks to sell-side.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 5m at about 8:50 ET (before the open): a down-close candle with price hammering the bottom of the preceding up-close candle. ICT says the pivot idea is bullish while the OB's mean threshold holds.
- **Timestamps:** [0:26:52](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=1612) mean threshold of 5m OB · [0:27:42](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=1662) body into lower half is the warning sign
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The caption says "water block" for order block here.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Tape Reading NQ \ October 02, 2024
head: Two stacked FVGs (allow for the second one)  (aliases: "Model 2022 logic", "breakaway gap")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - When price forms two FVGs close together, e.g. one small FVG above a lower one, applying the 2022 Mentorship model means you must allow price to reach into the second (upper) FVG before concluding the entry failed.
  - If you enter the lower one with a stop only just above the candle high, you can get stopped as price wicks up to the upper FVG.
  - Two approaches: (a) enter at the first FVG with a wider stop above the second, or (b) wait for price to trade into the upper FVG and use that as the entry, with a somewhat larger stop. Beginners especially need the extra forgiveness.
  - A third FVG further up is a "breakaway gap". It shows heaviness. Price does not need to go to it. The move stops before it.
  - The ideal case is that candle bodies stay in the lower half of the upper FVG while only the wick pokes the higher gap.
- **How to identify:** Count FVGs along the retracement. The first and second can be reached. The one beyond is a "breakaway" if price shows heaviness before it.
- **How to use:** Decide stop location to cover the second FVG. Check that the body stays in the lower half.
- **Example in this video:** NQ short at about 9:00 to minor sell-side: FVG at the first break lower and a small FVG just above. Price wicked into the upper FVG (a stop-loss based only on the first would have been hit) then dropped. Later at the open, a third FVG appeared higher up, was treated as a breakaway gap, and price did not reach it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:57:26](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=3446) two FVGs, allow the second · [0:58:14](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=3494) two schools of thought, wider stop · [1:37:53](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5873) breakaway gap · [1:38:40](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5920) stays in lower half
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Ties back to the 2022 model rule that you may need to wait for the second FVG.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Tape Reading NQ \ October 02, 2024
head: Inversion FVG (iFVG) and reclaimed FVG as a catalyst  (aliases: "reclaimed bearish fair value gap")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / example only
- **What ICT says:**
  - The weekly BISI (a bullish FVG) is, when price is above it and drops into it, a bullish FVG. If price trades below it and you are bearish, it becomes an inversion FVG, and you want to see price stay heavy at its midpoint or low and not explore the upper part.
  - A weekly sell-side-inefficiency gap sitting below price is a classic bearish FVG. If price trades back up into it, it becomes a "reclaimed" bearish FVG.
  - An inversion FVG is not meant to be a hold-and-run level. It is meant to stop price, let it run, and then a later FVG forms on the other side. In his drill: price dips to a discount level, a later FVG forms after the rally, and that can be the catalyst for a run to buy-side.
  - Using an iFVG as an entry point of interest, you grade where it sits within the dealing range (see below).
- **How to use:** Treat the old FVG as context. Wait for the second-leg FVG after the raid. Do not call a "failure" because price passed through the iFVG.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15s/1m: the early small FVG case study that "cancelled" when price traded below its low inside the BISI inefficiency. The next FVG after price dipped and rallied back became a catalyst candidate. After 9:30, price returned up into an iFVG then dropped to the primary sell-side.
- **Timestamps:** [1:00:50](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=3650) FVG inverts, future FVG as catalyst · [1:03:14](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=3794) reclaimed bearish FVG · [1:09:58](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=4198) BISI vs inversion classification
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Brief and loosely explained. Use as context, not a full rule set.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ Tape Reading NQ \ October 02, 2024
head: Premium / discount framing: Inception to Terminus  (aliases: "point of interest", "grading the unrealized dealing range", "Terminus" (new coinage use))
body:
- **Kind:** rule / new coinage
- **What ICT says:**
  - Before every trade you must know where price is going (the "Terminus", the liquidity target) and where you are entering (the "Inception" PD array, the point of interest where the move begins).
  - Frame the range from the entry-side Inception to the Terminus. The 50% equilibrium divides the range. For a short, only enter in premium (above equilibrium). Entries below equilibrium are "so close to where it's going to go" and are low probability.
  - Probability falls as your entry moves toward the target, which is how premium/discount ties to entry quality.
  - You can do this without a Fib tool. Visually, the midpoint between an iFVG and the relative equal lows is where the equilibrium sits. FVGs above that midpoint are premium arrays for a short. The ones in the lower half are not.
  - He calls this "grading the unrealized dealing range". The range has not delivered yet, but you can anticipate where setups will form.
  - To pick between several FVGs: ask where each sits relative to the 50% of Inception to Terminus. In his example the chosen FVG was in the upper half and the next one up was a breakaway gap.
- **How to identify:** Draw (or imagine) the range from entry zone to the liquidity target below the relative equal lows. Locate equilibrium. Classify each candidate PD array as premium or discount.
- **How to use:** Short only from premium arrays, long only from discount arrays. Target the Terminus (beyond the liquidity, since the liquidity has to be engaged).
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: Inception was a volume imbalance / FVG area after the pre-market rally. Terminus was just below the relative equal lows. Equilibrium divided the two. The volume imbalance and the first FVG sat in the premium half. The market respected them and delivered to the sell-side below.
- **Timestamps:** [1:20:33](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=4833) define range of opportunity, target is beyond the liquidity · [1:22:07](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=4927) equilibrium, short only in premium · [1:34:41](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5681) grading the unrealized dealing range · [1:35:29](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5729) pick the right FVG by premium/discount
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Here "Terminus" means the liquidity end of the move. He says the objective is not just to reach the price point but to trade below it, because the liquidity has to be engaged ([1:20:33](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=4833)).

head: Candle bodies vs wicks (where smart money is read)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:** The bulk of volume is in candle bodies, and the narrative is determined by the bodies. Smart money reads bodies. Retail ("street money") gets hurt in the wicks. When price wicks into a higher FVG but bodies stay below, that is the signature of respect. Orders resting above the wick do not matter to the algorithm (he mocks the "show me level 2 data" crowd).
- **How to use:** Judge FVG/OB respect by where bodies close, not by wick overshoot.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m: price wicked into the higher FVG, bodies remained in the lower half, then dropped.
- **Timestamps:** [1:39:27](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5967) bodies tell the narrative, victims live in wicks
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Ties to the OB mean threshold rule above.

head: RTH opening gap midpoint (CE) in the first 30 minutes  (aliases: "opening range gap", "mid gap", "opening gap is the initial bias")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - The opening gap is the initial bias. In the first 30 minutes after the open, "70% of the time" price trades to the midpoint (consequent encroachment) of the gap. If you gap down, the primary focus is up to the midpoint of the gap. He repeats the 70% number and calls it a 70% strike rate.
  - Size filter: an opening range gap of at least 40 handles (NQ) is his minimum interest for the first 30 minutes. A larger gap (e.g. 75 handles) makes him more interested in the day, and he would use most of his available leverage.
  - After the midpoint is hit, it often acts as the turning point to the primary sell-side.
- **How to identify:** Compare the 4:00 PM close (ET) and 9:30 AM open and mark the gap and its 50%. (Defined as the RTH opening gap in other lectures.)
- **How to use:** Gap down means expect a first-30-minute run up to the gap midpoint. Gap up means the reverse (inferred).
- **Example in this video:** NQ Wed 10-02: gap-down open. The midpoint sat at 19965. Price traded up to it in the first 30 minutes, then reversed and dropped to the primary sell-side below.
- **Timestamps:** [1:23:46](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5026) mid gap at 19965, 70% · [1:24:33](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5073) opening gap as initial bias · [1:25:23](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5123) 40-handle minimum · [1:32:16](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5536) recap, 70% strike rate
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** The "gap up" mirror is inferred. He only demonstrates a gap down.

head: Opening-gap turtle soup (buy stop at the open of the piercing candle)  (aliases: "mechanical turtle soup", "buy on a stop")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - Setup: a gap-down open (at least 40 handles), a minor sell-side low already identified, and the opening gap midpoint as the draw for the first 30 minutes.
  - When price pierces below the low, take the down-closed candle that pierced it. Treat it as an order block. Use that candle's opening price as a buy stop.
  - If price never trades back up to that open, you are never filled. If it does, you are kicked in long. Target the opening gap midpoint (CE) and be out ("small high-frequency entry").
  - It is "very, very mechanical". You are buying from flat, and the buy stop is the only order that executes.
  - You can then aim for the next sell-side (the equal lows) after the midpoint.
  - Backtest it. He says there are multiple ways to trade this tape and they are "equally effective".
- **How to identify:** Gap down at 9:30, a minor sell-side low, a down-closed candle piercing it. (The caption wording on which candle to use is ambiguous. Best reading is the piercing candle's own open.)
- **How to use:** Entry: buy stop at the open of the piercing candle. Target: gap midpoint. Stop: not stated in detail in this video.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m after the 9:30 open, gap down: price traded below a minor low with a down candle, rallied up to the midpoint, then fell on toward the equal lows.
- **Timestamps:** [1:25:23](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5123) ORG gap, turtle soup idea · [1:27:02](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5222) open of the piercing candle as buy stop · [1:27:49](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5269) why it is mechanical · [1:28:37](https://youtu.be/YxpHUwZhu80?t=5317) went to mid gap
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Stop-loss placement not stated. He says to backtest.

body:
- **Kind:** rule

  - NFP is highly manipulated. The data is already baked into price, but the sentiment it creates shifts investors' bullish/bearish feelings, so 8:30 on Friday will be a "carnival ride".
  - Classic advice for new students: trade the Monday of NFP week, trade Tuesday, do not trade Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

head: RTH opening range gap and its midpoint  (aliases: "opening range gap", "mid gap", "settlement")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - On a chart set to RTH, price delivery is 9:30 ET until 4:14 PM ET. The previous day's RTH settlement (at 4:14 ET, as he states it) to the 9:30 open is the opening range gap. The rectangle drawn between those two prices, together with the time, is the opening range gap and the opening range.
  - The midpoint of the gap is the key level. 70% of the time the gap gets filled to halfway. He pushes back on a Twitter study claiming less, saying he has data back about 40 years and has lived it.
  - Practical use: an opening gap down means the first-30-minutes bias is bullish (up to the midpoint). He calls this a nice scalping opportunity.
  - Next, price often reaches to the previous day's settlement as well.
- **How to identify:** Mark the previous RTH settlement price and the 9:30 open. Measure the 50% (CE).
- **How to use:** Gap down at the open means expect the first-30-minute run up to the gap midpoint. After that, look for a reversal if the higher-timeframe bias is bearish.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Thu 10-03, gap-down open. Price traded right back up to the mid-gap, pulled into a 1m FVG, found support at the mid-gap, rallied to previous settlement, formed another FVG, then cleared the buy-side and spent time there (he reads that as buy-stop accumulation by smart money so they can sell short). The market then broke lower.
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:23](https://youtu.be/Xyiw_IFE9yc?t=263) RTH lens and gap definition · [0:05:11](https://youtu.be/Xyiw_IFE9yc?t=311) 70% claim and defense · [0:06:00](https://youtu.be/Xyiw_IFE9yc?t=360) buy-stop accumulation then short
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same 70% claim as M24-040. He is defensive about it here.

title: October 03, 2024 NQ Market Review
head: Respect of the lower half of a bearish FVG (SIBI) as a continuation tell  (aliases: "sell side imbalance buy side inefficiency")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - On the 1m (ETH chart) price traded up to buy-side, broke lower, and came right back into a sell-side imbalance gap. Later, after much chopping, price entered only the lower half of that gap and never the upper half. That tells you price is more likely to break lower.
  - Wicks in the consolidation reached up to their own 50% (CE) levels, which supports the read.
  - After displacement lower there was a gap he first expected to be revisited, then corrected himself: it was a breakaway gap.
  - Price then attacked the sell-side below, then the weekly BISI CE, made the low of the day, and consolidated into the afternoon.
- **How to identify:** For a bearish FVG, note whether the highest price into the gap since formation stays below the midpoint (CE). If so, the gap is respected as resistance.
- **How to use:** Lower-half-only respect = lean continuation lower. Target the pool of sell-side liquidity below and the weekly CE.
- **Timestamps:** [0:06:00](https://youtu.be/Xyiw_IFE9yc?t=360) 1m RTH view · [0:06:49](https://youtu.be/Xyiw_IFE9yc?t=409) lower half only, breakaway gap · [0:07:37](https://youtu.be/Xyiw_IFE9yc?t=457) delivery to weekly CE
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the same logic as M24-040's "stay in the lower half" and "breakaway gap" rule, applied to a bearish gap on the opposite side.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ October NFP NQ \ October 04, 2024
head: News-day protocol: no positioning into 8:30, wait 15 minutes, no raw data  (aliases: "carnival ride", "treat it like FOMC / CPI / PPI")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - NFP, FOMC, CPI and PPI are all treated the same: you do not know where they go, so do not speculate ahead of them.
  - Wait about 15 minutes after the release, minimum. NFP at 8:30 ET means 8:45 ET is the green light to start looking and studying. Then see what inefficiencies are still in play and what smooth areas sit above or below.
  - An order placed right at the 8:30 release will not fill, or fills at the worst time with enormous slippage.
  - Brand-new students (including anyone coming from another teacher, who he treats as brand new): do not trade after Wednesday morning New York time on NFP weeks. Wednesday and Thursday were challenging this week.
  - Journal tip: give yourself written permission to never trade this day. Months later, with a model you have not tinkered with, consistent returns and no emotional swaying, you can trade it after the release plus 15 minutes, normally for the rest of the day.
  - He never reviews the number, jobless claims or the change from last month. He does not look at CPI, PPI or the FOMC rate decision. The market uses these as red herrings to manipulate sentiment. Candles are a seismograph of less-informed traders' sentiment.
  - He admits he does not know how to call NFP in advance, and says he is "generally wrong" on NFP. Short-term use of macro or interest-rate data (long-term carry-trade logic included) is useless intraday.
  - In his career some NFP weeks had very favorable Wednesday/Thursday price action, but that is rare and not the standard.
  - Before 8:30 NFP Friday: hold no bias and no expectation. Let price show you after. "An opportunity in the wrong conditions is a cleverly disguised impossibility."
  - He had no stop-loss he could trust for a long chasing the 8:30 run, so he would not take it even though the payout looks great.
- **How to use:** Mark levels at 8:15, sit through 8:30, resume study at 8:45 ET. Treat trade ideas before that as untradeable.
- **Example in this video:** NQ NFP Fri 10-04. The first 1-minute candle at 8:30 ran about 98 handles (caption: low "2064" to high "20,162", read as 20064 to 20162). ICT asks whether you could survive that with 15 contracts on a funded account.
- **Timestamps:** [0:05:56](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=356) wait 15 minutes, 8:45 ET green light · [0:06:46](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=406) new-student rule · [0:09:58](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=598) give yourself journal permission · [0:14:05](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=845) never review the number · [0:17:21](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=1041) no fills at 8:30 · [0:26:32](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=1592) 98 handles in one minute
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same protocol as M24-040 and M24-041. New in this video: the exact 8:45 ET restart time, and the "permission in your journal" device.

head: Minor vs primary liquidity drill (8:15 ET pre-news annotation)  (aliases: "minor buy side / sell side", "primary buy side / sell side")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / study drill
- **What ICT says:**
  - At about 8:15 ET, on a 15-minute chart, see where price is. Mark the closest buy-side and sell-side pool at that moment. Those are the "minor" pools. Then look a little broader, above and below, for the next logical level of liquidity. Those are the "primary" pools.
  - Minor buy side: here a recent high (after the previous high was already cleared). Minor sell side: the nearest low. He ignores small consolidation lows. Using lows that are lower than earlier lows is what makes the pool the "first minor sell side".
  - Primary: cut through the consolidation to the relative equal lows (primary sell side) or relative equal highs (primary buy side). "Primary is just the next logical level of liquidity below your near close proximity minor."
  - Study drill for every NFP: watch which pool is taken first, then look for the opposite side to be traded to.
  - He promises to explain why this will not work as a trading method. It is a study mechanism and not a signal. (The explanation is not clearly given. Caption unclear.)
  - Primary buy side: if price goes up there it will run through to clear it, because shorts above think they are safe behind "retail resistance".
- **How to identify:** Nearest high/low at 8:15 equals minor. Next clean relative-equal highs/lows equals primary.
- **How to use:** Watch the 8:30 reaction on the 15m or 5m. Record which pool engages first. Wait 15 minutes. Then look for the other side.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 15m: minor buy side was tagged within seconds at 8:30, and the first pool taken was the minor buy side. ICT then looked to see whether price would go down to the minor sell side. He viewed the run as a possible accumulation ahead of running the primary buy stops.
- **Timestamps:** [0:13:16](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=796) drill rules · [0:18:12](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=1092) minor identified · [0:20:54](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=1254) primary = next logical level · [0:27:19](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=1639) first pool taken is the minor buy side
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Same definition as M24-040 (minor before 9:00, primary at 9:00). Here it is anchored at 8:15 for the 8:30 event. It answers a viewer question on what constitutes minor vs primary.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ October NFP NQ \ October 04, 2024
head: NFP as the disruptor of profitable positions  (aliases: "Boogeyman trading", "pain mechanism")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / narrative rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - NFP is used many times to destabilize sentiment and unseat people who are currently profitable, then go the other way. Here the profitable ones were Tuesday's shorts after the drop into the weekly BISI.
  - Their stops would sit at least above the high of the consolidation. A high slightly lower than the previous one makes a high-probability relative equal high, which is a prime candidate to be taken.
  - Large institutions do not trail stops to breakeven after a 10-handle move. They leave core protective stops outside the normal range so they do not need a trade manager babysitting every fluctuation. So the large pool of orders is at the highs, not at the bottom of the nearby inefficiency.
  - He lists the scenarios and says he cannot pick one: (a) run up to knock out the shorts, then lower next week without taking out the lows. (b) Go down and trip shorts, then pump all day into the weekend, then lower next week. (c) Move around in the middle and leave both pools.
  - A move that rises straight from 8:30 with no stop run or candle taking out trailed sell stops is a premium being built ahead of the 9:30 open.
- **Example in this video:** NQ: price dropped to a weekly BISI (blue box, from Monday), then did little. NFP lifted price straight up from 8:30 toward a primary buy side above Tuesday's relative equal highs.
- **Timestamps:** [0:24:04](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=1444) pain mechanism and scenarios · [0:51:58](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3118) where short stops sit · [1:03:37](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3817) institutions do not trail stops · [1:31:10](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=5470) "Boogeyman trading"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** He says explicitly he can be wrong (and he was wrong on direction early).

head: Judas swing / bait before the 9:30 open
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - The one-way run from 8:30 is, to him, a Judas swing and bait for retail: a trader who just read Elliott wave, pitchforks, Dow theory, Wyckoff or supply/demand sees "clearly going up". Others put buy stops above the 8:30 candle and get tripped long.
  - It is a straight run with no stop run, so no one could get long safely. It builds a premium ahead of the 9:30 bell.
  - He wants a reason, inside the 9:30-10:00 window (it could happen earlier), to see price trade down into the minor sell side. If instead price just keeps running up to the primary buy side as the daily objective, he will miss the move and says that is fine.
  - He expects the 9:30-10:00 opening range to give an entry idea if the run to the buy side happens in that window.
- **Timestamps:** [0:41:29](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=2489) Judas swing / bait · [0:42:17](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=2537) retail buy-stop logic · [0:43:06](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=2586) premium ahead of 9:30 · [0:44:46](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=2686) accept missing the move

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ October NFP NQ \ October 04, 2024
head: Efficient delivery, rebalancing an inefficiency, and why liquidity still matters more  (aliases: "SIBI", "sell side imbalance buy side inefficiency", "efficient delivery", "balanced price range")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - A single candle with a sell-side delivery leaves an inefficiency on the buy side (an "island" between the previous candle's low and the next candle's high). The interval of time between those two prices has not been balanced with price in both directions, so price tends to return to overlap that range. The algorithm "reprices to engage liquidity" and also rebalances inefficiencies. It does not know how many stops are above an old high or below an old low.
  - Once price has traded back up over the single candle and touched its low, the inefficiency has been "efficiently delivered". That is not a balanced price range (BPR).
  - But reaching the top of an inefficiency is not enough as a target. The large pools of orders are at old highs (buy stops) and old lows (sell stops), not at the top of the inefficiency. Price is "offered" there for efficient delivery, and that is not the same as a stop pool.
  - He answers a viewer question: there are no larger pools of liquidity than those above old highs and below old lows. Anyone claiming otherwise is selling a new theory.
  - Time symmetry: the time it took to build the inefficiency is the time you should expect for the return delivery. Here it took two candles instead of one, which is fine.
  - Speed and magnitude: if the inefficiency was created by a quick sudden move, expect the buy-side repricing to be quick and made of large candles. If price instead sputters up and back inside the gap, it is "high resistance" and manual intervention.
  - Management when price sputters up inside an inefficiency (and it is not an NFP day): do not chase or trail the stop up. Lock in cover costs and let it go. Trades like that have many retracements.
- **How to identify:** One candle, or a short run, that traded away leaving a gap with no overlap. Check whether price has since traded back over the whole range.
- **How to use:** Use the gap as context for a draw. Target the higher-liquidity pool above or below and look for speed as confirmation. Slow grinding means do not trust it.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 1m/5m: a sell-side delivery candle formed on Tuesday (red shaded area). From 8:30, price repaid it (overlapping candles on top of it, then through it). ICT said it was now "efficiently delivered" but not a BPR, so a further run to the relative equal highs above was possible. He also recalled that people had thought price would go up just to fill the inefficiency, and he had said that it would go to where the positions are protected.
- **Timestamps:** [0:52:47](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3167) orders are at the highs, not at the gap top · [0:53:36](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3216) largest pools above old highs/below old lows · [0:55:25](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3325) algorithm reprices to engage liquidity and rebalance inefficiency · [0:56:59](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3419) efficiently delivered, not a BPR · [1:00:19](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3619) time symmetry and speed · [1:01:57](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3717) sputtering = manual intervention
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Refines the BPR definition: filling a single-sided inefficiency is not itself a BPR. Compare with the "still no precision" test in M24-040.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ October NFP NQ \ October 04, 2024
head: Opening range gap: ETH vs RTH, midpoint, and gap-closure scenarios  (aliases: "opening range gap", "mid gap", "gap closure half", "settlement")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Chart sessions: electronic trading hours (ETH) run 6:00 PM to 5:00 PM New York time. Regular trading hours (RTH) run 9:30 AM to 4:14 PM. The opening range gap is always defined by RTH: previous RTH settlement (4:14 PM) to the 9:30 open. Toggle between the two when planning.
  - Mid-gap (50%, consequent encroachment) is reached about 70% of the time within the first 30 minutes (9:30-10:00). He restates his 40 years of data (32 years watching the markets, bought historical data before he started trading) against a Twitter study that said otherwise.
  - Standard day: the gap is the initial bias. Scalp to the mid gap if you want. At mid gap, decide whether price continues in the gap's direction or fully closes the gap. If it closes a premium gap, use the bottom of the gap as resistance and expect a move down in multiples of the gap size, two to three standard deviations.
  - With a small gap, wait for the first presented FVG.
  - NFP scenario (this day): ETH price was sitting at the top of an enormous potential gap with relative equal highs just above. Possible script: open at 9:30, run up to those highs to accumulate buy stops (street money chases), then smart money sells into the flood of willing buyers and drives down to the mid gap, three-quarters, or full closure. The primary buy side may not appear on an RTH chart, so check ETH.
  - Conditional read: if the open pushes down to the mid gap early and then climbs all the way back up, that is not a turtle soup short setup. It suggests price is going much higher (consolidate, accumulate, higher). He would prefer a small drop first to make traders think lower and then a rally to the obvious buy side.
  - He says the mid-gap move may take longer than 30 minutes on a news day, and he "is not holding it to" the 70% on NFP.
- **How to identify:** Toggle ETH/RTH. Measure the RTH settlement to open, then the 50%. Note buy-side liquidity on ETH that is not visible on RTH.
- **How to use:** First-30-minute bias toward mid gap. After that, decide on full closure vs continuation using higher-timeframe bias and liquidity.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 10-04: large gap-up in the making. Price rallied from 8:30, opened, ran, then dropped to the mid gap before 10:00. ICT said "not a tick more" at the half of an FVG, then aggressive delivery to mid gap, the 70% strike rate by 10:00.
- **Timestamps:** [1:06:01](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=3961) ETH vs RTH view · [1:07:46](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=4066) mid gap script · [1:10:18](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=4218) session hours · [1:11:06](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=4266) smart money sells into buy stops · [1:13:32](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=4412) premium gap, 2-3 SD targets · [1:24:50](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=5090) 40 years of data · [1:28:01](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=5281) reading a mid-gap tag then rally
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Adds the ETH/RTH toggle and the 2-3 standard deviation (gap-size multiple) projection beyond M24-040/041. The "7%" jab in the transcript is a sarcastic aside, not a statistic.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ October NFP NQ \ October 04, 2024
head: FVG quadrants, body respect, "Mohawk", and the breakaway gap  (aliases: "grading the gap", "burying the bodies", "coloring outside the lines")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - Divide a bearish FVG into quadrants (grading). If candle bodies stay out of the upper half (specifically they respect the upper quadrant/CE), that is a bearish signature. In an ideal world the upper half of a bearish gap is not closed in.
  - Wicks outside the gap are normal and allowed. He calls this a "Mohawk" or coloring outside the lines. What counts is where bodies close ("where are they burying the bodies").
  - Draw the FVG rectangle carefully. Include any volume imbalance. When there is a volume imbalance inside what looks like an FVG, there is no body separation between candle 1 and candle 2, but there is a separation between the bodies of candle 2 and candle 3 (candle 2's close is lower than the next candle's open). The rectangle must reflect that so the quadrants are right. This is why it is not "supply and demand": the levels are specific.
  - If price leaves lower after respecting the upper quadrant and then creates another FVG, that new gap is a breakaway gap. It marks the Inception of the run. Next steps: the CE of the wick, then the half of the gap (the 50% of the opening range gap).
  - Breakaway gap definition requires enough context (here: opening-gap draw, prior respect) to set the stage.
- **How to identify:** Check bodies and quadrant of the FVG after retracement. Check for a following FVG after displacement.
- **How to use:** Bearish: bodies not entering the upper half means expect a drop, then the next FVG is your delivery path. Targets: FVG CE, then the mid gap.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 10-04 around 9:40-9:50 ET: price came back into a gap, bodies stopped at or under the upper quadrant (wicked outside, closed below), then it broke lower and left another FVG (breakaway). Price tagged the FVG's CE, then the half-gap before 10:00. ICT pointed to the FVG as it formed and said he was not taking it because it was NFP.
- **Timestamps:** [1:49:45](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=6585) upper quadrant signature · [1:50:33](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=6633) breakaway gap · [1:52:57](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=6777) "Mohawk" · [1:57:47](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=7067) draw the gap with the volume imbalance · [1:59:21](https://youtu.be/qcYYm1iNCIM?t=7161) delivery to mid gap
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** Consistent with M24-040/041 ("bodies in the lower half", "breakaway gap"). The new detail is the volume-imbalance handling for drawing the rectangle.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ October NFP NQ \ October 04, 2024
head: Trading Asia after a last-hour sell-side raid at the close  (aliases: "market on close", "Asia protocol", "6:50-7:10 macro", "7:50-8:10 macro")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Preconditions: no medium- or high-impact news and no speeches in the economic calendar between 8:30 and 10:00 of the next New York session. Bullish context is assumed.
  - During the last hour of the cash session, price trades down to take a pool of sell-side (below relative equal lows or a multi-day low) and is held there into the close. That is the setup. (The move below the low and then rallying in the last hour is not the same high-probability case, since then smart money is only using the last hour to accumulate sell stops and hold price.)
  - At 6:00 PM ET (not Friday) the new ETH session starts. Wait until about 6:50-7:10 ET and look for reasons to be long.
  - The 6:50-7:10 macro should start sending price higher if smart money is long. After roughly the first 50 minutes of Asia the algorithm "starts spooling" price. Each short-term discount array is used to accumulate more longs.
  - If the 6:50-7:10 macro is silent, the 7:50-8:10 macro can still deliver, in his opinion a better one. Typically 20-40 handles (he says "anywhere between 25 and 40" and "20 to 40"), not necessarily 100. This holds even if news is due the next morning.
  - Asia is often the low of the day when bullish, or the high of the day when bearish.
  - Working window: Asia 7:00 to 9:00, which can extend to 10:00 (PM ET, inferred from the 6:00 PM ETH open). At 10:00, square up, or take some profit and leave a runner if you expect a daily continuation and there is no news at 8:30-10:00 next day.
  - Best case: Asia runs to midnight, London consolidates (or Asia is the real run and London consolidates), New York gives a second stage. The day can total 500-700 handles from the 6:00 PM ETH open to the NY high of day. He says this is not an everyday event and not every Asia session is good.
  - Validation: study by contrast the last hour of cash trading before the better Asia days. Do not rely on the last two weeks only.
  - Daily-chart filter he mentions: the previous close and next open are often close, bodies near each other. (Brief. Not fully explained.)
- **How to identify:** Check the economic calendar for 8:30-10:00 next day. See whether the last hour of RTH raided a clear sell-side and stayed there into the close.
- **How to use:** Look for longs after 6:50 PM ET, with the macro as the timing window. Manage at 10:00 with partial plus a runner.
- **Example in this video:** A "couple weeks back" he bought into a market-on-close idea in an instrument whose name is unclear in the caption ("radi", caption unclear). Asia kept rising for hours. Viewers emailed asking what happened in Asia.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ NQ High Resistance Liquidity Conditions Tape Reading \ October 07, 2024
head: High / Low Resistance Liquidity Run Conditions  (aliases: "high resistance liquidity run", "low resistance liquidity run")
body:
- **Kind:** definition | rule (market-condition filter)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Ask yourself early in the session which condition delivery is in. He asks the viewers explicitly "are we in low resistance liquidity run conditions or high resistance," and answers: high resistance, "that's why it's [so] deliberate" (slow/choppy).
  - Diagnostic he gives: "are you seeing fair value gaps spending a lot of time inside them?" If price keeps spending time inside FVGs / inefficiencies, you are in high resistance.
  - High resistance means: lack of precision; moves are deferred; retracements are deeper; price runs pull back "real deep each time"; targets (PD arrays) are not delivered to as precisely. It is described as uncomfortable, especially when building larger positions.
  - Low resistance means: easy to time, easy to frame low risk, easy to find low-hanging objectives for partials and ultimate targets; price "goes where you want it to go"; smooth run to the target, then you go to the sidelines and wait for the next setup. It rewards patience and goes to targets "almost near effortlessly."
  - You can trade high resistance conditions, but expect many more stop-outs, frustration and anxiety in and during the trade.
  - Just because you see a setup does not make it high probability; in high resistance "nothing in here is high probability." The danger is looking back afterwards and thinking "I wish I'd done this."
  - He refers to this as a concept "I shared with you last week" (prior video in the series), and notes that knowing it lets you sit on your hands.
  - Observation that carries forward: if the morning session is high resistance and unclear, the lunch macro and afternoon session should be cleaner (setups easier to identify).
- **How to identify:** (1) FVGs/inefficiencies are being traded inside for long stretches rather than displaced away from; (2) price is range-bound and "disorganized" after the open; (3) retracements are deep and not precise; (4) no clean displacement leaving fresh FVGs.
- **How to use:** If high resistance: be slow to act, do not force the A+ model, expect the textbook return-to-PD-array entry NOT to come, and consider framing a different reference (here, an inefficiency that price was likely to be drawn to). If low resistance: take the clean model (see below) and target quickly.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Monday 7 Oct 2024, 9:30–10:30 ET. Price chops around the opening range gap area and the first presented FVG without displacing; the mid-gap is not reached within the first 30 minutes. ICT labels it high resistance at [0:51:04] and says that is why nothing "perfect" developed.
- **Timestamps:**
  - [0:51:04](https://youtu.be/DzJpkxI057g?t=3064) — asks viewers to classify delivery; high resistance diagnosed ("FVGs spending a lot of time inside them").
  - [0:52:42](https://youtu.be/DzJpkxI057g?t=3162) — contrast with low resistance: easy to time, easy low-risk framing, fewer stop-outs.
  - [0:56:55](https://youtu.be/DzJpkxI057g?t=3415) — high resistance pulls back deep each time; "not a fun market"; low resistance feels effortless.
  - [1:00:09](https://youtu.be/DzJpkxI057g?t=3609) — absence of precision means PD arrays are not delivered to as perfectly.
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** This is the practical filter that sits above the entry model: the same setup definition is valid in both conditions, but its probability and precision are not. He frames it as what he teaches "my son" and addresses a student, "Caleb", throughout (a teaching device, not a separate rule).
