head: Large-range day open near the low (bullish) + session Power of 3  (aliases: "open is the low of the day", "buy below the opening price", "Power of 3 / AMD", "Judas swing")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - On a bullish large-range day, the open is near the low of the daily range, in the lower quarter of the day's range (an observation he got from Larry Williams' material).
  - He maps a daily candle's open, high, low and close onto sessions. Manipulation is the drop below the opening price (Judas swing). Accumulation happens around and just above the open. Price may or may not come back to touch the open again. Distribution is the profit run to the DOL or a higher-timeframe PD array.
  - His own workaround for buying below the open was to use time: the day starts at midnight, so take the midnight open, let price drop below it, and buy there. In the 1990s he waited for a bullish divergence on the stochastic and a MACD histogram as his filter (not a current teaching).
  - Williams' own method (add about 20% of the average range of the last several days to the open, then buy) hurt ICT; he says it was drawdown he could not weather, not that it fails.
- **How to use:** on days expected to be large and bullish, look for longs below the midnight open (or session open) where smart money accumulates. Bearish days would be the mirror (open near the high).
- **Example in this video:** Fri 10/25 midnight open on NQ. Price dropped under it (the tail/low of the day), traded back up through it, and accumulated around it. The 9:30 morning session open was also the low of the session so far.
- **Timestamps:** [0:21:10](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1270) open in the lower quarter; [0:21:58](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1318) session Power of 3; [0:24:28](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1468) Williams' admitted weakness; [0:26:04](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1564) midnight open idea; [0:27:37](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1657) buy below the open.
- **Nuance / caveats:** the 1990s stochastic/MACD filter is storytelling about his past, not a rule he gives now.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How ICT Picks Winning FVG's & Orderblocks \ October 25, 2024
head: Low-resistance vs high-resistance liquidity runs  (aliases: "high/low resistance liquidity run conditions", "fuzzy price action")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - **Low-resistance run:** little give and take. Price goes straight to a PD array and "gone in 30 seconds". Down-close candles (in a bullish run) support price higher when price returns to them, and inefficiencies (FVGs) are left partly open instead of being fully closed. Retracements are shallow. Large-range days are about 90% low-resistance.
  - **High-resistance run:** lots of back-and-forth, overlapping ranges, every fair value gap gets closed in, and price spends a lot of time inside inefficiencies. That is the tell that you are in high resistance. Thursday was an example, visible on the 15m, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 minute and sub-minute charts. It can blow accounts (combines) or tilt you.
  - Write the two characteristic lists in your daily journal and have them in front of you at the start of each day.
- **How to use:**
  - **Low resistance:** pay at or below the PD arrays that will hold. Keep stops very tight (he was comfortable adding as price neared his stop). Do not rush partials. Manage with the stop and not with early partials.
  - **High resistance:** don't run the stop to breakeven quickly (let it move) or don't trade. It is the environment where a fast-trailed stop gets hit, and he treats the days as ones to avoid or trade lightly.
- **Example in this video:** Thursday 10/24 as high resistance and Friday 10/25 as low resistance. On Friday, the OB at the lower quadrant held, the FVG that formed left its lower portion open (a breakaway gap), and price ran in a straight line to the NWOG and the 15m smooth highs.
- **Timestamps:** [0:42:58](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=2578) large range days deliver as low-resistance runs; [0:51:44](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=3104) Thursday as high resistance; [1:19:04](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4744) low-resistance characteristics; [1:19:53](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4793) high-resistance characteristics; [1:25:28](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5128) "signatures of a low-resistance run".
- **Nuance / caveats:** he says nobody else teaches this and he did not know he needed it earlier in his career. The stop advice in the high-resistance context is loosely worded in the captions (lines around 1:19:53 and 1:42:29). See the stop-management concept below.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How ICT Picks Winning FVG's & Orderblocks \ October 25, 2024
head: Dealing range grading: equilibrium and quadrants  (aliases: "grading a price swing", "lower/upper quadrant", "the quadrant", "PD array matrix premium/discount")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement (the lecture's centerpiece)
- **What ICT says:**
  - Define a dealing range from the high of the retracement leg down to the low reference point. He is explicit that this is NOT quarters theory and NOT "quarterly theory". It is grading an actual dealing range or an actual price run he expects to enter or has entered.
  - Equilibrium is the halfway point. Ideal long entries ("lowest risk, highest R multiple yield") are at or below equilibrium. Pyramiding (adding) is limited to equilibrium: adding above it is "tossing good money after" a position.
  - The range is also split into upper and lower quadrants (the 75% and 25% levels, as spoken). When bullish, the PD array he chooses (OB or FVG) must be at or below the lower quadrant, or he will not use it. He says "it must be at or below the quadrant" with emphasis.
  - The measuring tool also shows extensions. He says these (based on the opening range gap and standard deviations) are being held for his book. He customises the fib levels (rounds the OTE level; exact numbers in the captions are unclear, see caveat).
  - He says he can predict where future PD arrays will form by doing this. He claims to know where fair value gaps must form before the dealing range even forms.
- **How to identify:**
  1. Find the swing high in the move and the pre-market/consolidation low reference. Use the bodies of the candles and ignore wicks that were stop runs ("doing damage"). For example, he disregarded a wick spike high as "a little bump" and drew the range from the bodies.
  2. Confirm a shift in market structure bullish (a break of a swing high, defined below) so that retracements into the inefficiency are treated as discount arrays.
  3. Mark equilibrium (50%) and the lower quadrant (25% from the low).
  4. Judge each FVG/OB: is it at or below the lower quadrant (primary), or around equilibrium (secondary)? A PD array whose body is mostly above the quadrant is skipped.
- **How to use:**
  - Primary entries: at or below the lower quadrant.
  - Pyramid: up to equilibrium only.
  - Anything above equilibrium (or the stated cut-off) is used for management purposes, not new entries. At [1:23:51] he says "you're trading ends on the entries here or less" and anything above that is for management.
  - For a short (not shown), invert.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 8:30 AM ET 10/25, range from the highest high of the retracement leg down to the pre-market low-body reference (15-second chart used to define the range). The OB and FVG at 8:30 were at or below the lower quadrant; a later FVG near equilibrium was handled differently (see CE-at-EQ entry below).
- **Timestamps:** [1:05:25](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=3925) dealing range and ignoring the stop-run wick; [1:07:01](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4021) "grading a price swing, not quarters theory"; [1:07:49](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4069) equilibrium and where best entries and pyramiding are; [1:09:28](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4168) quadrants and extensions; [1:11:50](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4310) "must be at or below the quadrant".
- **Nuance / caveats:**
  - At [1:08:41] and [1:09:28] he adjusts the OTE level (spoken "change the 0.75 to 0.725 or 0.79 because I round it" and "I don't do the 78% or 79%", caption unclear).
  - A tension in his own logic: he rejects the later FVG because its body is mostly above the lower quadrant, then says the same area is still tradable when its CE overlaps equilibrium (next concepts). Read it as: lower-quadrant = primary entry; EQ-or-below = adds and secondary entries.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How ICT Picks Winning FVG's & Orderblocks \ October 25, 2024
head: How ICT picks the FVG / order block (selection checklist)  (aliases: "why that fair value gap", "authorship / fingerprints", "PD arrays the algorithm goes back to")
body:
- **Kind:** rule (the answer the title promises)
- **What ICT says:** it is not "any down-close candle" (order block) and not "any 3-candle gap with a one-candle separation" (FVG). Someone teaching it that way is hurting students. He claims no one else teaches this correctly. A tradable PD array has to pass several filters at once:
  1. Bias/narrative is set and there is a DOL (e.g. smooth highs). In a bullish bias only bullish OBs, bullish breakers, bullish FVGs, and bearish-looking FVGs broken and inverted (iFVG) count.
  2. Time: a macro (8:30 for example) with the algorithm "spooling", and awareness of the economic calendar (here split 8:30/10:00 news) and day of week.
  3. The market first trades into a discount PD array and then must displace: it breaks a short-term/swing high (MSS) and leaves a BISI-type FVG or OB. "Let the algorithm tip its hand" and do not just buy because price is in the zone.
  4. The array must be at or below the lower quadrant of the dealing range (bullish).
  5. For OBs, take the lowest down-close candle's body (not wicks). Two consecutive down closes count as one range. Use the order block mean threshold.
  6. The FVG should be one that leaves a portion open (a breakaway gap) in low-resistance conditions.
- **How to use:** for the shortlist the algorithm "will go right back to". He does not "trade zones" and he does not trade supply and demand: "I don't trade zones". He wants a PD array reference point and not a zone.
- **Example in this video:** at 8:30 on 10/25 price traded into the discount array, displaced up through a short-term high (a 3-candle swing with lower highs each side), then broke a second swing high, leaving an FVG/OB at or below the lower quadrant. A later FVG formed at displacement near equilibrium and was NOT used for the primary entry because most of its body was above the lower quadrant.
- **Timestamps:** [1:03:49](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=3829) it's not every down-close candle or every 3-candle gap; [1:10:14](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4214) only bullish PD arrays when bullish; [1:13:27](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4407) "which OB and FVG I trade is the one the algorithm uses"; [1:18:15](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4695) why a nearby FVG was skipped.
- **Nuance / caveats:** he says he is not giving "the complete treatment to a fair value gap" here, only enough to "divide the waters". He expects more detail in a book.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How ICT Picks Winning FVG's & Orderblocks \ October 25, 2024
head: Market structure shift used to qualify the array  (aliases: "shift in market structure", "short-term high", "swing high", "displacement")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / entry condition
- **What ICT says:**
  - A short-term/swing high is a candle whose high is lower than the candle before and has a lower high on the next candle (a 3-candle formation).
  - When price breaks above it (candle by candle), that is a market structure shift to bullish. Displacement higher then leaves the inefficiency.
  - He says the setup is very similar to Model 2022 and tells viewers to rewatch those videos.
  - With two swing highs both broken, the break "qualifies it even further". Any retracement into the resulting inefficiency is a discount array.
  - If bullish and you want the stricter version, use the closer short-term high, or the higher one if you want to be really sure.
- **Example in this video:** 8:30 AM 10/25 NQ: price trades above a swing high (shift), displaces higher, then breaks a second swing high, leaving the BISI/OB.
- **Timestamps:** [1:06:12](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=3972) shift defined with candle highs; [1:11:03](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4263) two swing highs broken, displacement.
- **Nuance / caveats:** at [0:40:31] for Model 2022 with two inefficiencies in a discount (the two FVGs in the 7–8 AM area), he says to trade it but the stop has to respect the second fair value gap. He calls two PD arrays in agreement "conflation" (jokes he made the word up; he means confluence).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How ICT Picks Winning FVG's & Orderblocks \ October 25, 2024
head: Order block body, mean threshold and entry rule  (aliases: "bullish order block", "mean threshold", "down close candle supports price")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / refinement / entry rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Bullish OB = the down-close candle (or consecutive down closes as one range). Use the body (the lowest down close with a body), not the wick.
  - Half of an OB body is the mean threshold (MT). The term is for candle bodies. "Consequent encroachment" is the term for gaps, inefficiencies and wicks.
  - In the live example, price reacted at the OB's mean threshold. The low of the very next candle matched the MT price to the tick (spoken "42.75", 20,4x2.75, caption unclear; one tick of precision was the point).
  - He wants price to use the MT or higher (up to the OB's high) to trade down into the block and repel. He would never enter expecting a trade to the low of the candle, "I would never enter on a trade like that", even though it sometimes does that.
  - Wicks or tails below the candle body are inside-OB / inside-FVG formations and are expected when order flow is bullish. That is why his entries are on the lowest candle or one candle before or after it (bullish).
- **How to use:** entry at or near the OB mean threshold; very tight stops. Can add when price approaches the stop in a low-resistance run.
- **Example in this video:** the 8:30 OB (two consecutive down closes) near the lower quadrant: price delivers to the MT, reacts to the tick, and rallies into a volume imbalance.
- **Timestamps:** [1:14:15](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4455) OB body, MT vs CE; [1:15:03](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4503) "that's perfection to the tick"; [1:27:50](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5270) never enter assuming the low of the candle; [1:28:40](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5320) entries on the lowest candle or one before/after.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How ICT Picks Winning FVG's & Orderblocks \ October 25, 2024
head: Institutional Order Flow Entry Drill (IOFED)  (aliases: "institutional order entry drill", "institutional orderflow entry drill")
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - IOFED is an entry model where you expect a fair value gap to be traded into but not fully closed. You expect only a partial entry into the gap (the shaded area).
  - Entry is a very specific price and not a zone: the FVG's upper edge, with an extra tick (spoken "462 and 3/4 plus one tick"), as a limit order.
  - It suits low-resistance run conditions, where an FVG is expected to stay partly open. In such a run, a breakaway gap leaves the lower part open.
  - He ties it to the gap forming below the upper quadrant (the entry area at or below the quadrant, "anything above is for management").
  - The stop can sit just below the high of the lowest candle of the pattern (the bottom of the gap), because in a low-resistance run price should not trade down to the bottom.
  - He says in this environment it is "Flawless" and his stops are ultra tight.
- **How to identify:** in a bullish low-resistance run, a fresh FVG (leaves a gap behind the displacement) at or below the quadrant, with an order block (down-close candles) beneath that should support price.
- **How to use:** limit buy at the FVG's upper edge plus one tick (specific price, not a zone); stop just below the gap's bottom/candle high; add as price nears the stop if conditions remain low resistance.
- **Example in this video:** NQ 10/25 pre-market after the 8:30 displacement: an FVG formed whose upper edge was about 20,462.75 (spoken "462 and 3/4", the thousands digit is inferred from context). The limit at 20,462.75 + 1 tick (about 20,463.00) was the entry. Price traded into the gap partially and left the lower part open as the run went on.
- **Timestamps:** [1:21:29](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4889) IOFED named; [1:22:16](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4936) price plus one tick; [1:24:41](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5081) the partial-open idea; [1:26:14](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5174) stop placement.
- **Nuance / caveats:** caption unclear in places on exactly which edge the "plus one tick" applies to and where the stop sits. The stop description reads as "just below this candlestick's high" (the bottom edge of the gap). He also says other models are possible, but he follows his protocol, "stay on the right side of the road".

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ How ICT Picks Winning FVG's & Orderblocks \ October 25, 2024
head: Consequent encroachment of an FVG overlapping equilibrium  (aliases: "CE at EQ", "convergence of two midpoints")
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - A later displacement left an FVG whose CE (its 50%) overlapped the dealing range's equilibrium. That is a convergence of two midpoints.
  - When bullish you can place a limit buy right at the midpoint (CE), trusting the lower half stays open (a breakaway gap). It is a tradable FVG and a good candidate for the institutional entry drill, with only a partial fill expected into the shaded area.
  - It is also the boundary for pyramiding: all adds at or below equilibrium.
- **Example in this video:** after the OB entry, price rallied through the lower quadrant to equilibrium and meandered, then displaced again, leaving an FVG straddling EQ. The earlier question "why not this FVG?" was answered by: most of the body was above the lower quadrant, so it is not a primary entry. Later he says it is still usable because its CE overlaps EQ.
- **Timestamps:** [1:17:26](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4646) price returns to equilibrium and displaces again; [1:20:40](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4840) limit at the CE; [1:21:29](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4889) convergence of two midpoints.
- **Nuance / caveats:** this slightly softens the lower-quadrant rule. Treat lower-quadrant as the main entry and CE-at-EQ as a secondary or add entry (see dealing range concept).

head: Pre-market (7:00–9:00 AM) positioning on expected large-range days  (aliases: "trade before 9:30", "pre-market entries", "pyramid at lunch")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / entry model context
- **What ICT says:**
  - When a large-range day or a one-sided day is likely, he elects to trade pre-market and take no entries after the 9:30 bell. He is typically in between 7:00 and 9:00, holds, has taken multiple partials, and rides the opening-range expansion (9:30–10:00).
  - If the 10:00 AM Silver Bullet then offers a longer hold, he holds through lunch and can pyramid in the lunch macro retracement (re-adding what he took off, plus more, because of unrealized profit).
  - Not every pre-market should be traded. Many days are quiet pre-market and then easy at 9:30. He lists the coalescing factors that justified it that day: inside day, bullish DOL, Friday, split news at 8:30 and 10:00, large opening gap.
  - The Silver Bullet at 10:00 is a baseline/training-wheels model ("pushing my son Cameron into a mold"). There is a silver-bullet-style window every hour and there is more than one way to use his concepts.
- **Example in this video:** midnight open on 10/25; 3:00 AM (London) displacement through a short-term high, a drop to an OB without taking the low, rally again; volume imbalance and inversion FVG clustered; 3:30 AM rips higher; 4:00 AM trades back down into the middle of the consolidation (discount, equilibrium); 7:00 AM AM session starts and price runs the buy side then returns to two inefficiencies (Model 2022 with the stop respecting the second FVG); 8:30 AM macro entry at the lower-quadrant array (see above).
- **Timestamps:** [0:37:15](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=2235) 3:00 AM displacement; [0:40:31](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=2431) 2-FVG Model 2022 note; [0:54:11](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=3251) why trade before 9:30; [0:55:00](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=3300) Silver Bullet as a baseline; [0:59:48](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=3588) in by 7–9, partials, pyramid at lunch.
- **Nuance / caveats:** the 10:00 Silver Bullet is described as one option, not the only way. He warns not to take a Silver Bullet at 10:00 until a few minutes after a 10:00 medium-impact news release (first 5–10, worst case 15 minutes).

head: Macros (timing) as stated in this lecture  (aliases: "macro", "8:30 macro", "lunch macro")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - 8:30 AM ET is "the only 30-minute delineator for a macro". At 8:30 the algorithm starts spooling whether or not there is news. If price does not start running, wait for the 9:30 open.
  - Every other hourly macro runs from 10 minutes before the top of the hour to 10 minutes after it (e.g. :50–:10). The last-hour macro is 3:15–3:45 PM.
  - A pre-market macro around 8:50–9:10 is implied (spoken "8 or 10 minutes after 8", caption unclear).
  - The 10:30–11:30 hour typically forms a higher low of the morning session (in a bullish day) and invites the lunch macro.
  - **Lunch macro = 11:30 AM–1:30 PM ET (New York).** At about 10:30 the algorithm computes the range high and low, defines the midpoint as equilibrium, and below equilibrium looks for sell-side liquidity. The lunch macro "runs on those that are profitable". Two outcomes: it takes the first sell-side pool and then consolidates (no new high or low the rest of the day), or it trades down into trailing stops, triggers the sell side, then accumulates and runs higher into the close of the week.
- **Timestamps:** [0:31:38](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1898) lunch 11:30–1:30; [0:32:28](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1948) lunch macro mechanics; [1:12:38](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=4358) macro list; [1:35:11](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5711) lunch high/low as a draw.
- **Nuance / caveats:** the lunch-macro description was hypothetical ("play devil's advocate"); it was 10:30 AM on the live stream. For lunch he also lists the lunch range's high and low as liquidity targets.

head: Day of week (Friday) and split economic calendar  (aliases: "split delivery", "manual intervention", "day-of-week phenomenon", "last trading day of the week")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / context
- **What ICT says:**
  - On Friday (last trading day), there is little time, so price rushes at the open to the liquidity. The algorithm "doesn't want to offer the opportunity" for stops to stay. They also do not want positions held over the weekend with gap risk, so they "intervene manually". The 9:30 rip looks like FOMC and is "not algorithmic, that's intervention".
  - A 70% likelihood that the opening gap has its half repriced to in the first 30 minutes is thrown out on a day like this ("not today"). Do not look for the opening gap to fill; wait for it to run to unfinished business. He expected little or no retracement into the opening range gap.
  - Split news (8:30 and 10:00): can create a catapult or whiplash. The algorithm uses the first data as the fake run and the later one as the real run (like FOMC at 2:00 versus the 2:30 press conference). He can filter this out when the bias is already clear. That Friday had core durable goods (8:30, medium impact) and revised consumer sentiment (10:00, medium impact).
  - News drivers are used as a "smoke screen" to mask real intentions.
- **Example in this video:** at 9:00–9:30 price traded up to just short of the NWOG's CE, dropped, rallied to the NWOG high, dropped again to random levels and CE, and then at 9:30 "manual intervention" ripped to the buy stops. He hit the 20,495 target he had mentioned the day before.
- **Timestamps:** [0:20:22](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1222) algo rushes at the open; [0:28:23](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1703) split news explained; [0:29:59](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=1799) "not today" for the gap fill; [1:40:54](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=6054) Friday speed and gap risk over the weekend; [1:41:41](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=6101) "doesn't this look like FOMC".
- **Nuance / caveats:** the "70%" figure refers to opening gap midpoint behaviour (RTH or opening range gap). The captions do not say which gap, so treat as unclear.

head: New Week Opening Gap (NWOG) and consequent encroachment  (aliases: "NWOG", "new week opening gap CE")
body:
- **Kind:** definition / example
- **What ICT says:** NWOG is the difference between Friday's 4:59 PM ET close and Sunday's 6:00 PM ET open. The halfway point (dotted line) is its consequent encroachment. Keep only the current NWOG on the chart; you do not need every NWOG or NDOG ("kitchen sink"). He says he codified the use of the gap and did not invent Sunday's gap. A draw on liquidity can be a session high or low (previous PM session, London, Asian), a single high, or an opening gap level.

A short-side Model 2022 (shift in market structure, FVG, retrace up into premium/OTE) was delivered back down to the CE (three times) and then at 9:30 "all hell breaks loose" upward through the buy stops (this pre-9:30 sequence is described quickly and the captions are unclear in spots).

head: Stop and partial management in low-resistance runs  (aliases: "stops and partials", "walk away", "banking 80%")
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - In low-resistance run days, do not rush partials. Move the stop to a reasonable level where you can step away, have limit orders at the targets, and go for a walk or workout for 20–30 minutes. You get rewarded for staying in longer. Watching a 15-second chart will scare you out.
  - Trailing the stop to each swing is a high-resistance habit. In high resistance it gets you stopped out (with the wording unclear around [1:42:29]). Relaxing the stop in low resistance avoids premature stop-outs.
  - After the run: a morning-session trader is done. A position/swing trader should have about 80% of the position off by the end of the run; if not "you're doing it wrong". Afterwards see if it wants to continue into the afternoon.
  - If you are flat and were not in the trade, it is fine to sit still and call the week done.
- **Example in this video:** the price stopped dead at the NWOG CE twice, did not take the sell side, and ran to the buy-side targets.
- **Timestamps:** [1:36:46](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5806) 80% banked; [1:39:13](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=5953) don't rush partials, manage by the stop; [1:40:02](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=6002) walk away; [1:42:29](https://youtu.be/svYZKOrWPRo?t=6149) trailing stops differ by regime.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ High Resistance & Low Resistance Conditions \ October 28, 2024
head: High Resistance Liquidity Run Conditions  (aliases ICT uses: high resistance conditions, "harder delivery", fuzzy / scribbling back-and-forth price action)
body:
- **Kind:** definition (new framing; he says no other school teaches it this way)
- **What ICT says:**
  - It is a delivery type, not a direction. You can know the draw (where price will go) and still have a market that will not deliver to it in "a single one-way ticket ride".
  - Price will usually still reach the objective eventually, but through retracements, consolidation, deep pullbacks, and repeated re-tests. Example: the NWOG high target was first touched at 11:43 after hours of sideways price.
  - Inefficiencies (open FVGs) are "far and few between"; the market spends its time overlapping.
  - It is not Seek & Destroy (the aggressive form of this), although he says that day could have become one.
  - It is "not impossible to trade" but much harder for a new trader; he steers beginners (his sons, new students) away from it and tells them to cut leverage and frequency.
- **How to identify:**
  - Pre-session: Monday and no medium/high-impact news at 8:30 or between 9:30 and 10:30 on the economic calendar.
  - In price: each subsequent candle shares/overlaps the previous candle's range by "at least half" or the majority. He calls this the simplest, clearest visual definition.
  - Also: deep retracements, lots of consolidation, reclaimed FVGs/order blocks (see below).
- **How to use:**
  - Do not use maximum leverage; start with one contract (a multi-contract trader still uses one here).
  - Use the maximum stop on an FVG entry (candle 1 high + 1 tick, see stop concept below).
  - Aim only at the first, easiest objective; a draw like the NWOG high does not need to be reached.
  - Do not trail the stop (a "death knell").
  - Expect "heat" (drawdown) after entry and do not bail on it unless the model is invalidated.
  - Best approach: trade the pre-market session instead (see pre-market concept), or accept the day is a no-trade/low-effort day.
  - If the setup does not form in the first 30 minutes, toss the idea.
- **Example in this video:** NQ December contract, 1m (framed on 15s), Mon Oct 28 2024, no news. See "Caleb's FVG entry model" and "Opening Range Gap CE" for the step-by-step; the whole 9:30 to about 11:43 delivery overlaps candle-on-candle and first reaches NWOG high at 11:43.
- **Timestamps:** [1:35:59](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=5759) high-resistance defined by overlapping candles · [1:54:28](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=6868) "likely to overlap the previous candle's range" · [2:00:12](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=7212) first touch of NWOG high at 11:43 · [2:02:36](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=7356) clearest visual representation
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** A news driver does NOT guarantee low resistance, and no news does not guarantee high resistance; they are probabilities ("the climate they exist in"). Builds on his previous week's lectures (last week covered Monday/no-news = pre-market trading; first 20 min of this video recaps it).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ High Resistance & Low Resistance Conditions \ October 28, 2024
head: Low Resistance Liquidity Run Conditions  (aliases: low resistance runs, easy trading, "speed is the mechanism", one-shot run to target)
body:
- **Kind:** definition
- **What ICT says:**
  - Very fast runs to obvious targets, with an obvious stop level and an obvious draw. The market behaves "like it's in a hurry".
  - Speed is the mechanism of delivery; price books quickly in one direction. He types "speed and distance / speed and magnitude" as the signature in his recordings.
  - Candles are well separated (little shared range between consecutive candles), big displacement candles, lots of open inefficiencies, no meaningful retracement or consolidation.
  - In these conditions the trade quickly runs in your favor, you can take a partial or cover costs fast, and then manage (trail) the stop. He says he cannot do his "Mr. Wizard" stop management in high resistance to the same degree.
  - Not an every-day condition. That is why you will not trade every day and that is fine.
  - If you are on the right side, the market does not dilly-dally; if you are on the wrong side it is devastating.
- **How to identify (his "recipe", [2:29:00](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=8940)):**
  1. A medium- or high-impact news driver at 8:30 or inside the first hour of the 9:30 session.
  2. Not a Monday.
  3. Very clear draws on liquidity (clustered new week and/or new day opening gaps).
  4. An opening range gap of at least 45 handles (NQ), preferably 75 or more.
  - Not guaranteed, but "the probabilities are off the charts" and he is "all over that day like white on rice".
- **How to use:** trade larger/with confidence only here; simple targets hit quickly; take partials or cover costs and then trail the stop. He wants trades that do not sit in spread or initial drawdown.
- **Example in this video:** none shown live; contrast example is the "big, quick delivery and goes lower" versus the Oct 28 overlapping candles ([1:36:46](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=5806)).
- **Timestamps:** [0:04:33](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=273) first definition · [1:36:46](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=5806) low vs high contrast · [2:09:49](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=7789) why news = low resistance · [2:29:00](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=8940) recipe and thresholds
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** the "45 handles minimum, 75 preferred" opening range gap figure is stated here as a condition for the easy-day recipe. The 45-handle number is stated in passing and the transcript does not make clear which instrument it applies to beyond NQ context (caption unclear on instrument).

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ High Resistance & Low Resistance Conditions \ October 28, 2024
head: Economic calendar as resistance predictor / news driver "smoke screen"  (aliases: news driver, medium/high impact news)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Check the calendar on the weekend and plan the week. Look for medium- or high-impact releases at 8:30 or between 9:30 and 10:30 (first hour of the session).
  - News present means the climate for low resistance: the data is a smoke screen, not the cause of the move. Algorithms use the release to run a Judas-style manipulation, put retail on the wrong side in the first 30 minutes, set the session high/low, and then move fast so trapped traders cannot exit.
  - News absent (especially Monday) means higher likelihood of high resistance. The day could consolidate, or become one-sided with a large Judas swing, an "outlier" profile you might miss.
  - Reports never explain the market's direction. If price does the opposite of the headline, the excuse is always "it priced it in", which nobody said beforehand.
- **How to use:** calendar empty and Monday: do the work pre-market (7:00 to 9:30 ET). News present and not Monday: expect the recipe for low resistance and be aggressive there.
- **Timestamps:** [0:07:48](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=468) absence of news this Monday · [0:17:24](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=1044) smoke screen · [2:08:14](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=7694) news ≈ low resistance, with the "not guaranteed" caveat · [2:10:36](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=7836) retail trapped, price "falls out of bed"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he explicitly says news is "synonymous" with low resistance climate but "does not mean" you will automatically get it.

head: Monday and Non-Farm Payroll week rules  (aliases: Monday rules; NFP week)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - He denies the rumor that "ICT never trades Mondays". He has many rules for Mondays; Monday is "amateur hour" (traders who sat on their hands all weekend come out of the gate).
  - NFP week rule: trade Monday of NFP week (cleanest action). Be done trading by Wednesday morning AM session. Rarely trade Thursday or NFP Friday unless something is extremely obvious. Tuesday and Wednesday he does nothing if Monday made money; at worst a London session trade.
  - Non-NFP weeks: first check whether the calendar has a high/medium news driver at 8:30 or after the 9:30 open. If none and it is Monday, trade only the pre-market and avoid the 9:30 open.
- **How to use:** a hard discipline rule: "if these conditions are met, I know I will be punished with harder delivery". It does not mean targets will not trade, only that delivery is high resistance.
- **Example in this video:** Mon Oct 28 2024: no news at 8:30 or 9:30 to 10:30, so pre-market short only; he posted a live regulated-broker trade on X that morning hitting target (premarket short from clustering of previous-week gaps; he did not care about long after 9:30, Silver Bullet, OTE or 2022 model).

head: Pre-market session (7:00 to 9:30 ET), AM opening session, lunch reversal  (aliases: premarket, "hit and run")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / time window
- **What ICT says:**
  - Anything before the 9:30 bell is "pre-market" (London and the prior night's Asia included). The specific window he likes is 7:00 to 9:30 ET ("really good operating hours"; professionals kept it to themselves).
  - The "AM opening session" is 9:30 through lunch, defined by the opening bell.
  - Lunch hour is generally a reversal or consolidation of whatever was profitable in the morning (full reversal or large retracement); then from 1:30 PM ET the morning's direction tends to resume.
  - On a no-news Monday the pre-market gives lower risk and is more likely low resistance; the AM opening session is higher resistance.
- **How to use:** pick one window per day, get paid, and leave; he did not care about anything after 9:30 that Monday. Time-based models (e.g. a setup that forms between 10:00 and 11:00 and if it does not form you turn the charts off) create accountability.

head: Clustered New Week / New Day Opening Gaps as draw on liquidity  (aliases: NWOG/NDOG clusters, "black hole", "Event Horizon on steroids")
body:
- **Kind:** rule / refinement
- **What ICT says:**
  - NWOG = Friday settlement to Sunday 6 PM open. Compare the current NWOG with the last five NWOGs (or last five NDOGs). If any two overlap (even one level of one gap encroaching the range of another is enough), that is a "cluster".
  - Open (unfilled) overlapping gaps act as a magnet: no buying/selling occurred there, "natural value areas". More overlapping gaps mean a higher probability price is repriced there. Whether a gap has been traded through/filled in the past "matters not".
  - The cluster is a draw (right direction), not a requirement to reach it ("just a magnet draw on price"; the stadium-directions analogy: get close to the stadium and then find the signs).
  - A trader shorting from above takes the highest level of the cluster first (NWOG high); for longs, the lowest level.
  - Works as a session bias for any school of thought, and no moving averages, VWAP or HTF top-down needed.
- **How to identify:** current NWOG high / CE / low plus the prior week's NWOG sitting inside the current one (here in its lower half); price is above both.
- **How to use:** use as bias/draw; first (nearest) level is the target for a beginner. Combine with the opening-range-gap fill (below) for a 3/4 or full gap closure or more.
- **Example in this video:** Oct 28 2024 NQ: current NWOG is large (Friday settle to Sunday 6 PM open); last week's NWOG (purple) sits in its lower half. Price hit neither the current NWOG CE nor the low that day; the NWOG high was first touched at 11:43. His X post that morning called the draw down into this area.
- **Timestamps:** [0:22:13](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=1333) no news so move comes clean pre-market · [0:23:49](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=1429) layout of the two NWOGs · [0:39:03](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=2343) how to choose which gap / any two overlapping · [0:39:50](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=2390) black-hole effect · [1:29:34](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=5374) clustering defined

head: Low-hanging-fruit objective ("Caleb" beginner model)  (aliases: lowest threshold objective, hit-and-run, surgical strikes, enough is enough)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model / management rule (applied to this day)
- **What ICT says:**
  - The teaching model for his son: short bias from a cluster; take the first profitable exit, i.e. the first NWOG level reached plus a spread of one or two ticks, and get out. Do not hold for NWOG CE, NWOG low, or last week's gap CE/high.
  - Fixed daily threshold such as 10, 15 or 20 handles NQ, or 5 to 10 handles ES; "easy" objective in dollars like $100 to $250/day (he says a beginner should not exceed $250; honestly 100 to 200).
  - May need two trades; if trading off a 15-minute framework, one trade. Chart use: 15s, 30s, 45s or 1m entry charts reacting off a higher timeframe array; he says 15 minutes is the "high timeframe for day trading", no need for daily/hourly.
  - 90% of the time his own early exits had hit one or two PD arrays in his favor before the actual target (Terminus) so he made those his objective. The 90% is about trades executed on this basis, not a 90% win rate.
  - Terminus = best-case target; not needed for the model to pay.
  - Aim of the approach: higher strike rate, lower stress, build a consistent track record and rule-following, then graduate to holding for half-gap, NWOG threshold, and so on.
- **How to use:** stand aside on days without low resistance; do not chase momentum; do not use leverage to scale up.
- **Example in this video:** short; NWOG high is the highest cluster level, SIBI/FVG entry, exit below the prior low (see entry model).

head: Opening Range Gap consequent encroachment fill (70% in first 30 minutes)  (aliases: RTH opening gap half-gap, half-gap fill)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / statistic claim
- **What ICT says:**
  - Opening range gap = previous day settlement to 9:30 ET first print. Its CE (half) is traded to about 70% of the time in the first 30 minutes ("seven times out of ten").
  - A minute or two before 9:30 you can estimate where the mid-gap will be.
  - If gap-CE fill is also in the direction of a cluster of NWOG/NDOG, expect 3/4 gap, full closure, or more (the NWOG is beyond). You do not just stop at CE: "there is a draw still lower".
  - If it misses in the first 30 minutes but fills later (e.g. 11:00) that is still fine, though less valuable on a high-resistance day.
- **Example in this video:** Oct 28 NQ opened with a big gap up from Friday settlement; price opened inside an inversion FVG, traded down aggressively, and filled the half gap in 19 minutes (within the first 30), then did not reach the NWOG high until 11:43.

title: ICT 2024 Mentorship \ High Resistance & Low Resistance Conditions \ October 28, 2024
head: Caleb's FVG entry model and stop rule (short from a higher-timeframe inefficiency)  (aliases: FVG entry at the low of the gap, Silver-Bullet-like confirmation entry)
body:
- **Kind:** entry model
- **What ICT says:**
  - The PD array for this beginner is the fair value gap. Look for price to retrace into a 1-minute inefficiency (the higher-timeframe array here is a 1m SIBI), see displacement away, then use the first clean FVG on the lower timeframe (15s/30s/45s/1m).
  - A first FVG that forms in the 9:30 candle cannot be traded; you cannot enter on the first presented FVG until 9:31 or later. Here the usable FVG formed at about 9:37.
  - Check that candle bodies respect the SIBI low (bodies closing/staying below it), i.e. displacement.
  - Entry is taken as price trades one tick below the FVG's low (not mid-gap, not the high of the gap, no limit orders on wicks above the gap); caption unclear on the word he uses for limit entries on wicks ("Mohawks").
  - Stop: normally for a bearish FVG the low-risk stop is above candle 2 (the middle, gap-creating candle) high + 1 tick. But if price is close to the low of the reference SIBI, or in high-resistance conditions, use the maximum: candle 1's high + 1 tick, so you are inside the pink SIBI box rather than getting stopped on a retest.
  - One contract only on a day like this.
  - Expect heat: price may run in profit, then pull back above entry (but not to the stop), then break lower again.
- **How to identify:** (1) sell-side imbalance/buy-side inefficiency on 1m at the 9:30 open; (2) price rallies into it and overshoots slightly, trading into its upper part; (3) bodies respect/break below its low; (4) displacement leaves a clean FVG at or after 9:31; (5) retrace into FVG.
- **How to use:** short with the NWOG-high cluster as the directional bias; objective is a new low below the entry-leg low (sell-side); take it and leave.
- **Example in this video:** NQ, Mon Oct 28 2024, 15s/1m. Pre-market work traded up into old relative equal highs and a 9:00 high, then broke down aggressively at 9:30 on one large black 1m candle (that candle's range is the SIBI; on the 15s chart it takes two candles). Open sat inside an inversion FVG at a premium. Price rallied back up into the SIBI, slightly above it, then broke back below its low; displacement down left the first clean FVG at about 9:37. Price retraced up into that FVG (short entry one tick below FVG low), ran in profit, came back up above entry (stop sat above candle 1 high, inside the pink box, not hit), then broke lower, filled the opening range gap CE (about 9:49, 19 minutes in) and later (11:43) the NWOG high.
- **Timestamps:** [1:17:35](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=4655) the SIBI on the 9:30 candle · [1:35:12](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=5712) no first-minute FVG, need displacement · [1:38:20](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=5900) bodies respect SIBI low, first clean FVG · [1:47:16](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=6436) entry one tick below the gap low
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** he says he "covered in mentorship 2024" when to use the middle-candle versus candle-1 stop. The candle-1 stop is the maximum-risk option; the middle-candle stop is the low-risk default.

head: Stop-loss placement on an FVG entry (candle 2 vs candle 1)
body:
- **Kind:** refinement / rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - A fair value gap is always three candles: candle 1, candle 2 (the actual gap range, shares no space with candles 1 and 3), candle 3.
  - Low-risk stop for a short on a bearish FVG: high of candle 2 + 1 tick.
  - If price is very close to the low of the SIBI/reference range (a retest could reach it) or the day is high resistance, use candle 1's high + 1 tick (the "maximum").
  - Rationale: high-resistance days are likely to retrace into and above the gap, so a tight stop gets run even when the direction is right.
- **Timestamps:** [1:40:02](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=6002) choose candle 1 stop due to proximity to SIBI low · [1:40:50](https://youtu.be/3YfetuXVhOE?t=6050) three-candle definition and candle 2 stop

head: Trade management: do not trail in high resistance
body:

In his own trades he sometimes sets the stop to cover costs plus about $100 so the trade pays him for his time. Real management and tight trailing are for low-resistance. A recommended approach: if you get stopped out, you re-enter later rather than strangling price with a tight stop.

body:

head: Higher-timeframe bullish narrative and 25%-extension upside objective  (aliases: draw above November's high, upside objective 21580.25)
body:
- **Kind:** rule / example
- **What ICT says:**
  - Weekly NQ chart with November's high and low marked; there is an imbalance (a low through a candle's high) plus a volume imbalance on the chart, and buy side and sell side sitting at those areas before the open.
  - He favors a run higher and is "trying to avoid picking a top". If price keeps moving higher he expects a break of November's high, and one level to look for is 21580.25 from the retracement-leg-to-high extension (a quarter of the range above the high, which video 51 states explicitly as his rule of thumb).
  - He stays with the higher-timeframe bullish stance on stock indices until proven wrong by a breakdown; if the recent low (the 15-minute low marked) is lost "that changes things for the week".
  - He does not know the Sunday opening price ("no one knows that").
- **How to identify:** a range with a retracement low and a prior high; price near that high at the weekly close.
- **How to use:** if November's high is taken, target the extension level; ignore the minor wick/high on the way ("I'd like to see them completely ignore this wick").
- **Example in this video:** NQ December 2024 contract; objective 21580.25 above November's high.

title: NQ December 05, 2024 Seek & Destroy Review
head: One-quarter-of-the-broken-range extension as an upside objective  (aliases: rule of thumb, "easiest draw on liquidity", frame of reference for turtle soup)
body:
- **Kind:** rule
- **What ICT says:**
  - Once a range's high is taken out, look for an upside objective: simple, cut-and-dry draw on liquidity, or a frame of reference for a potential turtle soup.
  - His rule of thumb: one quarter of the previous range, projected beyond the broken high, is where he thinks markets can trade to. He says it is not based on anything in technical books, just something he has used over the years.
  - When the market is at all-time highs, you stay with going long until it proves otherwise.
  - The extension target does not need to be hit. Here price made a higher high but failed to reach it (the hourly high stopped just below 21580, at what the captions give as about 21567.25, caption unclear). He says it does not matter, and that it could rip through it later.
  - He told Sunday viewers "this is about as far as I would like to see it trade to" (21580.25).
- **How to identify:** a daily retracement leg (the high down to the retracement low) is the range; draw the extension of one quarter of that range above the old high with the Fib tool.
- **How to use:** draw/frame for targets or turtle-soup reversals at that level.
- **Example in this video:** NQ Dec 2024: Sunday video stated 21580.25 after the November/prior-week high was taken; Thursday traded above the high but stopped short of it.
- **Timestamps:** [0:00:52](https://youtu.be/403Dzt_Vl5Y?t=52) the level and the Fib reference · [0:01:40](https://youtu.be/403Dzt_Vl5Y?t=100) one-quarter rule · [0:02:27](https://youtu.be/403Dzt_Vl5Y?t=147) "not important for me to be accurate about that"
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** pairs with M24-050 where the same 21580.25 was introduced. Whether the "range" is measured from the retracement low or other swing is inferred from the Fib on his chart; the transcript only says "previous range".

title: NQ December 05, 2024 Seek & Destroy Review
head: Short entry with layered limit orders and market-structure shift off the 8 AM high
body:
- **Kind:** example only (live trade review)
- **What ICT says / what happened:**
  - Price traded up through the 8 AM high; on the rally the candle bodies broke down, a shift in market structure.
  - As price traded back above the old high, he went short; there was an immediate rebalance where price traded back up into the low, and he added there.
  - Price then attacked the level below; he had several limit orders layered below in case price did not reach 21490. Two limit orders filled; one went right to the target price but the spread prevented him exiting on it, and the remaining four contracts were not filled.
  - The market rallied back and hit his stop at about 21526 (caption reads "526"); he gave guidance on that live on X.
  - Price then went into range-bound consolidation.
- **How to use:** layered limit orders below allow for not reaching the ideal level; accept that partial fills and spread can prevent the last contracts from being filled.

title: NQ December 05, 2024 Seek & Destroy Review
head: 5-second chart short off a reclaimed SIBI (premium array), then sell-side run to the limit
body:
- **Kind:** entry model (example)
- **What ICT says / what happened:**
  - Price made high, higher high, higher high, then took out that high. In that small range he looks at the inefficiency and volume imbalance on a 5-second chart; candle bodies respect the SIBI's upper wick/high.
  - He went short aiming for the CE of the inefficiency and the volume imbalance. Entries on a 5-second chart are imperfect and he used market orders (buy/sell buttons) rather than limit orders, partly to show fills are real.
  - Price traded lower then back up into the array. He treats it as a premium array: a "reclaimed" SIBI (used once, then used again). Bodies respected the midpoint (CE) and then the high. He saw a bull-flag look that retail would buy and used the reclaimed SIBI to short again.
  - Price broke down and took out the low aggressively; thin price action on the way (versus back-and-forth chop earlier), leaving a nice new inefficiency; price came back up into it ("two of them; always give room for it to trade from the higher one") and then sold off aggressively into the 21490 level, where his limit order was filled.
- **How to identify:** SIBI in a short-term range at a premium; bodies (not just wicks) respecting its high/CE; retail-attractive bull flag pattern right at it.
- **How to use:** short with target at the CE/volume imbalance and the pre-planned level; reclaimed SIBI is a second chance entry.
- **Timestamps:** [0:08:06](https://youtu.be/403Dzt_Vl5Y?t=486) 5-second framing · [0:08:54](https://youtu.be/403Dzt_Vl5Y?t=534) bodies respecting the wick, short taken · [0:09:41](https://youtu.be/403Dzt_Vl5Y?t=581) reclaimed SIBI and bull flag · [0:10:30](https://youtu.be/403Dzt_Vl5Y?t=630) sell-off into 21490 limit fill
- **Nuance / caveats / changes:** his stated reason for not using limit orders on the 5-second entry: no time, and to prove fills with buy/sell buttons ("what you don't see when you're using Market Replay"). Mix of limit (planned level) and market (scalp entry) orders in the same day.
